entries.zh: 乾德元年正月，祀天南郊，大赦，加尊號為聖德明孝皇帝。
entries.en: In the first month of Qiande year 1 he sacrificed to Heaven at the southern suburb, proclaimed a general amnesty, and added the honorific Emperor Shengde Mingxiao.
entries.literal: In the first month of the first year of Qiande he sacrificed to Heaven at the southern suburb, proclaimed a general amnesty, and augmented his honorific to Emperor Shengde Mingxiao.

entries.zh: 二年冬，北巡，至於西縣，旌旗戈甲，連亙百餘里。
entries.en: In the winter of year 2 he toured north as far as Xixian, with banners, flags, weapons, and armor stretching more than a hundred li.
entries.literal: In the winter of the second year he toured north as far as Xixian; banners, flags, weapons, and armor stretched in an unbroken line for more than a hundred li.

entries.zh: 其還也，自閬州浮江而上，龍舟畫舸，昭耀江水，所在供億，人不堪命。
entries.en: On his return he went upriver from Lang Prefecture in dragon boats and painted barges that dazzled the waters. Every district along the route was levied beyond endurance.
entries.literal: On his return he went upriver by boat from Lang Prefecture; dragon boats and painted barges dazzled the river, and wherever he passed the levies of supplies were more than men could bear.

entries.zh: 三年正月，還成都。
entries.en: In the first month of year 3 he returned to Chengdu.
entries.literal: In the first month of the third year he returned to Chengdu.

entries.zh: 五年，起上清宮，塑王子晉像，尊以為聖祖至道玉宸皇帝，又塑建及衍像，侍立於其左右；
entries.en: In year 5 he built the Shangqing Palace, molded an image of Prince Zijin and honored him as the Holy Ancestor Emperor Yuchen of the Supreme Way, and molded images of Jian and Yan standing in attendance at his sides;
entries.literal: In the fifth year he built the Shangqing Palace, molded an image of Prince Zijin and honored him as the Holy Ancestor Emperor Yuchen of the Supreme Way, and also molded images of Jian and Yan standing in attendance at his left and right;

entries.zh: 又於正殿塑玄元皇帝及唐諸帝，備法駕而朝之。
entries.en: in the main hall he also molded the Mysterious Origin Emperor and the Tang emperors, arrayed the imperial equipage, and performed court before them.
entries.literal: in the main hall he also molded the Mysterious Origin Emperor and the emperors of Tang, arrayed the imperial equipage, and performed court to them.

entries.zh: 六年，以王承休為天雄節度使。
entries.en: In year 6 he appointed Wang Chengxiu military commissioner of Tianxiong.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he made Wang Chengxiu military commissioner of Tianxiong.

entries.zh: 天雄軍，秦州也。
entries.en: The Tianxiong army was stationed at Qin Prefecture.
entries.literal: The Tianxiong Army was at Qin Prefecture.

entries.zh: 承休以宦者得幸，為宣徽使，承休妻嚴氏，有絕色，衍通之。
entries.en: Chengxiu had gained favor as a eunuch and become palace attendant. His wife Lady Yan was surpassingly beautiful, and Yan took her as a lover.
entries.literal: Chengxiu as a eunuch had gained favor and become palace attendant; Chengxiu's wife Lady Yan was of surpassing beauty, and Yan had relations with her.

entries.zh: 是時，唐莊宗滅梁，蜀人皆懼。
entries.en: At this time Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong overthrew Liang, and the people of Shu were alarmed.
entries.literal: At this time Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong extinguished Liang, and the people of Shu were all afraid.

entries.zh: 莊宗遣李嚴聘蜀，衍與俱朝上清，而蜀都士庶，簾帷珠翠，夾道不絕。
entries.en: Zhuangzong sent Li Yan on a friendly mission to Shu. Yan accompanied him to court at Shangqing while the capital's gentry and commoners lined the road with curtains, pearls, and jade.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong sent Li Yan on a friendly mission to Shu; Yan accompanied him to court at Shangqing, while the gentry and commoners of the Shu capital with curtains, pearls, and jade lined the road without end.

entries.zh: 嚴見其人物富盛，而衍驕淫，歸乃獻策伐蜀。
entries.en: Yan saw a realm rich in people and goods but ruled by an arrogant, dissolute Yan, and on returning he urged an attack on Shu.
entries.literal: Yan saw its people and wealth in abundance yet Yan arrogant and dissolute; on returning he submitted a plan to attack Shu.

entries.zh: 明年，唐魏王繼岌、郭崇韜伐蜀。
entries.en: The next year Tang's Prince of Wei Jiji and Guo Chongtao invaded Shu.
entries.literal: The next year Tang's Prince of Wei Jiji and Guo Chongtao attacked Shu.

entries.zh: 是歲，衍改元曰咸康。
entries.en: That year Yan renamed the era Xiankang.
entries.literal: That year Yan changed the era name to Xiankang.

entries.zh: 衍自立，歲常獵於子來山。
entries.en: Since his accession Yan had hunted yearly at Mount Zilai.
entries.literal: Since Yan's accession he hunted yearly at Mount Zilai.

entries.zh: 是歲，又幸彭州陽平化、漢州三學山。
entries.en: That year he also visited Yangpinghua in Peng Prefecture and Sanxue Mountain in Han Prefecture.
entries.literal: That year he also visited Yangpinghua in Peng Prefecture and Sanxue Mountain in Han Prefecture.

entries.zh: 以王承休妻嚴氏故，十月，幸秦州，群臣切諫，衍不聽。
entries.en: For the sake of Wang Chengxiu's wife Lady Yan, in the tenth month he visited Qin Prefecture. His ministers urgently remonstrated, but Yan would not listen.
entries.literal: Because of Wang Chengxiu's wife Lady Yan, in the tenth month he visited Qin Prefecture; the ministers urgently remonstrated but Yan would not listen.

entries.zh: 行至梓潼，大風發屋拔木，太史曰：「此貪狼風也，當有敗軍殺將者。」
entries.en: At Zitong a great wind tore off roofs and uprooted trees. The grand astrologer said, "This is the Greedy Wolf wind—armies will be defeated and generals slain."
entries.literal: Reaching Zitong, a great wind tore off roofs and uprooted trees. The grand astrologer said: "This is the Greedy Wolf wind—there will be defeated armies and slain generals."

entries.zh: 衍不省。
entries.en: Yan took no notice.
entries.literal: Yan did not perceive it.

entries.zh: 衍至綿谷而唐師入其境，衍懼，遽還。
entries.en: When Yan reached Miangu and Tang troops entered Shu, he was alarmed and hurried back.
entries.literal: When Yan reached Miangu and Tang troops entered his territory, Yan was afraid and hurried back.

entries.zh: 唐師所至，州縣皆迎降。
entries.en: Wherever Tang troops went, prefectures and counties welcomed them and submitted.
entries.literal: Wherever Tang troops arrived, prefectures and counties all welcomed and submitted.

entries.zh: 衍留王宗弼守綿谷，遣王宗勛、宗儼、宗昱率兵以拒唐師。
entries.en: Yan left Wang Zongbi to hold Miangu and sent Wang Zongxun, Zongyan, and Zongyu with troops to resist Tang.
entries.literal: Yan left Wang Zongbi to hold Miangu and sent Wang Zongxun, Zongyan, and Zongyu to lead troops against the Tang army.

entries.zh: 宗勛等至三泉，望風退走。
entries.en: Zongxun and the others reached Sanquan and fled at the first sight of Tang forces.
entries.literal: Zongxun and the others reached Sanquan and fled at sight of the enemy.

entries.zh: 衍詔宗弼誅宗勛等，宗弼反與宗勛等合謀，送款於唐師。
entries.en: Yan ordered Zongbi to execute Zongxun and the others, but Zongbi instead conspired with them and submitted to Tang.
entries.literal: Yan ordered Zongbi to execute Zongxun and the others; Zongbi instead joined in conspiracy with them and sent submission to the Tang army.

entries.zh: 衍自綿谷還成都，百官及後宮迎謁七里亭，衍雜宮人作回鶻隊以入。
entries.en: Yan returned from Miangu to Chengdu. Officials and palace women welcomed him at Qili Pavilion, and he entered the city mixed with palace women arrayed as a Uighur company.
entries.literal: Yan returned from Miangu to Chengdu; the hundred officials and palace women welcomed him at Qili Pavilion, and Yan entered mixed with palace women formed as a Uighur company.

entries.zh: 明日，禦文明殿，與其群臣相對涕泣。
entries.en: The next day he held court at the Wenhua Hall and wept with his ministers face to face.
entries.literal: The next day he held court at the Wenhua Hall and wept face to face with his ministers.

entries.zh: 而宗弼亦自綿谷馳歸，登太玄門，收成都尹韓昭、宦者宋光嗣、景潤澄、歐陽晃等殺之，函首送於繼岌。
entries.en: Zongbi also galloped back from Miangu, mounted the Taixuan Gate, seized and killed Chengdu prefect Han Zhao and the eunuchs Song Guangsi, Jing Runcheng, and Ouyang Huang, boxed their heads, and sent them to Jiji.
entries.literal: Zongbi also galloped back from Miangu, mounted the Taixuan Gate, seized and killed Prefect of Chengdu Han Zhao and the eunuchs Song Guangsi, Jing Runcheng, and Ouyang Huang, boxed their heads and sent them to Jiji.

entries.zh: 衍即上表乞降，宗弼遷衍於天啟宮。
entries.en: Yan at once submitted a memorial begging to surrender, and Zongbi moved him to the Tianqi Palace.
entries.literal: Yan forthwith submitted a memorial begging to surrender; Zongbi moved Yan to the Tianqi Palace.

entries.zh: 魏王繼岌至成都，衍君臣面縛輿櫬，出降於七里亭。
entries.en: When the Prince of Wei Jiji reached Chengdu, Yan and his court came out bound, carrying coffins, and surrendered at Qili Pavilion.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Wei Jiji reached Chengdu, Yan and his court with faces bound and carrying coffins came out to surrender at Qili Pavilion.

entries.zh: 宗壽，許州民家子也。
entries.en: Zongshou was the son of a common family in Xuzhou.
entries.literal: Zongshou was the son of a common family in Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 建以同姓，錄之為子。
entries.en: Jian, sharing the surname Wang, adopted him as a son.
entries.literal: Jian, because they shared a surname, recorded him as a son.

entries.zh: 宗壽好學，工琴奕，為人恬退，喜道家之術，事建時為鎮江軍節度使。
entries.en: Zongshou loved learning and was skilled at the zither and go. Retiring by nature, he favored Daoist practices and served Jian as military commissioner of the Zhenjiang army.
entries.literal: Zongshou loved learning, was skilled at zither and go, by nature retiring and mild, fond of Daoist arts; while serving Jian he was military commissioner of the Zhenjiang Army.

entries.zh: 衍既立，宗壽為太子太保奉朝請，以煉丹養氣自娛。
entries.en: After Yan succeeded, Zongshou became junior guardian of the heir with court attendance and amused himself refining elixirs and cultivating breath.
entries.literal: After Yan succeeded, Zongshou became Junior Guardian of the Heir with attendance at court, amusing himself with elixir refinement and nourishing breath.

entries.zh: 衍為淫亂，獨宗壽常切諫之，後為武信軍節度使。
entries.en: Yan was dissolute, and only Zongshou often remonstrated sharply. He later became military commissioner of the Wuxin army.
entries.literal: Yan was dissolute; only Zongshou often remonstrated sharply, and later became military commissioner of the Wuxin Army.

entries.zh: 唐師伐蜀，所在迎降，魏王嘗以書招之，獨宗壽不降。
entries.en: When Tang invaded Shu, districts everywhere welcomed and submitted. The Prince of Wei once wrote to recruit him, but Zongshou alone refused.
entries.literal: When Tang troops attacked Shu, wherever they went they were welcomed in submission; the Prince of Wei once sent a letter to recruit him, but Zongshou alone did not submit.

entries.zh: 聞衍已銜璧，大慟，從衍東遷，至岐陽，以賂賂守者，得入見衍，衍泣下沾襟，曰：「早從王言，豈有今日！」
entries.en: Hearing that Yan had already surrendered with the jade disk, he grieved greatly and followed him east. At Qiyang he bribed the guards and gained an audience. Yan wept until his robe was soaked and said, "Had I followed your counsel earlier, how could this day have come!"
entries.literal: Hearing that Yan had already offered the jade disk in surrender, he grieved greatly and followed Yan eastward; reaching Qiyang, he bribed the guards and gained entry to see Yan. Yan wept until his breast was wet and said: "Had I early followed the prince's words, how could there be today!"

entries.zh: 衍死，宗壽走澠池，聞莊宗遇弒，亡入熊耳山。
entries.en: After Yan's death Zongshou fled to Mianchi. Hearing that Zhuangzong had been assassinated, he hid in Mount Xiong'er.
entries.literal: After Yan's death Zongshou fled to Mianchi; hearing that Zhuangzong had been assassinated, he went into hiding in Mount Xiong'er.

entries.zh: 天成二年，出詣京師，上書求衍宗族葬之。
entries.en: In Tiancheng year 2 he emerged and went to the capital, submitting a memorial asking permission to bury Yan's clan.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tiancheng he came out and went to the capital, submitting a memorial asking to bury Yan's clan.

entries.zh: 明宗嘉其忠，以為保義軍行軍司馬，封衍順正公，許以諸侯禮葬之。
entries.en: Emperor Ming praised his loyalty, appointed him acting military secretary of the Baoyi army, enfeoffed him as Duke Shunzheng of Yan, and permitted burial with feudal honors.
entries.literal: Emperor Ming praised his loyalty, made him acting military secretary of the Baoyi Army, enfeoffed Yan as Duke Shunzheng, and permitted burial with the rites of a feudal lord.

entries.zh: 宗壽得王氏十八喪，葬之長安南三趙村。
entries.en: Zongshou recovered the eighteen coffins of the Wang house and buried them at Sanzhao Village south of Chang'an.
entries.literal: Zongshou obtained the eighteen coffins of the Wang house and buried them at Sanzhao Village south of Chang'an.

entries.zh: 莊宗召衍入洛，賜衍詔曰：「固當列土而封，必不薄人於險，三辰在上，一言不欺！」
entries.en: Zhuangzong summoned Yan to Luoyang and bestowed an edict: "Surely you shall be enfeoffed with territory; surely no man shall be wronged in peril—the three luminaries are above, and not one word shall deceive!"
entries.literal: Zhuangzong summoned Yan to Luoyang and bestowed an edict on him: "Surely territory shall be enfeoffed to you; surely no man shall be wronged in peril—the three luminaries are above, and not one word shall deceive!"

entries.zh: 衍捧詔忻然就道，率其宗族及偽宰相王鍇、張格、瘐傳素、許寂、翰林學士李旻等，及諸將佐家族數千人以東。
entries.en: Yan received the edict gladly and set out east with his clan, the former chief ministers Wang Kai, Zhang Ge, Yu Chuansu, Xu Ji, Hanlin academician Li Min, and the families of his generals and aides—several thousand people in all.
entries.literal: Yan received the edict gladly and set out on the road, leading his clan and the false chief ministers Wang Kai, Zhang Ge, Yu Chuansu, Xu Ji, Hanlin Academician Li Min, and others, together with the families of generals and aides numbering several thousand, eastward.

entries.zh: 同光四年四月，行至秦川驛，莊宗用伶人景進計，遣宦者向延嗣誅其族。
entries.en: In the fourth month of Tongguang year 4, at Qinchuan Post Station, Zhuangzong followed the actor Jing Jin's advice and sent the eunuch Xiang Yansi to execute his entire clan.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year of Tongguang, reaching Qinchuan Post Station, Zhuangzong used the actor Jing Jin's plan and sent the eunuch Xiang Yansi to execute his clan.

entries.zh: 衍母徐氏臨刑呼曰：「吾兒以一國迎降，反以為戮，信義俱棄，吾知其禍不旋踵矣！」
entries.en: Yan's mother Lady Xu cried out at the execution, "My son surrendered a whole state and is repaid with slaughter—faith and righteousness both cast aside. I know disaster will follow without delay!"
entries.literal: Yan's mother Lady Xu cried out at execution: "My son surrendered a whole state and is repaid with slaughter—faith and righteousness both cast aside; I know disaster will not wait!"

entries.zh: 衍妾劉氏，鬒發如雲而有色，行刑者將免之，劉氏曰：「家國喪亡，義不受辱！」
entries.en: Yan's concubine Lady Liu, with hair black as clouds and great beauty, was about to be spared. She said, "State and house are lost—I will not accept disgrace!"
entries.literal: Yan's concubine Lady Liu, with black hair like clouds and great beauty, was about to be spared by the executioners; Lady Liu said: "State and house are lost—by right I will not accept disgrace!"

entries.zh: 遂就死。
entries.en: She then went to her death.
entries.literal: She then accepted death.

entries.zh: 宗弼，本姓魏，名弘夫，建錄為養子。
entries.en: Zongbi, born Wei Hongfu, was adopted by Jian.
entries.literal: Zongbi, original surname Wei, name Hongfu, was recorded by Jian as an adopted son.

entries.zh: 建攻顧彥暉，宗弼常以建語泄之彥暉者，彥暉敗，建待之如初。
entries.en: When Jian attacked Gu Yanhui, Zongbi had often leaked Jian's plans to Yanhui. After Yanhui's defeat, Jian treated him as before.
entries.literal: When Jian attacked Gu Yanhui, Zongbi had often leaked Jian's words to Yanhui; when Yanhui was defeated Jian treated him as before.

entries.zh: 建病且卒，宗弼守太師兼中書令、判六軍，輔政。
entries.en: When Jian fell ill near death, Zongbi served as grand preceptor and director of the Secretariat with charge of the Six Armies and assisted in government.
entries.literal: When Jian was ill and near death, Zongbi held Grand Preceptor with concurrent Director of the Secretariat and charge of the Six Armies, assisting in government.

entries.zh: 衍已降，宗弼以蜀珍寶奉魏王及郭崇韜，求為西川節度使，魏王曰：「此我家物也，何用獻為？」
entries.en: After Yan surrendered, Zongbi presented Shu's treasures to the Prince of Wei and Guo Chongtao and asked to be made Xichuan military commissioner. The prince said, "These are my family's things—why present them?"
entries.literal: After Yan had surrendered, Zongbi presented Shu's treasures to the Prince of Wei and Guo Chongtao and sought to be Xichuan military commissioner. The Prince of Wei said: "These are my family's things—why present them?"

entries.zh: 居數日，為崇韜所殺。
entries.en: A few days later Chongtao had him killed.
entries.literal: After several days he was killed by Chongtao.

entries.zh: 王建，字光圖，許州舞陽人也。
entries.en: Wang Jian, whose courtesy name was Guangtu, came from Wuyang in Xuzhou.
entries.literal: Wang Jian, courtesy name Guangtu, was a native of Wuyang in Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 隆眉廣顙，狀貌偉然。
entries.en: He had heavy brows and a broad forehead, and his bearing was imposing.
entries.literal: Heavy brows and a broad forehead, his appearance imposing.

entries.zh: 少無賴，以屠牛、盜驢、販私鹽為事，里人謂之「賊王八」。
entries.en: As a young man he was a rascal who made his living slaughtering oxen, stealing donkeys, and smuggling salt; neighbors called him "Bandit Wang Eight."
entries.literal: In youth he was a rascal, making his living slaughtering oxen, stealing donkeys, and trafficking in illicit salt; the neighborhood called him "Bandit Wang Eight."

entries.zh: 後為忠武軍卒，稍遷隊將。
entries.en: He later enlisted in the Zhongwu Army and gradually rose to company commander.
entries.literal: Later he became a soldier of the Zhongwu Army and gradually rose to company commander.

entries.zh: 是時，契丹滅晉，漢高祖起於太原，中國多故，雄武軍節度使何建以秦、成、階三州附於蜀，昶因遣孫漢韶攻下鳳州，於是悉有王衍故地。
entries.en: The Khitan had destroyed Jin and Han Gaozu had risen at Taiyuan; the central plains were in turmoil. Heroic Martial commissioner He Jian submitted Qin, Cheng, and Jie prefectures to Shu. Chang sent Sun Hanshao to take Feng Prefecture and thereby recovered all of Wang Yan's former territory.
entries.literal: At that time the Khitan destroyed Jin and Han Gaozu rose at Taiyuan; the central lands had many troubles. Heroic Martial Army military commissioner He Jian attached Qin, Cheng, and Jie prefectures to Shu. Chang thereupon sent Sun Hanshao to storm Feng Prefecture, and thereby possessed all of Wang Yan's former territory.

entries.zh: 漢將趙思綰據永興、王景崇據鳳翔反，皆送款於昶。
entries.en: Han generals Zhao Sixuan at Yongxing and Wang Jingchong at Fengxiang rebelled and both offered their allegiance to Chang.
entries.literal: Han generals Zhao Sixuan held Yongxing and Wang Jingchong held Fengxiang in rebellion; both sent pledges of allegiance to Chang.

entries.zh: 昶遣張虔釗出大散關，何建出隴右，李廷珪出子午谷，以應思綰。
entries.en: Chang sent Zhang Qianzhao through Great Scatter Pass, He Jian through the Longyou region, and Li Tinggui through Ziwu Valley to support Sixuan.
entries.literal: Chang sent Zhang Qianzhao out through Great Scatter Pass, He Jian out through the Longyou region, and Li Tinggui out through Ziwu Valley to respond to Sixuan.

entries.zh: 昶相母昭裔切諫，以為不可，然昶誌欲窺關中甚銳，乃遣安思謙益兵以東。
entries.en: Chancellor Mu Zhaoyi remonstrated sharply that the move was unwise, but Chang was eager to probe the Guanzhong region and sent An Siqian east with reinforcements.
entries.literal: Chancellor Mu Zhaoyi remonstrated urgently, thinking it could not be done, but Chang's will to peer into the Guanzhong region was very keen, and he therefore sent An Siqian with added troops east.

entries.zh: 已而漢誅思綰、景崇，虔釗等皆罷歸，而思謙恥於無功，多殺士卒以威眾。
entries.en: Han soon executed Sixuan and Jingchong, and Qianzhao and the others withdrew. Siqian, shamed by his failure, killed many soldiers to intimidate his men.
entries.literal: Before long Han executed Sixuan and Jingchong; Qianzhao and the others all withdrew and returned, while Siqian, ashamed at achieving nothing, killed many soldiers to awe the masses.

entries.zh: 昶與翰林使王藻謀殺思謙，而邊吏有急奏，藻不以時聞，輒啟其封，昶怒之。
entries.en: Chang plotted with Hanlin envoy Wang Zao to kill Siqian. When an urgent frontier report arrived, Zao failed to forward it promptly and opened the seal himself; Chang was furious.
entries.literal: Chang plotted with Hanlin envoy Wang Zao to kill Siqian. A frontier official had an urgent memorial, but Zao did not report it in time and opened its seal on his own; Chang was angry at him.

entries.zh: 其殺思謙也，藻方侍側，因並擒藻斬之。
entries.en: When Siqian was killed, Zao was attending at his side and was seized and beheaded as well.
entries.literal: When he killed Siqian, Zao was attending at his side; he therefore seized Zao as well and beheaded him.

entries.zh: 劉光乂攻夔州，守將高彥儔戰敗，閉牙城拒守，判官羅濟勸其走，彥儔曰：「吾昔不能守秦川，今又奔北，雖人主不殺我，我何面目見蜀人乎！」
entries.en: Liu Guangyi attacked Kui Prefecture. Garrison commander Gao Yanchou was beaten, shut himself in the headquarters city, and refused to yield. Administrative aide Luo Ji urged flight. Yanchou said: "I failed to hold Qinchuan before; if I flee north again, even if the emperor spares me, what face have I to show the people of Shu!"
entries.literal: Liu Guangyi attacked Kui Prefecture. Garrison commander Gao Yanchou was defeated in battle, closed the headquarters city and refused to yield. Administrative aide Luo Ji urged him to flee. Yanchou said: "I could not hold Qinchuan before; now if I flee north again, even if my lord does not kill me, what face have I to meet the people of Shu!"

entries.zh: 又勸其降，彥儔不許，乃自焚死。
entries.en: When Ji urged surrender, Yanchou refused and burned himself to death.
entries.literal: He again urged him to surrender; Yanchou would not agree and burned himself to death.

entries.zh: 而蜀兵所在奔潰，將帥多被擒獲。
entries.en: Shu troops everywhere broke and fled, and most commanders were captured.
entries.literal: Meanwhile Shu troops everywhere broke and fled; generals and commanders were mostly captured.

entries.zh: 昶問計於左右，老將石頵以謂東兵遠來，勢不能久，宜聚兵堅守以敝之。
entries.en: Chang asked his advisers for counsel. The veteran Shi Yun said the eastern army had come from far away and could not sustain a long campaign; they should mass their forces and hold out to wear the enemy down.
entries.literal: Chang asked those at his side for a plan. The old general Shi Yun said that eastern troops had come from afar and by their momentum could not last long; they should gather troops and hold firm to wear them down.

entries.zh: 昶嘆曰：「吾與先君以溫衣美食養士四十年，一旦臨敵，不能為吾東向放一箭，雖欲堅壁，誰與吾守者邪！」
entries.en: Chang sighed: "My father and I clothed and fed these men generously for forty years, yet when the enemy comes not one will shoot an arrow eastward for me. Even if I wanted to hold behind walls, who would stand with me!"
entries.literal: Chang sighed and said: "My late father and I fed and clothed soldiers warmly for forty years; yet once we face the enemy they cannot shoot a single arrow eastward for me. Even if I wished to hold firm behind walls, who would hold them with me!"

entries.zh: 乃命李昊草表以降，時乾德三年正月也。
entries.en: He ordered Li Hao to draft the surrender memorial. It was the first month of the third year of Qiande.
entries.literal: He then ordered Li Hao to draft a memorial of surrender; it was the first month of the third year of Qiande.

entries.zh: 自興師至昶降，凡六十六日。
entries.en: From the opening of the campaign to Chang's surrender, sixty-six days had passed.
entries.literal: From the raising of troops to Chang's surrender, altogether sixty-six days.

entries.zh: 初，昊事王衍為翰林學士，衍之亡也，昊為草降表，至是又草焉，蜀人夜表其門曰「世修降表李家」，當時傳以為笑。
entries.en: Hao had earlier served Wang Yan as Hanlin Academician and drafted Yan's surrender; now he drafted Chang's as well. The people of Shu posted on his gate by night: "The Li family—hereditary drafters of surrender memorials," and the line became a byword for ridicule.
entries.literal: Earlier Hao had served Wang Yan as Hanlin Academician; when Yan perished Hao drafted the surrender memorial, and now drafted it again. The people of Shu posted on his gate by night the words "The Li family, hereditary drafters of surrender memorials," and at the time it was passed around as a joke.

entries.zh: 孟知祥，字保胤，邢州龍岡人也。
entries.en: Meng Zhixiang, whose courtesy name was Baoyin, was a native of Longgang in Xing Prefecture.
entries.literal: Meng Zhixiang, style name Baoyin, was a man of Longgang in Xing Prefecture.

entries.zh: 其叔父遷，當唐之末，據邢、洺、磁三州，為晉所虜。
entries.en: His uncle Qian, in the closing years of the Tang, seized control of Xing, Ming, and Ci prefectures and was taken captive by Jin.
entries.literal: His uncle Qian, at the end of the Tang, held the three prefectures of Xing, Ming, and Ci, and was captured by Jin.

entries.zh: 晉王以遷守澤潞，梁兵攻晉，遷以澤潞降梁。
entries.en: The Prince of Jin put Qian in charge of Ze and Lu; when Liang forces attacked Jin, Qian surrendered those circuits to Liang.
entries.literal: The Prince of Jin had Qian defend Ze and Lu; Liang troops attacked Jin, and Qian surrendered Ze and Lu to Liang.

entries.zh: 知祥父道，獨留事晉而不顯。
entries.en: Zhixiang's father Dao alone stayed on to serve Jin and never rose to prominence.
entries.literal: Zhixiang's father Dao alone remained to serve Jin and did not become prominent.

entries.zh: 及知祥壯，晉王以其弟克讓女妻之，以為左教練使。
entries.en: Once Zhixiang reached manhood, the Prince of Jin married him to a daughter of his younger brother Kerang and made him Left Training Commissioner.
entries.literal: When Zhixiang came of age, the Prince of Jin gave him in marriage a daughter of his younger brother Kerang and appointed him Left Training Commissioner.

entries.zh: 莊宗為晉王，以知祥為中門使。
entries.en: While Zhuangzong was still Prince of Jin, he appointed Zhixiang Commissioner of the Inner Gate.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong was Prince of Jin, he made Zhixiang Commissioner of the Inner Gate.

entries.zh: 前此為中門使者多以罪誅，知祥懼，求他職，莊宗命知祥薦可代己者，知祥因薦郭崇韜自代，崇韜德之，知祥遷馬步軍都虞候。
entries.en: Earlier holders of the Inner Gate commission had mostly been put to death on criminal charges, and Zhixiang, fearing the same fate, asked for another post. Zhuangzong told him to name his own successor; Zhixiang recommended Guo Chongtao to take his place. Chongtao was grateful, and Zhixiang was promoted to Chief Garrison Officer of the horse and foot armies.
entries.literal: Previously those who served as Commissioner of the Inner Gate were mostly executed for crimes; Zhixiang was afraid and sought another post. Zhuangzong ordered Zhixiang to recommend someone who could replace him; Zhixiang therefore recommended Guo Chongtao to replace himself. Chongtao was grateful to him, and Zhixiang was transferred to Chief Garrison Officer of the horse and foot armies.

entries.zh: 莊宗建號，以太原為北京，以知祥為太原尹、北京留守。
entries.en: After Zhuangzong proclaimed his dynasty, he designated Taiyuan the Northern Capital and appointed Zhixiang Taiyuan Intendant and regent of the Northern Capital.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong established his reign title, he made Taiyuan the Northern Capital and appointed Zhixiang Taiyuan Intendant and Northern Capital regent.

entries.zh: 三年，殺其弟洪雅，又殺劉思潮等五人。
entries.en: In the third year he killed his younger brother Hongya and also killed Liu Sixiang and five others.
entries.literal: In the third year he killed his younger brother Hongya and also killed Liu Sixiang and five others.

entries.zh: 思潮等死，陳道庠懼，不自安，其友鄧伸以荀悅《漢紀》遺之，道庠莫能曉，伸罵曰：「憝獠！
entries.en: When Sixiang and the rest were dead, Chen Daoxiang was afraid and ill at ease. His friend Deng Shen gave him Xun Yue’s Hanji (Records of Han), but Daoxiang could not understand it. Shen cursed, "You brute!
entries.literal: When Sixiang and the rest died, Chen Daoxiang was afraid and ill at ease. His friend Deng Shen gave him Xun Yue’s Hanji (Records of Han), but Daoxiang could not understand it. Shen cursed: "You brute!

entries.zh: 韓信誅而彭越醢，皆在此書矣！」
entries.en: Han Xin was executed and Peng Yue was minced — it is all in this book!"
entries.literal: Han Xin was executed and Peng Yue was minced — it is all in this book!"

entries.zh: 道庠悟，益懼。
entries.en: Daoxiang understood and grew still more afraid.
entries.literal: Daoxiang understood and grew still more afraid.

entries.zh: 晟聞之大怒，以道庠、伸下獄，皆斬之於市，夷其族。
entries.en: When Sheng heard of it he was furious, threw Daoxiang and Shen into prison, beheaded them both in the market, and exterminated their clans.
entries.literal: When Sheng heard of it he was greatly angered, threw Daoxiang and Shen into prison, beheaded them both in the market, and exterminated their clans.

entries.zh: 以右僕射王翻為英州刺史，使人殺之於路。
entries.en: He appointed Right Vice Director Wang Fan prefect of Yingzhou and had men kill him on the road.
entries.literal: He appointed Right Vice Director Wang Fan prefect of Yingzhou and had men kill him on the road.

entries.zh: 劉隱，其祖安仁，上蔡人也，後徙閩中，商賈南海，因家焉。
entries.en: Liu Yin’s grandfather Anren was a native of Shangcai. The family later moved to Minzhong and went into trade in the Southern Sea, where they eventually settled.
entries.literal: Liu Yin — his grandfather Anren was a man of Shangcai; later the family moved to Minzhong, traded as merchants in the Southern Sea, and thus made their home there.

entries.zh: 父謙，為廣州牙將。
entries.en: His father Qian served as a military adjutant at Guangzhou.
entries.literal: His father Qian served as a military adjutant at Guangzhou.

entries.zh: 唐乾符五年，黃巢攻破廣州，去略湖、湘間，廣州表謙封州刺史、賀江鎮遏使，以禦梧、桂以西。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Qianfu of the Tang, Huang Chao took Guangzhou and then marched to plunder the lake country and the Xiang region. Guangzhou recommended Qian for prefect of Fengzhou and commissioner for suppressing Hejiang, to hold the line against foes west of Wuzhou and Guilin.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Qianfu of Tang, Huang Chao captured Guangzhou and then turned to ravage the lakes and Xiang region. Guangzhou memorialized recommending Qian as prefect of Fengzhou and military commissioner for suppressing Hejiang, to defend against threats west of Wuzhou and Guilin.

entries.zh: 歲餘，有兵萬人，戰艦百餘艘。
entries.en: Within a year he had raised ten thousand troops and more than a hundred warships.
entries.literal: Within a year he had ten thousand troops and more than a hundred warships.

entries.zh: 謙三子，曰隱、台、巖。
entries.en: Qian had three sons: Yin, Tai, and Yan.
entries.literal: Qian had three sons, named Yin, Tai, and Yan.

entries.zh: 天復二年，封镠越王。
entries.en: In the second year of Tianfu, Qian Liu was enfeoffed as King of Yue.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tianfu, Liu was enfeoffed as King of Yue.

entries.zh: 镠巡衣錦城，武勇右都指揮使徐綰與左都指揮使許再思叛，焚掠城郭，攻內城，镠子傳瑛及其將馬綽、陳為等閉門拒之。
entries.en: While Qian Liu was touring Brocade-Robed City, Xu Kuo, Right Commandant of Martial Valour, and Xu Zaisi, Left Commandant, rose in revolt. They burned and looted the outer city and assaulted the inner citadel. Liu's son Chuanying, with the generals Ma Chuo and Chen Wei among others, barred the gates and held them off.
entries.literal: While Liu was inspecting Brocade-Robed City, Right Commandant of Martial Valor Xu Kuo and Left Commandant Xu Zaisi rebelled, burned and plundered the city walls, attacked the inner city, and Liu's son Chuanying together with his generals Ma Chuo, Chen Wei, and others shut the gates to resist them.

entries.zh: 镠歸，至北郭門不得入。
entries.en: When Qian Liu returned he found himself shut out at the North Suburban Gate.
entries.literal: Liu returned, reached the North Suburban Gate, and could not enter.

entries.zh: 成及代镠與綰戰，斬首百餘級，綰屯龍興寺。
entries.en: Cheng Ji fought Kuo in Liu's place, took more than a hundred heads, and Kuo withdrew to Longxing Temple.
entries.literal: Cheng Ji fought in Liu's stead against Kuo, beheaded more than a hundred, and Kuo encamped at Longxing Temple.

entries.zh: 镠微服逾城而入，遣馬綽、王榮、杜建徽等分屯諸門，使顧全武備東府，全武曰：「東府不足慮，可慮者淮南爾，綰急，必召淮兵至，患不細矣。
entries.en: Liu slipped in disguised as a commoner. He posted Ma Chuo, Wang Rong, and Du Jianhui at the various gates and ordered Gu Quanwu to secure the Eastern Capital. Quanwu said: "The Eastern Capital is no great concern—the real worry is Huainan. Once Kuo grows desperate he will call in troops from the Huai, and the trouble will be serious.
entries.literal: Liu in plain dress crossed the wall to enter, dispatched Ma Chuo, Wang Rong, Du Jianhui, and others to encamp separately at the various gates, and had Gu Quanwu prepare defenses for the Eastern Capital; Quanwu said: "The Eastern Capital is not worth worrying over—what is worrisome is Huainan alone; when Kuo grows desperate he is sure to summon Huainan troops, and the danger will not be small.

entries.zh: 楊公大丈夫，今以難告，必能閔我。」
entries.en: Lord Yang is a man of stature. If we confide our plight to him now, he will surely show us mercy."
entries.literal: Lord Yang is a true great man; if we now tell him of our distress, he will surely pity us."

entries.zh: 鏐以為然。
entries.en: Qian Liu agreed.
entries.literal: Liu thought this correct.

entries.zh: 全武曰：「獨行，事必不濟，請擇諸公子可行者。」
entries.en: Quanwu said: "If one man goes alone the mission will fail. Choose whichever of your sons is fit to accompany me."
entries.literal: Quanwu said: "Alone, the affair will certainly not succeed; please choose from among your sons one who can go."

entries.zh: 镠曰：「吾嘗欲以元璙婚楊氏。」
entries.en: Qian Liu replied: "I have long wished to marry Qian Yuan Liao into the Yang family."
entries.literal: Liu said: "I have long wished to marry Yuan Liao to the Yang clan."

entries.zh: 乃使隨全武如廣陵。
entries.en: He sent Qian Yuan Liao to accompany Quanwu to Guangling.
entries.literal: He then had him follow Quanwu to Guangling.

entries.zh: 綰果召田頵於宣州。
entries.en: As expected, Xu Kuo summoned Tian Jun from Xuanzhou.
entries.literal: Kuo indeed summoned Tian Jun from Xuanzhou.

entries.zh: 全武等至廣陵，行密以女妻元璙，亟召頵還。
entries.en: When Quanwu and his party reached Guangling, Yang Xingmi gave his daughter to Qian Yuan Liao in marriage and urgently recalled Tian Jun.
entries.literal: Quanwu and the others reached Guangling; Xingmi gave his daughter in marriage to Yuan Liao and urgently summoned Jun back.

entries.zh: 頵取镠錢百萬，質镠子元瓘而歸。
entries.en: Tian Jun took a million strings of Qian Liu's silver, accepted Liu's son Qian Yuanguan as hostage, and marched home.
entries.literal: Jun took one million of Liu's cash, took Liu's son Yuanguan as hostage, and returned.

entries.zh: 王延義、延政兄弟相攻，卓儼明、朱文進、李仁達等自相篡殺，連兵不解者數年。
entries.en: The brothers Wang Yanyi and Wang Yanzheng turned on each other; Zhuo Yanming, Zhu Wenjin, Li Renda, and others seized and slaughtered one another in turn. War dragged on for years without pause.
entries.literal: The brothers Wang Yanyi and Yanzheng fought each other; Zhuo Yanming, Zhu Wenjin, Li Renda, and others overthrew and killed one another in succession; armies were continuously engaged for several years.

entries.zh: 仁達附於李景，已而又叛，景兵攻之，仁達求救於佐。
entries.en: Li Renda submitted to Li Jing, then rebelled again. When Jing's army attacked him, Renda begged Qian Zuo for aid.
entries.literal: Renda submitted to Li Jing, then rebelled again; Jing's army attacked him; Renda begged Zuo for rescue.

entries.zh: 佐召諸將計事，諸將皆不欲行，佐奮然曰：「吾為元帥，而不能舉兵邪？
entries.en: Zuo called his generals to council. None wanted to march. He flushed and said, "I am commander-in-chief—can I not raise an army?
entries.literal: Zuo summoned the generals to discuss the matter; none wished to go; Zuo stirred himself and said: "I am commander-in-chief—can I not raise troops?

entries.zh: 諸將吾家素畜養，獨不肯以身先我乎？
entries.en: You generals my house has fed and kept all these years—will not one of you go before me?
entries.literal: You generals my family has always kept and nurtured—will none of you alone lead the way before me?

entries.zh: 有異吾議者斬！」
entries.en: Whoever opposes me—off with his head!"
entries.literal: Whoever disagrees with me, behead him!”

entries.zh: 乃遣其統軍使張筠、趙承泰等率兵三萬，水陸赴之。
entries.en: He sent Army Controller Zhang Yun, Zhao Chengtai, and others with thirty thousand men by land and water to their relief.
entries.literal: Thereupon he sent his army controller Zhang Yun, Zhao Chengtai, and others with thirty thousand troops, going by land and water to hurry to their aid.

entries.zh: 遣將誓軍，號令齊整。
entries.en: He dispatched a general to swear in the troops; commands rang out in tight order.
entries.literal: He sent a general to swear in the army; orders and ranks were arrayed in good order.

entries.zh: 筠等大敗景兵，俘馘萬計，獲其將楊業、蔡遇等，遂取福州而還，由是諸將皆服。
entries.en: Zhang Yun and the rest routed Li Jing's army. Captives and severed heads numbered in the tens of thousands; they took Jing's generals Yang Ye, Cai Yu, and others, seized Fuzhou, and returned. From that day the generals submitted in earnest.
entries.literal: Yun and the others utterly defeated Jing's army; captives and severed heads numbered in the tens of thousands; they took his generals Yang Ye, Cai Yu, and others; they then took Fuzhou and returned—and from this the generals all submitted.

entries.zh: 世宗征淮南，詔俶攻常、宣二州以牽李景，俶治國中兵以待。
entries.en: When Emperor Shizong marched on Huainan, he ordered Chu to strike Chang and Xuan prefectures to pin down Li Jing. Chu mustered the realm's forces and waited.
entries.literal: When Emperor Shizong campaigned against Huainan, he ordered Chu to attack Chang and Xuan prefectures to tie down Li Jing; Chu prepared the realm's troops and waited.

entries.zh: 景聞周師將大舉，乃遣使安撫，境上皆戒嚴。
entries.en: Li Jing heard the Zhou army was about to move in strength and sent envoys to soothe the borders. Every frontier post went on alert.
entries.literal: Jing heard the Zhou army was about to march in force; he sent envoys to mollify border regions; all along the frontier they went on alert.

entries.zh: 蘇州候吏陳滿不知景使，以謂朝廷已克諸州，遣使安撫矣，亟言於俶，請舉兵以應。
entries.en: Chen Man, a border clerk at Suzhou, did not know Jing's envoys had arrived. He thought the court had already captured the prefectures and sent pacifying envoys, and urgently urged Chu to raise troops in response.
entries.literal: Chen Man, a frontier clerk at Suzhou, did not know Jing's envoys had come; thinking the court had already taken the prefectures and sent envoys to pacify the region, he urgently reported to Chu and asked that troops be raised in response.

entries.zh: 俶相國吳程遽調兵以出，相國元德昭以為王師必未渡淮，與程爭於俶前，不可奪。
entries.en: Chancellor Wu Cheng hurriedly mobilized and marched out. Chancellor Yuan Dezhao argued before Chu that the imperial army surely had not yet crossed the Huai and disputed with Cheng, but could not prevail.
entries.literal: Chu's chancellor Wu Cheng hurriedly mobilized and marched out; Chancellor Yuan Dezhao held that the imperial army surely had not yet crossed the Huai, and disputed with Cheng before Chu—he could not be overborne.

entries.zh: 程等攻常州，果為景將柴克宏所敗，程裨將邵可遷力戰，可遷子死馬前，猶戰不顧，程等僅以身免。
entries.en: Wu Cheng and the rest attacked Changzhou and were beaten by Li Jing's general Chai Kehong. Cheng's lieutenant Shao Keqian fought on fiercely; his son fell dead before his horse, yet he still would not turn back. Cheng and the others barely escaped with their lives.
entries.literal: Cheng and the others attacked Changzhou and were indeed defeated by Jing's general Chai Kehong; Cheng's lieutenant Shao Keqian fought hard; Keqian's son died before his horse yet he still fought without looking back; Cheng and the others barely escaped with their lives.

entries.zh: 周師渡淮，俶乃盡括國中丁民益兵，使邵可遷等以戰船四百艘、水軍萬七千人至於通州以會期。
entries.en: Once the Zhou army crossed the Huai, Chu conscripted every able-bodied man in the realm to swell his ranks and sent Shao Keqian and others with four hundred warships and seventeen thousand sailors to Tongzhou for the rendezvous.
entries.literal: When the Zhou army crossed the Huai, Chu then conscripted every able-bodied man in the realm to augment his forces and sent Shao Keqian and others with four hundred warships and seventeen thousand naval troops to Tongzhou to meet the appointed rendezvous.

entries.zh: 錢镠，字具美，杭州臨安人也。
entries.en: Qian Liu, whose style name was Jumei, came from Lin'an in Hangzhou.
entries.literal: Qian Liu, styled Jumei, was a native of Lin'an in Hangzhou.

entries.zh: 臨安里中有大木，镠幼時與群兒戲木下，镠坐大石指麾群兒為隊伍，號令頗有法，群兒皆憚之。
entries.en: A great tree stood in his neighborhood in Lin'an. As a boy Liu played beneath it, seated on a large stone while he drilled the other children into formation; his commands were surprisingly disciplined, and the boys all stood in awe of him.
entries.literal: In his village in Lin'an there was a great tree; when Liu was young he played with other boys beneath it, sitting on a large stone and directing them into ranks; his orders were quite orderly, and all the boys feared him.

entries.zh: 及壯，無賴，不喜事生業，以販鹽為盜。
entries.en: When he came of age he was a wastrel who shunned honest work and lived by smuggling salt and raiding as an outlaw.
entries.literal: When he grew up he was a ruffian, took no interest in honest livelihood, and made a living smuggling salt as a bandit.

entries.zh: 縣錄事鐘起有子數人，與镠飲博，起嘗禁其諸子，諸子多竊從之遊。
entries.en: Zhong Qi, the county registrar, had several sons who drank and gambled with Liu. Qi tried to keep his sons away, but they often slipped off to join Liu anyway.
entries.literal: The county registrar Zhong Qi had several sons who drank and gambled with Liu; Qi once forbade his sons, but they often stole away to keep company with him.

entries.zh: 豫章人有善術者，望牛鬥間有王氣。
entries.en: A practitioner of divination from Yuzhang observed the Ox and Dipper asterisms and discerned an aura of kingship there.
entries.literal: A man of Yuzhang skilled in occult arts gazed at the region between the Ox and Dipper constellations and saw a kingly aura.

entries.zh: 牛鬥，錢塘分也，因遊錢塘。
entries.en: Since those constellations corresponded to the Qiantang area, he went there to investigate.
entries.literal: The Ox and Dipper lay in the Qiantang region, so he traveled to Qiantang.

entries.zh: 占之在臨安，乃之臨安，以相法隱市中，陰求其人。
entries.en: His readings pointed to Lin'an, so he went there, set up as a face-reader in the marketplace, and quietly searched for the man of destiny.
entries.literal: His divination placed the man in Lin'an; he went to Lin'an, concealed himself in the market practicing physiognomy, and secretly sought the person.

entries.zh: 起與術者善，術者私謂起曰：「占君縣有貴人，求之市中不可得，視君之相貴矣，然不足當之。」
entries.en: Qi knew the diviner well. The man took Qi aside and said, "My readings say a man of great rank is in your county, but I cannot find him in the markets. You yourself look distinguished, yet you are not the one the stars foretell."
entries.literal: Qi was on good terms with the adept, who privately told Qi, "Your county has a noble man; I cannot find him in the market. By your features you are noble, yet not noble enough to match it."

entries.zh: 起乃為置酒，悉召賢豪為會，陰令術者遍視之，皆不足當。
entries.en: Qi hosted a feast and invited every leading man in the district, while the diviner studied each guest in secret. None of them matched the omen.
entries.literal: Qi then set out wine, summoned all the local worthies to a gathering, and secretly had the adept examine them one by one; none measured up.

entries.zh: 術者過起家，镠適從外來，見起，反走，術者望見之，大驚曰：「此真貴人也！」
entries.en: The diviner happened to pass Qi's home as Liu was returning from outside. Liu saw Qi and ran the other way, but the diviner glimpsed him and exclaimed in shock, "There is the man of destiny!"
entries.literal: The adept passed Qi's house just as Liu was coming in from outside; seeing Qi he turned to flee. The adept caught sight of him and cried in alarm, "This is the true noble!"

entries.zh: 起笑曰：「此吾旁舍錢生爾。」
entries.en: Qi laughed. "That is just the Qian boy from next door."
entries.literal: Qi laughed and said, "That is only young Qian from next door."

entries.zh: 術者召镠至，熟視之，顧起曰：「君之貴者，因此人也。」
entries.en: The diviner called Liu over, studied his face at length, then told Qi, "Whatever greatness awaits you will come through this youth."
entries.literal: The adept summoned Liu, studied him closely, and turning to Qi said, "The nobility destined for you comes through this man."

entries.zh: 乃慰镠曰：「子骨法非常，願自愛。」
entries.en: He urged Liu gently, "Your features are unlike any I have seen. Guard yourself well."
entries.literal: He then comforted Liu, saying, "Your bone structure is extraordinary; take good care of yourself."

entries.zh: 因與起訣曰：「吾求其人者，非有所欲也，直欲質吾術爾。」
entries.en: Bidding Qi farewell, he added, "I sought him with no ulterior motive—only to prove whether my craft was true."
entries.literal: He then took leave of Qi, saying, "In seeking this man I wanted nothing for myself; I only wished to test my art."

entries.zh: 明日乃去。
entries.en: He left the following day.
entries.literal: The next day he departed.

entries.zh: 起始縱其子等與镠遊，時時貸其窮乏。
entries.en: Qi then began to let his sons and others associate with Qian Liu, and from time to time helped him out when he was short of means.
entries.literal: Qi then began allowing his sons and others to go about with Qian Liu, and from time to time lent him relief when he was poor and in want.

entries.zh: 是時，南唐李景聞閩亂，發兵攻之，延政遣其從子繼昌守福州，而南唐兵方急攻延政，福州將李仁達謂其徒曰：「唐兵攻建州，富沙王不能自保，其能有此土也？」
entries.en: Li Jing of Southern Tang, hearing of chaos in Min, sent an army to attack. Yanzheng sent his nephew Jichang to hold Fuzhou. While Tang forces pressed Yanzheng hard, Fuzhou general Li Renda told his men, "Tang troops are attacking Jianzhou. The Prince of Fusha cannot even save himself—how can he hold this land?"
entries.literal: At that time Li Jing of Southern Tang, hearing of turmoil in Min, sent troops to attack; Yanzheng dispatched his nephew Jichang to hold Fuzhou; while Southern Tang forces were pressing hard against Yanzheng, the Fuzhou general Li Renda said to his followers: "Tang troops are attacking Jian Prefecture; the Prince of Fusha cannot even protect himself—how could he hold this territory?"

entries.zh: 乃擒繼昌殺之。
entries.en: He seized Jichang and killed him.
entries.literal: He then seized Jichang and killed him.

entries.zh: 欲自立，懼眾不附，以雪峰寺僧卓儼明示眾曰：「此非常人也。」
entries.en: Wishing to rule himself but fearing the troops would not follow him, he presented the monk Zhuo Yanming of Xuefeng Temple to the crowd, declaring, "This is no ordinary man."
entries.literal: Wishing to rule himself but fearing the multitude would not follow, he had the Xuefeng Temple monk Zhuo Yanming show himself to the crowd, saying: "This is no ordinary man."

entries.zh: 被以袞冕，率諸將吏北面而臣之。
entries.en: They dressed him in imperial robes and led the generals and officials to bow to him as their sovereign.
entries.literal: They clothed him in imperial robes and caps, and the generals and officials led them all to face north and serve him as sovereign.

entries.zh: 已而又殺儼明，乃自立，送款於李景，景以仁達為威武軍節度使，更其名曰弘義。
entries.en: Soon he killed Yanming as well and ruled in his own name. He submitted to Li Jing, who appointed him military governor of the Weiwu Army and changed his name to Hongyi.
entries.literal: Before long he killed Yanming as well and ruled himself; he sent submission to Li Jing; Jing appointed Renda military governor of the Weiwu Army and changed his name to Hongyi.

entries.zh: 而景兵攻破建州，遷延政族於金陵，封鄱陽王。
entries.en: Tang forces then captured Jianzhou, moved Yanzheng's clan to Jinling, and enfeoffed him as Prince of Poyang.
entries.literal: Jing's troops then captured Jian Prefecture, moved Yanzheng's clan to Jinling, and enfeoffed him as Prince of Poyang.

entries.zh: 是歲，景保大四年也。
entries.en: This occurred in the fourth year of Jing's Baoda era.
entries.literal: That year was the fourth year of Baoda of Jing.

entries.zh: 留從效聞延政降唐，執王繼勛送於金陵，李景以泉州為清源軍，以從效為節度使。
entries.en: When Liu Congxiao learned Yanzheng had surrendered to Tang, he seized Wang Jixun and sent him to Jinling. Li Jing organized Quanzhou as the Qingyuan military circuit and appointed Congxiao its governor.
entries.literal: Liu Congxiao, hearing that Yanzheng had submitted to Tang, seized Wang Jixun and sent him to Jinling; Li Jing made Quanzhou the Qingyuan Army district and appointed Congxiao its military governor.

entries.zh: 景已破延政，遣人召李仁達入朝，仁達不從，遂降於吳越。
entries.en: After defeating Yanzheng, Jing summoned Li Renda to court. Renda refused and submitted to Wuyue instead.
entries.literal: Jing had already defeated Yanzheng and sent someone to summon Li Renda to court; Renda would not obey and therefore submitted to Wuyue.

entries.zh: 而留從效亦逐景守兵，據泉、漳二州，景猶封從效晉江王。
entries.en: Liu Congxiao also expelled Tang garrisons and held Quanzhou and Zhangzhou. Jing still enfeoffed him as Prince of Jinjiang.
entries.literal: Liu Congxiao also drove out Jing's garrison troops and held the two prefectures of Quan and Zhang; Jing still enfeoffed Congxiao as Prince of Jinjiang.

entries.zh: 周世宗時，從效遣牙將蔡仲興為商人，間道至京師，求置邸內屬。
entries.en: During the reign of Emperor Shizong of Zhou, Congxiao sent general Cai Zhongxing disguised as a merchant along a secret route to the capital to request a diplomatic lodge and recognition as a Zhou dependency.
entries.literal: During the reign of Emperor Shizong of Zhou, Congxiao sent general Cai Zhongxing disguised as a merchant along a secret route to the capital to request a diplomatic lodge and recognition as a Zhou dependency.

entries.zh: 是時，世宗與李景畫江為界，遂不納，從效仍臣於南唐。
entries.en: Shizong had just drawn the Yangtze as his boundary with Li Jing and declined the request. Congxiao remained a vassal of Southern Tang.
entries.literal: At that time Shizong and Li Jing had drawn the Yangtze as a boundary, so he did not accept them; Congxiao still submitted to Southern Tang.

entries.zh: 其後事具國史。
entries.en: Later events are recorded in full in the dynastic histories.
entries.literal: Subsequent events are fully recorded in the dynastic histories.

entries.zh: 晉開運三年丙午，南唐保大四年也。
entries.en: The third year of Kaiyun of Jin, the bingwu year, was the fourth year of Baoda of Southern Tang.
entries.literal: In the third year of Kaiyun of Jin, bingwu—the fourth year of Baoda of Southern Tang.

entries.zh: 是歲，李景兵破建州，王氏滅。
entries.en: That year Li Jing's army captured Jianzhou and the Wang clan was destroyed.
entries.literal: That year Li Jing's troops captured Jianzhou and the Wang clan was destroyed.

entries.zh: 江南錄云：「保大三年，虜王氏之族，遷于金陵。」
entries.en: The Jiangnan Record says, "In the third year of Baoda the Wang clan was taken captive and moved to Jinling."
entries.literal: The Jiangnan Record says: "In the third year of Baoda the Wang clan was taken captive and moved to Jinling."

entries.zh: 謬也。
entries.en: This is wrong.
entries.literal: This is mistaken.

entries.zh: 據王潮實以唐景福元年入福州，拜觀察使，而後人紀錄者，乃用「騎馬來、騎馬去」之讖以為據，遂以王潮光啟二年歲在丙午拜泉州刺史為始年，至保大四年，歲復在丙午而滅，故為六十一年。
entries.en: Wang Chao actually entered Fuzhou in the first year of Jingfu of Tang and was appointed observation commissioner. Later chroniclers, guided by the prophecy "came on horseback, left on horseback," took Wang Chao's appointment as Quanzhou prefect in the second year of Guangqi, a bingwu year, as the founding date. The state fell in the fourth year of Baoda, when bingwu came round again—hence sixty-one years.
entries.literal: In fact Wang Chao entered Fuzhou in the first year of Jingfu of Tang and was appointed observation commissioner. Later chroniclers, relying on the prophecy "came on horseback, left on horseback," took Wang Chao's appointment as Quanzhou prefect in the second year of Guangqi, a bingwu year, as the founding date. The state was destroyed in the fourth year of Baoda, when bingwu came round again—hence sixty-one years.

entries.zh: 然其奄有閩國，則當自景福元年為始，實五十五年也。
entries.en: But from the time they fully held the Min realm, the count should begin with the first year of Jingfu—fifty-five years in all.
entries.literal: But from the time the Wangs fully held the Min realm, the count should begin with the first year of Jingfu—fifty-five years in fact.

entries.zh: 今諸家記其國滅丙午是也。
entries.en: Present accounts correctly record the state's destruction in a bingwu year.
entries.literal: Current accounts correctly record the state's destruction in a bingwu year.

entries.zh: 其始年則牽於讖書，繆矣。
entries.en: The founding date is wrong because it was dictated by a prophecy text.
entries.literal: The error lies in the founding date, which was dictated by a prophecy text.

entries.zh: 惟江南錄又差其末年也。
entries.en: Only the Jiangnan Record is also one year off at the end.
entries.literal: Only the Jiangnan Record is also off by one year at the end.

entries.zh: 王審知，字信通，光州固始人也。
entries.en: Wang Shenzhi, whose style name was Xintong, came from Gushi in Guang Prefecture.
entries.literal: Wang Shenzhi, styled Xintong, was a native of Gushi in Guang Prefecture.

entries.zh: 父恁，世為農。
entries.en: His father Ren's family had farmed for generations.
entries.literal: His father Ren's family had been farmers for generations.

entries.zh: 兄潮，為縣史。
entries.en: His elder brother Chao held the post of county clerk.
entries.literal: His elder brother Chao served as a county clerk.

entries.zh: 唐末群盜起，壽州人王緒攻陷固始，緒聞潮兄弟材勇，召置軍中，以潮為軍校。
entries.en: When the Tang dynasty was collapsing and rebels swarmed the realm, a man from Shou Prefecture named Wang Xu seized Gushi. Hearing of the Chao brothers' courage and ability, Xu enrolled them in his forces and appointed Chao a company commander.
entries.literal: At the end of the Tang, bandits rose everywhere; Wang Xu of Shou Prefecture captured Gushi; Xu heard that the Chao brothers were talented and brave, summoned them into his army, and made Chao a military officer.

entries.zh: 是時，蔡州秦宗權方募士以益兵，乃以緒為光州刺史，召其兵會擊黃巢。
entries.en: Qin Zongquan of Cai Prefecture was then recruiting soldiers to swell his ranks. He named Xu governor of Guang Prefecture and called on his troops to march with him against Huang Chao.
entries.literal: At that time Qin Zongquan of Cai Prefecture was recruiting men to augment his troops; he therefore appointed Xu governor of Guang Prefecture and summoned his army to join in attacking Huang Chao.

entries.zh: 緒遲留不行，宗權發兵攻緒。
entries.en: Xu lingered and refused to move, so Zongquan sent an army against him.
entries.literal: Xu delayed and would not advance; Zongquan sent troops to attack him.

entries.zh: 緒率眾南奔，所至剽掠，自南康入臨汀，陷漳浦，有眾數萬。
entries.en: Xu fled south with his host, looting every district they passed through. They marched from Nankang into Linting, took Zhangpu, and mustered a force of tens of thousands.
entries.literal: Xu led his multitude south in flight, plundering wherever they went; from Nankang they entered Linting, captured Zhangpu, and had a force of several tens of thousands.

entries.zh: 緒性猜忌，部將有材能者，多因事殺之，潮頗自懼。
entries.en: Xu was suspicious by temperament and routinely found excuses to kill capable subordinates. Chao began to fear for his life.
entries.literal: Xu was by nature suspicious; subordinate officers who had ability he often killed on one pretext or another, and Chao grew quite fearful for himself.

entries.zh: 軍次南安，潮說其前鋒將曰：「吾屬棄墳墓、妻子而為盜者，為緒所脅爾，豈其本心哉！
entries.en: When the army encamped at Nan'an, Chao addressed the vanguard commander: "We left our ancestors' graves and our families behind to live as outlaws only because Xu forced us—surely that was never what we wanted!
entries.literal: When the army halted at Nan'an, Chao said to the vanguard commander: "We abandoned graves, wives, and children to become bandits only because Xu coerced us—was that truly our hearts' desire!

entries.zh: 今緒雄猜，將吏之材能者必死，吾屬不自保朝夕，況欲圖成事哉！」
entries.en: Xu is brutal and mistrustful now; any officer with talent is as good as dead. We cannot count on living from one day to the next, much less hope to achieve anything lasting!"
entries.literal: Now Xu is fierce and suspicious; officers and clerks with ability are certain to die—we cannot preserve ourselves from morning to night, let alone plan to accomplish great deeds!"

entries.zh: 前鋒將大悟，與潮相持而泣。
entries.en: The vanguard commander was deeply moved; he and Chao clung to each other and wept.
entries.literal: The vanguard commander was greatly enlightened and, embracing Chao, wept with him.

entries.zh: 乃選壯士數十人，伏篁竹間，伺緒至，躍出擒之，囚之軍中，緒所自殺。
entries.en: They chose several dozen strong men, concealed them in a bamboo thicket, and when Xu arrived sprang out to seize him and hold him prisoner in the camp. Xu then killed himself.
entries.literal: They then selected several dozen stalwart men, hid among bamboo groves, waited until Xu arrived, leaped out and seized him, and imprisoned him in the camp; Xu killed himself.

entries.zh: 高季興，字貽孫，陜州硤石人也。
entries.en: Gao Jixing, whose courtesy name was Yisun, came from Xiaashi in Shaan Prefecture.
entries.literal: Gao Jixing, courtesy name Yisun, was a man of Xiaashi in Shaan Prefecture.

entries.zh: 本名季昌，避後唐獻祖廟諱，更名季興。
entries.en: He had originally been named Jichang, but to avoid the taboo on the temple name of Later Tang's founding ancestor, he took the name Jixing.
entries.literal: His original name was Jichang; to avoid the taboo of the temple name of Later Tang's founding ancestor, he was renamed Jixing.

entries.zh: 季興少為汴州富人李讓家僮。
entries.en: As a young man, Jixing served as a household slave in the home of Li Rang, a wealthy man of Bian Prefecture.
entries.literal: In his youth Jixing was a household slave in the home of Li Rang, a wealthy man of Bian Prefecture.

entries.zh: 梁太祖初鎮宣武，讓以入貲得幸，養為子，易其姓名曰朱友讓。
entries.en: When the Founding Emperor of Liang first took charge of Xuanyi, Rang won his favor by paying a large contribution and was adopted as a son; his name was then changed to Zhu Yourang.
entries.literal: When the Founding Emperor of Liang first governed Xuanyi, Rang gained favor by contributing wealth, was adopted as a son, and his name was changed to Zhu Yourang.

entries.zh: 季興以友讓故得進見，太祖奇其材，命友讓以子畜之，因冒姓朱氏，補制勝軍使，遷毅勇指揮使。
entries.en: Through Yourang, Jixing obtained an audience with the emperor, who was impressed by his ability and told Yourang to raise him as a son. He thereupon took the Zhu surname for a time, was appointed commissioner of the Victorious Army, and later became commander of the Resolute and Brave Command.
entries.literal: Jixing was able to gain an audience because of Yourang; the Founding Emperor was struck by his talent, ordered Yourang to rear him as a son, and he therefore falsely took the surname Zhu; he was appointed military commissioner of the Victorious Army and was transferred to commander of the Resolute and Brave Command.

entries.zh: 太祖崩，季興見梁日以衰弱，乃謀阻兵自固，治城隍，設樓櫓。
entries.en: After the Founding Emperor's death, Jixing watched Liang weaken day by day and set about strengthening his own position: he repaired the city walls and moats and built watchtowers.
entries.literal: When the Founding Emperor died, Jixing saw that Liang grew weaker day by day; he then plotted to hold troops and secure himself, repaired the moat and walls, and set up watchtowers.

entries.zh: 以兵攻歸、峽，為蜀將王宗壽所敗。
entries.en: He attacked Gui and Xia Prefectures but was defeated by the Shu general Wang Zongshou.
entries.literal: He sent troops to attack Gui and Xia, and was defeated by the Shu general Wang Zongshou.

entries.zh: 又發兵聲言助梁擊晉，以侵襄州，為孔所敗，乃絕貢賦累年。
entries.en: He raised troops again, publicly claiming to aid Liang against Jin while actually moving against Xiang Prefecture. Kong Qing defeated him, and he then withheld tribute for many years.
entries.literal: He again raised troops, claiming publicly to help Liang attack Jin, in order to invade Xiang Prefecture; he was defeated by Kong Qing, and then cut off tribute and taxes for many years.

entries.zh: 梁末帝優容之，封季興渤海王，賜以袞冕劍佩。
entries.en: The Last Emperor of Liang indulged him, enfeoffed him as Prince of Bohai, and granted him imperial robes, sword, and belt ornaments.
entries.literal: The Last Emperor of Liang treated him leniently, enfeoffed Jixing as Prince of Bohai, and bestowed on him imperial robes, sword, and belt ornaments.

entries.zh: 貞明三年，始復修貢。
entries.en: In the third year of Zhenming he finally resumed tribute payments.
entries.literal: In the third year of Zhenming he at last resumed sending tribute.

entries.zh: 天復二年，梁兵攻鳳翔，李茂貞堅壁不出，太祖議欲收軍還河中，季興獨進曰：「天下豪傑窺此舉者一歲矣，今岐人已憊，破在旦夕，而大王之所慮者，閉壁以老我師，此可以誘致之也。」
entries.en: In the second year of Tianfu, Liang forces besieged Fengxiang while Li Maozhen held the walls and refused to give battle. The Founding Emperor considered withdrawing to Hezhong, but Jixing alone stepped forward and said, "For a year the empire's strongmen have watched this campaign. The Qi forces are worn out now and will fall any day. What worries you, my lord, is their strategy of shutting the gates to exhaust our army—that is something we can lure them out of."
entries.literal: In the second year of Tianfu, Liang troops attacked Fengxiang; Li Maozhen held his walls and would not come out; the Founding Emperor discussed withdrawing the army back to Hezhong; Jixing alone advanced and said: "For a year now the heroes of the realm have been watching this campaign; today the men of Qi are exhausted and defeat is imminent; what Your Highness fears is that they will shut their walls to wear down our army—this can be lured out."

entries.zh: 太祖壯其言，命季興募勇敢士，得騎士馬景，季興授以計，引見太祖。
entries.en: The emperor was struck by his counsel and told Jixing to recruit daring men. Jixing found the cavalryman Ma Jing, taught him the stratagem, and presented him to the emperor.
entries.literal: The Founding Emperor was impressed by his words, ordered Jixing to recruit brave men, obtained the cavalryman Ma Jing, Jixing gave him the plan, and introduced him to the Founding Emperor.

entries.zh: 景曰：「此行無還理，願錄其後嗣。」
entries.en: Jing said, "There is no coming back from this mission. I ask that my descendants be provided for."
entries.literal: Jing said: "On this mission there is no prospect of return; I ask that my descendants be recorded."

entries.zh: 太祖惻然止之，景固請，乃行。
entries.en: The emperor, moved, tried to dissuade him, but Jing insisted and set out.
entries.literal: The Founding Emperor, moved with pity, tried to stop him; Jing firmly requested to go, and then set out.

entries.zh: 景以數騎馳叩城門告曰：「梁兵將東，前鋒去矣。」
entries.en: Riding with a few horsemen, Jing galloped to the gate and shouted, "The Liang army is about to march east; the vanguard has already gone."
entries.literal: Jing with several horsemen galloped to knock on the city gate and announced: "The Liang army is about to march east; the vanguard has already gone."

entries.zh: 岐人以為然，開門出追梁軍，梁兵隨景後以進，殺其九千餘人，景死之。
entries.en: The defenders believed him, opened the gates, and rushed out in pursuit. Liang troops followed close behind Jing and cut down more than nine thousand men; Jing himself was killed in the fight.
entries.literal: The men of Qi believed it, opened the gate and came out to pursue the Liang army; Liang troops followed behind Jing and advanced, killing more than nine thousand of them; Jing died in the action.

entries.zh: 茂貞後與梁和，昭宗出，贈景官，謚曰忠壯。
entries.en: Maozhen later made peace with Liang. When Emperor Zhaozong was released, he granted Jing a posthumous office and the posthumous title Loyal and Stalwart.
entries.literal: Later Maozhen made peace with Liang; when Emperor Zhaozong came out, he conferred posthumous office on Jing and gave him the posthumous title Loyal and Stalwart.

entries.zh: 季興由是知名。
entries.en: From this Jixing won renown.
entries.literal: Jixing thereby became well known.

entries.zh: 明年，拜宋州刺史。
entries.en: The following year he was appointed prefect of Song Prefecture.
entries.literal: The next year he was appointed prefect of Song Prefecture.

entries.zh: 從破青州，徙潁州防禦使，復姓高氏。
entries.en: After taking part in the conquest of Qing Prefecture, he was transferred to defender of Ying Prefecture and restored the Gao surname.
entries.literal: He followed in the capture of Qing Prefecture, was transferred to defender of Ying Prefecture, and resumed the surname Gao.

entries.zh: 當唐之末，襄州趙匡凝襲破雷彥恭於荊南，以其弟匡明為留後。
entries.en: Near the end of Tang, Zhao Kuangning of Xiang Prefecture surprised and defeated Lei Yangong in Jingnan, then installed his younger brother Kuangming as acting governor.
entries.literal: At the end of Tang, Zhao Kuangning of Xiang Prefecture made a surprise attack and defeated Lei Yangong in Jingnan, and appointed his younger brother Kuangming as acting governor.

entries.zh: 梁兵攻破襄州，匡凝奔於吳，匡明奔於蜀，乃以季興為荊南節度觀察留後。
entries.en: When Liang forces took Xiang Prefecture, Kuangning fled to Wu and Kuangming to Shu. Jixing was then appointed acting military governor and surveillance commissioner of Jingnan.
entries.literal: Liang troops captured Xiang Prefecture; Kuangning fled to Wu and Kuangming fled to Shu; Jixing was then made acting military governor and surveillance commissioner of Jingnan.

entries.zh: 開平元年，拜季興節度使。
entries.en: In the first year of Kaiping he was formally appointed military governor.
entries.literal: In the first year of Kaiping he was appointed military governor.

entries.zh: 二年，加同中書門下平章事。
entries.en: In the second year he was also made co-acting associate minister of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
entries.literal: In the second year he was given the additional title of co-acting associate minister of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

entries.zh: 荊南節度十州，當唐之末，為諸道所侵，季興始至，江陵一城而已，兵火之後，井邑雕零。
entries.en: The Jingnan command comprised ten prefectures, but by the end of Tang neighboring circuits had stripped them away. When Jixing first took office, only Jiangling itself was left; after years of war, towns and villages lay in ruins.
entries.literal: The ten prefectures of the Jingnan command had, at the end of Tang, been encroached upon by the various circuits; when Jixing first arrived, only the single city of Jiangling remained; after the fires of war, towns and hamlets lay in ruins.

entries.zh: 季興招緝綏撫，人士歸之，乃以倪可福、鮑唐為將帥，梁震、司空熏、王保義等為賓客。
entries.en: Jixing recruited refugees, eased their hardships, and won people back to the region. He appointed Ni Kefu and Bao Tang as his commanders and took Liang Zhen, Sikong Xun, Wang Baoyi, and others as his advisers.
entries.literal: Jixing gathered, soothed, and comforted the people; men of talent came to him; he then made Ni Kefu and Bao Tang his generals, and Liang Zhen, Sikong Xun, Wang Baoyi, and others his retainers.

entries.zh: 梁亡，唐莊宗入洛，下詔慰諭季興，司空薰等皆勸季興入朝京師，梁震以為不可，曰：「梁、唐世為仇敵，夾河血戰垂二十年，今主上新滅梁，而大王梁室故臣，握強兵，居重鎮，以身入朝，行為虜爾。」
entries.en: When Liang fell, Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang entered Luoyang and sent an edict of reassurance to Jixing. Sikong Xun and others urged him to attend court in the capital, but Liang Zhen objected: "Liang and Tang were hereditary foes who fought bloody battles along the Yellow River for nearly twenty years. Your new sovereign has just destroyed Liang. You are a former Liang minister who still commands a strong army and holds a strategic post. If you go to court in person, you will walk straight into captivity."
entries.literal: When Liang perished, Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang entered Luoyang and issued an edict to comfort and instruct Jixing; Sikong Xun and others all urged Jixing to go to court in the capital; Liang Zhen thought it inadvisable and said: "Liang and Tang have been enemies for generations; for nearly twenty years they fought bloody battles along the Yellow River; now the ruler has newly destroyed Liang, while Your Highness is a former minister of the Liang house, holding strong troops and occupying a key post—if you go to court in person, you will in effect become a captive."

entries.zh: 季興不聽，留其二子，以騎士三百為衛，朝於洛陽。
entries.en: Jixing would not listen. He left his two sons behind, took three hundred horsemen as an escort, and went to court in Luoyang.
entries.literal: Jixing would not listen; he left his two sons behind, took three hundred cavalrymen as escort, and went to court in Luoyang.

entries.zh: 莊宗果欲留之，郭崇韜諫曰：「唐新滅梁得天下，方以大信示人，今四方諸侯相繼入貢，不過遣子弟將吏，而季興以身述職，為諸侯率，宜加恩禮，以諷動來者。
entries.en: Zhuangzong did intend to detain him, but Guo Chongtao remonstrated: "Tang has just overthrown Liang and won the realm. We are trying to show the world that we govern by trust. The regional lords are sending tribute one after another, but only through sons, officers, or deputies. Jixing has come in person to report for duty and has set an example for them all. We should honor him generously to encourage others to follow.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong indeed wished to detain him; Guo Chongtao remonstrated and said: "Tang has newly destroyed Liang and gained the realm; it is just now showing great trust to the people; the feudatories of the four quarters are coming in tribute one after another, but none more than sending sons, younger brothers, generals, and officials—yet Jixing has come in person to report his duties, taking the lead among the feudatories; he should be treated with added favor and ceremony to encourage those who will come.

entries.zh: 而反縻之，示天下以不廣，且絕四方內向之意，不可。」
entries.en: If we detain him instead, we will show the world that we lack magnanimity and cut off the willingness of the regions to submit. That must not be done."
entries.literal: Yet if we instead hold him captive, we show the realm a lack of magnanimity and cut off the inclination of the four quarters to turn inward—this cannot be done."

entries.zh: 莊宗乃止，厚禮而遣之。
entries.en: Zhuangzong relented, treated him with great courtesy, and sent him home.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong then stopped, treated him generously, and sent him away.

entries.zh: 莊宗嘗問季興曰：「吾已滅梁，欲征吳、蜀，何者為先？」
entries.en: Zhuangzong once asked Jixing, "I have destroyed Liang and now mean to campaign against Wu and Shu. Which should I strike first?"
entries.literal: Zhuangzong once asked Jixing: "I have already destroyed Liang and wish to campaign against Wu and Shu—which should come first?"

entries.zh: 季興曰：「宜先蜀，臣請以本道兵先進。」
entries.en: Jixing replied, "Shu should come first. I ask leave to advance ahead with the forces of my own circuit."
entries.literal: Jixing said: "Shu should come first; your servant asks to advance first with the troops of this circuit."

entries.zh: 莊宗大悅，以手拊其背，季興因命工繡其手跡於衣，歸以為榮耀。
entries.en: Zhuangzong was delighted and clapped him on the back. Jixing had artisans embroider the imprint of the emperor's hand on his robe and regarded it as a mark of glory when he returned home.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong was greatly pleased and clapped him on the back with his hand; Jixing thereupon ordered craftsmen to embroider the imprint of that hand on his robe, and on returning regarded it as an honor.

entries.zh: 季興已去，莊宗心悔遣之，密詔襄州劉訓圖之。
entries.en: Once Jixing had left, Zhuangzong regretted letting him go and secretly ordered Liu Xun of Xiang Prefecture to seize him.
entries.literal: After Jixing had gone, Zhuangzong regretted in his heart having sent him away and secretly ordered Liu Xun of Xiang Prefecture to plot against him.

entries.zh: 季興行至襄州，心動，夜斬關而出。
entries.en: When Jixing reached Xiang Prefecture he sensed danger, broke through the pass by night, and fled.
entries.literal: When Jixing reached Xiang Prefecture his heart was stirred; in the night he cut through the pass and went out.

entries.zh: 已去，而詔書夜至。
entries.en: He was already gone when the arrest edict arrived that same night.
entries.literal: He had already gone when the edict arrived that night.

entries.zh: 季興歸而謂梁震曰：「不聽子言，幾不免。」
entries.en: After he returned, Jixing told Liang Zhen, "I did not listen to your words, and barely escaped with my life."
entries.literal: On returning, Jixing said to Liang Zhen: "Had I not listened to your words, I would barely have escaped."

entries.zh: 因曰：「吾行有二失；
entries.en: He added, "That journey taught me two mistakes.
entries.literal: He then said: "On this journey I made two mistakes.

entries.zh: 來朝一失，放還一失。
entries.en: Coming to court was one mistake on my part; letting me leave was one on his.
entries.literal: Coming to court was one mistake; letting me go was another.

entries.zh: 且主上百戰以取河南，對功臣誇手抄《春秋》；
entries.en: Moreover, after a hundred battles to win the Central Plains, the emperor boasted to his meritorious ministers that he had copied the Spring and Autumn Annals by hand;
entries.literal: Moreover the ruler, after a hundred battles to take the lands south of the Yellow River, boasted to his meritorious ministers that he had copied the Spring and Autumn Annals by hand;

entries.zh: 又曰：『我於手指上得天下。』
entries.en: and also said, "I won the realm on my fingertips."
entries.literal: and again said: "I gained the realm on my fingertips."

entries.zh: 其自矜伐如此。
entries.en: That is how vain and boastful he is.
entries.literal: Such was the way he vaunted himself.

entries.zh: 而荒於遊畋，政事多廢，吾可無慮矣。」
entries.en: Yet he neglects government for hunting and sport. I have nothing left to fear from him."
entries.literal: Yet he is dissolute in hunting and excursions, and government affairs are largely neglected—I need have no worries."

entries.zh: 同光三年，封南平王。
entries.en: In the third year of Tongguang he was enfeoffed as Prince of Nanping.
entries.literal: In the third year of Tongguang he was enfeoffed as Prince of Nanping.

entries.zh: 魏王繼岌已破蜀，得蜀金帛四十餘萬，自峽而下，而莊宗之難作。
entries.en: Prince of Wei Jiji had conquered Shu and was bringing more than four hundred thousand strings' worth of Shu gold and silk down through the gorges when the crisis at Zhuangzong's court erupted.
entries.literal: Prince of Wei Jiji had already defeated Shu and obtained more than four hundred thousand strings of Shu gold and silk, and was coming down from the gorges when Zhuangzong's calamity broke out.

entries.zh: 季興聞京師有變，乃悉邀留蜀物，而殺其使者韓珙等十餘人。
entries.en: Hearing of turmoil in the capital, Jixing seized the entire Shu convoy and killed more than ten of its envoys, including Han Gong.
entries.literal: When Jixing heard that there was turmoil in the capital, he detained all the Shu goods and killed more than ten of its envoys, including Han Gong.

entries.zh: 初，唐兵伐蜀，季興請以本道兵自取夔、忠、萬、歸、峽等州，乃以季興為峽路東南面招討使，而季興未嘗出兵。
entries.en: Earlier, when Tang forces invaded Shu, Jixing had asked to seize Kui, Zhong, Wan, Gui, Xia, and the other prefectures with his own troops. He was appointed eastern-southern campaign commissioner of the Gorges Route, but never actually marched.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Tang troops campaigned against Shu, Jixing asked to take Qian, Zhong, Wan, Gui, Xia, and other prefectures himself with the troops of his circuit; he was then made eastern-southern campaign commissioner of the Gorges Route, yet Jixing never once sent out troops.

entries.zh: 魏王已破蜀，而明宗入立，季興因請夔、忠等州為屬郡，唐大臣以為季興請自取之，而兵出無功，不與。
entries.en: After the Prince of Wei conquered Shu and Emperor Mingzong took the throne, Jixing asked that Kui, Zhong, and the other prefectures be annexed to his domain. Tang ministers argued that he had promised to take them himself yet had never contributed troops, and refused.
entries.literal: After the Prince of Wei had defeated Shu and Emperor Mingzong had taken the throne, Jixing thereupon asked that Qian, Zhong, and other prefectures be made his subordinate commanderies; Tang ministers held that Jixing had asked to take them himself yet had sent out troops without success, and would not grant them.

entries.zh: 季興屢請，雖不得已而與之，而唐猶自除刺史，季興拒而不納。
entries.en: Jixing pressed the request repeatedly. The court reluctantly granted the prefectures but still appointed its own prefects. Jixing refused to accept them.
entries.literal: Jixing repeatedly requested them; although they were granted him against their will, Tang still appointed the prefects itself, and Jixing refused and would not accept them.

entries.zh: 明宗乃以襄州劉訓為招討使，攻之，不克，而唐別將西方鄴克其夔、忠、萬三州，季興遂以荊、歸、峽三州臣於吳，吳冊季興秦王。
entries.en: Mingzong appointed Liu Xun of Xiang Prefecture as campaign commissioner and attacked him without success. Meanwhile the Tang general Xi Fangye seized Kui, Zhong, and Wan. Jixing then submitted Jing, Gui, and Xia to Wu, and Wu enfeoffed him as King of Qin.
entries.literal: Mingzong then made Liu Xun of Xiang Prefecture campaign commissioner and attacked him, but could not overcome him; meanwhile a separate Tang general, Xi Fangye, captured his three prefectures of Qian, Zhong, and Wan; Jixing thereupon submitted the three prefectures of Jing, Gui, and Xia to Wu, and Wu enfeoffed Jixing as King of Qin.

entries.zh: 天成三年冬卒，年七十一，謚曰武信。
entries.en: He died in the winter of the third year of Tiancheng at the age of seventy-one. His posthumous title was Martial and Trustworthy.
entries.literal: He died in the winter of the third year of Tiancheng, aged seventy-one; his posthumous title was Martial and Trustworthy.

entries.zh: 季興子九人，長子從誨立。
entries.en: Jixing had nine sons. His eldest son Conghui succeeded him.
entries.literal: Jixing had nine sons; his eldest son Conghui succeeded him.

entries.zh: 從誨為人明敏，多權詐。
entries.en: Conghui was clever and quick-witted, and skilled in deceit.
entries.literal: Conghui as a man was sharp and clever, and full of stratagems.

entries.zh: 晉高祖遣翰林學士陶穀為從誨生辰國信使，從誨宴穀望沙樓，大陳戰艦於樓下，謂穀曰：「吳、蜀不賓久矣，願修武備，習水戰，以待師期。」
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu of Jin sent the Hanlin academician Tao Gu as birthday envoy to Conghui. Conghui entertained him at the Wangsha Tower with a great display of warships below and said, "Wu and Shu have long withheld submission. I mean to strengthen my defenses, train for naval warfare, and await the day when your armies march."
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu of Jin sent Hanlin academician Tao Gu as birthday envoy to Conghui; Conghui entertained Gu at the Wangsha Tower and arrayed many warships below the tower, saying to Gu: "Wu and Shu have long refused submission; I wish to repair armaments, practice naval warfare, and await the day of the imperial army."

entries.zh: 穀還，具道其語，晉高祖大喜，復遣使賜以甲馬百匹。
entries.en: On his return Gu repeated the speech in full. Gaozu was delighted and sent another envoy with a gift of a hundred suits of armor and horses.
entries.literal: When Gu returned he reported his words in full; Emperor Gaozu of Jin was greatly pleased and again sent envoys to bestow a hundred suits of armor and horses.

entries.zh: 襄州安從進反，結從誨為援，從誨外為拒絕，陰與之通。
entries.en: When An Congjin of Xiang Prefecture rebelled, he sought Conghui as an ally. Conghui publicly refused but secretly aided him.
entries.literal: An Congjin of Xiang Prefecture rebelled and sought Conghui as an ally; Conghui outwardly refused but secretly communicated with him.

entries.zh: 晉師致討，從誨遣將李端以舟師為應，從進誅，從誨求郢州為屬郡，高祖不許。
entries.en: When Jin forces moved against An Congjin, Conghui sent the general Li Duan with a fleet in support. After Congjin was executed, Conghui asked that Ying Prefecture be annexed to his domain, but Gaozu refused.
entries.literal: Jin troops came to punish him; Conghui sent the general Li Duan with a naval force in support; Congjin was executed; Conghui asked that Ying Prefecture be made a subordinate commandery, and Gaozu would not grant it.

entries.zh: 契丹滅晉，漢高祖起太原，從誨遣人間道奉表勸進，且言漢得天下，願乞郢州為屬，漢高祖陽諾之。
entries.en: When the Khitans destroyed Jin, Emperor Gaozu of Han rose at Taiyuan. Conghui sent envoys by secret routes urging him to take the throne and promising that if Han won the realm, he would seek Ying Prefecture as a dependency. Gaozu pretended to agree.
entries.literal: When the Khitans destroyed Jin, Emperor Gaozu of Han rose at Taiyuan; Conghui sent men by secret routes with memorials urging him to take the throne, and also said that if Han gained the realm he wished to beg Ying Prefecture as a dependency; Emperor Gaozu of Han pretended to agree.

entries.zh: 高祖入汴，從誨遣使朝貢，因求郢州，高祖不與。
entries.en: When Gaozu entered Bian, Conghui sent tribute envoys and again asked for Ying Prefecture. Gaozu again refused.
entries.literal: When Gaozu entered Bian, Conghui sent envoys with tribute and again asked for Ying Prefecture; Gaozu would not grant it.

entries.zh: 從誨怒，發兵攻郢州，為刺史尹實所敗。
entries.en: Enraged, Conghui attacked Ying Prefecture and was defeated by its prefect Yin Shi.
entries.literal: Conghui was angry, raised troops to attack Ying Prefecture, and was defeated by the prefect Yin Shi.

entries.zh: 漢遣國子祭酒田敏使於楚，假道荊南，從誨問敏中國虛實，以為契丹之後，兵食皆殫，意欲以誚敏，敏為言：「杜重威悉以晉戈甲降虜，虜置之鎮州，未嘗以北，而晉兵皆漢有也。」
entries.en: Han sent the Guozi libationer Tian Min as envoy to Chu, traveling through Jingnan. Conghui asked about the central state's strength, assuming that after the Khitan invasion its armies and supplies were exhausted, and meant to mock him. Min replied, "Du Chongwei surrendered all Jin arms and armor to the invaders. The Khitans stored them at Zhen Prefecture and have never brought them north, while the Jin soldiers themselves are now Han's."
