entries.en: Even when they are treated as beyond ordinary administration, the moments of loose control—when favor and awe are applied—must never be neglected.
entries.literal: Although they have sometimes been placed outside regular governance, in the intervals of loose control, restraint, favor, and awe one must not lose hold.

entries.zh: 其得之未必為利，失之有足為患，可不慎哉！
entries.en: Winning their allegiance is not always an advantage; losing it can become a grave danger. How could one be careless?
entries.literal: Gaining them is not necessarily profit; losing them is sufficient to become a calamity—how can one not be cautious!

entries.zh: 作《四夷附錄》。
entries.en: Hence this "Appendix on the Four Barbarian Peoples."
entries.literal: I compose the "Appendix on the Four Barbarians."

entries.zh: 兀欲，東丹王突欲子也。
entries.en: Wuyu was a son of Tuyu, the Dongdan King.
entries.literal: Wuyu was the son of the Dongdan King Tuyu.

entries.zh: 突欲奔于唐，兀欲留不從，號永康王。
entries.en: When Tuyu defected to Tang, Wuyu remained in Khitan territory and refused to go with him, taking the title Prince of Yongkang.
entries.literal: Tuyu fled to Tang, but Wuyu stayed behind and would not follow; he was styled Prince of Yongkang.

entries.zh: 契丹好飲人血，突欲左右姬妾，多刺其臂吮之，其小過輒挑目、刲灼，不勝其毒。
entries.en: The Khitan custom favored drinking human blood; Tuyu's women and attendants often let him prick their arms and suck the blood, while petty offenses brought gouged eyes, branding, and cautery until they could bear no more.
entries.literal: The Khitan were fond of drinking human blood; Tuyu's concubines and attendants often pricked their arms for him to suck, and for minor faults he would gouge out eyes or brand and burn them, and they could not endure the cruelty.

entries.zh: 然喜賔客，好飲酒，工畫，頗知書。
entries.en: Even so he welcomed guests, loved wine, painted well, and was fairly literate.
entries.literal: Yet he delighted in entertaining guests, loved wine, was skilled at painting, and was quite learned in books.

entries.zh: 其自契丹歸中國，載書數千卷，樞密使趙延壽每假其異書、醫經，皆中國所無者。
entries.en: On returning from Khitan lands to China he carried thousands of books; Zhao Yanshou, the Privy Council commissioner, often borrowed his exotic texts and medical treatises—works none in China had.
entries.literal: When he came from the Khitan to China, he brought several thousand volumes of books; Privy Council Commissioner Zhao Yanshou often borrowed his rare books and medical classics, works China did not possess.

entries.zh: 明宗時，自滑州朝京師，遙領武信軍節度使，食其俸，賜甲第一區，宮女數人。
entries.en: Under Emperor Mingzong he traveled from Hua Prefecture to the capital, held the Wuxin circuit commission in absentia with its stipend, and received a top-grade mansion and several palace women.
entries.literal: In the Mingzong era he came from Hua Prefecture to court at the capital, held the post of Military Commissioner of Wuxin in absentia, drew its salary, and was granted a first-rank residence and several palace women.

entries.zh: 契丹兵助晉于太原，唐廢帝遣宦者秦繼旻、皇城使李彥紳殺突欲于其第。
entries.en: While Khitan forces were aiding Jin at Taiyuan, the deposed Tang emperor sent the eunuch Qin Jimin and Imperial City commissioner Li Yanshen to kill Tuyu in his mansion.
entries.literal: When Khitan troops aided Jin at Taiyuan, the deposed Tang emperor sent the eunuch Qin Jimin and Imperial City Commissioner Li Yanshen to kill Tuyu in his residence.

entries.zh: 晉高祖追封突欲為燕王。
entries.en: Gaozu of Jin posthumously enfeoffed Tuyu as Prince of Yan.
entries.literal: Jin Gaozu posthumously enfeoffed Tuyu as Prince of Yan.

entries.zh: 兀欲更名阮，號天授皇帝，改元曰天祿。
entries.en: Wuyu took the name Ruan, styled himself Emperor of Heaven's Gift, and proclaimed the era Tianlu.
entries.literal: Wuyu changed his name to Ruan, styled himself Emperor of Heaven's Gift, and adopted the era name Tianlu.

entries.zh: 是歲八月，葬德光於木葉山，遣人至鎮州召馮道、和凝等會葬。
entries.en: That eighth month Deguang was buried at Mount Muye, and messengers were sent to Zhen Prefecture to summon Feng Dao, He Ning, and others.
entries.literal: In the eighth month of that year Deguang was buried at Mount Muye; envoys were sent to Zhen Prefecture to summon Feng Dao, He Ning, and others to the funeral.

entries.zh: 使者至鎮州，鎮州軍亂，大將白再榮等逐出麻荅。
entries.en: The envoys arrived to find Zhen Prefecture in revolt; Bai Zairong and other commanders expelled Mada.
entries.literal: When the envoys reached Zhen Prefecture, the army there mutinied; the great general Bai Zairong and others drove Mada out.

entries.zh: 據定州，已而悉其衆以北。
entries.en: Mada occupied Ding Prefecture, then led his entire force north.
entries.literal: They held Ding Prefecture, then soon led all their forces north.

entries.zh: 麻荅者，德光之從弟也。
entries.en: Mada was Deguang's younger cousin.
entries.literal: Mada was Deguang's younger cousin.

entries.zh: 德光滅晉，以為邢州節度使，元欲立，命守鎮州。
entries.en: After the fall of Jin he became military commissioner of Xing; when Wuyu was enthroned he was left to hold Zhen Prefecture.
entries.literal: When Deguang destroyed Jin he was made Military Commissioner of Xing Prefecture; when Wuyu took the throne he was ordered to guard Zhen Prefecture.

entries.zh: 麻荅尤酷虐，多略中國人，剝面，抉目，拔髮，斷腕而殺之，出入常以鉗鑿挑割之具自隨，寢處前後掛人肝、脛、手、足，言笑自若，鎮、定之人不勝其毒。
entries.en: Mada was savagely cruel: he seized Chinese captives, flayed faces, gouged eyes, tore out hair, severed wrists, and killed; he carried pincers and chisels everywhere, hung livers, shins, hands, and feet around his bed, and chatted calmly while the people of Zhen and Ding were tortured past endurance.
entries.literal: Mada was especially cruel; he seized many Chinese, flayed their faces, gouged out eyes, plucked out hair, severed wrists, and killed them; he always carried pincers and chisels for picking and cutting, and before and behind his sleeping place hung human livers, shins, hands, and feet; he spoke and laughed as if at ease, and the people of Zhen and Ding could not endure the torment.

entries.zh: 麻荅已去，馮道等乃南歸。
entries.en: Once Mada had withdrawn, Feng Dao and his party went south again.
entries.literal: After Mada had gone, Feng Dao and the others returned south.

entries.zh: 德光滅晉，兀欲從至京師。
entries.en: After Deguang overthrew Jin, Wuyu accompanied him to the capital.
entries.literal: When Deguang destroyed Jin, Wuyu followed him to the capital.

entries.zh: 德光殺繼旻、彥紳，籍其家貲，悉以賜兀欲。
entries.en: Deguang put Jimin and Yanshen to death, inventoried their estates, and bestowed everything on Wuyu.
entries.literal: Deguang executed Jimin and Yanshen, registered their household goods, and gave the whole to Wuyu.

entries.zh: 德光死欒城，兀欲與趙延壽及諸大將等俱入鎮州。
entries.en: When Deguang died at Luancheng, Wuyu entered Zhen Prefecture with Zhao Yanshou and the other senior commanders.
entries.literal: Deguang died at Luancheng; Wuyu entered Zhen Prefecture together with Zhao Yanshou and the other great generals.

entries.zh: 延壽自稱權知軍國事，遣人求鎮州管鑰于兀欲，兀欲不與。
entries.en: Yanshou proclaimed himself provisional overseer of military and state affairs and sent men to demand the keys to Zhen Prefecture from Wuyu, but Wuyu refused.
entries.literal: Yanshou styled himself provisional overseer of military and state affairs and sent men to ask Wuyu for the keys to Zhen Prefecture; Wuyu would not give them.

entries.zh: 延壽左右曰：「契丹大人聚而謀者詾詾，必有變，宜備之。
entries.en: His advisers said, "The Khitan chiefs are meeting in a noisy council—something is surely afoot; you must guard against it.
entries.literal: Yanshou's attendants said, "The Khitan elders are gathering in council with much clamor—there must be a change; you should prepare for it.

entries.zh: 今中國之兵，猶有萬人，可以擊虜；
entries.en: Our Chinese forces still number ten thousand and can strike the Khitan;
entries.literal: The Chinese troops here still number ten thousand and can strike the barbarians;

entries.zh: 不然，事必不成。」
entries.en: otherwise your plan will never succeed."
entries.literal: otherwise the affair will certainly fail."

entries.zh: 延壽猶豫不決。
entries.en: Yanshou wavered and could not decide.
entries.literal: Yanshou hesitated and could not decide.

entries.zh: 兀欲妻，延壽以為妹，五月朔旦，兀欲召延壽及張礪、李崧、馮道等置酒，酒數行，兀欲謂延壽曰：「妹自上國來，當一見之。」
entries.en: On the first day of the fifth month Wuyu invited Yanshou, Zhang Li, Li Song, Feng Dao, and others to drink; after several rounds he said, "My wife has just arrived from the north—she is your sister by marriage and you should meet her."
entries.literal: Wuyu's wife—whom Yanshou regarded as his younger sister—on the first day of the fifth month Wuyu summoned Yanshou together with Zhang Li, Li Song, Feng Dao, and others to a banquet; after several rounds of wine Wuyu said to Yanshou, "My wife has come from the Upper State and ought to be seen."

entries.zh: 延壽欣然與兀欲俱入。
entries.en: Yanshou went in with Wuyu in high spirits.
entries.literal: Yanshou gladly entered together with Wuyu.

entries.zh: 食頃，兀欲出坐，笑謂礪等曰：「燕王謀反，鎖之矣。
entries.en: Before long Wuyu reappeared and told Li and the rest with a smile, "The Prince of Yan was plotting rebellion; I have put him in chains.
entries.literal: After the space of a meal Wuyu came out and sat down, smiling as he said to Li and the others, "The Prince of Yan is plotting rebellion—I have locked him up.

entries.zh: 諸君可無慮也。」
entries.en: You need not worry."
entries.literal: You gentlemen need have no concern."

entries.zh: 又曰：「先帝在汴州與我算子一莖，許我知南朝軍國事，昨聞寢疾，無遺命，燕王安得自擅邪？」
entries.en: He went on, "At Bianzhou the late emperor gave me a single counting rod and promised I would govern the Southern Court's armies and state; when he fell ill without a final order, how could the Prince of Yan seize power on his own?"
entries.literal: He added, "The late emperor at Bianzhou gave me one counting rod and promised I should oversee the Southern Court's military and state affairs; yesterday I heard he was gravely ill and left no testament—how could the Prince of Yan act on his own?"

entries.zh: 礪等罷去。
entries.en: Li and the others took their leave.
entries.literal: Li and the others withdrew.

entries.zh: 兀欲召延壽廷立而詰之，延壽不能對。
entries.en: Wuyu had Yanshou brought before him in the hall and interrogated him; Yanshou had no reply.
entries.literal: Wuyu summoned Yanshou to stand in the hall and questioned him; Yanshou could not answer.

entries.zh: 乃遣人監之，而籍其家貲。
entries.en: He placed guards over him and inventoried his property.
entries.literal: He then sent men to guard him and registered his household goods.

entries.zh: 兀欲宣德光遺制曰：「永康王，大聖皇帝之嫡孫，人皇王之長子，可於中京即皇帝位。」
entries.en: Wuyu announced Deguang's testament: "Prince of Yongkang, legitimate grandson of the Great Sage Emperor and eldest son of the Human Emperor, shall ascend the throne at the Central Capital."
entries.literal: Wuyu proclaimed Deguang's testament, saying, "The Prince of Yongkang, the Great Sage Emperor's legitimate grandson and the Human Emperor's eldest son, may take the throne at the Central Capital."

entries.zh: 中京，契丹謂鎮州也。
entries.en: The Central Capital is what the Khitan call Zhen Prefecture.
entries.literal: The Central Capital is what the Khitan call Zhen Prefecture.

entries.zh: 遣使者告哀於諸鎮。
entries.en: He dispatched envoys to announce the mourning to the prefectures.
entries.literal: He sent envoys to announce the mourning to the various prefectures.

entries.zh: 蕭翰聞德光死，棄汴州而北，至鎮州，兀欲已去。
entries.en: Xiao Han, hearing of Deguang's death, abandoned Bian Prefecture and marched north; when he reached Zhen Prefecture, Wuyu was already gone.
entries.literal: When Xiao Han heard that Deguang was dead, he abandoned Bian Prefecture and went north; reaching Zhen Prefecture, Wuyu had already left.

entries.zh: 翰以騎圍張礪宅，執礪而責曰：「汝教先帝勿用胡人為節度使，何也？」
entries.en: Han ringed Zhang Li's house with cavalry, seized him, and demanded, "Why did you tell the late emperor not to appoint non-Chinese as military commissioners?"
entries.literal: Han surrounded Zhang Li's residence with horsemen, seized Li, and rebuked him, saying, "You advised the late emperor not to appoint non-Chinese as military commissioners—why?"

entries.zh: 礪對不屈，翰鎖之。
entries.en: Li answered without yielding; Han put him in chains.
entries.literal: Li answered without yielding; Han locked him up.

entries.zh: 是夕，礪卒。
entries.en: That night Zhang Li died.
entries.literal: That evening Li died.

entries.zh: 漢乾祐元年，兀欲率萬騎攻邢州，陷內丘。
entries.en: In the first year of Qianyou of Later Han, Wuyu led ten thousand cavalry against Xing Prefecture and seized Neiqiu.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qianyou of Han, Wuyu led ten thousand horsemen to attack Xing Prefecture and took Neiqiu.

entries.zh: 契丹入寇，常以馬嘶為候。
entries.en: On southern raids the Khitan usually watched for horses' neighing as a sign.
entries.literal: When the Khitan raided south, they usually took horses' neighing as an omen.

entries.zh: 其來也，馬不嘶鳴，而矛戟夜有光，又月食，虜眾皆懼，以為凶，雖破內丘而人馬傷死者太半。
entries.en: This time the horses were silent, spears and halberds gleamed at night, and a lunar eclipse appeared. The Khitan troops took it as a bad omen; though they took Neiqiu, they lost more than half their men and horses.
entries.literal: This time the horses did not neigh; spears and halberds glowed at night, and there was a lunar eclipse. The barbarian host were all afraid, taking it for ill omen; though they broke Neiqiu, more than half their men and horses were killed or wounded.

entries.zh: 兀欲立五年，會諸部酋長，復謀入寇，諸部大人皆不欲，兀欲彊之。
entries.en: In his fifth year on the throne Wuyu summoned the tribal chiefs to plan another raid south. The elders refused, but Wuyu pressed them.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Wuyu's reign he gathered the chiefs of the tribes and again plotted a southern raid; the tribal elders all refused, but Wuyu forced them.

entries.zh: 燕王述軋與太寧王嘔里僧等率兵殺兀欲於大神淀。
entries.en: Prince of Yan Shuzha, Prince of Taining Aoliseng, and others killed Wuyu at Dashen Marsh.
entries.literal: The Prince of Yan Shuzha and the Prince of Taining Aoliseng and others led troops and killed Wuyu at Dashen Marsh.

entries.zh: 德光子齊王述律聞亂，走南山。
entries.en: Deguang's son, Prince of Qi Shulü, heard of the upheaval and fled to South Mountain.
entries.literal: Deguang's son, Prince of Qi Shulü, heard of the turmoil and fled to South Mountain.

entries.zh: 契丹擊殺述軋、嘔里僧，而迎述律以立。
entries.en: The Khitan killed Shuzha and Aoliseng and enthroned Shulü in his place.
entries.literal: The Khitan struck down Shuzha and Aoliseng and welcomed Shulü to the throne.

entries.zh: 兀欲為人俊偉，亦工畫，能飲酒，好禮士，德光甞賜以絹數千匹，兀欲散之，一日而盡。
entries.en: Wuyu was tall and striking, painted well, drank heavily, and honored men of letters; Deguang had once given him thousands of bolts of silk, which he gave away until none remained within a day.
entries.literal: Wuyu was handsome and imposing, also skilled at painting, able to drink heavily, fond of honoring scholars; Deguang had once given him several thousand bolts of silk, which Wuyu distributed until they were gone in a single day.

entries.zh: 兀欲已立，先遣人報其祖母述律。
entries.en: Once enthroned, Wuyu first reported to his grandmother Shulü.
entries.literal: After Wuyu had taken the throne, he first sent word to his grandmother Shulü.

entries.zh: 述律怒曰：「我兒平晉取天下，有大功業，其子在我側者當立，而人皇王背我歸中國，其子豈得立邪？」
entries.en: Empress Dowager Shulü raged: "My son conquered Jin and won the realm with great merit; the son at my side should rule, yet the Human Emperor's heir forsook me for China—how can his son take the throne?"
entries.literal: Shulü said in anger, "My son pacified Jin and took the realm—he achieved great merit; the son at my side ought to be enthroned, while the Human Emperor's son turned his back on me and went to China—how can his son be enthroned?"

entries.zh: 乃率兵逆兀欲，將廢之。
entries.en: She marched against Wuyu to remove him.
entries.literal: She then led troops against Wuyu to depose him.

entries.zh: 兀欲留其將麻荅守鎮州，晉諸將相隨德光在鎮州者皆留之而去。
entries.en: Wuyu left his general Mada to guard Zhen Prefecture and detained the Jin officials who had accompanied Deguang there before setting out.
entries.literal: Wuyu left his general Mada to hold Zhen Prefecture; the Jin ministers and generals who had followed Deguang at Zhen were all detained as he departed.

entries.zh: 以翰林學士徐台符、李澣從行，與其祖母述律相距于石橋。
entries.en: Hanlin academicians Xu Taifu and Li Huan went with him and confronted his grandmother Shulü at Shiqiao.
entries.literal: Hanlin Academicians Xu Taifu and Li Huan accompanied him; he met his grandmother Shulü at Shiqiao.

entries.zh: 述律所將兵多亡歸兀欲。
entries.en: Much of Shulü's army deserted to Wuyu.
entries.literal: Many of the troops Shulü led deserted back to Wuyu.

entries.zh: 兀欲乃幽述律於祖州。
entries.en: Wuyu imprisoned Empress Dowager Shulü at Zuzhou.
entries.literal: Wuyu then imprisoned Shulü at Zuzhou.

entries.zh: 祖州，阿保機墓所也。
entries.en: Zuzhou is the site of Abaoji's tomb.
entries.literal: Zuzhou is where Abaoji's tomb lies.

entries.zh: 初，蕭翰聞德光死，北歸，有同州郃陽縣令胡嶠為翰掌書記，隨入契丹。
entries.en: When Xiao Han heard Deguang was dead he marched north; Hu Qiao, magistrate of Heyang in Tong Prefecture, had been Han's secretary and went with him into Khitan territory.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Xiao Han heard Deguang was dead he went north; Hu Qiao of Heyang County in Tong Prefecture served Han as secretary and followed him into Khitan lands.

entries.zh: 而翰妻爭妒，告翰謀反，翰見殺，嶠無所依，居虜中七年。
entries.en: Han's wife, in jealousy, denounced him for rebellion; Han was executed, and Qiao, stranded, spent seven years among the Khitan.
entries.literal: Han's wife, jealous, accused Han of plotting rebellion; Han was killed, and Qiao had nowhere to turn and lived among the barbarians for seven years.

entries.zh: 當周廣順三年，亡歸中國，略能道其所見。
entries.en: In Zhou's third year of Guangshun he fled home and could recount in outline what he had witnessed.
entries.literal: In the third year of Guangshun of Zhou he escaped back to China and could relate in outline what he had seen.

entries.zh: 云：「自幽州西北入居庸關，明日，又西北入石門關，關路崖狹，一夫可以當百，此中國控扼契丹之險也。
entries.en: He said, "From You Prefecture we entered Juyong Pass to the northwest; next day Shimen Pass—the cliff road so narrow one man could hold a hundred; China's barrier against the Khitan.
entries.literal: He said: "From You Prefecture one goes northwest into Juyong Pass; the next day northwest again into Shimen Pass—the road narrow between cliffs, one man able to hold off a hundred; this is China's choke point against the Khitan.

entries.zh: 又三日，至可汗州，南望五臺山，其一峰最高者，東臺也。
entries.en: Three days on to Khan Prefecture, with Mount Wutai to the south; its tallest peak is the Eastern Terrace.
entries.literal: Three days more to Khan Prefecture; looking south one sees Mount Wutai, and the highest peak is the Eastern Terrace.

entries.zh: 又三日，至新武州，西北行五十里有雞鳴山，云唐太宗北伐聞雞鳴于此，因之名山。
entries.en: Three days more to Xinwu Prefecture; fifty li northwest stands Cockcrow Mountain, named because Tang Taizong heard a cock crow there on his northern campaign.
entries.literal: Three days more to Xinwu Prefecture; fifty li northwest is Cockcrow Mountain—they say Tang Taizong on his northern campaign heard a cock crow here and named the mountain.

entries.zh: 明日，入永定關，此唐故關也。
entries.en: Next day Yongding Pass, an old Tang barrier.
entries.literal: The next day he entered Yongding Pass—an old Tang pass.

entries.zh: 又四日，至歸化州。
entries.en: Four days on to Guihua Prefecture.
entries.literal: Four days more to Guihua Prefecture.

entries.zh: 又三日，登天嶺，嶺東西連亙，有路北下，四顧冥然，黃雲白草，不可窮極。
entries.en: Three days more to Heaven Ridge, stretching east and west; a road dropped north into a dim expanse of yellow cloud and white grass without limit.
entries.literal: Three days more he climbed Heaven Ridge, which runs east and west; a road led down to the north, and on every side was dim emptiness—yellow clouds, white grass, without end.

entries.zh: 契丹謂嶠曰：『此辭郷嶺也，可一南望而為永訣。』
entries.en: The Khitan told him, "This is the Ridge of Parting from Home—look south once and bid farewell forever."
entries.literal: The Khitan told Qiao, "This is the Ridge of Parting from Home—you may look once to the south and take your eternal farewell."

entries.zh: 同行者皆慟哭，往往絕而復蘇。
entries.en: His companions wept until many fainted and woke again.
entries.literal: Those traveling with him all wept bitterly, many fainting and reviving.

entries.zh: 又行三四日，至黑榆林，時七月，寒如深冬。
entries.en: Three or four days more to Black Poplar Grove, in the seventh month as cold as deep winter.
entries.literal: Three or four days more to Black Poplar Grove—in the seventh month, cold as deep winter.

entries.zh: 又明日，入斜谷，谷長五十里，高崖峻谷，仰不見日，而寒尤甚。
entries.en: Next day the Slanting Valley, fifty li of towering cliffs and narrow gorge where the sun never showed and the cold was worse still.
entries.literal: The next day he entered the Slanting Valley, fifty li long, with high cliffs and steep ravines where one could not see the sun overhead, and the cold was even worse.

entries.zh: 已出谷，得平地，氣稍溫。
entries.en: Out of the valley they found open ground and the air grew milder.
entries.literal: Having left the valley, they reached level ground and the air grew somewhat warmer.

entries.zh: 又行二日，渡湟水。
entries.en: Two days later they forded the Huang River.
entries.literal: Two days more and they crossed the Huang River.

entries.zh: 又明日，渡黑水。
entries.en: Next day they crossed the Black River.
entries.literal: The next day they crossed the Black River.

entries.zh: 又二日，至湯城淀，地氣最溫，契丹若大寒，則就溫于此。
entries.en: Two days on to Tangcheng Marsh, the warmest place in the land—when cold was fierce the Khitan wintered there.
entries.literal: Two days more to Tangcheng Marsh, where the climate was warmest; when the Khitan suffered extreme cold they would seek warmth here.

entries.zh: 其水泉清冷，草軟如茸，可藉以寢。
entries.en: The springs ran clear and cold, the turf soft as down, good for bedding.
entries.literal: Its springs were clear and cold, the grass soft as fleece and fit to sleep on.

entries.zh: 而多異花，記其二種：一曰旱金，大如掌，金色爍人；
entries.en: Strange flowers grew there; he named two: dry gold, palm-sized and dazzling gold;
entries.literal: There were many strange flowers; he noted two kinds: one called dry gold, as large as the palm, its golden color dazzling;

entries.zh: 一曰青囊，如中國金燈，而色類藍可愛。
entries.en: and green pouch, like China's golden lantern but tinged blue and lovely.
entries.literal: one called green pouch, like China's golden lantern flower but with a lovely bluish hue.

entries.zh: 又二日，至儀坤州，渡麝香河。
entries.en: Two days more brought Yikun Prefecture and a crossing of the Musk River.
entries.literal: Two days more to Yikun Prefecture, crossing the Musk River.

entries.zh: 自幽州至此無里候，其所向不知為南北。
entries.en: From You Prefecture onward there were no mile markers and no sense of direction.
entries.literal: From You Prefecture to here there were no mile markers, and one did not know which way was south or north.

entries.zh: 又二日，至赤崖，翰與兀欲相及，遂及述律戰于沙河。
entries.en: Two days on to Red Cliff, where Han joined Wuyu and they battled Empress Dowager Shulü on the Sha River.
entries.literal: Two days more to Red Cliff; Han caught up with Wuyu, and they fought Shulü at the Sha River.

entries.zh: 述律兵敗而北，兀欲追至獨樹渡，遂囚述律于撲馬山。
entries.en: Shulü was beaten and fled north; Wuyu chased her to Dushu Ford and imprisoned her at Puma Mountain.
entries.literal: Shulü's army was defeated and fled north; Wuyu pursued to Dushu Ford and then imprisoned Shulü at Puma Mountain.

entries.zh: 又行三日、遂至上京，所謂西樓也。
entries.en: Three days later they reached the Upper Capital, known as the Western Tower.
entries.literal: Three days more and they reached the Upper Capital, called the Western Tower.

entries.zh: 西樓有邑屋市肆，交易無錢而用布。
entries.en: The Western Tower had streets, houses, and markets; they bartered in cloth, not coin.
entries.literal: The Western Tower had towns, houses, and market stalls; trade used cloth instead of coin.

entries.zh: 有綾錦諸工作、宦者、翰林、伎術、教坊、角觝、秀才、僧、尼、道士等，皆中國人，而并、汾、幽、薊之人尤多。
entries.en: Brocade workshops stood beside eunuchs, Hanlin academicians, artisans, music schools, wrestlers, candidates, monks, nuns, and Daoists—almost all Chinese, especially from Bing, Fen, You, and Ji.
entries.literal: There were brocade workshops, eunuchs, Hanlin scholars, artisans, music offices, wrestlers, examination candidates, monks, nuns, Daoist priests, and the like—all Chinese, with men from Bing, Fen, You, and Ji especially numerous.

entries.zh: 自上京東去四十里，至真珠寨，始食菜。
entries.en: Forty li east of the capital lay Pearl Stockade, where they first tasted greens.
entries.literal: Forty li east from the Upper Capital one reached Pearl Stockade and could eat vegetables for the first time.

entries.zh: 明日，東行，地勢漸高，西望平地松林鬱然數十里。
entries.en: Next day they marched east over rising ground; to the west a level pine forest stretched tens of li.
entries.literal: The next day, traveling east, the ground rose gradually; looking west one saw level pine forest stretching densely for dozens of li.

entries.zh: 遂入平川，多草木，始食西瓜，云契丹破回紇得此種，以牛糞覆棚而種，大如中國冬瓜而味甘。
entries.en: They entered a fertile plain and first tasted watermelon—the Khitan said they took the seed from the Uyghurs, grew it under dung-heated frames, and the fruit rivaled China's winter melon in size and sweetness.
entries.literal: They then entered a broad plain rich in grass and trees and first ate watermelon—they say the Khitan obtained the seed by defeating the Uyghurs, covered frames with cattle dung to grow it, and the fruit was as large as China's winter melon and sweet.

entries.zh: 又東行，至褭潭，始有柳，而水草豐美，有息雞草尤美，而本大，馬食不過十本而飽。
entries.en: Farther east lay Niao Pool, the first willows, rich pasture, and rest-chicken grass so nourishing ten stalks filled a horse.
entries.literal: Traveling east again they reached Niao Pool, where willows first appeared; water and grass were lush, and there was a grass called rest-chicken especially fine, with thick roots—a horse eating no more than ten stalks would be full.

entries.zh: 自褭潭入大山，行十餘日而出，過一大林，長二三里，皆蕪荑，枝葉有芒刺如箭羽，其地皆無草。
entries.en: From the pool they entered high mountains for ten-odd days, crossed a forest miles long of thorny colewort whose barbed leaves left the soil bare.
entries.literal: From Niao Pool they entered great mountains and traveled more than ten days before emerging; they passed a great forest two or three li long, all colewort, its branches and leaves bearing barbs like arrow feathers, and the ground beneath had no grass.

entries.zh: 兀欲時卓帳于此，會諸部人葬德光。
entries.en: Wuyu had camped there to gather the tribes for Deguang's burial.
entries.literal: Wuyu at that time pitched his tent here and gathered the tribes to bury Deguang.

entries.zh: 自此西南行，日六十里，行七日，至大山門，兩高山相去一里，而長松豐草，珍禽野卉，有屋室碑石，曰『陵所也。』
entries.en: Southwest sixty li a day for seven days brought Great Mountain Gate—two peaks a li apart, pine-clad, strewn with rare birds and flowers, with houses and inscribed stones marking the tomb.
entries.literal: From here they went southwest sixty li a day for seven days to Great Mountain Gate, two high peaks a li apart with long pines, rich grass, rare birds, and wild flowers; there were houses, steles, and stones, and it was said, "This is the mausoleum."

entries.zh: 兀欲入祭，諸部大人惟執祭器者得入。
entries.en: Wuyu entered to sacrifice; only elders bearing ritual vessels were admitted.
entries.literal: Wuyu entered to offer sacrifice; only the tribal elders holding ritual vessels might enter.

entries.zh: 入而門闔。
entries.en: The gate closed behind them.
entries.literal: Once inside, the gate was shut.

entries.zh: 明日開門，曰『拋盞』，禮畢。
entries.en: Next day the gate opened for the rite called Casting the Cup, and the service ended.
entries.literal: The next day the gate opened in a rite called "Casting the Cup," and the ceremony was complete.

entries.zh: 問其禮，皆祕不肯言。」
entries.en: Asked about the rites, none would explain—they were secret."
entries.literal: When he asked about the ritual, all kept it secret and would not speak."

entries.zh: 嶠所目見囚述律、葬德光等事，與中國所記差異。
entries.en: Qiao's eyewitness account of imprisoning Shulü, burying Deguang, and the like differed from Chinese records.
entries.literal: What Qiao saw with his own eyes—the imprisonment of Shulü, the burial of Deguang, and such matters—differed from China's records.

entries.zh: 述律為人多智而忍。
entries.en: The empress dowager was clever and pitiless.
entries.literal: Shulü was by nature clever and ruthless.

entries.zh: 阿保機死，悉召從行大將等妻，謂曰：「我今為寡婦矣，汝等豈宜有夫。」
entries.en: After Abaoji died she summoned the wives of the generals on the campaign and said, "I am a widow now—you should have no husbands either."
entries.literal: When Abaoji died, she summoned the wives of the great generals who had accompanied him and said, "I am now a widow—how can you still have husbands?"

entries.zh: 乃殺其大將百餘人，曰：「可往從先帝。」
entries.en: She killed more than a hundred of those generals, saying, "Go join the late emperor."
entries.literal: She then killed more than a hundred of their husbands, saying, "You may go join the late emperor."

entries.zh: 左右有過者，多送木葉山，殺於阿保機墓隧中，曰：「為我見先帝于地下。」
entries.en: Subordinates who erred were often sent to Mount Muye and slain in the tomb passage with the message, "Tell the late emperor I sent you."
entries.literal: Those about her who offended were often sent to Mount Muye and killed in Abaoji's tomb passage, with the words, "Go see the late emperor for me in the underworld."

entries.zh: 大將趙思溫，本中國人也，以材勇為阿保機所寵，述律後以事怒之，使送木葉山，思溫辭不肯行。
entries.en: General Zhao Siwen, a Chinese by birth whom Abaoji favored for courage and skill, later angered her over some affair; when she ordered him to Mount Muye he refused.
entries.literal: The great general Zhao Siwen, originally a man of China, was favored by Abaoji for his talent and courage; later Shulü grew angry over some matter and ordered him sent to Mount Muye, but Siwen refused to go.

entries.zh: 述律曰：「爾，先帝親信，安得不往見之？」
entries.en: She said, "You were the late emperor's intimate—will you not go to him?"
entries.literal: Shulü said, "You were the late emperor's trusted man—how can you fail to go see him?"

entries.zh: 思溫對曰：「親莫如后，后何不行？」
entries.en: Siwen answered, "No one was closer than the empress—why does the empress not go?"
entries.literal: Siwen replied, "No kin is closer than the empress—why does the empress not go?"

entries.zh: 述律曰：「我本欲從先帝于地下，以子幼，國中多故，未能也。
entries.en: She said, "I meant to follow him underground, but the heir was young and the state unsettled, so I could not.
entries.literal: Shulü said, "I originally meant to follow the late emperor underground, but because the heir was young and the realm had many troubles, I could not.

entries.zh: 然可斷吾一臂以送之。」
entries.en: Still, you may cut off one of my arms and send it with you."
entries.literal: Yet you may cut off one of my arms to send with you."

entries.zh: 左右切諫之，乃斷其一腕，而釋思溫不殺。
entries.en: Attendants pleaded urgently; she severed one wrist instead and spared Siwen.
entries.literal: Those at her side urgently remonstrated; she then cut off one wrist and released Siwen without killing him.

entries.zh: 初，德光之擊晉也，述律常非之，曰：「吾國用一漢人為主可乎？」
entries.en: When Deguang marched on Jin she had often objected: "Can our nation be ruled by a single Han?"
entries.literal: Earlier, when Deguang attacked Jin, Shulü often opposed it, saying, "Can our state take a single Han as master?"

entries.zh: 德光曰「不可也。」
entries.en: Deguang answered, "It cannot."
entries.literal: Deguang said, "It cannot."

entries.zh: 述律曰：「然則汝得中國不能有，後必有禍，悔無及矣。」
entries.en: She said, "Then even if you seize China you cannot keep it; ruin will follow and regret will be too late."
entries.literal: Shulü said, "Then though you win China you cannot hold it; disaster will follow and regret will be useless."

entries.zh: 德光死，載其尸歸，述律不哭而撫其尸曰：「待我國中人畜如故，然後葬汝。」
entries.en: When Deguang died and his body was brought home, she did not weep but stroked the corpse: "When our people and herds are restored, then I will bury you."
entries.literal: When Deguang died and his corpse was brought back, Shulü did not weep but stroked the body and said, "Wait until the people and livestock of our land are as before, then I will bury you."

entries.zh: 已而，兀欲囚之，後死于木葉山。
entries.en: Soon Wuyu imprisoned her, and she later died at Mount Muye.
entries.literal: Before long Wuyu imprisoned her, and later she died at Mount Muye.

entries.zh: 初，兀欲常遣使聘漢，使者至中國而周太祖入立。
entries.en: Wuyu had often sent envoys to the Han court; they arrived just as Zhou Taizu took power.
entries.literal: Earlier Wuyu had often sent envoys to Han; the envoys reached China just as Zhou Taizu seized the throne.

entries.zh: 太祖復遣將軍朱憲報聘，憲還而兀欲死。
entries.en: Taizu sent General Zhu Xian on a return embassy; by the time Xian came back, Wuyu was dead.
entries.literal: Taizu sent the general Zhu Xian in return; when Xian returned, Wuyu was dead.

entries.zh: 述律立，遂不復南寇。
entries.en: Once Shulü was enthroned he ceased southern raids.
entries.literal: When Shulü took the throne he no longer raided south.

entries.zh: 顯德六年夏，世宗北伐，以保大軍節度使田景咸為淤口關部署，右神武統軍李洪信為合流口部署，前鳳翔節度使王晏為益津關部署，侍衛親軍馬步都虞候韓通為陸路都部署。
entries.en: In summer, the sixth year of Xiande, Shizong marched north, appointing Tian Jingxian of Baoda to Yankou Pass, Li Hongxin of the Right Divine Martial Guard to the He-Liu mouth, Wang Yan, former Fengxiang commissioner, to Yijin Pass, and Han Tong, director of the palace guard, overall land commander.
entries.literal: In the summer of the sixth year of Xiande, Shizong marched north; he made Baoda Army Commissioner Tian Jingxian commander at Yankou Pass, Right Divine Martial Commander Li Hongxin commander at the He-Liu mouth, former Fengxiang Commissioner Wang Yan commander at Yijin Pass, and Palace Guard Director Han Tong overall land commander.

entries.zh: 世宗自乾寧軍御龍舟，艛船戰艦，首尾數十里，至益津關，降其守將，而河路漸狹，舟不能進，乃捨舟陸行。
entries.en: Shizong sailed from Qianning on the imperial dragon boat with a fleet dozens of li long; at Yijin Pass the garrison surrendered, but the channel narrowed and the boats could go no farther, so he abandoned the river and marched overland.
entries.literal: Shizong himself sailed from Qianning on the imperial dragon boat with warships stretching for dozens of li; reaching Yijin Pass he accepted the surrender of its garrison, but the river route grew narrow and boats could not advance, so he left the fleet and marched by land.

entries.zh: 瓦橋淤口關、瀛莫州守將，皆迎降。
entries.en: Commanders at Waqiao, Yankou, and Ying and Mo prefectures all surrendered.
entries.literal: The garrison commanders of Waqiao, Yankou, and Ying and Mo prefectures all came out to surrender.

entries.zh: 方下令進攻幽州，世宗遇疾，乃置雄州於瓦橋關、霸州於益津關而還。
entries.en: As he was ordering the assault on You Prefecture, Shizong fell ill; he set up Xiong Prefecture at Waqiao Pass and Ba Prefecture at Yijin Pass, then withdrew.
entries.literal: Just as he ordered an attack on You Prefecture, Shizong fell ill; he then established Xiong Prefecture at Waqiao Pass and Ba Prefecture at Yijin Pass and returned.

entries.zh: 周師下三關、瀛、莫，兵不血刃。
entries.en: Zhou forces took the three passes and Ying and Mo without bloodshed.
entries.literal: The Zhou army took the three passes and Ying and Mo without shedding blood.

entries.zh: 述律聞之，謂其國人曰：「此本漢地，今以還漢，又何惜耶？」
entries.en: Hearing this, Shulü told his people, "This was always Han territory; now that Han has it back, why regret it?"
entries.literal: When Shulü heard of it he told his people, "This was originally Han land; now that it is returned to Han, what is there to regret?"

entries.zh: 述律後為庖者因其醉而殺之。
entries.en: Later a kitchen servant killed him while he was drunk.
entries.literal: Later a cook killed Shulü while he was drunk.

entries.zh: 契丹謂嶠曰：「夷狄之人豈能勝中國？
entries.en: The Khitan told Qiao, "How could barbarians ever conquer China?
entries.literal: The Khitan said to Qiao, "How could barbarians overcome China?

entries.zh: 然晉所以敗者，主暗而臣不忠。」
entries.en: Jin fell because its ruler was blind and his ministers faithless."
entries.literal: Yet Jin was defeated because its ruler was dim and his ministers disloyal."

entries.zh: 因具道諸國事，曰：「子歸悉以語漢人，使漢人努力事其主，無為夷狄所虜，吾國非人境也。」
entries.en: He described every realm and said, "Tell the Han on your return to serve their sovereign faithfully and avoid capture—our country is no human habitation."
entries.literal: He then described the affairs of the various states in detail and said, "When you return, tell the Han everything so they will serve their lord diligently and not be captured by barbarians—our land is no place for men."

entries.zh: 嶠歸，錄以為陷虜記云。
entries.en: Qiao came home and wrote it up as the Captive's Record.
entries.literal: When Qiao returned he recorded it as Captive's Record.

entries.zh: 契丹年號，諸家所記，舛謬非一，莫可考正，惟嘗見於中國者可據也。
entries.en: Khitan reign eras as various writers record them are full of errors and mostly beyond verification; only those attested in Chinese sources can be trusted.
entries.literal: Khitan era names as recorded by various writers contain many errors and cannot all be verified; only those once seen in Chinese records may be relied on.

entries.zh: 據耶律德光立晉高祖冊文云：「惟天顯九年，歲次丙申。」
entries.en: The investiture document by which Yelü Deguang enthroned Jin Gaozu reads: "In the ninth year of Tianxian, the year is bingchen."
entries.literal: According to the investiture document in which Yelü Deguang enthroned Jin Gaozu, it says: "In the ninth year of Tianxian, the year is bingchen."

entries.zh: 是歲，乃晉天福元年。
entries.en: That year was the first year of Tianfu under Jin.
entries.literal: That year was the first year of Tianfu of Jin.

entries.zh: 推而上之，得唐天成三年戊子，為天顯元年。
entries.en: Working backward, Tang Tiancheng 3, the wuzi year, becomes Tianxian 1.
entries.literal: Counting backward, one reaches the third year of Tiancheng of Tang, wuzi, as the first year of Tianxian.

entries.zh: 按契丹附錄，德光與唐明宗同年而立，立三年改元天顯，與此正合矣。
entries.en: The Khitan appendix says Deguang and Tang Mingzong came to the throne in the same year and that he adopted Tianxian in his third year—exactly matching this reckoning.
entries.literal: According to the Khitan appendix, Deguang and Tang Mingzong took the throne in the same year; in the third year of his reign he changed the era to Tianxian, which matches this exactly.

entries.zh: 又據開運四年德光滅晉入汴，肆赦，稱會同十年，推而上之，得天福三年為會同元年，是天顯盡十年，而十一年改為會同矣。
entries.en: Likewise, in Kaiyun 4 Deguang overthrew Jin, entered Bian, and proclaimed amnesty as Huitong 10; counting back, Jin Tianfu 3 becomes Huitong 1. Tianxian thus lasted ten years, and year eleven was renamed Huitong.
entries.literal: Again, according to the fourth year of Kaiyun, when Deguang destroyed Jin and entered Bian, proclaimed a general amnesty, and styled it the tenth year of Huitong—counting backward, the third year of Tianfu becomes the first year of Huitong; Tianxian thus ran ten full years, and the eleventh year was changed to Huitong.

entries.zh: 惟此二者，其據甚明。
entries.en: Only these two reckonings rest on clear evidence.
entries.literal: These two cases alone have very clear evidence.

entries.zh: 餘皆不足考也。
entries.en: The rest cannot be verified with confidence.
entries.literal: The rest are not worth verifying.

entries.zh: 附錄所載夷狄年號，多略不書，蓋無所用，故不必備也。
entries.en: Barbarian reign titles in the appendix are mostly left out—they serve little purpose and need not be listed in full.
entries.literal: The barbarian era names recorded in the appendix are mostly omitted, since they serve no use and need not be given in full.

entries.zh: 述律立，改元應曆，號天順皇帝，後更名璟。
entries.en: Shulü succeeded him, adopted the era Yingli, styled himself Emperor of Heaven's Accord, and later renamed himself Jing.
entries.literal: Shulü took the throne, changed the era name to Yingli, styled himself Emperor of Heaven's Accord, and later changed his name to Jing.

entries.zh: 述律有疾，不能近婦人，左右給事，多以宦者。
entries.en: Shulü was ill and could not be with women; his personal attendants were largely eunuchs.
entries.literal: Shulü was ill and could not approach women; those who served him close at hand were mostly eunuchs.

entries.zh: 然畋獵好飲酒，不恤國事，每酣飲，自夜至旦，晝則常睡，國人謂之「睡王」。
entries.en: He loved the hunt and wine, neglected government, drank from night till dawn, and slept by day—the realm called him the "Sleep King."
entries.literal: Yet he loved hunting and drinking, cared nothing for state affairs, and whenever he drank deeply he did so from night until dawn while sleeping by day; the people called him the "Sleep King."

entries.zh: 嗚呼！
entries.en: Alas!
entries.literal: Alas!

entries.zh: 自古夷狄服叛，雖不繫中國之盛衰，而中國之制夷狄則必因其彊弱。
entries.en: Since antiquity whether the barbarians submit or rebel has not hinged on China's rise or fall, yet China's handling of them has always followed their strength.
entries.literal: From antiquity the submission and rebellion of the Yi and Di has never depended on whether China was flourishing or declining, yet China's control of the Yi and Di has always followed their strength or weakness.

entries.zh: 予讀周日曆，見世宗取瀛、莫，定三關，兵不血刃，而史官譏其以王者之師，馳千里而襲人，輕萬乘之重於萑葦之間，以僥倖一勝。
entries.en: In the Zhou Daily Calendar I read that Shizong took Ying and Mo and fixed the three passes without a blow, yet the historians still scorned him for driving the royal host a thousand li to raid an enemy—risking the imperial carriage among the reeds for one lucky stroke.
entries.literal: Reading the Zhou Daily Calendar, I see that when Shizong took Ying and Mo and secured the three passes without bloodshed, the historians still mocked him for sending the army of a true king a thousand li to strike a foe, placing the weight of the imperial chariot among the reeds for the sake of a lucky victory.

entries.zh: 夫兵法，決機因勢，有不可失之時。
entries.en: War turns on timing and circumstance; some moments cannot be lost.
entries.literal: In warfare one seizes the moment according to circumstance; there are times that cannot be missed.

entries.zh: 世宗南平淮甸，北伐契丹，乘其勝威，擊其昏殆，世徒見周師之出何速，而不知述律有可取之機也。
entries.en: Shizong had pacified the Huai in the south and struck north against the Khitan on the momentum of victory, hitting their disorder and decay; men saw only how fast the Zhou marched, not that Shulü's court was ripe for the taking.
entries.literal: Shizong had pacified the Huai region in the south and marched north against the Khitan, riding his victory to strike their confusion and weakness; the age only saw how swiftly the Zhou army marched, and did not know that Shulü offered a chance to be taken.

entries.zh: 是時，述律以謂周之所取，皆漢故地，不足顧也。
entries.en: Shulü then believed Zhou was merely recovering former Han lands and not worth defending.
entries.literal: At that time Shulü thought what Zhou seized was all old Han territory and not worth guarding.

entries.zh: 然則十四州之故地，皆可指麾而取矣。
entries.en: The Fourteen Prefectures might have been recovered at a wave of the hand.
entries.literal: Then the old territory of the Fourteen Prefectures could all have been taken at a gesture.

entries.zh: 不幸世宗遇疾，功志不就。
entries.en: Sadly Shizong fell ill and his design was cut short.
entries.literal: Unfortunately Shizong fell ill and his ambition was left unfinished.

entries.zh: 然瀛、莫、三關，遂得復為中國之人，而十四州之俗，至今陷於夷狄。
entries.en: Still, Ying, Mo, and the three passes returned to China, while the folk of the Fourteen Prefectures remain under barbarian rule even now.
entries.literal: Yet Ying, Mo, and the three passes were restored to Chinese rule, while the people of the Fourteen Prefectures remain trapped among the barbarians to this day.

entries.zh: 彼其為志豈不可惜，而其功不亦壯哉！
entries.en: His purpose was cut short—yet what a bold achievement!
entries.literal: Was his aim not lamentable—and yet was his achievement not magnificent!

entries.zh: 夫兵之變化屈伸，豈區區守常談者所可識也！
entries.en: The twists of war are not for pedants who know only fixed formulas.
entries.literal: The flexing and bending of military affairs—how can pedants who cling to routine talk understand them!

entries.zh: 同光三年，魏王繼岌及郭崇韜等破蜀，得王衍時所俘南詔蠻數十人，又得徐藹，自言嘗使南詔，乃矯詔還其所俘，遣藹等持金帛招撫南詔，諭以威德，南詔不納。
entries.en: In the third year of Tongguang Prince Jiji of Wei and Guo Chongtao conquered Shu, recovered dozens of Nanzhao captives taken under Wang Yan, and found Xu Ai, who claimed prior service as envoy. They forged an edict returning the captives and sent Ai with gold and silk to win Nanzhao over—but Nanzhao refused.
entries.literal: In the third year of Tongguang Prince of Wei Jiji and Guo Chongtao and others defeated Shu, obtained several dozen Nanzhao captives from Wang Yan's time, and also Xu Ai, who said he had once been envoy to Nanzhao; they forged an edict to return the captives and sent Ai and others with gold and silk to win over Nanzhao, instructing them in power and virtue—Nanzhao did not accept.

entries.zh: 至明宗時，巂州山后兩林百蠻都鬼主、右武衛大將軍李卑晚，遣大鬼主傅能何華來朝貢，明宗拜卑晚甯遠將軍，又以大渡河南山前邛州六姓都鬼主懷安郡王勿定摽莎爲定遠將軍。
entries.en: Under Mingzong, Li Beiwan, paramount lord of the Two Forests tribes behind Xizhou and a Right Martial Guard general, sent the great ghost lord Fu Nenghua with tribute. Mingzong made Beiwan a General Who Pacifies the Distance and appointed Wuding Biaosha of the Six Clans south of the Dadu River a General Who Fixes the Distance.
entries.literal: By Mingzong's time the Xizhou mountain rear Two Forests Hundred Barbarians paramount ghost lord and Right Martial Guard senior general Li Beiwan sent the great ghost lord Fu Nenghua to pay tribute; Mingzong appointed Beiwan General Who Pacifies the Distance, and also made the Qiongzhou Six Clans paramount ghost lord south of the Dadu River, Prince of Huai'an Wuding Biaosha, General Who Fixes the Distance.

entries.zh: 明年遣左金吾衛將軍烏昭遠爲入蠻國信使，昭遠不能達而還。
entries.en: The next year Left Golden Crow Guard general Wu Zhaoyuan was sent as envoy to the barbarian lands but could not get through and returned.
entries.literal: The next year they sent Left Golden Crow Guard general Wu Zhaoyuan as credentialed envoy into the barbarian state; Zhaoyuan could not reach it and returned.

entries.zh: 奚 吐渾 達靼 党項 突厥 吐蕃 回鶻 于闐 高麗 渤海 新羅 黑水靺鞨 南詔蠻 牂牁 昆明 占城
entries.en: Xi, Tuyuhun, Dada, Tangut, Turks, Tibetans, Uyghurs, Khotan, Goryeo, Bohai, Silla, Heishui Mohe, Nanzhao, Zhangke, Kunming, and Champa.
entries.literal: Xi, Tuyuhun, Dada, Tangut, Turk, Tibet, Uyghur, Khotan, Goryeo, Bohai, Silla, Heishui Mohe, Nanzhao, Zhangke, Kunming, Champa.

entries.zh: 秋月，帝自將南伐，皇弟拖雷、皇侄蒙哥率師從，拔天成等堡，遂渡河攻鳳翔。
entries.en: In autumn the Emperor personally led a southern campaign, with his brother Tolui and his nephew Möngke following at the head of their armies. They took Tiancheng and other forts, crossed the river, and attacked Fengxiang.
entries.literal: In autumn the Emperor personally led a southern campaign; his imperial brother Tolui and imperial nephew Möngke led armies following him. They took Tiancheng and other forts, crossed the river, and attacked Fengxiang.

entries.zh: 冬十一月，始置十路徵收課稅使，以陳時可、趙昉使燕京，劉中、劉桓使宣德，周立和、王貞使西京，呂振、劉子振使太原，楊簡、高廷英使平陽，王晉、賈從使真定，張瑜、王銳使東平，王德亨、侯顯使北京，夾谷永、程泰使平州，田木西、李天翼使濟南。
entries.en: In the eleventh month of winter, tax-collection commissioners were first appointed for ten circuits: Chen Shike and Zhao Fang for Yanjing; Liu Zhong and Liu Huan for Xuande; Zhou Lihe and Wang Zhen for Xijing; Lü Zhen and Liu Zizhen for Taiyuan; Yang Jian and Gao Tingying for Pingyang; Wang Jin and Jia Cong for Zhending; Zhang Yu and Wang Rui for Dongping; Wang Deheng and Hou Xian for Beiping; Jiagu Yong and Cheng Tai for Pingzhou; and Tianmuxi and Li Tianyi for Jinan.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month of winter, ten circuit tax-collection commissioners were first established: Chen Shike and Zhao Fang for Yanjing; Liu Zhong and Liu Huan for Xuande; Zhou Lihe and Wang Zhen for Xijing; Lü Zhen and Liu Zizhen for Taiyuan; Yang Jian and Gao Tingying for Pingyang; Wang Jin and Jia Cong for Zhending; Zhang Yu and Wang Rui for Dongping; Wang Deheng and Hou Xian for Beiping; Jiagu Yong and Cheng Tai for Pingzhou; Tianmuxi and Li Tianyi for Jinan.

entries.zh: 是月，師攻潼關、藍關，不克。
entries.en: That month the army attacked Tong Pass and Lan Pass but could not take them.
entries.literal: That month the army attacked Tong Pass and Lan Pass but failed to take them.

entries.zh: 十二月，拔天勝寨及韓城、蒲城。
entries.en: In the twelfth month Tian Sheng stronghold, Hancheng, and Pucheng were taken.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month Tian Sheng stronghold and Hancheng and Pucheng were taken.

entries.zh: 九年丁酉春，獵於揭揭察哈之澤。
entries.en: In the spring of the ninth year, dingyou, the Emperor hunted at Jiejiechaha Marsh.
entries.literal: In the spring of the ninth year, dingyou, the Emperor hunted at the Jiejiechaha Marsh.

entries.zh: 蒙哥征欽察部，破之，擒其酋八赤蠻。
entries.en: Möngke marched against the Qipchaq tribes, broke them, and took their chieftain Bachman prisoner.
entries.literal: Möngke campaigned against the Qipchaq tribes, defeated them, and captured their chieftain Bachman.

entries.zh: 夏四月，築掃鄰城，作迦堅茶寒殿。
entries.en: In the fourth summer month they built Saolin City and erected the Qiajianchahan Hall.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of summer, Saolin City was built and the Qiajianchahan Hall constructed.

entries.zh: 六月，左翼諸部訛言括民女，帝怒，因括以賜麾下。
entries.en: In the sixth month the left-wing tribes spread word that commoners' daughters were being seized; enraged, the Emperor had girls rounded up and given to his men.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, the left-wing tribes spread a false report that commoners' daughters were being conscripted; the Emperor was enraged and had girls conscripted and bestowed upon his followers.

entries.zh: 秋八月，命術虎乃、劉中試諸路儒士，中選者除本貫議事官，得四千三十人。
entries.en: In the eighth autumn month Shihu Nai and Liu Zhong were ordered to test Confucian scholars on every circuit. Four thousand and thirty who passed were made deliberative officers in their home districts.
entries.literal: In the eighth month of autumn, Shihu Nai and Liu Zhong were ordered to examine Confucian scholars throughout the circuits; those selected were appointed native-district deliberative officers — four thousand thirty men in all.

entries.zh: 冬十月，獵於野馬川，幸龍庭，遂至行宮。
entries.en: That winter, in the tenth month, he hunted at Yema River, visited the Dragon Court, and then went on to the traveling palace.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of winter, he hunted at Yema River, visited the Dragon Court, and then proceeded to the traveling palace.

entries.zh: 是冬，口溫不花等圍光州，命張柔、鞏彥暉、史天澤攻下之，遂別攻蘄州，降隨州，略地至黃州，宋懼請和，乃還。
entries.en: That winter Köten Buqa and others invested Guang Prefecture. Zhang Rou, Gong Yanhui, and Shi Tianze were ordered to storm it, then struck Qi Prefecture, accepted the surrender of Suizhou, and raided as far as Huang Prefecture. Frightened, the Song sued for peace, and the army withdrew.
entries.literal: That winter, Köten Buqa and others besieged Guang Prefecture; Zhang Rou, Gong Yanhui, and Shi Tianze were ordered to attack and take it, then separately attacked Qi Prefecture, reduced Suizhou, raided as far as Huang Prefecture; the Song, in fear, sued for peace, and the army returned.

entries.zh: 本紀第二 太宗
entries.en: Annals, Part Two: Taizong
entries.literal: Annals, Part Two: Taizong

entries.zh: 元年辛亥夏六月，西方諸王別兒哥、脫哈帖木兒，東方諸王也古、脫忽、亦孫哥、按只帶、塔察兒、別裏古帶，西方諸大將班裏赤等，東方諸大將也速不花等，復大會於闊帖兀阿闌之地，共推帝即皇帝位於斡難河。
entries.en: In the first year (xinhai), in the sixth month of summer, the western princes Berke and Toghtamur, the eastern princes Yeke, Toghu, Yissüngge, Ajai, Tachar, and Belgütei, the western generals led by Barchin, and the eastern generals led by Yesu Buqa met again at Kötö'ü Adal and together enthroned him on the Onon River.
entries.literal: In the first year, xinhai, summer, sixth month: the western princes Berke and Toghtamur; the eastern princes Yeke, Toghu, Yissüngge, Ajai, Tachar, and Belgütei; the western generals, including Barchin; and the eastern generals, including Yesu Buqa, met again at Kötö'ü Adal and together raised the Emperor to the throne on the Onon River.

entries.zh: 失烈門及諸弟腦忽等心不能平，有後言。
entries.en: Shiremün and his brothers, among them Naqu, nursed their resentment and murmured against the choice.
entries.literal: Shiremün and his younger brothers, including Naqu, were inwardly discontented and spoke afterward against the decision.

entries.zh: 帝遣諸王旭烈與忙可撒兒帥兵覘之。
entries.en: The Emperor sent Prince Hulagu and Mangqasar with troops to keep watch over them.
entries.literal: The Emperor sent Prince Hulagu and Mangqasar at the head of troops to watch them.

entries.zh: 諸王也速忙可、不裏、火者等後期不至，遣不憐吉䚟率兵備之。
entries.en: Princes Yesü Möngke, Buri, Qoja, and others failed to appear on time; Bulghu was dispatched with troops to stand ready against them.
entries.literal: The princes Yesü Möngke, Buri, and Qoja and others arrived late and did not come; Bulghu was sent with troops to guard against them.

entries.zh: 遂改更庶政：命皇弟忽必烈領治蒙古、漢地民戶；
entries.en: He then reorganized the government: his brother Kublai was put in charge of Mongol and Han households;
entries.literal: He then reformed the government at large: he ordered his imperial brother Kublai to administer the Mongol and Han households;

entries.zh: 遣塔兒、斡魯不、察乞剌、賽典赤、趙璧等詣燕京，撫諭軍民；
entries.en: Taer, Orbu, Chaqil, Saiyid Ajall, Zhao Bi, and others were sent to Yanjing to reassure the army and people;
entries.literal: Taer, Orbu, Chaqil, Saiyid Ajall, Zhao Bi, and others were sent to Yanjing to reassure soldiers and civilians;

entries.zh: 以忙哥撒兒為斷事官；
entries.en: Mangqasar was appointed chief judge;
entries.literal: Mangqasar was made chief judge;

entries.zh: 以孛魯合掌宣發號令、朝覲貢獻及內外聞奏諸事；
entries.en: Bolghu was charged with issuing orders, receiving tribute and petitions, and handling all reports from within and without;
entries.literal: Bolghu was charged with proclaiming edicts, receiving tribute at court, and all internal and external memorials;

entries.zh: 以晃兀兒留守和林宮闕、帑藏，阿藍答兒副之；
entries.en: Qongqor was left to guard the Karakorum palace and treasury, assisted by Arghun Aqa;
entries.literal: Qongqor was left to guard the Karakorum palace and treasury, with Arghun Aqa as his deputy;

entries.zh: 以牙剌瓦赤、不只兒、斡魯不、睹答兒等充燕京等處行尚書省事，賽典赤、匿昝馬丁佐之；
entries.en: Yarlaghchi, Bujir, Orbu, Tuda'er, and others were made heads of the Yanjing Branch Secretariat, with Saiyid Ajall and Nizam al-Din as deputies;
entries.literal: Yarlaghchi, Bujir, Orbu, Tuda'er, and others were appointed to the Yanjing Branch Secretariat, assisted by Saiyid Ajall and Nizam al-Din;

entries.zh: 以訥懷、塔剌海、麻速忽等充別失八里等處行尚書省事，暗都剌兀尊、阿合馬、也的沙佐之；
entries.en: Negü, Talqai, Mas'ud, and others were appointed to the Beshbaligh Branch Secretariat, with Endureltü, Ahmad, and Yazid assisting;
entries.literal: Negü, Talqai, Mas'ud, and others were appointed to the Beshbaligh Branch Secretariat, assisted by Endureltü, Ahmad, and Yazid;

entries.zh: 以阿兒渾充阿毋河等處行尚書省事，法合魯丁、匿只馬丁佐之；
entries.en: Arghun was put in charge of the Amu Darya Branch Secretariat, with Fakhr al-Din and Nizam al-Din as deputies;
entries.literal: Arghun was appointed to the Amu Darya Branch Secretariat, assisted by Fakhr al-Din and Nizam al-Din;

entries.zh: 以茶寒、葉了幹統兩淮等處蒙古、漢軍，以帶答兒統四川等處蒙古、漢軍，以和裏䚟統土蕃等處蒙古、漢軍，皆仍前征進；
entries.en: Chaghan and Yol Qan were given command of the Mongol and Han forces in the Two Huai; Taidar of those in Sichuan; and Qoridai of those in Tibet — each continuing the campaigns already under way;
entries.literal: Chaghan and Yol Qan were put in command of the Mongol and Han armies of the Two Huai region; Taidar of those in Sichuan; and Qoridai of those in Tibet — all continuing the prior advance;

entries.zh: 以僧海雲掌釋教事，以道士李真常掌道教事。
entries.en: the monk Haiyun was placed over Buddhist affairs and the Daoist Li Zhenchang over Daoist affairs.
entries.literal: the monk Haiyun was put in charge of Buddhist affairs, and the Daoist Li Zhenchang of Daoist affairs.

entries.zh: 葉孫脫、按只䚟、暢吉、爪難、合答曲憐、阿裏出及剛疙疸、阿散、忽都魯等，務持兩端，坐誘諸王為亂，並伏誅。
entries.en: Yesünto, Ajai, Changgi, Jaqan, Qadaqutling, Ariq, Gang Qudan, Asan, Qutluq, and others who had straddled both factions were found guilty of inciting princes to revolt and were all put to death.
entries.literal: Yesünto, Ajai, Changgi, Jaqan, Qadaqutling, Ariq, and others — together with Gang Qudan, Asan, Qutluq, and the rest — kept to both sides and were convicted of inciting the princes to rebellion; all were executed.

entries.zh: 遂頒便益事宜于國中：凡朝廷及諸王濫發牌印、詔旨、宣命，盡收之；
entries.en: Useful reforms were then proclaimed throughout the realm: every seal, edict, and commission wrongly issued by court or princes was recalled;
entries.literal: Beneficial measures were then promulgated throughout the realm: all seals, edicts, and commissions improperly issued by the court or by princes were recalled;

entries.zh: 諸王馳驛，許乘三馬，遠行亦不過四；
entries.en: princes using the post roads were limited to three horses, and to four even on long journeys;
entries.literal: princes on courier service were permitted three horses, and even on long journeys no more than four;

entries.zh: 諸王不得擅招民戶；
entries.en: princes were forbidden to recruit households on their own authority;
entries.literal: princes might not privately recruit households;

entries.zh: 諸官屬不得以朝覲為名賦斂民財；
entries.en: officials might not extort the people under the pretense of attending court;
entries.literal: officials might not levy the people's wealth under the pretext of coming to court;

entries.zh: 民糧遠輸者，許於近倉輸之。
entries.en: where grain had to be transported a great distance, payment into a nearer granary was allowed.
entries.literal: where grain taxes had to be transported far, delivery at a nearer granary was permitted.

entries.zh: 罷築和林城役千五百人。
entries.en: Work on Karakorum was stopped, freeing fifteen hundred laborers.
entries.literal: The corvée building Karakorum was halted, releasing fifteen hundred laborers.

entries.zh: 冬，以宴只吉帶違命，遣合丹誅之，仍籍其家。
entries.en: That winter Yeshügü was executed by Qadan for disobedience, and his property was confiscated.
entries.literal: In winter, because Yeshügü had disobeyed orders, Qadan was sent to execute him and his household goods were confiscated.

entries.zh: 二年壬子春正月，幸失灰之地，遣乞都不花攻末來吉兒都怯寨。
entries.en: In the second year (renzi), in the first month of spring, he visited Shihui and sent Qutuq Buqa to attack the fortress of Mergen.
entries.literal: In the second year, renzi, spring, first month, the Emperor visited Shihui; Qutuq Buqa was sent to attack the fortress of Mergen.

entries.zh: 皇太后崩。
entries.en: The Empress Dowager died.
entries.literal: The Empress Dowager died.

entries.zh: 夏，駐蹕和林。
entries.en: In summer he halted at Karakorum.
entries.literal: In summer he halted at Karakorum.

entries.zh: 分遷諸王於各所：各丹于別石八里地，蔑裏于葉兒的石河，海都於海押立地，別兒哥于曲兒只地，脫脫于葉密立地，蒙哥都及太宗皇后乞裏吉忽帖尼於擴端所居地之西。
entries.en: The princes were sent to their assigned territories: Kadan to Beshbaligh, Möri to the Irtysh River, Kaidu to Aybagh, Berke to Quriltai, Tögtö to Yemek, and Möngke Quduq with Ögedei's empress Qurijin Khatun to the west of Kuoto.
entries.literal: The princes were dispersed to their posts: Kadan to Beshbaligh; Möri to the Irtysh River; Kaidu to the Aybagh; Berke to Quriltai; Tögtö to Yemek; and Möngke Quduq, together with Ögedei's empress Qurijin Khatun, to the west of Kuoto.

entries.zh: 仍乙太宗諸后妃家貲分賜親王。
entries.en: Ögedei's consorts and concubines had their goods divided anew and distributed among the princes.
entries.literal: The goods of Ögedei's consorts and concubines were again divided and bestowed upon the imperial princes.

entries.zh: 定宗後及失烈門母以厭禳事覺，並賜死，謫失烈門、也速、孛裏等於沒脫赤之地，禁錮和只、納忽、也孫脫等於軍營。
entries.en: Güyük's empress and Shiremün's mother were found guilty of sorcery and put to death; Shiremün, Yesü, and Buri were exiled to Motuo under guard, while Qoju, Naqu, and Yesünto were held in the camps.
entries.literal: Güyük's empress and Shiremün's mother were discovered in sorcery and both were granted death; Shiremün, Yesü, and Buri were banished to Motuo and placed under restraint, and Qoju, Naqu, and Yesünto were confined in the camps.

entries.zh: 秋七月，命忽必烈征大理，諸王禿兒花、撒立征身毒，怯的不花征沒裏奚，旭烈征西域素丹諸國。
entries.en: In the seventh month of autumn Kublai was ordered against Dali; Princes Törel and Sali against Sind; Qutuq Buqa against the Merkit; and Hulagu against the sultanates of the west.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, Kublai was ordered to campaign against Dali; the princes Törel and Sali against Sind; Qutuq Buqa against the Merkit; and Hulagu against the sultanates of the Western Regions.

entries.zh: 詔諭宋荊南、襄陽、樊城、均州諸守將，使求附。
entries.en: Edicts were sent to the Song garrison commanders at Jingnan, Xiangyang, Fancheng, and Junzhou inviting them to submit.
entries.literal: An edict was sent to the Song commanders at Jingnan, Xiangyang, Fancheng, and Junzhou, urging them to submit.

entries.zh: 八月，忽必烈次臨洮，命總帥汪田哥以城利州聞，欲為取蜀之計。
entries.en: In the eighth month Kublai halted at Lintao and ordered the commander Wang Tiange to hold Lizhou as the first step toward taking Shu.
entries.literal: In the eighth month Kublai halted at Lintao and ordered the commander Wang Tiange to hold Lizhou, intending this as the opening move for taking Shu.

entries.zh: 冬十月，命諸王也古征高麗。
entries.en: In the tenth month of winter Prince Yeke was ordered to campaign against Goryeo.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of winter the prince Yeke was ordered to campaign against Goryeo.

entries.zh: 帝駐蹕月帖古忽闌之地。
entries.en: The Emperor halted at Yedige Qulan.
entries.literal: The Emperor halted at Yedige Qulan.

entries.zh: 時帝因獵墮馬傷臂，不視朝百餘日。
entries.en: While hunting he fell from his horse and injured his arm, and for more than a hundred days he did not hold audience.
entries.literal: At that time, while hunting, the Emperor fell from his horse and injured his arm; for more than a hundred days he did not hold court.

entries.zh: 三年癸丑春正月，汪田哥修治利州，且屯田，蜀人莫敢侵軼。
entries.en: In the third year (guichou), in the first month of spring, Wang Tiange repaired Lizhou and opened garrison farms; the people of Shu did not dare raid across the border.
entries.literal: In the third year, guichou, spring, first month, Wang Tiange repaired Lizhou and opened fields for garrison farming; the people of Shu did not dare encroach.

entries.zh: 帝獵于怯蹇叉罕之地。
entries.en: The Emperor hunted at Qeqen Chaqan.
entries.literal: The Emperor hunted at Qeqen Chaqan.

entries.zh: 諸王也古以怨襲諸王塔剌兒營。
entries.en: Prince Yeke, nursing a grievance, raided Prince Tachar's camp.
entries.literal: Prince Yeke, nursing a grievance, attacked Prince Tachar's camp.

entries.zh: 帝遂會諸王于斡難河北，賜予甚厚。
entries.en: The Emperor then assembled the princes north of the Onon and rewarded them generously.
entries.literal: The Emperor then summoned the princes north of the Onon and lavished gifts upon them.

entries.zh: 罷也古征高麗兵，以劄剌兒帶為征東元帥。
entries.en: Yeke's Goryeo expedition was recalled, and Jachar was made commander of the eastern campaign.
entries.literal: Yeke's army against Goryeo was withdrawn, and Jachar was made commander of the eastern campaign.

entries.zh: 遣必闍別兒哥括斡羅思戶口。
entries.en: Bijä Beg was sent to register Rus' households.
entries.literal: Bijä Beg was sent to register the households of the Rus'.

entries.zh: 三月，大兵攻海州，戍將王國昌逆戰於城下，敗之，獲都統一人。
entries.en: In the third month the main army attacked Haizhou. The garrison commander Wang Guochang gave battle beneath the walls and was defeated; one Song commander was taken.
entries.literal: In the third month the great army attacked Haizhou; the garrison commander Wang Guochang met them beneath the walls and was defeated; one Song commander was captured.

entries.zh: 夏六月，命諸王旭烈兀及兀良合台等帥師征西域哈裏發八哈塔等國。
entries.en: In the sixth month of summer Prince Hulagu, Uriyangqadai, and others were ordered west against the caliphates of Baghdad and the surrounding lands.
entries.literal: In the sixth month of summer, Prince Hulagu and Uriyangqadai and others were ordered to lead armies against the caliphates of Baghdad and elsewhere in the Western Regions.

entries.zh: 又命塔塔兒帶撒裏、土魯花等征欣都思、怯失迷兒等國。
entries.en: Tatar was likewise ordered, with Sali, Tuluhua, and others, against Hindustan, Kashmir, and neighboring realms.
entries.literal: Tatar was also ordered, with Sali, Tuluhua, and others, to campaign against Hindustan, Kashmir, and the like.

entries.zh: 帝幸火兒忽納要不兒之地。
entries.en: The Emperor visited Qorqonaq Buir.
entries.literal: The Emperor visited Qorqonaq Buir.

entries.zh: 諸王拔都遣脫必察詣行在，乞買珠銀萬錠，以千錠授之，仍詔諭之曰：「太祖、太宗之財，若此費用，何以給諸王之賜！
entries.en: Prince Batu sent Töbchä to the imperial camp to request ten thousand ingots of pearls and silver. One thousand were granted, with an admonition: "If Taizu and Ögedei's treasure is squandered thus, how are the princes' yearly grants to be paid?
entries.literal: Prince Batu sent Töbchä to the imperial camp, requesting ten thousand ingots of pearls and silver; one thousand ingots were granted, and an edict admonished him: "If the wealth of Taizu and Ögedei is spent in this way, how will the princes' allotments be met!

entries.zh: 王宜詳審之。
entries.en: You should weigh the matter carefully.
entries.literal: The prince ought to consider this carefully.

entries.zh: 此銀就充今後歲賜之數。」
entries.en: Consider this silver as part of your yearly allotment from now on."
entries.literal: Let this silver count toward your yearly grant from this time forward."

entries.zh: 秋，幸軍腦兒。
entries.en: In autumn he visited Jünna'ur.
entries.literal: In autumn he visited Jünna'ur.

entries.zh: 以忙可撒兒為萬戶，哈丹為劄魯花赤。
entries.en: Mangqasar was made commander of ten thousand, and Qadan jarquchi.
entries.literal: Mangqasar was made a commander of ten thousand; Qadan was made jarquchi.

entries.zh: 九月，忽必烈次忒剌地，分兵三道以進。
entries.en: In the ninth month Kublai halted at Tere and divided his force into three columns for the advance.
entries.literal: In the ninth month Kublai halted at Tere and divided his army into three columns to advance.

entries.zh: 冬十二月，大理平。
entries.en: Dali was pacified in the twelfth month of winter.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month of winter Dali was pacified.

entries.zh: 帝駐蹕汪吉地。
entries.en: The Emperor halted at Wangi.
entries.literal: The Emperor halted at Wangi.

entries.zh: 命宗王耶虎與洪福源同領軍征高麗，攻拔禾山、東州、春州、三角山、楊根、天龍等城。
entries.en: Prince Yehu and Hong Wonyuan were ordered to lead a joint expedition against Goryeo and captured Hesam, Dongju, Chunju, Samgaksan, Yanggeun, Cheonnyong, and other cities.
entries.literal: Prince Yehu and Hong Wonyuan were ordered jointly to lead troops against Goryeo and took the cities of Hesam, Dongju, Chunju, Samgaksan, Yanggeun, and Cheonnyong, among others.

entries.zh: 是歲，斷事官忙哥撒兒卒。
entries.en: That year the chief judge Mangqasar died.
entries.literal: That year the chief judge Mangqasar died.

entries.zh: 四年甲寅春，帝獵于怯蹇叉罕。
entries.en: In the fourth year (jiayin), in spring, the Emperor hunted at Qeqen Chaqan.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, jiayin, spring, the Emperor hunted at Qeqen Chaqan.

entries.zh: 夏，幸月兒滅怯土之地。
entries.en: In summer he visited Yürümiq Tütu.
entries.literal: In summer he visited Yürümiq Tütu.

entries.zh: 遣劄剌亦兒部人火兒赤征高麗。
entries.en: Qorichi of the Jadran was sent against Goryeo.
entries.literal: Qorichi of the Jadran tribe was sent to campaign against Goryeo.

entries.zh: 秋七月，詔官吏之赴朝理算錢糧者，許自首不公，仍禁以後浮費。
entries.en: In the seventh month of autumn an edict allowed officials arriving for court audits to confess past irregularities and still be pardoned, while forbidding further waste.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of autumn an edict declared that officials coming to court to settle accounts might confess prior injustice and would still be pardoned, while future waste was forbidden.

entries.zh: 冬，大獵于也滅干哈里叉海之地。
entries.en: In winter a great hunt was held at Yemüqan Qariqai.
entries.literal: In winter a great hunt was held at Yemüqan Qariqai.

entries.zh: 忽必烈還自大理，留兀良合台攻諸夷之未附者，入覲於獵所。
entries.en: Kublai returned from Dali, left Uriyangqadai to subdue the tribes still holding out, and came to the hunt to pay homage.
entries.literal: Kublai returned from Dali, leaving Uriyangqadai to attack the unsubdued tribes and coming himself to the hunt to pay homage.

entries.zh: 是歲，會諸王於顆顆腦兒之西，乃祭天於日月山。
entries.en: That year the princes were assembled west of Gegen Na'ur, and sacrifice was offered to Heaven at Sun-and-Moon Mountain.
entries.literal: That year the princes were assembled west of Gegen Na'ur, and Heaven was worshipped at Sun-and-Moon Mountain.

entries.zh: 初籍新軍。
entries.en: New troops were registered for the first time.
entries.literal: New troops were first registered.

entries.zh: 帝謂大臣，求可以慎固封守、閑於將略者。
entries.en: The Emperor asked his ministers to find men capable of securing the borders and skilled in command.
entries.literal: The Emperor told his ministers that he sought men skilled in holding the frontiers firm and versed in military strategy.

entries.zh: 擢史樞征行萬戶，配以真定、相、衛、懷、孟諸軍，駐唐、鄧。
entries.en: Shi Shu was promoted to campaigning commander of ten thousand, given the forces of Zhending, Xiang, Wei, Huai, and Meng, and posted at Tang and Deng.
entries.literal: Shi Shu was promoted to campaigning commander of ten thousand, given the armies of Zhending, Xiang, Wei, Huai, and Meng, and stationed at Tang and Deng.

entries.zh: 張柔移鎮亳州。
entries.en: Zhang Rou was transferred to garrison Bozhou.
entries.literal: Zhang Rou was transferred to garrison Bozhou.

entries.zh: 權萬戶史權屯鄧州。
entries.en: Acting commander Shi Quan was posted at Dengzhou.
entries.literal: Acting commander of ten thousand Shi Quan was stationed at Dengzhou.

entries.zh: 張柔遣張信將八漢軍戍潁州。
entries.en: Zhang Rou sent Zhang Xin with the Eight Han Armies to garrison Yingzhou.
entries.literal: Zhang Rou sent Zhang Xin with the Eight Han Armies to garrison Yingzhou.

entries.zh: 王安國將四千戶渡漢南，深入而還。
entries.en: Wang Anguo led four thousand households south across the Han, raided deep into Song territory, and returned.
entries.literal: Wang Anguo led four thousand households across the Han southward, raided deep into enemy territory, and returned.

entries.zh: 張柔以連歲勤兵，兩淮艱於糧運，奏據亳之利。
entries.en: Zhang Rou, having campaigned year after year while grain transport in the Two Huai grew ever harder, memorialized to hold Bozhou for its logistical advantages.
entries.literal: Because Zhang Rou had kept his army in the field year after year and grain transport in the Two Huai was difficult, he memorialized to hold Bozhou for its advantages.

entries.zh: 詔柔率山前八軍，城而戍之。
entries.en: An edict ordered Rou to lead the Eight Armies south of the mountains, build a fortified city, and garrison it.
entries.literal: An edict ordered Rou to lead the Eight Armies south of the mountains, build a city, and garrison it.

entries.zh: 柔又以渦水北隘淺不可舟，軍既病涉，曹、濮、魏、博粟皆不至，乃築甬路自亳抵汴，堤百二十里，流深而不能築，復為橋十五，或廣八十尺，橫以二堡戍之。
entries.en: Rou found the Guo River north of the city too shallow for boats; the army suffered on the crossings, and grain from Cao, Pu, Wei, and Bo never arrived. He built a raised causeway from Bozhou to Bian, a hundred and twenty li of embankment; where the water ran too deep to embank, he threw fifteen bridges across it, some eighty feet wide, each flanked by a fort.
entries.literal: Rou also found the Guo River north of the city too narrow and shallow for boats; with the army suffering from the crossings, grain from Cao, Pu, Wei, and Bo failed to arrive. He therefore built a raised road from Bozhou to Bian, a dike one hundred twenty li long; where the current ran too deep to dike, he built fifteen bridges, some eighty feet wide, and guarded them with two forts.

entries.zh: 均州總管孫嗣遣人齎蠟書降，且乞援，史權以精甲備宋人之要，遂援嗣而來。
entries.en: Sun Si, prefect of Junzhou, sent envoys with a sealed letter of surrender and a plea for aid; Shi Quan, with elite troops, guarded against Song interception and went to bring him in.
entries.literal: Sun Si, administrator of Junzhou, sent men bearing a letter of surrender in wax and begged for relief; Shi Quan, with picked armor, guarded against a Song ambush and went to bring Si in.

entries.zh: 其後驍將鐘顯、王梅、杜柔、袁師信各帥所部來降。
entries.en: Afterward the fierce commanders Zhong Xian, Wang Mei, Du Rou, and Yuan Shixin each brought their forces in to surrender.
entries.literal: Thereafter the valiant generals Zhong Xian, Wang Mei, Du Rou, and Yuan Shixin each led their units to come over in submission.

entries.zh: 六年丙辰春，大風起北方，砂礫飛揚，白日晦冥。
entries.en: In the spring of the sixth year (bingchen) a gale blew out of the north, sand and gravel whirling until broad daylight went dim.
entries.literal: In the spring of the sixth year, bingchen, a great wind rose from the north; sand and gravel flew about, and the bright day turned dark.

entries.zh: 帝會諸王、百官於欲兒陌哥都之地，設宴六十餘日，賜金帛有差，仍定擬諸王歲賜錢谷。
entries.en: The Emperor gathered princes and officials at Yier-mogedu, feasted for more than sixty days, distributed gold and silk in graded gifts, and set the princes' yearly grants of money and grain.
entries.literal: The Emperor assembled princes and officials at Yier-mogedu, feasted for more than sixty days, granted gold and silk in varying measure, and fixed the annual allotments of money and grain for the princes.

entries.zh: 忽必烈遣沒兒合石詣行在所，奏請續簽內郡漢軍，從之。
entries.en: Kublai dispatched Mör-gechi to the mobile court to ask for further conscription of Han troops from the interior circuits, and the petition was approved.
entries.literal: Kublai sent Mör-gechi to the imperial camp to petition for conscripting more Han troops from the interior circuits; the request was granted.

entries.zh: 夏四月，駐蹕於塔密兒。
entries.en: In the fourth summer month he encamped at Tamir.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of summer he halted at Tamir.

entries.zh: 五月，幸昔剌兀魯朵。
entries.en: In the fifth month he went to Sire Ordo.
entries.literal: In the fifth month he visited Sire Ordo.

entries.zh: 六月，太白晝見。
entries.en: In the sixth month Venus was seen in daylight.
entries.literal: In the sixth month Venus appeared in the daytime sky.

entries.zh: 幸䚟亦兒阿塔。
entries.en: He traveled to Yier-ata.
entries.literal: He visited Yier-ata.

entries.zh: 諸王亦孫哥、駙馬也速兒等請伐宋。
entries.en: Prince Yisun, the imperial son-in-law Yesür, and others asked leave to march against the Song.
entries.literal: The princes Yisun and the imperial son-in-law Yesür and others petitioned to attack the Song.

entries.zh: 帝亦以宋人違命囚使，會議伐之。
entries.en: The Emperor, angered that the Song had defied his commands and held his envoys captive, called a council to plan war against them.
entries.literal: The Emperor too, because the Song had defied his orders and imprisoned his envoys, convened a council to discuss campaigning against them.

entries.zh: 秋七月，命諸王各還所部以居。
entries.en: In the seventh month of autumn he sent each prince back to his own domain to take up residence.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of autumn he ordered the princes each to return to their appanages and dwell there.

entries.zh: 諸王塔察兒、駙馬帖裏垓軍過東平諸處，掠民羊豕，帝聞，遣使問罪，由是諸軍無犯者。
entries.en: Prince Tachar and the imperial son-in-law Teligai led their troops through Dongping and the surrounding districts, seizing the people's sheep and swine. When word reached the Emperor he sent envoys to demand an accounting, and from then on no army dared molest the populace.
entries.literal: When the army of Prince Tachar and the imperial son-in-law Teligai passed through Dongping and neighboring districts, it plundered the people's sheep and pigs. On hearing of this the Emperor sent envoys to demand an accounting, whereupon no army dared offend again.

entries.zh: 是歲，波麗國王細嵯甫、雲南酋長摩合羅嵯及素丹諸國來覲。
entries.en: That year King Xicuofu of Poli, the Yunnan chieftain Moheluo-cuo, and envoys from the Sultan lands all came to court.
entries.literal: That year the King of Poli, Xicuofu; the Yunnan chieftain Moheluo-cuo; and envoys from the Sultan states came to audience.

entries.zh: 兀良合台討白蠻等，克之；
entries.en: Uriyangqadai marched against the White Man and other tribes and broke them;
entries.literal: Uriyangqadai suppressed the White Man tribes and others, defeating them;

entries.zh: 遂自昔八兒地還至重慶府，敗宋將張都統。
entries.en: then, coming back from Sibar, he reached Chongqing Prefecture and routed the Song commander Zhang Dutong.
entries.literal: he then returned from Sibar territory to Chongqing Prefecture and routed the Song commander Zhang Dutong.

entries.zh: 賜金縷織文衣一襲、銀五十兩、彩帛萬二百匹，以賚軍士。
entries.en: He received one gold-thread embroidered robe, fifty taels of silver, and ten thousand two hundred bolts of colored silk with which to reward his soldiers.
entries.literal: He was granted one gold-thread embroidered robe, fifty taels of silver, and ten thousand two hundred bolts of colored silk to reward the troops.

entries.zh: 冬，帝駐蹕阿塔哈帖乞兒蠻。
entries.en: That winter the Emperor encamped at Ataha-teqirmen.
entries.literal: In winter the Emperor halted at Ataha-teqirmen.

entries.zh: 以阿木河回回降民分賜諸王百官。
entries.en: The Muslim subjects who had surrendered along the Amu River were divided up and granted to princes and officials.
entries.literal: The Muslim populace that had submitted on the Amu River was divided and granted to princes and officials.

entries.zh: 七年丁巳春，幸忽闌也兒吉。
entries.en: In the spring of the seventh year (dingsi) he went to Hulan-yierji.
entries.literal: In the spring of the seventh year, dingsi, he visited Hulan-yierji.

entries.zh: 詔諸王出師征宋。
entries.en: An edict commanded the princes to take the field against the Song.
entries.literal: An edict ordered the princes to take the field against the Song.

entries.zh: 乞都不花等討末來吉兒都怯寨，平之。
entries.en: Qutuq-buqa and his commanders reduced the Melaiji'r-duqie stockade and pacified the region.
entries.literal: Qutuq-buqa and others suppressed the Melaiji'r-duqie stockade and pacified it.

entries.zh: 夏六月，謁太祖行宮，祭旗鼓，復會于怯魯連之地，還幸月兒滅怯土。
entries.en: In the sixth summer month he visited Taizu's traveling palace, offered sacrifice to the banners and drums, met again at Kerulen, and returned to Yier-mieqietu.
entries.literal: In the sixth month of summer he visited the mobile palace of Taizu, sacrificed to the banners and drums, assembled again at Kerulen, and returned to Yier-mieqietu.

entries.zh: 秋，駐蹕於軍腦兒，釃馬乳祭天。
entries.en: That autumn he encamped at Junnao'er and poured fermented mare's milk in sacrifice to Heaven.
entries.literal: In autumn he halted at Junnao'er and poured fermented mare's milk in sacrifice to Heaven.

entries.zh: 九月，出師南征。
entries.en: In the ninth month the army set out on the southern campaign.
entries.literal: In the ninth month the army marched south on campaign.

entries.zh: 以駙馬剌真之子乞䚟為達魯花赤，鎮守斡羅思，仍賜馬三百、羊五千。
entries.en: Qachi, son of the imperial son-in-law Racheen, was made darughachi to hold Rus', and was given three hundred horses and five thousand sheep besides.
entries.literal: Qachi, son of the imperial son-in-law Racheen, was appointed darughachi to garrison Rus', and was further granted three hundred horses and five thousand sheep.

entries.zh: 回鶻獻水精盆、珍珠傘等物，可直銀三萬餘錠。
entries.en: The Uighurs offered a crystal basin, a pearl umbrella, and other treasures worth more than thirty thousand taels of silver.
entries.literal: The Uighurs presented a crystal basin, a pearl umbrella, and other objects worth more than thirty thousand taels of silver.

entries.zh: 帝曰：「方今百姓疲弊，所急者錢爾，朕獨有此何為？」
entries.en: The Emperor said, "The people are worn out; what they need is money. What good does it do for me alone to keep such things?"
entries.literal: The Emperor said, "The people are exhausted now; what they need is money. Of what use is it for me alone to possess these things?"

entries.zh: 卻之。
entries.en: He sent them back.
entries.literal: He refused them.

entries.zh: 賽典赤以為言，帝稍償其直，且禁其勿復有所獻。
entries.en: Sayyid Ajall pleaded their case; the Emperor paid part of the value and forbade further tribute of that kind.
entries.literal: Sayyid Ajall spoke on their behalf; the Emperor partially compensated their value and forbade them from presenting gifts again.

entries.zh: 宗王塔察兒率諸軍南征，圍樊城，霖雨連月，乃班師。
entries.en: Prince Tachar led the southern armies against Fancheng, but month after month of rain forced him to withdraw.
entries.literal: Prince Tachar led the armies south, besieged Fancheng, but after rains persisted for months, withdrew.

entries.zh: 元帥卜鄰吉䚟軍自鄧州略地，遂渡漢江。
entries.en: Marshal Qorichin's force raided out of Dengzhou and crossed the Han River.
entries.literal: The marshal Qorichin's army raided from Dengzhou and crossed the Han River.

entries.zh: 冬十一月，兀良合台伐交趾，敗之，入其國。
entries.en: In the eleventh winter month Uriyangqadai invaded Annam, broke its armies, and entered the realm.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month of winter Uriyangqadai attacked Annam, defeated it, and entered the country.
