entries.zh: 安南主陳日煚竄海島，遂班師。
entries.en: King Trần Thái Tông of Annam fled to an offshore island, and the army withdrew.
entries.literal: King Trần Thái Tông of Annam fled to a sea island, and the army withdrew.

entries.zh: 遣阿藍答兒、脫因、囊加台等詣陝西等處理算錢谷。
entries.en: Arghun Aqa, To'in, Nangatai, and others were sent to Shaanxi and neighboring circuits to settle accounts of taxes and grain.
entries.literal: Arghun Aqa, To'in, Nangatai, and others were dispatched to Shaanxi and other regions to audit taxes and grain.

entries.zh: 冬，帝度漠南，至於玉龍棧。
entries.en: That winter the Emperor crossed south of the desert and reached Yulongzhan.
entries.literal: In winter the Emperor crossed south of the desert as far as Yulongzhan.

entries.zh: 忽必烈及諸王阿裏不哥、八里土、出木哈兒、玉龍塔失、昔烈吉、公主脫滅幹等來迎，大燕，既而各遣歸所部。
entries.en: Kublai and the princes Ariq Böke, Bari-tu, Chumqar, Yulutas, and Siregi, together with Princess Tuomiegan, came out to meet him. A great feast was held, and afterward each was sent home to his domain.
entries.literal: Kublai and the princes Ariq Böke, Bari-tu, Chumqar, Yulutas, Siregi, and Princess Tuomiegan came to meet him; a great banquet was held, and afterward each was sent back to his appanage.

entries.zh: 八年戊午春正月朔，幸也裏本朵哈之地，受朝賀。
entries.en: On New Year's Day in the spring of the eighth year (wuwu) he went to Yilibenduoha and received the court's congratulations.
entries.literal: On the first day of the first month of spring in the eighth year, wuwu, he visited Yilibenduoha and received court congratulations.

entries.zh: 二月，陳日煚傳國于長子光昺。
entries.en: In the second month Trần Thái Tông abdicated in favor of his eldest son Quang Hựu.
entries.literal: In the second month Trần Thái Tông passed the realm to his eldest son Quang Hựu.

entries.zh: 光昺遣婿與其國人以方物來見，兀良合台送詣行在所。
entries.en: Quang Hựu sent his son-in-law with Annamese envoys bearing tribute; Uriyangqadai escorted them to the mobile court.
entries.literal: Quang Hựu sent his son-in-law with his countrymen bearing tribute to audience; Uriyangqadai escorted them to the imperial camp.

entries.zh: 諸王旭烈兀討回回哈裏發，平之，禽其王，遣使來獻捷。
entries.en: Prince Hulagu crushed the Muslim caliphate, brought the land to order, took its king prisoner, and sent envoys bearing news of victory.
entries.literal: Prince Hulagu suppressed the Muslim caliphate, pacified it, captured its king, and sent envoys to report victory.

entries.zh: 帝獵於也裏海牙之地。
entries.en: The Emperor hunted at Yilihaiya.
entries.literal: The Emperor hunted at Yilihaiya.

entries.zh: 師南征，次於河。
entries.en: The southern army advanced and encamped on the river.
entries.literal: The army marched south and halted at the river.

entries.zh: 適冰合，以土覆之而渡。
entries.en: The river had just frozen over; they spread earth atop the ice and crossed.
entries.literal: The ice had just formed; they covered it with earth and crossed.

entries.zh: 帝自將伐宋，由西蜀以入。
entries.en: The Emperor took personal command of the war against the Song, entering by way of western Shu.
entries.literal: The Emperor personally commanded the campaign against the Song, entering through western Shu.

entries.zh: 命張柔從忽必烈征鄂，趨杭州。
entries.en: Zhang Rou was ordered to march with Kublai against Ezhou and drive toward Hangzhou.
entries.literal: Zhang Rou was ordered to follow Kublai in the campaign against Ezhou, pressing toward Hangzhou.

entries.zh: 命塔察攻荊山，分宋兵力。
entries.en: Tachar was ordered to strike Jingshan and split the Song armies.
entries.literal: Tachar was ordered to attack Jingshan, dividing Song forces.

entries.zh: 宋四川制置使蒲澤之攻成都，紐鄰率師與戰，敗之；
entries.en: Pu Zezhi, the Song commissioner of Sichuan, attacked Chengdu; Nüyan met him in battle and routed him;
entries.literal: Song Sichuan commissioner Pu Zezhi attacked Chengdu; Nüyan led troops to engage him and defeated him;

entries.zh: 進攻雲頂山，守將姚某等以眾相繼來降。
entries.en: then pressed on to Yunding Mountain, where the garrison commanders Yao and others surrendered one after another with their troops.
entries.literal: advancing to attack Yunding Mountain, where the garrison commanders Yao and others successively came over with their forces.

entries.zh: 詔以紐鄰為都元帥。
entries.en: An edict made Nüyan supreme commander.
entries.literal: An edict appointed Nüyan supreme commander.

entries.zh: 帝由東勝渡河。
entries.en: The Emperor forded the river from Dongsheng.
entries.literal: The Emperor crossed the river from Dongsheng.

entries.zh: 遣參知政事劉太平括興元戶口。
entries.en: Vice Grand Councillor Liu Taiping was sent to register the households of Xingyuan.
entries.literal: Vice Grand Councillor Liu Taiping was dispatched to register the households of Xingyuan.

entries.zh: 三月，命洪茶丘率師從劄剌䚟同征高麗。
entries.en: In the third month Hong Chagiu was ordered to take troops and join Qarachar in the campaign against Goryeo.
entries.literal: In the third month Hong Chagiu was ordered to lead troops following Qarachar in the campaign against Goryeo.

entries.zh: 夏四月，駐蹕六盤山，諸郡縣守令來覲。
entries.en: In the fourth summer month he encamped at Liupan Mountain, and the prefectural and county magistrates came to audience.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of summer he halted at Liupan Mountain; the magistrates of the commanderies and counties came to audience.

entries.zh: 豐州千戶郭燧奏請續簽軍千人修治金州，從之。
entries.en: Guo Sui, thousand-household commander of Fengzhou, asked to conscript another thousand men to repair Jinzhou, and the petition was granted.
entries.literal: Guo Sui, thousand-household commander of Fengzhou, petitioned to conscript another thousand troops to repair Jinzhou; the request was granted.

entries.zh: 是時，軍四萬，號十萬，分三道而進：帝由隴州入散關，諸王莫哥由洋州入米倉關，孛裏義萬戶由漁關入沔州。
entries.en: The army then stood at forty thousand but marched under the banner of one hundred thousand, split into three columns: the Emperor entered by San Pass from Longzhou; Prince Möge by Micang Pass from Yangzhou; and the thousand-household commander Boriy by Yu Pass into Mianzhou.
entries.literal: At this time the army numbered forty thousand but was proclaimed as one hundred thousand, advancing in three columns: the Emperor entered through San Pass from Longzhou; Prince Möge entered through Micang Pass from Yangzhou; and the thousand-household commander Boriy entered through Yu Pass into Mianzhou.

entries.zh: 以明安答兒為太傅，守京兆。
entries.en: Minggansar was made Grand Preceptor and left to hold Jingzhao.
entries.literal: Minggansar was appointed Grand Preceptor to guard Jingzhao.

entries.zh: 詔征益都行省李璮兵，璮來言：「益都南北要衝，兵不可撤。」
entries.en: An edict called up the troops of Li Tan, chief of the Yidu Branch Secretariat. Tan came in person and said, "Yidu is the hinge between north and south; the army cannot be pulled away."
entries.literal: An edict summoned the forces of Li Tan, chief of the Yidu Branch Secretariat. Tan came and said, "Yidu is the vital junction between north and south; the troops cannot be withdrawn."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: His plea was granted.
entries.literal: The request was granted.

entries.zh: 璮還，擊海州、漣水等處。
entries.en: Tan returned and struck Haizhou, Lianshui, and neighboring districts.
entries.literal: Tan returned and attacked Haizhou, Lianshui, and other places.

entries.zh: 五月，皇子阿速帶因獵獨騎傷民稼，帝見讓之，遂撻近侍數人。
entries.en: In the fifth month Prince Asudai, hunting alone, rode through the peasants' fields and ruined the crop. When the Emperor saw it he rebuked him and had several attendants whipped.
entries.literal: In the fifth month the prince Asudai, while hunting alone on horseback, trampled the people's crops. The Emperor reproached him upon seeing it and had several attendants flogged.

entries.zh: 士卒有拔民蔥者，即斬以徇。
entries.en: A soldier who so much as pulled an onion from a farmer's plot was beheaded on the spot.
entries.literal: Any soldier who pulled up scallions from civilian fields was immediately beheaded as an example.

entries.zh: 由是秋毫莫敢犯。
entries.en: After that not a blade of grass was touched.
entries.literal: Henceforth not even the slightest thing dared be touched.

entries.zh: 仍賜所經郡守各有差。
entries.en: The magistrates of the districts the army passed through were rewarded in turn, each according to his merit.
entries.literal: The magistrates of the districts passed through were further rewarded in varying measure.

entries.zh: 秋七月，留輜重於六盤山，率兵由寶雞攻重貴山，所至輒平。
entries.en: In the seventh month of autumn he left the baggage at Liupan Mountain and led the army through Baoji against Chongguishan, reducing every place they reached.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of autumn he left the baggage train at Liupan Mountain and led troops through Baoji to attack Chongguishan; wherever they went they pacified the land.

entries.zh: 八月辛丑，璮與宋人戰，殺宋師殆盡。
entries.en: On xinchou day in the eighth month Tan met the Song in battle and cut their force nearly to the last man.
entries.literal: On xinchou day in the eighth month Tan fought the Song and slaughtered their army nearly to the last man.

entries.zh: 九月，駐蹕漢中。
entries.en: In the ninth month he encamped at Hanzhong.
entries.literal: In the ninth month he halted at Hanzhong.

entries.zh: 都元帥紐鄰留密裏火者、劉黑馬等守成都，悉率余兵渡馬湖，禽宋制置使張實，遂遣實招諭苦竹隘，實遁。
entries.en: Supreme commander Nüyan left Milihuozhe, Liu Heima, and others to hold Chengdu, then crossed Mahu Lake with the rest of his force, captured the Song commissioner Zhang Shi, and sent him to call on Kuzhu Pass to surrender; Shi fled.
entries.literal: Supreme commander Nüyan left Milihuozhe, Liu Heima, and others to guard Chengdu, then led the remaining troops across Mahu Lake, captured the Song commissioner Zhang Shi, and sent Shi to summon Kuzhu Pass to surrender; Shi fled.

entries.zh: 冬十月壬午，帝次寶峰。
entries.en: On renwu day in the tenth winter month the Emperor encamped at Baofeng.
entries.literal: On renwu day in the tenth month of winter the Emperor halted at Baofeng.

entries.zh: 癸未，如利州，觀其城池並非深固，以汪田哥能守，蜀不敢犯，賜卮酒獎諭之。
entries.en: On guiwei day he entered Lizhou. The walls were neither deep nor strong, but Wang Tiange had held them so well that Shu had never dared strike; the Emperor raised a cup of wine in praise.
entries.literal: On guiwei day he went to Lizhou. Seeing that its walls were not especially deep or strong, yet because Wang Tiange had held them ably and Shu had not dared attack, he granted a cup of wine in commendation.

entries.zh: 帝渡嘉陵江，至白水江，命田哥造浮梁以濟，梁成，賜田哥等金帛有差。
entries.en: The Emperor crossed the Jialing to the Baishui and ordered Tiange to build a pontoon bridge. When it was ready he rewarded Tiange and his men with gold and silk in graded gifts.
entries.literal: The Emperor crossed the Jialing River to the Baishui River, ordered Tiange to build a pontoon bridge for the crossing; when it was finished, he granted Tiange and the others gold and silk in varying measure.

entries.zh: 帝駐蹕劍門。
entries.en: The Emperor encamped at Jianmen.
entries.literal: The Emperor halted at Jianmen.

entries.zh: 戊子，攻苦竹隘，裨將趙仲竊獻東南門，師入，與其守將楊立戰，敗之，殺立，眾皆奔潰。
entries.en: On wuzi day they assaulted Kuzhu Pass. Vice-commander Zhao Zhong opened the southeast gate from within; the army poured in, fought the garrison commander Yang Li, broke him, and killed him, and the defenders fled in rout.
entries.literal: On wuzi day they attacked Kuzhu Pass. Vice-commander Zhao Zhong secretly opened the southeast gate; the army entered, fought the garrison commander Yang Li, defeated him, killed Li, and the troops all fled in rout.

entries.zh: 詔毋犯趙仲家屬，仍賜仲衣帽，徙于隆慶。
entries.en: An edict protected Zhao Zhong's household from reprisal, granted him hat and robes, and moved him to Longqing.
entries.literal: An edict forbade harming Zhao Zhong's family; Zhong was further granted hat and robes and transferred to Longqing.

entries.zh: 己亥，獲張實，支解之。
entries.en: On jihai day Zhang Shi was taken and torn limb from limb.
entries.literal: On jihai day Zhang Shi was captured and dismembered.

entries.zh: 賜田哥玉帶及犒賞士卒，留精兵五百守之。
entries.en: Tiange received a jade belt and the troops were given bounty; five hundred picked men were left to hold the pass.
entries.literal: Tiange was granted a jade belt and the troops were rewarded; five hundred picked soldiers were left to garrison the pass.

entries.zh: 遣使招諭龍州。
entries.en: Envoys were dispatched to call on Longzhou to submit.
entries.literal: Envoys were sent to summon Longzhou to surrender.

entries.zh: 帝至高峰。
entries.en: The Emperor advanced to Gaofeng.
entries.literal: The Emperor reached Gaofeng.

entries.zh: 庚子，圍長寧山，守將王佐、裨將徐昕等率兵出戰，敗之。
entries.en: On gengzi day they invested Changning Mountain; garrison commander Wang Zuo and vice-commander Xu Xin sallied out and were beaten back.
entries.literal: On gengzi day they besieged Changning Mountain; garrison commander Wang Zuo and vice-commander Xu Xin led troops out to fight and were defeated.

entries.zh: 十一月己酉，帝督軍先攻鵝頂堡。
entries.en: On jiyou day in the eleventh month the Emperor took command in person and opened the assault on Eding Fort.
entries.literal: On jiyou day in the eleventh month the Emperor personally directed the army, first attacking Eding Fort.

entries.zh: 壬子，力戰於望喜門。
entries.en: On renzi day they fought hard at Wangxi Gate.
entries.literal: On renzi day they fought fiercely at Wangxi Gate.

entries.zh: 薄暮，宋知縣王仲由鵝頂堡出降。
entries.en: At dusk the Song magistrate Wang Zhong came down from Eding Fort to surrender.
entries.literal: At dusk Song magistrate Wang Zhong came out from Eding Fort to surrender.

entries.zh: 是夜破其城，王佐死焉。
entries.en: That night the city fell; Wang Zuo died in the fighting.
entries.literal: That night the city was taken; Wang Zuo died in the fighting.

entries.zh: 癸丑，誅佐之子及徐昕等四十餘人。
entries.en: On guichou day Zuo's sons, Xu Xin, and more than forty others were put to death.
entries.literal: On guichou day Zuo's sons and Xu Xin and more than forty others were executed.

entries.zh: 以彭天祥為達魯花赤治其事，王仲副之。
entries.en: Peng Tianxiang was made darughachi to govern the district, with Wang Zhong as his deputy.
entries.literal: Peng Tianxiang was appointed darughachi to administer the place, with Wang Zhong as his deputy.

entries.zh: 丙辰，進攻大獲山，守將楊大淵降，命大淵為四川侍郎，仍以其兵從。
entries.en: On bingchen day they pressed the attack on Daguo Mountain; garrison commander Yang Dayuan came over, was named Vice Minister of Sichuan, and marched on with his men.
entries.literal: On bingchen day they advanced to attack Daguo Mountain; garrison commander Yang Dayuan submitted and was appointed Vice Minister of Sichuan, and his troops followed with the army.

entries.zh: 庚午，次和溪口，遣驍騎略青居山。
entries.en: On gengwu day they halted at Hexikou and sent swift cavalry to sweep Qingju Mountain.
entries.literal: On gengwu day they halted at Hexikou and sent bold cavalry to raid Qingju Mountain.

entries.zh: 是月，龍州王知府降。
entries.en: That month Prefect Wang of Longzhou submitted.
entries.literal: That month the Wang prefect of Longzhou submitted.

entries.zh: 諸王莫哥都攻禮義山不克，諸王塔察兒略地至江而還，並會於行在所。
entries.en: Prince Mögedü assaulted Liyi Mountain without success; Prince Tachar raided to the river and turned back; both rejoined the Emperor at the mobile court.
entries.literal: Prince Mögedü attacked Liyi Mountain but could not take it; Prince Tachar raided as far as the river and returned; both joined the Emperor at the mobile court.

entries.zh: 命忽必烈統諸路蒙古、漢軍伐宋。
entries.en: Kublai was ordered to take command of the Mongol and Han armies of every circuit for the war against the Song.
entries.literal: Kublai was ordered to command the Mongol and Han armies of all circuits in the campaign against the Song.

entries.zh: 十二月壬午，楊大淵率所部兵與汪田哥分擊相如等縣。
entries.en: On renwu day in the twelfth month Yang Dayuan and Wang Tiange split their forces to strike Xiangru and neighboring counties.
entries.literal: On renwu day in the twelfth month Yang Dayuan led his troops with Wang Tiange to strike Xiangru and other counties separately.

entries.zh: 都元帥紐鄰攻簡州，以宋降將張威率眾為先鋒。
entries.en: Supreme commander Nüyan invested Jianzhou, with the Song turncoat Zhang Wei at the head of the van.
entries.literal: Supreme commander Nüyan attacked Jianzhou, with the Song surrendered general Zhang Wei leading the vanguard.

entries.zh: 乙酉，帝次於運山。
entries.en: On yiyou day the Emperor encamped at Yunshan.
entries.literal: On yiyou day the Emperor halted at Yunshan.

entries.zh: 大 淵遣人招降其守將張大悅，仍以大悅為元帥。
entries.en: Dayuan sent envoys to win over the garrison commander Zhang Dayue and made Dayue commander-in-chief once he submitted.
entries.literal: Dayuan sent men to summon the garrison commander Zhang Dayue to submit, and appointed Dayue commander-in-chief.

entries.zh: 師至青居山，裨將劉淵等殺都統段元鑒降。
entries.en: The army reached Qingju Mountain, where the assistant commander Liu Yuan and his officers killed the garrison commander Duan Yuanjian and submitted.
entries.literal: The army reached Qingju Mountain; the assistant general Liu Yuan and others killed the commander Duan Yuanjian and surrendered.

entries.zh: 庚寅，遣使招諭未附。
entries.en: On gengyin day, envoys were dispatched to call in those who had not yet submitted.
entries.literal: On gengyin day, envoys were sent to summon and instruct those not yet submitted.

entries.zh: 丁酉，隆州守縣降。
entries.en: On dingyou day, the magistrate holding Long Prefecture surrendered.
entries.literal: On dingyou day, the district magistrate defending Long Prefecture surrendered.

entries.zh: 己亥，大良山守將蒲元圭降。
entries.en: On jihai day, Pu Yuangui, who held Daliang Mountain, came over.
entries.literal: On jihai day, the defending general Pu Yuangui of Daliang Mountain surrendered.

entries.zh: 詔諸軍毋俘掠。
entries.en: An edict forbade the armies to loot or take prisoners.
entries.literal: An edict ordered all armies not to take captives or plunder.

entries.zh: 癸卯，攻雅州，拔之。
entries.en: On guimao day they stormed Ya Prefecture and captured it.
entries.literal: On guimao day, they attacked Ya Prefecture and took it.

entries.zh: 石泉守將趙順降。
entries.en: Zhao Shun, the garrison commander at Shiquan, submitted.
entries.literal: The defending general Zhao Shun of Shiquan surrendered.

entries.zh: 甲辰，遣宋人晉國寶招諭合州守將王堅，堅辭之，國寶遂歸。
entries.en: On jiachen day the Emperor sent the Song defector Jin Guobao to treat with Wang Jian, He Prefecture's commander; Wang Jian refused, and Guobao turned back.
entries.literal: On jiachen day, the Song man Jin Guobao was sent to summon and instruct Wang Jian, the defending general of He Prefecture; Wang Jian declined, and Guobao then returned.

entries.zh: 是歲，皇子辨都薨于吉河之南。
entries.en: That year Prince Bian Du died on the south bank of the Ji River.
entries.literal: That year, the prince Bian Du died south of the Ji River.

entries.zh: 九年己未春正月乙巳朔，駐蹕重貴山北，置酒大會，因問諸王、駙馬、百官曰：「今在宋境，夏暑且至，汝等其謂可居否乎？」
entries.en: In the ninth year (jiwei), on the yisi day, the new moon of the first spring month, the Emperor encamped north of Zhongguishan and held a great feast. He asked his princes, sons-in-law, and ministers, "We are deep in Song territory, and the summer heat is coming — can we endure it here?"
entries.literal: In the ninth year, jiwei, spring, first month, on yisi day (new moon), the Emperor halted north of Zhongguishan, set out wine at a great assembly, and asked the princes, imperial sons-in-law, and officials: "We are now in Song territory; the summer heat is about to come — do you think we can remain here?"

entries.zh: 劄剌亦兒部人脫歡曰：「南土瘴癘，上宜北還，所獲人民，委吏治之便。」
entries.en: Toqur of the Jadaran tribe replied, "These southern lands breed pestilence. Your Majesty should withdraw north and leave the people we have taken to be governed by appointed officials."
entries.literal: Toqur of the Jadaran tribe said, "The southern lands are malarial; Your Majesty should return north. It would be best to leave the people we have taken to be administered by officials."

entries.zh: 阿兒剌部人八里赤曰：「脫歡怯，臣願往居焉。」
entries.en: Baraq of the Arlat tribe answered, "Toqur lacks nerve. Your servant will gladly stay and hold these lands."
entries.literal: Baraq of the Arlat tribe said, "Toqur is faint-hearted. Your servant is willing to remain and dwell there."

entries.zh: 帝善之。
entries.en: The Emperor was pleased by this.
entries.literal: The Emperor approved of this.

entries.zh: 戊申，晉國寶歸次峽口，王堅追還殺之。
entries.en: On wushen day Guobao was making his way back when he halted at the gorge mouth; Wang Jian overtook him, hauled him back, and executed him.
entries.literal: On wushen day, Jin Guobao, on his return, halted at Xiakou; Wang Jian pursued, brought him back, and killed him.

entries.zh: 諸王莫哥都復攻渠州禮義山，曳剌禿魯雄攻巴州平梁山。
entries.en: Prince Mogedu renewed the assault on Liyi Mountain in Qu Prefecture, while Yelü Chulu Xiong attacked Pingliang Mountain in Ba Prefecture.
entries.literal: Prince Mogedu again attacked Liyi Mountain in Qu Prefecture; Yelü Chulu Xiong attacked Pingliang Mountain in Ba Prefecture.

entries.zh: 丁卯，大淵請攻合州，俘男女八萬餘。
entries.en: On dingmao day Yang Dayuan asked leave to assault He Prefecture and brought in more than eighty thousand captives, men and women together.
entries.literal: On dingmao day, Dayuan requested to attack He Prefecture and took more than eighty thousand men and women captive.

entries.zh: 二月丙子，帝悉率諸兵渡雞爪灘，至石子山。
entries.en: In the second month, on bingzi day, the Emperor led the full host across Chicken-claw Beach to Stone Mountain.
entries.literal: In the second month, on bingzi day, the Emperor led all troops across Jizhuo Beach to Shizi Mountain.

entries.zh: 丁丑，督諸軍戰城下。
entries.en: On dingchou day he drove his armies to battle beneath the walls.
entries.literal: On dingchou day, he supervised the armies fighting below the city walls.

entries.zh: 辛巳，攻一字城。
entries.en: On xinsi day they assaulted the One-character Fort.
entries.literal: On xinsi day, they attacked Yizi Fort.

entries.zh: 癸未，攻鎮西門。
entries.en: On guiwei day they struck the Western Gate bastion.
entries.literal: On guiwei day, they attacked Zhenxi Gate.

entries.zh: 三月，攻東新門、奇勝門、鎮西門小堡。
entries.en: In the third month they pressed the Eastern New Gate, the Gate of Strange Victories, and the outer works of the Western Gate.
entries.literal: In the third month, they attacked the Eastern New Gate, the Qisheng Gate, and the small fort at the Western Gate bastion.

entries.zh: 夏四月丙子，大雷雨凡二十日。
entries.en: In the fourth summer month, on bingzi day, torrential storms rolled on for twenty days.
entries.literal: In the fourth summer month, on bingzi day, great thunder and rain lasted twenty days altogether.

entries.zh: 乙未，攻護國門。
entries.en: On yiwei day they stormed the Gate of Guarding the State.
entries.literal: On yiwei day, they attacked the Gate of Guarding the State.

entries.zh: 丁酉，夜登外城，殺宋兵甚眾。
entries.en: On dingyou day, under cover of night, they climbed the outer wall and cut down large numbers of Song defenders.
entries.literal: On dingyou day, at night they scaled the outer wall and killed a great many Song soldiers.

entries.zh: 五月，屢攻不克。
entries.en: Through the fifth month they battered the fortress again and again without success.
entries.literal: In the fifth month, repeated attacks failed to take the city.

entries.zh: 六月丁巳，汪田哥復選兵夜登外城馬軍寨，殺寨主及守城者。
entries.en: In the sixth month, on dingsi day, Wang Tiange again handpicked a force that climbed the cavalry redoubt on the outer wall by night and killed its commander and the men holding it.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, on dingsi day, Wang Tiange again selected troops, and at night scaled the outer-wall Cavalry Fort, killing the fort commander and the defenders.

entries.zh: 王堅率兵來戰。
entries.en: Wang Jian came out to fight.
entries.literal: Wang Jian led troops to give battle.

entries.zh: 遲明，遇雨，梯折，後軍不克進而止。
entries.en: Near daybreak rain swept in; the ladders snapped, the rear columns could not follow, and the assault was called off.
entries.literal: At dawn, rain fell; the siege ladders broke, and the rear army could not advance, so they halted.

entries.zh: 是月，帝不豫。
entries.en: That month the Emperor took ill.
entries.literal: That month, the Emperor fell ill.

entries.zh: 秋七月辛亥，留精兵三千守之，余悉攻重慶。
entries.en: In the seventh autumn month, on xinhai day, he left three thousand elite troops to hold the siege and marched the rest against Chongqing.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on xinhai day, three thousand picked troops were left to hold the place, and the rest all attacked Chongqing.

entries.zh: 癸亥，帝崩於釣魚山，壽五十有二，在位九年。
entries.en: On guihai day the Emperor died at Diaoyu Mountain. He was fifty-two and had ruled nine years.
entries.literal: On guihai day, the Emperor died at Diaoyu Mountain; he was fifty-two years old and had reigned nine years.

entries.zh: 追諡桓肅皇帝，廟號憲宗。
entries.en: Posthumously he was styled Emperor Huansu; his temple name was Xianzong.
entries.literal: Posthumously he was titled Emperor Huansu; his temple name was Xianzong.

entries.zh: 憲宗桓肅皇帝，諱蒙哥，睿宗拖雷之長子也。
entries.en: Xianzong, styled the Emperor Huansu, bore the personal name Möngke and was the eldest son of Ruizong Tolui.
entries.literal: Xianzong, the Emperor Huansu — taboo name Möngke — was the eldest son of Ruizong Tolui.

entries.zh: 母曰莊聖太后，怯烈氏，諱唆魯禾帖尼。
entries.en: His mother was Empress Dowager Zhuang Sheng of the Kereit, Sorghaghtani Beki.
entries.literal: His mother was Empress Dowager Zhuang Sheng of the Kereit clan, personal name Sorghaghtani Beki.

entries.zh: 歲戊辰，十二月三日生帝。
entries.en: He was born on the third day of the twelfth month of the wuchen year.
entries.literal: In the year wuchen, on the third day of the twelfth month, the Emperor was born.

entries.zh: 時有黃忽答部知天象者，言帝后必大貴，故以蒙哥為名。
entries.en: A stargazer of the Yellow Quda tribe declared that the child was destined for greatness, and for that reason he was named Möngke.
entries.literal: At that time a diviner of the Yellow Quda tribe who read the heavens said the child would surely attain the greatest eminence, and so he was named Möngke.

entries.zh: 蒙哥，華言長子也。
entries.en: Möngke, in Chinese, means "eldest son."
entries.literal: Möngke, in Chinese speech, means "eldest son."

entries.zh: 太宗在潛邸，養以為子，屬昂灰皇后撫育之。
entries.en: While Ögedei was still heir apparent, he took the boy as a son and placed him under the care of Empress Anggwi.
entries.literal: When Ögedei was still heir apparent, he raised the boy as his own son and entrusted his upbringing to Empress Anggwi.

entries.zh: 既長，為娶火魯剌部女火裏差為妃，分之部民。
entries.en: When he came of age he was given Huolicha, a daughter of the Qorolas, as his consort, together with a portion of that tribe's households.
entries.literal: When he had grown, a wife was taken for him — Huolicha, daughter of the Qorolas tribe — and a share of the tribe's households was allotted to him.

entries.zh: 及睿宗薨，乃命歸籓邸。
entries.en: After Ruizong's death he was ordered back to his own princely establishment.
entries.literal: When Ruizong died, he was ordered to return to his princely residence.

entries.zh: 從征伐，屢立奇功。
entries.en: On campaign after campaign he won distinction again and again.
entries.literal: He followed on campaigns and repeatedly won extraordinary merit.

entries.zh: 嘗攻欽察部，其酋八赤蠻逃於海島。
entries.en: Once, in an attack on the Qipchaq, their chieftain Bachman escaped to a sea island.
entries.literal: Once, attacking the Qipchaq, their chieftain Bachman fled to an island in the sea.

entries.zh: 帝聞，亟進師，至其地，適大風刮海水去，其淺可渡。
entries.en: When he heard this, he pressed the army forward at once. At the site a great wind drove the sea back, and the shallows became fordable.
entries.literal: Hearing of it, the Emperor hurried the army forward. When they reached the place, a great wind happened to blow the seawater back, leaving the shallows passable on foot.

entries.zh: 帝喜曰：「此天開道與我也。」
entries.en: Delighted, he said, "Heaven has cleared a path for me."
entries.literal: The Emperor said in delight: "Heaven has opened a road for me."

entries.zh: 遂進屠其眾，擒八赤蠻，命之跪，八赤蠻曰：「我為一國主，豈苟求生？
entries.en: He advanced, cut down Bachman's followers, and seized Bachman himself. Ordered to kneel, Bachman replied, "I am king of a nation — shall I grovel merely to survive?
entries.literal: He then pressed forward, slaughtered Bachman's force, and captured Bachman. He ordered Bachman to kneel. Bachman said: "I am sovereign of a realm — would I beg merely to live?

entries.zh: 且身非駝，何以跪人為？」
entries.en: And I am no camel — why should I kneel to another man?"
entries.literal: Besides, my body is not a camel's — why should I kneel before another man?"

entries.zh: 乃命囚之。
entries.en: He was taken and imprisoned.
entries.literal: He was therefore ordered imprisoned.

entries.zh: 八赤蠻謂守者曰：「我之竄入於海，與魚何異，然終見擒，天也。
entries.en: Bachman told his guards, "When I fled into the sea I was little better than a fish, yet I was taken in the end — Heaven willed it.
entries.literal: Bachman said to his guards: "When I hid myself in the sea I was no different from a fish, yet in the end I was captured — it was Heaven's will.

entries.zh: 今水回期且至，軍宜早還。」
entries.en: The returning tide is nearly upon us. The army should withdraw while it still can."
entries.literal: The tide will soon return; the army ought to withdraw at once."

entries.zh: 帝聞之，即班師，而水已至，後軍有浮渡者。
entries.en: The Emperor heard him and ordered an immediate withdrawal. The water was already rising; in the rear some men were swept away as they crossed.
entries.literal: When the Emperor heard this, he at once ordered the army to withdraw; the water had already risen, and in the rear some men were carried off while crossing.

entries.zh: 復與諸王拔都征斡羅思部，至也烈贊城，躬自搏戰，破之。
entries.en: He campaigned again with Prince Batu against the Rus', reached Yaroslavl, fought in the front ranks himself, and took the city.
entries.literal: Again, with Prince Batu, he campaigned against the Rus' and came to Yaroslavl, where he fought hand to hand himself and broke the city.

entries.zh: 三月辛酉朔，烏蒙民叛，敕那懷、火魯思迷率蒙古、漢人新附軍討之。
entries.en: In the third month, on the xinyou new moon, Wumeng people rebelled; an edict ordered Naqun and Qorqas Timish to lead Mongol and newly submitted Han troops to suppress them.
entries.literal: Third month, on the xinyou new moon, Wumeng people rebelled; an edict ordered Naqun and Qorqas Timish to lead Mongol and newly submitted Han troops to suppress them.

entries.zh: 賞忽都答兒等戰功牛羊馬。
entries.en: Cattle, sheep, and horses were granted to reward the battle merit of Qutuq Dar and others.
entries.literal: Cattle, sheep, and horses were granted to reward the battle merit of Qutuq Dar and others.

entries.zh: 益都千戶王著，以阿合馬蠹國害民，與高和尚合謀殺之。
entries.en: Yidu qianhu Wang Zhu, because Ahmad had corrupted the state and harmed the people, joined Gao Heshang in a plot to kill him.
entries.literal: Yidu qianhu Wang Zhu, because Ahmad had corrupted the state and harmed the people, joined Gao Heshang in a plot to kill him.

entries.zh: 壬午，誅王著、張易、高和尚於市，皆醢之，余黨悉伏誅。
entries.en: On renwu day Wang Zhu, Zhang Yi, and Gao Heshang were executed in the market and their bodies pickled; all remaining accomplices were executed.
entries.literal: On renwu day Wang Zhu, Zhang Yi, and Gao Heshang were executed in the market, all pickled; remaining accomplices were entirely executed.

entries.zh: 甲申，的斤帖林以己貲充屯田之費，諸王阿只吉以聞，敕酬其直。
entries.en: On jiashen day Dejin Telin used his own funds for garrison-farm expenses; Prince Ajiji reported it; an edict compensated him at fair value.
entries.literal: On jiashen day Dejin Telin used his own funds for garrison-farm expenses; Prince Ajiji reported it; an edict compensated him at fair value.

entries.zh: 丙戌，禁益都、東平、沿淮諸郡軍民官捕獵。
entries.en: On bingxu day hunting by military and civilian officials of Yidu, Dongping, and commanderies along the Huai was forbidden.
entries.literal: On bingxu day hunting by military and civilian officials of Yidu, Dongping, and commanderies along the Huai was forbidden.

entries.zh: 戊子，立塔兒八合你驛，以烏蒙阿謀歲輸騬馬給之。
entries.en: On wuzi day Tatarbaqani Station was established, supplied annually with gelded horses from Wumeng Amu.
entries.literal: On wuzi day Tatarbaqani Station was established, supplied annually with gelded horses from Wumeng Amu.

entries.zh: 以領北庭都護阿必失哈為御史大夫，行御史臺事。
entries.en: Beshbaligh protector-general Abishaq was made censor-in-chief, conducting branch censorate affairs.
entries.literal: Beshbaligh protector-general Abishaq was made censor-in-chief, conducting branch censorate affairs.

entries.zh: 十九年春正月壬戌朔，高麗國王王春遣其大將軍金子廷來賀。
entries.en: In the nineteenth year, on the renxu new moon of the first month of spring, King Wang Chun of Goryeo sent his general-in-chief Jin Ziting to offer congratulations.
entries.literal: In the nineteenth year, spring, first month, on the renxu new moon, King Wang Chun of Goryeo dispatched his general-in-chief Jin Ziting to offer congratulations.

entries.zh: 丙寅，罷征東行中書省。
entries.en: On bingyin day the Japan expedition branch secretariat was abolished.
entries.literal: On bingyin day the Japan Expedition Branch Secretariat was abolished.

entries.zh: 丁卯，諸王劄剌忽至自軍中。
entries.en: On dingmao day Prince Zhalahu arrived from the army.
entries.literal: On dingmao day Prince Zhalahu arrived from the army.

entries.zh: 時皇子北平王以軍鎮阿裏麻裏之地，以禦海都。
entries.en: At that time the imperial son, Prince of Beiping, had troops garrison Alimali to guard against Kaidu.
entries.literal: At that time the imperial son, Prince of Beiping, had troops garrison the land of Alimali to guard against Kaidu.

entries.zh: 諸王昔裏吉與脫脫木兒、棨木忽兒、撒裏蠻等謀劫皇子北平王以叛，欲與劄剌忽結援於海都，海都不從。
entries.en: Prince Sheraqi, together with Tuotuo Mier, Qimuhuer, Sariman, and others, plotted to seize the Prince of Beiping and rebel, hoping to ally through Zhalahu with Kaidu; Kaidu refused.
entries.literal: Prince Sheraqi, together with Tuotuo Mier, Qimuhuer, Sariman, and others, plotted to seize the Prince of Beiping and rebel, wishing to link arms through Zhalahu with Kaidu; Kaidu would not agree.

entries.zh: 撒裏蠻悔過，執昔裏吉等，北平王遣劄剌忽以聞。
entries.en: Sariman repented, seized Sheraqi and the others, and the Prince of Beiping sent Zhalahu to report it.
entries.literal: Sariman repented, seized Sheraqi and the others, and the Prince of Beiping sent Zhalahu to report it.

entries.zh: 妖民張圓光伏誅。
entries.en: The sorcerer-subversive Zhang Roundong was executed.
entries.literal: The sorcerer-subversive Zhang Roundong was executed.

entries.zh: 立太僕院。
entries.en: The Grand Stable Office was established.
entries.literal: The Grand Stable Office was established.

entries.zh: 撥信州民四百八戶隸諸王柏木兒。
entries.en: 408 Xinzhou households were assigned to Prince Bomuer.
entries.literal: Four hundred eight Xinzhou households were assigned to Prince Bomuer.

entries.zh: 丙子，車駕畋於近郊。
entries.en: On bingzi day the imperial carriage hunted near the capital.
entries.literal: On bingzi day the imperial carriage hunted in the near suburbs.

entries.zh: 丁丑，高麗國王貢綢布四百匹。
entries.en: On dingchou day the king of Goryeo presented 400 bolts of silk cloth as tribute.
entries.literal: On dingchou day the king of Goryeo presented four hundred bolts of silk cloth as tribute.

entries.zh: 丙戌，賜西平王怯薛那懷等鈔一萬一千五百二十一錠。
entries.en: On bingxu day Keshig Naqun, Prince of Xiping, and others were granted 11,521 ingots of paper currency.
entries.literal: On bingxu day Keshig Naqun, Prince of Xiping, and others were granted eleven thousand five hundred twenty-one ingots of paper currency.

entries.zh: 三月戊午朔，次潔堅察罕之地。
entries.en: Third month, on wuwu new moon, he halted at Jegianchaghan.
entries.literal: Third month, on wuwu new moon, he halted at Jegianchaghan.

entries.zh: 辛酉，文宗遣右丞相燕鐵木兒奉皇帝寶來上，御史中丞八即剌、知樞密院事禿兒哈帖木兒等，各率其屬以從。
entries.en: On xinyou day Wenzong dispatched right chancellor Yan Temür to present the imperial seal; surveillance vice censor Ba'irq, privy council administrator Tughqa Temür, and others each led their subordinates to follow.
entries.literal: On xinyou day Wenzong dispatched right chancellor Yan Temür to present the imperial seal; surveillance vice censor Ba'irq, privy council administrator Tughqa Temür, and others each led their subordinates to follow.

entries.zh: 壬戌，造乘輿服御及近侍諸服用。
entries.en: On renxu day imperial chariots, robes, and the apparel of close attendants were made.
entries.literal: On renxu day imperial chariots, robes, and the apparel of close attendants were made.

entries.zh: 丙寅，帝謂中書左丞躍裏帖木兒曰：「朕至上都，宗藩諸王必皆來會，非尋常朝會比也，諸王察阿臺今亦從朕遠來，有司供張，皆宜豫備。
entries.en: On bingyin day the Emperor said to central secretariat left vice chancellor Yolqi Temür, "When I reach Shangdu, the princes of the imperial domains will surely all come to assemble — this is not comparable to an ordinary court audience; Prince Cha'atai now also follows me from afar; the relevant offices' provisions for guests must all be prepared in advance.
entries.literal: On bingyin day the Emperor said to central secretariat left vice chancellor Yolqi Temür, "When I reach Shangdu, the princes of the imperial domains will surely all come to assemble — this is not comparable to an ordinary court audience; Prince Cha'atai now also follows me from afar; the relevant offices' provisions for guests must all be prepared in advance.

entries.zh: 卿其與中書臣僚議之。」
entries.en: You should deliberate on this with the secretariat ministers."
entries.literal: You should deliberate on this with the secretariat ministers."

entries.zh: 丁亥，雨土，霾。
entries.en: On dinghai day earth rained; there was haze.
entries.literal: On dinghai day earth rained; there was haze.

entries.zh: 四月癸巳，燕鐵木兒見帝於行在，率百官上皇帝寶，帝嘉其勛，拜太師，仍命為中書右丞相，開府儀同三司、上柱國、錄軍國重事、監修國史、答剌罕、太平王並如故。
entries.en: Fourth month, on guisi day Yan Temür saw the Emperor at the traveling palace and led the hundred officials in presenting the imperial seal; the Emperor praised his merit and made him grand preceptor, still appointing him central secretariat right chancellor, commissioner with the same trappings as the Three Excellencies of an opened princely household, pillar of state of the upper grade, recorder of state military affairs, supervisor of the state history, darughachi, and Prince of Taiping — all as before.
entries.literal: Fourth month, on guisi day Yan Temür saw the Emperor at the traveling palace and led the hundred officials in presenting the imperial seal; the Emperor praised his merit and made him grand preceptor, still appointing him central secretariat right chancellor, commissioner with the same trappings as the Three Excellencies of an opened princely household, pillar of state of the upper grade, recorder of state military affairs, supervisor of the state history, darughachi, and Prince of Taiping — all as before.

entries.zh: 復諭燕鐵木兒等曰：「凡京師百官，朕弟所用者，並仍其舊，卿等其以朕意諭之。」
entries.en: He again instructed Yan Temür and the others, saying, "Of the hundred officials at the capital whom my younger brother employs, all shall remain as before; you should convey my intent to them."
entries.literal: He again instructed Yan Temür and the others, saying, "Of the hundred officials at the capital whom my younger brother employs, all shall remain as before; you should convey my intent to them."

entries.zh: 燕鐵木兒奏：「陛下君臨萬方，國家大事所系者，中書省、樞密院、御史臺而已，宜擇人居之。」
entries.en: Yan Temür memorialized, "Your Majesty rules the myriad regions; what the state's great affairs depend upon is only the Central Secretariat, the Privy Council, and the Censorate — suitable men should be chosen to fill them."
entries.literal: Yan Temür memorialized, "Your Majesty rules the myriad regions; what the state's great affairs depend upon is only the Central Secretariat, the Privy Council, and the Censorate — suitable men should be chosen to fill them."

entries.zh: 帝然其言，以武宗舊人哈八兒禿為中書平章政事，前中書平章政事伯帖木兒知樞密院事，常侍孛羅為御史大夫。
entries.en: The Emperor approved his words and made Wuzong's old follower Qabarqu central secretariat grand councillor, former central secretariat grand councillor Bo Temür privy council administrator, and attendant Boluo censor-in-chief.
entries.literal: The Emperor approved his words and made Wuzong's old follower Qabarqu central secretariat grand councillor, former central secretariat grand councillor Bo Temür privy council administrator, and attendant Boluo censor-in-chief.

entries.zh: 甲午，立行樞密院，命昭武王、知樞密院事火沙領行樞密院事，賽帖木兒、買奴並同知行樞密院事。
entries.en: On jiawu day a traveling privy council was established; Prince Zhaowu and privy council administrator Huosha was put in charge of traveling privy council affairs; Sa Temür, Mainu, and others were made associate traveling privy council administrators.
entries.literal: On jiawu day a traveling privy council was established; Prince Zhaowu and privy council administrator Huosha was put in charge of traveling privy council affairs; Sa Temür, Mainu, and others were made associate traveling privy council administrators.

entries.zh: 是日，帝宴諸王、大臣於行殿，燕鐵木兒、哈八兒禿、伯帖木兒、孛羅等侍。
entries.en: That day the Emperor feasted the princes and great ministers in the traveling hall; Yan Temür, Qabarqu, Bo Temür, Boluo, and others attended.
entries.literal: That day the Emperor feasted the princes and great ministers in the traveling hall; Yan Temür, Qabarqu, Bo Temür, Boluo, and others attended.

entries.zh: 帝特命臺臣曰：「太祖皇帝嘗訓敕臣下云：『美色、名馬，人皆悅之，然方寸一有系累，即能壞名敗德。』
entries.en: The Emperor specially charged the censorate officials, saying, "Taizu once admonished his ministers, saying, 'Beautiful women and famous horses — all men delight in them; yet if the heart's inch is once entangled, it can ruin name and virtue.'
entries.literal: The Emperor specially charged the censorate officials, saying, "Taizu once admonished his ministers, saying, 'Beautiful women and famous horses — all men delight in them; yet if the heart's inch is once entangled, it can ruin name and virtue.'

entries.zh: 卿等居風紀之司，亦嘗念及此乎？
entries.en: You who hold the office of wind and discipline — have you also ever borne this in mind?
entries.literal: You who hold the office of wind and discipline — have you also ever borne this in mind?

entries.zh: 世祖初立御史臺，首命塔察兒、奔帖傑兒二人協司其政。
entries.en: When Shizu first established the Censorate, he first appointed Taqachar and Bentejir to jointly administer its affairs.
entries.literal: When Shizu first established the Censorate, he first appointed Taqachar and Bentejir to jointly administer its affairs.

entries.zh: 天下國家，譬猶一人之身，中書則右手也，樞密則左手也。
entries.en: All under Heaven and the state are like a single person's body — the Secretariat is the right hand, the Privy Council the left hand.
entries.literal: All under Heaven and the state are like a single person's body — the Secretariat is the right hand, the Privy Council the left hand.

entries.zh: 左右手有病，治之以良醫，省、院闕失，不以御史臺治之可乎？
entries.en: When the left and right hands are ill, one treats them with a good physician — when the Secretariat and Privy Council have faults and omissions, can one fail to treat them through the Censorate?
entries.literal: When the left and right hands are ill, one treats them with a good physician — when the Secretariat and Privy Council have faults and omissions, can one fail to treat them through the Censorate?

entries.zh: 凡諸王、百司，違法越禮，一聽舉劾。
entries.en: For all princes and the hundred offices, whoever violates law or oversteps ritual — all alike are to be impeached.
entries.literal: For all princes and the hundred offices, whoever violates law or oversteps ritual — all alike are to be impeached.

entries.zh: 風紀重則貪墨懼，猶斧斤重則入木深，其勢然也。
entries.en: When wind and discipline are weighty, the greedy and corrupt will fear — as when the axe is heavy, it enters the wood deeply; such is the force of it.
entries.literal: When wind and discipline are weighty, the greedy and corrupt will fear — as when the axe is heavy, it enters the wood deeply; such is the force of it.

entries.zh: 朕有闕失，卿亦以聞，朕不爾責也。」
entries.en: If I have faults and omissions, you too should report them — I shall not blame you for it."
entries.literal: If I have faults and omissions, you too should report them — I shall not blame you for it."

entries.zh: 乙未，特命孛羅等傳旨，宣諭燕鐵木兒、伯答沙、火沙、哈八兒禿、八即剌等曰：「世祖皇帝立中書省、樞密院、御史臺及百司庶府，共治天下，大小職掌，已有定制。
entries.en: On yimao day Boluo and others were specially charged to transmit the intent and proclaim to Yan Temür, Badashah, Huosha, Qabarqu, Ba'irq, and others, saying, "Shizu established the Central Secretariat, the Privy Council, the Censorate, and the hundred offices and various bureaus to jointly govern all under Heaven; great and small duties already have fixed regulations.
entries.literal: On yimao day Boluo and others were specially charged to transmit the intent and proclaim to Yan Temür, Badashah, Huosha, Qabarqu, Ba'irq, and others, saying, "Shizu established the Central Secretariat, the Privy Council, the Censorate, and the hundred offices and various bureaus to jointly govern all under Heaven; great and small duties already have fixed regulations.

entries.zh: 世祖命廷臣集律令章程，以為萬世法。
entries.en: Shizu ordered court ministers to compile statutes and regulations as law for ten thousand generations.
entries.literal: Shizu ordered court ministers to compile statutes and regulations as law for ten thousand generations.

entries.zh: 成宗以來，列聖相承，罔不恪遵成憲。
entries.en: From Chengzong onward, successive sage emperors have none failed to reverently observe the established constitution.
entries.literal: From Chengzong onward, successive sage emperors have none failed to reverently observe the established constitution.

entries.zh: 朕今居太祖、世祖所居之位，凡省、院、臺、百司庶政，詢謀僉同，摽譯所奏，以告於朕。
entries.en: I now occupy the seat where Taizu and Shizu dwelt; for all Secretariat, Privy Council, Censorate, and hundred-office affairs, after consultation and unanimous deliberation, translate what is memorialized and report it to me.
entries.literal: I now occupy the seat where Taizu and Shizu dwelt; for all Secretariat, Privy Council, Censorate, and hundred-office affairs, after consultation and unanimous deliberation, translate what is memorialized and report it to me.

entries.zh: 軍務機密，樞密院當即以聞，毋以夙夜為間而稽留之。
entries.en: Military affairs of secrecy — the Privy Council should report them immediately; do not delay on account of early or late hour.
entries.literal: Military affairs of secrecy — the Privy Council should report them immediately; do not delay on account of early or late hour.

entries.zh: 其他事務，果有所言，必先中書、院、臺，其下百司及纮禦之臣，毋得隔越陳請。
entries.en: For other affairs, if there is truly something to say, one must first go through the Secretariat, Privy Council, and Censorate; subordinate hundred offices and ministers of the broad defense must not overstep ranks in submitting requests.
entries.literal: For other affairs, if there is truly something to say, one must first go through the Secretariat, Privy Council, and Censorate; subordinate hundred offices and ministers of the broad defense must not overstep ranks in submitting requests.

entries.zh: 宜宣諭諸司，咸俾聞知。
entries.en: This should be proclaimed to the various offices, so that all may hear and know.
entries.literal: This should be proclaimed to the various offices, so that all may hear and know.

entries.zh: 儻違朕意，必罰無赦。」
entries.en: If anyone violates my intent, punishment shall be without pardon."
entries.literal: If anyone violates my intent, punishment shall be without pardon."

entries.zh: 丁酉，以陜西行臺御史大夫鐵木兒脫為上都留守。
entries.en: On dingyou day Shaanxi branch surveillance censor-in-chief Temür Toq was made Shangdu garrison commissioner.
entries.literal: On dingyou day Shaanxi branch surveillance censor-in-chief Temür Toq was made Shangdu garrison commissioner.

entries.zh: 辛丑，文宗立都督府於京師，遣使來奏，又以臺憲官除目來上，並從之。
entries.en: On xinchou day Wenzong established a commandery-general's office at the capital and dispatched envoys to memorialize; censorate and surveillance appointment orders were also submitted — all were approved.
entries.literal: On xinchou day Wenzong established a commandery-general's office at the capital and dispatched envoys to memorialize; censorate and surveillance appointment orders were also submitted — all were approved.

entries.zh: 癸卯，遣使如京師，卜日命中書左丞相鐵木兒補化攝告即位於郊廟、社稷。
entries.en: On guimao day envoys were dispatched to the capital to select a day; left chancellor Temür Buqa was ordered to perform the proxy announcement of accession at the suburban altars and the altars of soil and grain.
entries.literal: On guimao day envoys were dispatched to the capital to select a day; left chancellor Temür Buqa was ordered to perform the proxy announcement of accession at the suburban altars and the altars of soil and grain.

entries.zh: 遣武寧王徹徹禿及哈八兒禿立文宗為皇太子，仍立詹事院，罷儲慶司，以徹裏鐵木兒為中書平章政事，闊兒吉司為中書右丞，怯來、只兒哈郎並為甘肅行省平章政事，忽剌臺為江浙行省平章政事，那海為嶺北行省平章政事。
entries.en: Prince Wuning Chechequ and Qabarqu were dispatched to install Wenzong as crown prince; the Crown Prince's Household was still established and the Office of Stored Blessings abolished; Cheli Temür was made central secretariat grand councillor, Kokejis central secretariat right vice chancellor, Qelai and Jirhalang were both made Gansu branch secretariat grand councillors, Hulatai was made Jiang-Zhe branch secretariat grand councillor, and Nohai was made Lingbei branch secretariat grand councillor.
entries.literal: Prince Wuning Chechequ and Qabarqu were dispatched to install Wenzong as crown prince; the Crown Prince's Household was still established and the Office of Stored Blessings abolished; Cheli Temür was made central secretariat grand councillor, Kokejis central secretariat right vice chancellor, Qelai and Jirhalang were both made Gansu branch secretariat grand councillors, Hulatai was made Jiang-Zhe branch secretariat grand councillor, and Nohai was made Lingbei branch secretariat grand councillor.

entries.zh: 甲辰，敕中書省賜官吏送寶者秩一等，從者賚以幣帛。
entries.en: On jiachen day the Central Secretariat was ordered to grant one rank higher to officials who delivered the seal; followers were rewarded with coins and silks.
entries.literal: On jiachen day the Central Secretariat was ordered to grant one rank higher to officials who delivered the seal; followers were rewarded with coins and silks.

entries.zh: 乙巳，監察御史言：「嶺北行省，控制一方，廣輪萬里，實為太祖肇基之地，國家根本系焉。
entries.en: On yisi day a supervising censor said, "The Lingbei branch secretariat controls one region, its breadth ten thousand li — it is truly the land where Taizu first laid the foundation; the state's root is bound up with it.
entries.literal: On yisi day a supervising censor said, "The Lingbei branch secretariat controls one region, its breadth ten thousand li — it is truly the land where Taizu first laid the foundation; the state's root is bound up with it.

entries.zh: 方面之寄，豈可輕任。
entries.en: The trust reposed in a frontier post — how can it be lightly assigned?
entries.literal: The trust reposed in a frontier post — how can it be lightly assigned?

entries.zh: 平章塔即吉素非勛舊，奴事倒剌沙，倔起宿衛，輒為右丞，俄升平章，年已七十，毛昏殊甚。
entries.en: Grand councillor Taqaji was never a meritorious old follower; he slavishly served Doresh, rose abruptly from night guard duty, and was immediately made right vice chancellor, then soon promoted grand councillor; he is already 70, and his hair and eyes are extremely dim.
entries.literal: Grand councillor Taqaji was never a meritorious old follower; he slavishly served Doresh, rose abruptly from night guard duty, and was immediately made right vice chancellor, then soon promoted grand councillor; he is already seventy, and his hair and eyes are extremely dim.

entries.zh: 左丞馬謀，本晉邸部民，以女妻倒剌沙，引為都水，遂除左丞。
entries.en: Left vice chancellor Ma Mou was originally a follower of the Jin residence; he gave his daughter in marriage to Doresh, was introduced as director of waterways, and was then appointed left vice chancellor.
entries.literal: Left vice chancellor Ma Mou was originally a follower of the Jin residence; he gave his daughter in marriage to Doresh, was introduced as director of waterways, and was then appointed left vice chancellor.

entries.zh: 郎中羅裏，市井小人，禿魯忽乃晉邸衛卒，不諳政務。
entries.en: Section director Luoli was a marketplace petty man; Tughlughunai was a Jin residence guard soldier — neither understands government affairs.
entries.literal: Section director Luoli was a marketplace petty man; Tughlughunai was a Jin residence guard soldier — neither understands government affairs.

entries.zh: 並宜黜退。」
entries.en: All should be dismissed and demoted."
entries.literal: All should be dismissed and demoted."

entries.zh: 臺臣以聞，帝曰：「御史言甚善，其並黜之。」
entries.en: The censorate officials reported this; the Emperor said, "The censor's words are very good — dismiss them all."
entries.literal: The censorate officials reported this; the Emperor said, "The censor's words are very good — dismiss them all."

entries.zh: 又諭臺臣曰：「御史劾嶺北省臣，朕甚嘉之。
entries.en: He again instructed the censorate officials, saying, "The censor impeached the Lingbei provincial ministers — I greatly commend it.
entries.literal: He again instructed the censorate officials, saying, "The censor impeached the Lingbei provincial ministers — I greatly commend it.

entries.zh: 繼今所當言者，毋有所憚。
entries.en: Hereafter, whatever ought to be spoken — do not hold back.
entries.literal: Hereafter, whatever ought to be spoken — do not hold back.

entries.zh: 被劾之人，茍營求申訴，朕必罪之。
entries.en: If the impeached seek by improper means to appeal, I shall punish them.
entries.literal: If the impeached seek by improper means to appeal, I shall punish them.

entries.zh: 或廉非其實，毋輒以聞。」
entries.en: If the impeachment is not true to fact, do not rashly report it."
entries.literal: If the impeachment is not true to fact, do not rashly report it."

entries.zh: 五月丁巳朔，次朵裏伯真之地。
entries.en: Fifth month, on dingsi new moon, he halted at Doreberjen.
entries.literal: Fifth month, on dingsi new moon, he halted at Doreberjen.

entries.zh: 戊午，遣西安王阿剌忒納失裏還京師，封帖木兒為保德郡王。
entries.en: On wuwu day Prince of Xi'an Alaqtenashiri was dispatched back to the capital; Temür was enfeoffed Prince of Baode Commandery.
entries.literal: On wuwu day Prince of Xi'an Alaqtenashiri was dispatched back to the capital; Temür was enfeoffed Prince of Baode Commandery.

entries.zh: 賜扈駕宿衛士等幣帛有差。
entries.en: Escort night guards and others were granted coins and silks in varying amounts.
entries.literal: Escort night guards and others were granted coins and silks in varying amounts.

entries.zh: 己未，皇太子遣翰林學士承旨阿鄰帖木兒來覲。
entries.en: On jiwei day the crown prince dispatched Hanlin academician exemplar Alin Temür to pay court.
entries.literal: On jiwei day the crown prince dispatched Hanlin academician exemplar Alin Temür to pay court.

entries.zh: 庚申，次斡耳罕木東。
entries.en: On gengshen day the court halted east of Orda-erqen Mu.
entries.literal: On gengshen day the court halted east of Orda-erqen Mu.

entries.zh: 辛酉，御史大夫孛羅、中政使尚家奴，並特授開府儀同三司，以典四番宿衛。
entries.en: On xinyou day censor-in-chief Boluo and Central Domestic Affairs Court commissioner Shangjianu were both specially granted commissioner with the Ceremonial Standing Equal to the Three Excellencies, to supervise the four palace guard corps.
entries.literal: On xinyou day censor-in-chief Boluo and Central Domestic Affairs Court commissioner Shangjianu were both specially granted commissioner with the Ceremonial Standing Equal to the Three Excellencies, to supervise the four palace guard corps.

entries.zh: 癸亥，次必忒怯禿之地，翰林學士承旨斡耳朵自京師來覲。
entries.en: On guihai day the court halted at Biteqetu; Hanlin academician-director Orda-erqen came from the capital to have audience.
entries.literal: On guihai day the court halted at Biteqetu; Hanlin academician-director Orda-erqen came from the capital to have audience.

entries.zh: 命有司新武宗幄殿、車輿。
entries.en: Orders were issued to the relevant offices to renew Wuzong's tent palace and imperial carriages.
entries.literal: Orders were issued to the relevant offices to renew Wuzong's tent palace and imperial carriages.

entries.zh: 庚午，命燕鐵木兒升用嶺北行省官吏，其餘官吏並賜散官一級。
entries.en: On gengwu day Yan Timur was ordered to promote officials of the Lingbei Branch Secretariat; the remaining officials were all granted one grade of honorary rank.
entries.literal: On gengwu day Yan Timur was ordered to promote officials of the Lingbei Branch Secretariat; the remaining officials were all granted one grade of honorary rank.

entries.zh: 選用潛邸舊臣及扈從士，受制命者八十有五人，六品以下二十有六人。
entries.en: Former officials of the latent residence and attendant officers were selected for appointment; 85 who received commission edicts, and 26 of sixth rank and below.
entries.literal: Former officials of the latent residence and attendant officers were selected for appointment; eighty-five who received commission edicts, and twenty-six of sixth rank and below.

entries.zh: 壬申，次探禿兒海之地。
entries.en: On renshen day the court halted at Tantuo'erhai.
entries.literal: On renshen day the court halted at Tantuo'erhai.

entries.zh: 封亦憐真八為柳城郡王，以八即剌為陜西行臺御史大夫，眾家奴為御史中丞。
entries.en: Yilin Zhenba was enfeoffed Prince of Liucheng Commandery; Bajila was made Shaanxi branch censorate grand councillor; Zhongjianu was made associate censor-in-chief.
entries.literal: Yilin Zhenba was enfeoffed Prince of Liucheng Commandery; Bajila was made Shaanxi branch censorate grand councillor; Zhongjianu was made associate censor-in-chief.

entries.zh: 乙亥，次禿忽剌。
entries.en: On yihai day the court halted at Tuhula.
entries.literal: On yihai day the court halted at Tuhula.

entries.zh: 敕大都省臣鑄皇太子寶。
entries.en: An edict directed the Dadu provincial officials to cast the crown prince's seal.
entries.literal: An edict directed the Dadu provincial officials to cast the crown prince's seal.

entries.zh: 時求太子故寶不知所在，近侍伯不花言寶藏於上都行幄，遣人至上都索之，無所得，乃命更鑄之。
entries.en: At the time the former crown prince's seal could not be found; attendant Bobuhua said the seal was stored in the Shangdu travel encampment; men were sent to Shangdu to seek it but nothing was obtained, and orders were then issued to cast a new one.
entries.literal: At the time the former crown prince's seal could not be found; attendant Bobuhua said the seal was stored in the Shangdu travel encampment; men were sent to Shangdu to seek it but nothing was obtained, and orders were then issued to cast a new one.

entries.zh: 西木鄰等四十三驛旱災，命中書以糧賑之，計八千二百石。
entries.en: Forty-three relay stations including Ximulin suffered drought disaster; the central secretariat was ordered to grant grain in relief, totaling 8,200 shi.
entries.literal: Forty-three relay stations including Ximulin suffered drought disaster; the central secretariat was ordered to grant grain in relief, totaling eight thousand two hundred shi.

entries.zh: 丁丑，皇太子發京師。
entries.en: On dingchou day the crown prince departed the capital.
entries.literal: On dingchou day the crown prince departed the capital.

entries.zh: 鎮南王帖木兒不花，諸王也速、斡即、答來不花、朵來只班、伯顏也不幹，駙馬別阇裏及扈衛百官，悉從行。
entries.en: Prince of Zhennan Tiemur Buqa, princes Yesu, Woji, Dalaibuhua, Duolaizhiban, and Boyeyebogan, imperial son-in-law Biejanli, and attendant guards and the hundred offices all followed on the journey.
entries.literal: Prince of Zhennan Tiemur Buqa, princes Yesu, Woji, Dalaibuhua, Duolaizhiban, and Boyeyebogan, imperial son-in-law Biejanli, and attendant guards and the hundred offices all followed on the journey.

entries.zh: 戊寅，京師市馬二百八十匹，載乘輿服御送行在所。
entries.en: On wuyin day 280 horses were purchased in the capital and loaded with imperial carriage accoutrements to be sent to the imperial whereabouts.
entries.literal: On wuyin day two hundred eighty horses were purchased in the capital and loaded with imperial carriage accoutrements to be sent to the imperial whereabouts.

entries.zh: 己卯，次禿忽剌河東。
entries.en: On jimao day the court halted east of the Tuhula River.
entries.literal: On jimao day the court halted east of the Tuhula River.

entries.zh: 加翰林學士承旨唐兀為太尉。
entries.en: Hanlin academician-director Tangut was promoted to grand marshal.
entries.literal: Hanlin academician-director Tangut was promoted to grand marshal.

entries.zh: 趙王馬劄罕部落旱，民五萬五千四百口不能自存，敕河東宣慰司賑糧兩月。
entries.en: The tribes of Prince of Zhao Mazahan suffered drought; 55,400 persons could not support themselves; the Hedong pacification commission was ordered to grant 2 months' relief grain.
entries.literal: The tribes of Prince of Zhao Mazahan suffered drought; fifty-five thousand four hundred persons could not support themselves; the Hedong pacification commission was ordered to grant two months' relief grain.

entries.zh: 庚辰，賜諸王燕只哥臺鈔二百錠、幣帛二千匹。
entries.en: On gengchen day Prince Yanzigetai was granted 200 ingots of notes and 2,000 bolts of silks.
entries.literal: On gengchen day Prince Yanzigetai was granted two hundred ingots of notes and two thousand bolts of silks.

entries.zh: 辛巳，次斡羅斡禿之地。
entries.en: On xinsi day the court halted at Oloroqutu.
entries.literal: On xinsi day the court halted at Oloroqutu.

entries.zh: 壬午，次不魯通之地。
entries.en: On renwu day the court halted at Bulutong.
entries.literal: On renwu day the court halted at Bulutong.

entries.zh: 是日，左丞相鐵木兒補化等以帝即位，攝告南郊。
entries.en: That day left grand councillor Temur Buqa and others, on account of the Emperor's accession, reported by proxy at the Southern Suburb.
entries.literal: That day left grand councillor Temur Buqa and others, on account of the Emperor's accession, reported by proxy at the Southern Suburb.

entries.zh: 甲申，次忽剌火失溫之地。
entries.en: On jiashen day the court halted at Hulahuo Shiwen.
entries.literal: On jiashen day the court halted at Hulahuo Shiwen.

entries.zh: 六月丁亥朔，次坤都也不剌之地。
entries.en: Sixth month, on dinghai new moon, the court halted at Kundu ye Bulaq.
entries.literal: Sixth month, on dinghai new moon, the court halted at Kundu ye Bulaq.

entries.zh: 是日，鐵木兒補化等以帝即位，攝告於宗廟、社稷。
entries.en: That day Temur Buqa and others, on account of the Emperor's accession, reported by proxy at the Imperial Ancestral Temple and the altars of soil and grain.
entries.literal: That day Temur Buqa and others, on account of the Emperor's accession, reported by proxy at the Imperial Ancestral Temple and the altars of soil and grain.

entries.zh: 戊子，燕鐵木兒等奏：「中政院越中書擅奏除授，移文來征制敕，已如所請授之，然於大體非宜，乞申命禁止，庶使政權歸一。」
entries.en: On wuzi day Yan Timur and others memorialized: "The Central Domestic Affairs Court, overstepping the central secretariat, has on its own authority memorialized appointments and removals, and sent documents demanding commission edicts; appointments have already been made as requested, yet this is not proper in the larger scheme of affairs; we request that orders be issued forbidding this, so that governmental authority may be unified."
entries.literal: On wuzi day Yan Timur and others memorialized: "The Central Domestic Affairs Court, overstepping the central secretariat, has on its own authority memorialized appointments and removals, and sent documents demanding commission edicts; appointments have already been made as requested, yet this is not proper in the larger scheme of affairs; we request that orders be issued forbidding this, so that governmental authority may be unified."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: Approval was granted.
entries.literal: Approval was granted.

entries.zh: 庚寅，次撒里之地。
entries.en: On gengyin day the court halted at Sali.
entries.literal: On gengyin day the court halted at Sali.

entries.zh: 陜西行省告饑，遣使還都，與諸老臣議賑救之。
entries.en: The Shaanxi Branch Secretariat reported famine; envoys were sent back to the capital to consult with the senior ministers on relief.
entries.literal: The Shaanxi Branch Secretariat reported famine; envoys were sent back to the capital to consult with the senior ministers on relief.

entries.zh: 丁酉，次兀納八之地。
entries.en: On dingyou day the court halted at Wuna'ba.
entries.literal: On dingyou day the court halted at Wuna'ba.

entries.zh: 升都督府為大都督府。
entries.en: The Commissionerate was promoted to Grand Commissionerate.
entries.literal: The Commissionerate was promoted to Grand Commissionerate.

entries.zh: 己亥，次闊朵之地。
entries.en: On jihai day the court halted at Kuoduo.
entries.literal: On jihai day the court halted at Kuoduo.

entries.zh: 樞密院奏：「皇太子遣使來言，近已頒敕，四川諸省兵悉遣還營，惟雲南逆謀叵測，兵未可即罷，令臣等以聞。」
entries.en: The privy council memorialized: "The crown prince has sent envoys saying that edicts have recently been issued directing that troops of the various Sichuan provinces all be sent back to their camps; only Yunnan's rebellious designs cannot be measured, and the troops cannot immediately be disbanded; your subjects report this for the throne's information."
entries.literal: The privy council memorialized: "The crown prince has sent envoys saying that edicts have recently been issued directing that troops of the various Sichuan provinces all be sent back to their camps; only Yunnan's rebellious designs cannot be measured, and the troops cannot immediately be disbanded; your subjects report this for the throne's information."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「可仍屯戍，俟平定而後罷。」
entries.en: The Emperor said: "They may continue garrison duty; disband them only after pacification is complete."
entries.literal: The Emperor said: "They may continue garrison duty; disband them only after pacification is complete."

entries.zh: 辛丑，次撒裏怯兒之地。
entries.en: On xinchou day the court halted at Saliqier.
entries.literal: On xinchou day the court halted at Saliqier.

entries.zh: 壬寅，戒近侍毋得輒有奏請。
entries.en: On renyin day attendants were admonished not to memorialize on their own authority.
entries.literal: On renyin day attendants were admonished not to memorialize on their own authority.

entries.zh: 甲辰，賜駙馬脫必兒鈔千錠，往雲南。
entries.en: On jiachen day imperial son-in-law Tobu'er was granted 1,000 ingots of notes and sent to Yunnan.
entries.literal: On jiachen day imperial son-in-law Tobu'er was granted one thousand ingots of notes and sent to Yunnan.

entries.zh: 丁未，次哈里溫。
entries.en: On dingwei day the court halted at Haliwen.
entries.literal: On dingwei day the court halted at Haliwen.

entries.zh: 戊申，次闊朵傑阿剌倫。
entries.en: On wushen day the court halted at Kuoduo Jie Alun.
entries.literal: On wushen day the court halted at Kuoduo Jie Alun.

entries.zh: 辛亥，次哈兒哈納禿之地。
entries.en: On xinhai day the court halted at Harqanatu.
entries.literal: On xinhai day the court halted at Harqanatu.

entries.zh: 詔諭中書省臣：「凡國家錢谷、銓選諸大政事，先啟皇太子，然後以聞。」
entries.en: An edict instructed the central secretariat officials: "For all major state affairs concerning revenue and grain and appointments and removals, first inform the crown prince, and then report to Us."
entries.literal: An edict instructed the central secretariat officials: "For all major state affairs concerning revenue and grain and appointments and removals, first inform the crown prince, and then report to Us."

entries.zh: 癸丑，次忽禿之地。
entries.en: On guichou day the court halted at Huttu.
entries.literal: On guichou day the court halted at Huttu.

entries.zh: 甲寅，賑陜西臨潼、華陰二十三驛鈔一千八百錠，晉寧路十五驛鈔八百錠。
entries.en: On jiayin day 1,800 ingots of notes were granted in relief to 23 relay stations of Lintong and Huayin in Shaanxi, and 800 ingots of notes to 15 relay stations of Jinning Route.
entries.literal: On jiayin day one thousand eight hundred ingots of notes were granted in relief to twenty-three relay stations of Lintong and Huayin in Shaanxi, and eight hundred ingots of notes to fifteen relay stations of Jinning Route.

entries.zh: 是月，鐵木兒補化以久旱啟於皇太子，辭相位，乞更選賢德，委以燮理，皇太子遣使以聞。
entries.en: That month Temur Buqa, on account of prolonged drought, reported to the crown prince, resigned his chancellorship, and requested that another worthy be selected and entrusted with harmonizing governance; the crown prince sent envoys to report this.
entries.literal: That month Temur Buqa, on account of prolonged drought, reported to the crown prince, resigned his chancellorship, and requested that another worthy be selected and entrusted with harmonizing governance; the crown prince sent envoys to report this.

entries.zh: 帝諭闊兒吉思等曰：「修德應天，乃君臣當為之事，鐵木兒補化所言良是。
entries.en: The Emperor instructed Kuorugusi and others: "Cultivating virtue to respond to Heaven is what ruler and ministers ought to do; what Temur Buqa said is indeed right.
entries.literal: The Emperor instructed Kuorugusi and others: "Cultivating virtue to respond to Heaven is what ruler and ministers ought to do; what Temur Buqa said is indeed right.

entries.zh: 天明可畏，朕未嘗斯須忘於懷也。
entries.en: Heaven's clarity is to be feared; We have never for an instant forgotten this in Our heart.
entries.literal: Heaven's clarity is to be feared; We have never for an instant forgotten this in Our heart.

entries.zh: 皇太子來會，當與共圖其可以澤民利物者行之。
entries.en: When the crown prince comes to meet Us, We should together plan what can benefit the people and bring them material good, and put it into practice.
entries.literal: When the crown prince comes to meet Us, We should together plan what can benefit the people and bring them material good, and put it into practice.

entries.zh: 卿等其以朕意諭群臣。」
entries.en: You should convey Our meaning to the hundred officials."
entries.literal: You should convey Our meaning to the hundred officials."

entries.zh: 七月丙辰朔，日有食之。
entries.en: Seventh month, on bingchen new moon, there was a solar eclipse.
entries.literal: Seventh month, on bingchen new moon, there was a solar eclipse.

entries.zh: 甲子，次孛羅火你之地。
entries.en: On jiazi day the court halted at Boluo Huoni.
entries.literal: On jiazi day the court halted at Boluo Huoni.

entries.zh: 壬申，監察御史把的於思言：「朝廷自去秋命將出師，戡定禍亂，其供給軍需，賞賚將士，所費不可勝紀。
entries.en: On renshen day surveillance censor Badi Yusi memorialized: "Since last autumn the court has ordered generals to take the field and suppress calamitous disorder; supplies for the armies, rewards for officers and soldiers, and expenditures cannot be reckoned.
entries.literal: On renshen day surveillance censor Badi Yusi memorialized: "Since last autumn the court has ordered generals to take the field and suppress calamitous disorder; supplies for the armies, rewards for officers and soldiers, and expenditures cannot be reckoned.

entries.zh: 若以歲入經賦較之，則其所出已過數倍。
entries.en: If compared with annual revenue from regular taxes, what has been spent already exceeds it several times over.
entries.literal: If compared with annual revenue from regular taxes, what has been spent already exceeds it several times over.

entries.zh: 況今諸王朝會，舊制一切供億，俱尚未給，而陜西等處饑饉薦臻，餓殍枕籍，加以冬春之交，雪雨愆期，麥苗槁死，秋田未種，民庶遑遑，流移者眾。
entries.en: Moreover, the princes' assemblies according to former custom have not yet been fully supplied in any respect; Shaanxi and other places have been repeatedly stricken by famine; the starved lie pillow to pillow; and with the turn from winter to spring, snow and rain have missed their season, wheat seedlings have withered and died, and autumn fields remain unplanted; the people are anxious, and those drifting away in migration are many.
entries.literal: Moreover, the princes' assemblies according to former custom have not yet been fully supplied in any respect; Shaanxi and other places have been repeatedly stricken by famine; the starved lie pillow to pillow; and with the turn from winter to spring, snow and rain have missed their season, wheat seedlings have withered and died, and autumn fields remain unplanted; the people are anxious, and those drifting away in migration are many.

entries.zh: 臣伏思之，此正國家節用之時也。
entries.en: Your subject reflects that this is precisely the time for the state to economize.
entries.literal: Your subject reflects that this is precisely the time for the state to economize.

entries.zh: 如果有功必當賞賚者，宜視其官之崇卑而輕重之，不惟省費，亦可示勸。
entries.en: If there are those who must be rewarded for merit, their offices' high or low standing should be weighed in granting lighter or heavier rewards; not only would expenses be saved, encouragement could also be shown.
entries.literal: If there are those who must be rewarded for merit, their offices' high or low standing should be weighed in granting lighter or heavier rewards; not only would expenses be saved, encouragement could also be shown.

entries.zh: 其近侍諸臣奏請恩賜，宜悉停罷，以紓民力。」
entries.en: The attendant ministers' memorial requests for gracious grants should all be halted, to ease the people's strength."
entries.literal: The attendant ministers' memorial requests for gracious grants should all be halted, to ease the people's strength."

entries.zh: 臺臣以聞，帝嘉納之，仍敕中書省以其所言示百司。
entries.en: The censorate reported this; the Emperor praised and accepted it, and still ordered the central secretariat to show what was said to the hundred offices.
entries.literal: The censorate reported this; the Emperor praised and accepted it, and still ordered the central secretariat to show what was said to the hundred offices.

entries.zh: 乙亥，次不羅察罕之地。
entries.en: On yihai day the court halted at Buluo Chahan.
entries.literal: On yihai day the court halted at Buluo Chahan.

entries.zh: 丙子，文宗受皇太子寶。
entries.en: On bingzi day Wenzong received the crown prince's seal.
entries.literal: On bingzi day Wenzong received the crown prince's seal.

entries.zh: 戊寅，次小只之地。
entries.en: On wuyin day the court halted at Xiaozhi.
entries.literal: On wuyin day the court halted at Xiaozhi.

entries.zh: 壬午，遣使詣京師，敕中書平章政事哈八兒禿同翰林國史院官致祭太祖、太宗、睿宗三朝御容。
entries.en: On renwu day envoys were dispatched to the capital, directing central secretariat grand councillor Qabarqu together with Hanlin National History Academy officials to perform sacrifice to the imperial portraits of the three reigns of Taizu, Taizong, and Ruizong.
entries.literal: On renwu day envoys were dispatched to the capital, directing central secretariat associate administrator Qabildar together with Hanlin National History Academy officials to perform sacrifice to the imperial portraits of the three reigns of Taizu, Taizong, and Ruizong.

entries.zh: 發諸衛軍六千完京城。
entries.en: 6,000 troops from the various guards were dispatched to complete the capital's defenses.
entries.literal: Six thousand troops from the various guards were dispatched to complete the capital's defenses.

entries.zh: 八月乙酉朔，次王忽察都之地。
entries.en: Eighth month, on yiyou new moon, the court halted at Wanghuchadu.
entries.literal: Eighth month, on yiyou new moon, the court halted at Wanghuchadu.

entries.zh: 丙戌，皇太子入見。
entries.en: On bingxu day the crown prince entered to have audience.
entries.literal: On bingxu day the crown prince entered to have audience.

entries.zh: 是日，宴皇太子及諸王、大臣於行殿。
entries.en: That day the crown prince and the princes and great ministers were feasted at the travel palace.
entries.literal: That day the crown prince and the princes and great ministers were feasted at the travel palace.

entries.zh: 庚寅，帝暴崩，年三十，葬起輦谷，從諸陵。
entries.en: On gengyin day the Emperor died suddenly; he was 30 years old and was buried at Qilian Valley, following the imperial tombs.
entries.literal: On gengyin day the Emperor died suddenly; he was thirty years old and was buried at Qilian Valley, following the imperial tombs.

entries.zh: 是月己亥，皇太子復即皇帝位。
entries.en: That month, on jihai day, the crown prince again assumed the imperial throne.
entries.literal: That month, on jihai day, the crown prince again assumed the imperial throne.

entries.zh: 十二月乙巳，知樞密院事臣也不倫等議請上尊謚曰翼獻景孝皇帝，廟號明宗。
entries.en: Twelfth month, on yisi day, privy council administrator Yebulun and others deliberated and requested the posthumous title Emperor Yixian Jingxiao and the temple name Mingzong.
entries.literal: Twelfth month, on yisi day, privy council administrator Yebulun and others deliberated and requested the posthumous title Emperor Yixian Jingxiao and the temple name Mingzong.

entries.zh: 三年三月壬申，祔於太廟。
entries.en: Third year, third month, on renshen day, he was enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
entries.literal: Third year, third month, on renshen day, he was enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

entries.zh: 明宗翼獻景孝皇帝，諱和世㻋，武宗長子也。
entries.en: Emperor Mingzong, posthumous name Yixian Jingxiao, taboo name Khoshila, was Wuzong's eldest son.
entries.literal: Emperor Mingzong, posthumous name Yixian Jingxiao, taboo name Khoshila, was Wuzong's eldest son.

entries.zh: 母曰仁獻章聖皇后，亦乞烈氏。
entries.en: His mother was Empress Renxian Zhangsheng of the Yiqilie clan.
entries.literal: His mother was Empress Renxian Zhangsheng of the Yiqilie clan.

entries.zh: 成宗大德三年，命武宗撫軍北邊，帝以四年十一月壬子生。
entries.en: In the third year of Dade under Chengzong, Wuzong was ordered to command troops on the northern frontier; he was born on renzi day in the eleventh month of the fourth year.
entries.literal: In the third year of Dade under Chengzong, Wuzong was ordered to command troops on the northern frontier; he was born on renzi day in the eleventh month of the fourth year.

entries.zh: 成宗崩，十一年，武宗入繼大統，立仁宗為皇太子，命以次傳於帝。
entries.en: Chengzong died; in the eleventh year, Wuzong entered to succeed to the Great Foundation, installed Renzong as crown prince, and ordered that succession pass to him in order.
entries.literal: Chengzong died; in the eleventh year, Wuzong entered to succeed to the Great Foundation, installed Renzong as crown prince, and ordered that succession pass to him in order.

entries.zh: 武宗崩，仁宗立，延祐三年春，議建東宮，時丞相鐵木叠而欲固位取寵，乃議立英宗為皇太子，又與太后幸臣識烈門譖帝於兩宮，浸潤久之，其計遂行。
entries.en: Wuzong died; Renzong ascended the throne; spring of the third year of Yanyou, when the Eastern Palace was under deliberation, Chancellor Tiemudie'er, wishing to secure his position and win favor, proposed installing Shidebala as crown prince; together with the empress dowager's favorite minister Shiliemen he slandered him before the two palaces; after long insinuation, the scheme succeeded.
entries.literal: Wuzong died; Renzong ascended the throne; spring of the third year of YanYou, when the Eastern Palace was under deliberation, Chancellor Tiemudie'er, wishing to secure his position and win favor, proposed installing Shidebala as crown prince; together with the empress dowager's favorite minister Shiliemen he slandered him before the two palaces; after long insinuation, the scheme succeeded.

entries.zh: 於是封帝為周王，出鎮雲南。
entries.en: Thereupon he was enfeoffed Prince of Zhou and sent out to garrison Yunnan.
entries.literal: Thereupon he was enfeoffed Prince of Zhou and sent out to garrison Yunnan.

entries.zh: 置常侍府官屬，以遙授中書左丞相禿忽魯、大司徒斡耳朵、中政使尚家奴、山北遼陽等路蒙古軍萬戶孛羅、翰林侍講學士教化等並為常侍，中衛親軍都指揮使唐兀、兵部尚書賽罕八都魯為中尉，仍置諮議、記室各二員，遣就鎮。
entries.en: Attendants' Office officials were appointed; Tughluq, remotely invested as central secretariat left grand councillor, Orda the grand minister of husbandry, Central Domestic Affairs Court commissioner Shangjianu, commander of ten-thousands of Mongol troops of Shanbei Liaoyang and other routes Boluo, Hanlin expositor academician Jiaohua, and others were all made attendants; Central Guard elite army commander Tangut and Ministry of War minister Saqan Baduqu were made chamberlains; 2 deliberators and 2 recorders were still appointed, and they were dispatched to take up the garrison.
entries.literal: Attendants' Office officials were appointed; Tughluq, remotely invested as central secretariat left grand councillor, Orda the grand minister of husbandry, Central Domestic Affairs Court commissioner Shangjianu, commander of ten-thousands of Mongol troops of Shanbei Liaoyang and other routes Boluo, Hanlin expositor academician Jiaohua, and others were all made attendants; Central Guard elite army commander Tangut and Ministry of War minister Saqan Baduqu were made chamberlains; two deliberators and two recorders were still appointed, and they were dispatched to take up the garrison.

entries.zh: 是年冬十一月，帝次延安，禿忽魯、尚家奴、孛羅及武宗舊臣釐日、沙不丁、哈八兒禿等皆來會。
entries.en: That year, eleventh month of winter, he halted at Yan'an; Tughluq, Shangjianu, Boluo, and Wuzong's old ministers Chiri, Shabuding, Qabarqu, and others all came to meet.
entries.literal: That year, eleventh month of winter, he halted at Yan'an; Tughluq, Shangjianu, Boluo, and Wuzong's old ministers Chiri, Shabuding, Qabarqu, and others all came to meet.

entries.zh: 教化謀曰：「天下者，我武皇之天下也，出鎮之事，本非上意，由左右構間致然。
entries.en: Jiaohua plotted, saying, "The realm is our Martial Emperor's realm; the matter of being sent out to garrison was originally not the Supreme One's intent — it came about because those at the ruler's side sowed discord.
entries.literal: Jiaohua plotted, saying, "The realm is our Martial Emperor's realm; the matter of being sent out to garrison was originally not the Supreme One's intent — it came about because those at the ruler's side sowed discord.

entries.zh: 請以其故白行省，俾聞之朝廷，庶可杜塞離間，不然，事變叵測。」
