entries.en: Please report the reason to the branch secretariat, so that it may be brought to the court's attention — then perhaps the sowing of discord can be blocked; otherwise, unforeseen changes may arise."
entries.literal: Please report the reason to the branch secretariat, so that it may be brought to the court's attention — then perhaps the sowing of discord can be blocked; otherwise, unforeseen changes may arise."

entries.zh: 遂與數騎馳去。
entries.en: Thereupon with several horsemen he galloped away.
entries.literal: Thereupon with several horsemen he galloped away.

entries.zh: 先是，阿思罕為太師，鐵木叠兒奪其位，出之為陜西行省丞相，及教化等至，即與平章政事塔察兒、行臺御史大夫脫裏伯、中丞脫歡，悉發關中兵，分道自潼關、河中府入。
entries.en: Earlier, Ashan had been grand preceptor; Tiemudie'er seized his post and sent him out as Shaanxi branch secretariat grand councillor; when Jiaohua and the others arrived, he immediately joined branch secretariat grand councillor Taqachar, branch surveillance censor-in-chief Tulibai, and surveillance vice censor Tughon in fully mobilizing the Guanzhong armies, advancing in separate columns through Tong Pass and Hezhong Prefecture.
entries.literal: Earlier, Ashan had been grand preceptor; Tiemudie'er seized his post and sent him out as Shaanxi branch secretariat grand councillor; when Jiaohua and the others arrived, he immediately joined branch secretariat grand councillor Taqachar, branch surveillance censor-in-chief Tulibai, and surveillance vice censor Tughon in fully mobilizing the Guanzhong armies, advancing in separate columns through Tong Pass and Hezhong Prefecture.

entries.zh: 已而塔察兒、脫歡襲殺阿思罕、教化於河中，帝遂西行，至北邊金山。
entries.en: Before long Taqachar and Tughon launched a surprise attack and killed Ashan and Jiaohua at Hezhong; he then went west and reached the Golden Mountain on the northern frontier.
entries.literal: Before long Taqachar and Tughon launched a surprise attack and killed Ashan and Jiaohua at Hezhong; he then went west and reached the Golden Mountain on the northern frontier.

entries.zh: 西北諸王察阿臺等聞帝至，咸率眾來附。
entries.en: Northwestern princes including Cha'atai, hearing he had arrived, all led their followings to submit.
entries.literal: Northwestern princes including Cha'atai, hearing he had arrived, all led their followings to submit.

entries.zh: 帝至其部，與定約束，每歲冬居紥顏，夏居斡羅斡察山，春則命從者耕於野泥，十餘年間，邊境寧謐。
entries.en: When he reached their territory, he fixed regulations with them: each year they wintered at Jaya'an, summered at Olokoch'a Mountain, and in spring ordered their followers to farm at Yeni; for more than 10 years the frontier was tranquil.
entries.literal: When he reached their territory, he fixed regulations with them: each year they wintered at Jaya'an, summered at Olokoch'a Mountain, and in spring ordered their followers to farm at Yeni; for more than ten years the frontier was tranquil.

entries.zh: 洪惟太祖皇帝，啟辟疆宇；
entries.en: Grandly considering the Taizu Emperor, who opened and extended the realm;
entries.literal: Grandly considering the Taizu Emperor, who opened and extended the realm;

entries.zh: 世祖皇帝，統一萬方；
entries.en: the Shizu Emperor, who unified the myriad regions;
entries.literal: the Shizu Emperor, who unified the myriad regions;

entries.zh: 列聖相承，法度明著。
entries.en: the successive sagely emperors who inherited one another, with laws and standards clearly established.
entries.literal: the successive sagely emperors who inherited one another, with laws and standards clearly established.

entries.zh: 我曲律皇帝入纂大統，修舉庶政，動合成法，授大寶位於普顏篤皇帝以及格堅皇帝。
entries.en: Our Emperor Qutuqtu entered to succeed to the Great Foundation, repaired and raised all government affairs, and in action conformed to law; he bestowed the Great Treasure upon Emperors Buyan Toq and Gegegen.
entries.literal: Our Emperor Qutuqtu entered to succeed to the Great Foundation, repaired and raised all government affairs, and in action conformed to law; he bestowed the Great Treasure upon Emperors Buyan Toq and Gegegen.

entries.zh: 歷數之歸，實當在我忽都篤皇帝、紥牙篤皇帝，而各播越遼遠。
entries.en: The mandate of Heaven's return truly rested with Us upon Emperors Qoshila and Jaya'adu, yet each was cast far and wandered in distant lands.
entries.literal: The mandate of Heaven's return truly rested with Us upon Emperors Qoshila and Jaya'adu, yet each was cast far and wandered in distant lands.

entries.zh: 時則有若燕鐵木兒，建義效忠，戢平內難，以定邦國，協恭推戴紥牙篤皇帝。
entries.en: At that time there was one such as Yan Temür, who raised righteous loyalty and served with devotion, quelled and pacified inner turmoil, settled the state, and with united reverence supported and installed Emperor Jaya'adu.
entries.literal: At that time there was one such as Yan Temür, who raised righteous loyalty and served with devotion, quelled and pacified inner turmoil, settled the state, and with united reverence supported and installed Emperor Jaya'adu.

entries.zh: 登極之始，即以讓兄之詔明告天下。
entries.en: At the beginning of his accession he forthwith made clear to all under Heaven the edict yielding to his elder brother.
entries.literal: At the beginning of his accession he forthwith made clear to all under Heaven the edict yielding to his elder brother.

entries.zh: 隨奉璽紱，遠迓忽都篤皇帝，朔方言還，奄棄臣庶。
entries.en: Then bearing the seal and cord he went far to welcome Emperor Qoshila; when word came from the northern frontier that he was returning, he suddenly abandoned his subjects.
entries.literal: Then bearing the seal and cord he went far to welcome Emperor Qoshila; when word came from the northern frontier that he was returning, he suddenly abandoned his subjects.

entries.zh: 紥牙篤皇帝，薦正宸極，仁義之至，視民如傷，恩澤旁被，無間遠邇。
entries.en: Emperor Jaya'adu ascended and rectified the imperial throne; his benevolence and righteousness reached the utmost — viewing the people as wounded, his grace spread on every side, without distinction between far and near.
entries.literal: Emperor Jaya'adu ascended and rectified the imperial throne; his benevolence and righteousness reached the utmost — viewing the people as wounded, his grace spread on every side, without distinction between far and near.

entries.zh: 顧育眇躬，尤篤慈愛。
entries.en: In nurturing Our young person he was especially deep in compassionate love.
entries.literal: In nurturing Our young person he was especially deep in compassionate love.

entries.zh: 賓天之日，皇后傳顧命於太師、太平王、右丞相、答剌罕燕帖木兒，太保、浚寧王、知樞密院事伯顏等，謂聖體彌留，益推固讓之初誌，以宗社之重，屬諸大兄忽都篤皇帝之世嫡。
entries.en: On the day he ascended to Heaven, the empress transmitted the final command to Grand Preceptor, Prince of Taiping, right chancellor, and dalaqan Yan Temür, Grand Guardian, Prince of Jünning, and privy council administrator Bayan, and others, saying the sacred person was critically lingering and should further advance the original intent of firm yielding; for the weight of altars and state, the charge was placed upon the legitimate heir in the line of the Great Elder Brother Emperor Qoshila.
entries.literal: On the day he ascended to Heaven, the empress transmitted the final command to Grand Preceptor, Prince of Taiping, right chancellor, and dalaqan Yan Temür, Grand Guardian, Prince of Jünning, and privy council administrator Bayan, and others, saying the sacred person was critically lingering and should further advance the original intent of firm yielding; for the weight of altars and state, the charge was placed upon the legitimate heir in the line of the Great Elder Brother Emperor Qoshila.

entries.zh: 乃遣使召諸王宗親，以十月一日來會於大都，與宗王、大臣同奉遺詔。
entries.en: Envoys were then dispatched to summon the princes and imperial kin to assemble at Dadu on the 1st day of the 10th month, jointly to follow the testamentary edict together with the princes and great ministers.
entries.literal: Envoys were then dispatched to summon the princes and imperial kin to assemble at Dadu on the first day of the tenth month, jointly to follow the testamentary edict together with the princes and great ministers.

entries.zh: 揆諸成憲，宜禦神器，以至順三年十月初四日，即皇帝位於大明殿，可大赦天下。
entries.en: Measured against the established statutes, he ought to undertake the sacred regalia; on the 4th day of the 10th month of the third year of Zhishun, he ascended the imperial throne in Daming Hall — a general amnesty throughout the realm may be proclaimed.
entries.literal: Measured against the established statutes, he ought to undertake the sacred regalia; on the fourth day of the tenth month of the third year of Zhishun, he ascended the imperial throne in Daming Hall — a general amnesty throughout the realm may be proclaimed.

entries.zh: 自至順三年十月初四日昧爽以前，除謀反大逆、謀殺祖父母父母、妻妾殺夫、奴婢殺主、謀故殺人、但犯強盜、印造偽鈔、蠱毒魘魅犯上者不赦外，其餘一切罪犯，咸赦除之。
entries.en: From before dawn on the 4th day of the 10th month of the third year of Zhishun, except for plotting rebellion or great treason, plotting to kill grandparents or parents, wives or concubines killing husbands, slaves or bondmaids killing masters, plotting deliberate murder, those who committed robbery, forging false notes, or sorcery and malign enchantment offending superiors — all not pardoned — all other crimes whatsoever are pardoned and remitted.
entries.literal: From before dawn on the fourth day of the tenth month of the third year of Zhishun, except for plotting rebellion or great treason, plotting to kill grandparents or parents, wives or concubines killing husbands, slaves or bondmaids killing masters, plotting deliberate murder, those who committed robbery, forging false notes, or sorcery and malign enchantment offending superiors — all not pardoned — all other crimes whatsoever are pardoned and remitted.

entries.zh: 大都、上都、興和三路，差稅免三年。
entries.en: In Dadu, Shangdu, and Xinghe the 3 routes, corvée tax is remitted for 3 years.
entries.literal: In Dadu, Shangdu, and Xinghe the three routes, corvée tax is remitted for three years.

entries.zh: 腹裏差發並其餘諸郡不納差發去處，稅糧十分為率，免二分。
entries.en: Within the metropolitan region, corvée levies and all other commanderies that do not submit corvée levies — grain tax at the rate of 10 parts, 2 parts remitted.
entries.literal: Within the metropolitan region, corvée levies and all other commanderies that do not submit corvée levies — grain tax at the rate of ten parts, two parts remitted.

entries.zh: 江淮以南，夏稅亦免二分。
entries.en: South of the Yangzi and Huai, summer tax also has 2 parts remitted.
entries.literal: South of the Yangzi and Huai, summer tax also has two parts remitted.

entries.zh: 土木工役，除倉庫必合修理外，毋復創造，以紓民力。
entries.en: Civil engineering labor — except warehouses that must be repaired, no further new construction, to ease the people's strength.
entries.literal: Civil engineering labor — except warehouses that must be repaired, no further new construction, to ease the people's strength.

entries.zh: 民間在前應有逋欠差稅課程，盡行蠲免。
entries.en: Among the people, all past overdue corvée taxes and levies are entirely remitted.
entries.literal: Among the people, all past overdue corvée taxes and levies are entirely remitted.

entries.zh: 監察御史、肅政廉訪司官並內外三品以上正官，歲舉才堪守令者一人，申達省部，先行錄用。
entries.en: Surveillance censors, integrity and investigation officials, and regular officials of the 3rd rank and above within and without — each year recommend 1 person fit to serve as prefect or magistrate, report upward to the provincial departments, and employ first on record.
entries.literal: Surveillance censors, integrity and investigation officials, and regular officials of the third rank and above within and without — each year recommend one person fit to serve as prefect or magistrate, report upward to the provincial departments, and employ first on record.

entries.zh: 如果稱職，舉官優加旌擢。
entries.en: If they prove competent in office, the recommending official is specially rewarded and promoted.
entries.literal: If they prove competent in office, the recommending official is specially rewarded and promoted.

entries.zh: 一任之內，或犯贓私者，量其輕重黜罰。
entries.en: Within 1 term of office, if they commit corruption for private gain, according to the severity they are dismissed and punished.
entries.literal: Within one term of office, if they commit corruption for private gain, according to the severity they are dismissed and punished.

entries.zh: 其不該原免重囚，淹禁三年以上、疑不能決者，申達省部，詳讞釋放。
entries.en: Those serious criminals who ought not be pardoned, detained 3 years or more with doubts preventing decision — report upward to the provincial departments for detailed review and release.
entries.literal: Those serious criminals who ought not be pardoned, detained three years or more with doubts preventing decision — report upward to the provincial departments for detailed review and release.

entries.zh: 學校農桑、孝義貞節、科舉取士、國學貢試，並依舊制。
entries.en: Schools and agriculture, filial conduct and chaste integrity, examination recruitment of scholars, and National University tribute examinations — all follow the old statutes.
entries.literal: Schools and agriculture, filial conduct and chaste integrity, examination recruitment of scholars, and National University tribute examinations — all follow the old statutes.

entries.zh: 廣海、雲南梗化之民，詔書到日，限六十日內出官，與免本罪，許以自新。
entries.en: Among the recalcitrant peoples of Guanghai and Yunnan, from the day the edict arrives they are limited to 60 days to surrender to officials; their original crimes are remitted and self-renewal is permitted.
entries.literal: Among the recalcitrant peoples of Guanghai and Yunnan, from the day the edict arrives they are limited to sixty days to surrender to officials; their original crimes are remitted and self-renewal is permitted.

entries.zh: 於戲！
entries.en: Alas!
entries.literal: Alas!

entries.zh: 肆予沖人，托於天下臣民之上，任大守重，若涉淵冰。
entries.en: Now I, a young person, am set upon all under Heaven's subjects; the charge is great and the guardianship heavy — like treading upon deep ice.
entries.literal: Now I, a young person, am set upon all under Heaven's subjects; the charge is great and the guardianship heavy — like treading upon deep ice.

entries.zh: 尚賴宗王大臣、百司庶府，交修乃職，思盡厥忠。
entries.en: I still rely upon the imperial princes, great ministers, and the hundred offices and many agencies jointly to repair their duties and think to exhaust their loyalty.
entries.literal: I still rely upon the imperial princes, great ministers, and the hundred offices and many agencies jointly to repair their duties and think to exhaust their loyalty.

entries.zh: 嘉與億兆之民，共保承平之治。
entries.en: May We together with the hundred millions of the people jointly preserve the governance of enduring peace.
entries.literal: May We together with the hundred millions of the people jointly preserve the governance of enduring peace.

entries.zh: 咨爾多方，體予至意！
entries.en: I announce to you of the many regions — embody My utmost intent!
entries.literal: I announce to you of the many regions — embody My utmost intent!

entries.zh: 故茲詔示，想知悉。
entries.en: Therefore this edict is proclaimed — let it be known.
entries.literal: Therefore this edict is proclaimed — let it be known.

entries.zh: 十月庚子，帝即位於大明殿，大赦天下，詔曰：
entries.en: Tenth month, on gengzi day, the Emperor ascended the throne in Daming Hall, proclaimed a general amnesty throughout the realm, and the edict said:
entries.literal: Tenth month, on gengzi day, the Emperor ascended the throne in Daming Hall, proclaimed a general amnesty throughout the realm, and the edict said:

entries.zh: 寧宗沖聖嗣孝皇帝，諱懿璘質班，明宗第二子也。
entries.en: Emperor Ningzong Chong Sheng Si Xiao, taboo name Yilianzhen Shiraban, was Mingzong's second son.
entries.literal: Emperor Ningzong Chong Sheng Si Xiao, taboo name Yilianzhen Shiraban, was Mingzong's second son.

entries.zh: 母曰八不沙皇后，乃蠻真氏。
entries.en: His mother was Empress Babusha of the Naiman Zhen clan.
entries.literal: His mother was Empress Babusha of the Naiman Zhen clan.

entries.zh: 初，武宗有子二人，長明宗，次文宗。
entries.en: Earlier, Wuzong had two sons — the elder Mingzong, the younger Wenzong.
entries.literal: Earlier, Wuzong had two sons — the elder Mingzong, the younger Wenzong.

entries.zh: 延祐中，明宗封周王，出居朔漠。
entries.en: During Yanyou, Mingzong was enfeoffed Prince of Zhou and went out to dwell in the northern desert.
entries.literal: During Yanyou, Mingzong was enfeoffed Prince of Zhou and went out to dwell in the northern desert.

entries.zh: 泰定之際，正統遂偏。
entries.en: At the time of Taiding, orthodox succession was thereby skewed.
entries.literal: At the time of Taiding, orthodox succession was thereby skewed.

entries.zh: 天歷元年，文宗入紹大統，內難既平，即遣使奉皇帝璽綬，北迎明宗。
entries.en: First year of Tianli, Wenzong entered to continue the Great Foundation; once the inner turmoil was pacified, he immediately dispatched envoys bearing the imperial seal and cord to welcome Mingzong from the north.
entries.literal: First year of Tianli, Wenzong entered to continue the Great Foundation; once the inner turmoil was pacified, he immediately dispatched envoys bearing the imperial seal and cord to welcome Mingzong from the north.

entries.zh: 明宗崩，文宗復即皇帝位。
entries.en: Mingzong died; Wenzong again ascended the imperial throne.
entries.literal: Mingzong died; Wenzong again ascended the imperial throne.

entries.zh: 明宗有子二人，長妥歡帖木耳，次即帝也。
entries.en: Mingzong had two sons — the elder Toghan Temür, the younger being the Emperor.
entries.literal: Mingzong had two sons — the elder Toghan Temür, the younger being the Emperor.

entries.zh: 天歷三年二月乙巳，封帝為鄜王。
entries.en: Third year of Tianli, second month, on yisi day, the Emperor was enfeoffed Prince of Fu.
entries.literal: Third year of Tianli, second month, on yisi day, the Emperor was enfeoffed Prince of Fu.

entries.zh: 冬十月丁酉，享於太廟。
entries.en: In winter, on the dingyou day of the tenth month, offerings were presented at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
entries.literal: Winter, tenth month, on dingyou day, offerings were presented at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

entries.zh: 庚子，太白經天。
entries.en: On the gengzi day, Venus crossed the sky.
entries.literal: On gengzi day, Venus crossed the sky.

entries.zh: 癸卯，以江浙行省參知政事買住丁升本省右丞，提調明年海運。
entries.en: On the guimao day, Maizhuding, vice chief minister of the Jiangzhe branch secretariat, was promoted to right vice director of that province and ordered to supervise the following year's sea transport.
entries.literal: On guimao day, Maizhuding, vice chief minister of the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat, was promoted to right vice director of that province and ordered to supervise next year's sea transport.

entries.zh: 甲辰，歲星犯氐宿。
entries.en: On the jiachen day, Jupiter transgressed the Di mansion.
entries.literal: On jiachen day, Jupiter transgressed the Di mansion.

entries.zh: 丁未，廣西元帥甄崇福復道州，誅賊將周伯顏。
entries.en: On the dingwei day, Zhen Chongfu, marshal of Guangxi, recovered Daozhou and executed the bandit general Zhou Boyan.
entries.literal: On dingwei day, Zhen Chongfu, marshal of Guangxi, recovered Daozhou and executed the bandit general Zhou Boyan.

entries.zh: 庚戌，從帖裏帖木兒、左答納失裏之請，授方國珍徽州路治中，國璋廣德路治中，國瑛信州路治中，督遣之任，國珍疑懼，不受命。
entries.en: On the gengxu day, at the request of Tie'er Temür and Zuo Danashiri, Fang Guozhen was appointed administrative vice-director of Huizhou Circuit, Guozhang of Guangde Circuit, and Guoying of Xinzhou Circuit, and they were urged to take up their posts; Fang Guozhen, suspicious and afraid, did not accept the appointments.
entries.literal: On gengxu day, at the request of Tie'er Temür and Zuo Danashiri, Fang Guozhen was appointed administrative vice-director of Huizhou Circuit, Guozhang of Guangde Circuit, and Guoying of Xinzhou Circuit, and they were urged to take up their posts; Fang Guozhen was suspicious and afraid and did not accept the appointments.

entries.zh: 立水軍都萬戶府於昆山州，以浙東宣慰使納麟哈剌為正萬戶，宣慰使董摶霄為副萬戶。
entries.en: A Naval Commandery of Ten Thousand Households was established at Kunshan Prefecture; Nalin Hala, pacification commissioner of eastern Zhe, was appointed chief commander of ten thousand, and Dong Tuanxiao, pacification commissioner, was appointed deputy commander of ten thousand.
entries.literal: A Naval Commandery of Ten Thousand Households was established at Kunshan Prefecture; Nalin Hala, pacification commissioner of eastern Zhe, was made chief commander of ten thousand; Dong Tuanxiao, pacification commissioner, was made deputy commander of ten thousand.

entries.zh: 庚申，賜皇太子妃鈔十萬錠。
entries.en: On the gengshen day, the crown prince's consort was granted one hundred thousand ingots of paper currency.
entries.literal: On gengshen day, the crown prince's consort was granted 100,000 ingots of paper currency.

entries.zh: 壬戌，賜皇太子五愛馬怯薛丹二百五十人鈔各一百一十錠。
entries.en: On the renxu day, each of the crown prince's two hundred fifty beloved-horse keshig guards was granted one hundred ten ingots of paper currency.
entries.literal: On renxu day, the crown prince's two hundred fifty beloved-horse keshig guards were each granted 110 ingots of paper currency.

entries.zh: 癸亥，太白犯亢宿。
entries.en: On the guihai day, Venus transgressed the Kang mansion.
entries.literal: On guihai day, Venus transgressed the Kang mansion.

entries.zh: 是月，撤世祖所立氈殿，改建殿宇。
entries.en: That month, the felt hall established by Kublai was removed and permanent palace buildings were erected in its place.
entries.literal: That month, the felt hall established by Shizu was removed and palace buildings were rebuilt.

entries.zh: 順帝六
entries.en: Shundi 6
entries.literal: Shundi 6

entries.zh: 夏四月辛丑朔，大明兵取英德州。
entries.en: In the fourth month of summer, on the new moon of xinchou, Ming forces captured Yingde Prefecture.
entries.literal: Summer, fourth month, xinchou new moon; Ming forces took Yingde Prefecture.

entries.zh: 丙午，隕霜殺菽。
entries.en: On the bingwu day falling frost killed beans.
entries.literal: On bingwu day, falling frost killed beans.

entries.zh: 戊申，大明兵取廣州路，又取嵩、陜、汝等州。
entries.en: On the wushen day Ming forces captured Guangzhou Circuit and also took Song, Shaan, and Ru prefectures.
entries.literal: On wushen day, Ming forces took Guangzhou Circuit and also took Song, Shaan, and Ru prefectures.

entries.zh: 五月庚午朔，大明兵取道州。
entries.en: In the fifth month, on the new moon of gengwu, Ming forces captured Daozhou.
entries.literal: Fifth month, gengwu new moon; Ming forces took Daozhou.

entries.zh: 李克彜棄河南城，奔陜西，推李思齊為總兵，駐兵岐山。
entries.en: Li Keyi abandoned Henan city and fled to Shaanxi, acclaiming Li Siqi as overall commander and stationing troops at Qishan.
entries.literal: Li Keyi abandoned Henan city and fled to Shaanxi, acclaiming Li Siqi as overall commander and stationing troops at Qishan.

entries.zh: 是月，李思齊部將忽林赤、脫脫、張意據盩啡，高暠據武功，李克彜據岐山，任從政據隴州。
entries.en: That month Li Siqi's subordinates Qolin Či, Totoγan, and Zhang Yi held Zhouzhi; Gao Shao held Wugong; Li Keyi held Qishan; and Ren Congzheng held Longzhou.
entries.literal: That month, Li Siqi's subordinates Qolin Či, Totoγan, and Zhang Yi held Zhouzhi; Gao Shao held Wugong; Li Keyi held Qishan; Ren Congzheng held Longzhou.

entries.zh: 六月庚子朔，徐溝縣地震。
entries.en: In the sixth month, on the new moon of gengzi, Xugou County was shaken by earthquake.
entries.literal: Sixth month, gengzi new moon; Xugou County was shaken by earthquake.

entries.zh: 癸丑，大明兵取全州、郴州、梧州、藤州、潯州、貴、象、郁林等郡。
entries.en: On the guichou day Ming forces captured Quan, Chen, Wuzhou, Teng, Xun, Gui, Xiang, and Yulin prefectures.
entries.literal: On guichou day, Ming forces took Quan, Chen, Wuzhou, Teng, Xun, Gui, Xiang, and Yulin prefectures.

entries.zh: 甲寅，雷雨中有火自天墜，焚大聖壽萬安寺。
entries.en: On the jiayin day, amid thunder and rain, fire fell from the sky and burned the Temple of Great Sagely Longevity and Ten Thousand Peace.
entries.literal: On jiayin day, amid thunder and rain fire fell from the sky and burned the Temple of Great Sagely Longevity and Ten Thousand Peace.

entries.zh: 壬戌，臨州、保德州地震，五日不止。
entries.en: On the renxu day Linzhou and Baode Prefecture were shaken by earthquake for five days without stopping.
entries.literal: On renxu day, Linzhou and Baode Prefecture were shaken by earthquake for five days without stopping.

entries.zh: 大明兵取靜江路。
entries.en: Ming forces captured Jingjiang Circuit.
entries.literal: Ming forces took Jingjiang Circuit.

entries.zh: 是月，廣西諸郡縣皆附於大明。
entries.en: That month all prefectures and counties in Guangxi submitted to the Ming.
entries.literal: That month, all prefectures and counties in Guangxi submitted to the Ming.

entries.zh: 秋七月癸酉，京城紅氣滿空，如火照人，自旦至辰方息。
entries.en: In the seventh month of autumn, on the guiyou day, red vapor filled the capital sky, shining on people like fire from dawn until the chen hour before it ceased.
entries.literal: Autumn, seventh month, guiyou day; red vapor filled the capital sky, shining on people like fire from dawn until the chen hour before it ceased.

entries.zh: 乙亥，京城黑氣起，百步內不見人，從寅至巳方消。
entries.en: On the yihai day black vapor rose in the capital; within a hundred paces people could not be seen; it dissipated from yin to si.
entries.literal: On yihai day, black vapor rose in the capital; within a hundred paces people could not be seen; it dissipated from yin to si.

entries.zh: 貊高、關保以兵攻晉寧。
entries.en: Mo Gao and Guan Bao attacked Jinning with troops.
entries.literal: Mo Gao and Guan Bao attacked Jinning with troops.

entries.zh: 是月，李思齊會李克彜、商暠、張意、脫列伯等於鳳翔。
entries.en: That month Li Siqi joined Li Keyi, Shang Gao, Zhang Yi, Toliber, and others at Fengxiang.
entries.literal: That month, Li Siqi joined Li Keyi, Shang Gao, Zhang Yi, Toliber, and others at Fengxiang.

entries.zh: 海南、海北諸郡縣皆降於大明。
entries.en: All prefectures and counties in Hainan and Haibei submitted to the Ming.
entries.literal: All prefectures and counties in Hainan and Haibei submitted to the Ming.

entries.zh: 閏月己亥朔，擴廓帖木兒與貊高、關保戰，敗之，擒關保、貊高，遣其斷事官以聞。
entries.en: In the intercalary seventh month, on the new moon of jihai, Köke Temür fought Mo Gao and Guan Bao and defeated them, capturing Guan Bao and Mo Gao, and sent his judicial officer to report.
entries.literal: Intercalary seventh month, jihai new moon; Köke Temür fought Mo Gao and Guan Bao and defeated them, capturing Guan Bao and Mo Gao, and sent his judicial officer to report.

entries.zh: 詔：「關保、貊高，間諜構兵，可依軍法處治。」
entries.en: An edict stated: "Guan Bao and Mo Gao, as spies, raised armies in discord — they may be dealt with according to military law."
entries.literal: An edict stated: "Guan Bao and Mo Gao, as spies, raised armies in discord — they may be dealt with according to military law."

entries.zh: 關保、貊高皆被殺。
entries.en: Guan Bao and Mo Gao were both executed.
entries.literal: Guan Bao and Mo Gao were both executed.

entries.zh: 辛丑，大明兵取衛輝路。
entries.en: On the xinchou day Ming forces captured Weihui Circuit.
entries.literal: On xinchou day, Ming forces took Weihui Circuit.

entries.zh: 癸卯，大明兵取彰德路。
entries.en: On the guimao day Ming forces captured Zhangde Circuit.
entries.literal: On guimao day, Ming forces took Zhangde Circuit.

entries.zh: 乙巳，左江、右江諸路皆降於大明。
entries.en: On the yisi day the left and right Jiang circuits all submitted to the Ming.
entries.literal: On yisi day, the left and right Jiang circuits all submitted to the Ming.

entries.zh: 丁未，大明兵取廣平路。
entries.en: On the dingwei day Ming forces captured Guangping Circuit.
entries.literal: On dingwei day, Ming forces took Guangping Circuit.

entries.zh: 丁巳，詔罷大撫軍院，誅知大撫軍院事伯顏帖木兒等。
entries.en: On the dingsi day an edict abolished the Great Pacification Army Office and executed Bayan Temür and others who managed its affairs.
entries.literal: On dingsi day, an edict abolished the Great Pacification Army Office and executed Bayan Temür and others who managed its affairs.

entries.zh: 詔復命擴廓帖木兒仍前河南王、太傅、中書左丞相，統領見部軍馬，由中道直抵彰德、衛輝；
entries.en: An edict again appointed Köke Temür to his former posts as Prince of Henan, Grand Tutor, and left chief minister of the Secretariat, to take overall command of his present forces and, by the central route, advance straight to Zhangde and Weihui;
entries.literal: An edict again appointed Köke Temür to his former posts as Prince of Henan, Grand Tutor, and left chief minister of the Secretariat, to take overall command of his present forces and, by the central route, advance straight to Zhangde and Weihui;

entries.zh: 太保、中書右丞相也速統率大軍，經由東道，水陸並進；
entries.en: Grand guardian and right chief minister Yesu was to lead the great army by the eastern route, advancing by land and water together;
entries.literal: Grand Guardian and right chief minister Yesu was to lead the great army by the eastern route, advancing by land and water together;

entries.zh: 少保、陜西行省左丞相禿魯統率關陜諸軍，東出潼關，攻取河洛；
entries.en: Junior guardian and Shaanxi left chief minister Tolu was to lead the Guan and Shaanxi armies, marching east out of Tong Pass to attack and take Heluo;
entries.literal: Junior Guardian and Shaanxi left chief minister Tolu was to lead the Guan and Shaanxi armies, marching east out of Tong Pass to attack and take Heluo;

entries.zh: 太尉、平章政事李思齊統率軍馬，南出七盤、金、商，克復汴洛。
entries.en: Grand Commandant and chief minister Li Siqi was to lead his army south out of Qipan, Jin, and Shang to recover Bian and Luo.
entries.literal: Grand Commandant and chief minister Li Siqi was to lead his army south out of Qipan, Jin, and Shang to recover Bian and Luo.

entries.zh: 四道進兵，掎角剿捕，毋分彼此。
entries.en: The four routes were to advance in concert, supporting one another in pursuit and suppression, without distinguishing priority.
entries.literal: The four routes were to advance in concert, supporting one another in pursuit and suppression, without distinguishing priority.

entries.zh: 秦國公、平章、知院俺普，平章瑣住等軍，東西布列，乘機掃殄。
entries.en: State duke and chief minister Anpu, chief minister Suoju, and other armies were to be deployed east and west, seizing opportunities to sweep away the enemy.
entries.literal: State Duke and chief minister Anpu, chief minister Suoju, and other armies were to be deployed east and west, seizing opportunities to sweep away the enemy.

entries.zh: 太尉、遼陽左丞相也先不花，郡王、知院厚孫等軍，捍禦海口，藩屏畿輔。
entries.en: Grand Commandant and Liaoyang left chief minister Yexian Buhua, prince and Bureau director Husun, and other armies were to defend the sea mouth and shield the capital region.
entries.literal: Grand Commandant and Liaoyang left chief minister Yexian Buhua, prince and Bureau director Husun, and other armies were to defend the sea mouth and shield the capital region.

entries.zh: 皇太子愛猷識理達臘悉總天下兵馬，裁決庶務，具如前詔。
entries.en: The heir apparent Ayushiridara was to take overall command of all military forces under Heaven and decide all affairs, as in the former edict.
entries.literal: The heir apparent Ayushiridara was to take overall command of all military forces under Heaven and decide all affairs, as in the former edict.

entries.zh: 壬戌，白虹貫日。
entries.en: On the renxu day a white rainbow pierced the sun.
entries.literal: On renxu day, a white rainbow pierced the sun.

entries.zh: 癸亥，罷內府河役。
entries.en: On the guihai day corvée on the inner palace river works was suspended.
entries.literal: On guihai day, corvée on the inner palace river works was suspended.

entries.zh: 甲子，擴廓帖木兒自晉寧退守冀寧。
entries.en: On the jiazi day Köke Temür withdrew from Jinning to hold Jining.
entries.literal: On jiazi day, Köke Temür withdrew from Jinning to hold Jining.

entries.zh: 大明兵至通州。
entries.en: Ming forces reached Tongzhou.
entries.literal: Ming forces reached Tongzhou.

entries.zh: 知樞密院事卜顏帖木兒力戰，被擒死之。
entries.en: Bureau director Buyan Temür fought fiercely and was captured and killed.
entries.literal: Bureau director Buyan Temür fought fiercely and was captured and killed.

entries.zh: 左丞相失列門傳旨，令太常禮儀院使阿魯渾等，奉太廟列室神主與皇太子同北行。
entries.en: Left chief minister Shiremen transmitted an order for director of imperial sacrifices Aruqun and others to escort the spirit tablets of the ancestral temple side chambers north together with the heir apparent.
entries.literal: Left chief minister Shiremen transmitted an order for Director of Imperial Sacrifices Aruqun and others to escort the spirit tablets of the ancestral temple side chambers north together with the heir apparent.

entries.zh: 阿魯渾等即至太廟，與署令王嗣宗、太祝哈剌不華襲護神主畢，仍留室內。
entries.en: When Aruqun and the others reached the Imperial Ancestral Temple together with acting director Wang Sizong and libationer Qara Buqa, they had finished escorting the spirit tablets but still left them within the chambers.
entries.literal: When Aruqun and the others reached the Imperial Ancestral Temple together with acting director Wang Sizong and libationer Qara Buqa, they had finished escorting the spirit tablets but still left them within the chambers.

entries.zh: 乙丑，白虹貫日。
entries.en: On the yichou day a white rainbow pierced the sun.
entries.literal: On yichou day, a white rainbow pierced the sun.

entries.zh: 罷內府興造。
entries.en: Inner palace construction works were suspended.
entries.literal: Inner palace construction works were suspended.

entries.zh: 詔淮王帖木兒不花監國，慶童為中書左丞相，同守京城。
entries.en: An edict appointed Prince of Huai, Temür Buhua to supervise the state, with Qingtong as left chief minister of the Secretariat, jointly guarding the capital.
entries.literal: An edict appointed Prince of Huai, Temür Buhua to supervise the state, with Qingtong as left chief minister of the Secretariat, jointly guarding the capital.

entries.zh: 丙寅，帝御清寧殿，集三宮后妃、皇太子、皇太子妃，同議避兵北行。
entries.en: On the bingyin day the emperor attended at the Qingning Hall and gathered the three palaces' empresses and consorts, the heir apparent, and the heir apparent's consort to discuss avoiding warfare by fleeing north.
entries.literal: On bingyin day, the emperor attended at the Qingning Hall and gathered the three palaces' empresses and consorts, the heir apparent, and the heir apparent's consort to discuss avoiding warfare by fleeing north.

entries.zh: 失列門及知樞密院事黑廝、宦者趙伯顏不花等諫，以為不可行，不聽。
entries.en: Shiremen and Bureau director Heisi and the eunuch Zhao Boyan Buhua remonstrated that this could not be done, but he would not listen.
entries.literal: Shiremen and Bureau director Heisi and the eunuch Zhao Boyan Buhua remonstrated that this could not be done, but he would not listen.

entries.zh: 伯顏不花慟哭諫曰：「天下者，世祖之天下，陛下當以死守，奈何棄之！
entries.en: Boyan Buhua wept and remonstrated, saying: "The realm is the realm of Kublai; Your Majesty ought to defend it to the death — how can you abandon it!
entries.literal: Boyan Buhua wept and remonstrated, saying: "The realm is the realm of Kublai; Your Majesty ought to defend it to the death — how can you abandon it!

entries.zh: 臣等願率軍民及諸怯薛歹出城拒戰，願陛下固守京城。」
entries.en: We your subjects are willing to lead troops and people and all the keshig to go out of the city and resist battle; we beg Your Majesty to hold the capital firm."
entries.literal: We your subjects are willing to lead troops and people and all the keshig to go out of the city and resist battle; we beg Your Majesty to hold the capital firm."

entries.zh: 卒不聽。
entries.en: In the end he would not listen.
entries.literal: In the end he would not listen.

entries.zh: 至夜半，開健德門北奔。
entries.en: At midnight the Jiande Gate was opened and they fled north.
entries.literal: At midnight the Jiande Gate was opened and they fled north.

entries.zh: 八月庚午，大明兵入京城，國亡。
entries.en: In the eighth month, on the gengwu day, Ming forces entered the capital and the state perished.
entries.literal: Eighth month, gengwu day; Ming forces entered the capital and the state perished.

entries.en: Accumulated years: 383,768,657.

entries.en: Day fraction: 5,230.
entries.literal: Day fraction, 5230.

entries.zh: 元興，其初未有法守，百司斷理獄訟，循用金律，頗傷嚴刻。
entries.en: When the Yuan dynasty first rose, it had no code of its own; government offices tried cases by the Jin statutes, which proved unduly harsh.
entries.literal: When the Yuan arose, at first there were no laws to observe; when the hundred offices adjudicated cases and lawsuits, they followed the Jin code, which was rather harsh and severe.

entries.zh: 及世祖平宋，疆理混一，由是簡除繁苛，始定新律，頒之有司，號曰《至元新格》。
entries.en: After Kublai conquered the Song and unified the realm, redundant and oppressive provisions were cut away, a new code was drawn up, and issued to the bureaucracy under the title Regulations of the Zhiyuan Era.
entries.literal: When the Founder conquered Song and the territorial administration was unified, they therefore simplified and removed what was burdensome and harsh, first fixed new statutes, and promulgated them to the offices, titled the Zhiyuan New Regulations.

entries.zh: 仁宗之時，又以格例條畫有關於風紀者，類集成書，號曰《風憲宏綱》。
entries.en: Under Renzong, statutes and precedents touching public morals were gathered into a compendium called the Broad Outline of Censorial Law.
entries.literal: In the time of Renzong, regulations and precedents bearing on public morals were further classified and compiled into a book titled the Broad Outline of Censorial Law.

entries.zh: 至英宗時，復命宰執儒臣取前書而加損益焉，書成，號曰《大元通制》。
entries.en: Under Yingzong, chief ministers and scholar-officials were ordered to revise the earlier compilations; the finished work was named the Comprehensive Institutions of the Great Yuan.
entries.literal: By the time of Yingzong, the chief ministers and Confucian scholars were again ordered to take the previous books and add or subtract from them; when the book was completed it was titled the Comprehensive Institutions of the Great Yuan.

entries.zh: 其書之大綱有三：一曰詔制，二曰條格，三曰斷例。
entries.en: The work falls into three main divisions: imperial edicts, regulatory articles, and adjudicated precedents.
entries.literal: The great outline of the book has three parts: first, imperial edicts and institutions; second, regulatory articles; third, adjudicated precedents.

entries.zh: 凡詔制為條九十有四，條格為條一千一百五十有一，斷例為條七百十有七，大概纂集世祖以來法制事例而已。
entries.en: It contains ninety-four articles of edicts and institutions, 1,151 regulatory articles, and 717 adjudicated precedents—essentially a digest of legal practice from Kublai's reign onward.
entries.literal: In all, imperial edicts and institutions number ninety-four articles, regulatory articles number one thousand one hundred fifty-one, and adjudicated precedents number seven hundred seventeen—on the whole merely a compilation of legal institutions and cases since the Founder.

entries.zh: 其五刑之目：凡七下至五十七，謂之笞刑；
entries.en: The five punishments were defined as follows: blows from seven through fifty-seven constituted flogging (chi);
entries.literal: The categories of the five punishments: from seven blows through fifty-seven are called the flogging punishment;

entries.zh: 凡六十七至一百七，謂之杖刑；
entries.en: from sixty-seven through one hundred seven constituted beating with the heavy stick (zhang);
entries.literal: from sixty-seven to one hundred seven are called the cudgel punishment;

entries.zh: 其徒法，年數杖數，相附麗為加減，鹽徒盜賊既決而又鐐之；
entries.en: Penal servitude paired term of years with a prescribed number of blows, increasing or decreasing together; salt laborers and convicted thieves were shackled even after sentence;
entries.literal: As for the law of penal servitude, years of servitude and number of blows were attached to one another for increase or decrease; salt convicts and robbers, after judgment, were again fettered;

entries.zh: 流則南人遷於遼陽迤北之地，北人遷於南方湖廣之鄉；
entries.en: exile sent southerners to Liaoyang and the far north, and northerners to the lake districts of Huguang in the south;
entries.literal: for exile, southerners were relocated to the region of Liaoyang and northward beyond; northerners were relocated to the southern lands of Huguang;

entries.zh: 死刑，則有斬而無絞，惡逆之極者，又有淩遲處死之法焉。
entries.en: capital punishment allowed decapitation but not strangulation; the gravest cases of treasonous villainy could be punished by death through dismemberment (lingchi).
entries.literal: for the death penalty, there was decapitation but no strangulation; for the most extreme cases of abominable rebellion, there was also the method of execution by dismemberment.

entries.zh: 蓋古者以墨、劓、剕、宮、大辟為五刑，後世除肉刑，乃以笞、杖、徒、流、死備五刑之數。
entries.en: Ancient law took branding, nose-cutting, foot-cutting, castration, and death as the five punishments; later dynasties abolished bodily mutilation and substituted flogging, beating, servitude, exile, and execution.
entries.literal: In antiquity the five punishments were tattooing, cutting off the nose, cutting off the feet, castration, and the great execution; later ages abolished the corporal mutilations and used flogging, cudgeling, servitude, exile, and death to complete the number of five punishments.

entries.zh: 元因之，更用輕典，蓋亦仁矣。
entries.en: The Yuan adopted that scheme and leaned toward milder penalties—a measure of humane intent.
entries.literal: The Yuan followed this and further employed a lenient code—this too was humane.

entries.zh: 世祖謂宰臣曰：「朕或怒，有罪者使汝殺，汝勿殺，必遲回一二日乃覆奏。」
entries.en: Kublai told his ministers: "When I am angry and tell you to execute a criminal, do not obey at once—wait a day or two, then report back to me."
entries.literal: The Founder said to his chief ministers: "If I am angry and order you to kill one who has committed a crime, do not kill him; you must wait a day or two and then report back to me."

entries.zh: 斯言也，雖古仁君，何以過之。
entries.en: Even the most merciful sovereigns of old could hardly have spoken more wisely.
entries.literal: In these words, even the humane rulers of antiquity—how could they surpass them?

entries.zh: 自後繼體之君，惟刑之恤，凡郡國有疑獄，必遣官覆讞而從輕，死罪審錄無冤者，亦必待報，然後加刑。
entries.en: Later emperors likewise showed concern for undue severity: doubtful cases in the provinces were sent up for re-review with a bias toward mercy, and even confirmed capital sentences were not carried out until imperial approval arrived.
entries.literal: From then on the succeeding heirs to the throne were sparing in punishments; whenever commanderies and kingdoms had doubtful cases, officials were always dispatched to review the verdicts and lean toward leniency; for death sentences, after examination and recording showed no injustice, punishment was still applied only after awaiting imperial response.

entries.zh: 而大德間，王約復上言：「國朝之制，笞杖十減為七，今之杖一百者，宜止九十七，不當又加十也。」
entries.en: During the Dade reign, Wang Yue urged again: "Under our law, every ten strokes of flogging or beating is counted as seven; a sentence of one hundred blows should therefore stop at ninety-seven, not rise by another ten."
entries.literal: In the Dade era, Wang Yue again submitted a memorial: "Our dynasty's institution reduces every ten blows of flogging or cudgeling to seven; today's punishment of one hundred blows should stop at ninety-seven and ought not to add another ten."

entries.zh: 此其君臣之間，唯知輕典之為尚，百年之間，天下乂寧，亦豈偶然而致哉！
entries.en: Ruler and ministers alike prized lenient law; that the realm enjoyed a century of peace was hardly accidental.
entries.literal: Between ruler and ministers, they knew only to esteem a lenient code; that within a hundred years the realm under Heaven was well governed—how could that have come about by mere chance!

entries.zh: 然其弊也，南北異制，事類繁瑣，挾情之吏，舞弄文法，出入比附，用譎行私，而凶頑不法之徒，又數以赦宥獲免；
entries.en: Yet the system also bred abuse: separate rules for north and south, endlessly tangled categories, and venal clerks who twisted statutes by analogy to serve private ends, while hardened criminals repeatedly walked free under general amnesties;
entries.literal: Yet its abuses were these: different institutions for north and south, categories of affairs numerous and trivial, officials who harbored private motives who manipulated the letter of the law, going in and out through analogies and comparisons, employing deceit to pursue private ends—and violent and lawless persons again and again escaped through amnesties;

entries.zh: 至於西僧歲作佛事，或恣意縱囚，以售其奸宄，俾善良者喑啞而飲恨，識者病之。
entries.en: Western monks holding annual Buddhist ceremonies sometimes released prisoners at will to advance their schemes, leaving honest people voiceless with bitter grievance—a practice thoughtful observers deplored.
entries.literal: As for the Western monks who each year performed Buddhist rites, they sometimes arbitrarily released prisoners to sell their treachery and villainy, causing the good and honest to be silenced and swallow resentment—those with understanding were distressed by this.

entries.zh: 然而元之刑法，其得在仁厚，其失在乎緩弛而不知檢也。
entries.en: On balance, Yuan criminal law succeeded in humanity and failed through laxity and insufficient discipline.
entries.literal: Yet in the Yuan's penal law, its gain lay in humane generosity, and its loss lay in lax indulgence without knowing restraint.

entries.zh: 今按其實，條列而次第之，使後世有以考其得失，作《刑法志》。
entries.en: The present account sets out the facts in order, so that posterity may judge what worked and what did not—hence this Treatise on Punishment and Law.
entries.literal: Now, according to the facts, items are listed and arranged in order, so that later ages may have means to examine its gains and losses—thus is composed the Treatise on Punishment and Law.

entries.zh: 諸有司事關蒙古軍者，與管軍官約會問。
entries.en: Civil cases involving Mongol troops must be heard jointly with the commanding officer.
entries.literal: As to offices whose matters concern Mongol troops, they consult jointly with the military commander in questioning.

entries.zh: 諸管軍官、奧魯官及鹽運司、打捕鷹坊軍匠、各投下管領諸色人等，但犯強竊盜賊、偽造寶鈔、略賣人口、發冢放火、犯奸及諸死罪，並從有司歸問。
entries.en: Military commanders, auruq officials, salt transport staff, hunting and falconry artisans, military craftsmen, and appanage dependents who commit robbery, counterfeiting, kidnapping, tomb robbery, arson, adultery, or any capital crime are tried by civil authorities.
entries.literal: As to military commanders, auruq officials, salt transport offices, hunting and falconry artisans, military craftsmen, and persons of every category under the management of appanages—whoever commits robbery, theft, counterfeiting treasure notes, abducting and selling persons, opening tombs, arson, adultery, and all capital crimes—is returned to the civil offices for trial.

entries.zh: 其鬥訟、婚田、良賤、錢債、財產、宗從繼絕及科差不公自相告言者，從本管理問。
entries.en: Brawls, marriage and land disputes, status disputes, debts, property, succession, and unfair corvée complaints are tried by the defendant's supervising authority.
entries.literal: As for brawls and lawsuits, marriage and fields, free and base status, money debts, property, extinction of a lineage branch, and unfair corvée levies where parties accuse one another, they are tried by their own supervising authority.

entries.zh: 若事關民戶者，從有司約會歸問，並從有司追逮，三約不至者，有司就便歸斷。
entries.en: Cases involving civilian households are heard jointly with civil offices, which also make arrests; after three failed summonses, civil offices judge immediately.
entries.literal: If the matter concerns civilian households, the civil offices consult jointly for trial, and likewise pursue and arrest; if after three summonses the other party does not appear, the civil offices judge on the spot.

entries.zh: 諸州縣鄰境軍民相關詞訟，元告就被論官司歸斷，不在約會之例。
entries.en: Cross-border suits between soldiers and civilians are judged by the defendant's local office where suit was brought, without joint consultation.
entries.literal: As to lawsuits between military and civilians across neighboring prefectures and counties, the original plaintiff is judged by the office of the party sued in the place where suit was brought—not within the scope of joint consultation.

entries.zh: 斷不當理，許赴上司陳訴，罪及元斷官吏。
entries.en: Unjust judgments may be appealed to superiors, and the original judges are punished.
entries.literal: If judgment is improper in principle, appeal to a superior is permitted, and guilt extends to the original judging officials.

entries.zh: 諸僧、道、儒人有爭，有司勿問，止令三家所掌會問。
entries.en: Disputes among Buddhist, Daoist, and Confucian clergy are not tried by civil offices but by the authorities of the three traditions jointly.
entries.literal: As to disputes among Buddhist monks, Daoist priests, and Confucian scholars, civil offices do not inquire; they are only ordered to be jointly heard by the authorities of the three traditions.

entries.zh: 諸哈的大師，止令掌教念經，回回人應有刑名、戶婚、錢糧、詞訟並從有司問之。
entries.en: Qadi masters may teach scripture only; criminal, household, fiscal, and civil matters of Huihui persons are tried by civil offices.
entries.literal: As to qadi masters, they are only ordered to preside over teaching and recitation of scripture; Huihui persons' criminal matters, household and marriage, grain and cash, and lawsuits are all tried by the civil offices.

entries.zh: 諸僧人但犯奸盜詐偽，致傷人命及諸重罪，有司歸問。
entries.en: Monks who commit adultery, theft, fraud, homicide, or other grave crimes are tried by civil authorities.
entries.literal: As to Buddhist monks who commit adultery, theft, fraud, cause injury to human life, and all grave crimes, they are returned to the civil offices for trial.

entries.zh: 其自相爭告，從各寺院住持本管頭目歸問。
entries.en: Disputes among monks are tried by each monastery's abbot and supervising chief.
entries.literal: When they sue one another, trial is returned to each monastery's abbot and the supervising chief in charge.

entries.zh: 若僧俗相爭田土，與有司約會；
entries.en: Land disputes between monks and laypersons require joint consultation with civil offices;
entries.literal: If monks and laypersons dispute over fields, they consult jointly with the civil offices;

entries.zh: 約會不至，有司就便歸問。
entries.en: if the other party fails to appear, civil offices judge immediately.
entries.literal: if the other party fails to appear for consultation, the civil offices judge on the spot.

entries.zh: 諸各寺院稅糧，除前宋所有常住及世祖所賜田土免納稅糧外，已後諸人布施並己力典買者，依例納糧。
entries.en: Monastery lands are taxed except for former Song endowments and fields granted by Kublai; later donations and purchased lands pay tax as usual.
entries.literal: As to tax grain of the various monasteries, except for permanent endowments of the former Song and fields bestowed by the Founder which are exempt from tax grain, thereafter donations by various persons and fields bought with one's own funds pay grain according to precedent.

entries.zh: 諸管民官以公事攝所部，並用信牌，其差人擾眾者，禁之。
entries.en: Officials summoning subordinates on public business must use credential tallies; agents who harass the people are forbidden.
entries.literal: As to officials who oversee the people and summon subordinates on public business, all use credential tallies; those whose dispatched agents harass the multitude are forbidden.

entries.zh: 帖古倫大皇后 右大斡耳朵 察必皇后 （弘吉列氏，魯忠武王按嗔那顏女也。中統初立為皇后，至元十年授冊寶，尋又上尊號曰貞懿昭順天睿文光應皇后。十八年崩，三十一年上尊諡曰昭睿順聖皇后。后性明敏，達於事機，至元之政，左右彌縫，當時以為蓋有力焉。） 南必皇后 （弘吉列氏。至元二十年納為皇后，時世祖春秋高，后頗預政，相臣常不得見帝，輒因后奏事焉。） 右第二斡耳朵 塔剌海皇后 奴罕皇后 右第三斡耳朵 伯要兀真皇后 闊闊倫皇后 右第四斡耳朵 八八罕妃子 右見歲賜錄，不知所守斡耳朵。 速哥答（思）里皇后 （泰定三年詔守世祖斡耳朵。） 撒不忽妃子
entries.en: Great Empress Tegulün. Right Great Orda: Empress Chabi (Kongirat, daughter of the loyal and martial King Anchannayan of Lu; made empress at the start of the Zhongtong era, invested with seal and regalia in 1273, and soon given the honorific Empress Zhenyi Zhaoshun Tianrui Wenguang Ying; she died in 1281 and was posthumously titled Empress Zhaorui Shunsheng in 1294. Intelligent and politically astute, she was widely thought to have significantly shaped Zhiyuan-era governance). Empress Nanbi (Kongirat; taken as empress in 1283 when Kublai was elderly; she often intervened in government, and ministers who could not reach the emperor would report through her). Right Second Orda: Empress Talahai; Empress Nuhan. Right Third Orda: Empress Boyaowuzhen; Empress Kuokuolun. Right Fourth Orda: Consort Babuhan (listed in the annual grant register but with no orda recorded). Empress Sugedali (in 1326 ordered by edict to maintain Kublai's orda). Consort Sabuhu.
entries.literal: Great Empress Tegulün. Right Great Orda: Empress Chabi (Kongirat clan, daughter of King Anchannayan of Lu, loyal and martial; established as empress at the beginning of Zhongtong; in the tenth year of Zhiyuan invested with seal and treasure; soon after elevated with honorific title Empress Zhenyi Zhaoshun Tianrui Wenguang Ying; died in the eighteenth year; in the thirty-first year honored with posthumous title Empress Zhaorui Shunsheng. The empress was intelligent and clear, adept at affairs; in the governance of Zhiyuan she mediated left and right—contemporaries thought she surely had great force). Empress Nanbi (Kongirat clan; in the twentieth year of Zhiyuan taken in as empress; at that time Shizu was advanced in years and the empress often participated in government; chief ministers frequently could not see the emperor and would present affairs through the empress). Right Second Orda: Empress Talahai. Empress Nuhan. Right Third Orda: Empress Boyaowuzhen. Empress Kuokuolun. Right Fourth Orda: Consort Babuhan. As seen in the record of annual grants, her orda guarded is unknown. Empress Sugedali (in the third year of Taiding an edict ordered her to guard Shizu's orda). Consort Sabuhu.

entries.zh: 卜魯罕皇后 （伯岳吾氏，勳臣普化之孫，駙馬脫里忽思之女。元貞初立為皇后，大德三年授冊寶。十一年帝崩，武宗立，廢后，徙東安州，尋賜死。成宗晚年多疾，后居中用事，而能信任相臣哈剌哈孫，以卒成大德之治，識者猶有取焉。） 失憐答里元妃 （弘吉列氏，早薨。至大元年追尊諡曰貞慈靜懿皇后，配享成廟。） 乞里吉忽帖尼皇后
entries.en: Empress Buluhan (Baiyuewu, granddaughter of the meritorious minister Puhua and daughter of the imperial son-in-law Telihusi; made empress at the start of Yuanzhen and invested in 1299; when Temür died in 1307 Külüg deposed her, exiled her to Dong'an, and soon had her executed. Though she dominated the inner court during Temür's late illnesses, she trusted the chief minister Harqasun and helped bring the Dade reign to a stable close—a point critics still acknowledged). Primary Consort Shilian Dali (Kongirat; died young; posthumously titled Empress Zhenci Jingyi in 1308 and enshrined at Chengzong's temple). Empress Qilijihutieni.
entries.literal: Empress Buluhan (Baiyuewu clan, granddaughter of meritorious minister Puhua, daughter of consort Telihusi; established as empress at the beginning of Yuanzhen; in the third year of Dade invested with seal and treasure; in the eleventh year the emperor died, Wuzong was established, the empress was deposed, moved to Dong'an Prefecture, and soon ordered to die by grant. In Chengzong's later years he had many illnesses; the empress held power within the palace yet was able to trust chief minister Harqasun, thereby completing the governance of Dade—those of discernment still found something to approve). Primary Consort Shilian Dali (Kongirat clan, early death; in the first year of Zhida posthumously honored with title Empress Zhenci Jingyi, enshrined with Chengzong's temple). Empress Qilijihutieni.

entries.zh: 真哥皇后 （弘吉列氏，至大三年冊為皇后。泰定四年上尊諡曰宣慈惠聖皇后。） 速哥失里皇后 （真哥妹也。） 完者歹皇后 妃子亦乞列氏 （明宗母也，天曆二年追諡仁獻章聖皇后。） 妃子唐兀氏 （文宗母也，天曆二年追諡文獻昭聖皇后。）
entries.en: Empress Zhenge (Kongirat; enregistered as empress in 1310; posthumously titled Empress Xuanci Huisheng in 1327). Empress Sugeshili (Zhenge's younger sister). Empress Wanzhedai. Consort Yiqiliesi (Mingzong's mother; posthumously titled Empress Renxian Zhangsheng in 1329). Consort Tangwu (Wenzong's mother; posthumously titled Empress Wenxian Zhaosheng in 1329).
entries.literal: Empress Zhenge (Kongirat clan; in the third year of Zhida enregistered as empress; in the fourth year of Taiding honored with posthumous title Empress Xuanci Huisheng). Empress Sugeshili (younger sister of Zhenge). Empress Wanzhedai. Consort Yiqiliesi (mother of Mingzong; in the second year of Tianli posthumously titled Empress Renxian Zhangsheng). Consort Tangwu (mother of Wenzong; in the second year of Tianli posthumously titled Empress Wenxian Zhaosheng).

entries.zh: 阿納失舍里皇后 （弘吉烈氏。皇慶二年冊為皇后。延祐七年上尊諡曰莊懿慈聖皇后。） 答里麻失里皇后
entries.en: Empress Anashisheli (Kongirat; enregistered as empress in 1313; posthumously titled Empress Zhuangyi Cisheng in 1320). Empress Dalimashili.
entries.literal: Empress Anashisheli (Kongirat clan; in the second year of Huangqing enregistered as empress; in the seventh year of Yanyou honored with posthumous title Empress Zhuangyi Cisheng). Empress Dalimashili.

entries.zh: 后妃之制，厥有等威，其來尚矣。
entries.en: The ranks and authority governing empresses and consorts are ancient institutions.
entries.literal: The institution of empresses and consorts has its ranks and authority; its origin is of long standing.

entries.zh: 元初，因其國俗，不娶庶姓，非此族也，不居嫡選。
entries.en: Early in the dynasty the Mongols followed their own custom of not marrying outside certain clans; only women of the designated lineage could be chosen as principal consorts.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Yuan, following their national custom, they did not marry common clans; those not of this clan could not hold the principal selection.

entries.zh: 當時史臣以為舅甥之貴，蓋有周姬、齊姜之遺意，歷世守之，固可嘉也。
entries.en: Contemporary historians held that the esteem accorded maternal-kin marriage preserved something of the Zhou custom of taking brides from the Ji of Zhou and the Jiang of Qi—a practice maintained for generations and rightly praised.
entries.literal: The historians of that time regarded the honor of uncle and nephew [alliances] as preserving something of the Zhou practice of Ji brides and Qi Jiang brides; to preserve this through generations was indeed commendable.

entries.zh: 然其居則有曰斡耳朵之分，沒復有繼承守宮之法。
entries.en: Yet their households were divided into separate ordas, and after a consort's death there arose the practice of heirs inheriting and maintaining her palace establishment.
entries.literal: Yet in residence there were divisions called orda; after death there was again the method of inheriting and guarding the palace.

entries.zh: 位號之淆，名分之瀆，則亦甚矣。
entries.en: The confusion of titles and the breach of proper status were extreme as well.
entries.literal: The confusion of titles and ranks, the violation of name and status, was indeed extreme.

entries.zh: 累朝嘗詔有司修后妃傳，而未見成書。
entries.en: Dynasty after dynasty the court ordered officials to compile biographies of empresses and consorts, yet no finished book ever appeared.
entries.literal: Over successive reigns they often ordered the relevant offices to compile biographies of empresses and consorts, but no completed work is seen.

entries.zh: 內廷事祕，今莫之考，則其氏名之僅見簡牘者，尚可遺而不錄乎？
entries.en: Inner-palace affairs are secret and cannot now be fully verified; yet the clan names that survive on scattered documents surely ought not to be omitted.
entries.literal: Inner-palace affairs are secret; none can examine them today—can the clan names that appear only on scattered documents still be left unrecorded?

entries.zh: 且一代之制存焉，闕疑而慎言，斯可矣。
entries.en: What remains here still preserves the institutions of an age; to note uncertainties and speak with caution is enough.
entries.literal: Moreover, the institutions of a dynasty are preserved here; to leave doubts unspoken and speak cautiously is sufficient.

entries.zh: 作后妃表。
entries.en: Hence this table of empresses and consorts.
entries.literal: [I therefore] compose the Table of Empresses and Consorts.

entries.zh: 太祖
entries.en: Taizu (Genghis Khan)
entries.literal: Taizu.

entries.zh: 太宗
entries.en: Taizong (Ögedei)
entries.literal: Taizong.

entries.zh: 定宗
entries.en: Dingzong (Güyük)
entries.literal: Dingzong.

entries.zh: 憲宗
entries.en: Xianzong (Möngke)
entries.literal: Xianzong.

entries.zh: 昌國大長公主帖木倫，烈祖女，適昌忠武王孛禿，主薨，繼室以太祖女昌國大長公主火臣別吉。 昌國大長公主亦乞列思，適孛禿子帖堅干，繼室以昌國大長公主茶倫。 昌國大長公主安禿，太宗子闊出女，適孛禿子昌武定王瑣兒哈。 吾魯真公主，世祖女，適帖木干子孛花。 昌國大長公主也孫真，適鎖兒哈子昌（武）忠靖王札忽爾陳。 魯魯罕公主，適孛花弟寧昌郡王唆都哥。繼室以魯倫公主。 昌國大長公主伯雅倫，憲宗女，適札忽爾陳子昌忠宣王忽鄰。繼室以昌國大長公主卜蘭奚。 普顏可里美思公主，適唆都哥子寧昌郡王不鄰吉歹。 昌國大長公主益里海涯，成宗女，適忽鄰子昌王阿失。繼室以昌國大長公主買的，憲宗曾孫女也。 昌國大長公主烟合牙，適昌王八剌失里。 昌國大長公主月魯，適八剌失里子昌王沙藍朵兒。 奴兀倫公主，安西王女，適忽鄰弟瑣郎哈。
entries.en: Grand Princess of Chang, Temülün, daughter of the founding ancestor, married Bo'ertu, the loyal and martial King of Chang. After her death, Taizu's daughter Grand Princess of Chang Huochen Bieji became his successor consort. Grand Princess of Chang Yiqiliesi married Bo'ertu's son Tieqian'gan; after her death, Grand Princess of Chang Chalun succeeded her. Grand Princess of Chang Antu, daughter of Ögedei's son Kuochu, married Bo'ertu's son Suo'erha, the martial and stabilizing King of Chang. Princess Wuluzhen, Kublai's daughter, married Tieqian'gan's son Bohua. Grand Princess of Chang Yesunzhen married Suo'erha's son Zhahuer Chen, the loyal and tranquil King of Chang. Princess Luluhan married Bohua's younger brother Soduge, Prince of Ningchang; Princess Lulun was the successor consort. Grand Princess of Chang Boyalun, Möngke's daughter, married Zhahuer Chen's son Hulin, the loyal and illustrious King of Chang; Grand Princess of Chang Bulanxi succeeded her. Princess Puyan Kelimeisi married Soduge's son Bulinjidai, Prince of Ningchang. Grand Princess of Chang Yili Haiya, Temür's daughter, married Hulin's son Ashi, King of Chang; Grand Princess of Chang Maidi, a great-granddaughter of Möngke, was the successor consort. Grand Princess of Chang Yanheya married King of Chang Balashili. Grand Princess of Chang Yuelu married Balashili's son King of Chang Shalanduo'er. Princess Nuwulun, daughter of the Prince of Anxi, married Hulin's younger brother Suolangha.
entries.literal: Grand Princess of Chang, Temülün, daughter of the Founding Ancestor; married Bo'ertu, King of Chang, loyal and martial. When the princess died, the successor consort was Grand Princess of Chang, Huochen Biejilie, daughter of Taizu. Grand Princess of Chang, Yiqiliesi; married Bo'ertu's son Tieqian'gan; successor consort Grand Princess of Chang, Chalun. Grand Princess of Chang, Antu, daughter of Taizong's son Kuochu; married Bo'ertu's son Suo'erha, King of Chang, martial and stabilizing. Princess Wuluzhen, daughter of Shizu; married Tieqian'gan's son Bohua. Grand Princess of Chang, Yesunzhen; married Suo'erha's son Zhahuer Chen, King of Chang, loyal and tranquil. Princess Luluhan; married Bohua's younger brother Soduge, Prince of Ningchang. Successor consort Princess Lulun. Grand Princess of Chang, Boyalun, daughter of Xianzong; married Zhahuer Chen's son Hulin, King of Chang, loyal and illustrious. Successor consort Grand Princess of Chang, Bulanxi. Princess Puyan Kelimeisi; married Soduge's son Bulinjidai, Prince of Ningchang. Grand Princess of Chang, Yili Haiya, daughter of Chengzong; married Hulin's son Ashi, King of Chang. Successor consort Grand Princess of Chang, Maidi, a great-granddaughter of Xianzong. Grand Princess of Chang, Yanheya; married King of Chang Balashili. Grand Princess of Chang, Yuelu; married Balashili's son King of Chang Shalanduo'er. Princess Nuwulun, daughter of the Prince of Anxi; married Hulin's younger brother Suolangha.

entries.zh: 趙國大長公主阿剌海別吉，太祖女，適趙武毅王孛要合。 獨木干公主，睿宗女，適拜哈弟鄃王聶古䚟。 趙國大長公主月烈，世祖女，適拜哈子趙武襄王愛不花。 趙國大長公主葉里迷失，定宗女，適孛（答）要合子趙忠襄王君不花。 趙國大長公主忽答迭迷失，裕宗女，適（君）愛不花子趙忠獻王闊里吉思，繼室以趙國大長公主愛牙（迷）失里，成宗女也。 趙國大長公主亦憐真，適君不花子趙忠烈王囊家台。 趙國大長公主回紇，適君不花弟趙康禧王喬鄰察。 趙國大長公主阿失禿魯，適愛不花子鄃忠襄王朮忽難。 大長公主（桑）速哥八剌，適囊家台子趙王馬札罕。
entries.en: Grand Princess of Zhao Alahaibieji, Genghis's daughter, married Boyaohe, the martial and resolute King of Zhao. Princess Dumugan, Tolui's daughter, married Baiha's younger brother Nieguqi, Prince of Yu. Grand Princess of Zhao Yuelie, Kublai's daughter, married Baiha's son Aibuhua, the martial and supportive King of Zhao. Grand Princess of Zhao Yelimi Shi, Güyük's daughter, married Boyaohe's son Junbuhua, the loyal and supportive King of Zhao. Grand Princess of Zhao Hudadiemi Shi, Zhenjin's daughter, married Aibuhua's son Kuolijisi, the loyal and offering King of Zhao; Temür's daughter Grand Princess of Zhao Aiyamishili was the successor consort. Grand Princess of Zhao Yilianzhen married Junbuhua's son Nangjiatai, the loyal and stern King of Zhao. Grand Princess of Zhao Huihe married Junbuhua's younger brother Qiaolincha, the joyous and auspicious King of Zhao. Grand Princess of Zhao Ashitulu married Aibuhua's son Zhuhunan, the loyal and supportive King of Yu. Grand Princess Sugabieba married Nangjiatai's son Mazahan, King of Zhao.
entries.literal: Grand Princess of Zhao, Alahaibieji, daughter of Taizu; married Boyaohe, King of Zhao, martial and resolute. Princess Dumugan, daughter of Ruizong; married Baiha's younger brother Nieguqi, Prince of Yu. Grand Princess of Zhao, Yuelie, daughter of Shizu; married Baiha's son Aibuhua, King of Zhao, martial and supportive. Grand Princess of Zhao, Yelimi Shi, daughter of Dingzong; married Boyaohe's son Junbuhua, King of Zhao, loyal and supportive. Grand Princess of Zhao, Hudadiemi Shi, daughter of Yuzong; married Aibuhua's son Kuolijisi, King of Zhao, loyal and offering; successor consort Grand Princess of Zhao, Aiyamishili, daughter of Chengzong. Grand Princess of Zhao, Yilianzhen; married Junbuhua's son Nangjiatai, King of Zhao, loyal and stern. Grand Princess of Zhao, Huihe; married Junbuhua's younger brother Qiaolincha, King of Zhao, joyous and auspicious. Grand Princess of Zhao, Ashitulu; married Aibuhua's son Zhuhunan, King of Yu, loyal and supportive. Grand Princess, Sugabieba; married Nangjiatai's son Mazahan, King of Zhao.

entries.zh: 魯國大長公主也速不花，睿宗女也，適皇國舅魯忠武王按嗔那顏子斡陳駙馬。 魯國公主薛只干，太祖孫女，適斡陳弟納陳駙馬。 魯國長公主完澤，適斡陳男斡羅真駙馬。 魯國大長公主囊家真，世祖女，適納陳子帖木兒，再適帖木兒弟蠻子台。 魯國大長公主南阿不剌，裕宗女，適蠻子台。 魯國徽文懿福（真）貞壽大長公主祥哥剌吉，順宗女，適帖木兒子[弓+周]阿不剌。 魯國大長公主普納，適帖木兒子魯王桑哥不剌。 肅雍賢寧公主朵兒只班，適[弓+周]阿八剌子阿里嘉實利。 大長公主拜塔沙，適按陳裔孫買住罕。 台忽普都公主，適按陳裔孫安遠王丑漢。 唆兒哈罕公主，太宗女，適按陳孫納合。 斡可真公主，適火忽孫不只兒。 不魯罕公主，適特薛禪孫脫羅禾，繼室以仁宗女闊闊倫公主。
entries.en: Grand Princess of Lu Yesubuhua, also Tolui's daughter, married the son of the imperial uncle of Lu, the loyal and martial King Anchannayan—Consort Wochen. Princess Xuezhigan, a granddaughter of Genghis, married Wochen's younger brother Consort Nachen. Grand Princess of Lu Wanzhe married Wochen's son Consort Woluozhen. Grand Princess of Lu Nangjiazhen, Kublai's daughter, married Nachen's son Tiemuer and later his younger brother Manzitai. Grand Princess of Lu Nan'abula, Zhenjin's daughter, married Manzitai. Grand Princess of Lu Xianggezhiji, titled Huiwen Yifu Zhenshou, Shunzong's daughter, married Tiemuer's son Jiu'abulu. Grand Princess of Lu Puna married Tiemuer's son Sanggebula, King of Lu. Princess Suyong Xianning Duorizhiban married Jiu'abula's son Alijiashili. Grand Princess Baitasha married a descendant of Anchannayan, Maizhuhan. Princess Taihupudu married a descendant of Anchannayan, Chouhan, King of Anyuan. Princess Suo'erhahan, Ögedei's daughter, married Anchannayan's grandson Nahe. Princess Wokezhen married Huohu's grandson Buzhier. Princess Buluhan married Texuechan's grandson Tuoluohe; Renzong's daughter Princess Kuokuolun was the successor consort.
entries.literal: Grand Princess of Lu, Yesubuhua, also a daughter of Ruizong; married the imperial uncle's son Wochen, consort of Lu, loyal and martial King Anchannayan. Princess Xuezhigan, granddaughter of Taizu; married Wochen's younger brother Nachen, consort. Grand Princess of Lu, Wanzhe; married Wochen's son Woluozhen, consort. Grand Princess of Lu, Nangjiazhen, daughter of Shizu; married Nachen's son Tiemuer, and again married Tiemuer's younger brother Manzitai. Grand Princess of Lu, Nan'abula, daughter of Yuzong; married Manzitai. Grand Princess of Lu, Huiven Yifu Zhenshou, Xianggezhiji, daughter of Shunzong; married Tiemuer's son Jiu'abulu. Grand Princess of Lu, Puna; married Tiemuer's son Sanggebula, King of Lu. Princess Suyong Xianning, Duorizhiban; married Jiu'abula's son Alijiashili. Grand Princess Baitasha; married Anchannayan's descendant Maizhuhan. Princess Taihupudu; married Anchannayan's descendant Chouhan, King of Anyuan. Princess Suo'erhahan, daughter of Taizong; married Anchannayan's grandson Nahe. Princess Wokezhen; married Huohu's grandson Buzhier. Princess Buluhan; married Texuechan's grandson Tuoluohe; successor consort Princess Kuokuolun, daughter of Renzong.

entries.zh: 禿滿倫公主，適赤窟駙馬。 瓮吉八忽公主，適赤窟孫懷都駙馬。 采真公主，適懷都弟愛不哥駙馬。 鄆國大長公主忙哥台，適愛不哥子寧濮郡王昌吉。 大長公主桑哥不剌，適愛不哥子岐王脫脫木兒。 札牙八剌公主，適駙馬。
entries.en: Princess Tumanlun married Consort Chiku. Princess Wengjibahu married Chiku's grandson Consort Huaidu. Princess Caizhen married Huaidu's younger brother Consort Aibuge. Grand Princess of Yun Manggetai married Aibuge's son Changji, Prince of Ningpu. Grand Princess Sanggebula married Aibuge's son Tuotuomuer, King of Qi. Princess Zhayabala married a consort name not recorded.
entries.literal: Princess Tumanlun; married Chiku, consort. Princess Wengjibahu; married Chiku's grandson Huaidu, consort. Princess Caizhen; married Huaidu's younger brother Aibuge, consort. Grand Princess of Yun, Manggetai; married Aibuge's son Changji, Prince of Ningpu. Grand Princess Sanggebula; married Aibuge's son Tuotuomuer, King of Qi. Princess Zhayabala; married a consort.

entries.zh: 也立（可）安敦公主，太祖女，適亦都護巴而述阿兒忒的斤。 巴巴哈兒公主，定宗女，適巴而述阿而忒的斤曾孫亦都護火赤哈兒的斤。 不魯罕公主，太宗孫女，適火赤哈兒子高昌王紐林的斤。主薨，繼室以其妹八卜叉公主。又薨，繼室以兀剌真公主，世祖之孫安西王阿難答女也。 朵而只思蠻公主，太宗之子闊（瑞）端之女，適高昌王帖睦兒補化。
entries.en: Princess Yiliandun, Genghis's daughter, married the Iduhu (Protector-General) Barishu Aiertedijin. Princess Babaha'er, Güyük's daughter, married the Iduhu Huochiha'erdedijin, great-grandson of Barishu Aiertedijin. Princess Buluhan, Ögedei's granddaughter, married Huochiha'erdedijin's son Niulin'sijin, King of Gaochang. After her death, her younger sister Princess Babacha became the successor consort; when Babacha died as well, Princess Wulazhen, daughter of Kublai's grandson Ananda, Prince of Anxi, succeeded her. Princess Duo'erzhi Siman, daughter of Ögedei's son Kuoduan, married Timuer Buhua, King of Gaochang.
entries.literal: Princess Yiliandun, daughter of Taizu; married the Iduhu Barishu Aiertedijin. Princess Babaha'er, daughter of Dingzong; married the Iduhu Huochiha'erdedijin, great-grandson of Barishu Aiertedijin. Princess Buluhan, granddaughter of Taizong; married Huochiha'er's son Niulin'sijin, King of Gaochang. When the princess died, the successor consort was her younger sister Princess Babacha. When she too died, the successor consort was Princess Wulazhen, daughter of Shizu's grandson Ananda, Prince of Anxi. Princess Duo'erzhi Siman, daughter of Taizong's son Kuoduan; married Timuer Buhua, King of Gaochang.

entries.zh: 齊國大長公主忽都魯堅迷失，世祖之女，適高麗王愖，即王昛也。 薊國大長公主高麗王妃卜答失利，顯宗女，適瀋王王謜，即王璋也。 濮國長公主高麗王妃亦憐只班，世祖之孫營王也先帖木兒女，適瀋王王燾。主薨，繼室以曹國長公主高麗王妃金童，順宗子魏王女也。 □國公主，顯宗之子梁王松山女，適瀋王王暠。
entries.en: Grand Princess of Qi Hudulujianmi Shi, Kublai's daughter, married King Chun of Goryeo—that is, King Wang Hao. Grand Princess of Ji, the Goryeo consort Budashili, daughter of Manggala, married Prince Wang Yan of Shen—that is, Wang Zhang. Princess of Pu, the Goryeo consort Yilianzhiban, daughter of Kublai's grandson Yexiantiemuer, Prince of Ying, married Prince Wang Tao of Shen. After her death, the Goryeo consort Jintong, Princess of Cao and daughter of the Wei Prince, son of Shunzong, became the successor consort. A princess of an unnamed state, daughter of Manggala's son Prince Songshan of Liang, married Prince Wang Gao of Shen.
entries.literal: Grand Princess of Qi, Hudulujianmi Shi, daughter of Shizu; married the King of Goryeo Chun—that is, King Wang Hao. Grand Princess of Ji, Goryeo consort Budashili, daughter of Xianzong; married the Prince of Shen Wang Yan—that is, Wang Zhang. Princess of Pu, Goryeo consort Yilianzhiban, daughter of Shizu's grandson Yexiantiemuer, Prince of Ying; married the Prince of Shen Wang Tao. When the princess died, the successor consort was Princess of Cao, Goryeo consort Jintong, daughter of Shunzong's son, Prince of Wei. Princess of an unnamed state, daughter of Xianzong's son Liang Wang Songshan; married the Prince of Shen Wang Gao.

entries.zh: 阿昔倫公主，適阿脫駙馬。 搠只蠻公主，適阿脫弟忽都虎駙馬。
entries.en: Princess Axilun married Consort Atuo. Princess Shuozhiman married Atuo's younger brother Consort Huduhu.
entries.literal: Princess Axilun; married Atuo, consort. Princess Shuozhiman; married Atuo's younger brother Huduhu, consort.

entries.zh: 帶魯罕公主，適拔都駙馬。 搠思蠻公主，適拔都子阿朮魯駙馬。
entries.en: Princess Dailuhan married Consort Batu. Princess Shuosiman married Batu's son Consort Azhulu.
entries.literal: Princess Dailuhan; married Batu, consort. Princess Shuosiman; married Batu's son Azhulu, consort.

entries.zh: 火魯公主，適哈答駙馬。 闊闊干公主，適脫（亦禾）欒赤駙馬。 脫脫灰公主，世祖孫女，適禿滿答兒駙馬。 □□公主，適別里迷失駙馬。 □□公主，適沙藍駙馬。 延安公主，適延安王也不干。
entries.en: Princess Huolu married Consort Hada. Princess Kuokuogan married Consort Tuoluan Chi. Princess Tuotuohui, a granddaughter of Kublai, married Consort Tumanda'er. A princess name unreadable in source married Consort Bielimishi. A princess name unreadable in source married Consort Shalan. Princess Yan'an married Yebugan, King of Yan'an.
entries.literal: Princess Huolu; married Hada, consort. Princess Kuokuogan; married Tuoluan Chi, consort. Princess Tuotuohui, granddaughter of Shizu; married Tumanda'er, consort. Princess name unreadable in source; married Bielimishi, consort. Princess name unreadable in source; married Shalan, consort. Princess Yan'an; married Yebugan, King of Yan'an.

entries.zh: □□□公主，適塔出駙馬。 □□公主，適塔出子朮真伯駙馬。 □□公主，適朮真伯子別合剌駙馬。 □□公主，適別合剌子塔八駙馬。

entries.zh: 完者台公主，適永寧王卯澤。 英壽大長公主妥（安）妥輝，世祖孫女也。 壽寧大長公主，顯宗女，泰定皇帝伯姊也。 明慧貞懿大長公主不答昔你，明宗之女。 □□公主，適合納那顏孫奔忒古兒駙馬。 買買公主。 阿剌歹公主。 木答里公主。 雪雪的斤公主。 阿失禿公主。 失憐答里公主。

Grand Princess Shouning, daughter of Manggala, was the paternal aunt of Emperor Taiding. Grand Princess Minghui Zhenyi Budaxini was a daughter of Qoshila. entries.zh: 昔者史臣有言，婦人內夫家，雖天姬之貴，史氏猶外而弗詳。
entries.en: Historians of old observed that once a woman married into her husband's clan, even an emperor's daughter was regarded as outside the lineage and seldom recorded in full.
entries.literal: In former times the historiographers have said that when a woman enters her husband's family, even though she be as exalted as a daughter of Heaven, the historians still treat her as external and do not record her in detail.

entries.zh: 然元室之制，非勳臣世族及封國之君，則莫得尚主，是以世聯戚畹者，親視諸王，其藩翰屏垣之寄，蓋亦重矣。
entries.en: Under Yuan custom, however, only families of merit—hereditary nobles and enfeoffed lords—might marry imperial princesses. Those bound to the throne by such marriages were treated as kin to the princes themselves, and the trust placed in them as bulwarks of the dynasty was considerable.
entries.literal: Yet under the Yuan institution, unless one were a meritorious minister of a hereditary clan or the lord of an enfeoffed state, one could not marry an imperial princess; therefore those generationally joined by marriage to the imperial house were regarded as close as the princes, and the charge entrusted to them as screen and wall of the realm was indeed weighty.

entries.zh: 則其世次，顧可以弗之著耶？
entries.en: Surely their generations ought to be recorded?
entries.literal: As for their lineal generations, how could these fail to be set down?

entries.zh: 且秦漢以來，惟帝姬得號公主，而元則諸王之女亦概稱焉，是又不可不知也。
entries.en: Since Qin and Han times only an emperor's daughter had been called "princess," but under the Yuan the daughters of every prince were styled so as well—a distinction readers should bear in mind.
entries.literal: Moreover, since Qin and Han, only the emperor's daughters were styled princess; yet in Yuan the daughters of all princes were broadly so called—this too must be known.

entries.zh: 惜乎記載弗備，所可見者，僅此而已。
entries.en: Regrettably the records are fragmentary, and only what follows survives.
entries.literal: Alas, the records are incomplete; what can be seen is only this.

entries.zh: 作諸公主表。
entries.en: Hence this table of princesses.
entries.literal: [I therefore] compose the Table of Princesses.

entries.zh: 古者三公之職，寅亮天地，燮理陰陽，以論道經邦者也。
entries.en: In ancient times the Three Ducal Ministers were charged with honoring Heaven and Earth, harmonizing yin and yang, and guiding the realm through discourse on the Way.
entries.literal: In antiquity the office of the Three Ducal Ministers was to honor and illuminate Heaven and Earth, harmonize yin and yang, and discuss the Way to govern the state.

entries.zh: 元初，以太師、太傅、太保為三公，自木華黎國王始為太師，後凡為三公者，皆國之元勳，而漢人則惟劉秉忠嘗為太保，其後鮮有聞矣。
entries.en: Early in the Yuan dynasty the Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, and Grand Guardian constituted the Three Excellencies. Muqali, enfeoffed as king, was the first Grand Preceptor; thereafter every man raised to these three posts was a founding pillar of the realm. Among Han officials only Liu Bingzhong ever held Grand Guardian — and scarcely anyone among the Han after him.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Yuan, the Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, and Grand Guardian were made the Three Ducal Ministers. Starting from King Muqali as Grand Preceptor, thereafter all who became the Three Ducal Ministers were founding meritorious officials of the state; among Han Chinese only Liu Bingzhong once served as Grand Guardian — after that few are heard of.

entries.zh: 其制又有大司徒、司徒、太尉、司空之屬，然其置否不常，人品或混，故置者又或開府不開府焉。
entries.en: The institution also recognized Grand Minister of Education, Minister of Education, Grand Commandant, and Minister of Works, among others; but these offices were not consistently filled, and appointees varied in standing — so some appointees opened a formal bureau and others did not.
entries.literal: The system also had such posts as Grand Minister of Education, Minister of Education, Grand Commandant, and Minister of Works; yet whether they were established was not constant, and the caliber of appointees might be mixed; hence those who were appointed might or might not establish a bureau.

entries.zh: 若夫東宮，亦嘗置三師、三少，而不恒有也。
entries.en: The crown prince's establishment likewise sometimes included the Three Masters and Three Minor Mentors, though these posts were not kept permanently.
entries.literal: As for the Eastern Palace, it also at times had the Three Masters and Three Mentors, but they were not always in place.

entries.zh: 今固不得而悉著之，惟自木華黎而下，得拜三公者若干人，作三公表。
entries.en: A full record of every holder is impossible here; this table lists only those from Muqali onward who were appointed to the three great offices.
entries.literal: Now they cannot all be fully recorded; only from Muqali downward, the several men who received appointment as the Three Ducal Ministers are set forth in the Table of the Three Ducal Ministers.

entries.zh: 太祖光獻翼聖皇后，名孛兒臺旭真，弘吉剌氏，特薛禪之女也。
entries.en: Taizu's empress posthumously titled Guangxian Yisheng was Börte, styled Lady Ujin, of the Kongirat clan and daughter of Dei Sechen.
entries.literal: Taizu's Empress Guangxian Yisheng, named Börte, titled Lady Ujin, of the Kongirat clan, was the daughter of Dei Sechen.

entries.zh: 特薛禪與子按陳從太祖征伐有功，賜號國舅，封王爵，以統其部族。
entries.en: Dei Sechen and his son Anchün served Taizu on campaign with distinction, were granted the title Imperial Uncle and enfeoffed as kings, and were placed over their tribal division.
entries.literal: Dei Sechen and his son Anchün followed Taizu on campaigns with merit; they were granted the title Imperial Uncle, enfeoffed with princely rank, and put in charge of their tribal division.

entries.zh: 有旨：「生女為后，生男尚公主，世世不絕。」
entries.en: An imperial order declared: "Daughters born to this house shall be empresses; sons born shall marry imperial princesses—thus from age to age without end."
entries.literal: An edict declared: "Daughters born shall become empresses; sons born shall marry princesses, generation after generation without end."

entries.zh: 世祖至元二年十二月，追謚光獻翼聖皇后。
entries.en: In the twelfth month of Zhiyuan 2, Kublai posthumously enfeoffed her as Empress Guangxian Yisheng.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Zhiyuan, Shizu posthumously enfeoffed her as Empress Guangxian Yisheng.

entries.zh: 冊文曰：「尊祖宗，致誠孝，實王政之攸先；
entries.en: The enfeoffment text read: "Honoring the ancestors and practicing utmost filial piety are truly the first duties of kingship;
entries.literal: The patent read: "Honoring the ancestors and practicing utmost filial piety are truly foremost in true kingship;

entries.zh: 法天地，建鴻名，亦母儀之克稱。
entries.en: taking heaven and earth as one's model and establishing a great name is likewise what fully befits the standard of a mother of the realm.
entries.literal: Taking heaven and earth as model and establishing a great name is also what fully befits a mother's standard.

entries.zh: 肆先虔於太室，庸昭示於后昆，體茲至公，節以大惠。
entries.en: We therefore first offer sincerity in the Grand Temple, broadly proclaim this to posterity, embody supreme impartiality, and temper it with great grace.
entries.literal: We therefore first offer sincerity in the Grand Temple, broadly proclaim it to posterity, embody this supreme impartiality, and regulate it with great grace.

entries.zh: 欽惟光獻皇后，宅收淵靜，稟德柔嘉，當聖神創業之初，有夙夜求賢之助。
