entries.en: Reverently considering Empress Guangxian, who dwelt in deep stillness and was endowed with gentle excellence: at the beginning of the sage founder's enterprise she lent the aid of laboring through the nights to seek out the worthy.
entries.literal: Reverently considering Empress Guangxian — dwelling in deep stillness, endowed with gentle excellence — at the beginning when the sage founded the enterprise she had the assistance of working through the nights to seek the worthy.

entries.zh: 功施社稷，垂慈訓於景襄；
entries.en: Her merit reached the altars of state; she bestowed kindly instruction upon Jingxiang;
entries.literal: Her merit extended to the altars of state; she bestowed kindly instruction upon Jingxiang;

entries.zh: 慶衍宮闈，流徽音於莊聖。
entries.en: her blessing spread through the inner palace and passed down fine renown to Zhuang Sheng.
entries.literal: Her blessing spread through the palace; she passed down fine fame to Zhuang Sheng.

entries.zh: 協贊龍飛之運，永詒燕翼之謀。
entries.en: She assisted the fortune of the dragon's ascent and forever bequeathed the plan of sheltering the fledglings.
entries.literal: She assisted the fortune of the dragon's flight and forever bequeathed the plan of sheltering the fledglings.

entries.zh: 惟周人著稱《思齊》，亦推本興王之跡；
entries.en: The Zhou gave renown to the 《Si Qi》 and likewise traced their rise back to the founding king;
entries.literal: The Zhou people gave renown to the 《Si Qi》 and also traced back to the traces of the founding king;

entries.zh: 在漢世始謚光烈，蓋篤申追遠之情。
entries.en: in Han they first posthumously titled Guanglie, truly deepening the feeling of honoring those long gone.
entries.literal: In the Han dynasty they first posthumously titled Guanglie, truly deepening the feeling of honoring the remote past.

entries.zh: 是用稽迪舊章，增崇遺美。
entries.en: Therefore we examine and follow the old statutes and augment the praise of her departed excellence.
entries.literal: Therefore we examine and follow the old statutes and augment and exalt her departed excellence.

entries.zh: 謹遣攝太尉某，奉玉冊玉寶，加上尊謚曰光獻翼聖皇后。
entries.en: We respectfully send the Acting Grand Master of Ceremonies to present jade registers and jade seals and add the honorific posthumous title Empress Guangxian Yisheng.
entries.literal: We respectfully send the Acting Grand Master of Ceremonies to present jade registers and jade seals and add the honorific posthumous title Empress Guangxian Yisheng.

entries.zh: 伏惟淑靈降格，典禮備膺，於億萬年，茂隆丕祚。」
entries.en: Humbly: may her pure spirit descend, the rites be fully received, and through ten thousand years your great fortune flourish abundantly."
entries.literal: Humbly considering that her pure spirit descends and the rites are fully received — through ten thousand years may your great fortune flourish abundantly."

entries.zh: 升祔太祖廟。
entries.en: Her tablet was elevated to join Taizu in the ancestral temple.
entries.literal: Her tablet was elevated to join Taizu in the ancestral temple.

entries.zh: 其餘后妃，有四斡耳朵四十餘人，不記氏族，其名悉見於《表》。
entries.en: As for the other empresses and consorts, in the four ordas there were more than forty women whose clans are not recorded; their names all appear in the 《Tables》.
entries.literal: Of the other empresses and consorts, in the four ordas there were more than forty persons whose clans are not recorded; their names all appear in the 《Tables》.

entries.zh: 后皆仿此。
entries.en: The accounts of empresses below all follow this pattern.
entries.literal: Empresses below all follow this model.

entries.zh: 世祖昭睿順聖皇后，名察必，弘吉剌氏，濟寧忠武王按陳之女也。
entries.en: Shizu's Empress Zhaorui Shunsheng was Chabi, of the Kongirat clan and daughter of Anchün, loyal and martial King of Jining.
entries.literal: Shizu's Empress Zhaorui Shunsheng was named Chabi, of the Kongirat clan, daughter of Anchün, loyal and martial King of Jining.

entries.zh: 生裕宗。
entries.en: She bore Yuzong.
entries.literal: She bore Yuzong.

entries.zh: 中統初，立為皇后。
entries.en: At the beginning of Zhongtong she was established as empress.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Zhongtong she was established as empress.

entries.zh: 至元十年三月，授冊寶，上尊號貞懿昭聖順天睿文光應皇后。
entries.en: In the third month of Zhiyuan 10 she received registers and seals and was given the honorific title Empress Zhenyi Zhaosheng Shuntian Ruìwen Guangying.
entries.literal: In the third month of the tenth year of Zhiyuan she was invested with registers and seals and given the honorific title Empress Zhenyi Zhaosheng Shuntian Ruìwen Guangying.

entries.zh: 一日，四怯薛官奏割京城外近地牧馬，帝既允，方以圖進。
entries.en: One day an official of the four keshig memorialized to allot nearby land outside the capital for pasturing horses; the emperor had already assented and the map was about to be submitted.
entries.literal: One day an official of the four keshig memorialized to allot nearby land outside the capital for pasturing horses; the emperor had already assented and the map was just being presented.

entries.zh: 后至帝前，將諫，先陽責太保劉秉忠曰：「汝漢人聰明者，言則帝聽，汝何為不諫？
entries.en: The empress came before the emperor intending to remonstrate; she first openly rebuked Grand Guardian Liu Bingzhong: "You are a clever Han man, and when you speak the emperor listens — why did you not remonstrate?
entries.literal: The empress came before the emperor intending to remonstrate; she first openly rebuked Grand Guardian Liu Bingzhong, saying: "You are a clever Han man — when you speak the emperor listens; why did you not remonstrate?

entries.zh: 向初到定都時，若以地牧馬則可，今軍蘸俱分業已定，奪之可乎？」
entries.en: When we first chose the site for the capital, grazing there would have been fine; but now the military households and postal stations have all been assigned their occupations — can we take the land away?"
entries.literal: When we first chose the site for the capital, grazing there would have been acceptable; now the military households and postal stations have all been assigned their occupations — can we take the land away?"

entries.zh: 帝默然，命寢其事。
entries.en: The emperor fell silent and ordered the matter shelved.
entries.literal: The emperor was silent and ordered the matter shelved.

entries.zh: 后嘗於太府監支繒帛表裏各一，帝謂后曰：「此軍國所需，非私家物，后何可得支？」
entries.en: The empress once drew from the Directorate of Palace Supplies one bolt each of outer and lining silk; the emperor told her, "These are needed for army and state, not private goods — how can the empress draw on them?"
entries.literal: The empress once drew from the Directorate of Palace Supplies one bolt each of outer and lining silk; the emperor said to her: "These are needed for army and state, not private goods — how can the empress draw them?"

entries.zh: 后自是率宮人親執女工，拘諸舊弓弦練之，緝為綢，以為衣，其韌密比綾綺。
entries.en: From then on the empress led the palace women in needlework herself, collected old bowstrings and boiled them down, wove them into cloth, and made garments whose toughness and density rivaled damask.
entries.literal: From then on the empress led the palace women in doing needlework herself, collected old bowstrings and boiled them, wove them into silk, and made clothing; its toughness and density rivaled damask.

entries.zh: 宣徽院羊臑皮置不用，后取之，合縫為地毯。
entries.en: Sheep-flank hides set aside unused by the Xuanhui Court she took and stitched together into carpets.
entries.literal: Sheep-flank hides set aside unused by the Xuanhui Court she took and stitched together into carpets.

entries.zh: 其勤儉有節而無棄物，類如此。
entries.en: Her diligence, thrift, and refusal to waste usable materials were all of this kind.
entries.literal: Her diligence, thrift, and restraint without discarding usable things were all of this kind.

entries.zh: 十三年，平宋，幼主朝於上都。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year Song was pacified and the young Song ruler came to court at Shangdu.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year Song was pacified and the young ruler came to court at Shangdu.

entries.zh: 大宴，眾皆歡甚，唯后不樂。
entries.en: At a great banquet everyone was exceedingly joyful; only the empress was not pleased.
entries.literal: At a great banquet all were exceedingly joyful; only the empress was not pleased.

entries.zh: 帝曰：「我今平江南，自此不用兵甲，眾人皆喜，爾獨不樂，何耶？」
entries.en: The emperor said, "I have now pacified the south; from this time forth we need no more arms and armor; everyone is pleased — you alone are not. Why?"
entries.literal: The emperor said: "I have now pacified Jiangnan; from this time forth we need no more arms and armor; everyone is pleased — you alone are not pleased; why?"

entries.zh: 后跪奏曰：「妾聞自古無千歲之國，毋使吾子孫及此，則幸矣。」
entries.en: The empress knelt and said, "Your servant has heard that from antiquity no state has lasted a thousand years; if only our sons and grandsons do not come to this, it will be fortune enough."
entries.literal: The empress knelt and memorialized: "Your servant has heard that from antiquity there has been no state of a thousand years; if only our sons and grandsons do not come to this, it will be fortunate enough."

entries.zh: 帝以宋府庫故物各聚置殿庭上，召后視之，后遍視即去。
entries.en: The emperor had the old goods from the Song treasury gathered in the palace courtyard and summoned the empress to view them; she looked them all over and left at once.
entries.literal: The emperor had the old goods from the Song treasury all gathered and set out in the palace courtyard and summoned the empress to view them; she looked them all over and left at once.

entries.zh: 帝遣宦者追問后，欲何所取。
entries.en: The emperor sent a eunuch after the empress to ask what she wished to take.
entries.literal: The emperor sent a eunuch after the empress to ask what she wished to take.

entries.zh: 后曰：「宋人貯蓄以遺其子孫，子孫不能守，而歸於我，我何忍取一物耶！」
entries.en: The empress said, "The Song stored these up for their sons and grandsons; their sons and grandsons could not keep them, and they have come to us — how could I bear to take a single thing!"
entries.literal: The empress said: "The Song people stored these up to bequeath to their sons and grandsons; their sons and grandsons could not keep them, and they have come to us — how could I bear to take a single thing!"

entries.zh: 時宋太后全氏至京，不習北方風土，后為奏令回江南。
entries.en: At that time Empress Dowager Quan of Song had come to the capital and was unaccustomed to the northern climate; the empress memorialized to have her sent back to the south.
entries.literal: At that time Empress Dowager Quan of Song had come to the capital and was unaccustomed to the northern climate; the empress memorialized to have her sent back to Jiangnan.

entries.zh: 帝不允，至三奏，帝乃答曰：「爾婦人無遠慮，若使之南還，或浮言一動，即廢其家，非所以愛之也。
entries.en: The emperor did not consent; after three memorials he answered, "You women lack far-sightedness; if we sent her south, a single rumor might at once bring ruin on her house — that is not how to show love.
entries.literal: The emperor did not consent; after three memorials he answered: "You women lack far-sightedness; if we sent her south, a single floating rumor might at once bring ruin on her house — that is not how to love her.

entries.zh: 茍能愛之，時加存恤，使之便安可也。」
entries.en: If we truly love her, we need only show care and relief from time to time and make her comfortable — that will suffice."
entries.literal: If we can love her, from time to time show care and relief and make her comfortable, that will suffice."

entries.zh: 后退，益厚待之。
entries.en: The empress withdrew and treated her all the more generously.
entries.literal: The empress withdrew and treated her all the more generously.

entries.zh: 胡帽舊無前檐，帝因射日色炫目，以語后，后即益前檐。
entries.en: Mongol caps formerly had no front brim; while shooting the emperor found the sunlight dazzling and told the empress, who at once added a front brim.
entries.literal: Mongol caps formerly had no front brim; the emperor, while shooting, found the sunlight dazzling and told the empress; she at once added a front brim.

entries.zh: 帝大喜，遂命為式。
entries.en: The emperor was greatly pleased and ordered it made the standard pattern.
entries.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and ordered it made the standard pattern.

entries.zh: 又制一衣，前有裳無衽，后長倍於前，亦無領袖，綴以兩襻，名曰比甲，以便弓馬，時皆仿之。
entries.en: She also devised a garment with a skirt panel in front but no overlapping lapel, the back twice as long as the front and likewise without collar or sleeves, fastened with two loops and called a bijia, to facilitate archery and horsemanship; everyone at the time copied it.
entries.literal: She also devised a garment with a skirt in front but no overlapping lapel, the back twice as long as the front, likewise without collar or sleeves, fastened with two loops — called a bijia — to facilitate archery and horsemanship; all at the time copied it.

entries.zh: 后性明敏，達於事機，國家初政，左右匡正，當時與有力焉。
entries.en: The empress was intelligent and clear by nature and adept at affairs; in the founding government of the state she corrected matters on every side, and at the time she wielded real influence.
entries.literal: The empress was by nature intelligent and clear, adept at affairs; in the founding government of the state she corrected matters left and right, and at the time she had real force.

entries.zh: 十八年二月崩。
entries.en: She died in the second month of the eighteenth year.
entries.literal: She died in the second month of the eighteenth year.

entries.zh: 三十一年，成宗即位，五月，追謚昭睿順聖皇后，其冊文曰：「奉先思孝，臣子之至情；
entries.en: In the thirty-first year Chengzong took the throne; in the fifth month she was posthumously enfeoffed as Empress Zhaorui Shunsheng. The enfeoffment text read: "Serving the former and thinking of filial piety are the utmost feeling of subject and child;
entries.literal: In the thirty-first year Chengzong took the throne; in the fifth month she was posthumously enfeoffed as Empress Zhaorui Shunsheng; the patent read: "Serving the former and thinking of filial piety are the utmost feeling of subject and child;

entries.zh: 節惠易名，古今之大典。
entries.en: restraining grace during mourning and changing names are the great statutes of antiquity and today.
entries.literal: Restraining grace and changing names are the great statutes of antiquity and today.

entries.zh: 惟殷娥有明德之號，而周任著《思齊》之稱。
entries.en: Yin E bore the title of Bright Virtue, and Zhou Ren gave renown to the 《Si Qi》.
entries.literal: Yin E had the title of Bright Virtue, and Zhou Ren gave renown to the 《Si Qi》.

entries.zh: 爰考舊章，式崇尊諡。
entries.en: We therefore examine the old statutes and exalt the honorific posthumous title.
entries.literal: We therefore examine the old statutes and exalt the honorific posthumous title.

entries.zh: 恭惟先皇后，厚德載物，正位承天。
entries.en: Reverently considering the late empress: her thick virtue bore all things; she took the correct position and received heaven.
entries.literal: Reverently considering the late empress: her thick virtue bore all things; she took the correct position and received heaven.

entries.zh: 隆內治於公宮，綱大倫於天下。
entries.en: She elevated inner governance in the palace and set the great bonds in order throughout the realm.
entries.literal: She elevated inner governance in the public palace and set the great bonds in order throughout the realm.

entries.zh: 曩事龍潛之邸，及乘虎變之秋。
entries.en: Long ago she served in the lodge of the hidden dragon; when the season of the tiger's transformation came she was there.
entries.literal: Long ago she served in the lodge of the hidden dragon; when the tiger's transformation came in autumn she was there.

entries.zh: 鄂渚班師，洞識事機之會；
entries.en: When the army withdrew at Ezhou she deeply understood the moment of opportunity;
entries.literal: When the army withdrew at Ezhou she deeply understood the moment of opportunity;

entries.zh: 上都踐祚，居多輔佐之謀。
entries.en: when the throne was taken at Shangdu she largely supplied plans of assistance.
entries.literal: when the throne was taken at Shangdu she largely supplied plans of assistance.

entries.zh: 先物之明，獨斷於衷；
entries.en: Foreknowledge of things — she alone decided in her heart;
entries.literal: Foreknowledge of things — she alone decided in her heart;

entries.zh: 進賢之志，允葉於上。
entries.en: her will to advance the worthy truly accorded with her lord above.
entries.literal: her will to advance the worthy truly accorded with her lord above.

entries.zh: 左右我聖祖，建帝王之極功；
entries.en: She assisted our sage ancestor and established the utmost merit of emperors and kings;
entries.literal: She assisted our sage ancestor and established the utmost merit of emperors and kings;

entries.zh: 撫育我前人，嗣社稷之重托。
entries.en: she nurtured our forebear and succeeded to the heavy charge of the altars of state.
entries.literal: she nurtured our forebear and succeeded to the heavy charge of the altars of state.

entries.zh: 臣下之勸勞灼見，生民之疾苦周知。
entries.en: The toil and merit of officials were clearly seen; the suffering of the people was fully known.
entries.literal: The toil and merit of officials were clearly seen; the suffering of the people was fully known.

entries.zh: 儷宸極二十年，垂慈範千萬世。
entries.en: She matched the apex of heaven for twenty years and bestowed a model of kindness for ten thousand generations.
entries.literal: She matched the apex of heaven for twenty years and bestowed a model of kindness for ten thousand generations.

entries.zh: 惟全美聖而益聖，宜顯冊書而屢書。
entries.en: Only when fully beautiful in sagehood and ever more sage should registers be displayed and written again and again.
entries.literal: Only when fully beautiful in sagehood and ever more sage should registers be displayed and written again and again.

entries.zh: 不勝惓藐懇懇之誠，敬展尊尊親親之義，以揚盛烈，以對耿光。
entries.en: With insupportable earnest devotion we respectfully unfold the principle of honoring the honored and cherishing the near, to exalt the great achievement and answer the bright glory.
entries.literal: With insupportable earnest and sincere devotion we respectfully unfold the principle of honoring the honored and cherishing the near, to exalt the great achievement and answer the bright glory.

entries.zh: 謹遣某官某奉玉冊玉寶，上尊謚曰昭睿順聖皇后。
entries.en: We respectfully send an official to present jade registers and jade seals and bestow the honorific posthumous title Empress Zhaorui Shunsheng.
entries.literal: We respectfully send an official to present jade registers and jade seals and bestow the honorific posthumous title Empress Zhaorui Shunsheng.

entries.zh: 欽惟淑靈在天，明鑒逮下。
entries.en: Reverently: may her pure spirit be in heaven and her bright mirror reach below.
entries.literal: Reverently considering that her pure spirit is in heaven, her bright mirror reaches below.

entries.zh: 增輝煒管，茂揚徽懿之音；
entries.en: Add radiance to the brilliant pipes; abundantly raise the sound of fine virtue;
entries.literal: Add radiance to the brilliant pipes; abundantly raise the sound of fine virtue;

entries.zh: 合饗太宮，益衍壽昌之福。」
entries.en: join in offering at the Grand Temple and further extend the blessing of long life and prosperity."
entries.literal: join in offering at the Grand Temple and further extend the blessing of long life and prosperity."

entries.zh: 升祔世祖廟。
entries.en: Her tablet was elevated to join Shizu in the ancestral temple.
entries.literal: Her tablet was elevated to join Shizu in the ancestral temple.

entries.zh: 南必皇后，弘吉剌氏，納陳孫仙童之女也。
entries.en: Empress Nanbi, of the Kongirat clan, was the daughter of Xiantong, grandson of Nachin.
entries.literal: Empress Nanbi, of the Kongirat clan, was the daughter of Xiantong, grandson of Nachin.

entries.zh: 至元二十年，納為皇后，繼守正宮。
entries.en: In Zhiyuan 20 she was taken in as empress and succeeded to the principal palace.
entries.literal: In the twentieth year of Zhiyuan she was taken in as empress and succeeded in guarding the principal palace.

entries.zh: 時世祖春秋高，頗預政，相臣常不得見帝，輒因后奏事焉。
entries.en: At that time Kublai was advanced in years and the empress often participated in government; chief ministers frequently could not see the emperor and would present affairs through the empress instead.
entries.literal: At that time Shizu was advanced in years and the empress often participated in government; chief ministers frequently could not see the emperor and would present affairs through the empress.

entries.zh: 有子一人，名鐵蔑赤。
entries.en: She had one son, named Temürchik.
entries.literal: She had one son, named Temürchik.

entries.zh: 后妃一
entries.en: Empresses and Consorts I
entries.literal: Empresses and Consorts I

entries.zh: 五月，太宗不豫。
entries.en: In the fifth month Taizong fell ill.
entries.literal: In the fifth month Taizong fell ill.

entries.zh: 六月，疾甚。
entries.en: In the sixth month his illness grew severe.
entries.literal: In the sixth month his illness grew severe.

entries.zh: 拖雷禱於天地，請以身代之，又取巫覡祓除釁滌之水飲焉。
entries.en: Tolui prayed to Heaven and Earth, offering to take the illness upon himself, and also drank the exorcism and purification water prepared by shamans.
entries.literal: Tolui prayed to Heaven and Earth, asking to substitute his own body, and also took water of exorcism and purification from shamans and drank it.

entries.zh: 居數日，太宗疾愈，拖雷從之北還，至阿剌合的思之地，遇疾而薨，壽四十有
entries.en: Several days later Taizong recovered. Tolui accompanied him on the return north, but at Alaqadesi he fell ill and died at the age of forty-
entries.literal: After several days Taizong's illness abated; Tolui accompanied him on the return north; when they reached the land of Alaqadesi he fell ill and died, aged forty-

entries.en: Text lacuna in the manuscript.
entries.literal: Text lacuna in the manuscript.

entries.zh: 妃怯烈氏。
entries.en: His consort was of the Kereit clan.
entries.literal: His consort was of the Kereit clan.

entries.zh: 子十一人，長憲宗，次四則世祖也。
entries.en: He had eleven sons; the eldest was Xianzong, and the fourth was Shizu.
entries.literal: He had eleven sons; the eldest was Xianzong, and the fourth was Shizu.

entries.zh: 憲宗立，追謚曰英武皇帝，廟號睿宗。
entries.en: When Xianzong ascended the throne, he posthumously styled him the Emperor Yingwu with the temple name Ruizong.
entries.literal: When Xianzong took the throne he posthumously styled him the Emperor Yingwu with temple name Ruizong.

entries.zh: 二年，合祭昊天后土，以太祖、睿宗配享。
entries.en: In the second year, at the joint sacrifice to Heaven and Earth, Taizu and Ruizong were enshrined as spirit partners.
entries.literal: In the second year, in the joint sacrifice to Haotian and Houtu, Taizu and Ruizong were paired in worship.

entries.zh: 世祖至元二年，改謚景襄皇帝。
entries.en: In Shizu's second Zhiyuan year the posthumous title was changed to the Emperor Jingxiang.
entries.literal: In the second year of Shizu's Zhiyuan reign the posthumous title was changed to the Emperor Jingxiang.

entries.zh: 裕宗文惠明孝皇帝，諱真金，世祖嫡子也。
entries.en: Yuzong, the Emperor Wenhui Mingxiao, bore the personal name Zhenjin and was Shizu's son by the principal wife.
entries.literal: Yuzong, the Emperor Wenhui Mingxiao — taboo name Zhenjin — was Shizu's son by the principal wife.

entries.zh: 母昭睿順聖皇后，弘吉烈氏。
entries.en: His mother was Empress Zhaorui Shunsheng of the Onggirat.
entries.literal: His mother was Empress Zhaorui Shunsheng of the Onggirat clan.

entries.zh: 少從姚樞、竇默受《孝經》，及終卷，世祖大悅，設食饗樞等。
entries.en: In his youth he studied the Classic of Filial Piety under Yao Shu and Dou Mo. When he finished the text, Shizu was delighted and gave a feast in their honor.
entries.literal: In youth he studied the Classic of Filial Piety under Yao Shu and Dou Mo; when he finished the text Shizu was greatly pleased and set out a feast to honor Shu and the others.

entries.zh: 中統三年，封燕王，守中書令。
entries.en: In the third Zhongtong year he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yan and appointed Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: In the third year of Zhongtong he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yan and held the post of Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 丞相史天澤入啟事，王曰：「我幼，未嘗習祖宗典則，閑於政體，一旦當大任，惟汝耆德賴焉。」
entries.en: When Grand Councilor Shi Tianze came in to report affairs, the prince said, "I am young, have never studied our ancestral regulations, and know little of government. To be given such a great responsibility all at once, I must rely on your seasoned wisdom."
entries.literal: Grand Councilor Shi Tianze entered to report affairs; the Prince said: "I am young, have never studied the ancestral regulations, and am unskilled in the forms of government; suddenly to bear a great charge — I rely only on your aged virtue."

entries.zh: 復諭贊善王恂曰：「省臣所啟，等國事也。
entries.en: He also told his tutor Wang Xun, "What the Secretariat ministers report is state business.
entries.literal: He also instructed the tutor Wang Xun: "What the provincial ministers report is equal to state affairs.

entries.zh: 爾宜入與聞之。」
entries.en: You should attend and hear it yourself."
entries.literal: You ought to enter and take part in hearing it."

entries.zh: 四年，兼判樞密院事。
entries.en: In the fourth year he was also made concurrent administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he also concurrently adjudicated Bureau of Military Affairs affairs.

entries.zh: 至元初，省臣奏請王署敕，每月必再至中書。
entries.en: Early in the Zhiyuan period the Secretariat ministers memorialized that the prince should countersign edicts and attend the Secretariat twice each month.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Zhiyuan the provincial ministers memorialized that the Prince should countersign edicts and must come twice each month to the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 於是王將入中書，乳母進新衣，笑卻之曰：「吾何事美觀也。」
entries.en: As the prince was about to enter the Secretariat, his wet nurse brought him new clothes. He smiled and refused them, saying, "Why should I dress for show?"
entries.literal: When the Prince was about to enter the Secretariat his wet nurse brought new clothes; he smiled and refused them, saying: "Why should I dress for show?"

entries.zh: 嘗從幸宜興，世祖違豫，憂形於色，夕不能寐。
entries.en: Once when he accompanied Shizu to Yixing and Shizu fell ill, his worry showed plainly on his face and he could not sleep at night.
entries.literal: Once when he accompanied the emperor on a visit to Yixing, Shizu fell ill; worry showed on his face and at night he could not sleep.

entries.zh: 聞母皇后暴得風疾，即悲泣，衣不及帶而行。
entries.en: When he heard that the empress mother had suddenly suffered a stroke, he wept and set out without even fastening his belt.
entries.literal: Hearing that the empress mother had suddenly taken a wind ailment, he wept in grief and went without fastening his belt.

entries.zh: 七年秋，受詔巡撫稱海，至冬還京。
entries.en: In the autumn of the seventh year he received orders to tour and pacify Cheng-hai and returned to the capital by winter.
entries.literal: In autumn of the seventh year he received an edict to tour and pacify Cheng-hai; by winter he returned to the capital.

entries.zh: 間謂諸王劄剌忽及從官伯顏等曰：「吾屬適有茲暇，宜各悉乃心，慎言所守，俾吾聞之。」
entries.en: In the interval he said to Prince Zhalaqu and the attendant officials Bayan and others, "We happen to have this leisure. Each of you should speak frankly and carefully about what you uphold, so that I may hear it."
entries.literal: In an interval he said to Prince Zhalaqu and the attendant officials Bayan and others: "We happen to have this leisure; each of you should lay open your hearts, speak carefully of what you uphold, and let me hear it."

entries.zh: 於是撒裏蠻曰：「太祖有訓：欲治身，先治心；
entries.en: Sariman then said, "Taizu taught: to govern yourself, first govern your mind;
entries.literal: Thereupon Sariman said: "Taizu had an instruction: to govern the person, first govern the mind;

entries.zh: 欲責人，先責己。」
entries.en: to blame others, first blame yourself."
entries.literal: to blame others, first blame oneself."

entries.zh: 伯顏曰：「皇上有訓：欺罔盜竊，人之至惡。
entries.en: Bayan said, "The Emperor taught: deceit and theft are the worst of human faults.
entries.literal: Bayan said: "The Emperor had an instruction: deceit and theft are the utmost evils among men.

entries.zh: 一為欺罔，則後雖出善言，人終弗信；
entries.en: Once you deceive, even good words afterward will never be believed;
entries.literal: Once one has practiced deceit, afterward even if one speaks good words people in the end will not believe;

entries.zh: 一為盜竊，則事雖未覺，心常惴惴，若捕者將至。」
entries.en: once you steal, even if the deed is undiscovered your heart stays fearful, as though the pursuer were about to arrive."
entries.literal: once one has stolen, though the matter is not yet discovered the heart is constantly fearful, as if the catcher were about to arrive."

entries.zh: 劄剌忽曰：「我祖有訓：長者梢，深者底。
entries.en: Zhalaqu said, "My ancestor taught: what is long has its tip; what is deep has its bottom.
entries.literal: Zhalaqu said: "My ancestor had an instruction: what is long has a tip; what is deep has a bottom.

entries.zh: 蓋言貴有終始，長必極其杪，深必究其底，不可中輟也。」
entries.en: This means one must see things through: what is long must reach its end, what is deep must be traced to the bottom, and one must not stop halfway."
entries.literal: This means to value having beginning and end — what is long must reach its extremity, what is deep must probe its bottom; one must not break off midway."

entries.zh: 王曰：「皇上有訓：毋持大心。
entries.en: The prince said, "The Emperor taught: do not harbor grand ambitions.
entries.literal: The Prince said: "The Emperor had an instruction: do not harbor a great heart.

entries.zh: 大心一持，事即隳敗。
entries.en: Once grand ambitions take hold, affairs are ruined at once.
entries.literal: Once a great heart is held, affairs at once are ruined.

entries.zh: 吾觀孔子之語，即與聖訓合也。」
entries.en: When I read Confucius, his words match the sage's instructions."
entries.literal: When I observe Confucius's words, they accord with the sage's instructions."

entries.zh: 至王恂陳說尤多，事見恂傳。
entries.en: Wang Xun spoke at even greater length; see his biography for the details.
entries.literal: As for Wang Xun, his statements were especially numerous; the matter is seen in Xun's biography.

entries.zh: 太子嘗有疾，世祖臨幸，親和藥以賜之。
entries.en: When the crown prince fell ill, Shizu visited him in person and mixed medicine himself to give him.
entries.literal: The Crown Prince once fell ill; Shizu visited in person and mixed medicine himself to bestow it.

entries.zh: 遣侍臣李眾馳祀嶽瀆名山川，太子戒其所至郡邑，毋煩吏迎送，重擾民也。
entries.en: He sent the attendant minister Li Zhong to sacrifice at famous mountains and rivers. The crown prince warned the districts he passed through not to trouble officials with welcoming parties, lest the people be burdened again.
entries.literal: He sent the attendant minister Li Zhong to gallop and sacrifice at famous mountains and rivers; the Crown Prince warned the commanderies and districts he reached not to trouble officials with welcoming and escorting, lest the people be burdened again.

entries.zh: 詔以侍衛親軍萬人益隸東宮，太子命王慶端、董士亨選其驍勇者，教以兵法，時閱試焉。
entries.en: An edict added ten thousand palace guards to the Eastern Palace. The crown prince had Wang Qingduan and Dong Shiheng select the bravest men, taught them military tactics, and reviewed them regularly.
entries.literal: An edict added ten thousand personal guards of the palace to the Eastern Palace; the Crown Prince ordered Wang Qingduan and Dong Shiheng to select the bravest, taught them military methods, and from time to time reviewed them.

entries.zh: 太子服綾袷，為瀋所漬，命侍臣重加染治，侍臣請織綾更制之，太子曰：「吾欲織百端，非難也。
entries.en: The crown prince's lined gauze robe was stained with sweat, and he ordered his attendants to have it dyed again. They asked to weave a new robe instead. He said, "If I wanted a hundred bolts of gauze, that would not be difficult.
entries.literal: The Crown Prince wore a lined gauze robe that was stained by perspiration; he ordered attendants to dye it again. The attendants asked to weave new gauze and make another; the Crown Prince said: "If I wished to weave a hundred bolts, it would not be difficult.

entries.zh: 顧是物未敝，豈宜棄之。」
entries.en: But this garment is not yet worn out. How can I discard it?"
entries.literal: But this thing is not yet worn out — how should it be discarded?"

entries.zh: 東宮香殿成，工請鑿石為池，如曲水流觴故事。
entries.en: When the Eastern Palace incense hall was completed, the craftsmen asked to carve a stone pool in the manner of the floating-cup stream banquet.
entries.literal: When the Eastern Palace incense hall was completed, the craftsmen asked to carve stone into a pool after the old story of the winding stream and floating cup.

entries.zh: 太子曰：「古有肉林酒池，爾欲吾效之耶！」
entries.en: The crown prince said, "In antiquity there were meat forests and wine pools. Do you want me to imitate them!"
entries.literal: The Crown Prince said: "In antiquity there were meat forests and wine pools — do you want me to imitate them!"

entries.zh: 不許。
entries.en: He refused.
entries.literal: He did not permit it.

entries.zh: 每與諸王近臣習射之暇，輒講論經典，若《資治通鑒》、《貞觀政要》，王恂、許衡所述遼、金帝王行事要略，下至《武經》等書，從容片言之間，茍有允愜，未嘗不為之灑然改容。
entries.en: In intervals from archery practice with the princes and close ministers, he would discuss the classics, from Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance and Essentials of Government in the Zhenguan Reign to Wang Xun and Xu Heng's summaries of Liao and Jin rulers and even Military Classics. An apt remark would always make him brighten visibly.
entries.literal: Whenever he had leisure from practicing archery with the princes and close ministers, he would discuss the classics — such as Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Essentials of Government in the Zhenguan Reign, the summaries of Liao and Jin imperial conduct narrated by Wang Xun and Xu Heng, down to books such as Military Classics — and in a relaxed remark, if anything was apt and pleasing, he never failed to change expression with sudden clarity.

entries.zh: 時侍經幄者，如王恂、白棟皆朝夕不出東宮，而待制李謙、太常宋瑽尤加咨訪，蓋無間也。
entries.en: Those who attended his study sessions, such as Wang Xun and Bai Dong, scarcely left the Eastern Palace from morning to night, while Awaiting Draft Li Qian and Director of Ceremonies Song Cong were consulted especially often.
entries.literal: Those who attended the classics curtain at the time, such as Wang Xun and Bai Dong, morning and evening did not leave the Eastern Palace; while Awaiting Draft Li Qian and Director of Ceremonies Song Cong were especially consulted — there was virtually no interval.

entries.zh: 十年二月，立為皇太子，仍兼中書令，判樞密院事。
entries.en: In the second month of the tenth year he was installed as crown prince, while retaining the posts of Director of the Secretariat and administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
entries.literal: In the second month of the tenth year he was established as Crown Prince, still concurrently Director of the Secretariat and adjudicating Bureau of Military Affairs affairs.

entries.zh: 受玉冊：「皇帝若曰：咨爾皇太子真金，仰惟太祖皇帝遺訓，嫡子中有克嗣服繼統者，豫選定之。
entries.en: He received the jade register: "The Emperor speaks: Crown Prince Zhenjin, in accordance with Taizu's testament, among the sons of the principal wife, whoever is fit to succeed and continue the line should be chosen in advance.
entries.literal: He received the jade register: "The Emperor says: Consult you, Crown Prince Zhenjin — looking up to Taizu Emperor's testament, among sons by the principal wife, whoever can succeed in bearing the succession and continue the line, select and fix him beforehand.

entries.zh: 是用立太宗英文皇帝，以紹隆丕構。
entries.en: For this reason Taizong, the Emperor Yingwen, was established to carry on the great foundation.
entries.literal: Therefore Taizong, the Emperor Yingwen, was established to continue and exalt the great foundation.

entries.zh: 自時厥後，為不顯立冢嫡，遂啟爭端。
entries.en: From that time on, because the principal heir was not clearly designated, strife arose.
entries.literal: From that time onward, because the eldest son of the principal wife was not clearly established, strife was thereby opened.

entries.zh: 朕上遵祖宗宏規，下協昆弟僉同之議，乃從燕邸，即立爾為皇太子，積有日矣。
entries.en: I have followed our ancestors' great regulations above and my brothers' unanimous agreement below, and so, from the Yan residence, I established you as crown prince some time ago.
entries.literal: I, above, follow the ancestors' great regulations; below, I harmonize with my brothers' unanimous agreement — thus from the Yan residence I at once established you as Crown Prince; days have accumulated.

entries.zh: 比者儒臣敷奏，國家定立儲嗣，宜有冊命，此典禮也。
entries.en: Recently the Confucian ministers have memorialized that when the state formally establishes the heir, there should be an investiture decree; this is proper ritual.
entries.literal: Recently Confucian ministers have presented memorials: when the state fixes and establishes the heir, there ought to be investiture — this is ritual propriety.

entries.zh: 今遣攝太尉、左丞相伯顏持節授爾玉冊金寶。
entries.en: I now send Acting Grand Commandant and Left Grand Councilor Bayan, bearing credentials, to confer upon you the jade register and golden seal.
entries.literal: Now I send Acting Grand Commandant and Left Grand Councilor Bayan, bearing credentials, to confer upon you the jade register and golden seal.

entries.zh: 於戲！
entries.en: Alas!
entries.literal: Alas!

entries.zh: 聖武燕謀，爾其承奉。
entries.en: Uphold the sage's martial prowess and the founding designs of Yan.
entries.literal: The sage's martial prowess and Yan's stratagems — you must inherit and uphold them.

entries.zh: 昆弟宗親，爾其和協。
entries.en: Live in harmony with your brothers and kinsmen.
entries.literal: Brothers and clan kin — you must harmonize with them.

entries.zh: 使仁孝顯於躬行，抑可謂不負所托矣。
entries.en: Let benevolence and filial piety show in your own conduct, and you will not fail what has been entrusted to you.
entries.literal: Let benevolence and filial piety show in your personal conduct — then one may say you have not failed what was entrusted.

entries.zh: 尚其戒哉，勿替朕命。」
entries.en: Take heed, and do not neglect my command."
entries.literal: Take heed and be warned; do not neglect my command."

entries.zh: 九月丙戌，詔立宮師府，設官屬三十有八員。
entries.en: On the bingxu day of the ninth month an edict established the Palace Tutorate with thirty-eight staff posts.
entries.literal: On the bingxu day of the ninth month an edict established the Palace Tutorate with thirty-eight staff posts.

entries.zh: 起處士楊恭懿於京兆。
entries.en: The scholar Yang Gongyi was summoned from Jingzhao.
entries.literal: The reclusive gentleman Yang Gongyi was summoned from Jingzhao.

entries.zh: 二十年春，辟劉因於保定，因以疾辭，固辟之，乃至，拜右贊善大夫，以吏部郎中夾谷之奇為左贊善大夫。
entries.en: In the spring of the twentieth year he recruited Liu Yin from Baoding. Yin declined on grounds of illness, but when recruitment was pressed he came and was appointed Right Tutor, with Ministry of Personnel Director Jiagu Zhiqi as Left Tutor.
entries.literal: In spring of the twentieth year he recruited Liu Yin from Baoding; Yin declined on grounds of illness, but when recruitment was pressed he came; he was appointed Right Tutor, with Ministry of Personnel Director Jiagu Zhiqi as Left Tutor.

entries.zh: 是時已立國子學，李棟、宋瑽、李謙皆以東宮僚友，繼典教事，至是，命因專領之，而以瑽等仍備咨訪。
entries.en: By then the National University had been established. Li Dong, Song Cong, and Li Qian, all friends of the Eastern Palace, had successively directed instruction. Now he ordered Yin to take sole charge while Cong and the others still served for consultation.
entries.literal: By then the National University had been established; Li Dong, Song Cong, and Li Qian, all friends of the Eastern Palace, successively directed instruction; at this time he ordered Yin to take sole charge, while Cong and the others still served for consultation.

entries.zh: 嘗曰：「吾聞金章宗時，有司論太學生廩費太多，章宗謂養出一範文正公，所償顧豈少哉。
entries.en: He once said, "I hear that under Jin Emperor Zhangzong, officials said National University students' stipends were too costly. Zhangzong replied that nurturing one Fan Zhongyan repaid the cost.
entries.literal: He once said: "I hear that under Jin Emperor Zhangzong, officials discussed that National University students' stipends were too great; Zhangzong said that nurturing one Fan Zhongyan repaid the cost — his words were very good.

entries.zh: 其言甚善。」
entries.en: His words were excellent."
entries.literal: His words were very good."

entries.zh: 會因復以疾乞去。
entries.en: When Yin again begged leave on grounds of illness.
entries.literal: When Yin again begged leave on grounds of illness.

entries.zh: 二十二年，以長史耶律有尚為國子司業。
entries.en: In the twenty-second year Ye Lü Youshang was made National University Vice Director.
entries.literal: In the twenty-second year Ye Lü Youshang was made National University Vice Director.

entries.zh: 中庶子伯必以其子阿八赤入見，諭令入學，伯必即令其子入蒙古學。
entries.en: Junior Mentor Bo Bi brought his son Abachi to audience. The crown prince instructed him to enter study, and Bo Bi at once sent his son into Mongolian study.
entries.literal: Junior Mentor Bo Bi brought his son Abachi to audience; the Crown Prince instructed him to enter study; Bo Bi at once sent his son into Mongolian study.

entries.zh: 逾年又見，太子問讀何書，其子以蒙古書對，太子曰：「我命汝學漢人文字耳，其亟入胄監。」
entries.en: More than a year later he saw him again and asked what book he was reading. The son answered that he was reading Mongolian writing. The crown prince said, "I ordered you to study Chinese writing. Enter the Imperial College at once."
entries.literal: More than a year later he saw him again; the Crown Prince asked what book he was reading; the son answered that he was reading Mongolian writing; the Crown Prince said: "I ordered you to study Chinese writing — enter the Imperial College at once."

entries.zh: 遣使辟宋工部侍郎倪堅於開元，既至，訪以古今成敗得失，堅對言：「三代得天下以仁，其失也以不仁。
entries.en: He sent envoys to recruit Song Ministry of Works Vice Minister Ni Jian from Kaiyuan. When Jian arrived he was asked about success and failure through the ages. Jian replied, "The Three Dynasties gained the realm through benevolence and lost it through lack of benevolence.
entries.literal: He sent envoys to recruit Song Ministry of Works Vice Minister Ni Jian from Kaiyuan; when Jian arrived he was asked about success and failure through the ages; Jian replied: "The Three Dynasties gained the realm through benevolence and lost it through lack of benevolence.

entries.zh: 漢、唐之亡也，以外戚閹豎。
entries.en: Han and Tang fell through maternal kin and eunuchs.
entries.literal: The fall of Han and Tang was through maternal kin and eunuchs.

entries.zh: 宋之亡也，以奸黨權臣。」
entries.en: Song fell through treacherous factions and powerful ministers."
entries.literal: The fall of Song was through treacherous factions and powerful ministers."

entries.zh: 太子嘉納，賜酒，日昃乃罷。
entries.en: The crown prince approved and bestowed wine. They did not disperse until sundown.
entries.literal: The Crown Prince approved and bestowed wine; only at sundown did they disperse.

entries.zh: 諭德李謙、夾谷之奇嘗進言曰：「殿下睿性夙成，閱理久熟，方遵聖訓，參決庶務，如視膳問安之禮，固無待於贊諭。
entries.en: Moral Instructor Li Qian and Jiagu Zhiqi once said, "Your Highness's keen nature was formed early and you have long mastered principle. You now follow the sage's instructions and take part in deciding affairs. Rites such as presenting food and inquiring after health need no exhortation from us.
entries.literal: Moral Instructor Li Qian and Jiagu Zhiqi once advanced and said: "Your Highness's keen nature was formed early; you have long been versed in principle; now you follow the sage's instructions and take part in deciding the myriad affairs — such as presenting food and inquiring after health — and truly need no exhortation.

entries.zh: 至於軍民之利病，政令之得失，事關朝廷，責在臺院，有非宮臣所宜言者。
entries.en: What benefits or harms soldiers and civilians and what is gained or lost in government orders concern the court and are the Censorate's responsibility, not what palace officers should speak of.
entries.literal: As for what benefits or harms soldiers and civilians, what is gained or lost in government orders — matters that concern the court and are the responsibility of the Censorate — these are not what palace officers should speak of.

entries.zh: 獨有澄原固本，保守成業，殿下所當留心，臣等不容緘口者也。
entries.en: Only clarifying the source and securing the root and preserving the established enterprise are what Your Highness should attend to, and on these we cannot keep silent.
entries.literal: Only clarifying the source and securing the root, preserving the established enterprise — these Your Highness should attend to; we cannot keep silent.

entries.zh: 敬陳十事：曰正心，曰睦親，曰崇儉，曰親賢，曰幾諫，曰戢兵，曰尚文，曰定律，曰正名，曰革敝。」
entries.en: They respectfully presented ten matters: rectifying the mind, drawing kin close, esteeming frugality, cherishing the worthy, subtle remonstrance, restraining troops, honoring culture, fixing laws, correcting names, and reforming abuses."
entries.literal: Respectfully presenting ten matters: rectifying the mind, drawing kin close, esteeming frugality, cherishing the worthy, subtle remonstrance, restraining troops, honoring culture, fixing laws, correcting names, and reforming abuses."

entries.zh: 其論正心有云：「太子之心，天下之本也。
entries.en: On rectifying the mind they said, "The crown prince's mind is the root of the realm.
entries.literal: In discussing rectifying the mind it was said: "The crown prince's mind is the root of the realm.

entries.zh: 太子心正，則天心有所屬，人心有所系矣。
entries.en: When the crown prince's mind is correct, Heaven's mind has what to attach to and the people's hearts have what to bind them.
entries.literal: When the crown prince's mind is correct, then Heaven's mind has what to attach to and the people's hearts have what to bind them.

entries.zh: 唐太宗嘗言，人主一心，攻之者眾，或以勇力，或以辨口，或以諂諛，或以奸詐，或以嗜欲，輻輳攻之，各求自售。
entries.en: Tang Taizong once said that a ruler has but one mind, yet those who assail it are many, whether by force, eloquence, flattery, treachery, or craving, each wheeling in to sell himself.
entries.literal: Tang Taizong once said that a ruler has but one heart, yet those who attack it are many — some by force of arms, some by eloquent tongue, some by flattery, some by treachery, some by craving — wheeling in to attack, each seeking to sell himself.

entries.zh: 人主少懈，而受其一，則其害有不可勝言者。
entries.en: If the ruler relaxes even slightly and accepts one of them, the harm is beyond words.
entries.literal: If the ruler relaxes even slightly and accepts one of them, the harm is beyond words.

entries.zh: 殿下至尊之儲貳，人求自售者亦不為少，須常喚醒此心，不使為物欲所撓，則宗社生靈之福。
entries.en: Your Highness, as the supreme heir, also has no lack of those who seek to sell themselves. You must constantly awaken this mind and not let it be stirred by external things. Then the altars of state and the living will be blessed.
entries.literal: Your Highness, as the supreme heir, is not without those who seek to sell themselves; you must constantly awaken this mind and not let it be stirred by external things — then the altars of state and the living will be blessed.

entries.zh: 固本澄原，莫此為切。」
entries.en: To secure the root and clarify the source, nothing is more urgent."
entries.literal: To secure the root and clarify the source, nothing is more urgent."

entries.zh: 論睦親，以「宗親為王室之藩屏，人主之所自衛者也。
entries.en: On drawing kin close they said, "Clan kin are the screen of the royal house and what the ruler uses to defend himself.
entries.literal: On drawing kin close: "Clan kin are the screen of the royal house and what the ruler uses to defend himself.

entries.zh: 大分既定，尊卑懸殊，必恩意俯逮，然後得盡其歡心。
entries.en: Once rank is fixed and honor and baseness stand far apart, favor must reach down generously, and only then can their full hearts be won.
entries.literal: Once the great distinction is fixed and honor and baseness stand far apart, favor must reach down in condescension — only then can their full hearts be obtained.

entries.zh: 宗親之歡心得，則遠近之歡心得矣」。
entries.en: When the clan kin's hearts are won, the hearts of those far and near are won as well."
entries.literal: When the clan kin's full hearts are obtained, then the hearts of those far and near are obtained."

entries.zh: 其論正名、革敝，尤切中時政。
entries.en: Their discussions of correcting names and reforming abuses especially struck at the politics of the time.
entries.literal: Their discussions of correcting names and reforming abuses especially hit the politics of the time.

entries.zh: 太子在中書日久，明於聽斷，四方州郡科征、挽漕、造作、和市，有系民休戚者，聞之，即日奏罷。
entries.en: The crown prince had long served in the Secretariat and was clear in judgment. Whenever levies, transport, construction, or market purchases in the commanderies touched the people's welfare, he memorialized the same day to stop them.
entries.literal: The Crown Prince had long been in the Secretariat and was clear in hearing and deciding; whenever levies, transport, construction, or market purchases in commanderies and districts touched the people's weal and woe, on hearing of them he memorialized the same day to stop them.

entries.zh: 右丞盧世榮以言利進，太子意深非之。
entries.en: Right Vice Councilor Lu Shirong advanced by speaking of profit, which the crown prince deeply disapproved.
entries.literal: Right Vice Councilor Lu Shirong advanced by speaking of profit; the Crown Prince deeply disapproved.

entries.zh: 嘗曰：「財非天降，安得歲取贏乎！
entries.en: He once said, "Wealth does not fall from Heaven. How can one take surplus every year!
entries.literal: He once said: "Wealth does not fall from Heaven — how can one take surplus every year!

entries.zh: 恐生民膏血，竭於此也。
entries.en: I fear the people's fat and blood will be exhausted here.
entries.literal: I fear the people's fat and blood will be exhausted here.

entries.zh: 豈惟害民，實國之大蠹。」
entries.en: It will not only harm the people; it is truly the great bane of the state."
entries.literal: It will not only harm the people — it is truly the great bane of state."

entries.zh: 其後世榮果坐罪。
entries.en: Afterward Shirong was indeed punished for crime.
entries.literal: Afterward Shirong indeed was punished for crime.

entries.zh: 桑哥素主世榮，聞太子有言，訖箝口不敢救。
entries.en: Sangge had always championed Shirong, but hearing the crown prince's words, he kept silent to the end and dared not save him.
entries.literal: Sangge had always championed Shirong; hearing the Crown Prince's words, he kept silent to the end and dared not save him.

entries.zh: 至元以來，天下臻於太平，人材輩出，太子優禮遇之，在師友之列者，非朝廷名德，則布衣節行之士，德意未嘗少衰。
entries.en: Since the Zhiyuan period the realm had reached great peace and talented men emerged in succession. The crown prince treated them with exceptional courtesy. Those counted among his teachers and friends were either eminent court worthies or men of integrity from among the commoners, and his gracious intent never slackened.
entries.literal: Since the Zhiyuan period the realm had reached great peace and talented men emerged in succession; the Crown Prince treated them with exceptional courtesy. Those in the ranks of teacher and friend were either eminent worthies of the court or men of integrity among the commoners — his gracious intent never slackened.

entries.zh: 宋瑽目疾，賜鈔千五百緡。
entries.en: Song Cong suffered eye disease and was granted one thousand five hundred strings of paper money.
entries.literal: Song Cong suffered eye disease; he was granted one thousand five hundred strings of paper money.

entries.zh: 王磐告老而歸，官其壻于東平，以終養。
entries.en: Wang Pan reported his age and returned home. His son-in-law was given office in Dongping so he might complete his filial nurture.
entries.literal: Wang Pan reported his age and returned home; his son-in-law was given office in Dongping so he might complete his filial nurture.

entries.zh: 孔洙自江南入覲，則責張九思學聖人之道，不知有聖人之後。
entries.en: When Kong Zhu came from Jiangnan to pay homage, he reproached Zhang Jiusi for studying the Way of the sages yet not knowing that there was a descendant of the sage.
entries.literal: When Kong Zhu came from Jiangnan to pay homage, he reproached Zhang Jiusi for studying the Way of the sages yet not knowing there was a descendant of the sage.

entries.zh: 其大雅不羣，本於天性。
entries.en: His great refinement and standing apart from the crowd were rooted in his inborn nature.
entries.literal: His great refinement and standing apart from the crowd were rooted in his inborn nature.

entries.zh: 中外歸心焉。
entries.en: Within and without, hearts turned to him.
entries.literal: Within and without, hearts turned to him.

entries.zh: 於是世祖春秋高，江南行臺監察御史言事者請禪位於太子，太子聞之，懼。
entries.en: Then Shizu's years were advanced. A remonstrating Jiangnan Branch Censorate investigating censor requested that he abdicate in favor of the crown prince. When the crown prince heard of it, he was afraid.
entries.literal: Then Shizu's years were advanced; a remonstrating Jiangnan Branch Censorate investigating censor requested abdication in favor of the Crown Prince; when the Crown Prince heard of it he was afraid.

entries.zh: 臺臣寢其奏，不敢遽聞，而小人以臺臣隱匿，乘間發之。
entries.en: The censorial officials suppressed the memorial and dared not report it at once, but petty men, because the censors had concealed it, seized the opportunity and made it known.
entries.literal: The censorial officials suppressed the memorial and dared not report it at once, but petty men, because the censors had concealed it, seized the interval and made it known.

entries.zh: 世祖怒甚，太子愈益懼，未幾，遂薨，壽四十有三。
entries.en: Shizu was greatly angry and the crown prince grew ever more afraid. Before long he died, aged forty-three.
entries.literal: Shizu was greatly angry; the Crown Prince grew ever more afraid; before long he died, aged forty-three.

entries.zh: 成宗即位，追謚曰文惠明孝皇帝，廟號裕宗，祔于太廟。
entries.en: When Chengzong took the throne he posthumously styled him the Emperor Wenhui Mingxiao with the temple name Yuzong, enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
entries.literal: When Chengzong took the throne he posthumously styled him the Emperor Wenhui Mingxiao with temple name Yuzong, enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

entries.zh: 顯宗光聖仁孝皇帝，諱甘麻剌，裕宗長子也。
entries.en: Xianzong, the Emperor Guangsheng Renxiao, bore the personal name Gammala and was the eldest son of Yuzong.
entries.literal: Xianzong, the Emperor Guang Sheng Renxiao — taboo name Gammala — was the eldest son of Yuzong.

entries.zh: 母曰徽仁裕聖皇后，弘吉剌氏。
entries.en: His mother was Empress Hui Ren Yu Sheng of the Onggirat.
entries.literal: His mother was Empress Hui Ren Yu Sheng of the Onggirat clan.

entries.zh: 甘麻剌少育於祖母昭睿順聖皇后，日侍世祖，未嘗離左右，畏慎不妄言，言必無隱。
entries.en: Gammala was raised in youth by his grandmother Empress Zhaorui Shunsheng, daily attending Shizu and never leaving his side. He was cautious and did not speak rashly, but when he spoke he concealed nothing.
entries.literal: Gammala was raised in youth by his grandmother Empress Zhaorui Shunsheng, daily attending Shizu, never leaving his side; cautious and not speaking rashly — when he spoke he concealed nothing.

entries.zh: 至元中，奉旨鎮北邊，叛王嶽木忽兒等聞其至，望風請降。
entries.en: In the Zhiyuan period he was ordered to guard the northern frontier. Rebel princes such as Yüsmish, hearing he had arrived, submitted at once.
entries.literal: In the Zhiyuan period, by imperial order he guarded the northern frontier; rebel princes such as Yüsmish and others, hearing he had arrived, submitted on the wind.

entries.zh: 既而都阿、察八兒諸王遣使求和，邊境以寧。
entries.en: Before long Princes Dua, Chabar, and others sent envoys seeking peace, and the frontier was tranquil.
entries.literal: Before long the princes Dua and Chabar and others sent envoys seeking peace, and the frontier was thereby tranquil.

entries.zh: 嘗出征駐金山，會大雪，擁火坐帳內，歡甚，顧謂左右曰：「今日風雪如是，吾與卿處猶有寒色，彼從士亦人耳，腰弓矢、荷刃周廬之外，其苦可知。」
entries.en: Once on campaign he encamped at Jinshan. Heavy snow fell. Huddling by the fire in his tent he was merry and said to those at hand, "In wind and snow like this we still feel cold here. Our followers are men too, with bows at their waists and blades on their backs circling the camp outside. Their hardship is easy to imagine."
entries.literal: Once on campaign he encamped at Jinshan; a great snow fell; huddling by the fire inside the tent he was very merry and turned to those at hand: "Today the wind and snow are like this — you and I sitting here still feel cold; those followers are also men — with bow at waist and blade on back, circling the encampment outside — their hardship can be known."

entries.zh: 遂命饔人大為肉糜，親嘗而遍賜之。
entries.en: He ordered the provisioners to make meat porridge in quantity, tasted it himself, and gave it to all.
entries.literal: He then ordered the provisioners to make meat porridge in great quantity, tasted it himself, and bestowed it on all.

entries.zh: 撫循部曲之暇，則命也滅堅以國語講《通鑒》。
entries.en: In intervals of comforting the troops he had Yemujian lecture on Comprehensive Mirror in Mongolian.
entries.literal: In intervals of comforting the troops he ordered Yemujian to lecture on Comprehensive Mirror in Mongolian.

entries.zh: 戒其近侍太不花曰：「朝廷以藩屏寄我，事有不逮，正在汝輩輔助。
entries.en: He warned his close attendant Taibuhua, "The court has entrusted me as a frontier screen. If affairs are not fully handled, you must assist me.
entries.literal: He warned his close attendant Taibuhua: "The court has entrusted me as a screen; if affairs are not fully handled, that lies in you assisting.

entries.zh: 其或依勢作威，不用我命，輕者論遣，大者奏聞耳，宜各慎之。
entries.en: If any rely on power to act arrogantly and disobey my command, the lighter case is reprimand and dispatch, the heavier is memorialized. Each of you must be careful.
entries.literal: If any rely on power to act arrogantly and do not obey my command — the light case is reprimand and dispatch, the heavy case is memorialized — each of you must be careful.

entries.zh: 使百姓安業，主上無北顧之憂，則予與卿等亦樂處於此，乃所以報國家也。」
entries.en: If the common people settle in their occupations and the sovereign has no worry of looking north, then you and I may dwell here in peace as well. That is how we repay the state."
entries.literal: If the common people settle in their occupations and the sovereign has no worry of looking north, then you and I may also dwell here in pleasure — that is how we repay the state."

entries.zh: 二十六年，世祖以其居邊日久，特命獵於柳林之地。
entries.en: In the twenty-sixth year Shizu, because he had long dwelt on the frontier, specially ordered him to hunt in the Willow Grove.
entries.literal: In the twenty-sixth year Shizu, because he had long dwelt on the frontier, specially ordered him to hunt in the Willow Grove.

entries.zh: 率眾至漷州，恐廩膳不均，令左右司之，分給從士，仍飭其眾曰：「汝等飲食既足，若復侵漁百姓，是汝自取罪謫，無悔。」
entries.en: Leading his host to Huozhou, fearing uneven grain provisions, he had his attendants supervise distribution to the followers and admonished them, "You have enough food and drink. If you encroach on the common people again, you bring punishment on yourselves. Do not regret it."
entries.literal: Leading his host to Huozhou, fearing that grain provisions might be uneven, he had those at hand supervise distribution to the followers, and still admonished the host: "You have enough food and drink; if you again encroach on and plunder the common people, you bring punishment on yourselves — do not regret it."

entries.zh: 眾皆如約，民賴以安。
entries.en: The host all kept the agreement, and the people were left in peace.
entries.literal: The host all kept the agreement and the people relied on this for peace.

entries.zh: 北還，覲世祖於上京，世祖勞之曰：「汝在柳林，民不知擾，朕實嘉焉。」
entries.en: Returning north he paid homage to Shizu at Shangdu. Shizu praised him, "At Willow Grove the people were undisturbed. I truly commend this."
entries.literal: Returning north he paid homage to Shizu at Shangdu; Shizu comforted him: "You were at Willow Grove and the people did not know disturbance — I truly commend this."

entries.zh: 明年冬，封梁王，授以金印，出鎮雲南。
entries.en: The next winter he was enfeoffed Prince of Liang, granted the golden seal, and sent to guard Yunnan.
entries.literal: The next winter he was enfeoffed Prince of Liang and granted the golden seal, going out to guard Yunnan.

entries.zh: 過中山，又明年春過懷、孟，從卒馬駝之屬不下千百計，所至未嘗橫取於民。
entries.en: Passing through Zhongshan and the next spring through Huai and Meng, with followers, horses, and camels numbering no fewer than a thousand, he never took forcibly from the people wherever he went.
entries.literal: Passing Zhongshan, and the next spring passing Huai and Meng, with followers, horses, and camels numbering no fewer than a thousand — wherever he went he never took forcibly from the people.

entries.zh: 二十九年，改封晉王，移鎮北邊，統領太祖四大斡耳朵及軍馬、達達國土，更鑄晉王金印授之。
entries.en: In the twenty-ninth year he was changed to Prince of Jin, transferred to guard the northern frontier, commanding Taizu's four great ordos with troops, horses, and Tatar lands, and a new Jin Prince golden seal was cast and conferred.
entries.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was changed to Prince of Jin, transferred to guard the northern frontier, commanding Taizu's four great ordos together with troops and horses and Tatar lands; a new Jin Prince golden seal was cast and conferred.

entries.zh: 中書省臣言於世祖曰：「諸王皆置傳，今晉王守太祖肇基之地，視諸王宜有加，請置內史。」
entries.en: Secretariat ministers spoke to Shizu, "All princes are given tutors. The Jin Prince now guards the land where Taizu first raised the foundation and, compared with other princes, ought to receive more. Please establish an Inner Scribe."
entries.literal: Secretariat ministers spoke to Shizu: "All princes are given tutors; now the Jin Prince guards the land where Taizu first raised the foundation and, compared with other princes, ought to receive more — please establish an Inner Scribe."

entries.zh: 世祖從之，遂以北安王傅禿歸、梁王傅木八剌沙、雲南行省平章賽陽並為內史。
entries.en: Shizu agreed and appointed North Pacification King Tutor Tugui, Liang King Tutor Mubalasha, and Yunnan Branch Secretariat Grand Councilor Saiyang as Inner Scribes.
entries.literal: Shizu followed this and thereupon appointed North Pacification King Tutor Tugui, Liang King Tutor Mubalasha, and Yunnan Branch Secretariat Grand Councilor Saiyang all as Inner Scribes.

entries.zh: 明年，置內史府。
entries.en: The following year the Inner Scribe Office was established.
entries.literal: The next year the Inner Scribe Office was established.

entries.zh: 又明年，世祖崩，晉王聞訃，奔赴上都。
entries.en: The year after that Shizu died. Hearing the mourning announcement, the Jin Prince rushed to Shangdu.
entries.literal: The year after that Shizu died; the Jin Prince, hearing the mourning announcement, rushed to Shangdu.

entries.zh: 諸王大臣咸在，晉王曰：「昔皇祖命我鎮撫北方，以衛社稷，久歷邊事，願服厥職。
entries.en: All the princes and great ministers were present. The Jin Prince said, "Formerly the imperial grandfather ordered me to pacify the north and guard the altars of state. Having long handled frontier affairs, I wish to fulfill that duty.
entries.literal: All the princes and great ministers were present; the Jin Prince said: "Formerly the imperial grandfather ordered me to pacify and soothe the north to guard the altars of state; having long handled frontier affairs, I wish to fulfill that duty.

entries.zh: 母弟鐵木耳仁孝，宜嗣大統。」
entries.en: My younger brother by the same mother, Temür, is benevolent and filial and ought to succeed to the throne."
entries.literal: My younger brother by the same mother, Temür, is benevolent and filial and ought to succeed to the great succession."

entries.zh: 於是成宗即帝位，而晉王復歸藩邸。
entries.en: Chengzong then took the throne, and the Jin Prince returned to his princely residence.
entries.literal: Thereupon Chengzong took the imperial throne, and the Jin Prince returned to his princely residence.

entries.zh: ○順宗
entries.en: ◎ Shunzong
entries.literal: ◎ Shunzong

entries.zh: 順宗昭聖衍孝皇帝，諱答剌麻八剌，裕宗第二子也。
entries.en: Shunzong, styled the Emperor Zhaosheng Yanxiao, bore the personal name Dadarmabala and was Yuzong's second son.
entries.literal: Shunzong, the Emperor Zhaosheng Yanxiao — taboo name Dadarmabala — was Yuzong's second son.

entries.zh: 母曰徽仁裕聖皇后，弘吉剌氏。
entries.en: His mother was Empress Hui Ren Yu Sheng of the Onggirat.
entries.literal: His mother was Empress Hui Ren Yu Sheng of the Onggirat clan.

entries.zh: 至元初，裕宗為燕王，答剌麻八剌生于燕邸。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Zhiyuan period, when Yuzong was Prince of Yan, Dadarmabala was born in the Yan residence.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Zhiyuan, when Yuzong was Prince of Yan, Dadarmabala was born in the Yan residence.

entries.zh: 明年，詔裕宗居潮河。
entries.en: The following year an edict ordered Yuzong to reside at Chaohe.
entries.literal: The next year an edict ordered Yuzong to reside at Chaohe.

entries.zh: 八月，召至京師。
entries.en: In the eighth month he was summoned to the capital.
entries.literal: In the eighth month he was summoned to the capital.

entries.zh: 凡乘輿巡幸及歲時朝賀，未嘗不侍裕宗以行。
entries.en: Whenever the imperial carriage toured or seasonal court congratulations were held, he always attended Yuzong.
entries.literal: Whenever the imperial carriage toured or seasonal court congratulations were held, he never failed to attend Yuzong in going forth.

entries.zh: 稍長，世祖賜女侍郭氏，其後乃納弘吉剌氏為妃。
entries.en: When he grew somewhat older Shizu granted him the maid Guo. Afterward he took a consort of the Onggirat clan.
entries.literal: When he grew somewhat older Shizu granted him the maid Guo; afterward he took a consort of the Onggirat clan.

entries.zh: 二十二年，裕宗薨，答剌麻八剌以皇孫鍾愛，兩宮優其出閤之禮。
entries.en: In the twenty-second year Yuzong died. Dadarmabala, as a cherished imperial grandson, received from both palaces an enhanced ceremony for leaving the inner quarters.
entries.literal: In the twenty-second year Yuzong died; Dadarmabala, as a cherished imperial grandson, received from both palaces an enhanced ceremony for leaving the inner quarters.

entries.zh: 二十八年，始詔出鎮懷州，以侍衞都指揮使梭都、尚書王倚從行。
entries.en: In the twenty-eighth year he was first ordered out to guard Huaizhou, with Palace Guard Commander Suodu and Minister Wang Yi in attendance.
entries.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was first ordered out to guard Huaizhou, with Palace Guard Commander Suodu and Minister Wang Yi attending him.

entries.zh: 至趙州，從卒有伐民桑棗者，民遮訴于道，答剌麻八剌怒，杖從卒以懲眾，遣王倚入奏，世祖大悅。
entries.en: Reaching Zhaozhou, some followers were cutting the people's mulberry and jujube trees. The people blocked the road to complain. Dadarmabala was angry, beat the followers to warn the host, and sent Wang Yi in to memorialize. Shizu was greatly pleased.
entries.literal: Reaching Zhaozhou, followers were cutting the people's mulberry and jujube trees; the people blocked the road to complain; Dadarmabala was angry, beat the followers to warn the host, and sent Wang Yi in to memorialize; Shizu was greatly pleased.

entries.zh: 未至，以疾召還。
entries.en: Before he arrived he was recalled on account of illness.
entries.literal: Before he arrived he was recalled on account of illness.

entries.zh: 明年春，世祖北幸，留治疾京師，越兩月而薨，年二十有九。
entries.en: The following spring Shizu went north on tour. Dadarmabala remained in the capital to treat his illness and died after two months, aged twenty-nine.
entries.literal: The next spring Shizu went north on tour; he remained in the capital to treat his illness and died after two months, aged twenty-nine.

entries.zh: ◎睿宗
entries.en: ◎ Ruizong
entries.literal: ◎ Ruizong

entries.zh: 睿宗顯懿莊聖皇后，名唆魯和帖尼，怯烈氏，生子憲宗、世祖，相繼為帝。
entries.en: Empress Xianyi Zhuang Sheng of Emperor Ruizong Tolui was named Sorghaghtani Beki of the Kereit. She bore Möngke and Kublai, each of whom in turn became emperor.
entries.literal: Empress Xianyi Zhuang Sheng of Emperor Ruizong, personal name Sorghaghtani Beki, of the Kereit clan; she bore the Xianzong Emperor and the Shizu Emperor, who succeeded one another on the throne.

entries.zh: 至元二年，追上尊謚莊聖皇后，升祔睿宗廟。
entries.en: In 1265 she was given the posthumous title Empress Zhuang Sheng and enshrined in Emperor Ruizong's temple.
entries.literal: In the second year of Zhiyuan, the posthumous honorific title Empress Zhuang Sheng was conferred and she was installed in the temple of Emperor Ruizong.

entries.zh: 至大二年十二月，加謚顯懿莊聖皇后。
entries.en: In December 1309 her title was further augmented to Empress Xianyi Zhuang Sheng.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Zhida, the title was augmented to Empress Xianyi Zhuang Sheng.

entries.zh: 三年十月，又上玉冊，其文曰：「祖功宗德，稱誄於天。
entries.en: In the tenth month of 1310 a jade book was presented again. Its text read: "The achievements of the ancestors and the virtue of the forefathers are proclaimed in eulogy to Heaven.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of the third year, a jade book was again presented; its text read: "The achievements of the ancestors and the virtue of the forefathers are proclaimed in eulogy to Heaven.

entries.zh: 內則閫儀，受成於廟。
entries.en: The inner norms and the rites of the inner court receive their completion in the ancestral temple.
entries.literal: The inner norms and the rites of the inner court receive their completion in the ancestral temple.

entries.zh: 行之大者名必顯，恩之隆者報則豐。
entries.en: Great deeds demand that a name shine forth; profound favor calls for abundant recompense.
entries.literal: When great deeds are performed, the name must shine forth; when favor is profound, the recompense is abundant.

entries.zh: 上以增佐定之光，下以伸遹追之孝。
entries.en: Above, to add luster to the achievement of assisting in the founding; below, to extend the filial piety of distant commemoration.
entries.literal: Above, to add luster to the achievement of assisting in the founding; below, to extend the filial piety of distant commemoration.

entries.zh: 欽惟莊聖皇后，英明溥博，聖善柔嘉。
entries.en: Reverently considering Empress Zhuang Sheng: perspicacious and broadly accomplished, sagely, good, gentle, and excellent.
entries.literal: Reverently considering Empress Zhuang Sheng: perspicacious and broadly accomplished, sagely, good, gentle, and excellent.

entries.zh: 尊儷景襄，陰教純被。
entries.en: She honored and matched Emperor Jingxiang Tolui; the teachings of the inner court were purely diffused.
entries.literal: She honored and matched Emperor Jingxiang; the teachings of the inner court were purely diffused.

entries.zh: 逮事光獻，婦職勤修。
entries.en: When she came to serve Empress Guangxian, she diligently cultivated the duties of a wife.
entries.literal: When she came to serve Guangxian, she diligently cultivated the duties of a wife.

entries.zh: 勛聿著於承天，祥兩占於夢日。
entries.en: Her merit was forthwith displayed in receiving Heaven's mandate; auspicious omens of two suns were divined in a dream of the sun.
entries.literal: Her merit was forthwith displayed in receiving Heaven's mandate; auspicious omens of two suns were divined in a dream of the sun.

entries.zh: 跡聖緒洪源之有漸，知深仁厚澤之無垠。
entries.en: Tracing the sage succession, one sees the great source unfold by degrees and knows that deep benevolence and thick grace are boundless.
entries.literal: Tracing the sage succession, the great source had its gradual unfolding; knowing that deep benevolence and thick grace are boundless.

entries.zh: 玄符肇自塗山，顧前徽之未稱；
entries.en: The dark talisman arose from Mount Tu, yet the former excellence had not been fittingly honored;
entries.literal: The dark talisman arose from Mount Tu; yet the former excellence had not been fittingly honored;

entries.zh: 蒼箓興於文母，豈后嗣之能忘。
entries.en: the azure register rose from the civil mother — how could posterity forget?
entries.literal: the azure register rose from the civil mother — how could posterity forget?

entries.zh: 是用參考彜經，丕揚景鑠。
entries.en: Therefore the canonical classics were consulted and the great resplendent standard was raised high.
entries.literal: Therefore the canonical classics were consulted and the great resplendent standard was raised high.

entries.zh: 敷繹寶慈之誼，形容青史之規。
entries.en: The meaning of precious compassion was set forth and expounded, and the model for the blue annals was given form.
entries.literal: The meaning of precious compassion was set forth and expounded, and the model for the blue annals was given form.

entries.zh: 謹遣攝太尉某奉玉冊玉寶，加上尊謚曰顯懿莊聖皇后。
entries.en: We respectfully send the Acting Grand Commandant to present the jade book and jade seal and add the honorific posthumous title Empress Xianyi Zhuang Sheng.
entries.literal: We respectfully send the Acting Grand Commandant [name] to present the jade book and jade seal and add the honorific posthumous title Empress Xianyi Zhuang Sheng.

entries.zh: 伏惟睿靈，昭垂鑒格。
entries.en: We humbly trust that your wise spirit will brightly descend and grant inspection and acceptance.
entries.literal: We humbly trust that your wise spirit will brightly descend and grant inspection and acceptance.

entries.zh: 禮嚴閟宮，樂歌夷則。
entries.en: Rites were solemn in the secluded palace; music sang the yize mode.
entries.literal: Rites were solemn in the secluded palace; music sang the yize mode.

entries.zh: 億萬斯年，承休無斁。」
entries.en: For ten thousand myriad years may blessings be received without end."
entries.literal: For ten thousand myriad years may blessings be received without end."

entries.zh: 裕宗徽仁裕聖皇后伯藍也怯赤，一名闊闊真，弘吉剌氏，生順宗、成宗。
entries.en: Empress Huiren Yusheng of Emperor Yuzong Zhenjin was Bo'alaije'u, also called Kokejin, of the Hongjira clan. She bore Darmabala and Temür, who became Emperors Shunzong and Chengzong.
entries.literal: Empress Huiren Yusheng of Emperor Yuzong, Bo'alaije'u, also called Kokejin, of the Hongjira clan; she bore the Shunzong Emperor and the Chengzong Emperor.

entries.zh: 先是世祖出田獵，道渴，至一帳房，見一女子緝駝茸，世祖從覓馬湩。
entries.en: Earlier, when Kublai went out hunting, he grew thirsty on the road, came to a tent, and saw a girl sewing camel hair. He asked her for kumiss.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Shizu went out hunting, he grew thirsty on the road, came to a tent, and saw a girl sewing camel hair; Shizu asked her for kumiss.

entries.zh: 女子曰：「馬湩有之，但我父母諸兄皆不在，我女子難以與汝。」
entries.en: The girl said, "There is kumiss, but my parents and elder brothers are all away. As a girl alone I cannot easily give it to you."
entries.literal: The girl said: "There is kumiss, but my parents and elder brothers are all away; as a girl alone I find it hard to give it to you."

entries.zh: 世祖欲去之。
entries.en: Kublai was about to leave.
entries.literal: Shizu was about to leave.

entries.zh: 女子又曰：「我獨居此，汝自來自去，於理不宜。
entries.en: The girl said again, "I live here alone. For you to come and go by yourself is not proper.
entries.literal: The girl again said: "I live here alone; for you to come and go by yourself is not proper by reason.

entries.zh: 我父母即歸，姑待之。」
entries.en: My parents will return shortly. Please wait."
entries.literal: My parents will return at once — please wait a little."

entries.zh: 須臾果歸。
entries.en: In a moment they did return.
entries.literal: In a moment they indeed returned.

entries.zh: 出馬湩飲世祖。
entries.en: They brought out kumiss for Kublai to drink.
entries.literal: They brought out kumiss for Shizu to drink.

entries.zh: 世祖既去，嘆息曰：「得此等女子為人家婦，豈不美耶！」
entries.en: After Kublai had gone, he sighed and said, "To obtain a girl like this as a wife for one's household — would it not be fine!"
entries.literal: After Shizu had gone, he sighed and said: "To obtain a girl like this as a wife for one's household — would it not be fine!"

entries.zh: 后與諸臣謀擇太子妃，世祖俱不允。
entries.en: Later the empress and the ministers deliberated on choosing a crown princess, but Kublai would not approve any of them.
entries.literal: Later the empress and the ministers deliberated on choosing a crown princess; Shizu would not approve any of them.

entries.zh: 有一老臣嘗知向者之言，知其未許嫁，言於世祖。
entries.en: An old minister had once heard what Kublai had said. Knowing that the girl was not yet betrothed, he spoke of it to Kublai.
entries.literal: An old minister had once heard what Shizu had said; knowing that she was not yet betrothed, he spoke of it to Shizu.

entries.zh: 世祖大喜，納為太子妃。
entries.en: Kublai was greatly pleased and took her in as crown princess.
entries.literal: Shizu was greatly pleased and took her in as crown princess.

entries.zh: 后性孝謹，善事中宮，世祖每稱之為賢德媳婦。
entries.en: The consort was by nature filial and careful and good at serving the inner palace. Kublai always called her a worthy and virtuous daughter-in-law.
entries.literal: The consort was by nature filial and careful, good at serving the inner palace; Shizu always called her a worthy and virtuous daughter-in-law.

entries.zh: 侍昭睿順聖皇后，不離左右，至混廁所用紙，亦以面擦，令柔軟以進。
entries.en: She attended Empress Zhaorui Shunsheng and never left her side. Even the paper used in the privy she rubbed with her face to soften before presenting it.
entries.literal: She attended Empress Zhaorui Shunsheng and never left her side; even the paper used in the privy she rubbed with her face to make it soft before presenting it.

entries.zh: 一日，裕宗有病，世祖往視，見床上設織金臥褥。
entries.en: One day Zhenjin was ill. Kublai went to visit and saw a brocaded gold sleeping mat on the bed.
entries.literal: One day Yuzong was ill; Shizu went to visit and saw a brocaded gold sleeping mat set on the bed.

entries.zh: 世祖慍而語之曰：「我嘗以汝為賢，何乃若此耶？」
entries.en: Kublai grew angry and said to her, "I once regarded you as worthy. How can you be like this?"
entries.literal: Shizu grew angry and said to her: "I once regarded you as worthy — how can you be like this?"

entries.zh: 后跪答曰：「常時不曾敢用，今為太子病，恐有濕氣，因用之。」
entries.en: The consort knelt and answered, "At ordinary times I never dared use it. Now, because the crown prince is ill, I feared dampness and therefore used it."
entries.literal: The consort knelt and answered: "At ordinary times I never dared use it; now, because the crown prince is ill, I feared dampness and therefore used it."

entries.zh: 即時徹去。
entries.en: She immediately had it removed.
entries.literal: She immediately had it removed.

entries.zh: 世祖崩，成宗至上都，諸王畢會。
entries.en: When Kublai died, Temür arrived at Shangdu and all the princes assembled.
entries.literal: When Shizu died, Chengzong arrived at Shangdu and all the princes assembled.

entries.zh: 先是，御史中丞崔彧得玉璽於木華黎國王曾孫世德家，其文曰「受命於天，既壽永昌」，上之於后，至是，后手授成宗。
entries.en: Earlier the Censor-in-Chief Cui Yu had obtained the jade seal in the home of Shide, great-grandson of Prince Muqali. Its inscription read "Receiving the mandate from Heaven, long life and eternal prosperity." He presented it to the empress, and on this occasion she personally handed it to Temür.
entries.literal: Earlier, the Censor-in-Chief Cui Yu had obtained the jade seal in the home of Shide, great-grandson of Prince Muqali; its inscription read "Receiving the mandate from Heaven, long life and eternal prosperity." He presented it to the empress; at this time the empress personally handed it to Chengzong.

entries.zh: 即皇帝位，尊后為皇太后，冊文曰：「自家而國，治道必有所先；
entries.en: Upon assuming the imperial throne, he honored the empress as Empress Dowager. The investiture text read: "From the family to the state, the way of governance must have what comes first;
entries.literal: Upon assuming the imperial throne, he honored the empress as Empress Dowager; the investiture text read: "From the family to the state, the way of governance must have what comes first;

entries.zh: 立愛惟親，君德莫先於孝。
entries.en: establishing love begins with kin, and among the virtues of a ruler none comes before filial piety.
entries.literal: establishing love begins with kin; among the virtues of a ruler none comes before filial piety.

entries.zh: 況恩深於鞠我，而禮重於正名。
entries.en: How much more when favor is deep in nurturing me, and ritual weighs heavily in rectifying the name!
entries.literal: How much more when favor is deep in nurturing me, and ritual weighs heavily in rectifying the name!

entries.zh: 歷代以來，令儀可考。
entries.en: Through successive dynasties, excellent precedents may be examined.
entries.literal: Through successive dynasties, excellent precedents may be examined.

entries.zh: 人子之職所在，天下之母宜尊。
entries.en: Where the duty of a son lies, the mother of the realm should be honored.
entries.literal: Where the duty of a son lies, the mother of the realm should be honored.

entries.zh: 恭惟聖母，聖善本乎天資，靜專法乎地道。
entries.en: Reverently considering the Holy Mother: sagely goodness is rooted in Heaven-given nature, and stillness and concentration follow the way of Earth.
entries.literal: Reverently considering the Holy Mother: sagely goodness is rooted in Heaven-given nature; stillness and concentration follow the way of Earth.

entries.zh: 上以奉宗祏之重，下以敘倫紀之常。
entries.en: Above, to uphold the weight of the ancestral tablets; below, to set in order the constants of human relations.
entries.literal: Above, to uphold the weight of the ancestral tablets; below, to set in order the constants of human relations.

entries.zh: 助我前人，守《卷耳》憂勤之志；
entries.en: She aided my forebears, keeping the anxious diligence of "Roll up your sleeves";
entries.literal: She aided my forebears, keeping the anxious diligence of "Roll up your sleeves";

entries.zh: 保予沖子，成《思齊》雍肅之風。
entries.en: she protected my young heir and completed the harmonious solemnity of "Be like him."
