entries.literal: she protected my young heir and completed the harmonious solemnity of "Be like him."

entries.zh: 肆神器之有歸，知孫謀之素定。
entries.en: Now that the sacred vessel has its destination, we know that the grandson's design was long settled.
entries.literal: Now that the sacred vessel has its destination, we know that the grandson's design was long settled.

entries.zh: 畀付雖由於歷數，規摹一出於庭闈。
entries.en: Though the conferral follows the sequence of fate, the plan and model issued from the inner court.
entries.literal: Though the conferral follows the sequence of fate, the plan and model issued from the inner court.

entries.zh: 是用率籲眾心，章明巨度，不勝拳拳大願。
entries.en: Therefore we lead and call forth the hearts of the multitude, proclaim the great measure, and cannot overcome our earnest great wish.
entries.literal: Therefore we lead and call forth the hearts of the multitude, proclaim the great measure, and cannot overcome our earnest great wish.

entries.zh: 謹奉冊寶，上尊稱曰皇太后。
entries.en: We respectfully present the book and seal and raise the honorific title Empress Dowager.
entries.literal: We respectfully present the book and seal and raise the honorific title Empress Dowager.

entries.zh: 伏惟長信穆穆，周宗綿綿。
entries.en: We humbly trust that long faith will be solemn and the Zhou lineage unending.
entries.literal: We humbly trust that long faith will be solemn and the Zhou lineage unending.

entries.zh: 備《洛書》之錫福，粲慈極之儀天。
entries.en: Complete with the blessings granted in the Luo Document, resplendent as the compassionate pole in honoring Heaven.
entries.literal: Complete with the blessings granted in the Luo Document, resplendent as the compassionate pole in honoring Heaven.

entries.zh: 瑤圖寶運，於萬斯年。」
entries.en: The jade chart and precious destiny — for ten thousand years."
entries.literal: The jade chart and precious destiny — for ten thousand years."

entries.zh: 命設官屬，置徽政院。
entries.en: He ordered officials to be appointed and established the Bureau of Imperial Governance.
entries.literal: He ordered officials to be appointed and established the Bureau of Imperial Governance.

entries.zh: 后院官有受獻浙西田七百頃，籍於位下，太后曰：「我寡居婦人，衣食自有餘，況江南率土，皆國家所有，我曷敢私之。」
entries.en: An official of the rear palace had received as tribute seven hundred qing of land in western Zhejiang, registered under her station. The Empress Dowager said, "I am a widow living alone — food and clothing are already more than enough. Moreover, all the lands south of the Yangtze belong to the state. How dare I make them private?"
entries.literal: An official of the rear palace had received as tribute seven hundred qing of land in western Zhejiang, registered under her station; the Empress Dowager said: "I am a widow living alone — food and clothing are already more than enough; moreover, all the lands south of the Yangtze belong to the state. How dare I make them private?"

entries.zh: 即命中書省盡易院官之受獻者。
entries.en: She immediately ordered the Secretariat to replace entirely those bureau officials who had received such tribute.
entries.literal: She immediately ordered the Secretariat to replace entirely those bureau officials who had received such tribute.

entries.zh: 后之弟欲因后求官，后語之曰：「若欲求官耶？
entries.en: The empress's younger brother wished to seek office through her. The empress said to him, "If you wish to seek office,
entries.literal: The empress's younger brother wished to seek office through her; the empress said to him: "If you wish to seek office,

entries.zh: 汝自為之，勿以累我也。」
entries.en: do it yourself. Do not involve me."
entries.literal: do it yourself — do not involve me."

entries.zh: 其后，弟果被黜，人皆服后之先見。
entries.en: Afterward his younger brother was indeed dismissed, and everyone admired the empress's foresight.
entries.literal: Afterward his younger brother was indeed dismissed, and everyone admired the empress's foresight.

entries.zh: 大德四年二月崩，祔葬先陵，謚曰裕聖皇后，升祔裕宗廟。
entries.en: In the second month of 1300 she died, was buried beside the former imperial tombs, posthumously titled Empress Yusheng, and installed in the temple of Emperor Yuzong.
entries.literal: In the second month of the fourth year of Dade she died, was buried beside the former imperial tombs, posthumously titled Empress Yusheng, and installed in the temple of Emperor Yuzong.

entries.zh: 至大三年十月，又追尊謚曰徽仁裕聖皇后。
entries.en: In the tenth month of 1310 the title was further raised to Empress Huiren Yusheng.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of the third year of Zhida, the title was further raised to Empress Huiren Yusheng.

entries.zh: 順宗昭獻元聖皇后，名答己，弘吉剌氏，按陳孫渾都帖木兒之女。
entries.en: Empress Zhaoxian Yuansheng of Emperor Shunzong Darmabala was named Daji of the Hongjira clan, daughter of Qundutemür, grandson of Anchen.
entries.literal: Empress Zhaoxian Yuansheng of Emperor Shunzong, personal name Daji, of the Hongjira clan, daughter of Anchen's grandson Qundutemür.

entries.zh: 裕宗居燕邸及潮河，順宗俱在侍，稍長，世祖賜女侍郭氏，後乃納后為妃，生武宗及仁宗。
entries.en: When Zhenjin resided at the Yan residence and at Chaohe, Darmabala was always in attendance. When he grew somewhat older, Kublai granted him the attendant Guo, and later he took Daji as consort. She bore Külüg Khan and Ayurbarwada, who became Emperors Wuzong and Renzong.
entries.literal: When Yuzong resided at the Yan residence and at Chaohe, Shunzong was always in attendance; when he grew somewhat older, Shizu granted him the attendant Guo, and later he took the empress as consort; she bore the Wuzong Emperor and the Renzong Emperor.

entries.zh: 大德九年，成宗不豫，卜魯罕皇后秉政，遣仁宗母子出居懷州。
entries.en: In 1305 Chengzong fell ill. Empress Buluqan held power and sent Ayurbarwada and his mother out to reside at Huaizhou.
entries.literal: In the ninth year of Dade, Chengzong fell ill; Empress Buluqan held power and sent the Renzong Emperor and his mother out to reside at Huaizhou.

entries.zh: 十年十二月，后至懷州。
entries.en: In the twelfth month of 1306 the empress arrived at Huaizhou.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month of the tenth year, the empress arrived at Huaizhou.

entries.zh: 十一年正月，成宗崩。
entries.en: In the first month of 1307 Chengzong died.
entries.literal: In the first month of the eleventh year, Chengzong died.

entries.zh: 時武宗總兵北邊，右丞相答剌罕哈剌哈孫陰遣使報仁宗，與后奔還京師。
entries.en: At that time Külüg Khan commanded troops on the northern frontier. The Right Chancellor Daraqan Qaraqas secretly sent envoys to inform Ayurbarwada, and the empress and he rushed back to the capital.
entries.literal: At that time Wuzong commanded troops on the northern frontier; the Right Chancellor Daraqan Qaraqas secretly sent envoys to inform Renzong, and the empress and he rushed back to the capital.

entries.zh: 后與仁宗入內哭，復出居舊邸，朝夕入奠。
entries.en: The empress and Ayurbarwada entered the palace to weep, then returned to their former residence, morning and evening entering to offer libations.
entries.literal: The empress and Renzong entered within to weep, then went out again to reside at their former residence, morning and evening entering to offer libations.

entries.zh: 即遣使迎武宗還，以五月即位。
entries.en: They immediately sent envoys to welcome Külüg Khan back, and in the fifth month he took the throne.
entries.literal: They immediately sent envoys to welcome Wuzong back; in the fifth month he took the throne.

entries.zh: 先是，太后以兩太子星命付陰陽家推算，問所宜立，對曰：「重光大荒落有災，旃蒙作噩長久。」
entries.en: Earlier the Empress Dowager had given the nativities of the two crown princes to yin-yang masters to calculate and asked which should be established. They answered, "Chongguang and Dahuangluo have calamity; Zhanmeng and Zuo'e are long-lasting."
entries.literal: Earlier, the Empress Dowager had given the nativities of the two crown princes to yin-yang masters to calculate and asked which should be established; they answered: "Chongguang and Dahuangluo have calamity; Zhanmeng and Zuo'e are long-lasting."

entries.zh: 重光為武宗生年，旃蒙為仁宗生年。
entries.en: Chongguang was Külüg Khan's birth year; Zhanmeng was Ayurbarwada's birth year.
entries.literal: Chongguang was Wuzong's birth year; Zhanmeng was Renzong's birth year.

entries.zh: 太后頗惑其言，遣近臣朵耳諭旨武宗曰：「汝兄弟二人，皆我所出，豈有親疏。
entries.en: The Empress Dowager was rather swayed by their words and sent a close attendant, Dor, to convey her instruction to Külüg Khan: "You two brothers were both born of me. How could there be closeness or distance?
entries.literal: The Empress Dowager was rather swayed by their words and sent a close attendant, Dor, to convey her instruction to Wuzong: "You two brothers were both born of me — how could there be closeness or distance?

entries.zh: 陰陽家所言，運祚修短，不容不思也。」
entries.en: What the yin-yang masters say about the length of fortune and fate — one cannot fail to consider it."
entries.literal: What the yin-yang masters say about the length of fortune and fate — one cannot fail to consider it."

entries.zh: 武宗聞之默然，進康裏脫脫而言曰：「我捍北邊十年，又胤次居長，太后以星命為言，茫昧難信。
entries.en: Külüg Khan heard this and was silent. He advanced Kangli Toqto'a and said, "I have defended the northern frontier for ten years, and by birth order I am the elder. The Empress Dowager speaks of star-fate — it is obscure and hard to trust.
entries.literal: Wuzong heard this and was silent; he advanced Kangli Toqto'a and said: "I have defended the northern frontier for ten years, and by birth order I am the elder. The Empress Dowager speaks of star-fate — it is obscure and hard to trust.

entries.zh: 使我設施合於天心民望，雖一日之短，亦足垂名萬世。
entries.en: If my measures accord with Heaven's mind and the people's hopes, even a reign of one day would be enough to leave a name for ten thousand generations.
entries.literal: If my measures accord with Heaven's mind and the people's hopes, even a reign of one day would be enough to leave a name for ten thousand generations.

entries.zh: 何可以陰陽家言，而乖祖宗之托哉！」
entries.en: How can one go against the charge of the ancestors because of what yin-yang masters say!"
entries.literal: How can one go against the charge of the ancestors because of what yin-yang masters say!"

entries.zh: 脫脫以聞，太后愕然曰：「修短之說，雖出術家，吾為太子遠慮，所以深愛太子也。
entries.en: Toqto'a reported this. The Empress Dowager was startled and said, "The talk of long and short reigns, though it comes from specialists, is my far-sighted concern for the crown prince. That is why I deeply love the crown prince.
entries.literal: Toqto'a reported this; the Empress Dowager was startled and said: "The talk of long and short reigns, though it comes from specialists, is my far-sighted concern for the crown prince — that is why I deeply love the crown prince.

entries.zh: 太子既如是言，今當速來耳。」
entries.en: Since the crown prince has spoken thus, he should come quickly now."
entries.literal: Since the crown prince has spoken thus, he should come quickly now."

entries.zh: 詳見《康里脫脫傳》中。
entries.en: For details see the biography of Kangli Toqto'a.
entries.literal: For details see the biography of Kangli Toqto'a.

entries.zh: 后妃二
entries.en: Empresses and Consorts 2
entries.literal: Empresses and Consorts 2

entries.zh: 罕禿忽，性剛猛，知兵。
entries.en: Qutugtu was fierce by nature and skilled in the art of war.
entries.literal: Qutugtu was by nature fierce and bold and understood warfare.

entries.zh: 從憲宗征伐，多立戰功，及攻釣魚山而還，道由河南，招來流亡百餘戶，悉以入籍。
entries.en: He followed Emperor Xianzong on campaign and won distinction again and again; returning from the siege of Diaoyu Mountain, he passed through Henan and brought in more than a hundred refugee households, registering every one.
entries.literal: He followed Emperor Xianzong on campaigns and won many battle merits; on returning from the assault on Diaoyu Mountain, his route passed through Henan, where he gathered more than a hundred refugee households and enrolled them all in the registers.

entries.zh: 罕禿忽子曰霍歷極，以疾廢，不能軍，世祖俾居於恩，以統其藩人。
entries.en: Qutugtu's son Qolije was crippled by illness and could not command troops; the Shizu Emperor therefore settled him at En to govern the family's retainers.
entries.literal: Qutugtu's son was Qolije; disabled by illness and unable to take the field, Shizu had him dwell at En to govern the prince's retainers.

entries.zh: 至大三年，霍歷極薨，子塔出嗣。
entries.en: In the third year of Zhida, Qolije died and was succeeded by his son Tachu.
entries.literal: In the third year of Zhida, Qolije died, and his son Tachu succeeded.

entries.zh: 塔出性溫厚，謙恭好學，通經史，能撫恤其民云。
entries.en: Tachu was gentle and even-tempered, modest and eager to learn, well read in the classics and histories, and able to win the loyalty of his people — or so the record runs.
entries.literal: Tachu was mild and generous by nature, humble and fond of learning, versed in the classics and histories, and able to comfort and care for his people — so it is said.

entries.zh: 牙忽都年十三，世祖命襲其祖父統軍。
entries.en: At thirteen, Yahudou was ordered by the Shizu Emperor to succeed his grandfather in command of the army.
entries.literal: When Yahudou was thirteen, Shizu ordered him to succeed his grandfather in command of the army.

entries.zh: 至元十二年，從北安王北征。
entries.en: In the twelfth year of Zhiyuan he followed the Prince of Bei'an on the northern campaign.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhiyuan, he followed the Prince of Bei'an on the northern campaign.

entries.zh: 十三年，失列吉叛，遣人誘脅之，牙忽都不從，事王益忠謹。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year Shiregi rebelled and sent envoys to win him over by threats and blandishments; Yahudou refused and served his prince with redoubled loyalty.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year, Shiregi rebelled and sent men to entice and coerce him; Yahudou would not follow, and served the prince with still greater loyalty and care.

entries.zh: 八魯渾拔都兒、粘闿與海都通，相率引去，王遣牙忽都將兵追之，擒八魯渾等以獻。
entries.en: Baluqun Batu'er and Nenkai were in league with Qaidu and withdrew their forces together; the prince sent Yahudou in pursuit, seized Baluqun and his fellows, and presented them as captives.
entries.literal: Baluqun Batu'er and Nenkai were in communication with Qaidu and led their men away in concert; the prince sent Yahudou with troops in pursuit, captured Baluqun and the others, and presented them.

entries.zh: 未幾，失列吉、約木忽兒、脫帖木兒等反，以兵攻王。
entries.en: Before long Shiregi, Yomuqur, Tötämur, and others rose in revolt and attacked the prince with an army.
entries.literal: Before long, Shiregi, Yomuqur, and Tötämur and others rebelled and attacked the prince with troops.

entries.zh: 脫帖木兒生致牙忽都，使失列吉拘系之。
entries.en: Tötämur captured Yahudou alive and handed him to Shiregi for imprisonment.
entries.literal: Tötämur took Yahudou alive and had Shiregi imprison him.

entries.zh: 牙忽都與王親臣那臺等謀逃歸，事覺，那臺等被殺，復系牙忽都，困辱備至。
entries.en: Yahudou conspired with the prince's close retainers Natai and others to flee home; the plot was discovered, Natai and his fellows were put to death, Yahudou was bound again, and subjected to every manner of abuse and hardship.
entries.literal: Yahudou plotted with the prince's intimate retainers Natai and others to escape and return; the affair was discovered, Natai and the others were killed, Yahudou was bound again, and humiliation and hardship were heaped on him to the full.

entries.zh: 十四年，兀魯兀臺、伯顏帥師討叛，失列吉、約木忽兒迎戰，牙忽都潛結赤斤帖木兒、禿禿哈亂其陣。
entries.en: In the fourteenth year Ulutai and Bayan marched against the rebels; as Shiregi and Yomuqur gave battle, Yahudou secretly coordinated with Chijin Temür and Tutuqa to throw their ranks into confusion.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year, Ulutai and Bayan led armies to suppress the rebels; Shiregi and Yomuqur met them in battle, and Yahudou secretly joined with Chijin Temür and Tutuqa to throw their formations into disorder.

entries.zh: 失列吉軍亂，因得脫走。
entries.en: Shiregi's army broke in disorder, and he slipped away in the confusion.
entries.literal: Shiregi's army fell into chaos, and he was thus able to escape.

entries.zh: 見帝，鬚髮盡白。
entries.en: When he came before the emperor, his beard and hair had turned completely white.
entries.literal: When he saw the Emperor, his beard and hair had turned entirely white.

entries.zh: 帝閔之，賞賚甚厚。
entries.en: The emperor took pity on him and lavished rewards upon him.
entries.literal: The Emperor pitied him and rewarded him very generously.

entries.zh: 至元十八年，加封耒陽州五千三百四十七戶。
entries.en: In the eighteenth year of Zhiyuan he received an additional grant of 5,347 households in Leiyang prefecture.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year of Zhiyuan, he was further granted 5,347 households of Leiyang prefecture.

entries.zh: 至大三年，察八兒來歸，宗親皆會。
entries.en: In the third year of Zhida, Chabar came in submission, and the imperial kin all gathered.
entries.literal: In the third year of Zhida, Chabar came to submit; the imperial clansmen all assembled.

entries.zh: 牙忽都進曰：「太祖皇帝削平四方，惟南土未定，列聖嗣位，未遑統一。
entries.en: Yahudou stepped forward and said, "The Great Ancestor subdued the four quarters, yet the south remained unsettled; each succeeding sovereign had no leisure to finish the work of unification.
entries.literal: Yahudou advanced and said: "The Great Ancestor Emperor subdued the four quarters, yet only the southern lands remained unsettled; successive sacred emperors succeeded to the throne but had no leisure to complete unification.

entries.zh: 世祖皇帝混一四海，顧惟宗室諸王，弗克同堂而燕。
entries.en: The Shizu Emperor united the four seas, yet the princes of the blood could not gather as one family under a single roof.
entries.literal: The Shizu Emperor unified the four seas, yet as for the princes of the imperial clan, they could not feast together under one roof.

entries.zh: 今陛下洪福齊天，拔都罕之裔，首已附順，叛王察八兒舉族來歸，人民境土，悉為一家。
entries.en: Now Your Majesty's fortune matches Heaven itself: the line of Batu Khan has led the way in submission, the rebel prince Chabar has brought his whole clan home, and peoples and lands are at last one household.
entries.literal: Now Your Majesty's vast fortune equals Heaven; the descendants of Batu Khan have been the first to submit, the rebel prince Chabar has come with his whole clan, and people, territory, and lands are all one household.

entries.zh: 地大物眾，有可恃者焉，有不可恃者焉。
entries.en: The realm is vast and its peoples many — there are things to rely upon, and things that must not be relied upon.
entries.literal: The realm is vast and its goods abundant — there are things on which one may rely, and things on which one may not rely.

entries.zh: 昔我太祖有訓，世祖誦之，臣與有聞，治亂國者，宜以法齊之，所以辨上下，定民誌。
entries.en: Long ago our Great Ancestor left a teaching that the Shizu Emperor used to recite — I was among those who heard it: whether a realm is well ordered or in turmoil, it should be brought into harmony by law, so that high and low are distinguished and the people's aims are fixed.
entries.literal: Formerly our Great Ancestor left an instruction that Shizu recited — your servant was among those who heard it: whoever governs a realm in order or in disorder should bring it into alignment by law, thereby distinguishing high and low and fixing the people's aims.

entries.zh: 今請有以氏整飭之，則人將有所勸懲，惟陛下鑒之。」
entries.en: I beg now that the imperial clan be regulated and set in order, so that men may know both reward and restraint — may Your Majesty take this to heart."
entries.literal: I now beg that there be means to regulate and put in order the clans, so that people will have encouragement and warning — may Your Majesty consider this."

entries.zh: 帝嘉納其言。
entries.en: The emperor approved his counsel warmly.
entries.literal: The Emperor praised and accepted his words.

entries.zh: 二十一年，命與禿禿哈同討海都，牙忽都先進，邏得諜人，知其虛實，直前沖敵陣，破其精兵，海都敗走，得所俘掠軍民而還。
entries.en: In the twenty-first year he was ordered to campaign against Qaidu alongside Tutuqa. Yahudou led the advance, took spies on the march and learned the enemy's strength, drove straight into their line, shattered their elite force, and put Qaidu to flight, recovering the soldiers and civilians who had been carried off before returning in triumph.
entries.literal: In the twenty-first year, he was ordered to join Tutuqa in campaigning against Qaidu; Yahudou advanced first, on the road captured spies and learned the enemy's condition, charged straight into the enemy formation, broke their elite troops, Qaidu was defeated and fled, and he recovered the soldiers and civilians who had been seized and returned.

entries.zh: 朵兒朵哈上其功，詔賜鈔幣、鎧甲、弓矢。
entries.en: Dordoq reported his achievements to the throne, and an edict rewarded him with banknotes, armor, bows, and arrows.
entries.literal: Dordoq reported his merit, and an edict granted him paper money, armor, bows, and arrows.

entries.zh: 其後北安王駐帖木兒河。
entries.en: Thereafter the Prince of Bei'an encamped on the Tümel River.
entries.literal: Afterward the Prince of Bei'an encamped on the Tümel River.

entries.zh: 乃顏、也不堅有異圖，也不堅引兵趨怯綠憐河大帳。
entries.en: Nayan and Yebuqa harbored treasonous designs, and Yebuqa marched his troops toward the great tent on the Qielülin River.
entries.literal: Nayan and Yebuqa harbored disloyal designs; Yebuqa led troops toward the great tent on the Qielülin River.

entries.zh: 王遣闊闊出、禿禿哈率眾追之。
entries.en: The prince sent Kököchü and Tutuqa in pursuit at the head of the host.
entries.literal: The prince sent Kököchü and Tutuqa to lead the host in pursuit.

entries.zh: 那懷之民擾攘不知所從。
entries.en: The people of Nayir were thrown into confusion, unsure whom to follow.
entries.literal: The people of Nayir were in turmoil and did not know whom to follow.

entries.zh: 牙忽都將三百騎，進至阿赤怯地。
entries.en: Yahudou led three hundred horsemen forward to Aqiqie.
entries.literal: Yahudou led three hundred horsemen and advanced to Aqiqie.

entries.zh: 會王帳下遜篤思部兵逃去，牙忽都諭之使還。
entries.en: At that moment troops of the Sundusi division under the prince's command had deserted; Yahudou persuaded them to return.
entries.literal: It happened that troops of the Sundusi division under the prince's tent had fled; Yahudou admonished them and had them return.

entries.zh: 時怯必禿忽兒霍臺誘蒙古軍二萬從乃顏，牙忽都知之，夜襲其河上軍，突入帳中，遇忽都滅兒堅，幾獲之，間道逸去。
entries.en: Qibitughur Huotai had meanwhile won twenty thousand Mongol troops to Nayan's side; learning of this, Yahudou struck their riverside camp by night, broke into the tent, and nearly seized Hudumirjian, who escaped by a hidden route.
entries.literal: At that time Qibitughur Huotai had enticed twenty thousand Mongol troops to follow Nayan; Yahudou learned of it, raided their river-bank army by night, burst into the tent, encountered Hudumirjian, nearly captured him, but he escaped by a bypath.

entries.zh: 二十七年，海都入寇。
entries.en: In the twenty-seventh year Qaidu invaded.
entries.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, Qaidu invaded.

entries.zh: 時朵兒哈方居守大帳，詔遣牙忽都同力備禦。
entries.en: Dordoq was then stationed to guard the great tent; an edict sent Yahudou to join him in the defense.
entries.literal: At that time Dordoq was stationed guarding the great tent; an edict sent Yahudou to join forces in defense.

entries.zh: 軍未戰而潰，牙忽都妻帑輜重駐不思哈剌嶺上，悉為藥木忽兒、明理帖木兒所掠。
entries.en: The army broke before a blow was struck; Yahudou's wife, household, baggage train, and supplies, encamped on Mount Busihala, were all seized by Yomuqur and Mingli Temür.
entries.literal: The army collapsed before battle was joined; Yahudou's wife, dependents, baggage, and supplies, encamped on Mount Busihala, were all plundered by Yomuqur and Mingli Temür.

entries.zh: 牙忽都與其子脫列帖木兒相失，獨與十三騎奔還。
entries.en: Yahudou was separated from his son Tele Temür and fled back with only thirteen horsemen.
entries.literal: Yahudou was separated from his son Tele Temür and fled back with only thirteen riders.

entries.zh: 世祖撫慰嘉嘆，賜爵鎮遠王，塗金銀印，以弘吉剌氏女賜之，資裝特厚。
entries.en: The Shizu Emperor comforted and praised him, enfeoffed him as Prince Who Pacifies the Distant, granted a gilded silver seal, gave him a Kongirat bride, and endowed him with exceptional wealth.
entries.literal: Shizu comforted and praised him, granted him the title Prince Who Pacifies the Distant, a gilded silver seal, and a daughter of the Kongirat clan in marriage, with exceptionally rich endowment.

entries.zh: 復命納裏忽、徹徹不花往錫命其部屬同時被剽掠者，以故相桑哥家財分賜之，仍各賜白金五十兩、珠子一酒扈，鈔幣稱是。
entries.en: He further ordered Nariqhu and Cheche Buqa to go and comfort his retainers who had suffered the same raids, distributing among them the household wealth of the late Chancellor Sangha, and granting each fifty taels of silver, a measure of pearls, and banknotes in proportion besides.
entries.literal: He further ordered Nariqhu and Cheche Buqa to go and bestow favors on his retainers who had likewise been plundered, dividing among them the household wealth of the former chancellor Sangha, and still granting each fifty taels of white silver, one wine-measure of pearls, and paper money in proportion.

entries.zh: 又命牙忽都居北安王第二帳。
entries.en: He also assigned Yahudou to the Prince of Bei'an's second encampment.
entries.literal: He also ordered Yahudou to dwell at the Prince of Bei'an's second tent.

entries.zh: 王薨，帝命掌大帳，固辭。
entries.en: When the prince died, the emperor ordered him to take charge of the great tent, but he firmly declined.
entries.literal: When the prince died, the Emperor ordered him to take charge of the great tent, but he firmly declined.

entries.zh: 成宗立，命牙忽都常侍左右。
entries.en: When Emperor Chengzong ascended the throne, he kept Yahudou constantly at his side.
entries.literal: When Emperor Chengzong took the throne, he ordered Yahudou to attend constantly at his side.

entries.zh: 武宗撫兵漠北，請以子脫列帖木兒從。
entries.en: When Emperor Wuzong raised troops in the northern steppe, he asked that Yahudou's son Tele Temür accompany him.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wuzong mustered troops in the northern deserts, he requested that Yahudou's son Tele Temür follow him.

entries.zh: 大德五年，海都、篤哇合軍入寇，脫列帖木兒將兵千人擁護，先後力戰，功多，在軍十年。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Dade, Qaidu and Duwa joined forces and invaded; Tele Temür commanded a thousand men in the imperial guard, fought again and again with distinction, and served in the field for ten years.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Dade, Qaidu and Duwa combined their armies and invaded; Tele Temür led a thousand troops in escort, fought strenuously again and again, won much merit, and was in the army for ten years.

entries.zh: 成宗崩，安西王阿難答與明理帖木兒窺望神器。
entries.en: When Emperor Chengzong died, Prince of Anxi Ananda and Mingli Temür cast covetous eyes on the throne.
entries.literal: When Emperor Chengzong died, Prince of Anxi Ananda and Mingli Temür cast covetous eyes on the imperial succession.

entries.zh: 牙忽都曰：「世祖皇帝之嫡孫在，神器所當屬。
entries.en: Yahudou said, "The legitimate grandson of the Shizu Emperor is here; the throne ought to belong to him.
entries.literal: Yahudou said: "The legitimate grandson of Emperor Shizu is present; the sacred vessel ought to belong to him.

entries.zh: 安西藩王也，入繼非制。」
entries.en: He is Prince of Anxi — for a border prince to enter and succeed is against precedent."
entries.literal: He is a border prince of Anxi — for him to enter and succeed is against precedent."

entries.zh: 武宗即位，以其父子勞效忠勤，益厚遇之，進封楚王，賜金印，置王傅，以駙馬都尉都剌哈之女弟弘吉剌氏為楚王妃，又以叛王察八兒親屬賜之。
entries.en: When Emperor Wuzong ascended the throne, honoring the father and son's labor, merit, loyalty, and diligence, he treated them still more generously, advanced Yahudou to Prince of Chu, granted a gold seal, appointed a prince's tutor, made the younger sister of Chief Commandant of Horse Dulaqa of the Kongirat clan Princess of Chu, and also granted him relatives of the rebel prince Chabar.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wuzong took the throne, in recognition of the father and son's labor, merit, loyalty, and diligence, he treated them still more generously, advanced Yahudou to Prince of Chu, granted a gold seal, established a prince's tutor, made the younger sister of Chief Commandant of Horse Dulaqa of the Kongirat clan Princess of Chu, and also granted him relatives of the rebel prince Chabar.

entries.zh: 脫列帖木兒襲封鎮遠王。
entries.en: Tele Temür succeeded as Prince Who Pacifies the Distant.
entries.literal: Tele Temür succeeded as Prince Who Pacifies the Distant.

entries.zh: 寬徹普化，世祖之孫，鎮南王脫歡子也。
entries.en: Kuanchepuhua was a grandson of the Shizu Emperor and son of Prince of Zhennan Togan.
entries.literal: Kuanchepuhua was a grandson of Shizu and son of the Prince of Zhennan, Togan.

entries.zh: 泰定三年，封威順王，鎮武昌，賜金印，撥付怯薛丹五百名，又自募至一千名。
entries.en: In the third year of Taiding he was enfeoffed as Prince of Weishun and posted to Wuchang with a gold seal, five hundred keshik guards assigned to him, and recruits of his own bringing the total to a thousand.
entries.literal: In the third year of Taiding he was enfeoffed as Prince of Weishun, stationed at Wuchang, granted a gold seal, allotted five hundred keshik guards, and himself recruited up to a thousand.

entries.zh: 設王傳官屬。
entries.en: A prince's tutor and full staff of officials were appointed.
entries.literal: He established the prince's tutor and official staff.

entries.zh: 湖廣行省供億錢糧衣裝，歲支米三萬石，錢三萬二千錠，又日給王子諸妃飲膳。
entries.en: The Huguang branch secretariat supplied his funds, grain, clothing, and equipment — thirty thousand shi of grain and thirty-two thousand ding of money each year — and provided daily for the prince and his consorts at table.
entries.literal: The Huguang Branch Secretariat supplied funds, grain, clothing, and equipment — annually disbursing thirty thousand shi of grain and thirty-two thousand ding of money — and also provided daily for the prince's and consorts' food and drink.

entries.zh: 文宗天歷初，賜寬徹普化金銀各五十兩、幣三十匹，仍鎮湖廣，而寬徹普化縱怯薛等官侵奪民利，民頗患苦之。
entries.en: At the opening of the Tianli reign under Emperor Wenzong, Kuanchepuhua received fifty taels each of gold and silver and thirty bolts of silk, and remained in command of Huguang — yet he allowed his keshik and other officers to prey on the people's livelihood, to the people's great distress.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianli under Emperor Wenzong, Kuanchepuhua was granted fifty taels each of gold and silver and thirty bolts of silks, and continued to guard Huguang; yet Kuanchepuhua indulged his keshik and other officials in seizing the people's profits, and the people suffered greatly from it.

entries.zh: 至元五年，太師伯顏矯制召赴京，貶之。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Zhiyuan, Grand Preceptor Bayan summoned him to the capital under a forged edict and had him degraded.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Zhiyuan, Grand Preceptor Bayan, by a forged edict, summoned him to the capital and degraded him.

entries.zh: 及脫脫為相，始明其無辜，命復還鎮。
entries.en: When Toqto became chancellor, his innocence was finally established, and he was ordered back to his command.
entries.literal: When Toqto became chancellor, his innocence was at last made clear, and he was ordered to return to his post.

entries.zh: 至正二年，湖北廉訪司糾言，寬徹普化恃以宗室，恣行不法。
entries.en: In the second year of Zhizheng the Hubei surveillance commission impeached him, charging that Kuanchepuhua, trusting in his imperial birth, acted lawlessly at will.
entries.literal: In the second year of Zhizheng, the Hubei surveillance commission impeached him, saying Kuanchepuhua relied on his status as imperial clansman and acted lawlessly at will.

entries.zh: 不報。
entries.en: The court took no action.
entries.literal: No response was given.

entries.zh: 帖木兒不花，世祖孫，鎮南王脫歡第四子也。
entries.en: Tiemu'er Buhua was a grandson of the Shizu Emperor and the fourth son of Prince of Zhennan Togan.
entries.literal: Tiemu'er Buhua was a grandson of Shizu and the fourth son of the Prince of Zhennan, Togan.

entries.zh: 初，世祖第九子脫歡以討安南無成功，終身不許見，遂封鎮南王，出鎮揚州。
entries.en: At first Shizu's ninth son Togan, having failed in his campaign against Annam, was denied audience for the rest of his life; he was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhennan and posted to Yangzhou.
entries.literal: At first, Shizu's ninth son Togan, having campaigned against Annam without success, was never permitted an audience for the rest of his life; he was therefore enfeoffed as Prince of Zhennan and sent out to guard Yangzhou.

entries.zh: 脫歡薨，子老章襲封鎮南王。
entries.en: When Togan died, his son Laozhang succeeded as Prince of Zhennan.
entries.literal: When Togan died, his son Laozhang succeeded to the title Prince of Zhennan.

entries.zh: 老章薨，弟脫不花襲封鎮南王。
entries.en: When Laozhang died, his younger brother Tuobuhua succeeded as Prince of Zhennan.
entries.literal: When Laozhang died, his younger brother Tuobuhua succeeded as Prince of Zhennan.

entries.zh: 脫不花薨，子孛羅不花幼，帖木兒不花乃嗣為鎮南王。
entries.en: When Tuobuhua died his son Boluo Buhua was still a child, and Tiemu'er Buhua succeeded as Prince of Zhennan.
entries.literal: When Tuobuhua died, his son Boluo Buhua was still young, and Tiemu'er Buhua therefore succeeded as Prince of Zhennan.

entries.zh: 文宗天歷初，賜帖木兒不花黃金五十兩、白金五十兩、幣三十匹。
entries.en: At the opening of the Tianli reign under Emperor Wenzong, Tiemu'er Buhua received fifty taels of gold, fifty of silver, and thirty bolts of silk.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianli under Emperor Wenzong, Tiemu'er Buhua was granted fifty taels of gold, fifty of silver, and thirty bolts of silks.

entries.zh: 二年，孛羅不花已長，帖木兒不花請以其位復還孛羅不花。
entries.en: In the second year Boluo Buhua had come of age, and Tiemu'er Buhua asked to return the title to him.
entries.literal: In the second year, Boluo Buhua had come of age, and Tiemu'er Buhua requested to restore the title to Boluo Buhua.

entries.zh: 朝廷以其讓而不居也，改封宣讓王，賜金印，移鎮於廬州。
entries.en: The court, honoring his willingness to yield the title, enfeoffed him instead as Prince of Xuanrang, granted a gold seal, and transferred his command to Luzhou.
entries.literal: The court, because he yielded and would not hold the post, changed his enfeoffment to Prince of Xuanrang, granted a gold seal, and moved his command to Luzhou.

entries.zh: 順帝至元元年，撥廬州、饒州牧地一百頃賜之。
entries.en: In the first year of Zhiyuan under Emperor Shundi he received a grant of one hundred qing of pasture in Luzhou and Raozhou.
entries.literal: In the first year of Zhiyuan under Emperor Shundi, one hundred qing of pasture land in Luzhou and Raozhou were allotted and granted to him.

entries.zh: 二年，賜市宅錢四千錠，命其王府官凡班次列於有司之右。
entries.en: In the second year he received four thousand ding to purchase a residence, and the officials of his princely household were ranked above those of the regular administration.
entries.literal: In the second year, four thousand ding were granted for purchasing a residence, and his princely household officials were ordered to rank above the regular offices in precedence.

entries.zh: 五年，伯彥擅權，矯制貶帖木兒不花及威順王寬徹普化。
entries.en: In the fifth year Bayan seized power and, by forged edict, degraded Tiemu'er Buhua and Prince of Weishun Kuanchepuhua.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, Bayan seized power arbitrarily and, by a forged edict, degraded Tiemu'er Buhua and the Prince of Weishun, Kuanchepuhua.

entries.zh: 至脫脫為相，始言於帝，明此兩王者皆無辜，詔令復還鎮。
entries.en: When Toqto became chancellor he laid the matter before the emperor, showing that both princes were innocent, and an edict restored them to their commands.
entries.literal: When Toqto became chancellor, he first spoke to the Emperor and made clear that both these princes were innocent; an edict ordered them to return to their posts.

entries.zh: 至正十二年，廬州境內賊起，淮西廉訪使陳思謙言於帖木兒不花曰：「王以帝室之胄，鎮撫淮甸，豈宜坐視。
entries.en: In the twelfth year of Zhizheng rebels rose within Luzhou, and Huai-Xi surveillance commissioner Chen Siqian said to Tiemu'er Buhua, "Your Highness, as blood of the imperial house charged with pacifying the Huai region, how can you stand aside?
entries.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhizheng, bandits rose within Luzhou; the Huai-Xi surveillance commissioner Chen Siqian said to Tiemu'er Buhua: "Your Highness, as a scion of the imperial house charged with pacifying the Huai region, how can you sit and watch?

entries.zh: 且府中官屬及怯薛丹人等數甚多，必有可使摧鋒陷陣者，惟王圖之。」
entries.en: Your household officials and keshik are many — surely some can break the enemy line and drive into their ranks. The rest is for Your Highness to decide."
entries.literal: Moreover, the officials of your household and the keshik and others are very numerous — there must be men who can break the enemy line and drive into their ranks; only Your Highness need plan it."

entries.zh: 帖木兒不花大悟其言，曰：「此吾責也。」
entries.en: Tiemu'er Buhua took his meaning at once and said, "This is my duty."
entries.literal: Tiemu'er Buhua was greatly enlightened by his words and said: "This is my duty."

entries.zh: 即命以所部兵及諸王乞塔歹等，分道擊賊，擒其渠帥，廬州境內皆平。
entries.en: He at once sent his own troops and the princes Qitadai and others against the rebels by separate routes, captured their leaders, and pacified the whole of Luzhou.
entries.literal: He immediately ordered his own troops and the princes Qitadai and others to strike the rebels by separate routes, captured their chieftains, and the whole territory within Luzhou was pacified.

entries.zh: 帝聞之，賜金帶、銀鈔，以賞其功。
entries.en: When the emperor heard of it, he rewarded him with a gold belt and silver banknotes.
entries.literal: When the Emperor heard of it, he granted a gold belt and silver notes to reward his merit.

entries.zh: 十六年，命帖木兒不花與寬徹普化以兵鎮遏懷慶路，賜金銀各一錠、幣帛九匹、鈔二十錠。
entries.en: In the sixteenth year Tiemu'er Buhua and Kuanchepuhua were ordered to garrison the Huaiqing circuit; each received one ingot of gold and silver, nine bolts of silk, and twenty ding of banknotes.
entries.literal: In the sixteenth year, Tiemu'er Buhua and Kuanchepuhua were ordered to hold the Huaiqing circuit with troops; each was granted one ingot of gold and silver, nine bolts of silks, and twenty ding of paper money.

entries.zh: 既而汝、潁之寇南渡淮，帖木兒不花復以便宜，調芍陂屯軍拒之。
entries.en: Before long the rebels of Ru and Ying crossed the Huai southward; Tiemu'er Buhua on his own authority mobilized the garrison at Quepi to hold them.
entries.literal: Before long the raiders of Ru and Ying crossed the Huai southward; Tiemu'er Buhua again on his own authority mobilized the garrison troops at Quepi to resist them.

entries.zh: 及廬州不守，乃挈身北歸，留京師。
entries.en: When Luzhou could no longer be held, he withdrew north and remained at the capital.
entries.literal: When Luzhou could no longer be held, he took himself north and remained in the capital.

entries.zh: 二十七年，進封淮王，賜金印，設王傅等官。
entries.en: In the twenty-seventh year he was advanced to Prince of Huai, granted a gold seal, and given a prince's tutor and full staff of officials.
entries.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, he was advanced to Prince of Huai, granted a gold seal, and a prince's tutor and other offices were established.

entries.zh: 二十八年，大明兵逼京師，順帝北奔，詔以帖木兒不花監國，而拜慶童中書左丞相輔之。
entries.en: In the twenty-eighth year, as the armies of the Great Ming closed on the capital, Emperor Shundi fled north; an edict named Tiemu'er Buhua to oversee the realm, with Qing Tong as left chancellor of the Secretariat to assist him.
entries.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, as the Great Ming army pressed the capital, Emperor Shundi fled north; an edict appointed Tiemu'er Buhua to oversee the state, with Qing Tong made left chancellor of the Secretariat to assist him.

entries.zh: 俄而城破，帖木兒不花死之，年八十三。
entries.en: Before long the city fell, and Tiemu'er Buhua perished at the age of eighty-three.
entries.literal: Before long the city fell, and Tiemu'er Buhua died — aged eighty-three.

entries.zh: 別裏古臺
entries.en: Belgutei
entries.literal: Belgutei

entries.zh: 特薛禪，姓孛思忽兒，弘吉剌氏，世居朔漠。
entries.en: Texuechan, of the Besihuer branch of the Hongjila clan, had lived for generations in the northern steppe.
entries.literal: Texuechan, surname Besihuer, of the Hongjila clan, for generations dwelt in the northern desert.

entries.zh: 本名特，因從太祖起兵有功，賜名薛禪，故兼稱曰特薛禪。
entries.en: Originally named Te, he earned the name Xuechan for meritorious service when Genghis Khan raised his army, and was thereafter known as Texuechan.
entries.literal: His original name was Te; because he had merit following Taizu in raising troops, he was granted the name Xuechan, hence he was also called Texuechan.

entries.zh: 女曰孛兒台，太祖光獻翼聖皇后。
entries.en: His daughter Boertai became Genghis Khan's Radiant Offering Assisting Sagely Empress.
entries.literal: His daughter was Boertai, Taizus Radiant Offering Assisting Sagely Empress.

entries.zh: 子曰按陳，從太祖征伐，凡三十二戰，平西夏，斷潼關道，取回紇尋斯干城，皆與有功。
entries.en: His son Anchen followed Genghis Khan on thirty-two campaigns, helping pacify Western Xia, sever the Tong Pass route, and capture the Uyghur city of Xingsigan.
entries.literal: His son was Anchannayan, who followed Taizu on campaigns—in all thirty-two battles, pacifying Western Xia, cutting the Tong Pass road, and taking the Uyghur city of Xingsigan—all with merit.

entries.zh: 歲丁亥，賜號國舅按陳那顏。
entries.en: In the dinghai year he received the title Imperial Uncle Anchannayan Noyan.
entries.literal: In the dinghai year he was granted the title Imperial Uncle Anchannayan Noyan.

entries.zh: 壬辰，賜銀印，封河西王，以統其國族。
entries.en: In renchen he received a silver seal and was enfeoffed King of Hexi to govern his people.
entries.literal: In renchen he was granted a silver seal and enfeoffed King of Hexi to command his clansmen.

entries.zh: 丁酉，賜錢二十萬緡，有旨：「弘吉剌氏生女世以為后，生男世尚公主，每歲四時孟月，聽讀所賜旨，世世不絕。」
entries.en: In dingyou he received two hundred thousand strings of cash along with an edict: "Hongjila daughters shall become empresses for generations; Hongjila sons shall marry imperial princesses for generations; in the first month of each season they shall hear this edict read—forever without end."
entries.literal: In dingyou he was granted two hundred thousand strings of cash, with an edict: "Hongjila daughters shall generation after generation become empresses; Hongjila sons shall generation after generation marry imperial princesses; in the first month of each of the four seasons every year they shall hear the granted edict read—generation after generation without end."

entries.zh: 又賜所俘獲軍民五千二百，仍授萬戶以領之。
entries.en: He was further granted five thousand two hundred captured soldiers and civilians and appointed myriarch over them.
entries.literal: Again he was granted five thousand two hundred captured soldiers and civilians and appointed myriarch to command them.

entries.zh: 按陳薨，葬官人山。
entries.en: Anchannayan died and was buried at Mount Guanren.
entries.literal: Anchannayan died and was buried at Mount Guanren.

entries.zh: 元貞元年二月，追封濟寧王，諡忠武；
entries.en: In the second month of 1295 he was posthumously enfeoffed as King of Jining with the epithet Loyal Martial;
entries.literal: In the second month of the first year of Yuanzhen he was posthumously enfeoffed King of Jining with posthumous epithet Loyal Martial;

entries.zh: 妻哈真，追封濟寧王妃。
entries.en: his wife Hazhen was posthumously made Princess of Jining.
entries.literal: his wife Hazhen was posthumously enfeoffed Princess of Jining.

entries.zh: 子斡陳，歲戊戌授萬戶，尚睿宗女也速不花公主。
entries.en: His son Wochen was appointed myriarch in wuxu and married Toluis daughter Princess Yesubuhua.
entries.literal: His son Wochen, in the wuxu year appointed myriarch, married Ruizongs daughter Princess Yesubuhua.

entries.zh: 斡陳薨，葬不海韓。
entries.en: Wochen died and was buried at Buhaihan.
entries.literal: Wochen died and was buried at Buhaihan.

entries.zh: 弟納陳，歲丁巳襲萬戶，奉旨伐宋，攻釣魚山。
entries.en: His younger brother Nachan inherited the myriarchate in dingsi, received orders to campaign against Song, and attacked Diaoyu Mountain.
entries.literal: His younger brother Nachan, in the dingsi year inheriting the myriarchate, received orders to attack Song and assault Diaoyu Mountain.

entries.zh: 又從世祖南涉淮甸，下大清口，獲船百餘艘。
entries.en: He also followed Kublai south across the Huai region, seized Daqingkou, and captured more than a hundred ships.
entries.literal: Again he followed Shizu south across the Huai region, took Daqingkou, and captured more than a hundred vessels.

entries.zh: 又率兵平山東濟、兖、單等州。
entries.en: He further led troops to pacify the Shandong prefectures of Ji, Yan, Shan, and others.
entries.literal: Again he led troops to pacify the Shandong prefectures Ji, Yan, Shan, and others.

entries.zh: 及阿里不哥叛，中統二年與諸王北伐，以其子哈海、脫歡、斡羅陳等十人自從，至于莽來，由失木魯與阿里不哥之黨八兒哈八兒思等戰，追北至孛羅克禿，復戰，自旦及夕，斬首萬級，僵尸被野。
entries.en: When Ariq Böke rebelled, in 1261 he joined the princes on the northern campaign with ten sons including Hahai, Tuohuan, and Woluochen. At Manglai he fought Ariq Böke's partisan Baerhabaersi from Shimur, pursued north to Boluoketu, and fought again from dawn to dusk, taking ten thousand heads until corpses covered the plain.
entries.literal: When Ariq Böke rebelled, in the second year of Zhongtong he joined the northern campaign with the princes, taking ten of his sons including Hahai, Tuohuan, and Woluochen; reaching Manglai, from Shimur he fought Ariq Bökes partisan Baerhabaersi and others, pursued north to Boluoketu, fought again from dawn to evening, beheaded ten thousand ranks, and corpses covered the fields.

entries.zh: 薨，葬末懷禿。
entries.en: He died and was buried at Mohuaitu.
entries.literal: He died and was buried at Mohuaitu.

entries.zh: 斡羅陳襲萬戶，尚完澤公主。
entries.en: Woluochen inherited the myriarchate and married Princess Wanzhe.
entries.literal: Woluochen inherited the myriarchate and married Princess Wanzhe.

entries.zh: 完澤公主薨，繼尚囊加真公主。
entries.en: After Princess Wanzhe died he married Princess Nangjiazhen.
entries.literal: When Princess Wanzhe died he next married Princess Nangjiazhen.

entries.zh: 至元十四年薨，葬拓剌里。
entries.en: He died in 1277 and was buried at Tuolali.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhiyuan he died and was buried at Tuolali.

entries.zh: 無子。
entries.en: He left no son.
entries.literal: He had no son.

entries.zh: 弟曰帖木兒，至元十八年襲萬戶。
entries.en: His younger brother Tiemuer inherited the myriarchate in 1281.
entries.literal: His younger brother was Tiemuer; in the eighteenth year of Zhiyuan he inherited the myriarchate.

entries.zh: 二十四年，乃顏叛，從帝親征，以功封濟寧郡王，賜白傘蓋以寵之。
entries.en: In the twenty-fourth year, when Nayan rebelled, he joined the emperor's personal campaign, was enfeoffed as Prince of Jining Commandery for his merit, and granted a white parasol canopy.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, when Nayan rebelled, he followed the emperor on the personal campaign; for merit he was enfeoffed Prince of Jining Commandery and granted a white parasol canopy as favor.

entries.zh: 二十五年，諸王哈丹禿魯干叛，與諸王及統兵官玉速帖木兒等率兵討之，由龜剌河與哈丹等遇，轉戰至惱木連河，殲其眾。
entries.en: In the twenty-fifth year, when Prince Hadantuolugan rebelled, he joined princes and the commander Yusutiemuer, met Hadan at the Guila River, fought through to the Naomulian River, and destroyed their army.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fifth year Prince Hadantuolugan rebelled; with princes and the commanding officer Yusutiemuer and others he led troops to suppress them; from Guila River he met Hadan and the rest, fought through to Naomulian River, and annihilated their forces.

entries.zh: 帝賜名按答兒禿那顏，以旌其功。
entries.en: The emperor granted him the name Anchadartu Noyan to honor his achievement.
entries.literal: The emperor granted him the name Anchadartu Noyan to honor his merit.

entries.zh: 薨，葬末懷禿。
entries.en: He died and was buried at Mohuaitu.
entries.literal: He died and was buried at Mohuaitu.

entries.zh: 子二人：長曰琱阿不剌，次曰桑哥不剌，皆幼。
entries.en: He had two sons: the elder Diaobubula and the younger Sangebubula, both still young.
entries.literal: He had two sons: the elder Diaobubula and the younger Sangebubula—both young.

entries.zh: 至元二十七年，以其弟蠻子台襲萬戶。
entries.en: In 1290 his younger brother Manzitai inherited the myriarchate.
entries.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Zhiyuan his younger brother Manzitai inherited the myriarchate.

entries.zh: 亦尚囊加真公主。
entries.en: He also married Princess Nangjiazhen.
entries.literal: He also married Princess Nangjiazhen.

entries.zh: 成宗即位，封皇姑魯國大長公主，以金印封蠻子台為濟寧王。
entries.en: When Temür acceded, the imperial paternal aunt was made Grand Princess of Lu, and Manzitai was enfeoffed King of Jining with a gold seal.
entries.literal: When Chengzong acceded, the imperial paternal aunt was enfeoffed Grand Princess of Lu; with a gold seal Manzitai was enfeoffed King of Jining.

entries.zh: 奉旨率本部兵討叛王海都、篤哇，既與之遇，方約戰，行伍未定，單騎突入陣中，往復數四，敵兵大擾，一戰遂大捷。
entries.en: Ordered to lead his tribesmen against the rebel princes Qaidu and Duwa, he met the enemy just as battle was forming. Before the ranks were set he charged alone into their lines several times, threw them into disorder, and won a great victory.
entries.literal: By imperial order he led his tribes troops to suppress the rebel princes Qaidu and Duwa; having met them, just as battle was to be joined and ranks not yet set, he charged alone into the enemy array back and forth several times; the enemy troops were greatly thrown into disorder and one battle brought a great victory.

entries.zh: 時武宗在藩邸，統大軍以鎮朔方，有旨令蠻子台總領蒙古軍民官，轉武宗守莽來，以遏北方。
entries.en: At that time Wuzong was holding a princely command, leading a great army to guard the northern frontier; an edict ordered Manzitai to take overall charge of Mongol military and civilian offices and transfer to Wuzong's garrison at Manglai to check the north.
entries.literal: At that time Wuzong was at the princely residence commanding a great army to guard the northern frontier; an edict ordered Manzitai to take overall charge of Mongol military and civilian offices and transfer to Wuzongs garrison at Manglai to check the north.

entries.zh: 囊加真公主薨，繼尚裕宗女喃哥不剌公主。
entries.en: After Princess Nangjiazhen died he married Yuzongs daughter Princess Nangebubula.
entries.literal: When Princess Nangjiazhen died he next married Yuzongs daughter Princess Nangebubula.

entries.zh: 蠻子台薨，年五十有二。
entries.en: Manzitai died at the age of fifty-two.
entries.literal: Manzitai died at age fifty-two.

entries.zh: 大德十一年三月，按答兒禿長子琱阿不剌襲萬戶，尚祥哥剌吉公主。
entries.en: In the third month of 1307, Anchadartus eldest son Diaobubula inherited the myriarchate and married Princess Xianggeleji.
entries.literal: In the third month of the eleventh year of Dade, Anchadartus eldest son Diaobubula inherited the myriarchate and married Princess Xianggeleji.

entries.zh: 六月，封大長公主，賜琱阿不剌金印，加封魯王。
entries.en: In the sixth month she was made Grand Princess; Diaobubula received a gold seal and was further enfeoffed as King of Lu.
entries.literal: In the sixth month she was enfeoffed Grand Princess; Diaobubula was granted a gold seal and further enfeoffed King of Lu.

entries.zh: 至大二年，賜平江稻田一千五百頃。
entries.en: In 1309 he was granted fifteen hundred qing of rice paddies in Pingjiang.
entries.literal: In the second year of Zhida he was granted fifteen hundred qing of rice paddies in Pingjiang.

entries.zh: 皇慶間，加封皇姊大長公主。
entries.en: During Huangqing she was further enfeoffed as the emperor's elder sister, Grand Princess.
entries.literal: During Huangqing she was further enfeoffed Grand Princess, elder sister of the emperor.

entries.zh: 天曆間，加號皇姑徽文懿貞壽大長公主。
entries.en: During Tianli she received the further title Imperial Paternal Aunt, Grand Princess of Splendid Culture, Graceful Virtue, Chaste Longevity.
entries.literal: During Tianli her title was further raised to Imperial Paternal Aunt, Grand Princess of Splendid Culture, Graceful Virtue, Chaste Longevity.

entries.zh: 至大三年，琱阿不剌薨，葬末懷禿。
entries.en: In 1310 Diaobubula died and was buried at Mohuaitu.
entries.literal: In the third year of Zhida Diaobubula died and was buried at Mohuaitu.

entries.zh: 阿里嘉室利，琱阿不剌嫡子也。
entries.en: Alijiashili was Diaobubulas legitimate son.
entries.literal: Alijiashili was Diaobubulas legitimate son.

entries.zh: 至大三年，甫八歲，襲萬戶。
entries.en: In 1310, at only eight years of age, he inherited the myriarchate.
entries.literal: In the third year of Zhida, only eight years old, he inherited the myriarchate.

entries.zh: 四年七月，襲封魯王，尚朵兒只班公主。
entries.en: In the seventh month of the following year he inherited the title King of Lu and married Princess Duoerzhiban.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year he inherited enfeoffment as King of Lu and married Princess Duoerzhiban.

entries.zh: 元統元年，阿里嘉失利薨。
entries.en: In 1333 Alijiashili died.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yuantong Alijiashili died.

entries.zh: 至順間，封朵兒只班號肅雍賢寧公主。
entries.en: During Zhishun Duoerzhiban was enfeoffed as Princess Suyong Xianning.
entries.literal: During Zhishun Duoerzhiban was enfeoffed Princess Suoyong Xianning.

entries.zh: 桑哥不剌者，魯王琱阿不剌之弟、阿里嘉室利之叔也。
entries.en: Sangebubula was the younger brother of King of Lu Diaobubula and uncle of Alijiashili.
entries.literal: Sangebubula was King of Lu Diaobubulas younger brother and Alijiashilis uncle.

entries.zh: 自幼奉世皇旨，養于斡可珍公主所，是為不只兒駙馬，後襲統其本部民四百戶。
entries.en: From childhood, by Kublai's order, he was raised in Princess Wokezhen's household and became the consort Bozhuer; later he inherited four hundred households of his tribe's people.
entries.literal: From youth by Shizu emperors order he was raised in Princess Wokezhens household and became the consort Bozhuer; later he inherited command of four hundred households of his tribes people.

entries.zh: 成宗時，奉旨尚普納公主；
entries.en: Under Temür he was ordered to marry Princess Puna;
entries.literal: In Chengzongs time by imperial order he married Princess Puna;

entries.zh: 至順間，封鄆安大長公主，授桑哥不剌金印，封鄆安王，職千戶。
entries.en: during Zhishun she was made Grand Princess of Yun'an; Sangebubula received a gold seal and was enfeoffed as King of Yun'an with a chiliarchate.
entries.literal: during Zhishun she was enfeoffed Grand Princess of Yun'an; Sangebubula was granted a gold seal and enfeoffed King of Yun'an with the office of chiliarch.

entries.zh: 元統元年，授萬戶。
entries.en: In 1333 he was appointed myriarch.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yuantong he was appointed myriarch.

entries.zh: 二年三月，加封鄆安公主號皇姑大長公主；
entries.en: In the third month of the following year the Princess of Yun'an was further titled Imperial Paternal Aunt, Grand Princess;
entries.literal: In the third month of the second year the Princess of Yun'an was further enfeoffed Imperial Paternal Aunt Grand Princess;

entries.zh: 加封桑哥不剌魯王。
entries.en: and Sangebubula was further enfeoffed as King of Lu.
entries.literal: Sangebubula was further enfeoffed King of Lu.

entries.zh: 以疾薨，年六十一。
entries.en: He died of illness at the age of sixty-one.
entries.literal: He died of illness at age sixty-one.

entries.zh: 此皆以駙馬襲封王爵者也。
entries.en: These all inherited princely titles through imperial marriage.
entries.literal: These all inherited princely rank through service as imperial sons-in-law.

entries.zh: 唆兒火都者，亦按陳之子，以從征功，在太祖朝遙授左丞相，為千戶，仍賜以塗金銀章，及金銀字海青圓符五、驛馬券六。
entries.en: Suo'erhuodu, another son of Anchannayan, distinguished himself on campaign. Under Genghis Khan he received a distant appointment as Left Chancellor, was made commander of a thousand households, and was further awarded a gilt silver seal, five inscribed gyrfalcon round tallies, and six imperial relay vouchers.
entries.literal: Suo'erhuodu was also a son of Anchannayan; for merit on campaign, in Taizu's reign he was appointed from afar as Left Chancellor, made a chiliarch of a thousand households, and further granted a gilt silver seal, five gyrfalcon round tallies inscribed in gold and silver, and six relay-horse vouchers.

entries.zh: 其子曰阿哈駙馬，當憲宗朝嘗率兵破徐州，以功受賞黃金一鋌、白金十鋌及銀鞍勒，仍命襲父官。
entries.en: His son Aha, an imperial consort, led troops during Möngke's reign and seized Xuzhou. He was rewarded with one gold ingot, ten silver ingots, and silver saddle gear, and ordered to inherit his father's post.
entries.literal: His son was the consort Aha; in Xianzong's reign he once led troops and captured Xuzhou; for merit he received one ingot of gold, ten ingots of white metal, and silver saddle and bridle fittings, and was ordered to succeed to his father's office.

entries.zh: 至世祖時，有昭「弘吉剌萬戶所受驛券、圓符皆仍其舊，凡唆兒火都所受者，宜皆收之」，而唆兒火都之諸孫若孛羅沙、伯顏、蠻子、添壽不花、大都不花、掌吉等，及阿哈千戶之孫曰也速達兒與按陳之弟名冊者，在太祖世授官本藩蒙古軍站千戶。
entries.en: Under Kublai an edict declared: "The Hongjila chiliarch's relay vouchers and round tallies shall remain unchanged; Suo'erhuodu's shall be revoked." Suo'erhuodu's grandsons—including Boruosha, Bayan, Manzi, Tianshoubuhua, Dadubuhua, and Zhangji—as well as Aha's grandson Yesuda'er and Anchannayan's younger brother Ce had all been commissioned in Genghis Khan's time as chiliarchs of Mongol relay stations within their hereditary fief.
entries.literal: By Shizu's time there was an edict: "The relay vouchers and round tallies held by the Hongjila chiliarch are to remain as before; all those held by Suo'erhuodu are to be collected." Suo'erhuodu's grandsons Boruosha, Bayan, Manzi, Tianshoubuhua, Dadubuhua, Zhangji, and others, as well as the grandson of the chiliarch Aha named Yesuda'er and Anchannayan's younger brother named Ce, had in Taizu's time received appointment in their own fief as chiliarchs of Mongol military relay posts.

entries.zh: 冊之子曰哈兒哈孫，以平金功，賜號拔都兒。
entries.en: Ce's son Harhasun earned the heroic title Batuur for defeating the Jin.
entries.literal: Ce's son was named Harhasun; for merit in pacifying the Jin he was granted the title Batuur.

entries.zh: 哈兒哈孫之孫曰都羅兒，至元四年，授光祿大夫，以銀章封懿國公。
entries.en: Harhasun's grandson Duoluo'er was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness in 1267 and enfeoffed as Duke of Yi with a silver seal.
entries.literal: Harhasun's grandson was named Duoluo'er; in the fourth year of Zhiyuan he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and, with a silver seal, enfeoffed as Duke of Yi.

entries.zh: 有脫憐者，亦按陳之裔孫也，世祖授本藩千戶，仍賜驛券、圓符各四，令以兵守朔土之怯魯連。
entries.en: There was Tuolian, another descendant of Anchannayan. Kublai made him commander of a thousand households in his hereditary fief, granted four relay vouchers and four round tallies, and ordered him to garrison Qielulian on the northern frontier.
entries.literal: There was one named Tuolian, also a descendant of Anchannayan; Shizu appointed him chiliarch of his own fief, further granted four relay vouchers and four round tallies each, and ordered him to garrison Qielulian in the northern frontier with troops.

entries.zh: 二十四年，從族父按答兒禿征叛王乃顏有功，亦賜號拔都兒。
entries.en: In the twenty-fourth year he followed his kinsman Anchadartu against the rebel prince Nayan and distinguished himself, earning the heroic title Batuur.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, following his clansman Anchadartu in campaigning against the rebel prince Nayan, he had merit and was likewise granted the title Batuur.

entries.zh: 脫憐卒，子迸不剌嗣。
entries.en: When Tuolian died, his son Bengbula succeeded him.
entries.literal: Tuolian died; his son Bengbula succeeded.

entries.zh: 迸不剌卒，子買住罕嗣。
entries.en: When Bengbula died, his son Maizhuhan inherited the post.
entries.literal: Bengbula died; his son Maizhuhan succeeded.

entries.zh: 買住罕尚拜答沙公主。
entries.en: Maizhuhan married Princess Baidasha.
entries.literal: Maizhuhan married Princess Baidasha.

entries.zh: 卒，弟孛羅帖木兒嗣，以金章封毓德王。
entries.en: At his death his younger brother Boluotiemuer succeeded and was enfeoffed as King of Yude with a gold seal.
entries.literal: He died; his younger brother Boluotiemuer succeeded and, with a gold seal, was enfeoffed as King of Yude.

entries.zh: 孛羅帖木兒薨，買住罕孫阿失襲千戶。
entries.en: When Boluotiemuer died, Maizhuhan's grandson Ash inherited the chiliarchate.
entries.literal: Boluotiemuer died; Maizhuhans grandson Ash inherited the chiliarchate.

entries.zh: 有名醜漢者，按陳次子必哥之裔孫，尚臺忽魯都公主。
entries.en: A descendant of Anchannayan's second son Bike, known as Chouhan, married Princess Taihupudu.
entries.literal: There was one called Chouhan, a descendant of Anchannayan's second son Bike, who married Princess Taihupudu.

entries.zh: 仁宗朝，封安遠王，以兵守莽來。
entries.en: During Renzong's reign he was made King of Anyuan and garrisoned Manglai with his forces.
entries.literal: In Renzong's reign he was enfeoffed as King of Anyuan and stationed troops at Manglai.

entries.zh: 有答兒罕者，亦特薛禪之裔孫也，以從軍功，世祖亦賜以拔都兒之號，加賜黃金一鋌。
entries.en: Daerhan, another descendant of Texuechan, won military honors and received the Batuur title from Kublai along with an extra gold ingot.
entries.literal: There was one Daerhan, also a descendant of Texuechan; for military merit Shizu likewise granted him the title Batuur and an additional gift of one gold ingot.

entries.zh: 其子曰不只兒，從征乃顏，禽其黨金家奴，帝賞以金帶。
entries.en: His son Bozhuer joined the campaign against Nayan, seized the rebel partisan Jinjianu, and was awarded a gold belt.
entries.literal: His son was named Bozhuer; campaigning against Nayan he captured the rebel's partisan Jinjianu, and the emperor rewarded him with a gold belt.

entries.zh: 其後有曰伯奢者，即其孫也。
entries.en: Later there was Boshe, his grandson.
entries.literal: Later there was one named Boshe, who was his grandson.

entries.zh: 凡其女之為後者，自光獻翼聖皇后以降，憲宗貞節皇后諱忽都臺，及後妹也速兒，皆按陳從孫忙哥陳之女。
entries.en: Among the women who became empresses—beginning with the Radiant and Assisting Sagely Empress—Xianzong's Chaste and Constant Empress Hudutai and her sister Yesu'er were daughters of Anchannayan's collateral descendant Manggechen.
entries.literal: As for the women who became empresses, from the Radiant and Assisting Sagely Queen downward: Xianzong's Chaste and Constant Empress, tabooed Hudutai, and her younger sister Yesu'er, were all daughters of Anchannayan's collateral descendant Manggechen.

entries.zh: 世祖昭睿順聖皇后諱察必，濟寧忠武王按陳之女；
entries.en: Kublai's Sagacious and Farsighted Virtuous Sacred Empress Chabi was the daughter of Anchannayan, loyal and martial King of Jining;
entries.literal: Shizu's Sagacious and Farsighted Virtuous Sacred Empress, tabooed Chabi, was daughter of the loyal and martial King Anchannayan of Jining;

entries.zh: 其諱帖古倫者，按陳孫脫憐之女；
entries.en: another bore the taboo name Tiegulun and was Anchannayan's grandson Tuolian's daughter;
entries.literal: she tabooed Tiegulun, daughter of Anchannayan's grandson Tuolian;

entries.zh: 諱喃必冊繼守正宮者，納陳孫仙童之女。
entries.en: the empress tabooed Nanbice, who later held the principal palace, was Nachen's grandson Xiantong's daughter.
entries.literal: tabooed Nanbice, who succeeded in guarding the principal palace, was daughter of Nachen's grandson Xiantong.

entries.zh: 成宗貞慈靜懿皇后諱實憐答裏，斡羅陳之女也。
entries.en: Chengzong's Chaste, Kind, Serene, and Gracious Empress Shiliandali was Woluochen's daughter.
entries.literal: Chengzong's Chaste, Kind, Serene, and Gracious Empress, tabooed Shiliandali, was Woluochen's daughter.

entries.zh: 順宗昭獻元聖皇后諱答吉，大德十一年十一月，武宗冊上皇太后，至大三年十月，加上尊號曰儀天興聖慈仁昭懿壽元皇太后，仁宗延祐二年，加上尊號曰儀天興聖慈仁昭懿壽元全德泰寧福慶皇太后，延祐七年，又加徽文崇祐四字，尊號太皇太后，則按陳孫渾都帖木兒之女。
entries.en: Shunzong's Sagely and Offering Primordial Sacred Empress Daji—enrolled as Empress Dowager by Wuzong in 1307, given added honorifics as Empress Dowager in 1310 and again under Renzong in 1315, and in 1320 raised to Grand Empress Dowager—was the daughter of Anchannayan's grandson Hundutiemuer.
entries.literal: Shunzong's Sagely and Offering Primordial Sacred Empress, tabooed Daji—in the eleventh month of the eleventh year of Dade, Wuzong installed her as Grand Empress Dowager; in the tenth month of the third year of Zhida an honorific was added making her Grand Empress Dowager with the style 'Honoring Heaven, Rising Sage, Kind and Benevolent, Illustrious and Auspicious, Long-lived and Primordial'; in the second year of Yanyou, Renzong added further honorifics making her 'Grand Empress Dowager of Complete Virtue, Great Tranquility, and Fortunate Celebration'; in the seventh year of Yanyou four more characters of imperial commendation were added, raising her to Grand Empress Dowager—was daughter of Anchannayan's grandson Hundutiemuer.

entries.zh: 武宗宣慈惠聖皇后諱真哥，脫憐子迸不剌之女；
entries.en: Wuzong's Kind, Merciful, and Sagely Empress Zhenge was Tuolian's son Bengbula's daughter;
entries.literal: Wuzong's Kind, Merciful, and Sagely Empress, tabooed Zhenge, was daughter of Tuolian's son Bingbula;

entries.zh: 其諱速哥失裏者，按陳從孫哈兒只之女。
entries.en: another, tabooed Sugeshili, was daughter of Anchannayan's collateral descendant Harzhi.
entries.literal: she tabooed Sugeshili was daughter of Anchannayan's collateral descendant Harzhi.

entries.zh: 泰定皇后諱八不罕，按陳孫斡留察兒之女；
entries.en: Taiding's Empress Babuhan was Anchannayan's grandson Woluchu'er's daughter;
entries.literal: Taiding's Empress, tabooed Babuhan, was daughter of Anchannayan's grandson Woluchu'er;

entries.zh: 其諱必罕、諱速哥答裏者，皆脫憐孫買住罕之女。
entries.en: those tabooed Bihan and Sugedali were both daughters of Tuolian's grandson Maizhuhan.
entries.literal: those tabooed Bihan and Sugedali were both daughters of Tuolian's grandson Maizhuhan.

entries.zh: 文宗皇后諱不答失裏，雕阿不剌魯王之女。
entries.en: Wenzong's Empress Budashili was daughter of Diaoa'bula, King of Lu.
entries.literal: Wenzong's Empress, tabooed Budashili, was daughter of the King of Diaoa'abulu.

entries.zh: 此則弘吉剌氏之為後者也。
entries.en: These were the Hongjila women who ascended to the throne as empresses.
entries.literal: These, then, were Hongjila women who became empresses.

entries.zh: 忽憐，尚憲宗女伯牙魯罕公主。
entries.en: Hulian married Möngke's daughter Princess Boyaluohan.
entries.literal: Hulian married Xianzong's daughter Princess Boyaluohan.

entries.zh: 後脫黑帖木兒叛，世祖命忽憐與失列及等討之，大戰終日，脫黑帖木兒敗走，帝嘉之，復令尚憲宗孫女不蘭奚公主。
entries.en: Later, when Tuheitie'muer rebelled, Kublai ordered Hulian and Shilieji to suppress him. After a full day of fighting Tuheitie'muer fled. The emperor praised Hulian and gave him Möngke's granddaughter Princess Bulanxi in marriage.
entries.literal: Later when Tuheitie'muer rebelled, Shizu ordered Hulian with Shilieji and others to suppress him; they fought a full day; Tuheitie'muer fled in defeat; the emperor praised him and again had him marry Xianzong's granddaughter Princess Bulanxi.

entries.zh: 宋平，封以廣州。
entries.en: After the Song were pacified, he was enfeoffed with Guangzhou.
entries.literal: When the Song were pacified, he was enfeoffed with Guangzhou.

entries.zh: 乃顏、聲剌哈兒叛，世祖新征，薛徹堅等與哈答罕屢戰，帝召忽憐至。
entries.en: When Nayan and Shenglaha'er rebelled, Kublai was on campaign. Xuechejian and others fought repeatedly with Hadahan, and the emperor summoned Hulian.
entries.literal: When Nayan and Shenglaha'er rebelled, Shizu was newly on campaign; Xuechejian and others fought repeatedly with Hadahan; the emperor summoned Hulian.

entries.zh: 值薛徹堅等戰於程火失溫之地，哈答罕眾甚盛，忽憐以兵二百迎敵，敗之。
entries.en: When Xuechejian and others fought at Chenghuoshiwen, Hadahan's forces were overwhelming; Hulian met them with two hundred men and defeated them.
entries.literal: When Xuechejian and others fought at Chenghuoshiwen, Hadahan's forces were very strong; Hulian with two hundred men met the enemy and defeated them.

entries.zh: 哈答罕等走度猱河，還其巢穴。
entries.en: Hadahan and his men fled across the Nuoy River and retreated to their stronghold.
entries.literal: Hadahan and others fled across the Nuoy River and returned to their lair.

entries.zh: 逾年夏，帝命忽憐復征之。
entries.en: The following summer the emperor ordered Hulian to campaign against them again.
entries.literal: The next summer the emperor ordered Hulian again to campaign against them.

entries.zh: 至曲列兒、塔兀兒二河之間，大戰，其眾皆度塔兀河遁去。
entries.en: Between the Qulie'er and Ta'u'er rivers they fought a great battle, and the enemy forces all fled across the Ta'u River.
entries.literal: Between the Qulie'er and Ta'u'er rivers they fought a great battle; all his forces crossed the Ta'u River and fled away.

entries.zh: 余百人逃匿山谷，忽憐即率兵二百徒步追之。
entries.en: More than a hundred fugitives hid in the valleys; Hulian immediately led two hundred men on foot in pursuit.
entries.literal: More than a hundred men hid in mountain valleys; Hulian immediately led two hundred men on foot in pursuit.

entries.zh: 薛徹堅止之曰：「彼亡命者，安得徒行。」
entries.en: Xuechejian tried to stop him, saying, 'Those fugitives cannot possibly travel on foot.'
entries.literal: Xuechejian stopped him, saying: 'Those fugitives—how could they travel on foot.'

entries.zh: 忽憐不聽，往殺其眾。
entries.en: Hulian would not listen and went to slaughter them.
entries.literal: Hulian would not listen and went to kill their force.

entries.zh: 薛徹堅以聞，賜金一鋌、銀五鋌。
entries.en: Xuechejian reported the victory, and Hulian was rewarded with one gold ingot and five silver ingots.
entries.literal: Xuechejian reported it; he was granted one ingot of gold and five of silver.

entries.zh: 又逾年，復往征之，與哈答罕遇於兀剌河。
entries.en: Another year later he campaigned again and encountered Hadahan at the Wula River.
entries.literal: Another year passed and he again went on campaign; he met Hadahan at the Wula River.

entries.zh: 忽憐夜率千人潛入其軍，盡殺之。
entries.en: Hulian led a thousand men in a night raid on the enemy camp and killed them all.
entries.literal: Hulian at night led a thousand men to infiltrate his army and killed them all.

entries.zh: 帝賜鈔五萬貫、金一鋌、銀十鋌。
entries.en: The emperor rewarded him with fifty thousand strings of paper money, one gold ingot, and ten silver ingots.
entries.literal: The emperor granted fifty thousand strings of paper money, one ingot of gold, and ten of silver.

entries.zh: 忽憐薨，贈效忠保德輔運佐理功臣、太師、開府儀同三司、駙馬都尉、上柱國，追封昌王，謚忠宣。
entries.en: At Hulian's death he was posthumously granted the titles Effecting Loyalty in Preserving Virtue in Supporting Transport and Assisting Governance, Grand Preceptor, Equal in Rank to the Three Excellencies, Consort Commandant, and Chief Pillar of State, and posthumously enfeoffed as King of Chang with the epithet Loyal and Proclaiming.
entries.literal: When Hulian died he was posthumously granted the merit titles Effecting Loyalty in Preserving Virtue in Supporting Transport and Assisting Governance, Grand Preceptor, Equal in Rank to the Three Excellencies, Consort Commandant, and Chief Pillar of State; posthumously enfeoffed King of Chang with posthumous epithet Loyal and Proclaiming.

entries.zh: 子阿失，事成宗。
entries.en: His son Ash served Temür.
entries.literal: His son Ash served Chengzong.

entries.zh: 篤哇叛于海都，帝遣晉王甘麻剌并武宗帥師討之。
entries.en: When Duwa rebelled with Qaidu, the emperor sent Prince of Jin Gamala and Wuzong at the head of an army to suppress them.
entries.literal: When Duwa rebelled alongside Qaidu, the emperor dispatched Prince of Jin Gamala together with Wuzong to command troops against them.

entries.zh: 大德五年，戰哈剌答山，阿失射篤哇中其膝，擒殺甚多，篤哇號哭而遁，武宗賜之衣。
entries.en: In 1301 at Mount Halada, Ash shot Duwa in the knee, killed or captured many of his men, and drove Duwa off in tears; Wuzong rewarded him with garments.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Dade they fought at Mount Halada; Ash shot Duwa in the knee, captured and killed many; Duwa wailed and fled; Wuzong granted him clothing.

entries.zh: 成宗加賜珠衣，封為昌王，置王府官屬。
entries.en: Temür added pearl robes, enfeoffed him as King of Chang, and established a princely household staff.
entries.literal: Chengzong further granted pearl garments, enfeoffed him as King of Chang, and established princely household offices.

entries.zh: 仁宗朝，復賜以寧昌縣稅入。
entries.en: Under Renzong he was again granted the tax revenue of Ningchang County.
entries.literal: In Renzong's reign he was again granted the tax revenue of Ningchang County.

entries.zh: 阿失尚成宗女亦里哈牙公主，復尚憲宗曾孫女買的公主。
entries.en: Ash married Temür's daughter Princess Yilihaya and later Möngke's great-granddaughter Princess Maide.
entries.literal: Ash married Chengzongs daughter Princess Yilihaya and later Möngkes great-granddaughter Princess Maide.

entries.zh: 阿失薨，子八剌失里襲封昌王。
entries.en: When Ash died, his son Balashili inherited the title King of Chang.
entries.literal: Ash died; his son Balashili inherited enfeoffment as King of Chang.

entries.zh: 忽憐從弟不花，尚世祖女兀魯真公主；
entries.en: Hulian's cousin Buhua married Kublai's daughter Princess Wuluzhen;
entries.literal: Hulians younger cousin Buhua married Shizus daughter Princess Wuluzhen;

entries.zh: 其弟鎖郎哈，娶皇子忙哥剌女奴兀倫公主，生女，是為武宗仁獻章聖皇后，實生明宗。
entries.en: his younger brother Suolangha married Prince Mangge'a's daughter Princess Nuwulun; their daughter became Wuzong's Benevolent Offering Sagely Empress and bore Mingzong.
entries.literal: his younger brother Suolangha married Prince Mangge'as daughter Princess Nuwulun; the daughter born was Wuzongs Benevolent Offering Sagely Empress, who in fact bore Mingzong.

entries.zh: 子君不花，尚定宗長女葉裏迷失公主。
entries.en: His son Junbuhua married Güyük's eldest daughter Princess Yelimishi.
entries.literal: His son Junbuhua married Dingzong's eldest daughter Princess Yelimishi.

entries.zh: 愛不花，尚世祖季女月烈公主。
entries.en: Aibuhua married Kublai's youngest daughter Princess Yuelie.
entries.literal: Aibuhua married Shizu's youngest daughter Princess Yuelie.

entries.zh: 中統初，總兵討阿裏不哥，敗闊不花於按檀火爾歡之地。
entries.en: At the start of the Zhongtong era he led troops against Arigü and defeated Kuobuhua at Antanhuo'erhuan.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Zhongtong he commanded troops to suppress Arigü; he defeated Kuobuhua at the place Antanhuo'erhuan.

entries.zh: 三年，圍李亶於濟南，獨當一面。
entries.en: In the third year he besieged Li Tan at Jinan and held an entire front by himself.
entries.literal: In the third year he besieged Li Tan at Jinan, holding one front alone.

entries.zh: 事平，又從征西北，敗叛王之黨撒裏蠻於孔古烈。
entries.en: After the rebellion was suppressed he campaigned again in the northwest and defeated the rebel partisan Saliman at Kongulie.
entries.literal: When affairs were settled he again followed in campaign to the northwest and defeated the rebel prince's partisan Saliman at Kongulie.

entries.zh: 愛不花卒。
entries.en: Aibuhua died.
entries.literal: Aibuhua died.

entries.zh: 子闊裏吉思。
entries.en: His son was Kuolijisi.
entries.literal: His son was Kuolijisi.

entries.zh: 闊裏吉思，性勇毅，習武事，尤篤於儒術，築萬卷堂於私第，日與諸儒討論經史，性理、陰陽、術數，靡不該貫。
entries.en: Kuolijisi was brave and resolute, skilled in military affairs, and deeply devoted to Confucian learning. He built a Hall of Ten Thousand Scrolls at his residence and daily discussed the classics, history, metaphysics, yin-yang theory, and numerology with scholars—mastering them all.
entries.literal: Kuolijisi by nature was brave and resolute, practiced military affairs, and was especially devoted to Confucian learning; he built a Hall of Ten Thousand Scrolls in his private residence and daily with various scholars discussed the classics and histories, nature and principle, yin and yang, and numerology—there was none he did not master.

entries.zh: 尚忽答的迷失公主，繼尚愛牙失裏公主。
entries.en: He married Princess Hudeshimi and later Princess Aiyashili.
entries.literal: He married Princess Hudeshimi, and afterward married Princess Aiyashili.

entries.zh: 宗王也不幹叛，率精騎千餘，晝夜兼行，旬日追及之。
entries.en: When Imperial Prince Yebugan rebelled, Kuolijisi led more than a thousand elite horsemen in forced marches day and night and overtook him within ten days.
entries.literal: Imperial Prince Yebugan rebelled; he led more than a thousand elite horsemen, traveling day and night together, and in ten days overtook him.

entries.zh: 時方暑，將戰，北風大起，左右請待之，闊裏吉思曰：「當暑得風，天贊我也。」
entries.en: It was midsummer. As battle was about to begin a strong north wind arose. His attendants urged delay, but Kuolijisi said, "A wind in summer heat—Heaven favors me."
entries.literal: It was then midsummer; about to fight, a north wind rose greatly; those at his side asked to wait; Kuolijisi said: 'In midsummer to obtain wind—Heaven assists me.'

entries.zh: 策馬赴戰，騎士隨之，大殺其眾，也不幹以數騎遁去。
entries.en: He charged into battle at the head of his horsemen, slaughtered the enemy force, and Yebugan fled with only a few riders.
entries.literal: He spurred his horse into battle; horsemen followed; they greatly slaughtered the enemy force; Yebugan fled with a few riders.

entries.zh: 闊裏吉思身中三矢，斷其發。
entries.en: Kuolijisi was struck by three arrows that cut through his hair.
entries.literal: Kuolijisi was struck by three arrows, severing his hair.

entries.zh: 凱還，詔賜黃金三斤、白金千五百斤。
entries.en: On his triumphant return he was granted three jin of gold and fifteen hundred jin of silver.
entries.literal: Returning in triumph, an edict granted three jin of gold and fifteen hundred jin of white metal.

entries.zh: 成宗即位，封高唐王。
entries.en: When Chengzong ascended the throne he was enfeoffed as King of Gaotang.
entries.literal: When Chengzong took the throne he was enfeoffed as King of Gaotang.

entries.zh: 西北不安，請於帝，願往平之，再三請，帝乃許。
entries.en: When the northwest grew unsettled he petitioned the emperor to pacify it. After repeated requests the emperor consented.
entries.literal: The northwest was unsettled; he petitioned the emperor, wishing to go and pacify it; he petitioned again and again, and the emperor then granted permission.

entries.zh: 及行，且誓曰：「若不平定西北，吾馬首不南。」
entries.en: As he departed he swore, "Unless I pacify the northwest, my horse's head shall not turn south."
entries.literal: As he set out he also swore: 'If I do not pacify the northwest, my horse's head shall not turn south.'

entries.zh: 大德元年夏，遇敵於伯牙思之地，眾謂當俟大軍畢至，與戰未晚，闊裏吉思曰：「大丈夫報國，而待人耶！」
entries.en: In the summer of 1297 he met the enemy at Boyasi. His officers urged waiting for the main army, but Kuolijisi said, "A man serving his country does not wait on others!"
entries.literal: In the summer of the first year of Dade he met the enemy at Boyasi; the host said they ought to wait until the great army had fully arrived and fighting would not be late; Kuolijisi said: 'A great man serving the state—yet waiting for others!'

entries.zh: 即整眾鼓躁以進，大敗之，擒其將卒百數以獻。
entries.en: He immediately arrayed his troops, beat the drums, and charged, routing the enemy and capturing several hundred officers and men to present as trophies.
entries.literal: He immediately arrayed his forces, beat drums, and charged; he greatly defeated them and captured several hundred of their officers and soldiers to present.

entries.zh: 詔賜世祖所服貂裘、寶鞍，及繒錦七百、介胄、戈戟、弓矢等物。
entries.en: He was granted Kublai's own sable coat and precious saddle, seven hundred pieces of brocade silk, armor, halberds, bows, arrows, and other equipment.
entries.literal: An edict granted the sable fur coat Shizu had worn, a precious saddle, seven hundred pieces of silk brocade, armor, halberds, bows and arrows, and other items.

entries.zh: 二年秋，諸王將帥共議防邊，咸曰：「敵往歲不冬出，且可休兵於境。」
entries.en: That autumn the princes and generals discussed border defense. All agreed: "The enemy has not campaigned in winter before; we may rest our troops at the frontier."
entries.literal: In the autumn of the second year the princes and generals jointly discussed border defense; all said: 'The enemy in past years did not come out in winter; for now troops may rest at the frontier.'

entries.zh: 闊裏吉思曰：「不然，今秋候騎來者甚少，所謂鷙鳥將擊，必匿其形，備不可緩也。」
entries.en: Kuolijisi replied, "Not so. This autumn very few scouting parties have appeared. As the saying goes, when a fierce bird is about to strike it conceals itself—we cannot relax our guard."
entries.literal: Kuolijisi said: 'Not so; this autumn the scouting horsemen coming have been very few—what is called when a fierce bird is about to strike, it must hide its form; preparations cannot be delayed.'

entries.zh: 眾不以為然，闊裏吉思獨嚴兵以待之。
entries.en: The others disagreed, but Kuolijisi alone kept his troops on strict alert.
entries.literal: The host did not agree; Kuolijisi alone kept his troops strict in readiness.

entries.zh: 是冬，敵兵果大至，三戰三克，闊裏吉思乘勝逐北，深入險地，後騎不繼，馬躓陷敵，遂為所執。
entries.en: That winter the enemy did arrive in force. Kuolijisi won three battles in succession and pursued the fleeing enemy deep into difficult terrain. His rear guard failed to keep up, his horse stumbled, and he was captured.
entries.literal: That winter the enemy forces indeed came in great numbers; three battles, three victories; Kuolijisi riding victory pursued north, penetrating deep into dangerous ground; rear horsemen did not follow; his horse stumbled and he fell among the enemy, and thus was captured.

entries.zh: 敵誘使降，惟正言不屈，又欲以女妻之，闊裏吉思毅然曰：「我帝婿也，非帝後面命，而再娶可乎！」
entries.en: The enemy urged him to surrender, but he steadfastly refused. When they offered him a daughter in marriage he declared firmly, "I am the emperor's son-in-law—how could I marry again without his express command!"
entries.literal: The enemy tempted him to surrender; with upright words he would not yield; they again wished to give him a daughter in marriage; Kuolijisi resolutely said: 'I am the emperor's son-in-law; without the emperor's later command, how could I marry again!'

entries.zh: 敵不敢逼。
entries.en: The enemy did not dare press him further.
entries.literal: The enemy did not dare press him.

entries.zh: 帝嘗遣其家臣阿昔思特使敵境，見於人眾中，闊裏吉思一見輒問兩宮安否，次問嗣子何如，言未畢，左右即引其去。
