entries.en: The emperor once sent his household retainer Axisi as special envoy to the enemy territory. Spotted in the crowd, Kuolijisi immediately asked whether the two palaces were well and then how his heir was. Before he could finish speaking, attendants pulled Axisi away.
entries.literal: The emperor once sent his household retainer Axisi as special envoy to the enemy territory; seen among the crowd, Kuolijisi at once upon seeing him asked whether the two palaces were well, next asked how the heir was; before words were finished those at his side immediately led him away.

entries.zh: 明日，遣使者還，不復再見，竟不屈死焉。
entries.en: The next day the envoy was sent back and not permitted to see him again. Kuolijisi died unbroken in spirit.
entries.literal: The next day he sent the envoy back and would not see him again; in the end he died unyielding.

entries.zh: 九年，追封高唐忠獻王，加贈推忠宣力崇文守正亮節保德功臣、太師、開府儀同三司、上柱國、駙馬都尉，追封趙王。
entries.en: In the ninth year he was posthumously enfeoffed as the Loyal and Offering King of Gaotang and granted the titles Loyal in Supporting the Mandate, Illustrious in Culture, Upright in Integrity, and Preserving Virtue, along with Grand Preceptor, Equal in Rank to the Three Excellencies, Chief Pillar of State, and Consort Commandant, and posthumously made King of Zhao.
entries.literal: In the ninth year he was posthumously enfeoffed as the Loyal and Offering King of Gaotang, further granted the merit titles Loyal in Supporting the Mandate, Illustrious in Culture, Upright in Integrity, Preserving Virtue, Grand Preceptor, Holder of the Office of Equal Ranks with the Three Excellencies, Chief Pillar of State, Consort Commandant, and posthumously enfeoffed as King of Zhao.

entries.zh: 公主忽答的迷失追封齊國長公主，愛牙失裏封齊國公主，並加封趙國。
entries.en: Princess Hudeshimi was posthumously made Grand Princess of Qi; Aiyashili was made Princess of Qi; both were further elevated to Princess of Zhao.
entries.literal: Princess Hudeshimi was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Princess of Qi; Aiyashili was enfeoffed Princess of Qi; both were further enfeoffed as Zhao.

entries.zh: 純只海，散術臺氏。
entries.en: Chunzhihai belonged to the Sanshutai clan.
entries.literal: Chunzhihai was of the Sanshutai clan.

entries.zh: 弱冠宿衛太祖帳下，從征西域諸國有功。
entries.en: In his youth he served in Genghis Khan's guard and distinguished himself in campaigns across the Western Regions.
entries.literal: In his youth he served in the Great Khan's guard tent and followed campaigns in the Western Regions with merit.

entries.zh: 歲癸巳，太宗命佩金虎符，充益都行省軍民達魯花赤，從大帥太出破徐州，擒金帥國用安。
entries.en: In 1233 Emperor Ögedei ordered him to wear the gold tiger tally as chief military governor of the Yidu Branch Secretariat. He followed Grand Marshal Tachu in the capture of Xuzhou and took the Jin commander Guo Yong'an prisoner.
entries.literal: In the year guisi Emperor Taizong ordered him to wear the gold tiger tally and appointed him Chief Darughachi of the military and civilians of the Yidu Branch Secretariat; he followed Grand Marshal Tachu in breaking Xuzhou and captured the Jin commander Guo Yong'an.

entries.zh: 丁酉，以益都為皇太子分土，遷京兆行省都達魯花赤。
entries.en: In 1237, when Yidu became the crown prince's fief, he was transferred to chief military governor of the Jingzhao Branch Secretariat.
entries.literal: In dingyou Yidu became the crown prince's fief; he was transferred to Chief Darughachi of the Jingzhao Branch Secretariat.

entries.zh: 至懷，值大疫，士卒困憊，有旨以本部兵就鎮懷孟。
entries.en: On reaching Huai he encountered a great epidemic that left his soldiers exhausted. An order directed his forces to garrison Huai and Meng.
entries.literal: Arriving at Huai, he encountered a great epidemic; soldiers were exhausted and weary; an order directed his command to garrison at Huai and Meng.

entries.zh: 未幾，代察罕總軍河南，尋復懷孟。
entries.en: Before long he replaced Chahan as overall commander of the Henan army, then soon returned to Huai and Meng.
entries.literal: Before long he replaced Chahan in overall command of the Henan army, and soon returned to Huai and Meng.

entries.zh: 己亥，同僚王榮潛畜異志，欲殺純只海，伏甲縶之，斷其兩足跟，以帛緘純只海口，置佛祠中。
entries.en: In 1239 his colleague Wang Rong secretly plotted rebellion and attempted to kill Chunzhihai. Wang set armed men to seize him, severed both his Achilles tendons, bound his mouth with cloth, and left him in a Buddhist shrine.
entries.literal: In jihai his colleague Wang Rong secretly harbored rebellious intent and wished to kill Chunzhihai; he set armed men to seize him, cut both his heel tendons, bound Chunzhihai's mouth with cloth, and placed him in a Buddhist shrine.

entries.zh: 純只海妻喜禮伯倫聞之，率其眾攻榮家，奪出之。
entries.en: When Chunzhihai's wife Xilibolun learned of this, she led her followers in an assault on Wang Rong's house and rescued her husband.
entries.literal: When Chunzhihai's wife Xilibolun heard of this she led her followers to attack Rong's house and rescued him.

entries.zh: 純只海裹瘡從二子馳旁郡，請兵討榮，殺之。
entries.en: Wrapping his wounds, Chunzhihai rode with his two sons to a neighboring prefecture to raise troops, then returned to kill Wang Rong.
entries.literal: Chunzhihai wrapped his wounds and with his two sons galloped to a neighboring prefecture to request troops to punish Rong and killed him.

entries.zh: 朝廷遣使以榮妻孥貲產賜純只海家，且盡驅懷民萬餘口郭外，將戮之。
entries.en: The court sent envoys granting Wang Rong's wife, children, and property to Chunzhihai's family and ordered more than ten thousand residents of Huai driven outside the walls for execution.
entries.literal: The court sent envoys to grant Wang Rong's wife, children, and property to Chunzhihai's family, and moreover drove more than ten thousand Huai residents outside the walls, intending to slaughter them.

entries.zh: 純只海力爭曰：「為惡者止榮一人耳，其民何罪。
entries.en: Chunzhihai argued forcefully: "Only Wang Rong committed evil. What crime have the common people committed?
entries.literal: Chunzhihai argued forcefully, saying, "The one who did evil was only Rong alone; what crime have the people committed?

entries.zh: 若果盡誅，徒守空城何為？
entries.en: If they are all put to death, of what use is holding an empty city?
entries.literal: If they are indeed all put to death, of what use is merely holding an empty city?

entries.zh: 茍朝廷罪使者以不殺，吾請以身當之。」
entries.en: If the court would punish the envoy for failing to carry out the slaughter, I ask to answer for it with my own life."
entries.literal: If the court would punish the envoy for not killing them, I ask to answer for it with my own person."

entries.zh: 使者還奏，帝是其言，民賴不死。
entries.en: The envoy returned and reported to the Emperor, who approved his argument. The people were spared.
entries.literal: The envoy returned to report; the Emperor approved his words and the people relied on this and did not die.

entries.zh: 純只海給榮妻孥券，放為民，遂以其宅為官廨，秋毫無所取。
entries.en: Chunzhihai issued certificates freeing Wang Rong's wife and children as commoners, converted their residence into the government office, and took nothing for himself.
entries.literal: Chunzhihai issued certificates to Wang Rong's wife and children and released them as commoners; he then made their residence the government office and took not the slightest thing.

entries.zh: 郡人德之。
entries.en: The people of the prefecture revered him for this.
entries.literal: The people of the prefecture were grateful to him.

entries.zh: 既入覲，太宗以純只海先朝舊臣，功績昭著，賜第一區於和林，尋以疾卒。
entries.en: After he presented himself at court, Emperor Ögedei, recognizing Chunzhihai as a veteran minister of the previous reign with illustrious service, granted him a first-ranked residence at Karakorum. He soon died of illness.
entries.literal: After entering for audience, Emperor Taizong because Chunzhihai was an old minister of the previous reign with illustrious achievements granted him a first-ranked residence at Karakorum; soon he died of illness.

entries.zh: 敕葬山陵之側。
entries.en: An edict ordered him buried beside the imperial tombs.
entries.literal: An edict ordered him buried beside the imperial tombs.

entries.zh: 布智兒
entries.en: Buzhier
entries.literal: Buzhier

entries.zh: 李璮反山東，事連王文統，平章趙璧素忌希憲勳名，因言文統由張易、希憲薦引，遂至大用，且關中形勝之地，希憲得民心，有商挺、趙良弼為之輔，此事宜關聖慮。
entries.en: When Li Tan rebelled in Shandong, the affair implicated Wang Wentong. Grand Councillor Zhao Bi, who had long resented Lian Xixian's fame, said Wentong had risen through recommendations by Zhang Yi and Lian Xixian, that Lian Xixian held the strategic Guanzhong region and had won popular loyalty with Shang Ting and Zhao Liangbi as his aides—matters that should concern the throne.
entries.literal: Li Tan rebelled in Shandong and the affair implicated Wang Wentong. The Grand Councillor Zhao Bi had long resented Lian Xixian's merit and fame and therefore said that Wentong had been recommended and introduced by Zhang Yi and Lian Xixian and thus came to great employment, and moreover that in the strategically advantageous land of Guanzhong Lian Xixian had won the people's hearts, with Shang Ting and Zhao Liangbi as his assistants—this matter should concern the sage's consideration.

entries.zh: 帝曰：「希憲自幼事朕，朕知其心，挺、良弼皆正士，何慮焉。」
entries.en: The Emperor said, "Lian Xixian has served me since youth and I know his heart. Ting and Liangbi are both upright men—what is there to fear?"
entries.literal: The Emperor said, "Lian Xixian has served me since youth and I know his heart. Ting and Liangbi are both upright men—what is there to worry about?"

entries.zh: 蜀降人費正寅以私怨譖希憲因李璮叛，亦修城治兵，潛畜異志，帝因惑之，命中書右丞南合代希憲行省，且覆視所告事，卒無實狀。
entries.en: A surrendered Shu man, Fei Zhengyin, slandered Lian Xixian out of private spite, claiming that amid Li Tan's rebellion he too was fortifying cities, drilling troops, and harboring secret ambitions. The Emperor was unsettled and ordered Right Vice Director Nanhe to replace him in provincial administration and reinvestigate the charges. In the end nothing was substantiated.
entries.literal: A surrendered man of Shu, Fei Zhengyin, slandered Lian Xixian out of private resentment, saying that because of Li Tan's rebellion he too was repairing walls and training troops and secretly harbored a contrary intent. The Emperor was thereby misled and ordered the Right Vice Director of the Secretariat Nanhe to replace Lian Xixian in provincial administration and moreover reinvestigate the reported matters. In the end there was no substantiating evidence.

entries.zh: 詔希憲還京師，陛見，言曰：「方關陝叛亂，川蜀未寧，事急星火，臣隨宜行事，不謀佐貳，如寅所言，罪止在臣，臣請逮繫有司。」
entries.en: An edict recalled Lian Xixian to the capital. At audience he said, "When Guan-Shaan was in rebellion and Sichuan unsettled, affairs were urgent as fire. I acted as circumstances required without consulting colleagues. If Zhengyin's charges hold, guilt rests on me alone—I ask to be handed over to the authorities."
entries.literal: An edict ordered Lian Xixian back to the capital. At audience he said, "Just when Guan and Shaan were in rebellion and Chuan and Shu were not yet settled, affairs were urgent as sparks and fire. Your servant acted as circumstances required without consulting a second adviser. As Zhengyin said, guilt rests only on your servant. I request to be seized and handed to the responsible offices."

entries.zh: 帝撫御床曰：「當時之言，天知之，朕知之，卿果何罪！」
entries.en: The Emperor stroked the imperial couch and said, "Heaven knows what you did then, and so do I—what crime have you truly committed!"
entries.literal: The Emperor stroked the imperial couch and said, "What was said at the time—Heaven knows it, I know it—what crime do you truly have!"

entries.zh: 慰諭良久。
entries.en: He comforted and reassured him at length.
entries.literal: He comforted and instructed him at length.

entries.zh: 進拜中書平章政事。
entries.en: He was promoted to Grand Councillor of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: He was advanced to Grand Councillor of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 一日夜半，召希憲入禁中，從容道藩邸時事，因及趙璧所言。
entries.en: One night at midnight he summoned Lian Xixian into the inner palace, spoke at ease of affairs from the princely years, and brought up what Zhao Bi had said.
entries.literal: One day at midnight he summoned Lian Xixian into the inner palace, spoke at ease of affairs in the princely establishment, and thereby touched on what Zhao Bi had said.

entries.zh: 希憲曰：「昔攻鄂時，賈似道作木柵環城，一夕而成，陛下顧扈從諸臣曰『吾安得如似道者用之』。
entries.en: Lian Xixian said, "During the attack on Ezhou, Jia Sidao built wooden palisades around the city wall in a single night. Your Majesty turned to your attendants and said, 'How might I find and employ someone like Sidao?'
entries.literal: Lian Xixian said, "In the past when attacking Ezhou, Jia Sidao built wooden palisades encircling the city wall, completed in a single night. Your Majesty turned to the various ministers in attendance and said, 'How might I obtain and employ someone like Sidao?'

entries.zh: 劉秉忠、張易進曰『山東王文統，才智士也。
entries.en: Liu Bingzhong and Zhang Yi stepped forward and said, 'Wang Wentong of Shandong is a man of talent and wisdom.'
entries.literal: Liu Bingzhong and Zhang Yi advanced and said, 'Wang Wentong of Shandong is a man of talent and wisdom.'

entries.zh: 今為李璮幕僚』。
entries.en: He is now on Li Tan's staff.'
entries.literal: He is now a staff officer of Li Tan.'

entries.zh: 詔問臣，臣對『亦聞之，實未嘗識其人也』。」
entries.en: Your Majesty asked me, and I replied, 'I too have heard of him, but I have never actually known the man.'"
entries.literal: Your Majesty questioned your servant, and your servant replied, 'I too have heard of him, but in truth I have never known the man.'"

entries.zh: 帝曰：「朕亦記此。」
entries.en: The Emperor said, "I remember that as well."
entries.literal: The Emperor said, "I too remember this."

entries.zh: 五月，至上都，太常卿田忠良來問疾，希憲謂曰：「上都，聖上龍飛之地，天下視為根本近聞龍岡遺火，延燒民居，此常事耳，慎勿令妄談地理者惑動上意。」
entries.en: In the fifth month he reached Shangdu. Tian Zhongliang, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, came to inquire after his health. Lian Xixian told him, "Shangdu is where the Emperor rose to power—the realm regards it as the foundation. I have lately heard that stray fire at Dragon Mound spread to burn common dwellings. That is an ordinary matter. Be careful not to let geomancers who talk recklessly of fate sway the Emperor's mind."
entries.literal: In the fifth month he reached Shangdu. Taichangqing Tian Zhongliang came to inquire after his illness. Lian Xixian told him, "Shangdu is where the Sage ascended as dragon—the realm views it as root and foundation. Recently I heard Dragon Mound had stray fire spreading to burn common dwellings—this is an ordinary matter. Be careful not to let those who recklessly discuss geomancy stir the Emperor's mind."

entries.zh: 未幾，果有數輩以徙置都邑事奏，樞密副使張易、中書左丞張文謙與之廷辨，力言不可，帝不悅。
entries.en: Before long, several officials did indeed memorialize on moving the capital. Privy Council Vice Commissioner Zhang Yi and Secretariat Left Assistant Zhang Wenqian argued against them in open court, insisting it must not be done. Kublai was displeased.
entries.literal: Before long, indeed several people memorialized on relocating the capital city. Privy Council Vice Commissioner Zhang Yi and Secretariat Left Assistant Zhang Wenqian disputed with them in court, strenuously saying it could not be done—the Emperor was displeased.

entries.zh: 明日，召忠良質其事，忠良以希憲語對，帝曰：「希憲病甚，猶慮及此耶。」
entries.en: The next day Kublai summoned Zhongliang to question him about the matter. Zhongliang repeated Lian Xixian's words. Kublai said, "Lian Xixian is gravely ill—he still worries about this?"
entries.literal: The next day the Emperor summoned Zhongliang to verify the affair; Zhongliang answered with Lian Xixian's words. The Emperor said, "Lian Xixian is gravely ill—he still worries to this point?"

entries.zh: 其議遂止。
entries.en: The proposal was dropped.
entries.literal: That proposal was thereby stopped.

entries.zh: 安童，木華黎四世孫，霸突魯長子也。
entries.en: Antong, a fourth-generation descendant of Muqali, was the eldest son of Batu.
entries.literal: Antong was a fourth-generation descendant of Muqali and the eldest son of Batu.

entries.zh: 中統初，世祖追錄元勳，召入長宿衛，年方十三，位在百僚上。
entries.en: Early in the Zhongtong reign, Kublai posthumously recognized the founding merits of his forebears and summoned Antong into the permanent palace guard. Though only thirteen, he already stood above the entire bureaucracy.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Zhongtong era, the Shizu Emperor posthumously honored the founding merits and summoned him into the permanent palace guard; he was only thirteen, yet ranked above all officials.

entries.zh: 母弘吉剌氏，昭睿皇后之姊，通籍禁中。
entries.en: His mother belonged to the Hongjila Kereit clan, was the elder sister of Empress Zhaorui, and was registered to reside within the inner palace.
entries.literal: His mother was of the Hongjila Kereit clan, elder sister of Empress Zhaorui, and held registered residence in the inner palace.

entries.zh: 世祖一日見之，問及安童，對曰：「安童雖幼，公輔器也。」
entries.en: One day Kublai saw her and inquired about Antong. She answered, "Young as Antong is, he has the makings of a chief minister."
entries.literal: One day the Shizu Emperor saw her and asked about Antong; she replied, "Although Antong is young, he has the makings of a chief minister."

entries.zh: 世祖曰：「何以知之。」
entries.en: The emperor asked, "How do you know that?"
entries.literal: The emperor said, "How do you know this?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「每退朝必與老成人語，未嘗狎一年少，是以知之。」
entries.en: She said, "After every audience he talks with seasoned elders and never keeps company with the young—that is how I know."
entries.literal: She replied, "Whenever he leaves court he speaks with elderly men of experience and never keeps company with the young, and that is how I know."

entries.zh: 世祖悅。
entries.en: Kublai was pleased.
entries.literal: The emperor was pleased.

entries.zh: 阿禮海牙，畏吾氏，集賢大學士脫列之子也。
entries.en: Alihaiya was of Uyghur descent, the son of Tuolie, grand academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies.
entries.literal: Alihaiya was of the Uyghur clan; he was the son of Tuolie, Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies.

entries.zh: 兄野訥，事仁宗於潛邸。
entries.en: His elder brother Yene had served Renzong when he was still heir in waiting.
entries.literal: His elder brother Yene had served Renzong at his hidden residence.

entries.zh: 大德九年，仁宗奉興聖太后出居懷州。
entries.en: In 1305 Renzong escorted the Empress Dowager of Sagely Birth to take up residence in Huai prefecture.
entries.literal: In the ninth year of Dade (1305), Renzong escorted the Empress Dowager of Sagely Birth out to reside in Huai prefecture.

entries.zh: 從者單弱，多懷去計。
entries.en: Their following was thin, and many among them thought of leaving.
entries.literal: The followers were few and weak, and many harbored plans to leave.

entries.zh: 野訥獨無所畏難。
entries.en: Yene alone showed no fear or hesitation.
entries.literal: Yene alone showed no fear or difficulty.

entries.zh: 成宗崩，權臣阿附中宮，不遣使告哀宗藩。
entries.en: When Chengzong died, powerful ministers curried favor with the empress's palace and sent no envoys to announce the mourning to the imperial princes.
entries.literal: When Chengzong died, powerful ministers attached themselves to the empress's palace and did not send envoys to announce the mourning to the imperial princes.

entries.zh: 仁宗有聞，將自懷州入京，宮臣或持不可。
entries.en: When word reached Renzong, he prepared to enter the capital from Huai, but some palace attendants argued against it.
entries.literal: When word reached Renzong, he prepared to enter the capital from Huai prefecture, but some palace attendants held that this should not be done.

entries.zh: 野訥屏人密啟曰：「天子晏駕而皇子已早卒，天下無主，邪謀方興。
entries.en: Yene sent away his attendants and reported in secret: "The emperor is dead and the heir died long ago; the realm has no ruler, and treacherous schemes are already stirring.
entries.literal: Yene dismissed attendants and secretly reported, saying: "The Son of Heaven has passed away and the imperial prince died early; the realm has no master, and wicked plots are rising.

entries.zh: 懷寧王及殿下，世祖、裕皇賢孫，人心所屬久矣。
entries.en: The Prince of Huaining and Your Highness are worthy grandsons of Kublai and the Renowned Emperor; the people's loyalty has long rested with you.
entries.literal: The Prince of Huaining and Your Highness are worthy descendants of Shizu and Emperor Yuzong; the hearts of the people have long belonged to you.

entries.zh: 宜急奉太母入定大計，邪謀必止。
entries.en: You should hurry to bring the Grand Empress Dowager and settle the succession; the treacherous schemes will then collapse.
entries.literal: You should swiftly escort the Grand Empress Dowager to settle the great plan; the wicked plots will surely cease.

entries.zh: 迎立懷寧王以正神器，在此行矣。」
entries.en: Whether the throne can be set right by welcoming and enthroning the Prince of Huaining depends on what you do now."
entries.literal: To welcome and install the Prince of Huaining to set right the imperial regalia depends on this journey."

entries.zh: 仁宗即白太后，以二月至京師，遂誅柄臣二人，遣使迎武宗。
entries.en: Renzong at once reported to the empress dowager, reached the capital in the second month, executed two powerful ministers, and sent envoys to welcome Wuzong.
entries.literal: Renzong immediately informed the empress dowager, and in the second month arrived at the capital, then executed two power-holding ministers and dispatched envoys to welcome Wuzong.

entries.zh: 武宗即位，召野訥，賜玉帶，授嘉議大夫、祕書監。
entries.en: When Wuzong took the throne, he summoned Yene, granted him a jade belt, and appointed him Grand Master of Court Discussion and director of the Palace Secretariat.
entries.literal: When Wuzong ascended the throne, he summoned Yene, bestowed a jade belt, and appointed him Grand Master of Court Discussion and Director of the Palace Secretariat.

entries.zh: 仁宗居東宮，兼太子右庶子，遷侍御史、崇祥院使，兼將作院使。
entries.en: While Renzong was crown prince, Yene also served as right vice tutor to the heir apparent; he was later made attending censor and commissioner of the Chongxiang Court, with concurrent charge of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.
entries.literal: While Renzong resided in the Eastern Palace, Yene also served as Right Vice Tutor to the Heir Apparent; he was transferred to Attending Censor, Commissioner of the Chongxiang Court, and concurrently Commissioner of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.

entries.zh: 閩有綉工，工官大集民間子女居肆督責，吏因為奸利，野訥奏罷之，閩人感悅。
entries.en: In Fujian, craft officials had rounded up commoners' sons and daughters into supervised embroidery shops, and clerks profited from the abuse. Yene memorialized to abolish the practice, and the people of Min were deeply grateful.
entries.literal: In Min there were embroidery artisans; the craft officials greatly gathered the sons and daughters of common families to dwell in workshops under supervision and coercion, and the clerks thereby made illicit profit. Yene memorialized to abolish this, and the people of Min were grateful and pleased.

entries.zh: 尋兼太醫院使。
entries.en: He soon added the concurrent post of commissioner of the Imperial Medical Institute.
entries.literal: Before long he also served as Commissioner of the Imperial Medical Institute.

entries.zh: 仁宗即位，請召文武老臣，咨以朝政。
entries.en: When Renzong came to the throne, Yene asked that veteran civil and military officials be summoned to advise on state affairs.
entries.literal: When Renzong ascended the throne, Yene requested that veteran civil and military officials be summoned and consulted on court governance.

entries.zh: 又請以中都苑囿還諸民。
entries.en: He also asked that the parks and hunting grounds around the capital be returned to the people.
entries.literal: He also requested that the parks and preserves of the central capital be returned to the people.

entries.zh: 拜樞密院副使，進同知樞密院事。
entries.en: He was appointed vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and promoted to associate commissioner.
entries.literal: He was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and advanced to Associate Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

entries.zh: 命為中書平章政事，辭不拜。
entries.en: He was ordered to serve as grand councillor of the Central Secretariat, but declined the appointment.
entries.literal: He was ordered to serve as Grand Councillor of the Central Secretariat, but declined and did not accept the appointment.

entries.zh: 野訥之在臺及侍禁中，於國家事有不便，輒言之，言無不納。
entries.en: While serving at the Censorate and in attendance within the palace, Yene spoke out whenever he saw something harmful to the state, and his advice was always accepted.
entries.literal: While Yene served at the Censorate and attended within the forbidden precincts, whenever there was something inconvenient to state affairs he spoke of it, and his words were never rejected.

entries.zh: 然韜晦惡盈，不泄於外。
entries.en: Yet he kept a low profile, shunned self-importance, and disclosed nothing outside the palace.
entries.literal: Yet he kept himself restrained and hated excess, and did not reveal it outside.

entries.zh: 延祐四年卒，年四十。
entries.en: He died in 1317, at the age of forty.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Yanyou (1317) he died, at the age of forty.

entries.zh: 贈推誠保節翊運功臣、金紫光祿大夫、行中書省左丞相、上柱國、趙國公，諡忠靖。
entries.en: He was posthumously ennobled as a meritorious subject who sincerely upheld integrity and supported the dynasty, made Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, acting left grand councillor of the Central Secretariat, a Pillar of the State, and Duke of Zhao, with the posthumous name Loyal and Tranquil.
entries.literal: He was posthumously conferred the title Meritorious Subject Who Sincerely Upholds Integrity and Supports the Dynasty, Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Acting Left Grand Councillor of the Central Secretariat, Pillar of the State, and Duke of Zhao, with the posthumous name Zhongjing.

entries.zh: 察罕，西域板勒紇城人也。
entries.en: Chahan was a native of Banshilahe in the Western Regions.
entries.literal: Chahan was a man of Banshilahe city in the Western Regions.

entries.zh: 父伯德那，歲庚辰，國兵下西域，舉族來歸。
entries.en: His father Berdena had led the entire clan over in submission when the imperial armies swept the Western Regions in the gengchen year (1220).
entries.literal: His father Berdena—in the gengchen year, when the imperial army descended upon the Western Regions, brought the whole clan to submit.

entries.zh: 事親王旭烈，授河東民賦副緫管，因居河中猗氏縣，後徙解州。
entries.en: Serving Prince Xulie, he received appointment as deputy chief commissioner of the Hedong civilian tax levy; his household settled in Yishi county in Hezhong and later moved to Jie prefecture.
entries.literal: He served Prince Xulie and was appointed deputy chief commissioner for the civilian tax levy in Hedong; he therefore resided in Yishi county in Hezhong, and later moved to Jie prefecture.

entries.zh: 贈榮祿大夫、宣徽使、柱國、芮國公。
entries.en: He was posthumously ennobled as Grand Master for Glorious Happiness and Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, made a Pillar of the State, and created Duke of Rui.
entries.literal: [Posthumously] conferred: Grand Master for Glorious Happiness, Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, Pillar of the State, Duke of Rui.

entries.zh: 阿鲁图，博尔术四世孙。
entries.en: Alutu was a fourth-generation descendant of Borokhula.
entries.literal: Alutu was a fourth-generation descendant of Borokhula.

entries.zh: 父木剌忽。
entries.en: His father was Malahu.
entries.literal: His father was Malahu.

entries.zh: 阿鲁图由经正监袭职为怯薛官，掌环卫，遂拜翰林学士承旨，迁知枢密院事。
entries.en: Alutu succeeded through the Directorate of the Classics to office as a kheshig officer in charge of the imperial guard, was appointed Hanlin drafting academician, and was transferred to know the affairs of the privy council.
entries.literal: Alutu by the Directorate of the Classics succeeded to office as a kheshig officer in charge of the imperial guard, was then appointed Hanlin academician and drafting academician, and was transferred to know the affairs of the Privy Council.

entries.zh: 至元三年，袭封广平王。
entries.en: In the third year of Zhiyuan he succeeded to the enfeoffment as Prince of Guangping.
entries.literal: In the third year of Zhiyuan he succeeded to the enfeoffment as Prince of Guangping.

entries.zh: 至正四年，脱脱辞相位，顺帝问谁可代脱脱为相者，脱脱以阿鲁图荐。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Zhizheng, when Toghto resigned the chancellorship, Emperor Shundi asked who could replace him; Toghto recommended Alutu.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Zhizheng, when Toghto resigned the chancellorship, Emperor Shundi asked who could replace Toghto as chief minister; Toghto recommended Alutu.

entries.zh: 五月，诏拜中书右丞相、监修国史，而别兒怯不花为左丞相，从驾行幸，每同车出入，一时朝野以二相协和为喜。
entries.en: In the fifth month an edict appointed him right chief councilor of the Secretariat and supervisor of the national history, while Bieqiebuha was left chief councilor. They accompanied the imperial procession and each time rode in the same carriage; court and country rejoiced that the two chief ministers were in harmony.
entries.literal: In the fifth month an edict appointed him right chief councilor of the Secretariat and supervisor of the compilation of the national history, while Bieqiebuha was left chief councilor. They accompanied the imperial procession on tours and each time entered and left in the same carriage; for a time court and country rejoiced that the two chief ministers were in harmony.

entries.zh: 时诏修辽、金、宋三史，阿鲁图为总裁。
entries.en: At that time an edict ordered the compilation of the histories of Liao, Jin, and Song; Alutu was chief compiler.
entries.literal: At that time an edict ordered the compilation of the histories of Liao, Jin, and Song; Alutu was chief compiler.

entries.zh: 五年，三史成。
entries.en: In the fifth year the three histories were completed.
entries.literal: In the fifth year the three histories were completed.

entries.zh: 十月，阿鲁图等既以其书进，帝御宣文阁，阿鲁图复与平章政事帖木兒塔识、太平上奏：「太祖取金，世祖平宋，混一区宇，典章图籍皆归秘府。
entries.en: In the tenth month, after Alutu and the rest had presented the books, the emperor proceeded to the Hall of Promoting Culture. Alutu again with Manager of Governmental Affairs Temiertashi and Taiping submitted, "Taizu took the Jin, Shizu pacified the Song, and united the realm; canonical books and maps all returned to the secret repository.
entries.literal: In the tenth month, after Alutu and the rest had presented the books, the emperor proceeded to the Hall of Promoting Culture. Alutu again together with Manager of Governmental Affairs Temiertashi and Taiping submitted: "Taizu took the Jin, Shizu pacified the Song, and united the realm; canonical books and maps all returned to the secret repository.

entries.zh: 今陛下以三国事绩命儒士纂修，而臣阿鲁图总裁。
entries.en: Now Your Majesty has ordered Confucian scholars to compile the achievements of the three states, and your subject Alutu is chief compiler.
entries.literal: Now Your Majesty has ordered Confucian scholars to compile the achievements of the three states, and your subject Alutu is chief compiler.

entries.zh: 臣素不读汉人文书，未解其义。
entries.en: Your subject has never read Han literary works and does not understand their meaning.
entries.literal: Your subject has never read Han people's literary works and does not understand their meaning.

entries.zh: 今者进呈，万机之暇，乞以备乙览。」
entries.en: Now that we present them, in the leisure of ten thousand affairs we beg that they may be prepared for secondary perusal."
entries.literal: Now that we present them, in the leisure of ten thousand affairs we beg that they may be prepared for secondary perusal."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「此事卿诚未解，史书所系甚重，非儒士泛作文字也。
entries.en: The emperor said, "In this matter you indeed do not understand. Histories bear on matters of great weight—they are not literary works casually made by Confucian scholars.
entries.literal: The emperor said: "In this matter you indeed do not understand. Histories bear on matters of great weight—they are not literary works casually made by Confucian scholars.

entries.zh: 彼一国人君行善则国兴，朕为君者宜取以为法；
entries.en: When a ruler of one of those states did good, the state flourished—a ruler like Us ought to take it as a model;
entries.literal: When a ruler of one of those states did good, the state flourished—a ruler like Us ought to take it as a model;

entries.zh: 彼一朝行恶则国废，朕当取以为戒。
entries.en: when one court did evil, the state was ruined—We ought to take it as a warning.
entries.literal: when one court did evil, the state was ruined—We ought to take it as a warning.

entries.zh: 然岂止儆劝人君，其间亦有为宰相事，善则卿等宜仿效，恶则宜监戒。
entries.en: Yet it is not only to warn rulers; among them are also matters of chief ministers—what is good you ought to imitate, what is evil you ought to watch and warn against.
entries.literal: Yet it is not only to warn and encourage rulers; among them are also matters of chief ministers—what is good the likes of you ought to imitate, what is evil you ought to watch and warn against.

entries.zh: 朕与卿等皆当取前代善恶为勉。
entries.en: We and you should all take the good and evil of former ages as encouragement.
entries.literal: We and the likes of you should all take the good and evil of former ages as encouragement.

entries.zh: 朕或思有未至，卿等其言之。」
entries.en: If We think of something not yet reached, you should speak of it."
entries.literal: If We think of something not yet reached, you should speak of it."

entries.zh: 阿鲁图顿首舞蹈而出。
entries.en: Alutu bowed his head, danced, and withdrew.
entries.literal: Alutu bowed his head, danced, and withdrew.

entries.zh: 右司郎中陈思谦建言诸事，阿鲁图曰：「左右司之职所以赞助宰相。
entries.en: Right Secretariat Director Chen Siqian proposed various matters. Alutu said, "The duty of the left and right directorates is to assist the chief minister.
entries.literal: Right Secretariat Director Chen Siqian proposed various matters; Alutu said: "The duty of the left and right directorates is to assist the chief minister.

entries.zh: 今郎中有所言，与我辈共议见诸行事，何必别为文字自有所陈耶？
entries.en: If the director now has something to say, let him discuss it with us and see it carried out—why must he separately make writings and present matters on his own?
entries.literal: If the director now has something to say, let him discuss it with us and see it carried out in affairs—why must he separately make writings and present matters on his own?

entries.zh: 郎中若居他官，则可建言，今居左右司而建言，是徒欲显一己自能言耳。
entries.en: If the director held another office he could propose; now holding the left or right directorate yet proposing is merely wishing to show that he alone can speak.
entries.literal: If the director held another office, he could propose; now holding the left or right directorate yet proposing is merely wishing to show that he alone can speak.

entries.zh: 将置我辈于何地？」
entries.en: Where are you placing us?"
entries.literal: Where are you placing us?"

entries.zh: 思谦大惭服。
entries.en: Siqian was greatly ashamed and submitted.
entries.literal: Siqian was greatly ashamed and submitted.

entries.zh: 一日，与僚佐议除刑部尚书，宰执有所举，或难之曰：「此人柔软，非刑部所可用。」
entries.en: One day, discussing with subordinates the appointment of minister of justice, the chief ministers had someone to recommend. Some objected, saying, "This man is soft—not usable by the Ministry of Justice."
entries.literal: One day, discussing with subordinates the appointment of minister of justice, the chief ministers had someone to recommend; some made difficulties, saying: "This man is soft—not usable by the Ministry of Justice."

entries.zh: 阿鲁图曰：「庙堂即今选侩子耶？
entries.en: Alutu said, "Is the imperial temple selecting wrestlers today?
entries.literal: Alutu said: "Is the imperial temple selecting wrestlers today?

entries.zh: 若选侩子，须选强壮人。
entries.en: If selecting wrestlers, one must select strong men.
entries.literal: If selecting wrestlers, one must select strong men.

entries.zh: 尚书欲其详谳刑牍耳，若不枉人，不坏法，即是好刑官，何必求强壮人耶？」
entries.en: The minister of justice wishes only to examine criminal documents in detail. If he does not wrong people and does not break the law, he is a good justice official—why seek a strong man?"
entries.literal: The minister of justice wishes only to examine criminal documents in detail; if he does not wrong people and does not break the law, he is a good justice official—why must one seek a strong man?"

entries.zh: 左右无以答。
entries.en: Those at left and right had no answer.
entries.literal: Those at left and right had no answer.

entries.zh: 其为治知大体，类如此。
entries.en: In governing he knew the larger pattern, generally like this.
entries.literal: In governing he knew the larger pattern, generally like this.

entries.zh: 先是，别兒怯不花尝与阿鲁图谋挤害脱脱。
entries.en: Earlier Bieqiebuha had once plotted with Alutu to squeeze out and harm Toghto.
entries.literal: Earlier Bieqiebuha had once plotted with Alutu to squeeze out and harm Toghto.

entries.zh: 阿鲁图曰：「我等岂能久居相位，当亦有退休之日，人将谓我何？」
entries.en: Alutu said, "How can we long hold the chancellorship? There will also be a day of retirement—what will people say of us?"
entries.literal: Alutu said: "How can we long hold the chancellorship? There will also be a day of retirement—what will people say of us?"

entries.zh: 别兒怯不花屡以为言，终不从。
entries.en: Bieqiebuha repeatedly spoke of it but in the end Alutu would not follow.
entries.literal: Bieqiebuha repeatedly spoke of it but in the end he would not follow.

entries.zh: 六年，别兒怯不花乃讽监察御史劾奏阿鲁图不宜居相位，阿鲁图即避出城。
entries.en: In the sixth year Bieqiebuha prompted investigating censors to memorialize that Alutu ought not to hold the chancellorship; Alutu at once withdrew outside the city.
entries.literal: In the sixth year Bieqiebuha therefore prompted investigating censors to memorialize and impeach that Alutu ought not to hold the chancellorship; Alutu at once withdrew outside the city.

entries.zh: 其姻党皆为之不平，请曰：「丞相所行皆善，而御史言者无理，丞相何不见帝自陈，帝必辩焉。」
entries.en: His affines were indignant and said, "What the chief minister has done is all good, yet the censor's words are unreasonable. The chief minister ought to see the emperor and explain himself; the emperor will surely argue on his behalf."
entries.literal: His affines were all indignant on his behalf and requested: "What the chief minister has done is all good, yet the censor's words are unreasonable—the chief minister ought to see the emperor and explain himself; the emperor will surely argue on his behalf."

entries.zh: 阿鲁图曰：「我博尔术世裔，岂丞相为难得耶？
entries.en: Alutu said, "I am a Borokhula descendant of generations—how could the chancellorship be hard to obtain?
entries.literal: Alutu said: "I am a Borokhula descendant of generations—how could the chancellorship be hard to obtain?

entries.zh: 但帝命我不敢辞，今御史劾我，我宜即去。
entries.en: But the emperor's command I dared not decline; now the censor impeaches me—I ought to leave at once.
entries.literal: But the emperor's command I dared not decline; now the censor impeaches me—I ought to leave at once.

entries.zh: 盖御史臺乃世祖所设置，我若与御史抗，即与世祖抗矣。
entries.en: The censorate was established by Shizu; if I contend with the censor, I contend with Shizu.
entries.literal: The Censorate was established by Shizu; if I contend with the censor, I contend with Shizu.

entries.zh: 尔等无复言。」
entries.en: You need speak no more."
entries.literal: You need speak no more."

entries.zh: 阿鲁图既罢去，明年，别兒怯不花遂为右丞相，不久亦去。
entries.en: After Alutu had been dismissed, the next year Bieqiebuha became right chief councilor and before long also left.
entries.literal: After Alutu had been dismissed, the next year Bieqiebuha became right chief councilor and before long also left.

entries.zh: 十一年，阿鲁图复起为太傅，出守和林边，薨，无嗣。
entries.en: In the eleventh year Alutu was again raised as grand preceptor, went out to guard the Helin frontier, died, and had no heir.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year Alutu was again raised as Grand Preceptor, went out to guard the Helin frontier, died, and had no heir.

entries.zh: 乃蛮台
entries.en: Naimantai
entries.literal: Naimantai

entries.zh: 答里麻，高昌人。
entries.en: Dalima was from Gaochang.
entries.literal: Dalima was a man of Gaochang.

entries.zh: 大父撒吉斯，为辽王傅，世祖称其贤。
entries.en: His grandfather Sagisi had been tutor to the Prince of Liao, and Emperor Shizu had praised his virtue.
entries.literal: His grandfather Sagisi served as tutor to the Prince of Liao; the Shizu Emperor praised his worth.

entries.zh: 从讨李璮，以勋授山东行省大都督。
entries.en: He took part in the campaign against Li Tan and, for his achievements, was appointed Dadudu of the Shandong Branch Secretariat.
entries.literal: He followed in the campaign against Li Tan and, for meritorious service, was appointed Dadudu of the Shandong Branch Secretariat.

entries.zh: 答里麻弱冠入宿卫。
entries.en: Dalima joined the imperial guard in his early twenties.
entries.literal: Dalima entered palace guard service in his early twenties.

entries.zh: 大德十一年，授御药院达鲁花赤，迁回回药物院，寻出佥湖北、山南两道廉访司事，召拜监察御史。
entries.en: In 1307 he was made Darughachi of the Imperial Pharmacy, then moved to the Muslim Medicaments Office; shortly afterward he was sent out as an associate of the surveillance commissions for Hubei and Shannan, and was summoned to serve as a supervising censor.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year of Dade he was appointed Darughachi of the Imperial Pharmacy, transferred to the Muslim Medicaments Office, then sent out as associate of the surveillance commissions of the Hubei and Shannan circuits, and summoned to be appointed Supervising Censor.

entries.zh: 时丞相帖木迭兒专权贪肆，答里麻帅同寅亦怜真、马祖常劾其罪。
entries.en: At the time Chancellor Temuder held sole power and was rapacious; Dalima led his colleagues Yirenzhen and Ma Zuchang in impeaching him.
entries.literal: At that time the Chancellor Temuder monopolized power and was greedy and ruthless; Dalima led his colleagues Yirenzhen and Ma Zuchang in impeaching his crimes.

entries.zh: 高昌僧恃丞相威，违法娶妇南城，答里麻诘问之，奋不顾利害，风纪由是大振。
entries.en: A monk from Gaochang, relying on the chancellor's power, illegally took a wife in the southern capital; Dalima questioned him, caring nothing for personal risk, and official discipline was greatly restored.
entries.literal: A Gaochang monk, relying on the chancellor's might, unlawfully took a wife in the southern capital; Dalima interrogated him, heedless of profit or harm, and discipline was thereby greatly strengthened.

entries.zh: 擢河东道廉访副使。
entries.en: He was promoted to vice commissioner of the Hedong surveillance commission.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Hedong Circuit Surveillance Commission.

entries.zh: 隰州村民赛神，因醉殴杀姚甲，为首者乘闹逃去，有司逮同会者系狱，历岁不决。
entries.en: In Xi Prefecture, villagers were holding a temple festival when, in a drunken brawl, one man beat and killed Yao Jia. The ringleader fled in the uproar; officials arrested everyone who had been present and kept them in prison for a year without resolving the case.
entries.literal: Villagers in Xi Prefecture held a sacrifice to the gods; while drunk one beat and killed Yao Jia; the ringleader escaped amid the commotion; the authorities arrested those present at the gathering and imprisoned them, and for a year no verdict was reached.

entries.zh: 答里麻曰：「杀人者既逃，存亡不可知，此辈皆诖误无罪，而反桎梏耶？」
entries.en: Dalima said, "The killer has escaped and we do not even know whether he is alive or dead. These people are all innocent victims of mistaken implication—why should they be shackled?"
entries.literal: Dalima said: "The killer has fled and whether he lives or dies is unknown; these people are all wrongly implicated and without guilt—yet they are to be fettered?"

entries.zh: 悉纵之。
entries.en: He released them all.
entries.literal: He released them all.

entries.zh: 至治元年，帖木迭兒复相，以复仇为事，答里麻辞去。
entries.en: In 1321 Temuder returned as chancellor and pursued vendettas; Dalima resigned his post.
entries.literal: In the first year of Zhizhi, Temuder became chancellor again and made revenge his business; Dalima resigned.

entries.zh: 明年，改燕南道廉访副使。
entries.en: The following year he was appointed vice commissioner of the Yannan surveillance commission.
entries.literal: The next year, he was transferred to Vice Commissioner of the Yannan Circuit Surveillance Commission.

entries.zh: 开州达鲁花赤石不花歹颇著政绩，同僚忌之，嗾民诬其与民妻俞氏饮。
entries.en: Shibuhuadai, the Darughachi of Kai Prefecture, had distinguished himself in office; jealous colleagues incited locals to accuse him of drinking with a commoner's wife, Mistress Yu.
entries.literal: The Kai Prefecture Darughachi Shibuhuadai had achieved considerable administrative merit; colleagues envied him and incited the people to accuse him of drinking with a commoner's wife, Mistress Yu.

entries.zh: 答里麻察知俞氏乃八十老妪，石不花歹实不与饮酒，于是抵诬告者罪，石不花歹复还职。
entries.en: Dalima found that Mistress Yu was an eighty-year-old woman and that Shibuhuadai had never drunk with her; he punished the false accusers and restored Shibuhuadai to his post.
entries.literal: Dalima investigated and learned that Mistress Yu was an eighty-year-old woman and that Shibuhuadai had in fact not drunk with her; he therefore punished the false accusers, and Shibuhuadai was restored to office.

entries.zh: 行唐县民斫桑道侧，偶有人借斧削其杖，其人夜持杖劫民财，事觉，并逮斧主与盗同下狱。
entries.en: A man in Xingtang County was cutting mulberry trees by the roadside when someone borrowed his axe to trim a walking staff; that man later used the staff at night to rob a passerby. When the crime was discovered, both the axe owner and the robber were arrested and imprisoned together.
entries.literal: A man in Xingtang County was cutting mulberry trees beside the road; someone happened to borrow his axe to trim a staff; that person used the staff by night to rob a commoner of property; when the matter came to light, both the axe owner and the thief were arrested and imprisoned together.

entries.zh: 答里麻原其未尝知情，即纵之。
entries.en: Dalima found that the axe owner had known nothing of the crime and released him at once.
entries.literal: Dalima excused him on the ground that he had never known; he was immediately released.

entries.zh: 深州民媪怒殴兒妇死，妇方抱其子，子亦误触死。
entries.en: In Shen Prefecture an elderly woman beat her daughter-in-law to death in a rage; the daughter-in-law was holding her baby, and the child also died when struck in the struggle.
entries.literal: An old woman in Shen Prefecture beat her daughter-in-law to death in anger; the daughter-in-law was holding her child, and the child also died from accidental contact.

entries.zh: 媪年七十，同僚议免刑，答里麻不可，曰：「国制，罪人七十免刑，为其血气已衰，不任刑也。
entries.en: The woman was seventy, and colleagues argued she should be exempt from punishment. Dalima refused, saying, "Under the law of the realm, criminals aged seventy are spared punishment because their vital force has waned and they can no longer endure it.
entries.literal: The old woman was seventy; colleagues proposed exempting her from punishment; Dalima would not agree, saying: "By national law, criminals aged seventy are exempt from punishment because their vital force has declined and they cannot bear punishment.

entries.zh: 媪既能杀二人，何谓衰老？」
entries.en: Yet this woman was strong enough to kill two people—how can she be called decrepit?"
entries.literal: If this old woman could kill two people, what does 'decline of vital force' mean?"

entries.zh: 卒死狱中。
entries.en: She ultimately died in prison.
entries.literal: She ultimately died in prison.

entries.zh: 至治元年，除济宁路总管，兴学劝农，百废具修，府无停事。
entries.en: In 1321 he was appointed prefect of Jining Circuit, where he promoted schools and agriculture, restored neglected public works, and left the prefectural office with no backlog of cases.
entries.literal: In the first year of Zhizhi he was appointed Prefect of Jining Circuit; he promoted schools and encouraged agriculture; a hundred neglected tasks were all restored; the prefecture had no backlog of business.

entries.zh: 济阳县有牧童持铁连结击野雀，误杀同牧者，系狱数岁。
entries.en: In Jiyang County a shepherd boy was using an iron chain to strike at wild sparrows when he accidentally killed a companion; he remained in prison for several years.
entries.literal: In Jiyang County a shepherd boy held an iron chain to strike wild sparrows and accidentally killed a fellow shepherd; he was imprisoned for several years.

entries.zh: 答里麻曰：「小兒误杀同牧者，实无杀人意，难以定罪。」
entries.en: Dalima said, "The boy killed his companion by accident and had no intent to kill; he cannot properly be convicted of murder."
entries.literal: Dalima said: "The boy accidentally killed a fellow shepherd; he truly had no intent to kill; it is difficult to convict him."

entries.zh: 罚铜遣之。
entries.en: He imposed a fine in copper and released him.
entries.literal: He fined him in copper and sent him away.

entries.zh: 泰定元年，升福建廉访使。
entries.en: In 1324 he was promoted to commissioner of the Fujian surveillance commission.
entries.literal: In the first year of Taiding he was promoted to Commissioner of the Fujian Surveillance Commission.

entries.zh: 朝廷遣宦官伯颜催督绣段，横取民财，宣政院判官术邻亦取赂于富僧，答里麻皆劾之。
entries.en: The court had sent the eunuch Boyan to supervise the production of embroidered silks, and he extorted money from the people; Shulin, a judge of the Xuanzheng Yuan, also took bribes from wealthy monks; Dalima impeached them all.
entries.literal: The court sent the eunuch Boyan to urge and supervise embroidered silks, extorting the people's wealth; the Xuanzheng Yuan judge Shulin also took bribes from wealthy monks; Dalima impeached them all.

entries.zh: 迁浙西廉访使。
entries.en: He was transferred to commissioner of the Zhexi surveillance commission.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Commissioner of the Zhexi Surveillance Commission.

entries.zh: 会文宗发江陵，阿兒哈秃来谕旨，求赂不获，还谮于朝，召至京，处以重罪。
entries.en: When Emperor Wenzong set out from Jiangling, Arhatu came bearing the imperial command; when Dalima refused his demand for a bribe, Arhatu returned to court and slandered him; Dalima was summoned to the capital and sentenced to a heavy penalty.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wenzong set out from Jiangling, Arhatu came to convey the imperial command; Dalima would not give a bribe; Arhatu returned and slandered him at court; Dalima was summoned to the capital and sentenced to a heavy penalty.

entries.zh: 比至，帝怒解，迁上都同知留守。
entries.en: By the time he reached the capital, the emperor's anger had cooled; he was appointed associate defender of the Upper Capital.
entries.literal: By the time he arrived, the emperor's anger had subsided; he was transferred to Associate Defender of the Upper Capital.

entries.zh: 天历二年八月，明宗崩，文宗入正大统，使者旁午。
entries.en: In the eighth month of 1329 Emperor Mingzong died and Emperor Wenzong assumed the throne; messengers arrived in an unbroken stream.
entries.literal: In the eighth month of the second year of Tianli, Emperor Mingzong died; Emperor Wenzong entered and assumed the great succession; messengers came and went incessantly.

entries.zh: 答里麻朝暮尽力，事无缺失，帝特赐锦衣以嘉之。
entries.en: Dalima labored from morning to night without neglecting a single duty; the emperor specially rewarded him with brocade robes in recognition.
entries.literal: Dalima exerted himself morning and evening; no matter was neglected; the emperor specially bestowed brocade robes in commendation.

entries.zh: 天历三年，迁淮东廉访使。
entries.en: In 1330 he was transferred to commissioner of the Huaidong surveillance commission.
entries.literal: In the third year of Tianli he was transferred to Commissioner of the Huaidong Surveillance Commission.

entries.zh: 明年，召拜刑部尚书。
entries.en: The following year he was summoned and appointed Minister of Punishments.
entries.literal: The next year he was summoned and appointed Minister of Punishments.

entries.zh: 国制，新君即位，必赐诸王、驸马、妃主及宿卫官吏金帛。
entries.en: By established custom, when a new emperor took the throne, gold and silks were distributed to princes, imperial sons-in-law, consorts, and palace guard officials.
entries.literal: By national regulation, when a new ruler acceded, gold and silks must be bestowed on princes, imperial sons-in-law, imperial consorts, and palace guard officials.

entries.zh: 答里麻曰：「必唱名给散，无虚增之数。」
entries.en: Dalima insisted, "Distributions must be made only by calling out each recipient's name, with no inflated numbers on the rolls."
entries.literal: Dalima said: "Names must be called out when distributing; there must be no fictitious increase in numbers."

entries.zh: 国费大省，帝复赐黄金腰带以旌其能。
entries.en: State expenditure was greatly reduced, and the emperor again rewarded him with a golden belt in recognition of his efficiency.
entries.literal: State expenditure was greatly reduced; the emperor again bestowed a golden belt to commend his ability.

entries.zh: 元統元年，陞遼陽行省參知政事。
entries.en: In 1333 he was promoted to vice administrator of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yuantong he was promoted to Vice Administrator of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat.

entries.zh: 高丽国使朝京，道过辽阳，谒省官，各奉布四匹、书一幅，用征东省印封之。
entries.en: When a Goryeo envoy came to court and passed through Liaoyang, he called on the provincial officials, each of whom was offered four bolts of cloth and a letter sealed with the Eastern Campaign Secretariat's seal.
entries.literal: An envoy of the Goryeo state came to court; passing through Liaoyang he called on the provincial officials, each presenting four bolts of cloth and one letter, sealed with the seal of the Eastern Campaign Secretariat.

entries.zh: 答里麻诘其使曰：「国制，设印以署公牍、防奸伪，何为封私书？
entries.en: Dalima questioned the envoy: "Under the law of the realm, seals exist to authenticate official documents and prevent fraud—why use one to seal a private letter?
entries.literal: Dalima questioned the envoy, saying: "By national regulation, seals are established to affix official documents and guard against fraud—why seal a private letter?

entries.zh: 况汝出国时，我尚在京，未为辽阳省官，今何故有书遗我？
entries.en: Moreover, when you left your country I was still in the capital and was not yet an official in Liaoyang—why should you now have a letter for me?
entries.literal: Moreover, when you left your country I was still in the capital and was not yet an official of the Liaoyang Secretariat—why should there now be a letter left for me?

entries.zh: 汝君臣何欺诈如是耶？」
entries.en: Why are your sovereign and ministers so deceitful?"
entries.literal: Why are your ruler and ministers so deceitful as this?"

entries.zh: 使辞屈，还其书与布。
entries.en: The envoy had no reply and returned the letter and cloth.
entries.literal: The envoy was speechless; he returned the letter and cloth.

entries.zh: 元统三年，迁山东廉访使。
entries.en: In 1335 he was transferred to commissioner of the Shandong surveillance commission.
entries.literal: In the third year of Yuantong he was transferred to Commissioner of the Shandong Surveillance Commission.

entries.zh: 时山东盗起，陈马骡及新李白昼杀掠。
entries.en: At that time banditry broke out in Shandong; Chen Maluo and Xin Li led daylight raids and killings.
entries.literal: At that time bandits arose in Shandong; Chen Maluo and Xin Li robbed and killed by daylight.

entries.zh: 答里麻以为官吏贪污所致，先劾去之而后上擒贼方略。
entries.en: Dalima believed the unrest was caused by corrupt officials; he first impeached and removed them, then submitted a plan for capturing the bandits.
entries.literal: Dalima believed this was caused by the corruption of officials; he first impeached and removed them, then submitted a plan for capturing the bandits.

entries.zh: 朝廷嘉纳之，即遣兵擒获，齐鲁以安。
entries.en: The court approved his plan, troops were dispatched at once, the bandits were captured, and Qi and Lu were pacified.
entries.literal: The court approved and adopted it; troops were immediately dispatched and the bandits captured; Qi and Lu were thereby pacified.

entries.zh: 除大都路留守。
entries.en: He was appointed defender of the Dadu Circuit.
entries.literal: He was appointed Defender of the Dadu Circuit.

entries.zh: 帝宴大臣于延春阁，特赐答里麻白鹰以表其贞廉。
entries.en: At a feast for his ministers in the Yanchun Pavilion, the emperor specially gave Dalima a white hawk as a token of his integrity.
entries.literal: The emperor feasted his ministers at the Yanchun Pavilion and specially bestowed on Dalima a white hawk to mark his integrity and purity.

entries.zh: 帝尝命答里麻修七星堂，先是，修缮必用赤绿金银装饰，答里麻独务朴素，令画工图山林景物，左右年少皆不然。
entries.en: The emperor once ordered Dalima to renovate the Seven Stars Hall. Previous renovations had always used gold, silver, and bright pigments; Dalima insisted on simplicity and had painters depict mountain and forest scenery, to the disapproval of the younger attendants around him.
entries.literal: The emperor once ordered Dalima to repair the Seven Stars Hall; previously, repairs always used red, green, gold, and silver ornament; Dalima alone pursued simplicity, ordering painters to depict mountain and forest scenery; the young attendants on left and right all disapproved.

entries.zh: 是岁秋，车驾自上京还，入观之，乃大喜，以手抚壁叹曰：「有心哉，留守也！」
entries.en: That autumn, when the emperor returned from the Upper Capital and entered to view the hall, he was delighted; stroking the wall he exclaimed, "What thoughtful care the Defender has taken!"
entries.literal: That autumn, when the imperial carriage returned from the Upper Capital, the emperor entered to view it and was greatly pleased; he stroked the wall with his hand and sighed: "How thoughtful, this Defender!"

entries.zh: 賜白金五十兩、錦衣一襲。
entries.en: He rewarded him with fifty taels of white gold and a suit of brocade robes.
entries.literal: He bestowed fifty taels of white gold and one suit of brocade robes.

entries.zh: 至正六年，陞河南行省右丞，改翰林學士承旨。
entries.en: In 1346 he was promoted to right chancellor of the Henan Branch Secretariat, then transferred to Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Zhizheng he was promoted to Right Chancellor of the Henan Branch Secretariat, then changed to Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts.

entries.zh: 至正七年，遷陝西行臺中丞，時年六十九。
entries.en: In 1347 he was transferred to vice censor-in-chief of the Shaanxi Branch Censorate at the age of sixty-nine.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Zhizheng he was transferred to Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Shaanxi Branch Censorate; he was then sixty-nine years old.

entries.zh: 致事後，召商議中書平章政事，不拜，全俸優養終身。
entries.en: After his retirement he was summoned to serve as a deliberating Pingzhang of the Central Secretariat but declined; he received his full salary in generous support for the rest of his life.
entries.literal: After he retired from office, he was summoned to deliberate as Pingzhang of the Central Secretariat; he did not accept; he received his full salary in generous support for life.

entries.zh: 月魯帖木兒，卜領勤多禮伯臺氏。
entries.en: Yuelutiemuer was of the Bolingqinduoliboqitai clan.
entries.literal: Yuelutiemuer was of the Bolingqinduoliboqitai clan.

entries.zh: 曾祖贵裕，事太祖，为管领怯怜口怯薛官。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Guiyu had served Emperor Taizu as officer in charge of the qielian households of the imperial camp.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Guiyu served Emperor Taizu as the Keshig officer overseeing the qielian households.

entries.zh: 祖合剌，袭父职，事世祖。
entries.en: His grandfather Hela inherited his father's post and served Emperor Shizu.
entries.literal: His grandfather Hela inherited his father's post and served the Shizu Emperor.

entries.zh: 父普兰奚，由宿卫为中书右司员外郎，与丞相哈剌哈孙建议迎立武宗，累迁至山北辽东道肃政廉访使。
entries.en: His father Pulanxi rose from the imperial guard to outer section member of the right secretariat of the Central Secretariat; with Chancellor Halaqhasun he had urged the enthronement of Emperor Wuzong, and was eventually promoted to surveillance commissioner of the Shanbei Liaodong circuit.
entries.literal: His father Pulanxi, from palace guard service became Outer Section Member of the Right Secretariat of the Central Secretariat; with Chancellor Halaqhasun he proposed welcoming and establishing Emperor Wuzong; he was repeatedly promoted to Surveillance Commissioner of the Shanbei Liaodong Circuit.

entries.zh: 月鲁帖木兒幼警颖，读书强记，俶傥有大志。
entries.en: From childhood Yuelutiemuer was quick-witted and had an excellent memory; he was bold and ambitious.
entries.literal: Yuelutiemuer from youth was alert and clever; in reading he had a strong memory; he was unconventional and had great ambition.

entries.zh: 年十二，成宗命与哈剌哈孙之子脱欢同入国学。
entries.en: At twelve he was ordered by Emperor Chengzong to enter the National Academy together with Halaqhasun's son Tuohuan.
entries.literal: At age twelve, Emperor Chengzong ordered him to enter the National Academy together with Halaqhasun's son Tuohuan.

entries.zh: 仁宗时入宿卫，一日，帝顾问左右曰：「斯人容貌不凡，谁之子耶？」
entries.en: During Emperor Renzong's reign he joined the imperial guard; one day the emperor asked his attendants, "This man has an unusual bearing—whose son is he?"
entries.literal: During Emperor Renzong's reign he entered palace guard service; one day the emperor asked those beside him: "This man's appearance is extraordinary—whose son is he?"

entries.zh: 左右忘其父名，月鲁帖木兒即对曰：「臣父普兰奚也。」
entries.en: His attendants could not recall the father's name; Yuelutiemuer answered at once, "Your servant's father is Pulanxi."
entries.literal: Those beside him forgot his father's name; Yuelutiemuer immediately replied: "Your servant's father is Pulanxi."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「汝父赞谋以定国难，朕未尝忘。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "Your father counseled me through the national crisis; I have never forgotten him."
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Your father aided with counsel to settle the national crisis; I have never forgotten."

entries.zh: 因命脱忽台传旨四怯薛扎撒火孙，令常侍禁廷，毋止其入。
entries.en: He then ordered Tuohutai to convey to the four keshik and the imperial guard that Yuelutiemuer was to attend constantly at court and none was to bar his entry.
entries.literal: He therefore ordered Tuohutai to convey the command to the four keshik and the imperial guard: he was to attend constantly at the forbidden court and none was to bar his entry.

entries.zh: 哈剌哈孙欲用为中书蒙古必阇赤，辄辞焉。
entries.en: Halaqhasun wished to appoint him Mongol secretary of the Central Secretariat, but he repeatedly declined.
entries.literal: Halaqhasun wished to employ him as Mongol Secretary of the Central Secretariat; he repeatedly declined.

entries.zh: 哈剌哈孙曰：「汝年幼，欲何为乎？」
entries.en: Halaqhasun asked, "You are still young—what do you want to do?"
entries.literal: Halaqhasun said: "You are young—what do you wish to do?"

entries.zh: 对曰：「欲为御史尔。」
entries.en: He replied, "I wish to serve as a censor."
entries.literal: He replied: "I wish to be a censor, that is all."

entries.zh: 人壮其志。
entries.en: People admired his ambition.
entries.literal: People admired his ambition.

entries.zh: 久之，遂拜监察御史，巡按上都，劾奏太师、右丞相帖木迭兒受张弼赇六万贯，贷死。
entries.en: Eventually he was appointed supervising censor; while inspecting the Upper Capital he impeached Grand Preceptor and Right Chancellor Temuder for accepting a bribe of sixty thousand strings of cash from Zhang Bi and commuting a death sentence.
entries.literal: After a long time he was appointed Supervising Censor; inspecting the Upper Capital he impeached the Grand Preceptor and Right Chancellor Temuder for accepting sixty thousand strings of cash in bribes from Zhang Bi and commuting a death sentence.

entries.zh: 帝怒，碎太师印，赐月鲁帖木兒钞万贯，除兵部郎中，拜殿中侍御史。
entries.en: The emperor was enraged, destroyed the Grand Preceptor's seal, rewarded Yuelutiemuer with ten thousand strings of paper money, appointed him director of the Ministry of War, and made him palace attending censor.
entries.literal: The emperor was enraged, shattered the Grand Preceptor's seal, bestowed on Yuelutiemuer ten thousand strings of paper money, appointed him Director of the Ministry of War, and invested him as Palace Attending Censor.

entries.zh: 迁给事中、左侍仪、同修起居注。
entries.en: He was transferred to supervising secretary, left attendant of ceremonies, and associate compiler of the imperial diary.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Supervising Secretary, Left Attendant of Ceremonies, and Associate Compiler of the Imperial Diary.

entries.zh: 寻为右司郎中，赐坐便殿，帝顾左右谓曰：「月鲁帖木兒识量明远，可大用者也。」
entries.en: Soon he became director of the right secretariat; seated in the side hall, the emperor told his attendants, "Yuelutiemuer has clear vision and great capacity; he is fit for high office."
entries.literal: Shortly he became Director of the Right Secretariat; granted a seat in the side hall, the emperor turned to those beside him and said: "Yuelutiemuer's discernment and capacity are clear and far-reaching; he can be greatly employed."

entries.zh: 他日，帝语近臣曰：「朕闻前代皆有太上皇之号，今皇太子且长，可居大位，朕欲为太上皇，与若等游观西山以终天年。」
entries.en: On another occasion the emperor told his close ministers, "I have heard that previous dynasties all had retired emperors; now the crown prince has come of age and can take the throne. I wish to become a retired emperor and spend my remaining years roaming the Western Hills with you."
entries.literal: Another day the emperor said to his close ministers: "I have heard that previous dynasties all had the title Retired Emperor; now the Crown Prince has grown and can occupy the great position; I wish to become Retired Emperor and roam and view the Western Hills with you to end my days."

entries.zh: 御史中丞蛮子、翰林学士明里董阿皆称善。
entries.en: Censor-in-Chief Manzi and Hanlin academician Minglidong'a both praised the idea.
entries.literal: The Censor-in-Chief Manzi and Hanlin Academician Minglidong'a all praised it as good.

entries.zh: 月鲁帖木兒独起拜曰：「臣闻昔之所谓太上皇，若唐玄宗、宋徽宗，皆当祸乱，不得已而为之者也。
entries.en: Yuelutiemuer alone rose and bowed, saying, "Your servant has heard that the so-called retired emperors of old, such as Emperor Xuanzong of Tang and Emperor Huizong of Song, all took that title only amid calamity and disorder, when they had no other choice.
entries.literal: Yuelutiemuer alone rose and bowed, saying: "Your servant has heard that the so-called Retired Emperors of old, such as Emperor Xuanzong of Tang and Emperor Huizong of Song, all faced calamity and disorder and did so only because they had no choice.

entries.zh: 愿陛下正大位，以保万世无疆之业，前代虚名，何足慕哉！」
entries.en: I pray that Your Majesty will hold the throne firmly and preserve the realm's boundless inheritance; what is there to admire in the empty titles of former ages?"
entries.literal: I pray Your Majesty will hold the great position properly, to preserve the enterprise without boundary for ten thousand generations; the empty titles of previous ages—what is there to admire?"

entries.zh: 帝善其对。
entries.en: The emperor approved his reply.
entries.literal: The emperor approved his reply.

entries.zh: 仁宗崩，帖木迭兒复入中书，据相位。
entries.en: After Emperor Renzong's death, Temuder returned to the Central Secretariat and seized the chancellorship.
entries.literal: When Emperor Renzong died, Temuder re-entered the Central Secretariat and held the chancellorship.

entries.zh: 参议乞失监以受人金带系狱，帖木迭兒乃使乞失监诉月鲁帖木兒为御史时诬丞相受赇。
entries.en: Consultant Qishijian was imprisoned for accepting a golden belt as a bribe; Temuder then had Qishijian accuse Yuelutiemuer of having falsely charged the chancellor with bribery when he was a censor.
entries.literal: Consultant Qishijian was imprisoned for accepting a golden belt from someone; Temuder then had Qishijian accuse Yuelutiemuer of, when he was a censor, falsely charging the chancellor with taking bribes.

entries.zh: 皇太后命丞相哈散等即徽政院推问不实，事遂释。
entries.en: The empress dowager ordered Chancellor Hasan and others to investigate at once in the Huizheng Yuan; the charge proved false and the matter was dropped.
entries.literal: The Empress Dowager ordered Chancellor Hasan and others to conduct inquiry immediately at the Huizheng Yuan; the charge was found untrue and the matter was dismissed.

entries.zh: 帖木迭兒乃奏以月鲁帖木兒为山东盐运司副使，降亚中大夫为承事郎，期月间盐课增以万计。
entries.en: Temuder then had Yuelutiemuer appointed vice commissioner of the Shandong Salt Transport Office, demoting his civil prestige rank from Yazhong Dafu to Gentleman for Managing Affairs; within a month salt revenue increased by tens of thousands.
entries.literal: Temuder then memorialized appointing Yuelutiemuer Vice Commissioner of the Shandong Salt Transport Office, demoting his civil prestige rank from Yazhong Dafu to Gentleman for Managing Affairs; within a month salt revenue increased by tens of thousands.

entries.zh: 丁外艰，扶丧西还。
entries.en: Upon his father's death he escorted the coffin westward to return home.
entries.literal: He entered mourning for his father and escorted the coffin westward to return home.

entries.zh: 擢山南江北道肃政廉访副使。
entries.en: He was promoted to vice surveillance commissioner of the Shannan Jiangbei circuit.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Vice Surveillance Commissioner of the Shannan Jiangbei Circuit.

entries.zh: 泰定初，迁汴梁路总管，再调总管武昌，以养亲不赴。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Taiding reign he was appointed prefect of Bianliang Circuit and then transferred to prefect of Wuchang, but declined in order to care for his parents.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Taiding he was transferred to Prefect of Bianliang Circuit; he was again transferred to Prefect of Wuchang but did not take up the post in order to care for his parents.

entries.zh: 致和元年，河南行省平章伯颜矫制起月鲁帖木兒为本省参知政事，共议起兵。
entries.en: In 1328 Bayan, Pingzhang of the Henan Branch Secretariat, forged an imperial order summoning Yuelutiemuer as vice administrator of the province to join in planning a military rising.
entries.literal: In the first year of Zhihe, Henan Branch Secretariat Pingzhang Bayan, by forged imperial command, summoned Yuelutiemuer as Vice Administrator of that province to deliberate together on raising troops.

entries.zh: 月鲁帖木兒固辞曰：「皇子北还，问参政受命何人，则将何辞以对？」
entries.en: Yuelutiemuer firmly declined, saying, "When the prince returns from the north and asks the vice administrator who gave him his commission, what answer will he give?"
entries.literal: Yuelutiemuer firmly declined, saying: "When the prince returns from the north and asks the Vice Administrator from whom he received his commission, what words will he have to answer with?"

entries.zh: 伯颜怒。
entries.en: Bayan was enraged.
entries.literal: Bayan was enraged.

entries.zh: 会明里董阿迓皇子过河南，而月鲁帖木兒为御史时尝劾其娶娼女冒受封，明里董阿因说伯颜收之，丞相别不花亦与之有隙，乃谪月鲁帖木兒乾宁安抚司安置。
entries.en: Minglidong'a happened to be escorting the prince through Henan; when Yuelutiemuer had been a censor he had impeached Minglidong'a for marrying a prostitute and fraudulently receiving a title. Minglidong'a persuaded Bayan to act against him, and Chancellor Biebuhua, who also bore a grudge, joined in; Yuelutiemuer was demoted and placed under the Ganning Pacification Commission.
entries.literal: It happened that Minglidong'a was escorting the prince through Henan; when Yuelutiemuer had been a censor he had once impeached Minglidong'a for marrying a prostitute and fraudulently receiving a title; Minglidong'a therefore persuaded Bayan to take action against him; Chancellor Biebuhua also had a grudge against him; Yuelutiemuer was therefore demoted and placed under the Ganning Pacification Commission.

entries.zh: 至顺四年，移置雷州。
entries.en: In 1333 he was transferred to Lei Prefecture.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Zhishun he was transferred and placed at Lei Prefecture.

entries.zh: 至元六年，顺帝召之还。
entries.en: In 1340 Emperor Shundi summoned him back.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Zhiyuan, Emperor Shundi summoned him back.

entries.zh: 至正二年，入觐，帝欲留之，以母丧未葬辞。
entries.en: In 1342 he came to court; the emperor wished to retain him, but he declined because his mother's funeral had not yet been conducted.
entries.literal: In the second year of Zhizheng he came to audience; the emperor wished to retain him; he declined because his mother had not yet been buried.

entries.zh: 四年，乃起同知将作院事。
entries.en: In 1344 he was finally appointed associate director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he was finally summoned as Associate Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.

entries.zh: 寻除大宗正府也可札鲁花赤。
entries.en: Shortly afterward he was appointed Darughachi of the Court of the Imperial Clan.
entries.literal: Shortly he was appointed Darughachi of the Court of the Imperial Clan.

entries.zh: 九年，由太医院使拜翰林学士承旨、知经筵事。
entries.en: In 1349, after serving as commissioner of the Imperial Medical Service, he was appointed Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts and director of the Classics Mat lectures.
entries.literal: In the ninth year, after serving as Commissioner of the Imperial Medical Service, he was appointed Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts and Director of the Classics Mat lectures.

entries.zh: 进读之际，引援经史，一本于王道，帝嘉纳焉。
entries.en: In his lectures before the throne he drew on the classics and histories, grounding all in the principles of benevolent rule; the emperor warmly approved.
entries.literal: When lecturing before the throne, he cited the classics and histories, grounding all in the kingly way; the emperor approved and adopted his teaching.

entries.zh: 十二年，江南诸郡盗贼充斥，诏拜月鲁帖木兒平章政事，行省江浙，因言于丞相脱脱曰：「守御江南，为计已缓，若得从权行事，犹有可为。」
entries.en: In 1352 bandits overran the prefectures of Jiangnan; an edict appointed Yuelutiemuer Pingzhang and sent him to the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat. He told Chancellor Toghto, "Merely defending Jiangnan is already too late a strategy; if I may act with discretionary authority, there is still something that can be done."
entries.literal: In the twelfth year, bandits filled the various prefectures of Jiangnan; an edict appointed Yuelutiemuer Pingzhang and dispatched him to the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat; he therefore said to Chancellor Toghto: "Defending Jiangnan—the plan is already late; if one may act with discretionary authority, there is still something that can be done."

entries.zh: 不从。
entries.en: Toghto refused.
entries.literal: Toghto did not agree.

entries.zh: 陛辞，赐尚醖、御衣、弓矢、甲胄、卫卒十人、钞万五千贯以行。
entries.en: On taking leave of the court he was granted imperial wine, imperial robes, bow and arrows, armor, ten guard soldiers, and fifteen thousand strings of paper money for his journey.
entries.literal: Bidding farewell at court, he was bestowed imperial wine, imperial robes, bow and arrows, armor, ten guard soldiers, and fifteen thousand strings of paper money for his journey.

entries.zh: 比至镇，引僚属集父老询守备之方，招募民兵数千人，号令明肃。
entries.en: Upon reaching his post he gathered his staff and local elders to discuss defense, recruited several thousand militiamen, and enforced clear and strict discipline.
entries.literal: When he reached his post, he gathered subordinates and elders to inquire about methods of defense, recruited several thousand militia, and his commands were clear and strict.

entries.zh: 统师次建德，获首贼何福斩于市，遂复淳安等县，俘获万餘人，复业者三万餘家。
entries.en: Leading his troops he encamped at Jiande, captured the bandit leader He Fu and executed him in the market, then recovered Chun'an and other counties; more than ten thousand captives were taken and over thirty thousand households returned to their livelihoods.
entries.literal: Leading his army he halted at Jiande, captured the chief bandit He Fu and executed him in the market, then recovered Chun'an and other counties; over ten thousand were captured and more than thirty thousand households returned to their occupations.

entries.zh: 是年七月，次徽州，以疾卒于军中。
entries.en: In the seventh month of that year he reached Huizhou and died of illness in camp.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of that year he halted at Huizhou and died of illness in the army.

entries.zh: 星吉，字吉甫，河西人。
entries.en: Xingji, whose style name was Jifu, was from Hexi.
entries.literal: Xingji, style name Jifu, was a man of Hexi.

entries.zh: 曾祖朵吉，祖搠思吉朵而只，父搠思吉，世事太祖、宪宗、世祖为怯里马赤。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Duoji, grandfather Suosijiduorezhi, and father Suosiji had all served Emperors Taizu, Xianzong, and Shizu as qielimachi.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Duoji, grandfather Suosijiduorezhi, and father Suosiji all served Emperors Taizu, Xianzong, and Shizu as qielimachi.

entries.zh: 星吉少给事仁宗潜邸，以精敏称。
entries.en: From youth Xingji served in Emperor Renzong's household before his accession and was known for keen intelligence.
entries.literal: Xingji from youth served in Emperor Renzong's residence before accession and was known for keen intelligence.

entries.zh: 至治初，授中尚监，改右侍仪，兼修起居注。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Zhizhi reign he was appointed director of the Central Palace Service, then transferred to right attendant of ceremonies and associate compiler of the imperial diary.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Zhizhi he was appointed Director of the Central Palace Service, transferred to Right Attendant of Ceremonies, and concurrently Compiler of the Imperial Diary.

entries.zh: 拜监察御史，有直声。
entries.en: He was appointed supervising censor and earned a reputation for integrity.
entries.literal: He was appointed Supervising Censor and had a reputation for uprightness.

entries.zh: 自是十五迁为宣政院使，出为江南行御史臺御史大夫。
entries.en: He was promoted fifteen times in succession to commissioner of the Xuanzheng Yuan, then appointed censor-in-chief of the Jiangnan branch censorate.
entries.literal: From this he was promoted fifteen times to Commissioner of the Xuanzheng Yuan, then sent out as Censor-in-Chief of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate.

entries.zh: 时承平日久，内外方以观望为政，星吉独持风裁，御史行部，必敕厉而遣之。
entries.en: Peace had lasted so long that officials everywhere adopted a wait-and-see attitude; Xingji alone upheld strict discipline, and whenever he sent censors on circuit tours he admonished them sternly before their departure.
entries.literal: At that time peace had lasted long; inside and outside all took a wait-and-see attitude in government; Xingji alone upheld discipline; when censors toured the circuits he always admonished them sternly before dispatching them.

entries.zh: 湖东佥事三宝住，儒者也，性廉介，所至搏贪猾无所贷。
entries.en: Sanbaozhu, associate commissioner of Hudong, was a Confucian scholar of incorruptible character who struck at the greedy and cunning wherever he went without mercy.
entries.literal: Hudong Associate Commissioner Sanbaozhu was a Confucian scholar, upright and incorruptible by nature; wherever he went he struck at the greedy and cunning without mercy.

entries.zh: 御史有以自私请者，拒不纳，则诬以事劾之。
entries.en: When a censor made a private request of him, he refused; the censor then fabricated charges and impeached him.
entries.literal: A censor made a private request to him; he refused to accept it; the censor then falsely charged him with an offense and impeached him.

entries.zh: 章至，星吉怒曰：「若人之廉，孰不知之，乃敢为是言耶！」
entries.en: When the memorial arrived, Xingji said angrily, "Everyone knows that man's integrity—how dare you make such an accusation!"
entries.literal: When the memorial arrived, Xingji said in anger: "That man's integrity—who does not know it? Yet you dare speak such words!"

entries.zh: 即奏杖御史而白其誣。
entries.en: He immediately memorialized to have the censor caned and to clear the false charge.
entries.literal: He immediately memorialized to cane the censor and clear the false charge.

entries.zh: 执政者恶之，移湖广行省平章政事。
entries.en: The ruling faction disliked him and transferred him to Pingzhang of the Huguang Branch Secretariat.
entries.literal: Those in power disliked him and transferred him to Pingzhang of the Huguang Branch Secretariat.

entries.zh: 湖广地连江北，威顺王岁尝出猎，民病之。
entries.en: Huguang bordered the north bank of the Yangzi; Prince Weishun went hunting every year and the people suffered greatly.
entries.literal: Huguang bordered the north of the Yangzi; Prince Weishun went out hunting every year and the people suffered from it.

entries.zh: 又起广乐园，多萃名倡巨贾以网大利，有司莫敢忤。
entries.en: He also built the Guangle Garden, gathering famous entertainers and wealthy merchants to reap great profits, and no official dared oppose him.
entries.literal: He also built the Guangle Garden, gathering famous entertainers and great merchants to net great profit; no official dared oppose him.

entries.zh: 星吉至，谒王，王阖中门，启左扉，召以入。
entries.en: When Xingji arrived to call on the prince, the prince closed the central gate and opened only the left side door to admit him.
entries.literal: When Xingji arrived he called on the prince; the prince closed the central gate and opened the left side door, summoning him to enter.

entries.zh: 星吉引绳床坐王中门西，言曰：「吾受天子命来作牧，非王私臣也，焉得由不正之道入乎！」
entries.en: Xingji drew up a rope bed and sat west of the central gate, saying, "I have received the Son of Heaven's command to govern this region; I am not your private servant—how can I enter by an improper entrance!"
