entries.literal: Xingji drew a rope bed and sat west of the prince's central gate, saying: "I have received the Son of Heaven's command to come as governor; I am not the prince's private servant—how can I enter by an improper way!"

entries.zh: 阍者惧，入告王，王命启中门。
entries.en: The gatekeeper was alarmed and reported to the prince, who ordered the central gate opened.
entries.literal: The gatekeeper was afraid and went in to tell the prince; the prince ordered the central gate opened.

entries.zh: 星吉入，责王曰：「王帝室之懿，古之所谓伯父叔父者也。
entries.en: Xingji entered and reproached the prince: "Your Highness is a kinsman of the imperial house, what the ancients called a royal uncle.
entries.literal: Xingji entered and reproached the prince: "Your Highness is an honored member of the imperial house, what the ancients called paternal uncle or maternal uncle.

entries.zh: 今德音不闻，而骋猎宣淫，贾怨于下，恐非所以自贻多福也。」
entries.en: Yet no word of your virtue is heard, while you roam hunting and indulge in dissipation, earning resentment among the people—I fear this is not the way to secure blessings for yourself."
entries.literal: Now no virtuous reputation is heard, yet you roam hunting and indulge in dissipation, buying resentment below— I fear this is not the way to secure abundant blessings for yourself."

entries.zh: 王急握星吉手谢之，为悉罢其所为。
entries.en: The prince hastily grasped Xingji's hand and apologized, abolishing all his excesses.
entries.literal: The prince hastily grasped Xingji's hand and apologized, abolishing all that he had done.

entries.zh: 有胡僧曰小住持者，服三品命，恃宠横甚，数以事凌轹官府。
entries.en: There was a Hu monk called Little Abbot who held third-rank appointment, relied on imperial favor, and repeatedly bullied government offices.
entries.literal: There was a Hu monk called Little Abbot who held third-rank appointment, relied on favor and was extremely overbearing, repeatedly bullying the government offices on various pretexts.

entries.zh: 星吉命掩捕之，得妻妾女乐妇女十有八人，狱具，罪而籍之，由是豪强敛手，贫弱称快。
entries.en: Xingji had him secretly arrested. The search uncovered eighteen women, including wives, concubines, and female musicians. Once the case was complete, the monk was convicted and his property confiscated; thereafter the powerful restrained themselves, and the poor rejoiced.
entries.literal: Xingji ordered his secret arrest. Eighteen women, including wives, concubines, and female musicians, were found; once the case was complete, the monk was convicted and his property confiscated. From then on the powerful held back and the poor rejoiced.

entries.zh: 至正十一年，汝、颍妖贼起，会僚属议之，或曰：「有郑万户，老将也，宜起而用之。」
entries.en: In 1351 rebel bandits arose in Ru and Ying; when Xingji convened his staff to discuss the crisis, some said, "There is the ten-thousand household Zheng, an old general—we should summon and employ him."
entries.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhizheng, demonic bandits arose in Ru and Ying; convening his subordinates to discuss it, some said: "There is Ten-thousand Household Zheng, an old general—it is fitting to summon and employ him."

entries.zh: 星吉乃命募士兵，完城池，修器械，严巡警，悉以其事属郑。
entries.en: Xingji then ordered the recruitment of militia, repair of the city walls, preparation of weapons, and strict patrols, entrusting all these matters to Zheng.
entries.literal: Xingji then ordered recruitment of militia, repair of city walls, preparation of weapons, strict patrols, and entrusted all these matters to Zheng.

entries.zh: 贼闻之，遣其党二千来约降。
entries.en: When the bandits heard of this, they sent two thousand men to negotiate surrender.
entries.literal: The bandits heard of this and sent two thousand of their followers to negotiate surrender.

entries.zh: 星吉与郑谋曰：「此诈也，然降而却之，于是为不宜，宜受而审之可也。」
entries.en: Xingji and Zheng agreed: "This is a ruse, but to accept their surrender and then reject them would be improper; we should accept them and investigate."
entries.literal: Xingji and Zheng deliberated: "This is a deception; yet to accept surrender and then reject it would be improper—it is fitting to accept and investigate."

entries.zh: 果得其情，乃歼之，械其渠魁数十人以俟命。
entries.en: They confirmed the deception, annihilated the force, and shackled several dozen ringleaders to await orders.
entries.literal: They indeed obtained the truth, then annihilated them and shackled several dozen of their ringleaders to await orders.

entries.zh: 适有旨召为大司农。
entries.en: Just then an edict summoned him to the capital as Minister of Revenue.
entries.literal: Just then an edict summoned him as Minister of Revenue.

entries.zh: 同僚受贼赂，且嫉其功，乃诬郑罪，释其所械者。
entries.en: Colleagues who had taken bribes from the bandits and envied Xingji's achievements falsely charged Zheng with crimes and released the prisoners he had shackled.
entries.literal: Colleagues had accepted bribes from the bandits and, jealous of his achievements, falsely charged Zheng with crimes and released those he had shackled.

entries.zh: 明日，贼大至，内外响应，城遂陷。
entries.en: The next day the bandits arrived in force; the city rose in response inside and out, and the city fell.
entries.literal: The next day the bandits came in force; inside and outside responded; the city fell.

entries.zh: 武昌之人骈首夜泣曰：「大夫不去，吾岂为俘囚乎？」
entries.en: The people of Wuchang wept together by night: "Had our commissioner not left, how could we have become captives?"
entries.literal: The people of Wuchang, heads together, wept by night: "Had the Grandee not left, how could we have become captives?"

entries.zh: 星吉既入见，具陈贼本末。
entries.en: When Xingji appeared at court he gave a full account of the bandit uprising.
entries.literal: When Xingji had entered for audience, he fully reported the beginning and end of the bandit affair.

entries.zh: 帝大喜，命赐食。
entries.en: The emperor was greatly pleased and ordered a meal served.
entries.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and ordered food bestowed.

entries.zh: 时宰不悦，奏为江西行省平章政事，员外置。
entries.en: The chief ministers were displeased and had him appointed Pingzhang of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat on an extra-staff basis.
entries.literal: The chief ministers were displeased and memorialized appointing him Pingzhang of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat, established outside the regular quota.

entries.zh: 星吉至江东，诏令守江州。
entries.en: When Xingji reached Jiangdong, an edict ordered him to defend Jiang Prefecture.
entries.literal: When Xingji reached Jiangdong, an edict ordered him to defend Jiang Prefecture.

entries.zh: 时江州已陷，贼据池阳。
entries.en: Jiang Prefecture had already fallen and the bandits held Chiyang.
entries.literal: At that time Jiang Prefecture had already fallen and the bandits held Chiyang.

entries.zh: 太平官军止有三百人，贼号百万，众皆欲走。
entries.en: The government troops at Taiping numbered only three hundred; the bandits claimed a million men; everyone wished to flee.
entries.literal: The government troops at Taiping numbered only three hundred; the bandits claimed a million; all wished to flee.

entries.zh: 星吉曰：「畏贼而逃，非勇也；
entries.en: Xingji said, "To flee from fear of bandits is not courage;
entries.literal: Xingji said: "To flee from fear of bandits is not courage;

entries.zh: 坐而待攻，非智也。
entries.en: to sit and await attack is not wisdom.
entries.literal: to sit and await attack is not wisdom.

entries.zh: 汝等皆有妻子财物，纵逃其可免乎？」
entries.en: You all have wives, children, and property—even if you flee, can you escape?"
entries.literal: You all have wives, children, and property—even if you flee, can you escape?"

entries.zh: 乃贷富人钱，募人为兵。
entries.en: He borrowed money from the wealthy and recruited soldiers.
entries.literal: He then borrowed money from the wealthy and recruited men as soldiers.

entries.zh: 先是，行台募兵，人给百五十千，无应者。
entries.en: Previously the branch censorate had offered one hundred fifty thousand cash per recruit, with no takers.
entries.literal: Previously the Branch Censorate had recruited soldiers, offering one hundred fifty thousand cash per man, with no respondents.

entries.zh: 至是，星吉募兵，人五十千，从争赴之，一日得三千人。
entries.en: Now Xingji offered fifty thousand per recruit and men competed to join; in one day he raised three thousand.
entries.literal: Now Xingji recruited soldiers at fifty thousand per man; followers competed to join; in one day he obtained three thousand men.

entries.zh: 乃具舟楫直趋铜陵，克之。
entries.en: He equipped boats and sailed straight to Tongling, which he captured.
entries.literal: He then equipped boats and went straight to Tongling and captured it.

entries.zh: 又破贼白马湾。
entries.en: He again defeated the bandits at Baimawan.
entries.literal: He again defeated the bandits at Baimawan.

entries.zh: 贼败走，分兵蹑之，抵白湄。
entries.en: The bandits were routed and fled; he sent detachments in pursuit and reached Baimai.
entries.literal: The bandits were defeated and fled; he divided forces to pursue them and reached Baimai.

entries.zh: 贼穷急，回拒官军，官军乘胜奋击，贼尽殪，擒其渠魁周驴，夺船六百艘，军声大振，遂复池州。
entries.en: Cornered, the bandits turned to fight; the government forces pressed their advantage and killed them to the last man, capturing their leader Zhou Lv and seizing six hundred boats. Military prestige soared, and Chizhou was recovered.
entries.literal: The bandits in desperate straits turned to resist the government army; the government army seized victory and fought fiercely; the bandits were all killed; their ringleader Zhou Lv was captured; six hundred boats were seized; military prestige greatly rose; and Chizhou was recovered.

entries.zh: 乃命诸将分道讨贼，复石埭诸县。
entries.en: He then ordered his generals to pursue the bandits by separate routes and recovered Shizhi and other counties.
entries.literal: He then ordered the generals to pursue the bandits by separate routes and recovered Shizhi and other counties.

entries.zh: 贼复来攻，命王惟恭列阵当之，锋始交，出小舰从旁横击，大破走之，进据清水湾。
entries.en: When the bandits attacked again, he ordered Wang Weigong to form battle lines; as the vanguards engaged, he sent small boats to strike from the flank, routing the enemy and advancing to occupy Qingshuiwan.
entries.literal: The bandits again came to attack; he ordered Wang Weigong to form battle lines to meet them; as the vanguards had just engaged, he sent small boats to strike from the flank and inflicted a great defeat driving them off, advancing to occupy Qingshuiwan.

entries.zh: 伺者告贼舰至自上流，顺风举帆，众且数十倍，诸将失色。
entries.en: Scouts reported bandit ships approaching from upstream under full sail with favorable wind, nearly ten times their strength; the generals turned pale.
entries.literal: Scouts reported bandit ships arriving from upstream with favorable wind and sails raised; their numbers were nearly ten times greater; the generals turned pale.

entries.zh: 星吉曰：「无伤也，风势盛，彼仓卒必不得泊，但伏横港中偃旗以待，俟过而击之，无不胜矣。」
entries.en: Xingji said, "No matter—the wind is strong and they will not be able to moor in haste. Lie in ambush in the cross-channel with flags lowered and strike after they pass; you cannot fail."
entries.literal: Xingji said: "No harm; the wind is strong—they in haste surely cannot moor; only lie in ambush in the cross-channel with flags lowered and wait; strike after they pass—there is none you cannot defeat."

entries.zh: 风怒水驶，贼奄忽而过，乃命举旗张帆鼓噪而薄之，官军殊死战，风反为我用，又大破之。
entries.en: The wind roared and the current raced; the bandits swept past; he ordered flags raised, sails spread, and drums beaten as his forces closed in. The government troops fought to the death; the wind shifted in their favor, and they inflicted another crushing defeat.
entries.literal: The wind raged and the water rushed; the bandits suddenly passed; he then ordered flags raised, sails spread, and drums and shouts as they closed in; the government army fought to the death; the wind turned to their use; and they again inflicted a great defeat.

entries.zh: 时贼久围安庆，捷闻，遽烧营走。
entries.en: The bandits had long besieged Anqing; when news of the victory arrived, they hastily burned their camps and fled.
entries.literal: At that time the bandits had long besieged Anqing; when news of victory arrived, they hastily burned their camps and fled.

entries.zh: 进复湖口县，克江州，留兵守之。
entries.en: He advanced and recovered Hukou County, captured Jiang Prefecture, and left troops to garrison it.
entries.literal: Advancing he recovered Hukou County, captured Jiang Prefecture, and left troops to garrison it.

entries.zh: 命王惟恭栅小孤山，而星吉自据番阳口，缀江湖要冲以图恢复。
entries.en: He ordered Wang Weigong to fortify Xiaogushan while he himself held Panyangkou, controlling the vital river junctions to plan the recovery of the region.
entries.literal: He ordered Wang Weigong to fortify Xiaogushan while Xingji himself held Panyangkou, linking the vital points of rivers and lakes to plan recovery.

entries.zh: 时湖广已陷，江西被围，淮、浙亦多故，卒无继援之者，日久粮益乏，士卒咸困。
entries.en: Huguang had fallen, Jiangxi was besieged, and Huai and Zhe were also in turmoil; no relief came, and as time passed grain grew scarce and the soldiers were exhausted.
entries.literal: At that time Huguang had fallen, Jiangxi was besieged, Huai and Zhe also had many troubles; in the end there was no one to bring relief; as days lengthened grain grew ever scarcer and the soldiers were all distressed.

entries.zh: 或曰：「东南完实，盍因粮以图再举乎？」
entries.en: Someone said, "The southeast is still intact—why not withdraw there with its grain and plan another campaign?"
entries.literal: Someone said: "The southeast is intact and substantial—why not use its grain to plan another rising?"

entries.zh: 星吉曰：「吾受命守江西，必死于此。」
entries.en: Xingji said, "I have been ordered to defend Jiangxi—I will die here."
entries.literal: Xingji said: "I have received command to defend Jiangxi—I must die here."

entries.zh: 众莫敢复言。
entries.en: No one dared speak again.
entries.literal: None dared speak again.

entries.zh: 有顷，贼乘大船四集，来攻我军，取蒹苇编为大筏，塞上下流火之。
entries.en: Before long the bandits gathered four large ships and attacked the government forces; they wove reeds into great rafts, blocked the upper and lower reaches of the river, and set them ablaze.
entries.literal: Before long the bandits gathered in four great ships and came to attack the government army; they took reeds and rushes and wove them into great rafts, blocked the upper and lower reaches, and set them afire.

entries.zh: 我军力战，众死且尽。
entries.en: The government troops fought fiercely until nearly all were dead.
entries.literal: The government army fought fiercely; the host died to the last man.

entries.zh: 星吉之从子伯不华与亲兵数十人死之。
entries.en: Xingji's nephew Bobuhua and several dozen personal guards died fighting.
entries.literal: Xingji's nephew Bobuhua and several dozen personal guards died with them.

entries.zh: 星吉犹坚坐不动。
entries.en: Xingji remained seated, unmoving.
entries.literal: Xingji still sat firmly without moving.

entries.zh: 賊發矢射星吉，乃昏仆。
entries.en: The bandits shot arrows at Xingji, and he collapsed unconscious.
entries.literal: The bandits shot arrows at Xingji; he then fainted and fell.

entries.zh: 贼素闻星吉名，不忍害，舁置密室中，至旦乃苏。
entries.en: The bandits had long heard of Xingji's reputation and could not bring themselves to kill him; they carried him to a secret chamber, and by dawn he had revived.
entries.literal: The bandits had long heard Xingji's name and could not bear to harm him; they carried him to a secret chamber, and by dawn he revived.

entries.zh: 贼罗拜，争馈以食。
entries.en: The bandits bowed before him and competed to offer him food.
entries.literal: The bandits bowed in a circle and competed to offer him food.

entries.zh: 星吉斥之，遂不复食。
entries.en: Xingji rebuked them and refused to eat again.
entries.literal: Xingji rebuked them and thereafter ate no more.

entries.zh: 凡七日，乃自力而起，北面再拜曰：「臣力竭矣。」
entries.en: After seven days he rose by his own strength, bowed twice to the north, and said, "Your servant's strength is exhausted."
entries.literal: After seven days he rose by his own strength, bowed twice to the north, and said: "Your servant's strength is exhausted."

entries.zh: 遂绝，年五十七。
entries.en: He then died at the age of fifty-seven.
entries.literal: He then expired; he was fifty-seven years old.

entries.zh: 星吉为人公廉明决，及在军中，能与将士同甘苦，以忠义感激人心，故能以少击众、得人死力云。
entries.en: Xingji was fair, incorruptible, and decisive; in the army he shared hardship and comfort with his officers and soldiers, inspiring loyalty and righteousness in their hearts. Thus he could defeat larger forces with smaller ones and win men's utmost devotion unto death.
entries.literal: Xingji as a man was fair, incorruptible, clear, and decisive; when in the army he could share hardship and comfort with officers and soldiers, moving people's hearts with loyalty and righteousness; therefore he could strike the many with the few and win men's utmost effort unto death.

entries.zh: 答里麻
entries.en: Dalima
entries.literal: Dalima

entries.zh: 秋七月，忽都虎以民籍至，帝議裂州縣賜親王功臣。
entries.en: In the seventh month Huduqu delivered the household registers, and the emperor considered dividing prefectures among princes and meritorious ministers.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of autumn Huduqu arrived with the household registers; the Emperor deliberated on carving up prefectures and districts to bestow on imperial princes and meritorious ministers.

entries.zh: 楚材曰：「裂土分民，易生嫌隙，不如多以金帛與之。」
entries.en: Chucai said, "Dividing land and people breeds suspicion; better to reward them generously with gold and silk."
entries.literal: Chucai said, "To split land and divide the people easily breeds suspicion and rifts; it would be better to give them more gold and silk."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「已許奈何？」
entries.en: The emperor said, "I have already promised—what can be done?"
entries.literal: The Emperor said, "It has already been promised—what is to be done?"

entries.zh: 楚材曰：「若朝廷置吏，收其貢賦，歲終頒之，使毋擅科徵，可也。」
entries.en: Chucai said, "Let the court appoint officials to collect tribute and distribute it at year's end, forbidding private levies—that will suffice."
entries.literal: Chucai said, "If the court appoints officials, collects their tribute and levies, and at year's end distributes them, so that they may not levy on their own authority, that will do."

entries.zh: 帝然其計，遂定天下賦稅，每二戶出絲一斤，以給國用；
entries.en: The emperor approved and fixed the realm's taxes: every two households owed one jin of silk for state revenue;
entries.literal: The Emperor approved his plan and thereupon fixed the realm's taxes: every two households were to contribute one jin of silk for state use;

entries.zh: 五戶出絲一斤，以給諸王功臣湯沐之資。
entries.en: and every five households one jin for the princes' and ministers' maintenance allotments.
entries.literal: five households one jin of silk, to supply the bathing-fief funds of the princes and meritorious ministers.

entries.zh: 地稅，中田每畝二升又半，上田三升，下田二升，水田每畝五升；
entries.en: Land tax was set at two and a half sheng per mu for middling fields, three for upper fields, two for lower fields, and five for paddy;
entries.literal: Land tax: on middling fields two and a half sheng per mu, on upper fields three sheng, on lower fields two sheng, on paddy fields five sheng per mu;

entries.zh: 商稅，三十分而一；
entries.en: commercial tax at one-thirtieth;
entries.literal: commercial tax, one part in thirty;

entries.zh: 鹽價，銀一兩四十斤。
entries.en: and salt at forty jin per tael of silver.
entries.literal: salt price, one tael of silver for forty jin.

entries.zh: 既定常賦，朝議以為太輕，楚材曰：「作法於涼，其弊猶貪，後將有以利進者，則今已重矣。」
entries.en: When the regular levies were fixed, the court thought them too light; Chucai said, "Even lenient laws breed greed; once men advance by squeezing profit from the people, today's light burden will seem heavy enough."
entries.literal: Once the regular levies were fixed, the court considered them too light; Chucai said, "If one makes law in cool times, its abuse is still greed; later there will be those who advance by profit—then what is light today will already be heavy."

entries.zh: 時工匠製造，糜費官物，十私八九，楚材請皆考核之，以為定制。
entries.en: Artisans were wasting government materials, keeping eight or nine parts in ten for themselves; Chucai ordered audits and fixed standards.
entries.literal: At the time artisans in manufacture squandered government goods, eight or nine in ten for private use; Chucai requested that all be audited and made a fixed regulation.

entries.zh: 時侍臣脫歡奏簡天下室女，詔下，楚材尼之不行，帝怒。
entries.en: The attendant Toqan proposed selecting maidens empire-wide; when the edict was issued Chucai blocked its execution, and the emperor grew angry.
entries.literal: At the time the attendant Toqan memorialized to select maidens throughout the realm; when the edict was issued Chucai blocked it from being carried out, and the Emperor was angry.

entries.zh: 楚材進曰：「向擇美女二十有八人，足備使令。
entries.en: Chucai said, "Twenty-eight women have already been chosen—enough for the palace.
entries.literal: Chucai advanced and said, "Previously twenty-eight beautiful women were chosen—enough to serve at command.

entries.zh: 今復選拔，臣恐擾民，欲覆奏耳。」
entries.en: Another selection would distress the people; I only wished to report back to you."
entries.literal: To select again now—I fear disturbing the people and wished only to memorialize again."

entries.zh: 帝良久曰：「可罷之。」
entries.en: After a long silence the emperor said, "Let it be canceled."
entries.literal: After a long while the Emperor said, "It may be stopped."

entries.zh: 又欲收民牝馬，楚材曰：「田蠶之地，非馬所產，今若行之，後必為人害。」
entries.en: The emperor also wanted to seize the people's brood mares; Chucai said, "These are farming and silk country, not horse country; do this now and it will harm the people for years to come."
entries.literal: He also wished to collect the people's brood mares; Chucai said, "In lands of fields and silkworms horses are not produced; if this is done now, later it will surely harm the people."

entries.zh: 又從之。
entries.en: Again the emperor agreed.
entries.literal: Again this was followed.

entries.zh: 丁酉，楚材奏曰：「制器者必用良工，守成者必用儒臣。
entries.en: In the dingyou year Chucai memorialized, "Making vessels requires skilled craftsmen; preserving a realm requires Confucian ministers.
entries.literal: In the year dingyou Chucai memorialized, "Those who make vessels must use skilled artisans; those who preserve an inheritance must use Confucian ministers.

entries.zh: 儒臣之事業，非積數十年，殆未易成也。」
entries.en: Their craft is not mastered in a few decades—it is hard won."
entries.literal: The enterprise of Confucian ministers is not accumulated over mere decades—it is scarcely easy to accomplish."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「果爾，可官其人。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "If that is so, then give them office."
entries.literal: The Emperor said, "If it is truly so, their persons may be given office."

entries.zh: 楚材曰：「請校試之。」
entries.en: Chucai said, "Let them be examined first."
entries.literal: Chucai said, "I request that they be examined and tested."

entries.zh: 乃命宣德州宣課使劉中隨郡考試，以經義、詞賦、論分為三科，儒人被俘為奴者，亦令就試，其主匿弗遣者死。
entries.en: He ordered Liu Zhong, tax commissioner of Xuande, to hold examinations in every commandery in three fields—classics, rhapsodies, and policy essays. Captured scholars enslaved were also to sit the exam; masters who hid them were put to death.
entries.literal: Thereupon he ordered Liu Zhong, tax commissioner of Xuande Prefecture, to conduct examinations in each commandery, divided into three categories—classics, rhapsodies, and discourses; Confucian scholars taken captive as slaves were also ordered to sit the examination, and masters who concealed them and did not send them were to die.

entries.zh: 得士凡四千三十人，免為奴者四之一。
entries.en: Four thousand and thirty scholars passed; one in four were freed from slavery.
entries.literal: Scholars obtained numbered four thousand thirty in all; one in four were freed from slavery.

entries.zh: 先是，州郡長吏，多藉賈人銀以償官，息累數倍，曰羊羔兒利，至奴其妻子猶不足償。
entries.en: Previously local magistrates often borrowed silver from merchants to meet government quotas at usurious "lamb-kid" rates, until even selling their wives and children could not repay the debt.
entries.literal: Earlier, prefectural and district chiefs mostly borrowed merchants' silver to repay the government; interest accumulated several times over, called "lamb-kid interest," until even enslaving their wives and children was insufficient to repay.

entries.zh: 楚材奏令本利相侔而止，永為定制，民間所負者，官為代價之。
entries.en: Chucai memorialized that interest should not exceed principal and that the state would redeem private debts—a permanent rule.
entries.literal: Chucai memorialized that principal and interest should be made equal and then stop, permanently as a fixed regulation, and what the people owed the government would repay on their behalf.

entries.zh: 至一衡量，給符印，立鈔法，定均輸，布遞傳，明驛券，庶政略備，民稍蘇息焉。
entries.en: He standardized weights and measures, issued seals and tallies, established paper currency, fixed transport quotas, organized courier routes, and clarified post warrants; civil administration was largely in place, and the people began to recover.
entries.literal: He unified weights and measures, issued tallies and seals, established paper-note law, fixed equalized transport, deployed relay posts, clarified post warrants—in general administration was largely complete, and the people were somewhat revived.

entries.zh: 鑄字成仲，幼聰敏，善屬文，尤工騎射。
entries.en: Zhu, courtesy name Chengzhong, was clever as a child, skilled at writing, and especially adept at riding and archery.
entries.literal: Zhu, styled Chengzhong, was clever as a child, skilled in literary composition, and especially adept at riding and archery.

entries.zh: 楚材薨，嗣領中書省事，時年二十三。
entries.en: When Chucai died, Zhu succeeded him as head of the Secretariat at the age of twenty-three.
entries.literal: When Chucai died, Zhu succeeded to direct the affairs of the Secretariat; at the time he was twenty-three.

entries.zh: 鑄上言宜疏禁網，遂採歷代德政合於時宜者八十一章以進。
entries.en: Zhu memorialized that the laws should be eased and presented eighty-one examples of benevolent governance from past dynasties suited to the present.
entries.literal: Zhu memorialized that the prohibitions of the law should be loosened, and thereupon collected eighty-one items of benevolent government from successive ages suited to the times and presented them.

entries.zh: 戊午，憲宗徵蜀，詔鑄領侍衛驍果以從，屢出奇計，攻下城邑，賜以尚方金鎖甲及內厩驄馬。
entries.en: In the wuwu year, when Emperor Xianzong campaigned in Shu, Zhu led the palace guard; his repeated stratagems took cities, and he was rewarded with imperial armor and piebald horses from the royal stables.
entries.literal: In the year wuwu Emperor Xianzong campaigned against Shu; Zhu was ordered to lead the palace guard swift troops in attendance; he repeatedly devised surprising stratagems, captured walled cities, and was bestowed imperial gold-linked armor and piebald horses from the inner stables.

entries.zh: 乙未，憲宗崩，阿里不哥叛，鑄棄妻子，挺身自朔方來歸，世祖嘉其忠，即日召見，賞賜優厚。
entries.en: In the yiwei year, when Emperor Xianzong died and Ariq Böke rebelled, Zhu abandoned his family and came alone from the north to submit; Kublai praised his loyalty, received him that day, and rewarded him generously.
entries.literal: In the year yiwei Emperor Xianzong died; Ariq Böke rebelled; Zhu abandoned wife and children and came alone from the northern frontier to submit; Emperor Shizu praised his loyalty, summoned him that same day, and rewarded him generously.

entries.zh: 中統二年，拜中書左丞相。
entries.en: In the second year of Zhongtong he was appointed left chief director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: In the second year of Zhongtong he was appointed Left Chief Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 是年冬，詔將兵備禦北邊，後徵兵扈從，敗阿里不哥於上都之北。
entries.en: That winter he was ordered to guard the northern frontier; later he joined the imperial campaign and defeated Ariq Böke north of Shangdu.
entries.literal: That winter he was ordered to command troops to guard the northern frontier; later he was summoned with the army in attendance and defeated Ariq Böke north of Shangdu.

entries.zh: 至元元年，加光祿大夫。
entries.en: In the first year of Zhiyuan he was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
entries.literal: In the first year of Zhiyuan he was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

entries.zh: 奏定法令三十七章，吏民便之。
entries.en: He memorialized and codified thirty-seven chapters of law, to the benefit of officials and people alike.
entries.literal: He memorialized and fixed thirty-seven chapters of laws and regulations, to the convenience of officials and people.

entries.zh: 二年，行省山東。
entries.en: In the second year he served as branch secretariat of Shandong.
entries.literal: In the second year he served as Branch Secretariat of Shandong.

entries.zh: 未幾徵還。
entries.en: Before long he was recalled to court.
entries.literal: Before long he was recalled.

entries.zh: 初，清廟雅樂，止有登歌，詔鑄制宮懸八佾之舞。
entries.en: Previously the imperial temple music had only the ascending hymns; Zhu was ordered to compose the full court orchestra and the eight-row dance.
entries.literal: Earlier, for the refined music of the Imperial Temple there was only the ascending song; Zhu was ordered to compose the palace ensemble and the dance of eight rows.

entries.zh: 四年春三月，樂舞成，表上之，仍請賜名《大成》，制曰「可」。
entries.en: In the third month of the fourth year the music and dance were completed; he presented them and asked that they be named "Great Completion"; the emperor approved.
entries.literal: In the third month of spring in the fourth year the music and dance were completed; he memorialized and presented them, and also requested the bestowed name "Great Completion"; the decree said "Approved."

entries.zh: 六月，改榮祿大夫、平章政事。
entries.en: In the sixth month he was made Grand Master for Glorious Blessings and associate administrator of affairs.
entries.literal: In the sixth month he was changed to Grand Master for Glorious Blessings and Associate Administrator of Affairs.

entries.zh: 五年，復拜光祿大夫、中書左丞相。
entries.en: In the fifth year he was again appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and left chief director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: In the fifth year he was again appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Left Chief Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 十年，遷平章軍國重事。
entries.en: In the tenth year he was made associate administrator of important military and civil affairs.
entries.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to Associate Administrator of Important Military and Civil Affairs.

entries.zh: 十三年，詔監修國史。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year he was ordered to supervise compilation of the national history.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year he was ordered to supervise the compilation of the national history.

entries.zh: 朝廷有大事，必諮訪焉。
entries.en: On great matters of state the court always consulted him.
entries.literal: When the court had great affairs, it invariably consulted him.

entries.zh: 十九年，復拜中書左丞相。
entries.en: In the nineteenth year he was again appointed left chief director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: In the nineteenth year he was again appointed Left Chief Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 二十年冬十月，坐不納職印、妄奏東平人聚謀為逆、間諜幕僚、及黨罪囚阿里沙，遂罷免，仍沒其家貲之半，徙居山後。
entries.en: In the tenth month of the twentieth year he was dismissed for refusing his seal of office, falsely reporting a Dongping conspiracy, employing spies among his staff, and shielding the prisoner Alisha; half his property was confiscated and he was exiled north of the mountains.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of winter in the twentieth year, on charges of not accepting the seal of office, falsely memorializing that people of Dongping had gathered to plot rebellion, spying through staff, and shielding the guilty prisoner Alisha, he was dismissed, half his household property was confiscated, and he was moved to live behind the mountains.

entries.zh: 二十二年卒，年六十五。
entries.en: He died in the twenty-second year at the age of sixty-five.
entries.literal: In the twenty-second year he died, aged sixty-five.

entries.zh: 子十一人：希徵，希勃，希亮，希寬，希素，希固，希周，希光，希逸淮東宣慰使，餘失其名。
entries.en: He had eleven sons: Xizheng, Xibo, Xiliang, Xikuan, Xisu, Xigu, Xizhou, Xiguang, and Xiyi, who became pacification commissioner of Huaidong; the names of the rest are lost.
entries.literal: He had eleven sons: Xizheng, Xibo, Xiliang, Xikuan, Xisu, Xigu, Xizhou, Xiguang, Xiyi (Pacification Commissioner of Huaidong)—the rest have lost their names.

entries.zh: 至順元年，贈推忠保德宣力佐治功臣、太師、開府儀同三司、上柱國、懿寧王，諡文忠。
entries.en: In the first year of Zhishun he was posthumously honored as Merit-holder Who Promotes Loyalty, Preserves Virtue, and Expands Strength in Assisting Governance, Grand Preceptor, Grand Master with Honor Equal to the Three Excellencies, Upper Pillar of the State, and Prince of Yining, with the posthumous name Wenzhong.
entries.literal: In the first year of Zhishun he was posthumously given the title Merit-holder Who Promotes Loyalty, Preserves Virtue, and Expands Strength in Assisting Governance, Grand Preceptor, Grand Master with Honor Equal to the Three Excellencies, Upper Pillar of the State, Prince of Yining, with the posthumous name Wenzhong.

entries.zh: 十年，詔其子江淮安撫使南合嗣行軍前中書省事。
entries.en: In the tenth year an edict ordered his son Nanhe, Jiang-Huai pacification commissioner, to succeed to Secretariat affairs with the army.
entries.literal: In the tenth year an edict ordered his son Nanhe, Jiang-Huai pacification commissioner, to succeed to Secretariat affairs before the army.

entries.zh: 時大將察罕圍壽春，七日始下，欲屠其城，南合曰：「不降者獨守將耳，其民何罪？」
entries.en: When the great general Chaghan besieged Shouchun and took it only after seven days, he wished to massacre the city. Nanhe said, "Only the commander refused to surrender—what crime have the people committed?"
entries.literal: At the time the great general Chaghan besieged Shouchun and took it only after seven days; he wished to slaughter the city. Nanhe said, "Only the defending commander refused to surrender—what crime have the people committed?"

entries.zh: 由是獲免。
entries.en: The people were thereby spared.
entries.literal: The city was thereby spared.

entries.zh: 初，世祖伐宋軍于汴，南合進曰：「李璮承國厚恩，坐制一方，然其人多詐，叛無日矣。」
entries.en: Earlier, when Kublai campaigned against Song at Bian, Nanhe said, "Li Tan has received great favor from the state and holds a region on his own, yet he is deeply deceitful—rebellion is only a matter of time."
entries.literal: Earlier, when Shizu campaigned against Song at Bian, Nanhe advanced and said, "Li Tan has received deep favor from the state and controls a region on his own, yet he is full of deceit—rebellion is only a matter of time."

entries.zh: 帝亦患之。
entries.en: The emperor was troubled too.
entries.literal: The emperor was troubled as well.

entries.zh: 中統元年，兩遷宣撫使。
entries.en: In the first year of Zhongtong he was twice promoted as pacification commissioner.
entries.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong he was twice transferred as pacification commissioner.

entries.zh: 明年，授中書右丞、中興等路行中書省事。
entries.en: The next year he was appointed right vice director of the Secretariat and put in charge of Secretariat affairs for Zhongxing and other circuits.
entries.literal: The next year he was appointed right vice director of the Secretariat and put in charge of Secretariat affairs for the Zhongxing circuit and other routes.

entries.zh: 三年，遷秦蜀五路四川行中書省事。
entries.en: In the third year he was transferred to oversee Secretariat affairs for the five Qin-Shu circuits of Sichuan.
entries.literal: In the third year he was transferred to oversee Secretariat affairs for the five Qin-Shu circuits of Sichuan.

entries.zh: 其年，李璮反益都，帝使諭南合曰：「卿言猶在耳，璮果反矣。
entries.en: That year Li Tan rebelled at Yidu; the emperor sent word to Nanhe, "Your warning is still in my ears—Tan has rebelled as you said.
entries.literal: That year Li Tan rebelled at Yidu; the emperor sent word to Nanhe, saying, "Your words are still in my ears—Tan has indeed rebelled.

entries.zh: 卿宜謹守西鄙。」
entries.en: Guard the western frontier carefully."
entries.literal: You should diligently guard the western frontier."

entries.zh: 對曰：「臣謹受詔，不敢以西鄙為陛下憂。」
entries.en: He replied, "I accept the edict and will not trouble Your Majesty over the western marches."
entries.literal: He replied, "Your subject respectfully accepts the edict and dares not trouble Your Majesty over the western marches."

entries.zh: 明年，授中書平章政事。
entries.en: The next year he was appointed grand councillor of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: The next year he was appointed grand councillor of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 四年，病卒。
entries.en: In the fourth year he died of illness.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he died of illness.

entries.zh: 封魏國公，諡宣昭。
entries.en: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Wei with the posthumous name Xuanzhao.
entries.literal: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Wei with the posthumous name Xuanzhao.

entries.zh: 子博溫察兒，知河中府。
entries.en: His son Bowencha'er served as prefect of Hezhong.
entries.literal: His son Bowencha'er served as prefect of Hezhong.

entries.zh: 定宗即位，平陽道斷事官斜徹橫恣不法，詔惟中宣慰，惟中按誅之。
entries.en: When Emperor Dingzong ascended, Cheqie, judicial officer of Pingyang Circuit, ruled lawlessly; Weizhong was sent to pacify the region and had him executed after investigation.
entries.literal: When Emperor Dingzong ascended, the judicial officer of Pingyang Circuit, Cheqie, was violent and lawless; Weizhong was ordered to pacify and comfort; he investigated and executed him.

entries.zh: 金亡，其將武仙潰於鄧州，餘黨散入太原、真定間，據大明川，用金開興年號，眾至數万，剽掠數千里，詔會諸道兵討之，不克。
entries.en: After Jin fell, the general Wu Xian was routed at Dengzhou; remnants scattered between Taiyuan and Zhending, seized Damingchuan, used the Jin Kaixing reign title, and numbered tens of thousands, plundering for thousands of li; troops from all circuits failed to suppress them.
entries.literal: When Jin perished, its general Wu Xian was routed at Dengzhou; the remnant band scattered between Taiyuan and Zhending, occupied Damingchuan, used Jin's Kaixing reign title, numbered tens of thousands, and plundered for several thousand li; an edict gathered troops from all circuits to attack them but could not overcome them.

entries.zh: 惟中仗節開諭，降其渠帥，餘黨悉平。
entries.en: Weizhong went with imperial authority to persuade them; their leaders surrendered and the remnant was fully pacified.
entries.literal: Weizhong, bearing his staff, opened persuasion; their chieftains surrendered and the remnant band was entirely pacified.

entries.zh: 憲宗即位，世祖以太弟鎮金蓮川，得開府，專封拜。
entries.en: When Emperor Xianzong ascended, Kublai as senior imperial brother garrisoned Jinlianchuan with authority to open his own office and make appointments independently.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xianzong ascended, Shizu as the senior imperial brother garrisoned Jinlianchuan, obtained the right to open a government office, and had exclusive authority to appoint and enfeoff.

entries.zh: 乃立河南道經略司於汴梁，奏惟中等為使，俾屯田唐、鄧、申、裕、嵩、汝、蔡、息、亳、潁諸州。
entries.en: He established the Henan Circuit Pacification Commission at Bianliang, appointed Weizhong commissioner, and ordered garrison farming in Tang, Deng, Shen, Yu, Song, Ru, Cai, Xi, Bo, and Ying.
entries.literal: Thereupon he established the Henan Circuit Pacification Commission at Bianliang, memorialized Weizhong and others as commissioners, and ordered garrison farming in the prefectures of Tang, Deng, Shen, Yu, Song, Ru, Cai, Xi, Bo, and Ying.

entries.zh: 初，滅金時，以監河橋萬戶劉福為河南道總管，福貪鄙殘酷，虐害遺民二十餘年。
entries.en: When Jin was destroyed, Liu Fu, overseer of the river bridge, was made commander of Henan Circuit; greedy and cruel, he abused the surviving people for more than twenty years.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Jin was destroyed, the ten-thousand-household chief Liu Fu, overseer of the river bridge, was made Henan Circuit commander; Fu was greedy, base, and cruel, abusing and harming the surviving people for more than twenty years.

entries.zh: 惟中至，召福聽約束，福稱疾不至，惟中設大梃於坐，復召之，使謂福曰：「汝不奉命，吾以軍法從事。」
entries.en: When Weizhong arrived he summoned Fu to receive orders; Fu claimed illness and refused to come; Weizhong placed a heavy staff beside his seat and sent word: "If you disobey, I will deal with you by military law."
entries.literal: When Weizhong arrived, he summoned Fu to hear his orders of restraint; Fu claimed illness and did not come; Weizhong set a great staff by his seat and summoned him again, sending word to Fu, "If you do not obey the command, I will deal with you by military law."

entries.zh: 福不得已，以數千人擁衛見惟中，惟中即握大梃擊僕之。
entries.en: Fu had no choice but to come with several thousand guards; Weizhong seized the staff and struck him down on the spot.
entries.literal: Fu had no choice; with several thousand men escorting him he came to see Weizhong; Weizhong immediately seized the great staff and struck him down.

entries.zh: 數日福死，河南大治。
entries.en: Fu died within days, and Henan was brought to order.
entries.literal: Within several days Fu died, and Henan was greatly well governed.

entries.zh: 遷陝右四川宣撫使。
entries.en: He was transferred to pacification commissioner of Shaanxi and Sichuan.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Pacification Commissioner of Shaanxi Right and Sichuan.

entries.zh: 時諸軍帥橫侈病民，郭千戶者尤甚，殺人之夫而奪其妻，惟中戮之以徇，關中肅然。
entries.en: Army commanders were oppressing the people; the thousand-household chief Guo was worst of all, killing a man and seizing his wife; Weizhong executed him as a warning, and the region was brought to order.
entries.literal: At the time the various army commanders were overbearing and extravagant, harming the people; the thousand-household chief Guo was especially so, killing a man and seizing his wife; Weizhong executed him as a warning, and Guanzhong was awed into order.

entries.zh: 語人曰：「吾非好殺，國家綱紀不立，致此輩賊害良民，無所控告，雖慾不去，可乎！」
entries.en: He said, "I do not love killing, but when discipline fails and such men prey on the innocent with no recourse, how can I leave them unpunished?"
entries.literal: He told others, "I am not fond of killing; the state's discipline is not established, causing men like these to harm good people with nowhere to appeal; though I wish not to remove them, can it be done!"

entries.zh: 歲己未，世祖總統東師，奏惟中為江淮京湖南北路宣撫使，俾建行台，以先啟行，宣布恩信，蒙古、漢軍諸帥並聽節制。
entries.en: In the jiwei year Kublai commanded the eastern army and appointed Weizhong pacification commissioner of the Jianghuai and Jinghu circuits, with authority to establish a traveling office, advance ahead to proclaim imperial grace, and command all Mongol and Han generals.
entries.literal: In the year jiwei Shizu commanded the eastern army; he memorialized Weizhong as Pacification Commissioner of the Jianghuai, Jinghu, and North and South circuits, ordered him to establish a traveling office, go ahead to open the campaign, proclaim grace and trust, and all Mongol and Han army commanders were to obey his control.

entries.zh: 師還，卒於蔡州，年五十五。
entries.en: When the army returned he died at Caizhou at the age of fifty-five.
entries.literal: When the army returned, he died at Caizhou, aged fifty-five.

entries.zh: 中統二年，追諡曰忠肅公。
entries.en: In the second year of Zhongtong he was posthumously honored as Duke Zhongsu.
entries.literal: In the second year of Zhongtong he was posthumously given the title Duke Zhongsu.

entries.zh: 耶律楚材子鑄附
entries.en: An appendix concerning Yelü Chucai's son Zhu.
entries.literal: Appendix on Yelü Chucai's son Zhu.

entries.zh: 辛巳，金懷州元帥王榮、潞州元帥裴守謙、澤州太守王珍皆以城降。
entries.en: On xinsi day the Jin commanders Wang Rong of Huaizhou, Pei Shouqian of Luzhou, and Wang Zhen, defender of Zezhou, all surrendered their cities.
entries.literal: On the day xinsi the Jin commanders Wang Rong of Huaizhou, Pei Shouqian of Luzhou, and Defender Wang Zhen of Zezhou all surrendered their cities.

entries.zh: 壬午，攻濟南水寨，破之。
entries.en: On renwu day he attacked the Jinan river stockade and captured it.
entries.literal: On the day renwu he attacked the Jinan river stockade and broke it.

entries.zh: 癸未，徇山西，遂克三關，不浹旬，定四十餘寨。
entries.en: On guiwei day he swept through Shanxi and took the Three Passes. In less than ten days he secured more than forty stockades.
entries.literal: On the day guiwei he swept Shanxi, then took the Three Passes; in less than ten days he settled more than forty stockades.

entries.zh: 兵至河衛，喜曰：「河衛者，夷門之限也。
entries.en: When his army reached Hewei he rejoiced and said, "Hewei is the gateway to Yimen.
entries.literal: When the army reached Hewei he rejoiced: "Hewei is the barrier of Yimen.

entries.zh: 河衛既破，則夷門不能守矣。」
entries.en: Once Hewei falls, Yimen cannot be held."
entries.literal: Once Hewei is broken, Yimen cannot be held."

entries.zh: 嚴實以兵來會，請自攻河衛，天倪曰：「合達、蒲瓦，亦勍敵也。」
entries.en: Yan Shi arrived with troops to join him and asked to take Hewei himself. Tianni said, "Hedda and Puwa are formidable enemies as well."
entries.literal: Yan Shi came with troops to join him and asked to attack Hewei himself; Tianni said: "Hedda and Puwa are also formidable foes."

entries.zh: 實曰：「易與耳，保為公破之。」
entries.en: Shi replied, "They will be easy. I guarantee I will break them for you."
entries.literal: Shi said: "They are easy opponents—I guarantee to break them for you."

entries.zh: 明日，實與蒲瓦兵遇於南門，合達兵自北奄至，實兵敗，竟為所執。
entries.en: The next day Shi met Puwa's troops at the south gate. Hedda's forces swept down from the north. Shi's army was defeated and he was captured.
entries.literal: The next day Shi met Puwa's troops at the south gate; Hedda's forces suddenly arrived from the north; Shi's army was defeated and he was finally captured.

entries.zh: 天倪曰：「合達以實歸汴，必以今夕。」
entries.en: Tianni said, "Hedda will escort Shi back to Bian. It must happen tonight."
entries.literal: Tianni said: "Hedda will take Shi back to Bian—it must be tonight."

entries.zh: 急命馮存、杜必貴率壯士一千三百，伏延津柳渡。
entries.en: He urgently ordered Feng Cun and Du Bigui to lead thirteen hundred picked warriors in ambush at Yanjin Willow Ford.
entries.literal: He urgently ordered Feng Cun and Du Bigui to lead thirteen hundred stalwart warriors to ambush at Yanjin Willow Ford.

entries.zh: 果夜縛實過延津，遇存等，與戰，敗之，實得脫歸，必貴戰死。
entries.en: That night the escort bound Shi and passed through Yanjin. They met Feng Cun's ambush, were defeated, and Shi escaped. Du Bigui died in the fighting.
entries.literal: Indeed at night they bound Shi and passed Yanjin; they met Cun and others, fought, were defeated, Shi escaped and returned, and Bigui died in battle.

entries.zh: 未幾，帝命天倪回軍真定。
entries.en: Soon afterward the emperor ordered Tianni to return his army to Zhending.
entries.literal: Before long the emperor ordered Tianni to return his army to Zhending.

entries.zh: 甲申夏，大名總管彭義斌以宋兵犯河朔，天倪逆戰於恩州，義斌敗，入保大名。
entries.en: In the summer of the jiashen year, Peng Yibin, prefect of Daming, invaded Heshuo with Song troops. Tianni met him at Enzhou, routed him, and drove him back into Daming.
entries.literal: In summer of the year jiashen, Daming prefect Peng Yibin with Song troops invaded Heshuo; Tianni met them at Enzhou; Yibin was defeated and withdrew into Daming.

entries.zh: 乙酉，師還，聞武仙之黨據西山腰水、鐵壁二寨以叛，天倪直搗其巢穴，盡掩殺之。
entries.en: On yiyou day the army returned. Learning that Wu Xian's followers had rebelled and seized Yaoshui and Tiebi stockades in the Western Hills, Tianni struck their strongholds directly and slaughtered them to the last man.
entries.literal: On the day yiyou the army returned; hearing that Wu Xian's partisans held Yaoshui and Tiebi stockades in the Western Hills in rebellion, Tianni struck straight at their nests and slaughtered them all.

entries.zh: 仙怒，謀作亂，乃設宴邀天倪。
entries.en: Wu Xian, enraged, plotted rebellion and invited Tianni to a banquet.
entries.literal: Xian in anger plotted rebellion and set a banquet to invite Tianni.

entries.zh: 有知其謀者，止天倪毋往，天倪不從，遂為仙所殺。
entries.en: Someone who knew the plot warned Tianni not to go. He refused to listen and was killed by Wu Xian.
entries.literal: Someone who knew the plot urged Tianni not to go; Tianni would not listen and was thereupon killed by Xian.

entries.zh: 張柔，字德剛，易州定興人，世力農。
entries.en: Zhang Rou, styled Degang, came from Dingxing in Yizhou. His family had farmed the land for generations.
entries.literal: Zhang Rou, style name Degang, was a native of Dingxing in Yizhou; his family for generations labored as farmers.

entries.zh: 柔少慷慨，尚氣節，善騎射，以豪俠稱。
entries.en: As a young man Rou was open-handed and chivalrous, prized loyalty and courage, skilled in horsemanship and archery, and famed as a gallant free spirit.
entries.literal: In his youth Rou was magnanimous, esteemed integrity and honor, excelled at mounted archery, and was known as a bold hero.

entries.zh: 金貞祐間，河北盜起，柔聚族黨保西山東流寨，選壯士，結隊伍以自衛，盜不敢犯。
entries.en: In the Jinyou reign of the Jin, brigands spread across Hebei. Rou rallied his kinsmen to defend Dongliu Stockade in the Western Hills, picked stalwart fighters, and organized armed bands for protection so that raiders dared not trouble them.
entries.literal: During the Jinyou era of Jin, bandits rose in Hebei. Rou gathered his clan to hold Dongliu Stockade in the Western Hills, selected strong men, formed companies for self-defense, and bandits did not dare molest them.

entries.zh: 郡人張信假柔聲勢，納流人女為妻，柔鞭信百而還其女。
entries.en: A local man named Zhang Xin traded on Rou's reputation to seize a refugee woman as his wife. Rou had Xin whipped a hundred times and sent the woman back.
entries.literal: A townsman Zhang Xin borrowed Rou's prestige, took a refugee woman as wife; Rou flogged Xin a hundred strokes and returned the woman.

entries.zh: 信憾之，謀結黨害柔。
entries.en: Xin nursed a grudge and schemed with allies to destroy Rou.
entries.literal: Xin bore resentment and plotted with a faction to harm Rou.

entries.zh: 未幾，信有罪當誅，柔救之得免，於是驍勇之士，多慕義從之。
entries.en: Soon afterward Xin was condemned to death for a crime, but Rou intervened and he was pardoned. From then on many bold fighters were drawn to his sense of justice and joined his cause.
entries.literal: Before long Xin committed a crime warranting execution; Rou saved him and he was spared, whereupon many fierce warriors admired his righteousness and followed him.

entries.zh: 中都經略使苗道潤承製授柔定興令，累遷清州防禦使。
entries.en: Miao Daorun, military commissioner of the Central Capital, appointed Rou magistrate of Dingxing by imperial order, and Rou rose through successive posts to Defender of Qingzhou.
entries.literal: The Central Capital military commissioner Miao Daorun by imperial commission appointed Rou magistrate of Dingxing; he was promoted repeatedly to Defender of Qingzhou.

entries.zh: 道潤表其才，加昭毅大將軍，遙領永定軍節度使，兼雄州管內觀察使，權元帥左都監，行元帥府事。
entries.en: Daorun recommended his abilities to the throne. Rou was promoted to Grand General of Manifest Valor, given the nominal post of Military Commissioner of the Yongding Army, made concurrent Commissioner of Observation for Xiongzhou, named acting Left Overseer of the Marshalate, and entrusted with the affairs of the marshal's headquarters.
entries.literal: Daorun memorialized his talent; he was made Grand General of Manifest Valor, remotely bore Military Commissioner of Yongding Army, concurrently Commissioner of Observation within Xiongzhou, Acting Left Overseer of the Marshalate, and administered the Marshal's headquarters.

entries.zh: 繼而道潤為其副賈瑀所殺，瑀遣使以好辭來告曰：「吾得除道潤者，以君不助兵故也。」
entries.en: Daorun was soon killed by his deputy Jia Yu, who sent an envoy with soothing words: "I was able to eliminate Daorun because you did not send troops to help him."
entries.literal: Thereafter Daorun was killed by his deputy Jia Yu; Yu sent an envoy with conciliatory words saying: "I was able to remove Daorun because you did not aid his troops."

entries.zh: 柔怒叱使者曰：「瑀殺吾所事，吾食瑀肉且未足快意，反以此言相戲耶！」
entries.en: Rou thundered at the envoy: "Yu murdered the lord I served. I would not be satisfied even if I devoured his flesh—and you dare mock me with words like these!"
entries.literal: Rou angrily rebuked the envoy: "Yu killed the man I served; I would not yet be satisfied even if I ate Yu's flesh, and yet you jest with such words!"

entries.zh: 遂移檄道潤部曲，會易州軍市川，誓眾為之復仇，眾皆感泣。
entries.en: He issued a call to arms to Daorun's troops, mustered them at Junshichuan in Yizhou, and led the host in swearing vengeance. The men wept as one.
entries.literal: He then issued a proclamation to Daorun's troops, assembled them at Junshichuan in Yizhou, and swore the host to avenge him; all were moved to tears.

entries.zh: 適道潤麾下何伯祥得道潤所佩金虎符以獻，因推柔行經略使事。
entries.en: At that moment He Boxiang, a commander under Daorun, presented the golden tiger tally that Daorun had carried, and the troops pressed Rou to assume the duties of military commissioner.
entries.literal: Just then He Boxiang of Daorun's command obtained and presented the golden tiger tally Daorun had worn, and on that basis they urged Rou to act as military commissioner.

entries.zh: 事聞，加驃騎將軍、中都留守，兼大興府尹、本路經略使，行元帥事。
entries.en: When word reached the court, he was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry, made Garrison Commander of the Central Capital and concurrently Prefect of Daxing and military commissioner of the circuit, and entrusted with marshal's authority.
entries.literal: When the matter was reported, he was made General of Agile Cavalry, Garrison Commander of the Central Capital, concurrently Prefect of Daxing and military commissioner of the circuit, and acted as marshal.

entries.zh: 十一月，詔統水軍四萬戶。
entries.en: In the eleventh month an edict gave him command of forty thousand naval households.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month an edict placed him in command of forty thousand naval households.

entries.zh: 宋荊湖制置李庭芝以金印牙符，授整漢軍都元帥、盧龍軍節度使，封燕郡王，為書，使永寧僧持送整所，期以間整。
entries.en: Song Commissioner Li Tingzhi sent a gold seal and tally making Zheng Han supreme commander and Lulong Military Commissioner, enfeoffing him Prince of Yan, with a letter carried by a Yongning monk to sow discord.
entries.literal: The Song Jing-Hu Commissioner Li Tingzhi, with a gold seal and tally, appointed Zheng supreme commander of the Han armies and Military Commissioner of Lulong, enfeoffed him as Prince of Yan, wrote a letter, and had a Yongning monk carry it to Zheng's camp, intending to sow discord.

entries.zh: 永寧令得之，驛以聞于朝，敕張易、姚樞雜問，適整至自軍，言宋怒臣畫策攻襄陽，故設此以殺臣，臣實不知。
entries.en: The Yongning magistrate seized it and reported by courier. Zhang Yi and Yao Shu were ordered to interrogate him. Zheng had just arrived from camp and said the Song, furious at his Xiangyang strategy, fabricated this to destroy him—he knew nothing of it.
entries.literal: The Yongning magistrate obtained it and reported by post to court; the Emperor ordered Zhang Yi and Yao Shu to question him jointly. Zheng had just come from the army and said Song was enraged that he had planned the Xiangyang attack and therefore set this trap to kill him—he truly knew nothing of it.

entries.zh: 詔令整復書謂：「整受命以來，惟知督厲戎兵，舉垂亡孤城耳。
entries.en: An edict had Zheng reply: 'Since I took command I have done nothing but drive the troops and press this dying lone fortress.
entries.literal: An edict ordered Zheng to reply in a letter: 'Since receiving my commission I have known only to urge and discipline the troops and raise this nearly fallen lone city.

entries.zh: 宋若果以生靈為念，當重遣信使，請命朝廷，顧為此小數，何益於事！」
entries.en: If Song truly cares for the people, let it send envoys to beg the court's mercy—what use are such petty stratagems!'
entries.literal: If Song truly cares for the people, it should send trusted envoys again to beg mercy of the court—what good are such petty tricks!'

entries.zh: 楊大淵文安附
entries.en: Yang Dayuan (with biography of Wen'an appended)
entries.literal: Yang Dayuan, with Wen'an appended

entries.zh: 高觿，字彥解，渤海人。
entries.en: Gao Xi, whose style name was Yanjie, was a native of Bohai.
entries.literal: Gao Xi, styled Yanjie, was a man of Bohai.

entries.zh: 世仕金，祖彝，徙居上黨。
entries.en: His family had served the Jin for generations. His grandfather Yi relocated to Shangdang.
entries.literal: His family served Jin for generations; his grandfather Yi moved to reside in Shangdang.

entries.zh: 父守忠，國初為千戶。
entries.en: His father Shouzhong was a chiliarch in the early years of the dynasty.
entries.literal: His father Shouzhong was a chiliarch at the beginning of the dynasty.

entries.zh: 太宗九年，從親王口溫不花攻黃州，歿於兵。
entries.en: In the ninth year of Taizong's reign he followed Prince Köten in the attack on Huangzhou and died in battle.
entries.literal: In the ninth year of Taizong he followed Prince Köten in attacking Huangzhou and died in battle.

entries.zh: 觿事世祖，備宿衛，頗見親幸。
entries.en: Xi served Kublai in the palace guard and enjoyed considerable favor.
entries.literal: Xi served the Founder, stood ready in the palace guard, and was rather favored.

entries.zh: 至元初，立燕王為皇太子，詔選才雋士充官屬，以觿掌藝文，兼領中醖、宮衛監門事，又監作皇太子宮，規制有法，帝嘉之，錫以金幣、厩馬，因賜名失剌。
entries.en: Early in the Zhiyuan era the Prince of Yan was made crown prince, and talented scholars were selected for his staff. Xi was put in charge of literary affairs, concurrently headed central brewing and palace gatekeeping, and supervised construction of the crown prince's palace with sound regulations. The emperor was pleased, granted him gold and currency and stable horses, and gave him the name Shila.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Zhiyuan the Prince of Yan was established as crown prince; an edict selected talented scholars to fill his staff; Xi was put in charge of literary arts, concurrently headed central brewing and palace gate guard affairs, and also supervised construction of the crown prince's palace with regulated standards; the emperor praised this and granted gold and currency and stable horses, thereby granting the name Shila.

entries.zh: 十八年，授中議大夫、工部侍郎，行同知王府都總管府事。
entries.en: In the eighteenth year he was appointed Grand Master of Correct Counsel and vice minister of Works, acting associate director of the crown prince's chief steward's office.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year he was appointed Grand Master of Correct Counsel and vice minister of Works, acting associate director of the crown prince's chief steward's office.

entries.zh: 十九年春，皇太子從帝北幸。
entries.en: In the spring of the nineteenth year the crown prince accompanied the emperor on the northern progress.
entries.literal: In spring of the nineteenth year the crown prince followed the emperor on the northern progress.

entries.zh: 時丞相阿合馬留守大都，專權貪恣，人厭苦之。
entries.en: Chief Councillor Ahmad remained at Daidu, monopolizing power in greed and arrogance until the people were weary of his rule.
entries.literal: At that time Chief Councillor Ahmad remained at Daidu, monopolizing power and greedy and unrestrained; people were weary and suffering under him.

entries.zh: 益都千戶王著與高和尚等，因構變謀殺之。
entries.en: Wang Zhu, a chiliarch of Yidu, joined Gaoshanghe and others in a plot to murder him.
entries.literal: Yidu chiliarch Wang Zhu and Gaoshanghe and others therefore plotted a disturbance to murder him.

entries.zh: 三月十七日，觿宿衛宮中，西蕃僧二人至中書省，言今夕皇太子與國師來建佛事。
entries.en: On the seventeenth day of the third month Xi was on guard in the palace when two Tibetan monks came to the Secretariat and said the crown prince and the imperial preceptor would come that evening to perform Buddhist rites.
entries.literal: On the seventeenth day of the third month Xi was on guard in the palace; two Western Tibetan monks came to the Secretariat saying that this evening the crown prince and the imperial preceptor would come to perform Buddhist rites.

entries.zh: 省中疑之，俾嘗出入東宮者雜識視之，觿等皆莫識也，乃作西蕃語詢二僧曰：「皇太子及國師今至何處？」
entries.en: The Secretariat was suspicious and had men who knew the Eastern Palace staff examine them. Xi and the others recognized none of them. Xi questioned the monks in Tibetan: "Where are the crown prince and the imperial preceptor now?"
entries.literal: Those in the Secretariat were suspicious and had those who had gone in and out of the Eastern Palace mixed among them to look; Xi and the others all failed to recognize them, and therefore spoke in Western Tibetan to question the two monks: "Where have the crown prince and imperial preceptor arrived now?"

entries.zh: 二僧失色。
entries.en: The two monks turned pale.
entries.literal: The two monks changed color.

entries.zh: 又以漢語詰之，倉皇莫能對，遂執二僧屬吏。
entries.en: He questioned them again in Chinese. Flustered, they could not answer, and the two monks were seized and handed over to the authorities.
entries.literal: He again questioned them in Chinese; flustered they could not answer, and the two monks were seized and handed to officials.

entries.zh: 訊之皆不伏，觿恐有變，乃與尚書忙兀兒、張九思集衛士及官兵，各執弓矢以備。
entries.en: Under interrogation they confessed nothing. Fearing a disturbance, Xi joined Ministers Mangwuer and Zhang Jiusi in gathering palace guards and government troops, all armed with bows and arrows.
entries.literal: Under interrogation none confessed; Xi feared a disturbance and therefore joined with Ministers Mangwuer and Zhang Jiusi to gather guards and government troops, each holding bow and arrows in readiness.

entries.zh: 頃之，樞密副使張易亦領兵駐宮外。
entries.en: Shortly afterward Privy Council vice director Zhang Yi also led troops and encamped outside the palace.
entries.literal: Shortly after, Privy Council Vice Director Zhang Yi also led troops stationed outside the palace.

entries.zh: 觿問：「果何為？」
entries.en: Xi asked, "What is really going on?"
entries.literal: Xi asked: "What is really happening?"

entries.zh: 易曰：「夜後當自見。」
entries.en: Yi said, "You will see for yourself after nightfall."
entries.literal: Yi said: "After nightfall you will see for yourself."

entries.zh: 觿固問，乃附耳語曰：「皇太子來誅阿合馬也。」
entries.en: When Xi pressed him, Yi whispered in his ear, "The crown prince has come to kill Ahmad."
entries.literal: Xi pressed the question; Yi then whispered in his ear: "The crown prince has come to execute Ahmad."

entries.zh: 夜二鼓，忽聞人馬聲，遙見燭籠儀仗，將至宮門，其一人前呼啟關，觿謂九思曰：「他時殿下還宮，必以完澤、賽羊二人先，請得見二人，然後啟關。」
entries.en: At the second watch he suddenly heard the sound of men and horses and saw candle lanterns and ceremonial escort approaching the palace gate. One man came forward calling for the gate to be opened. Xi told Jiusi, "When His Highness returns to the palace, Wanzhe and Saiyang always come first. Do not open the gate until you have seen them both."
entries.literal: At the second watch of night suddenly the sound of men and horses was heard; from afar candle lanterns and ceremonial escort were seen approaching the palace gate; one man came forward calling to open the gate; Xi said to Jiusi: "When His Highness returns to the palace, Wanzhe and Saiyang must always come first—please see the two men, then open the gate."

entries.zh: 觿呼二人不應，即語之曰：「皇太子平日未嘗行此門，今何來此也？」
entries.en: Xi called for the two men, but there was no answer. He called out, "His Highness never uses this gate on ordinary days. Why come here now?"
entries.literal: Xi called for the two men but there was no answer; he then said to them: "His Highness the crown prince on ordinary days has never used this gate—why come here now?"

entries.zh: 賊計窮，趨南門。
entries.en: Their stratagem exhausted, the rebels rushed for the south gate.
entries.literal: The rebels' stratagem exhausted, they rushed for the south gate.

entries.zh: 觿留張子政等守西門，亟走南門伺之。
entries.en: Xi left Zhang Zizheng and others to guard the west gate and ran to the south gate to watch.
entries.literal: Xi left Zhang Zizheng and others to guard the west gate and ran swiftly to the south gate to watch.

entries.zh: 但聞傳呼省官姓名，燭影下遙見阿合馬及左丞郝禎已被殺。
entries.en: He heard only the calling of Secretariat officials' names. In the candlelight he saw from afar that Ahmad and left vice councillor Hao Zhen had already been killed.
entries.literal: He only heard the calling out of Secretariat officials' names; in the candlelight from afar he saw Ahmad and Left Vice Councillor Hao Zhen already killed.

entries.zh: 觿乃與九思大呼曰：「此賊也！」
entries.en: Xi and Jiusi shouted together, "These are rebels!"
entries.literal: Xi then with Jiusi shouted loudly: "These are rebels!"

entries.zh: 叱衛士急捕之，高和尚等皆潰去，惟王著就擒。
entries.en: He ordered the guards to seize them at once. Gaoshanghe and the others scattered and fled; only Wang Zhu was captured.
entries.literal: He ordered the guards to seize them swiftly; Gaoshanghe and others all scattered and fled, only Wang Zhu was captured.

entries.zh: 黎明，中丞也先帖木兒與觿等馳驛往上都，以其事聞。
entries.en: At dawn censor-in-chief Yesentiemur rode with Xi and others by relay to Shangdu to report what had happened.
entries.literal: At dawn Censor-in-chief Yesentiemur with Xi and others galloped by relay to Shangdu to report the affair.

entries.zh: 帝以中外未安，當益嚴武備，遂勞使遣亟還。
entries.en: Because the realm was not yet settled within and without, the emperor said military readiness must be tightened further, comforted the envoys, and ordered them to return at once.
entries.literal: The emperor, because within and without were not yet settled, should further tighten military readiness, therefore comforted the envoys and ordered them to return swiftly.

entries.zh: 高和尚等尋皆伏誅。
entries.en: Gaoshanghe and the others were soon all executed.
entries.literal: Gaoshanghe and others soon all were executed after confession.

entries.zh: 二十二年，遷嘉議大夫，同知大都留守司事，兼少府監。
entries.en: In the twenty-second year he was transferred to Grand Master of Advising Counsel, associate director of the Daidu garrison office, and concurrent director of the imperial household works.
entries.literal: In the twenty-second year he was transferred to Grand Master of Advising Counsel, associate director of the Daidu garrison office, and concurrent director of the Imperial Household Works.

entries.zh: 久之，遷中奉大夫、河南等路宣慰使。
entries.en: After some time he was transferred to Grand Master of Correct Service and pacification commissioner of Henan and other circuits.
entries.literal: After a long time he was transferred to Grand Master of Correct Service and pacification commissioner of Henan and other circuits.

entries.zh: 卒，年五十三。
entries.en: He died at the age of fifty-three.
entries.literal: He died, age fifty-three.

entries.zh: 張九思，字子有，燕宛平人。
entries.en: Zhang Jiusi, whose style name was Ziyou, was a native of Wanping in the Yan region.
entries.literal: Zhang Jiusi, styled Ziyou, was a native of Wanping in Yan.

entries.zh: 父滋，薊州節度使。
entries.en: His father Zi was military governor of Jizhou.
entries.literal: His father Zi was military governor of Jizhou.

entries.zh: 至元二年，九思入備宿衛，裕皇居東宮，一見奇之，以父廕當補外，特留不遣。
entries.en: In the second year of the Zhiyuan era Jiusi entered the palace guard. Prince Yu, dwelling in the Eastern Palace, took an immediate liking to him. Though entitled by his father's privilege to an outside appointment, he was specially retained at court.
entries.literal: In the second year of Zhiyuan Jiusi entered to stand ready in the palace guard; Prince Yu dwelt in the Eastern Palace and at one sight found him remarkable; by his father's privilege he should have been assigned outside, but he was specially kept and not sent away.

entries.zh: 江南既平，宋庫藏金帛輸內府，而分授東宮者多，置都總管府以主之，九思以工部尚書兼府事。
entries.en: After Jiangnan was pacified, Song treasury gold and silks were delivered to the inner court, much of it allotted to the Eastern Palace. A chief steward's office was established to oversee these assets, and Jiusi served as minister of works with concurrent duties in that office.
entries.literal: Once Jiangnan was pacified, Song treasury gold and silks were delivered to the inner court, but much was allotted to the Eastern Palace; a chief steward's office was established to oversee it, and Jiusi as Minister of Works concurrently held office affairs.

entries.zh: 十九年春，世祖巡幸上都，皇太子從，丞相阿合馬留守。
entries.en: In the spring of the nineteenth year Kublai progressed to Shangdu with the crown prince, while Chief Councillor Ahmad remained at Daidu.
entries.literal: In spring of the nineteenth year the Founder made a progress to Shangdu, the crown prince followed, and Chief Councillor Ahmad remained on guard.

entries.zh: 妖僧高和尚、千戶王著等謀殺之，夜聚數百人為儀衛，稱太子，入健德門，直趨東宮，傳令啟關甚遽。
entries.en: The sorcerer-monk Gaoshanghe, chiliarch Wang Zhu, and others plotted his murder. By night they gathered several hundred men as a ceremonial guard, claimed to be the crown prince, entered Jiande Gate, and rushed straight to the Eastern Palace, urgently demanding that the gate be opened.
entries.literal: The sorcerer-monk Gaoshanghe, chiliarch Wang Zhu, and others plotted to murder him; by night they gathered several hundred men as ceremonial guard, called themselves the crown prince, entered Jiande Gate, went straight to the Eastern Palace, and transmitted orders to open the gate with great urgency.

entries.zh: 九思適直宿宮中，命主者不得擅啟關，語在《高觿傳》。
entries.en: Jiusi happened to be on overnight guard in the palace and ordered the gatekeepers not to open the gate without authorization. The full account appears in the biography of Gao Xi.
entries.literal: Jiusi happened to be on overnight guard in the palace and ordered the gatekeepers not to open the gate on their own authority—the account is in the biography of Gao Xi.

entries.zh: 賊知不可紿，循垣趨南門外，擊殺丞相阿合馬、左丞郝禎。
entries.en: Seeing they could not be deceived, the rebels followed the wall to the south gate, where they struck down Chief Councillor Ahmad and left vice councillor Hao Zhen.
entries.literal: The rebels knew they could not be deceived, followed the wall to rush outside the south gate, and struck and killed Chief Councillor Ahmad and Left Vice Councillor Hao Zhen.

entries.zh: 時變起倉卒，且昏夜，眾莫知所為，九思審其詐，叱宿衛士並力擊賊，盡獲之。
entries.en: The disturbance broke out in haste on a dark night, and no one knew what to do. Jiusi saw through the deception, ordered the overnight guards to strike the rebels together, and captured them all.
entries.literal: The disturbance arose in haste and it was also dark night; the crowd did not know what to do; Jiusi judged their deception and ordered the overnight guards to strike the rebels together with full force, capturing them all.

entries.zh: 賊之入也，矯太子命，徵兵樞密副使張易，易不加審，遽以兵與之。
entries.en: On entering, the rebels forged the crown prince's order to summon troops from privy council vice director Zhang Yi. Yi did not investigate and hastily gave them troops.
entries.literal: When the rebels entered they forged the crown prince's order to summon troops from Privy Council Vice Director Zhang Yi; Yi did not examine it and hastily gave them troops.

entries.zh: 易既坐誅，而刑官复論以知情，將傳首四方。
entries.en: Yi was already executed, but the judicial officers argued that he had known of the plot and proposed sending his head to the four quarters as a warning.
entries.literal: Yi was already condemned and executed, but the judicial officers again argued he had known and planned to transmit his head to the four quarters.

entries.zh: 九思啟太子曰：「張易應變不審，而授賊以兵，死復何辭！
entries.en: Jiusi reported to the crown prince, "Zhang Yi failed to judge the emergency and gave the rebels troops. Death is his only answer for that.
entries.literal: Jiusi reported to the crown prince: "Zhang Yi did not examine the sudden change and gave the rebels troops—death leaves him nothing to say!

entries.zh: 若坐以與謀，則過矣，請免傳首。」
entries.en: But to convict him of joining the plot would be excessive. I beg that his head not be sent about the realm."
entries.literal: If he is convicted of joining the plot, that is excessive—I beg to exempt transmitting his head."

entries.zh: 皇太子言於帝，遂從之。
entries.en: The crown prince spoke to the emperor, and the request was granted.
entries.literal: The crown prince spoke to the emperor and it was followed.

entries.zh: 九思討賊時，右衛指揮使顏進在行，中流矢卒，怨家誣為賊黨，將籍其孥，九思力辯之，得不坐。
entries.en: During the suppression Right Guard commander Yan Jin was on the expedition, was struck by an arrow, and died. An enemy slandered him as a rebel accomplice and sought to punish his household. Jiusi argued forcefully on his behalf and the family was spared.
entries.literal: When Jiusi suppressed the rebels, Right Guard Commander Yan Jin was on the expedition, was struck by an arrow and died; an enemy slandered him as a rebel accomplice and planned to register his household for punishment; Jiusi argued forcefully and he was not convicted.

entries.zh: 賀仁傑
entries.en: He Renjie
entries.literal: He Renjie

entries.zh: 書上，朝廷不強致，帝聞之，亦曰：「古有所謂不召之臣，其斯人之徒歟！」
entries.en: When the letter was submitted, the court did not press him further. When the Emperor heard of it, he said, "Of old there were the so-called ministers who would not come when summoned—is this such a man?"
entries.literal: When the letter was submitted, the court did not press him; when the Emperor heard of it, he also said: "Of old there were the so-called ministers who would not come when summoned—is this the sort of man?"

entries.zh: 三十年夏四月十有六日卒，年四十五。
entries.en: On the sixteenth day of the fourth month in the thirtieth year of Zhiyuan (1293) he died, aged forty-five.
entries.literal: On the sixteenth day of the fourth month of summer in the thirtieth year he died, aged forty-five.

entries.zh: 無子，聞者嗟悼。
entries.en: He left no son; all who heard the news sighed in grief.
entries.literal: He had no son; those who heard of it sighed and mourned.

entries.zh: 延祐中，贈翰林學士、資善大夫、上護軍，追封容城郡公，諡文靖。
entries.en: During the Yanyou era he was posthumously appointed Hanlin Academician, Grand Master for Fostering Goodness, and Commander of the Upper Army, enfeoffed as Duke of Rongcheng Commandery, and given the posthumous title Wenjing.
entries.literal: During the Yanyou era he was posthumously made Hanlin Academician, Grand Master for Fostering Goodness, and Commander of the Upper Army, with enfeoffment as Duke of Rongcheng Commandery and the posthumous title Wenjing.

entries.zh: 歐陽玄嘗贊因畫像曰：「微點之狂，而有沂上風雩之樂；
entries.en: Ouyang Xuan once wrote in praise of Liu Yin's portrait: "With Dian's unrestrained spirit, yet with the joy of bathing at the Yi in the wind and rain;
entries.literal: Ouyang Xuan once praised Yin's portrait, saying: "With Dian's wildness, yet with the joy of bathing at the Yi above the wind;

entries.zh: 資由之勇，而無北鄙鼓瑟之聲。
entries.en: the courage of Zilu, yet without the sound of drumming at the northern frontier.
entries.literal: the courage of Zilu, yet without the sound of drumming at the northern frontier.

entries.zh: 於裕皇之仁，而見不可留之四皓；
entries.en: In the Heir Apparent's benevolence one sees the Four Hoary Heads who could not be kept;
entries.literal: In the benevolence of the Heir Apparent one sees the Four Hoary Heads who could not be detained;

entries.zh: 以世祖之略，而遇不能致之兩生。
entries.en: under the strategic grasp of Emperor Shizu one meets the two scholars who could not be summoned.
entries.literal: under the strategic grasp of Shizu one encounters the two scholars who could not be brought forth.

entries.zh: 烏乎！
entries.en: Alas!
entries.literal: Alas!

entries.zh: 麒麟鳳凰，固宇內之不常有也，然而一鳴而《六典》作，一出而《春秋》成。
entries.en: The qilin and phoenix are indeed rare under Heaven, yet with one cry the Six Canons were composed, with one emergence the Spring and Autumn was completed.
entries.literal: The qilin and phoenix are indeed not common within the four seas, yet with one cry the Six Canons were made, with one emergence the Spring and Autumn was completed.

entries.zh: 則其志不欲遺世而獨往也明矣，亦將從周公、孔子之後，為往聖繼絕學，為來世開太平者邪！」
entries.en: His will not to abandon the world and walk alone is clear enough; he was surely meant to follow the Duke of Zhou and Confucius, continuing the severed learning of past sages and opening an age of great peace for generations to come!"
entries.literal: Then his will not to leave the world and go alone is clear; he will also follow after the Duke of Zhou and Confucius, continuing the severed learning of past sages and opening great peace for generations to come!"

entries.zh: 論者以為知言。
entries.en: Critics regarded this as words of genuine insight.
entries.literal: Critics considered this discerning speech.

entries.zh: 英宗即位，超遷翰林學士，進階太中大夫。
entries.en: When Emperor Yingzong took the throne, Wu Cheng was exceptionally promoted to Hanlin Academician and advanced to the rank of Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yingzong took the throne, Cheng was exceptionally promoted to Hanlin Academician and advanced to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

entries.zh: 先是，有旨集善書者，粉黃金為泥，寫浮屠藏經。
entries.en: Earlier an edict had ordered skilled calligraphers gathered to grind gold into paste and copy the Buddhist canon.
entries.literal: Earlier, an edict had ordered gathering men skilled in calligraphy to grind gold into paste and copy the Buddhist canon.

entries.zh: 帝在上都，使左丞速速，詔澄為序，澄曰：「主上寫經，為民祈福，甚盛舉也。
entries.en: The Emperor was at Shangdu and sent Left Assistant Minister Susu to order Wu Cheng to write the preface. Cheng said, "When the sovereign copies sutras to pray for the people's blessings, it is a most splendid undertaking.
entries.literal: The Emperor was at Shangdu; he sent Left Assistant Minister Susu to order Cheng to write the preface. Cheng said: "When the sovereign copies sutras to pray for the people's blessings, it is a most splendid undertaking.

entries.zh: 若用以追薦，臣所未知。
entries.en: If it is meant for posthumous intercession, I do not yet understand it.
entries.literal: If it is to be used for posthumous intercession, your servant does not yet understand it.

entries.zh: 蓋福田利益，雖人所樂聞，而輪回之事，彼習其學者，猶或不言。
entries.en: Though the blessings of the field of merit are what everyone delights to hear, even those who study transmigration sometimes decline to speak of it.
entries.literal: For though the blessings of the field of merit are what all men delight to hear, as to the matter of transmigration, even those who study that learning sometimes decline to speak of it.

entries.zh: 不過謂為善之人，死則上通高明，其極品則與日月齊光；
entries.en: They merely say that the good, when they die, ascend to what is lofty and bright, and at the highest rank shine together with sun and moon;
entries.literal: They merely say that good men, when they die, ascend to what is lofty and bright, and at the highest rank shine together with sun and moon;

entries.zh: 為惡之人，死則下淪污穢，其極下則與沙蟲同類。
entries.en: while the wicked, when they die, sink into filth and defilement, and at the lowest rank are classed with sand worms.
entries.literal: evil men, when they die, sink down into filth and defilement, and at the lowest rank are of the same kind as sand worms.

entries.zh: 其徒遂為薦拔之說，以惑世人。
entries.en: Their followers then devised doctrines of intercession and deliverance to delude the people.
entries.literal: Their followers thereupon devised doctrines of intercession and deliverance to delude the people of the age.

entries.zh: 今列聖之神，上同日月，何庸薦拔！
entries.en: Now the spirits of the successive sage emperors are above, equal with sun and moon—what need is there for intercession!
entries.literal: Now the spirits of the successive sages are above, equal with sun and moon—what need is there for intercession!

entries.zh: 且國初以來，凡寫經追薦，不知幾舉。
entries.en: Moreover, since the founding of the dynasty, sutra-copying for posthumous intercession has been attempted beyond counting.
entries.literal: Moreover, since the founding of the dynasty, copyings of sutras for posthumous intercession have been attempted beyond counting.

entries.zh: 若未效，是無佛法矣；
entries.en: If they have had no effect, then Buddhism is false;
entries.literal: If they have had no effect, then there is no Buddhist dharma;

entries.zh: 若已效，是誣其祖矣。
entries.en: if they have had effect, then one has slandered one's ancestors.
entries.literal: if they have had effect, then one has slandered one's ancestors.

entries.zh: 撰為文辭，不可以示後世，請俟駕還奏之。」
entries.en: To compose this as a literary text and display it to later ages is impossible; I beg to memorialize it only after the imperial procession returns."
entries.literal: To compose this as literary text cannot be shown to later ages; I request to wait until the imperial procession returns to memorialize it."

entries.zh: 會帝崩而止。
entries.en: But the Emperor died and the matter ceased.
entries.literal: It happened that the Emperor died and the matter ceased.

entries.zh: 泰定元年，初開經筵，首命澄與平章政事張珪、國子祭酒鄧文原為講官。
entries.en: In the first year of Taiding (1324), when the Classics Lecture was first established, Wu Cheng was among the first appointed, together with Grand Councillor Zhang Gui and Director of Education Deng Wenyuan, to serve as lecturers.
entries.literal: In the first year of Taiding, when the Classics Lecture was first opened, Cheng was first ordered, together with Grand Councillor Zhang Gui and Director of Education Deng Wenyuan, to serve as lecturers.

entries.zh: 在至治末，詔作太廟，議者習見同堂異室之制，乃作十三室。
