entries.en: Late in the Zhizhi era an edict ordered construction of the Imperial Ancestral Temple. The officials, accustomed to the system of a shared hall with separate chambers, therefore built thirteen chambers.
entries.literal: Late in the Zhizhi era an edict ordered construction of the Imperial Ancestral Temple; the discussants, accustomed to the system of shared hall with separate chambers, therefore built thirteen chambers.

entries.zh: 未及遷奉，而國有大故，有司疑於昭穆之次，命集議之。
entries.en: Before the spirit tablets could be moved and installed, the state suffered a great calamity. The relevant office was uncertain about the order of zhao and mu shrines and ordered a collective deliberation.
entries.literal: Before the tablets could be moved and installed, the state suffered a great misfortune; the relevant office was uncertain about the order of zhao and mu and ordered a collective deliberation.

entries.zh: 澄議曰：「世祖混一天下，悉考古制而行之。
entries.en: Wu Cheng submitted his opinion, saying, "Emperor Shizu unified the realm under Heaven and broadly investigated ancient institutions in implementing them.
entries.literal: Cheng deliberated, saying: "Shizu unified the realm under Heaven and broadly investigated ancient institutions in carrying them out.

entries.zh: 古者天子七廟，廟各為宮，太祖居中，左三廟為昭，右三廟為穆，昭穆神主，各以次遞遷，其廟之宮，頗如今之中書六部。
entries.en: In antiquity the Son of Heaven maintained seven ancestral temples, each temple its own palace, with the Founding Ancestor in the center, three zhao temples on the left and three mu temples on the right. The spirit tablets of zhao and mu were moved in turn according to rank, and the temple palaces were rather like today's Six Departments of the Central Secretariat.
entries.literal: In antiquity the Son of Heaven had seven temples; each temple was a separate palace, the Founding Ancestor in the center, the three temples on the left being zhao, the three on the right mu; the spirit tablets of zhao and mu each moved in turn according to rank, and the palaces of the temples were rather like today's Six Departments of the Central Secretariat.

entries.zh: 夫省部之設，亦仿金、宋，豈以宗廟敘次而不考古乎！」
entries.en: The establishment of ministries and departments likewise follows Jin and Song models—how could one, merely because of ancestral temple ordering, fail to investigate antiquity!"
entries.literal: The establishment of ministries and departments also imitates Jin and Song—how could one, because of the ordering of the ancestral temple, fail to investigate antiquity!"

entries.zh: 有司急於行事，竟如舊次云。
entries.en: The relevant office, eager to proceed, in the end followed the old arrangement.
entries.literal: The relevant office, eager to act, in the end followed the old order.

entries.zh: 時澄已有去志，會修《英宗實錄》，命總其事。
entries.en: By then Wu Cheng already intended to resign. It happened that the Veritable Records of Emperor Yingzong were being compiled, and he was ordered to oversee the project.
entries.literal: At that time Cheng already had the will to leave; it happened that the Veritable Records of Emperor Yingzong were being compiled, and he was ordered to oversee the matter.

entries.zh: 居數月，《實錄》成，未上，即移疾不出。
entries.en: After several months the Veritable Records were completed. Before they could be submitted he pleaded illness and stopped coming to court.
entries.literal: After several months the Veritable Records were completed; before they were submitted he pleaded illness and did not come forth.

entries.zh: 中書左丞許師敬奉旨賜宴國史院，仍致朝廷勉留之意，宴罷，即出城登舟去。
entries.en: Left Assistant Minister of the Secretariat Xu Shijing, by imperial order, gave a banquet at the National History Academy and conveyed the court's wish that he remain. When the banquet ended, he left the city at once and boarded a boat to depart.
entries.literal: Left Assistant Minister of the Secretariat Xu Shijing, by imperial order, gave a banquet at the National History Academy and also conveyed the court's wish that he stay; when the banquet ended, he at once left the city and boarded a boat to depart.

entries.zh: 中書聞之，遣官驛追，不及而還，言於帝曰：「吳澄，國之名儒，朝之舊德，今請老而歸，不忍重勞之，宜有所褒異。」
entries.en: The Secretariat heard of this and sent an official by relay post to pursue him, but could not overtake him. The official returned and said to the Emperor, "Wu Cheng is a famous Confucian of the realm and an old worthy of the court. Now he asks to retire—I cannot bear to burden him further, and he should receive some special honor."
entries.literal: The Secretariat heard of it and sent an official by relay post to pursue him, but could not overtake him and returned, saying to the Emperor: "Wu Cheng is a famous Confucian of the state and an old worthy of the court; now he asks to retire and return home—I cannot bear to burden him further and he should receive some special honor."

entries.zh: 詔加資善大夫，仍以金織文綺二及鈔五千貫賜之。
entries.en: An edict promoted him to Grand Master for Fostering Goodness and bestowed two bolts of gold-woven patterned silk and five thousand strings of paper money.
entries.literal: An edict added the title Grand Master for Fostering Goodness and still bestowed two bolts of gold-woven patterned silk and five thousand strings of paper money.

entries.zh: 因自幼讀書，接聞大人君子之餘論，雖他無所得，至如君臣之義，自謂見之甚明。
entries.en: From childhood I have studied and absorbed whatever I could of the teachings left by great men and gentlemen. I may have gained little else, but regarding the duties of ruler and subject I believe my understanding is quite clear.
entries.literal: From childhood I have read books and received the remaining teachings of great men and gentlemen; though in other matters I have gained nothing, as to the meaning of ruler and subject I consider that I see it very clearly.

entries.zh: 如以日用近事言之，凡吾人之所以得安居而暇食，以遂其生聚之樂者，是誰之力與？
entries.en: To put it in terms of everyday life: by whose power is it that we can live in peace, eat at leisure, and enjoy the happiness of family and community?
entries.literal: If one speaks in terms of daily, near-at-hand affairs, by whose power is it that we are able to dwell in peace and eat at leisure and thereby enjoy the pleasures of family and community?

entries.zh: 皆君上之賜也。
entries.en: It is entirely the gift of our sovereign above.
entries.literal: All is the gift of our sovereign above.

entries.zh: 是以凡我有生之民，或給力役，或出知能，亦必各有以自效焉。
entries.en: Therefore every person alive must, whether by labor or by knowledge and ability, find some way to repay that obligation.
entries.literal: Therefore every living person under Heaven, whether supplying labor or offering knowledge and ability, must likewise have some way to repay the obligation.

entries.zh: 此理勢之必然，亙萬古而不可易，而莊周氏所謂無所逃於天地之間者也。
entries.en: This is a necessity of principle and circumstance, unchanging through all ages—what Zhuangzi meant when he said there is no escaping it between Heaven and Earth.
entries.literal: This is a necessity of principle and circumstance, unchanging through ten thousand ages, and is what Zhuang Zhou called having nowhere to escape between Heaven and Earth.

entries.zh: 因生四十三年，未嘗效尺寸之力，以報國家養育生成之德，而恩命連至，因尚敢偃蹇不出，貪高尚之名以自媚，以負我國家知遇之恩，而得罪於聖門中庸之教也哉！
entries.en: I have lived forty-three years without rendering even the smallest service to repay the state's grace in nourishing and sustaining my life. Yet favor after favor has arrived, and I still dare hold back and refuse to serve, cherishing a reputation for lofty withdrawal to flatter myself—thus failing the state's kindness and offending against the doctrine of the Mean taught by the sages!
entries.literal: I have lived forty-three years and never once rendered even the smallest service to repay the state's grace in nourishing and sustaining me; yet favor after favor has arrived, and I still dare to hold back and not come forth, cherishing a reputation for lofty withdrawal to flatter myself, thus failing the state's knowledge and favor and offending against the Mean taught by the sage school!

entries.zh: 且因之立心，自幼及長，未嘗一日敢為崖岸卓絕、甚高難繼之行，平昔交友，苟有一日之雅者，皆知因之此心也。
entries.en: Moreover, the mind I have held from childhood to maturity has never for a single day pursued precipitous, peerless conduct that is lofty and hard to emulate. Friends of even one day's standing all know this about me.
entries.literal: Moreover, the mind I have set from childhood to maturity has never for a single day dared to pursue precipitous, peerless conduct, lofty and hard to follow; friends of even one day's acquaintance all know this mind of mine.

entries.zh: 但或者得之傳聞，不求其實，止於縱蹟之近似者觀之，是以有高人隱士之目，惟閣下亦知因之未嘗以此自居也。
entries.en: But some people, hearing only rumors and not seeking the truth, judge me by outward traces that merely resemble withdrawal, and therefore call me a lofty recluse—though Your Excellency knows I have never regarded myself as one.
entries.literal: But some, hearing it only by rumor and not seeking the fact, stop at observing traces that merely resemble it, and therefore give me the label of lofty recluse; yet Your Excellency also knows that I have never taken myself for such.

entries.zh: 向者先儲皇以贊善之命來召，即與使者俱行，再奉旨令教學，亦即時應命。
entries.en: When the late Heir Apparent summoned me as Assistant, I set out at once with the envoy. When I received a second decree to teach, I responded immediately as well.
entries.literal: Formerly, when the late Heir Apparent summoned me with the appointment as Assistant, I set out at once with the envoy; when I again received the decree to teach, I likewise responded immediately.

entries.zh: 後以老母中風，請還家省視，不幸彌留，竟遭憂制，遂不復出，初豈有意於不仕邪？
entries.en: Later, when my aged mother suffered a stroke, I asked to return home to care for her. Unfortunately her illness lingered, and in the end she died; I entered mourning and did not come forth again. Was that truly an intention never to serve?
entries.literal: Later, because my aged mother suffered a stroke, I asked to return home to visit her; unfortunately her illness lingered, and in the end I encountered mourning and did not come forth again—was this truly an intention not to serve?

entries.zh: 今聖天子選用賢良，一新時政，雖前日隱晦之人，亦將出而仕矣，況因平昔非隱晦者邪！
entries.en: Now the sage Son of Heaven is selecting worthy men and renewing the policies of the age. Even those who were formerly obscure will come forth to serve—how much more should one who was never obscure!
entries.literal: Now the sage Son of Heaven is selecting the worthy and good and renewing the policies of the age; even those who were formerly obscure will come forth to serve—how much more one who was never obscure!

entries.zh: 況加以不次之寵，處之以優崇之地邪！
entries.en: And how much more when unmerited favor is heaped upon one and one is placed in an honored and exalted post!
entries.literal: How much more when unmerited favor is added and one is placed in an honored and exalted position!

entries.zh: 是以形留意往，命與心違，病臥空齋，惶恐待罪。
entries.en: Therefore my body and my intent pull in opposite directions; imperial command and my heart are at odds. I lie ill in an empty study, fearful and awaiting judgment.
entries.literal: Therefore body and intent go in opposite directions; command and mind are at odds; I lie ill in an empty study, fearful and awaiting judgment.

entries.zh: 不忽木以因學行薦於朝，至元十九年，有詔徵因，擢承德郎、右贊善大夫。
entries.en: Buqa recommended Liu Yin to the court for his scholarship and character. In the nineteenth year of the Zhiyuan era (1282), an imperial edict summoned him, and he was appointed Gentleman for Supporting Virtue and Right Assistant to the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: Buqa recommended Yin to the court for his learning and conduct; in the nineteenth year of Zhiyuan an edict summoned Yin, and he was promoted to Gentleman for Supporting Virtue and Right Assistant to the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 初，裕皇建學宮中，命贊善王恂教近侍子弟，恂卒，乃命因繼之。
entries.en: Earlier the Heir Apparent had established a school within the palace and appointed Wang Xun, Assistant to the Heir Apparent, to instruct the young attendants. When Wang Xun died, Liu Yin was ordered to take his place.
entries.literal: Earlier, the Heir Apparent had built a school within the palace and ordered the Assistant Wang Xun to teach the young attendants; when Xun died, Yin was ordered to succeed him.

entries.zh: 未幾，以母疾辭歸。
entries.en: Before long he resigned and returned home because his mother had fallen ill.
entries.literal: Before long, he resigned and returned home because of his mother's illness.

entries.zh: 明年，丁內艱。
entries.en: The following year he entered mourning for his mother.
entries.literal: The next year he entered mourning for his mother.

entries.zh: 二十八年，詔復遣使者，以集賢學士、嘉議大夫徵因，以疾固辭，且上書宰相曰：
entries.en: In the twenty-eighth year of Zhiyuan (1291), another edict sent envoys to summon him as Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies with the rank of Grand Master for Discussion of Governance. He firmly declined on account of illness and also submitted a letter to the chief minister, which read:
entries.literal: In the twenty-eighth year an edict again sent envoys to summon Yin as Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies and Grand Master for Discussion of Governance; he firmly declined on grounds of illness and moreover submitted a letter to the chief minister, saying:

entries.zh: 吳澄，字幼清，撫州崇仁人。
entries.en: Wu Cheng, whose courtesy name was Youqing, came from Chongren in Fuzhou.
entries.literal: Wu Cheng, courtesy name Youqing, was a man of Chongren in Fuzhou.

entries.zh: 高祖曄，初居咸口裡，當華蓋、臨川二山間，望氣者徐覺言其地當出異人。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Ye first settled at Xiankou Village, between Mount Huagai and Mount Linchuan. A geomancer named Xu Jue said the place would produce an extraordinary man.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Ye first dwelt at Xiankou Village, between Mount Huagai and Mount Linchuan; a geomancer, Xu Jue, said the place would produce an extraordinary man.

entries.zh: 澄生前一夕，鄉父老見異氣降其家，鄰媼复夢有物蜿蜓降其舍旁池中，旦以告於人，而澄生。
entries.en: On the night before Wu Cheng was born, village elders saw an unusual vapor descend upon his house. A neighboring old woman dreamed that something coiled descended into the pool beside their dwelling; at dawn she told others, and Cheng was born.
entries.literal: On the night before Cheng was born, village elders saw an unusual vapor descend upon his house; a neighboring old woman also dreamed that something coiled descended into the pool beside their dwelling; at dawn she told people, and Cheng was born.

entries.zh: 三歲，穎悟日發，教之古詩，隨口成誦。
entries.en: At three his keen intelligence unfolded day by day. When taught ancient poetry he could recite it at once.
entries.literal: At three his keen intelligence daily unfolded; when taught ancient poetry he could recite it at once.

entries.zh: 五歲，日受千餘言，夜讀書至旦，母憂其過勤，節膏火，不多與，澄候母寢，燃火復誦習。
entries.en: At five he memorized more than a thousand words a day and read until dawn. His mother, fearing he studied too hard, rationed lamp oil and gave him little; Cheng waited until she slept, then lit a lamp and went on reading.
entries.literal: At five he received more than a thousand words each day and read books until dawn; his mother worried he studied too hard, limited lamp oil, and did not give him much; Cheng waited until his mother slept, lit a fire, and resumed recitation.

entries.zh: 九歲，從群子弟試鄉校，每中前列。
entries.en: At nine he joined the village youths in examinations at the local school and always ranked at the top.
entries.literal: At nine he joined the village youths in testing at the local school and always placed at the head of the list.

entries.zh: 既長，於《經》、《傳》皆習通之，知用力聖賢之學，嘗舉進士不中。
entries.en: As he grew older he mastered the Classics and their commentaries and devoted himself to the learning of sages and worthies. He once took the jinshi examination but did not pass.
entries.literal: When grown, he thoroughly mastered the Classics and their commentaries, knew how to apply effort to the learning of sages and worthies, and once took the jinshi examination without success.

entries.zh: 至元十三年，民初附，盜賊所在蜂起，樂安鄭松，招澄居布水穀，乃著《孝經章句》，校定《易》、《書》、《詩》、《春秋》 、《儀禮》及大、小《戴記》。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year of Zhiyuan (1276), when the people had just submitted to Yuan rule, bandits swarmed everywhere. Zheng Song of Le'an invited Cheng to live at Bushui Valley, where he wrote Explications of the Filial Classic and collated the Changes, Documents, Odes, Spring and Autumn, Rites, and the Record of Rites of the Elder and Younger Dai.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhiyuan, when the people had just submitted, bandits rose everywhere like bees; Zheng Song of Le'an invited Cheng to dwell at Bushui Valley, and there he composed Explications of the Filial Classic, collated the Changes, Documents, Odes, Spring and Autumn, Rites, and the Record of Rites of the Elder and Younger Dai.

entries.zh: 侍御史程鉅夫，奉詔求賢江南，起澄至京師。
entries.en: Supervising Censor Cheng Jufu, bearing an edict to seek worthy men south of the Yangtze, summoned Wu Cheng to the capital.
entries.literal: Supervising Censor Cheng Jufu, bearing an edict to seek the worthy south of the Yangtze, summoned Cheng to the capital.

entries.zh: 未幾，以母老辭歸。
entries.en: Before long he resigned and returned home because his mother was elderly.
entries.literal: Before long he resigned and returned home because his mother was aged.

entries.zh: 鉅夫請置澄所著書於國子監，以資學者，朝廷命有司即其家錄上。
entries.en: Cheng Jufu asked that Wu Cheng's writings be placed in the Directorate of Education for the use of scholars. The court ordered the relevant office to copy them from his home and present them.
entries.literal: Jufu requested that Cheng's writings be placed in the Directorate of Education to aid scholars; the court ordered the relevant office to copy them from his home and present them.

entries.zh: 元貞初，遊龍興，按察司經歷郝文迎至郡學，日聽講論，錄其問答，凡數千言。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Yuanzhen era he traveled to Longxing. Surveillance Commissioner Hao Wen welcomed him to the prefectural school, where each day he heard his lectures and recorded his questions and answers—several thousand words in all.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yuanzhen he traveled to Longxing; Surveillance Commissioner Hao Wen welcomed him to the prefectural school, where daily he heard his lectures and recorded his questions and answers, altogether several thousand words.

entries.zh: 行省掾元明善以文學自負，嘗問澄《易》、《詩》、《書》、《春秋》奧義，歎曰：「與吳先生言，如探淵海。」
entries.en: Branch Secretariat Attendant Yuan Mingshan, proud of his literary accomplishments, once questioned Wu Cheng on the profound meaning of the Changes, Odes, Documents, and Spring and Autumn, and sighed, "Talking with Master Wu is like probing a deep sea."
entries.literal: Branch Secretariat Attendant Yuan Mingshan, proud of his literary learning, once questioned Cheng on the profound meaning of the Changes, Odes, Documents, and Spring and Autumn, and sighed: "Speaking with Master Wu is like probing a deep sea."

entries.zh: 遂執子弟禮終其身。
entries.en: He thereafter treated Wu Cheng with the rites due a master for the rest of his life.
entries.literal: He therefore performed the rites of a disciple toward him for the rest of his life.

entries.zh: 左丞董士選延之於家，親執饋食，曰：「吳先生，天下士也。」
entries.en: Left Assistant Minister Dong Shixuan invited him to his home and personally served him food, saying, "Master Wu is a scholar of the realm."
entries.literal: Left Assistant Minister Dong Shixuan invited him to his home and personally served him food, saying: "Master Wu is a scholar of the realm."

entries.zh: 既入朝，薦澄有道，擢應奉翰林文字。
entries.en: After entering court he recommended Wu Cheng as a man of the Way and had him appointed Hanlin Drafting Attendant for Imperial Orders.
entries.literal: After entering court he recommended Cheng as a man of the Way and promoted him to Hanlin Drafting Attendant for Imperial Orders.

entries.zh: 有司敦勸，久之乃至，而代者已至官，澄即日南歸。
entries.en: The relevant office urged him repeatedly. Only after a long delay did he come, but his replacement had already taken up the post, and Cheng returned south the same day.
entries.literal: The relevant office urged him repeatedly; only after a long time did he come, but his replacement had already arrived at the post, and Cheng returned south the same day.

entries.zh: 未幾，除江西儒學副提舉，居三月，以疾去官。
entries.en: Before long he was appointed Associate Commissioner of Jiangxi Confucian Schools. After three months he left office because of illness.
entries.literal: Before long he was made Associate Commissioner of Jiangxi Confucian Schools; after three months he left office because of illness.

entries.zh: 澄身若不勝衣，正坐拱手，氣融神邁，答問亹亹，使人渙若冰釋。
entries.en: Wu Cheng's frame seemed scarcely able to bear clothing. Sitting upright with joined hands, his spirit was harmonious and his bearing transcendent. In answering questions he was tireless, and listeners felt their doubts melt away like ice in spring.
entries.literal: Cheng's body seemed scarcely able to bear clothing; sitting upright with hands joined, his spirit was harmonious and his bearing transcendent; in answering questions he was tireless, making men melt as ice dissolves.

entries.zh: 弱冠時，嘗著說曰：「道之大原出於天，神聖繼之，堯、舜而上，道之元也；
entries.en: In his youth he once wrote a treatise, saying, "The great origin of the Way comes forth from Heaven, and the sages continue it. Above Yao and Shun lies the Origin of the Way;
entries.literal: In his weak-capped years he once wrote a treatise, saying: "The great origin of the Way comes forth from Heaven; the sage continues it. Above Yao and Shun is the Origin of the Way;

entries.zh: 堯、舜而下，其亨也；
entries.en: Below Yao and Shun comes its Flourishing;
entries.literal: Below Yao and Shun is its Flourishing;

entries.zh: 洙、泗、鄒、魯，其利也；
entries.en: Zhu, Si, Zou, and Lu represent its Advantage;
entries.literal: Zhu, Si, Zou, and Lu are its Advantage;

entries.zh: 濂、洛、關、閩，其貞也。
entries.en: Lian, Luo, Guan, and Min represent its Steadfastness.
entries.literal: Lian, Luo, Guan, and Min are its Steadfastness.

entries.zh: 分而言之，上古則羲、黃其元，堯、舜其亨，禹、湯其利，文、武、周公其貞乎！
entries.en: Speaking in detail: in high antiquity Fuxi and the Yellow Emperor are the Origin, Yao and Shun the Flourishing, Yu and Tang the Advantage, and King Wen, King Wu, and the Duke of Zhou the Steadfastness!
entries.literal: Speaking in detail, in high antiquity Fuxi and the Yellow Emperor are the Origin, Yao and Shun the Flourishing, Yu and Tang the Advantage, and Wen, Wu, and the Duke of Zhou the Steadfastness!

entries.zh: 中古之統：仲尼其元，顏、曾其亨乎，子思其利，孟子其貞乎！
entries.en: The lineage of middle antiquity: Confucius is the Origin, Yan Hui and Zeng Shen perhaps the Flourishing, Zisi the Advantage, Mencius the Steadfastness!
entries.literal: The lineage of the middle antiquity: Confucius is the Origin, Yan and Zeng perhaps the Flourishing, Zisi the Advantage, Mencius the Steadfastness!

entries.zh: 近古之統：周子其元，程、張其亨也，朱子其利也，孰為今日之貞乎？
entries.en: The lineage of recent antiquity: Zhou Dunyi is the Origin, the Cheng brothers and Zhang Zai the Flourishing, Zhu Xi the Advantage—who is today's Steadfastness?
entries.literal: The lineage of recent antiquity: Master Zhou is the Origin, the Cheng brothers and Zhang the Flourishing, Master Zhu the Advantage—who is today's Steadfastness?

entries.zh: 未之有也。
entries.en: There has not yet been such a one.
entries.literal: There has not yet been such a one.

entries.zh: 然則可以終無所歸哉！」
entries.en: Yet can the Way in the end have nowhere to return!"
entries.literal: Yet can one in the end have nowhere to return!"

entries.zh: 其早以斯文自任如此。
entries.en: Thus from early on he took upon himself this charge of civilization.
entries.literal: Thus early he took upon himself this charge of civilization.

entries.zh: 故出登朝署，退歸於家，與郡邑之所經由，士大夫皆迎請執業，而四方之士不憚數千里，躡屩負笈來學山中者，常不下千數百人。
entries.en: Therefore whether he went forth to hold office at court or withdrew to his home, in every prefecture and county he passed through, scholar-officials welcomed him to teach. Scholars from the four quarters did not shrink from traveling thousands of li, treading in sandals and bearing satchels to study with him in the mountains—often no fewer than a thousand or several hundred at a time.
entries.literal: Therefore when he went forth to take office at court or withdrew to his home, in every prefecture and county he passed through the scholar-officials all welcomed him to teach; scholars from the four quarters did not shrink from several thousand li, treading in sandals and bearing satchels to study in the mountains—often no fewer than a thousand or several hundred men.

entries.zh: 少暇即著書，至將終，猶不置也。
entries.en: Whenever he had a moment's leisure he wrote books, and even as death approached he did not set them aside.
entries.literal: In the brief leisure he had he wrote books, and even as death approached he did not set them aside.

entries.zh: 於《易》、《春秋》、《禮記》，各有纂言，盡破傳注穿鑿，以發其蘊，條歸紀敘，精明簡潔，卓然成一家言。
entries.en: On the Changes, Spring and Autumn, and Record of Rites he composed separate expository works, thoroughly breaking through the forced interpretations of transmitted commentaries to unfold their inner meaning. His arrangements by category and chronology were clear and concise, and he outstandingly formed a school of his own.
entries.literal: On the Changes, Spring and Autumn, and Record of Rites he each composed expository writings, thoroughly breaking through the forced interpretations of transmitted commentaries to unfold their inner meaning, arranging them by category and chronology, clear and concise, and outstandingly forming a school of his own.

entries.zh: 作《學基》、《學統》二篇，使人知學之本與為學之序，尤有得於邵子之學。
entries.en: He wrote the two treatises Foundations of Learning and Succession of Learning, to show people the root of learning and the proper order of pursuing it, drawing especially on Shao Yong's teachings.
entries.literal: He composed the two treatises Foundations of Learning and Succession of Learning, to make men know the root of learning and the order of pursuing it, especially gaining from Master Shao's learning.

entries.zh: 校定《皇極經世書》，又校正《老子》、《莊子》、《太玄經》、《樂律》，及《八陣圖》、郭璞《葬書》。
entries.en: He collated Shao Yong's Classic of the Supreme Ultimate Governing the Age, and also corrected the Laozi, Zhuangzi, Yang Xiong's Classic of the Supreme Mystery, treatises on music and pitch standards, the Eight-Formation Diagram, and Guo Pu's Book of Burial.
entries.literal: He collated the Classic of the Supreme Ultimate Governing the Age, and also corrected Laozi, Zhuangzi, the Classic of the Supreme Mystery, Music and Pitch Standards, the Eight-Formation Diagram, and Guo Pu's Book of Burial.

entries.zh: 初，澄所居草屋數間，程鉅夫題曰草廬，故學者稱之為草廬先生。
entries.en: Earlier Wu Cheng lived in a few thatched rooms. Cheng Jufu inscribed the name Thatched Hut over the door, and scholars therefore called him Master Thatched Hut.
entries.literal: Earlier, Cheng dwelt in a few thatched rooms; Cheng Jufu inscribed them "Thatched Hut," and therefore scholars called him Master Thatched Hut.

entries.zh: 天曆三年，朝廷以澄耆老，特命次子京為撫州教授，以便奉養。
entries.en: In the third year of Tianli (1330), because Wu Cheng was elderly, the court specially appointed his second son Jing professor at Fuzhou to facilitate his care.
entries.literal: In the third year of Tianli, because Cheng was aged, the court specially appointed his second son Jing professor at Fuzhou to facilitate his support.

entries.zh: 明年六月，得疾，有大星墜其舍東北，澄卒，年八十五。
entries.en: In the sixth month of the following year he fell ill. A great star fell to the northeast of his dwelling, and Wu Cheng died, aged eighty-five.
entries.literal: In the sixth month of the next year he fell ill; a great star fell to the northeast of his dwelling; Cheng died, aged eighty-five.

entries.zh: 贈江西行省左丞、上護軍，追封臨川郡公，諡文正。
entries.en: He was posthumously appointed Left Assistant Minister of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat and Commander of the Upper Army, enfeoffed as Duke of Linchuan Commandery, and given the posthumous title Wenzheng.
entries.literal: He was posthumously made Left Assistant Minister of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat and Commander of the Upper Army, with enfeoffment as Duke of Linchuan Commandery and the posthumous title Wenzheng.

entries.zh: 長子文，終同知柳州路總管府事；
entries.en: His eldest son Wen eventually served as Associate Administrator of the Liuzhou Circuit General Administration;
entries.literal: His eldest son Wen ended as Associate Administrator of the Liuzhou Circuit General Administration;

entries.zh: 京，終翰林國史院典籍官。
entries.en: Jing eventually served as Archivist of the Hanlin National History Academy.
entries.literal: Jing ended as Archivist of the Hanlin National History Academy.

entries.zh: 孫當，自有傳。
entries.en: His grandson Dang has his own biography.
entries.literal: His grandson Dang has his own biography.

entries.zh: 劉因，字夢吉，保定容城人。
entries.en: Liu Yin, whose courtesy name was Mengji, came from Rongcheng in Baoding.
entries.literal: Liu Yin, courtesy name Mengji, was a man of Rongcheng in Baoding.

entries.zh: 世為儒家，五世祖琮生敦武校尉、臨洮府錄事判官昉，昉生奉議大夫、中山府錄事俁，俁生秉善，金貞祐中南徙。
entries.en: The family had been Confucian scholars for generations. Liu Yin's fifth-generation ancestor Cong had a son Fang, who served as Dunwu Company Commander and Assistant Administrative Officer of Lintao Prefecture; Fang's son You held the rank of Grand Master for Discussion of Governance and was record keeper of Zhongshan Prefecture; You's son Bingshan moved the family south during the Jin dynasty's Zhenyou period.
entries.literal: For generations they were a Confucian family. His fifth-generation ancestor Cong was father to Fang, Dunwu Company Commander and Assistant Administrative Officer of Lintao Prefecture; Fang was father to You, Grand Master for Discussion of Governance and Record Keeper of Zhongshan Prefecture; You was father to Bingshan, who moved south during the Zhenyou era of Jin.

entries.zh: 其弟國寶，登興定進士第，終奉直大夫、樞密院經歷。
entries.en: His younger brother Guobao passed the jinshi examination in the Xingding era and eventually served as Assistant Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs with the rank of Master for Directing Government.
entries.literal: His younger brother Guobao passed the Xingding jinshi examination and ended as Assistant Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs with the title Master for Directing Government.

entries.zh: 秉善生述，述，因之父也。
entries.en: Bingshan had a son named Shu, who was Liu Yin's father.
entries.literal: Bingshan was father to Shu; Shu was Yin's father.

entries.zh: 歲壬辰，述始北歸，刻意問學，邃性理之說，好長嘯。
entries.en: In the renchen year (1232), Shu returned north for the first time, threw himself into learning, mastered Neo-Confucian teachings on nature and principle, and loved to give long whistles.
entries.literal: In the year renchen, Shu first returned north, devoted himself to study, penetrated the doctrines of nature and principle, and loved to whistle long and loud.

entries.zh: 中統初，左三部尚書劉肅宣撫真定，辟武邑令，以疾辭歸。
entries.en: Early in the Zhongtong era, when Liu Su of the Left Three Departments was pacifying Zhending, he appointed Shu magistrate of Wuyi; Shu resigned because of illness and went home.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Zhongtong era, Liu Su of the Left Three Departments, while pacifying Zhending, recruited him as magistrate of Wuyi, but he declined on grounds of illness and returned home.

entries.zh: 年四十未有子，歎曰：「天果使我無子則已，有子必令讀書。」
entries.en: By the age of forty he still had no son. He sighed and said, "If Heaven truly means me to remain childless, so be it; but if I do have a son, I shall certainly have him study the classics."
entries.literal: At forty he still had no son, and sighed: "If Heaven truly wills that I have no son, so be it; if I have a son, I shall surely make him read books."

entries.zh: 因生之夕，述夢神人馬載一兒至其家，曰：「善養之。」
entries.en: On the night Liu Yin was born, Shu dreamed that a divine figure on horseback brought a child to his door and said, "Nurture him well."
entries.literal: On the night Yin was born, Shu dreamed that a divine man on horseback brought a child to his house, saying: "Raise him well."

entries.zh: 既覺而生，乃名曰駰，字夢驥，後改今名及字。
entries.en: When he woke, the child had indeed been born. He was first named Yin with the courtesy name Mengji; later he received his present name and courtesy name.
entries.literal: When he awoke, the child was born; he was first named Yin, courtesy name Mengji, and later his present name and courtesy name were adopted.

entries.zh: 燧年三十八，始為秦王府文學。
entries.en: At thirty-eight Sui first became literary attendant in the Prince of Qin's establishment.
entries.literal: At the age of thirty-eight Sui first became literary attendant in the Prince of Qin's establishment.

entries.zh: 未幾，授奉議大夫，兼提舉陝西、四川、中興等路學校。
entries.en: Before long he was appointed Grand Master for Discussion and concurrently commissioner overseeing schools in the Shaanxi, Sichuan, Zhongxing, and other circuits.
entries.literal: Before long he was appointed Grand Master for Discussion and concurrently commissioner overseeing schools in the Shaanxi, Sichuan, Zhongxing, and other circuits.

entries.zh: 十二年，以秦王命，安輯庸、蜀。
entries.en: In the twelfth year, on the Prince of Qin's order, he pacified Yong and Shu.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year, on the Prince of Qin's order, he pacified Yong and Shu.

entries.zh: 明年，漢嘉新附，入諭其民。
entries.en: The following year, when Hanjia had newly submitted, he entered and instructed its people.
entries.literal: The following year, when Hanjia had newly submitted, he entered and instructed its people.

entries.zh: 又奉命招王立於合州。
entries.en: He was also ordered to recruit Wang Li at Hezhou.
entries.literal: He was also ordered to recruit Wang Li at Hezhou.

entries.zh: 又明年，撫循夔府。
entries.en: The year after that he pacified and comforted Kuifu.
entries.literal: The year after that he pacified and comforted Kuifu.

entries.zh: 凡三使蜀，皆稱職。
entries.en: He served on three missions to Shu, and in each was deemed competent.
entries.literal: He served on three missions to Shu, and in each was deemed competent.

entries.zh: 十七年，除陝西漢中道提刑按察司副使。
entries.en: In the seventeenth year he was made vice intendant of the Shaanxi Hanzhong Circuit Investigation and Punishment Commission.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year he was made vice intendant of the Shaanxi Hanzhong Circuit Investigation and Punishment Commission.

entries.zh: 錄囚延安，逮繫詿誤，皆縱釋之，人服其明決。
entries.en: Reviewing prisoners at Yan'an, he released all those wrongly detained; people admired his clarity and decisiveness.
entries.literal: Reviewing prisoners at Yan'an, he released all those wrongly detained; people admired his clarity and decisiveness.

entries.zh: 調山南湖北道。
entries.en: He was transferred to the Southern Mountains Hubei Circuit.
entries.literal: He was transferred to the Southern Mountains Hubei Circuit.

entries.zh: 按部澧州，興學賑民，孜孜如弗及。
entries.en: Touring Lizhou, he promoted schools and relieved the people, diligent as though he could never do enough.
entries.literal: Touring Lizhou, he promoted schools and relieved the people, diligent as though he could never do enough.

entries.zh: 二十三年，自湖北奉旨趨朝。
entries.en: In the twenty-third year he received imperial order from Hubei to hurry to court.
entries.literal: In the twenty-third year he received imperial order from Hubei to hurry to court.

entries.zh: 明年，為翰林直學士。
entries.en: The following year he became direct academician of the Hanlin Academy.
entries.literal: The following year he became direct academician of the Hanlin Academy.

entries.zh: 二十七年，授大司農丞。
entries.en: In the twenty-seventh year he was appointed assistant director of the Court of the Grand Minister of Agriculture.
entries.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was appointed assistant director of the Court of the Grand Minister of Agriculture.

entries.zh: 元貞元年，以翰林學士召修世祖實錄。
entries.en: In the first year of Yuanzhen (1295) he was summoned as Hanlin academician to compile the Veritable Record of Emperor Shizu.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yuanzhen he was summoned as Hanlin academician to compile the Veritable Record of Emperor Shizu.

entries.zh: 初置檢閱官，究覈故事，燧與侍讀高道凝總裁之，書成。
entries.en: When reviewing officers were first established to investigate historical precedents, Sui and the reader-in-waiting Gao Daoning served as chief compilers; the work was completed.
entries.literal: When reviewing officers were first established to investigate historical precedents, Sui and the reader-in-waiting Gao Daoning served as chief compilers; the work was completed.

entries.zh: 大德五年，授中憲大夫、江東廉訪使，移病太平。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Dade (1301) he received the rank of Grand Master of Palace Discipline and was made integrity commissioner of Jiangdong; citing illness, he moved to Taiping.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Dade he received the rank of Grand Master of Palace Discipline and was made integrity commissioner of Jiangdong; citing illness, he moved to Taiping.

entries.zh: 九年，拜中奉大夫、江西行省參知政事。
entries.en: In the ninth year (1305) he was appointed Grand Master of Special Grace and associate administrator of the Jiangxi branch secretariat.
entries.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed Grand Master of Special Grace and associate administrator of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat.

entries.zh: 至大元年，仁宗居藩邸，開宮師府，燧年已七十，遣正字呂洙，如漢徵四皓故事，起燧為太子賓客。
entries.en: In the first year of Zhida (1308), while Renzong still held his princely establishment and had opened a tutors' bureau, Sui was already seventy. Renzong sent the proofreader Lü Zhu, in deliberate echo of the Han summons to the Four Greybeards, to bring Sui out of retirement as guest of the heir apparent.
entries.literal: In the first year of Zhida, Renzong resided at the princely establishment and opened a palace tutors' office; Sui was already seventy; he sent the proofreader Lü Zhu, following the Han precedent of summoning the Four Hoary Heads, to raise Sui as Guest of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 未幾，除承旨學士，尋拜太子少傅。
entries.en: Before long he was appointed academician recipient of edicts, and shortly thereafter was appointed junior tutor to the heir apparent.
entries.literal: Before long he was appointed expositor academician; soon after he was invested as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 武宗面諭燧，燧拜辭，謝曰：「昔臣先伯父樞嘗除是官，尚不敢拜，臣何敢受！」
entries.en: Emperor Wuzong addressed him in person, but Sui bowed and declined, saying: "My late uncle Shu was once offered this same post and even he did not dare accept the seal—how could I?"
entries.literal: Emperor Wuzong instructed Sui in person; Sui bowed and declined, saying in thanks: "Formerly my late paternal uncle Shu was once appointed to this office and still did not dare accept the investiture—how dare I receive it!"

entries.zh: 明年，授榮祿大夫、翰林學士承旨、知制誥兼修國史。
entries.en: The following year he received the rank of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, with appointments as Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts, controller of imperial edicts, and concurrent compiler of the national history.
entries.literal: The next year he was granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts, Controller of Imperial Edicts, and concurrent Compiler of the National History.

entries.zh: 四年，得告南歸，中書以承旨召；
entries.en: In the fourth year he obtained leave and returned south; the Central Secretariat summoned him back as expositor;
entries.literal: In the fourth year he obtained leave to return south; the Central Secretariat summoned him as expositor;

entries.zh: 明年，復召。
entries.en: the next year he was summoned again.
entries.literal: the next year he was summoned again.

entries.zh: 燧以病，俱不赴。
entries.en: Both times Sui pleaded illness and did not go.
entries.literal: Sui pleaded illness and on both occasions did not go.

entries.zh: 卒於家，年七十六。
entries.en: He died at home at the age of seventy-six.
entries.literal: He died at home, aged seventy-six.

entries.zh: 諡曰文。
entries.en: He was given the posthumous title Wen.
entries.literal: His posthumous title was Wen.

entries.zh: 郝天挺，字繼先，出於朵魯別族，自曾祖而上，居安肅州。
entries.en: Hao Tianting, styled Jixian, came of the Dorben tribe; from his great-grandfather's generation the family lived in Ansu Prefecture.
entries.literal: Hao Tianting, styled Jixian, came from the Dorben tribe; from his great-grandfather upward the family resided in Ansu Prefecture.

entries.zh: 父和上拔都魯，太宗、憲宗之世多著武功，為河東行省五路軍民萬戶。
entries.en: His father Heshang Badulu won distinction in the campaigns of Taizong and Xianzong and served as commander of military and civilian households for the five circuits of the Hedong regional secretariat.
entries.literal: His father Heshang Badulu in the eras of Taizong and Xianzong achieved many military feats and served as commander of military and civilian households of the five circuits of the Hedong regional secretariat.

entries.zh: 天挺英爽剛直，有志略，受業於遺山元好問，以勳臣子，世祖召見，嘉其容止，有旨：宜任以政，俾執文字，備宿衛春宮。
entries.en: Tianting was brilliant, forthright, and ambitious; he studied under Yuan Haowen of Yishan. As the son of a meritorious minister he was summoned by Kublai, who admired his bearing and ordered that he be trained for government service, handle documents, and serve on night guard at the Eastern Palace.
entries.literal: Tianting was bright, forthright, and upright, with ambition and strategy; he received instruction from Yishan Yuan Haowen; as the son of a meritorious minister he was summoned for audience by Shizu, who admired his bearing and deportment; an edict stated that he should be entrusted with government, made to handle documents, and assigned to guard the Eastern Palace on night duty.

entries.zh: 裕宗遇之甚厚。
entries.en: Yuzong treated him with great favor.
entries.literal: Yuzong treated him very generously.

entries.zh: 建省雲南，選官屬，遂除參議雲南行尚書省事，尋升參知政事，又擢陝西漢中道廉訪使。
entries.en: When Yunnan province was established he was chosen as deliberator of its regional secretariat, soon promoted associate administrator, and then integrity commissioner of Shaanxi and Hanzhong.
entries.literal: When Yunnan Province was established and officials were selected, he was appointed deliberator of the Yunnan Regional Secretariat, soon promoted associate administrator, and then elevated integrity commissioner of Shaanxi and Hanzhong Circuit.

entries.zh: 未幾，入為吏部尚書，尋除陝西行御史臺中丞，又遷四川行省參政及江浙行省左丞，俱不赴。
entries.en: Before long he entered the capital as Minister of Personnel, then censor-in-chief of the Shaanxi Regional Censorate, and was offered posts as associate administrator of Sichuan and left chancellor of Jiang-Zhe—all of which he declined.
entries.literal: Before long he entered the capital as Minister of Personnel, soon was appointed censor-in-chief of the Shaanxi Regional Censorate, and was again transferred to associate administrator of Sichuan and left chancellor of Jiang-Zhe regional secretariats—all of which he did not take up.

entries.zh: 拜中書左丞，與宰相論事，有不合，輒面斥之。
entries.en: He accepted appointment as left chancellor of the Central Secretariat and, when he disagreed with the chief minister on policy, rebuked him to his face.
entries.literal: He was appointed left chancellor of the Central Secretariat; when he discussed affairs with the chief minister and there was disagreement, he would at once rebuke him to his face.

entries.zh: 一日，以奏事敷陳明允，特賜黃金百兩，不受。
entries.en: One day, after he presented a particularly clear and forceful memorial, the emperor granted him a hundred taels of gold, which he refused.
entries.literal: One day, because in memorializing affairs he set forth clear and fair arguments, he was specially granted one hundred taels of gold, which he did not accept.

entries.zh: 帝曰：「非利汝也，第旌汝肯言耳。」
entries.en: The emperor said: "This is not for your profit; it is only to honor your willingness to speak frankly."
entries.literal: The Emperor said: "This is not to enrich you; it is only to honor your willingness to speak out."

entries.zh: 時汴梁既下，太常樂師流寓東平，舊章缺落，止存登歌一章而已。
entries.en: After the fall of Bianliang, Court of Imperial Sacrifices musicians had taken refuge at Dongping; most of the old ritual music was lost, and only one ascending hymn survived.
entries.literal: At the time Bianliang had already fallen; Court of Imperial Sacrifices musicians were scattered and lodged at Dongping; the old regulations were lost, and only the ascending song in one section remained.

entries.zh: 世祖居潛邸，嘗召樂師至日月山觀之，至是，徐世隆奏帝，宜增設宮縣及文、武二舞，以備大典。
entries.en: When Kublai still held his princely establishment he had summoned the musicians to Sun-Moon Mountain for inspection. Xu Shilong now memorialized that palace bells and chimes and the civil and military dances should be restored for the great state ceremonies.
entries.literal: When Shizu resided at the princely establishment he once summoned the musicians to Sun-Moon Mountain to observe them; at this time Xu Shilong memorialized the Emperor that palace bells and chimes and the civil and military dances should be added to complete the great ritual.

entries.zh: 因詔徐世隆為太常卿，而孔孫以奉禮郎為之副，以董樂師，肄成，獻之京師。
entries.en: An edict appointed Xu Shilong Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Kongsun his deputy as ceremonial officer to supervise the musicians. When their work was complete they presented the restored music in the capital.
entries.literal: An edict thereupon appointed Xu Shilong Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Kongsun as his deputy in the post of ceremonial officer, to supervise the musicians; when practice was complete they presented the result in the capital.

entries.zh: 廉希憲居政府，辟為掾。
entries.en: When Lian Xixian held power in the government he recruited Kongsun as a clerk.
entries.literal: When Lian Xixian held office in the government he recruited Kongsun as a clerk.

entries.zh: 及安童為相，尤禮重之，授戶部員外郎，出為南京總管府判官。
entries.en: When An'tong became chancellor he treated Kongsun with special respect, appointed him vice director in the Ministry of Revenue, and sent him out as judge of the Nanjing Metropolitan Prefecture.
entries.literal: When An'tong became chancellor he especially honored and esteemed him, appointed him vice director in the Ministry of Revenue, and sent him out as judge of the Nanjing Metropolitan Prefecture.

entries.zh: 時方議下襄樊，朝廷急用兵，孔孫謂：「今以越境私販坐罪者，動以千數，宜開自新之條，俾得效戰贖死。」
entries.en: As the court debated the reduction of Xiangyang and Fancheng and urgently needed troops, Kongsun said: "Thousands are now imprisoned for cross-border smuggling. Open a path to repentance and let them redeem their lives by serving in battle."
entries.literal: At the time there was deliberation on reducing Xiang and Fan; the court urgently needed troops; Kongsun said: "Today those convicted for smuggling across borders number in the thousands; a clause for self-renewal should be opened so they may serve in battle to redeem death."

entries.zh: 朝論采之。
entries.en: The court adopted his proposal.
entries.literal: Court opinion adopted it.

entries.zh: 僉四川道提刑按察司事，尋升湖北道提刑按察副使。
entries.en: He was made vice commissioner of the Sichuan investigating commission and soon promoted vice commissioner of Hubei.
entries.literal: He was appointed vice commissioner of the Sichuan Circuit Commission for Investigation and Censorship, and soon was promoted vice commissioner of the Hubei Circuit Commission.

entries.zh: 行部巴陵，有囚三百人，因怒龔乙建言興銀利，發其墳墓而燒其家，燒死者三人。
entries.en: On circuit at Baling he found three hundred prisoners who, enraged by Gong Yi's proposal to revive silver mining, had desecrated his grave and burned his house, killing three people in the blaze.
entries.literal: When he conducted his tour at Baling there were three hundred prisoners who, in anger at Gong Yi's proposal to revive silver profits, had opened his grave and burned his house, and three died in the fire.

entries.zh: 有司以真圖財殺人坐之，孔孫原其情，減罪。
entries.en: Officials had charged them with murder for gain; Kongsun took account of their motives and reduced the sentences.
entries.literal: The responsible offices charged them with murder for gain; Kongsun excused their circumstances and reduced the punishment.

entries.zh: 遷浙西提刑按察副使，改同知保定路總管府事，俄拜侍御史，行御史臺事。
entries.en: He was transferred to vice commissioner of Zhexi, made vice administrator of Baoding Metropolitan Prefecture, and soon appointed attendant censor with charge of censorate affairs.
entries.literal: He was transferred to vice commissioner of the Zhexi investigating commission, was changed to vice administrator of the Baoding Metropolitan Prefecture, and soon was appointed attendant censor and directed censorate affairs.

entries.zh: 至元二十二年，安童復入相，言於帝曰：「阿合馬顓政十年，親故迎合者，往往驟進，據顯位；
entries.en: In the twenty-second year of Zhiyuan (1285) An'tong returned to the chancellorship and told the emperor: "For ten years Ahmad monopolized power; his kin and flatterers rose overnight to high office;
entries.literal: In the twenty-second year of Zhiyuan An'tong again entered the chancellorship and said to the Emperor: "Ahmad monopolized government for ten years; kinsmen and friends who flattered him often rose suddenly and held eminent posts;

entries.zh: 獨劉宣、張孔孫二人，恬守故常，終始如一。」
entries.en: only Liu Xuan and Zhang Kongsun remained unchanged from first to last."
entries.literal: only Liu Xuan and Zhang Kongsun, two men, calmly kept to their former ways, the same from beginning to end."

entries.zh: 乃除宣吏部尚書，孔孫禮部侍郎。
entries.en: Xuan was then made Minister of Personnel and Kongsun Vice Minister of Rites.
entries.literal: Thereupon Xuan was appointed Minister of Personnel and Kongsun Vice Minister of Rites.

entries.zh: 尋升孔孫禮部尚書，擢燕南提刑按察使。
entries.en: Kongsun was soon promoted Minister of Rites and made investigating commissioner of Yannan.
entries.literal: Soon Kongsun was promoted Minister of Rites and elevated investigating commissioner of Yannan.

entries.zh: 二十八年，提刑按察司改肅政廉訪司，仍為使，蒞治於大名，一以所沒贓糴粟五千斛賑饑民。
entries.en: In the twenty-eighth year (1291) the investigating commission became the Commission for Government Integrity; he remained commissioner at Daming and used confiscated illicit funds to buy five thousand hu of grain for famine relief.
entries.literal: In the twenty-eighth year the Commission for Investigation and Censorship was changed to the Commission for Government Integrity; he remained commissioner, administered at Daming, and with confiscated illicit goods purchased five thousand hu of grain to relieve famine victims.

entries.zh: 拜僉河南江北行中書省事。
entries.en: He was appointed associate administrator of the Henan and Jiangbei Regional Secretariat.
entries.literal: He was appointed associate administrator of the Henan and Jiangbei Regional Secretariat.

entries.zh: 亡何，除大名路總管，兼府尹，大興學校。
entries.en: Before long he was made metropolitan prefect of Daming, also serving as prefect, and greatly expanded the schools.
entries.literal: Before long he was appointed metropolitan prefect of Daming Circuit, concurrently prefect, and greatly promoted schools.

entries.zh: 有獻故河堤三百餘里於太后者，即上章，謂宜悉還細民，從之。
entries.en: When someone presented more than three hundred li of former river embankments to the empress dowager, he memorialized that they should all be returned to the common people, and the court agreed.
entries.literal: When someone presented more than three hundred li of former river embankments to the Empress Dowager, he at once submitted a memorial stating that all should be returned to the common people, and this was followed.

entries.zh: 擢淮東道肅政廉訪司使，因讞獄鹽場，民尹執中兄弟誣伏為強盜，平反之。
entries.en: Promoted commissioner of the Huaidong Commission for Government Integrity, he reversed a salt-works case in which the commoner Yin Zhizhong and his brothers had been forced to confess to banditry.
entries.literal: He was promoted commissioner of the Huaidong Commission for Government Integrity; because of a case at a salt works, the commoners Yin Zhizhong and his brothers had falsely confessed to being bandits, and he reversed the verdict.

entries.zh: 召還，拜集賢大學士、中奉大夫，商議中書省事。
entries.en: Recalled to court, he was made grand academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies and Grand Master of Palace Attendance with a seat in Central Secretariat deliberations.
entries.literal: He was recalled, appointed grand academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies and Grand Master of Palace Attendance, and deliberated on Central Secretariat affairs.

entries.zh: 丞相完澤卒，孔孫與陳天祥上封事，薦和禮霍孫可為相。
entries.en: When Chancellor Wanze died, Kongsun and Chen Tianxiang submitted a sealed memorial recommending Helihuosun for the chancellorship.
entries.literal: When Chancellor Wanze died, Kongsun and Chen Tianxiang submitted a sealed memorial recommending Helihuosun as fit for chancellor.

entries.zh: 會地震，詔問弭災之道，孔孫條對八事，其略曰：蠻夷諸國，不可窮兵遠討；
entries.en: After an earthquake the emperor asked how to avert calamity; Kongsun replied with eight points, in brief: do not exhaust the armies on distant campaigns against barbarian states;
entries.literal: When there was an earthquake, an edict asked the way to quell calamity; Kongsun itemized eight matters in reply; in summary: the various barbarian states should not be pursued with exhausted armies on distant campaigns;

entries.zh: 濫官放譴，不可復加任用；
entries.en: officials dismissed for misconduct should not be reappointed;
entries.literal: officials dismissed for abuse should not again be employed;

entries.zh: 賞善罰惡，不可數賜赦宥；
entries.en: in rewarding good and punishing evil, do not issue amnesties too often;
entries.literal: in rewarding good and punishing evil, amnesties should not be repeatedly granted;

entries.zh: 獻鬻寶貨，不可不為禁絕；
entries.en: the offering and sale of precious goods must be strictly forbidden;
entries.literal: the presentation and sale of precious goods must be strictly forbidden;

entries.zh: 供佛無益，不可虛費財用；
entries.en: Buddhist offerings bring no benefit and public funds should not be wasted on them;
entries.literal: supporting Buddhism is of no benefit and state funds should not be wasted on it;

entries.zh: 上下豪侈，不可不從儉約；
entries.en: extravagance at court and in the provinces must give way to frugality;
entries.literal: luxury above and below must be curbed through frugality;

entries.zh: 官冗吏繁，不可不為裁減；
entries.en: redundant offices and excessive clerical staffs must be cut;
entries.literal: redundant offices and numerous clerks must be reduced;

entries.zh: 太廟神主，不可不備祭享。
entries.en: sacrificial rites at the Imperial Ancestral Temple must not be neglected.
entries.literal: the spirit tablets of the Imperial Ancestral Temple must not lack sacrificial offerings.

entries.zh: 帝悉嘉納之，賜鈔五千貫。
entries.en: The emperor praised and accepted all his points and granted him five thousand strings of paper currency.
entries.literal: The Emperor praised and accepted all of them and bestowed five thousand strings of paper currency.

entries.zh: 又累疏言：「凡七十致仕者，宜加一官；
entries.en: He also memorialized repeatedly: "Officials who retire at seventy should receive one additional rank;
entries.literal: He also repeatedly memorialized: "All who retire at seventy should receive one additional rank;

entries.zh: 丁憂服闋者，宜待起復；
entries.en: those who have completed mourning should await recall before reappointment;
entries.literal: those who have completed mourning should await recall;

entries.zh: 宿衛之冒濫者，必當革；
entries.en: abuses in the palace guard must be eliminated;
entries.literal: those who have improperly entered palace guard service must be reformed;

entries.zh: 州郡之職，必當遴選，久任達魯花赤，宜量加遷轉；
entries.en: prefectural posts must be carefully filled; darughachi who serve too long in one place should be rotated;
entries.literal: prefectural and commandery posts must be carefully selected; darughachi who serve long in one place should be transferred in due measure;

entries.zh: 又宜增給官吏俸祿；
entries.en: official salaries should be increased;
entries.literal: official salaries should also be increased;

entries.zh: 修建京師廟學，設國子生徒，給賜曲阜孔廟灑掃戶；
entries.en: temple schools should be built in the capital, Imperial Academy students enrolled, and sweeping households granted for the Confucian temple at Qufu;
entries.literal: temple schools in the capital should be built, Imperial Academy disciples established, and sweeping households for the Qufu Temple of Confucius granted;

entries.zh: 相位宜參用儒臣，不可專任文吏；
entries.en: the chancellorship should include Confucian ministers and not be left to clerical officials alone;
entries.literal: the chancellorship should employ Confucian ministers jointly and not rely solely on clerical officials;

entries.zh: 故相安童、伯顏、和禮霍孫與廉希憲等，各宜贈諡。」
entries.en: the late chancellors An'tong, Bayan, Helihuosun, and Lian Xixian should each receive posthumous titles."
entries.literal: the former chancellors An'tong, Bayan, Helihuosun, and Lian Xixian and others should each be granted posthumous titles."

entries.zh: 久之，請老還家，拜翰林學士承旨、資善大夫，致仕，集賢大學士如故。
entries.en: After many years he asked to retire; he was made Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts and Grand Master for Goodness, retired from active service, and retained his grand academician title at the Hall of Gathered Worthies.
entries.literal: After a long time he requested to retire on account of age and return home; he was appointed Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts and Grand Master for Goodness, retired from office, and remained grand academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies as before.

entries.zh: 大德十一年卒，年七十有五。
entries.en: In the eleventh year of Dade (1307) he died at the age of seventy-five.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year of Dade he died, aged seventy-five.

entries.zh: 姚燧，字端甫，世系見燧伯父樞傳。
entries.en: Yao Sui, styled Duanfu, came of a family whose lineage is recorded in the biography of his paternal uncle Yao Shu.
entries.literal: Yao Sui, styled Duanfu; his lineage is set forth in the biography of Sui's paternal uncle Shu.

entries.zh: 父格。
entries.en: His father was Ge.
entries.literal: His father was Ge.

entries.zh: 燧生三歲而孤，育於伯父樞。
entries.en: Sui was orphaned at the age of three and was brought up by his uncle Yao Shu.
entries.literal: Sui lost his father at age three and was reared by his paternal uncle Shu.

entries.zh: 樞隱居蘇門，謂燧蒙暗，教督之甚急，燧不能堪。
entries.en: Shu had retired to Sumen and judged the boy slow-witted; he drove his studies relentlessly, and Sui found it unbearable.
entries.literal: Shu lived in retirement at Sumen, considered Sui dull and benighted, and urged and supervised his studies very strictly; Sui could not endure it.

entries.zh: 楊奐馳書止之曰：「燧，令器也，長自有成爾，何以急為！」
entries.en: Yang Huan wrote in haste to dissuade him: "Sui is promising timber; in time he will mature of his own accord—why press him so hard?"
entries.literal: Yang Huan sent a hurried letter to stop him, saying: "Sui is fine material; when grown he will achieve maturity on his own—why be so urgent!"

entries.zh: 且許醮以女。
entries.en: He also pledged his daughter in betrothal to the boy.
entries.literal: He also promised to betroth his daughter to him.

entries.zh: 年十三，見許衡於蘇門。
entries.en: At thirteen he met Xu Heng at Sumen.
entries.literal: At age thirteen he met Xu Heng at Sumen.

entries.zh: 十八，始受學於長安。
entries.en: At eighteen he began his formal studies in Chang'an.
entries.literal: At eighteen he first received instruction in Chang'an.

entries.zh: 時未嘗為文，視流輩所作，惟見其不如古人，則心弗是也。
entries.en: He had not yet tried his hand at writing, but when he read what his contemporaries produced he could see only how far it fell short of the ancients, and he inwardly rejected it.
entries.literal: At the time he had never yet composed essays; when he looked at what his contemporaries wrote, he saw only that it fell short of the ancients, and in his heart he disapproved.

entries.zh: 二十四，始讀韓退之文，試習為之，人謂有作者風。
entries.en: At twenty-four he first read Han Yu and tried writing in his manner; contemporaries said he already showed a master's touch.
entries.literal: At twenty-four he first read the writings of Han Tuizhi, tried practicing composition in that style, and people said he had the manner of a master writer.

entries.zh: 稍就正於衡，衡亦賞其辭，且戒之曰：「弓矢為物，以待盜也；
entries.en: He gradually submitted his work to Xu Heng for correction; Heng admired his prose but warned him: "Bows and arrows exist to meet robbers;
entries.literal: He gradually sought correction from Heng; Heng also admired his literary style and admonished him, saying: "Bow and arrow are things made to await robbers;

entries.zh: 使盜得之，亦將待人。
entries.en: if robbers seize them, they too will wait upon men.
entries.literal: if robbers obtain them, they too will await men.

entries.zh: 文章固發聞士子之利器，然先有能一世之名，將何以應人之見役者哉！
entries.en: Writing is the scholar's weapon for making a name, yet if you win a reputation that fills the age, how will you answer everyone who comes to command your pen?
entries.literal: Literary composition is indeed the sharp weapon by which a scholar makes his name heard, yet if one first gains a reputation able to command an age, how will one answer those who come to employ one!

entries.zh: 非其人而與之，與非其人而拒之，鈞罪也，非周身斯世之道也。」
entries.en: To grant your writing to the wrong man is as grave a fault as to refuse the right one; neither is the way to keep your footing in the world."
entries.literal: To give it to one who is not the right person, and to refuse one who is not the right person—the guilt is equal; neither is the way to preserve oneself in this world."

entries.zh: 至元七年，衡以國子祭酒教貴冑，奏召舊弟子十二人，燧自太原驛致館下。
entries.en: In the seventh year of Zhiyuan (1270), when Xu Heng served as director of the Imperial Academy and instructed the sons of the nobility, he memorialized to recall twelve former pupils; Sui traveled by relay from Taiyuan to join them at the academy.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Zhiyuan, Heng as Director of the Imperial Academy instructed the noble scions; he memorialized to summon twelve former disciples, and Sui came from Taiyuan by post-station relay to join them at the academy.

entries.zh: 張思明，字士瞻，其先獲嘉人，後​​徙居輝州。
entries.en: Zhang Siming, whose courtesy name was Shizhan, came from a family originally of Huojia that later relocated to Huizhou.
entries.literal: Zhang Siming, courtesy name Shizhan, his ancestors were from Huojia, and later moved to reside in Huizhou.

entries.zh: 思明穎悟過人，讀書日記千言。
entries.en: Siming was unusually gifted; when he read, he could commit a thousand characters to memory in a single day.
entries.literal: Siming was exceptionally quick-witted beyond others; in reading books he could memorize a thousand words per day.

entries.zh: 至元十九年，由侍儀司舍人辟御史臺掾，又辟尚書省掾。
entries.en: In 1282, while serving as an usher in the Ceremonial Institute, he was recruited first as a clerk in the Censorate and then in the Secretariat.
entries.literal: In the nineteenth year of Zhiyuan, from his post as usher of the Ceremonial Institute he was recruited as clerk of the Censorate, and again recruited as clerk of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 左丞相阿合馬既死，世祖追咎其奸欺，命尚書簿問遺孽。
entries.en: After the Left Chancellor Ahmad was dead, Kublai held him accountable for his deceit and ordered the Secretariat to investigate and record his remaining associates.
entries.literal: After Left Chancellor Ahmad died, Shizu pursued blame for his treachery and fraud, ordering the Secretariat to register and interrogate his surviving accomplices.

entries.zh: 一日，召右丞何榮祖、左丞馬紹，盡輸其贓以入，思明抱牘從，日已昏，命讀之，自昏達曙，帝聽忘疲，曰：「讀人吐音，大似侍儀舍人。」
entries.en: On one occasion the Emperor summoned the Right Chancellor He Rongzu and the Left Chancellor Ma Shao to deliver in full the confiscated illicit gains. Siming followed with the documents in his arms. Night had fallen, yet the Emperor ordered them read aloud, and listened from dusk until dawn without tiring. He remarked, "The reader's delivery sounds very much like one of our Ceremonial Institute ushers."
entries.literal: One day he summoned Right Chancellor He Rongzu and Left Chancellor Ma Shao to submit all the illicit gains in full; Siming carried documents and followed. The day had already grown dark; he ordered them read aloud—from dusk until dawn. The Emperor listened, forgetting fatigue, and said: "The reader's enunciation greatly resembles a Ceremonial Institute usher."

entries.zh: 右丞對曰：「正由舍人選為掾。」
entries.en: The Right Chancellor answered, "That is because he was chosen from among the ushers for this clerkship."
entries.literal: The Right Chancellor replied: "It is precisely because he was selected from among the ushers to become a clerk."

entries.zh: 帝奇之，曰：「斯人可用。」
entries.en: The Emperor was impressed and said, "This man is fit for service."
entries.literal: The Emperor marveled at him and said: "This man can be used."

entries.zh: 明日，擢為大都路治中。
entries.en: The following day Siming was promoted to Assistant Administrator of the Dadu metropolitan circuit.
entries.literal: The next day he was promoted to Assistant Administrator of the Dadu Circuit.

entries.zh: 思明以超遷逾等，固辭，乃改湖廣行省都事。
entries.en: Siming declined firmly on the grounds that the promotion skipped too many ranks, and was instead appointed Chief Secretary of the Huguang Branch Secretariat.
entries.literal: Siming, because the promotion exceeded his proper rank, firmly declined, and was therefore transferred to be Chief Secretary of the Huguang Branch Secretariat.

entries.zh: 元貞元年，召為中書省檢校，六曹無滯案，遷戶部主事。
entries.en: In 1295 he was recalled to serve as a reviewer in the Central Secretariat, where he cleared every bureau's backlog of cases and was promoted to principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yuanzhen he was summoned as Reviewer of the Central Secretariat; in the six bureaus there were no backlog cases, and he was transferred to be Principal Clerk of the Ministry of Revenue.

entries.zh: 大德初，擢左司都事，有獻西域秤法，思明以惑眾不用。
entries.en: Early in the Dade reign he rose to chief secretary of the Left Secretariat. When someone proposed a new weighing system from the Western Regions, Siming refused to adopt it, judging that it would only confuse the public.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Dade he was promoted to Chief Secretary of the Left Secretariat; someone presented a Western Regions method of weighing, and Siming, holding that it would mislead the people, did not adopt it.

entries.zh: 初立海道運糧萬戶府於江浙，受除者憚涉險，不行，思明請升等以優之，因著為令。
entries.en: When the maritime grain-transport office was first set up in Jiang-Zhe, appointees shrank from the dangers of the sea route and refused to take up their posts. Siming urged that their rank be raised as an incentive, and the measure was enacted as law.
entries.literal: When the Maritime Grain Transport Ten-thousand Households Office was first established in Jiang-Zhe, those who received appointments feared the perils of the voyage and would not go; Siming requested raising their rank grades as an incentive, and this was accordingly written into regulation.

entries.zh: 五年，轉吏部郎中。
entries.en: In the fifth year of the reign he was transferred to director in the Ministry of Personnel.
entries.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to be Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 九年，改集賢司直。
entries.en: In the ninth year he was reassigned as direct attendant of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.
entries.literal: In the ninth year he was changed to Direct Attendant of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.

entries.zh: 十年，除江浙行中書省左右司郎中。
entries.en: In the tenth year he was appointed director in the left and right secretariats of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.
entries.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed Director of the Left and Right Secretariats of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.

entries.zh: 十一年春，兩浙大饑，首贊發廩賑之。
entries.en: In the spring of the eleventh year both Zhe regions were stricken by severe famine, and he was the first to urge opening the public granaries for relief.
entries.literal: In the spring of the eleventh year, the two Zhe regions suffered great famine; he was the first to urge opening the granaries to relieve them.

entries.zh: 至大三年，遷兩浙鹽運使，未上，入參議樞密院事，改中書省左司郎中。
entries.en: In 1310 he was appointed salt transport commissioner for the two Zhe regions, but before he could take up that post he was made a discussant in the Bureau of Military Affairs and then director of the Central Secretariat's left office.
entries.literal: In the third year of Zhida he was transferred to Salt Transport Commissioner of the two Zhe regions; before taking up the post he entered to serve as Discussant of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and was changed to Director of the Left Secretariat of the Central Secretariat.

entries.zh: 皇慶元年，再授兩浙鹽運使，歲課羨贏，僚屬請上增數，思明曰：「贏縮不常，萬一以增為額，是我希一己之榮，遺百世之害。」
entries.en: In 1312 he was again appointed salt commissioner for the two Zhe regions. When that year's receipts ran above quota, his staff urged reporting the surplus as a permanent increase. Siming objected: "Revenues rise and fall; if we lock in a bumper year as the standard quota, I would be trading a moment's credit for generations of harm."
entries.literal: In the first year of Huangqing he was again appointed Salt Transport Commissioner of the two Zhe regions. That year's tax receipts exceeded the quota, and his subordinates asked to report the increase; Siming said: "Surplus and shortfall are not constant; if by chance the increase were made the fixed quota, this would be my seeking personal glory at the cost of harm lasting a hundred generations."

entries.zh: 二年，召為戶部尚書。
entries.en: The following year he was recalled to serve as Minister of Revenue.
entries.literal: In the second year he was summoned to be Minister of Revenue.

entries.zh: 延祐元年，進參議中書省事；
entries.en: In 1314 he was promoted to discussant of Central Secretariat affairs;
entries.literal: In the first year of Yanyou he was advanced to Discussant of Central Secretariat Affairs;

entries.zh: 三年，拜中書參知政事。
entries.en: and in the third year he was appointed assistant administrator of the Central Secretariat.
entries.literal: in the third year he was appointed Assistant Administrator of the Central Secretariat.

entries.zh: 吳元珪，字君璋，廣平人。
entries.en: Wu Yuangui, whose courtesy name was Junzhang, was a native of Guangping.
entries.literal: Wu Yuangui, courtesy name Junzhang, was a man of Guangping.

entries.zh: 父鼎，燕南提刑按察副使。
entries.en: His father Ding had served as vice commissioner of the Yannan circuit for punishments and investigations.
entries.literal: His father Ding was Vice Commissioner of the Yannan Circuit for Punishments and Investigations.

entries.zh: 元珪簡重，好深沉之思，凡徵謀治法、律令章程，皆得於家庭之所授受。
entries.en: Yuangui was reserved and serious, inclined to deep reflection; he learned statecraft, law, and administrative procedure entirely through instruction in his own household.
entries.literal: Yuangui was reserved and grave, fond of deep reflection; all matters of policy, law, statutes, and regulations he received from instruction within the family.

entries.zh: 至元十四年，世祖召見，命侍左右，授後衛經歷，佩金符。
entries.en: In 1277 Kublai summoned him to court, kept him in attendance at his side, appointed him administrator of the Rear Guard, and granted him a gold tally.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhiyuan, Shizu summoned him for audience, ordered him to attend at his side, appointed him Administrator of the Rear Guard, and bestowed a gold tally.

entries.zh: 十七年，從幸上都，受命取禦藥於大都萬歲山，元珪乘傳，未盡一晝夜而至。
entries.en: In 1280, while accompanying the court to Shangdu, he was sent to fetch imperial medicine from Wansui Mountain in Dadu. Traveling by relay post, he arrived in less than a full day and night.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year he accompanied the imperial progress to Shangdu and was ordered to fetch imperial medicine from Wansui Mountain in Dadu; Yuangui traveled by relay post and arrived in less than a day and night.

entries.zh: 帝奇其速，擢樞密都事，升經歷。
entries.en: The Emperor was astonished at his speed, promoted him to chief secretary in the Bureau of Military Affairs, and then to administrator.
entries.literal: The Emperor marveled at his speed, promoted him to Chief Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and advanced him to Administrator.

entries.zh: 嘗從同知樞密院事俺伯進西蕃鎧甲，帝問其制度，元珪應對詳明，帝益奇之。
entries.en: On one occasion he accompanied Vice Director Anbo in presenting Tibetan armor at court. When the Emperor asked about its design, Yuangui answered in meticulous detail and impressed him still more.
entries.literal: Once he followed Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Anbo in presenting Western Regions armor; the Emperor asked about its design, and Yuangui answered in full detail, so that the Emperor marveled at him all the more.

entries.zh: 仁宗即位，詔元珪與十六人議時政。
entries.en: When Renzong came to the throne, he ordered Yuangui and sixteen others to deliberate on current affairs.
entries.literal: When Renzong took the throne, an edict ordered Yuangui and sixteen others to deliberate on current policy.

entries.zh: 皇慶元年，出拜江浙行省左丞。
entries.en: In 1312 he was sent out to serve as Left Chancellor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.
entries.literal: In the first year of Huangqing he was sent out to serve as Left Chancellor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.

entries.zh: 江淮漕臣言：「江南殷富，蓋由多匿腴田，若再行檢覆之法，當益田畝累萬計。」
entries.en: The Jiang-Huai grain transport officials argued: "Jiangnan appears prosperous chiefly because many fertile fields are concealed from the registers. If we reinstated field inspections, we could add tens of thousands of acres to the tax rolls."
entries.literal: The grain transport officials of the Jiang-Huai region said: "The south of the Yangtze is wealthy and abundant, largely because many fertile fields are concealed; if the method of re-inspection and verification were applied again, field acreage would increase by tens of thousands."

entries.zh: 元珪曰：「江南之平，幾四十年，戶有定籍，田有定畝，一有動搖，其害不細。」
entries.en: Yuangui objected: "Jiangnan has been at peace for nearly forty years. Household registers and field acreage are fixed. Disturb them and the harm will be grave."
entries.literal: Yuangui said: "The south of the Yangtze has been pacified for nearly forty years; households have fixed registers and fields have fixed acreage—once this is disturbed, the harm will not be slight."

entries.zh: 執其論固爭，月餘不能止，移疾去。
entries.en: He held to his position and argued for more than a month without success, then resigned on grounds of illness.
entries.literal: He held to his view and argued firmly; for more than a month he could not stop it, and he submitted notice of illness and left.

entries.zh: 延祐元年，拜甘肅行省左丞。
entries.en: In 1314 he was appointed Left Chancellor of the Gansu Branch Secretariat.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yanyou he was appointed Left Chancellor of the Gansu Branch Secretariat.

entries.zh: 歲餘，召還，俾宣撫遼陽諸郡，復為樞密副使，召見嘉禧殿，帝曰：「卿先朝舊臣，宜在舊服。」
entries.en: After a little more than a year he was recalled, sent to pacify the commanderies of Liaoyang, and restored as vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs. Received in audience at Jiaxi Hall, the Emperor said, "You are a veteran of the previous reign and belong in your old post."
entries.literal: After more than a year he was recalled, made to pacify and console the commanderies of Liaoyang, and again became Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs. Summoned to audience in Jiaxi Hall, the Emperor said: "You are an old minister of the previous reign and ought to resume your former office."

entries.zh: 特加榮祿大夫，賜鈔五千緡、貂裘二襲。
entries.en: He was specially promoted to Grand Master for Glorious Blessing and granted five thousand strings of paper money and two sable coats.
entries.literal: He was specially advanced to Grand Master for Glorious Blessing and granted five thousand strings of paper money and two sable fur coats.

entries.zh: 元珪奏曰：「昔世祖限田四百畝，以給軍需，餘田悉貢賦稅。
entries.en: Yuangui memorialized: "In Kublai's day fields were capped at four hundred mu for military supply, and all surplus land paid tribute and tax.
entries.literal: Yuangui memorialized, saying: "Formerly Shizu limited fields to four hundred mu to supply military needs; all remaining fields were to pay tribute and taxes.

entries.zh: 今經理江淮田土，第以增金為能，加以有司頭會箕斂，俾元元之民，困苦日甚，臣恐變生不測，非國之福，惟陛下少加意焉。」
entries.en: Today officials managing Jiang-Huai land are praised only for raising revenue, while local officers squeeze the people with every levy. The common folk grow more wretched by the day. I fear unrest may follow—this cannot benefit the state. I beg your Majesty to take heed."
entries.literal: Now in managing the fields and lands of the Jiang-Huai region, merit is measured solely by increasing revenue; moreover the officials scrape together levies with combs and rakes, so that the common people grow daily more distressed. I fear unforeseen disturbances may arise—this is not a blessing to the state. I beg Your Majesty to give this a little attention."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「凡爾軍士之田，並遵舊制。」
entries.en: The Emperor replied, "All land held by soldiers shall follow the old regulations."
entries.literal: The Emperor said: "As for all fields belonging to soldiers, let the old regulations be followed throughout."

entries.zh: 張昇，字伯高，其先定州人，後徙平州。
entries.en: Zhang Sheng, whose courtesy name was Bogao, came from a family originally of Dingzhou that later moved to Pingzhou.
entries.literal: Zhang Sheng, courtesy name Bogao, his ancestors were from Dingzhou and later moved to Pingzhou.

entries.zh: 升幼警敏過人，學語時，輒能辨字音，應對異於常兒；
entries.en: As a child Sheng was unusually quick-witted; even while learning to speak he could distinguish character sounds, and his replies were unlike those of other children;
entries.literal: Sheng as a child was alert and clever beyond others; when learning to speak he could distinguish character pronunciations, and his replies differed from ordinary children;

entries.zh: 既長，力學，工文辭。
entries.en: when he grew older he studied hard and became accomplished in literary composition.
entries.literal: when he grew up he studied diligently and was skilled in literary composition.

entries.zh: 至元二十九年，用薦者授將仕郎、翰林國史院編修官，預修《世祖實錄》。
entries.en: In 1292, on recommendation, he was appointed Gentleman-in-Attendance and compiler in the Hanlin Academy's National History Office, where he helped compile the 《Veritable Records of Kublai》.
entries.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Zhiyuan, through a recommender he was appointed Gentleman-in-Attendance and Compiler in the Hanlin Academy National History Office, participating in the compilation of the Veritable Records of Shizu.

entries.zh: 升應奉翰林文字，尋升修撰，歷興文署令，遷太常博士。
entries.en: Sheng served as Hanlin attendant for composition, was soon promoted to compiler, became director of the Office for the Promotion of Literature, and was then transferred to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
entries.literal: Sheng served as Hanlin Attendant for Composition, was soon promoted to Compiler, served as Director of the Office for the Promotion of Literature, and was transferred to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

entries.zh: 成宗崩，大臣承中旨，議奉徽號，饗宗廟，升曰：「在故典，凡有事於宗廟，必書嗣皇帝名，今將何書？」
entries.en: When Chengzong died, the chief ministers, acting on a secret edict, debated posthumous honors and ancestral sacrifices. Sheng asked, "According to precedent, any ancestral temple rite must record the succeeding emperor's name—whose name should be entered now?"
entries.literal: When Chengzong died, the great ministers, acting on an inner edict, deliberated on bestowing a posthumous honorific title and offering sacrifices at the ancestral temple. Sheng said: "In the old statutes, whenever there is an affair at the ancestral temple, the name of the succeeding emperor must be written—what name shall be written now?"

entries.zh: 議遂寢。
entries.en: The proposal was dropped.
entries.literal: The deliberation was thereupon dropped.

entries.zh: 武宗即位，議躬祀禮，升據經引古，參酌時宜以對，帝嘉納之。
entries.en: When Wuzong came to the throne, the court debated the rites of personal sacrifice. Sheng answered by citing the classics and ancient precedent while adapting them to present needs, and the Emperor approved.
entries.literal: When Wuzong took the throne, they deliberated on the rites of personal sacrifice. Sheng cited the classics and ancient precedents, weighing present circumstances in his reply, and the Emperor praised and accepted it.

entries.zh: 至大初，改太常寺為太常禮儀院，即除升為判官。
entries.en: Early in the Zhida reign the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was reorganized as the Court of Imperial Sacrificial Rites, and Sheng was appointed its vice director.
