entries.literal: At the beginning of Zhida the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was changed to the Court of Imperial Sacrificial Rites, and Sheng was immediately appointed its Vice Director.

entries.zh: 張思明
entries.en: Zhang Siming
entries.literal: Zhang Siming

entries.zh: 至治元年，英宗即位，帖木迭兒復相，約辭職不出。
entries.en: In Zhizhi 1 (1321), when Emperor Yingzong acceded, Temür returned as chancellor; Yue resigned and stayed home.
entries.literal: In the first year of Zhizhi, Emperor Yingzong took the throne; Temür again became chancellor; Yue resigned and did not come forth.

entries.zh: 二年，以年七十致仕。
entries.en: In year 2, at seventy, he retired.
entries.literal: In the second year, at age seventy he retired from office.

entries.zh: 三年，丞相拜住一新政務，尊禮老臣，傳詔起約，復拜集賢大學士，商議中書省事，以其祿居家，每日一至中書省議事，至治之政，多所參酌。
entries.en: In year 3 Chancellor Bayiju reformed the government, honored veteran ministers, and recalled Yue as Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies to advise on Secretariat affairs; living at home on his salary, he came daily to deliberate, and Zhizhi policy owed much to him.
entries.literal: In the third year Chancellor Bayiju undertook a new administration, honored old ministers, and by transmitted edict raised Yue; he was again appointed Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies to deliberate on Central Secretariat affairs, living at home on his salary, coming once each day to the Central Secretariat to deliberate on affairs; Zhizhi policies were largely shaped by his counsel.

entries.zh: 又嘗奉詔與中書省官及他舊臣，條定國初以來律令，名曰《大元通制》，頒行天下。
entries.en: He also helped codify laws since the founding of the dynasty into the Comprehensive Regulations of the Great Yuan, promulgated empire-wide.
entries.literal: He also once received an edict, together with Central Secretariat officials and other old ministers, to itemize and fix laws and ordinances from the founding of the state onward, entitled Comprehensive Regulations of the Great Yuan, and promulgate them throughout the empire.

entries.zh: 朝廷議罷征東省，立三韓省，制式如他省，詔下中書雜議，約對曰：「高麗去京師四千里，地瘠民貧，夷俗雜尚，非中原比，萬一梗化，疲力治之，非幸事也，不如守祖宗舊制。」
entries.en: When the court debated abolishing the Eastern Campaign Secretariat and creating a Three Han province like the others, Yue replied, "Goryeo lies four thousand li from the capital, its land is poor and its customs unlike the Central Plains; if it resisted, pacification would exhaust us—better keep the ancestral arrangement."
entries.literal: The court deliberated abolishing the Eastern Campaign Secretariat and establishing a Three Han Secretariat with forms like other provinces; an edict was sent down to the Central Secretariat for mixed discussion; Yue replied: "Goryeo is four thousand li from the capital, its land poor and its people impoverished, its barbarian customs mixed and diverse—not comparable to the Central Plains; if by chance they resisted transformation, to exhaust strength governing them would not be a fortunate affair; better to keep the ancestral old system."

entries.zh: 丞相稱善，奏罷議不行。
entries.en: The chancellor approved, and the proposal was dropped.
entries.literal: The Chancellor praised it and memorialized that the proposal be dropped and not carried out.

entries.zh: 高麗人聞之，圖公像歸，祠而事之，曰：「不絕國祀者，王公也。」
entries.en: Goryeo people heard of it, brought his portrait home, and worshipped him, saying, "Lord Wang preserved our state's rites."
entries.literal: When Goryeo people heard of it they took his portrait home, enshrined and served it, saying: "He who did not cut off our state's sacrifices is Lord Wang."

entries.zh: 泰定元年，奉詔廷策天下士，第八剌、張益等八十五人，始增乙科員額至一十五人。
entries.en: In Taiding 1 (1324) he conducted the palace examination; Balha, Zhang Yi, and eighty-five others passed, and the second-class quota was raised to fifteen for the first time.
entries.literal: In the first year of Taiding he received an edict to conduct palace examinations of scholars empire-wide; Balha, Zhang Yi, and eighty-five others passed; the quota for the second class was for the first time increased to fifteen persons.

entries.zh: 梁曾，字貢父，燕人。
entries.en: Liang Ceng, whose courtesy name was Gongfu, came from the Yan region.
entries.literal: Liang Ceng, styled Gongfu, was a man of Yan.

entries.zh: 祖守正，父德，皆以曾貴，贈安定郡公。
entries.en: Because of Ceng's prominence, both his grandfather Shouzheng and his father De were posthumously ennobled as Dukes of Anding.
entries.literal: His grandfather Shouzheng and his father De, both because of Ceng's eminence, were posthumously enfeoffed as Dukes of Anding.

entries.zh: 曾少好學，日記書數千言。
entries.en: From childhood Ceng loved study and could commit several thousand characters to memory each day.
entries.literal: Ceng from youth loved learning; each day he could memorize several thousand characters in writing.

entries.zh: 中統四年，以翰林學士承旨王鶚薦，辟中書左三部令史，三轉為中書省掾。
entries.en: In Zhongtong 4 (1263), on the recommendation of Wang E, Grand Preceptor of the Hanlin Academy, he was appointed clerk of the Secretariat's left three departments and, after three promotions, rose to secretary in the Central Secretariat.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Zhongtong, on the recommendation of Hanlin Academician Grand Preceptor Wang E, he was summoned as a clerk of the Left Three Departments of the Central Secretariat, and after three promotions became a secretary of the Central Secretariat.

entries.zh: 至元十年，用累考及格，授雲南諸路行省都事，佩銀符。
entries.en: In Zhiyuan 10 (1273), having passed the cumulative examinations, he was made chief administrator of the Yunnan regional secretariat and granted a silver tally.
entries.literal: In the tenth year of Zhiyuan, through accumulated examinations passing the standard, he was appointed Chief Administrator of the Yunnan Branch Secretariat for All Circuits, wearing a silver tally.

entries.zh: 久之，升員外郎。
entries.en: After a time he was promoted to vice director.
entries.literal: After some time he was promoted to Vice Director.

entries.zh: 十五年，轉同知廣南西道左右兩江宣撫司事。
entries.en: In year 15 he was transferred to associate commissioner of the pacification commission for the left and right two rivers of western Guangnan.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year he was transferred to serve as Associate Commissioner of the Pacification Commission for the Left and Right Two Rivers of Western Guangnan Circuit.

entries.zh: 明年，除知南陽府。
entries.en: The next year he was appointed prefect of Nanyang.
entries.literal: The following year he was appointed Prefect of Nanyang.

entries.zh: 唐、鄧二屬州為襄陽府所奪，曾按圖經、稽國製以聞，事得復舊。
entries.en: The subordinate prefectures of Tang and Deng had been absorbed by Xiangyang; Ceng checked the gazetteers and national regulations, reported the case, and jurisdiction was restored as before.
entries.literal: The two subordinate prefectures Tang and Deng had been seized by Xiangyang Prefecture; Ceng consulted the gazetteers and examined the national regulations, reported the matter, and the former arrangement was restored.

entries.zh: 南陽在宋末為邊鄙，桑柘未成，而歲賦絲，民甚苦之，曾請折輸布，民便之。
entries.en: At the end of the Song Nanyang had been a border district where mulberry groves were not yet established, yet the annual tax was levied in silk, which greatly burdened the people; Ceng petitioned to substitute cloth, to their relief.
entries.literal: Nanyang at the end of the Song had been a frontier region; mulberry and catalpa were not yet established, yet the annual levy was in silk, and the people suffered greatly; Ceng requested conversion of the tribute to cloth, to the people's convenience.

entries.zh: 賀胜，仁杰子也，字貞卿，一字舉安，小字伯顏，以小字行。
entries.en: He Sheng was a son of He Renjie. His courtesy name was Zhenqing; he also used Ju'an as an alternate courtesy name. His childhood name was Bayan, and he was commonly known by that name.
entries.literal: He Sheng was the son of He Renjie; his courtesy name was Zhenqing, his alternate courtesy name was Ju'an, his childhood name was Bayan, and he was known by his childhood name.

entries.zh: 嘗從許衡學，通經傳大義。
entries.en: He had studied under Xu Heng and gained a thorough understanding of the core meaning of the Classics.
entries.literal: He once studied under Xu Heng and mastered the great principles of the Classics and their commentaries.

entries.zh: 年十六，入宿衛，凝重寡言，世祖甚器重之。
entries.en: At sixteen he joined the imperial bodyguard. Grave and sparing of speech, he won the deep esteem of Kublai Khan.
entries.literal: At age sixteen he entered the imperial guard; he was grave and taciturn, and Shizu greatly valued him.

entries.zh: 大臣有密奏，輒屏左右，獨留勝，許聽之。
entries.en: Whenever a minister brought a confidential report, the emperor would send everyone else away and keep only Sheng, allowing him to hear it.
entries.literal: When ministers made secret memorials, the Emperor would always dismiss those nearby and leave only Sheng, permitting him to listen.

entries.zh: 出則參乘輿，入則侍帷幄，非休沐不得至家。
entries.en: When the emperor went out, he rode in the carriage beside him; when at court, he waited on him in the inner chambers. He could not go home except on his allotted rest days.
entries.literal: When going out he rode in the imperial carriage; when inside he attended in the inner chambers; only on days of rest could he go home.

entries.zh: 至元二十四年，乃顏叛，帝親征，勝直武帳中，雖親王不得輒至。
entries.en: In 1287, when Nayan rebelled, the emperor led the campaign in person. Sheng stayed in the military headquarters throughout, and even princes were not allowed to approach without permission.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Zhiyuan, Nayan rebelled; the Emperor personally went on campaign, and Sheng remained in the military headquarters — even princes were not permitted to enter casually.

entries.zh: 勝傳旨飭諸將，詰旦合戰，還侍帝側，矢交帳前，勝立侍不動。
entries.en: Sheng carried the emperor's orders to the generals. At dawn the armies engaged; when he returned to the emperor's side, arrows were flying before the tent, yet he stood at attendance without flinching.
entries.literal: Sheng transmitted orders to admonish the generals; at dawn they joined battle; returning to attend at the Emperor's side, arrows crossed before the tent, yet Sheng stood in attendance without moving.

entries.zh: 乃顏既敗，帝還都，乘輿夜行，足苦寒，勝解衣，以身溫之。
entries.en: After Nayan's defeat, as the emperor made the night journey back to the capital, his feet grew bitterly cold. Sheng took off his own clothes and warmed them against his body.
entries.literal: After Nayan was defeated, the Emperor returned to the capital; traveling by carriage at night, his feet suffered bitter cold; Sheng removed his clothes and warmed them with his body.

entries.zh: 帝一日獵還，勝參乘，伶人蒙採毳作獅子舞以迎駕，輿象驚，奔逸不可製，勝投身當象前，後至者斷靷縱象，乘輿乃安。
entries.en: Once, returning from a hunt with Sheng in the carriage, entertainers in feathered costumes performed a lion dance to greet the procession. The carriage elephants panicked and ran out of control. Sheng threw himself in front of them; men arriving behind cut the harness traces and freed the elephants, and the imperial carriage was brought to safety.
entries.literal: One day when the Emperor returned from hunting with Sheng riding in the carriage, entertainers wearing feathers dressed as lions danced to welcome the imperial procession; the elephants drawing the carriage were startled and bolted beyond control; Sheng threw himself before the elephants; those who came later cut the traces and released the elephants, and the imperial carriage was secured.

entries.zh: 勝退，創甚，帝親撫之，遣尚醫、尚食視護。
entries.en: When Sheng withdrew, badly wounded, the emperor comforted him in person and sent the chief physicians and provisioners to care for him.
entries.literal: Sheng withdrew, severely wounded; the Emperor personally comforted him and sent the chief physicians and chief provisioners to attend to him.

entries.zh: 拜集賢學士，領太史院事，詔賜一品服。
entries.en: He was appointed Academician of the Hall of Encouraging Literature and put in charge of the Directorate of Astronomy, and by imperial edict was granted first-rank court robes.
entries.literal: He was appointed Academician of the Hall of Encouragement of Literature, put in charge of the Directorate of Astronomy, and by edict granted first-rank robes.

entries.zh: 盧世榮、桑哥秉政，勢焰熏灼，勝父仁傑留守上都，不肯為之下，桑哥欲陰中之，累數十奏，帝皆不聽。
entries.en: Under Lu Shirong and Sangge, who wielded power with intimidating force, Sheng's father Renjie, serving as governor of Shangdu, refused to bow to them. Sangge tried to destroy him in secret, filing dozens of accusations, but the emperor paid no heed.
entries.literal: When Lu Shirong and Sangge held power, their authority blazed fiercely; Sheng's father Renjie, staying behind as governor of Shangdu, refused to submit to them; Sangge wished secretly to ruin him and repeatedly memorialized dozens of times, but the Emperor would not listen.

entries.zh: 初，武宗崩，皇太后在興聖宮，鐵木迭兒為丞相，踰月，仁宗即位，因遂相之。
entries.en: Earlier, when Emperor Wuzong died, the empress dowager was at Xingsheng Palace and Temüder served as chief minister. More than a month later, when Emperor Renzong came to the throne, he retained Temüder as chief minister.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Wuzong died, the Empress Dowager was at Xingsheng Palace; Temüder was chief minister; after more than a month Emperor Renzong ascended the throne and accordingly made him chief minister.

entries.zh: 居兩歲，得罪斥罷，更自結徽政近臣，复再入相，恃勢貪虐，凶穢愈甚，中外切齒，群臣不知所為。
entries.en: After two years he gave offense and was dismissed, then cultivated allies among the close associates of the Office of Imperial Provisions and returned to the chief ministership. Relying on his power, he grew greedier and crueler. Hatred for him spread inside and outside the court, and the ministers were at a loss.
entries.literal: After two years he offended and was dismissed; he then renewed ties with close associates of the Office of Imperial Provisions and re-entered the chief ministership; relying on power he was greedy and cruel, his wickedness grew worse, all within and without gnashed their teeth, and the ministers did not know what to do.

entries.zh: 御史中丞蕭拜住拜中書右丞，又拜平章政事，稍牽制之。
entries.en: The Censor-in-Chief Xiao Baizhu was appointed Right Assistant Administrator of the Secretariat and then Assistant Administrator, and began to check Temüder's conduct.
entries.literal: The Censor-in-Chief Xiao Baizhu was appointed Right Assistant Administrator of the Secretariat, then Assistant Administrator, and somewhat checked him.

entries.zh: 朵兒只自侍御史拜御史中丞，慨然以糾正其罪為己任。
entries.en: Promoted from Investigating Censor to Censor-in-Chief, Duoerzhi resolutely made it his duty to bring Temüder's crimes to justice.
entries.literal: Duoerzhi, from Investigating Censor promoted to Censor-in-Chief, resolutely took correcting his crimes as his own duty.

entries.zh: 上都富民張弼殺人繫獄，鐵木迭兒使大奴脅留守賀伯顏出之，及強以他姦利事，不能得。
entries.en: Zhang Bi, a wealthy man of Shangdu, was imprisoned for murder. Temüder sent his chief slave to intimidate Governor He Bayan into releasing him and also tried to extort other illicit gains, but failed.
entries.literal: Zhang Bi, a wealthy man of Shangdu, was imprisoned for murder; Temüder sent his chief slave to threaten the Governor He Bayan to release him, and also tried to force other illicit profit matters, but could not obtain them.

entries.zh: 一日，坐都堂，盛怒，以官事召留守，將罪之，留守昌言：「大奴所干非法，不敢從，他實無罪。」
entries.en: One day Temüder sat in the chief minister's hall in a rage and summoned the governor on official business, intending to punish him. The governor spoke plainly: "Your chief slave's demands were illegal, and I refused them. In other matters I am guilty of nothing."
entries.literal: One day, sitting in the chief minister's hall in great anger, he summoned the governor on official business intending to punish him; the governor spoke forthrightly: "What the chief slave undertook was illegal — I dared not comply; in other matters I am truly without guilt."

entries.zh: 鐵木迭兒語詘，得解去。
entries.en: Temüder was silenced and let him go.
entries.literal: Temüder's words were defeated, and he was able to leave and be released.

entries.zh: 朵兒只廉得其所受弼贓巨萬萬，大奴猶數千，使御史徐元素按得實，入奏。
entries.en: Through investigation Duoerzhi learned that Temüder had taken bribes from Bi worth tens of millions, and from the chief slave several thousand more. He had Investigating Censor Xu Yuansu establish the facts and memorialized the throne.
entries.literal: Duoerzhi through investigation learned that he had received bribes from Bi worth tens of millions, and from the chief slave still several thousand; he had Investigating Censor Xu Yuansu verify the facts and memorialized.

entries.zh: 而御史亦輦真又發其私罪二十餘事。
entries.en: Meanwhile Investigating Censor Yilinzhen also exposed more than twenty additional private offenses.
entries.literal: Meanwhile Investigating Censor Yilinzhen also exposed more than twenty private crimes.

entries.zh: 帝震怒，有詔逮問，鐵木迭兒逃匿，帝為不御酒數日，以待決獄，盡誅其大奴同惡數人，鐵木迭兒終不能得。
entries.en: The emperor was furious. An edict ordered Temüder arrested and interrogated, but he fled into hiding. For several days the emperor abstained from wine while awaiting the outcome of the case. Several of Temüder's chief slaves and accomplices were executed, but Temüder himself could not be found.
entries.literal: The Emperor was greatly angered; an edict was issued to arrest and interrogate; Temüder fled and hid; the Emperor for several days abstained from wine awaiting the trial's conclusion; all of Temüder's chief slaves and accomplices were executed; Temüder ultimately could not be captured.

entries.zh: 朵兒只持之急，徽政近臣以太后旨，召朵兒隻至宮門，責以違旨意者。
entries.en: As Duoerzhi pressed the case hard, close associates of the Office of Imperial Provisions, acting on the empress dowager's order, summoned him to the palace gate and rebuked him for defying the imperial will.
entries.literal: Duoerzhi pressed the case urgently; close associates of the Office of Imperial Provisions, by the Empress Dowager's order, summoned Duoerzhi to the palace gate and rebuked him for violating the imperial will.

entries.zh: 對曰：「待罪御史，奉行祖宗法，必得罪人，非敢違太后旨也。」
entries.en: He replied, "I am a censor who stands ready to accept punishment. In enforcing the laws of our ancestors I must inevitably give offense. I do not defy the empress dowager's will lightly."
entries.literal: He replied: "Your servant, a censor awaiting punishment, carries out the laws of the ancestors and must inevitably give offense — I do not dare violate the Empress Dowager's will."

entries.zh: 帝仁孝，恐誠出太后意，不忍重傷咈之，但罷其相位，而遷朵兒只為集賢學士。
entries.en: The emperor, filial by nature, feared that the empress dowager truly meant it and could not bear to wound her deeply. He merely removed Temüder from the chief ministership and transferred Duoerzhi to Academician of the Hall of Encouraging Literature.
entries.literal: The Emperor was filial and benevolent; fearing it truly came from the Empress Dowager's will, he could not bear to deeply wound her feelings, but only removed Temüder from the chief ministership and transferred Duoerzhi to Academician of the Hall of Encouragement of Literature.

entries.zh: 帝猶數以台事問之，對曰：「非臣職事，臣不敢與聞。
entries.en: The emperor still repeatedly asked him about Censorate affairs. He replied, "That is no longer my duty, and I dare not involve myself.
entries.literal: The Emperor still repeatedly asked him about Censorate affairs; he replied: "It is not within your servant's duties; your servant does not dare to hear of them.

entries.zh: 所念者，鐵木迭兒雖去君側，反得為東宮師傅，在太子左右，恐售其姦，則禍有不可勝言者。」
entries.en: What troubles me is that although Temüder has left your side, he has become tutor in the Eastern Palace and stands at the heir apparent's elbow. I fear he will work his treachery there, and the harm will be beyond telling."
entries.literal: What concerns me is that although Temüder has left the Emperor's side, he has instead become tutor to the Eastern Palace, at the Heir Apparent's side — I fear he will sell his treachery, and then disaster will be beyond words."

entries.zh: 初，開平人張弼，家富。
entries.en: Earlier, there was a wealthy man named Zhang Bi of Kaiping.
entries.literal: Earlier, Zhang Bi of Kaiping was a wealthy man.

entries.zh: 弼死，其奴索錢民家，弗得，毆負錢者至死。
entries.en: After Bi's death, his slave went to a commoner's home to collect a debt. When the man could not pay, the slave beat him to death.
entries.literal: After Bi died, his slave went to a commoner's household to collect a debt; failing to obtain it, he beat the debtor to death.

entries.zh: 有治其獄者，教奴引弼子，並下之獄。
entries.en: The official handling the case coached the slave to implicate Bi's son, and both were imprisoned.
entries.literal: The magistrate handling the case instructed the slave to implicate Bi's son, and both were put in prison.

entries.zh: 丞相鐵木迭兒受其賂六萬緡，終不為直。
entries.en: Chief Minister Temüder accepted a bribe of sixty thousand strings of cash and ultimately failed to see justice done.
entries.literal: Chief Minister Temüder received a bribe of sixty thousand strings of cash and ultimately did not render justice.

entries.zh: 勝素惡鐵木迭兒貪暴，居同巷，不與往來。
entries.en: Sheng had long despised Temüder for his greed and cruelty. Though they lived on the same lane, Sheng refused any contact with him.
entries.literal: Sheng had long detested Temüder's greed and brutality; though they lived in the same lane, he had no dealings with him.

entries.zh: 聞弼事，以語御史中丞楊朵兒只。
entries.en: When he learned of the Bi case, he brought it to the Censor-in-Chief Yang Duoerzhi.
entries.literal: Hearing of Bi's case, he told it to the Censor-in-Chief Yang Duoerzhi.

entries.zh: 楊朵兒只以語監察御史玉龍帖木兒、徐元素。
entries.en: Yang Duoerzhi in turn informed the Investigating Censors Yulong Temür and Xu Yuansu.
entries.literal: Yang Duoerzhi told the Investigating Censors Yulong Temür and Xu Yuansu.

entries.zh: 遂劾奏丞相，逮治其左右，得所賂事實以聞。
entries.en: They then memorialized against the chief minister, arrested and interrogated his associates, established the facts of the bribery, and reported them to the throne.
entries.literal: They accordingly memorialized accusing the chief minister, arrested and tried his attendants, obtained proof of the bribery, and reported it.

entries.zh: 帝亦素惡鐵木迭兒，欲誅之。
entries.en: The emperor had likewise long hated Temüder and wished to put him to death.
entries.literal: The Emperor also had long detested Temüder and wished to execute him.

entries.zh: 鐵木迭兒走匿太后宮中，太后為言，僅奪其印綬而罷之。
entries.en: Temüder fled and hid in the empress dowager's palace. She pleaded for him, and he was merely stripped of rank and dismissed.
entries.literal: Temüder fled and hid in the Empress Dowager's palace; the Empress Dowager interceded for him, and he was merely stripped of his seal and sash and dismissed.

entries.zh: 及英宗即位，在諒暗中，鐵木迭兒遂復出據相位，乃執楊朵兒隻及中書平章政事蕭拜住，同日戮於市。
entries.en: When Emperor Yingzong came to the throne, Temüder reappeared during the mourning period and reclaimed the chief ministership. He then had Yang Duoerzhi and Assistant Administrator Xiao Baizhu arrested and executed in the market on the same day.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yingzong ascended the throne, during the mourning period Temüder re-emerged and seized the chief ministership; he then arrested Yang Duoerzhi and the Assistant Administrator Xiao Baizhu and executed them in the market on the same day.

entries.zh: 且復誣勝乘賜車迎詔，不敬，並殺之。
entries.en: He also framed Sheng on the charge of disrespect for failing to receive an edict properly while riding in the granted carriage, and had him killed too.
entries.literal: He further falsely accused Sheng of receiving an imperial edict in the granted carriage without due respect, and had him killed as well.

entries.zh: 勝死之日，百姓爭持紙錢，哭於屍傍甚哀。
entries.en: On the day Sheng died, common people crowded forward with paper money to mourn him, weeping beside his body in deep grief.
entries.literal: On the day Sheng died, common people vied to hold paper money and wept beside his corpse with great grief.

entries.zh: 泰定初，詔雪其冤，贈推忠宣力保德功臣、太傅、開府儀同三司、上柱國，追封秦國公，諡惠愍。
entries.en: Early in the Taiding reign, an edict cleared his wrongful conviction and posthumously granted him the titles of Merit for Extending Loyalty, Proclaiming Merit, and Preserving Virtue, Grand Preceptor, Grand Preceptor with Honored Ceremony Equal to the Three Dukes, and Senior Pillar of State. He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Qin with the posthumous name Huimin.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Taiding reign, an edict cleared his unjust conviction and posthumously granted him the title of Merit for Extending Loyalty, Proclaiming Merit, and Preserving Virtue, Grand Preceptor, Grand Preceptor with Honored Ceremony Equaling the Three Dukes, Senior Pillar of State, posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Qin, with the posthumous name Huimin.

entries.zh: 至正三年，加贈推忠亮節同德翊戴功臣、太師、開府儀同三司、上柱國，追封涇陽王，改諡忠宣。
entries.en: In 1343 he was further granted the titles of Merit for Extending Loyalty with Bright Integrity, Sharing Virtue and Supporting the Throne, Grand Preceptor, Grand Preceptor with Honored Ceremony Equal to the Three Dukes, and Senior Pillar of State. He was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Jingyang, and his posthumous name was changed to Zhongxuan.
entries.literal: In the third year of Zhizheng he was additionally granted the title of Merit for Extending Loyalty with Bright Integrity, Sharing Virtue and Supporting the Throne, Grand Preceptor, Grand Preceptor with Honored Ceremony Equaling the Three Dukes, Senior Pillar of State, posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Jingyang, and his posthumous name was changed to Zhongxuan.

entries.zh: 至元二十八年，桑哥敗，罷尚書省，政歸中書。
entries.en: In 1291, Sangge fell from power, the Secretariat was abolished, and governance reverted to the Central Secretariat.
entries.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of Zhiyuan, Sangge fell; the Secretariat was abolished, and government returned to the Central Secretariat.

entries.zh: 帝問誰可相者，胜對曰：「天下公論，皆屬完澤。」
entries.en: When the emperor asked who should serve as chief minister, Sheng replied, "By general consensus throughout the empire, Wanzhe is the choice."
entries.literal: The Emperor asked who could serve as chief minister; Sheng replied: "By public consensus throughout the realm, all agree on Wanzhe."

entries.zh: 遂相完澤，而以勝參知政事。
entries.en: Wanzhe was duly appointed chief minister, and Sheng was made Assistant Administrator of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: Wanzhe was accordingly made chief minister, and Sheng was made Assistant Administrator of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 三十年，僉樞密院事，遷大都護。
entries.en: In 1293 he was appointed to the Bureau of Military Affairs and promoted to Defender of the Great Capital.
entries.literal: In the thirtieth year he was appointed to the Bureau of Military Affairs and transferred to be Defender of the Great Capital.

entries.zh: 大德九年，勝父仁傑請老，以勝代為上都留守，兼本路都總管、開平府尹、虎賁親軍都指揮使。
entries.en: In 1305, when Sheng's father Renjie retired, Sheng succeeded him as Governor of Shangdu, simultaneously serving as Chief Administrator of the circuit, Magistrate of Kaiping Prefecture, and Commander-in-Chief of the Tiger Guard.
entries.literal: In the ninth year of Dade, Sheng's father Renjie requested retirement; Sheng was appointed in his place as Governor of Shangdu, concurrently Chief Administrator of the Circuit, Magistrate of Kaiping Prefecture, and Commander-in-Chief of the Tiger Guard.

entries.zh: 既至，通商賈，抑豪縱，出納有法，裁量有度，供億不匱，民賴以安。
entries.en: Once in office, he encouraged trade, checked the powerful, and restrained the lawless. He kept accounts properly, exercised measured judgment in supplies, and never let provisions run short. The people lived in security under his rule.
entries.literal: Once he arrived, he facilitated commerce, checked the powerful and restrained the unruly, kept receipts and disbursements by rule, measured with restraint, supplies were never exhausted, and the people relied on him for security.

entries.zh: 諸權貴子弟奴隸有暴橫驕縱者，悉繩以法。
entries.en: Any sons or slaves of the powerful who were violent or arrogant were brought to justice.
entries.literal: Among the sons and slaves of the powerful and noble, those who were violent, arrogant, and unrestrained were all punished by law.

entries.zh: 至大三年，進光祿大夫、左丞相，行上都留守，兼本路總管府達魯花赤。
entries.en: In 1310 he was promoted to Grand Master for Glorious Blessing and Left Chief Minister, serving as Acting Governor of Shangdu and concurrently as Darughachi of the circuit administration.
entries.literal: In the third year of Zhida he was promoted to Grand Master for Glorious Blessing and Left Chief Minister, serving as Acting Governor of Shangdu and concurrently Darughachi of the Circuit Administration.

entries.zh: 尋又加開府儀同三司、上柱國。
entries.en: Shortly thereafter he was further granted the title of Grand Preceptor with Honored Ceremony Equal to the Three Dukes and Senior Pillar of State.
entries.literal: Soon after he was additionally granted the title of Grand Preceptor with Honored Ceremony Equaling the Three Dukes and Senior Pillar of State.

entries.zh: 奉聖州民高氏，籍虎賁，以貲雄鄉里，身死子幼。
entries.en: A Gao family of Fengshengzhou, enrolled in the Tiger Guard, dominated their locality through wealth. The husband died leaving a young son.
entries.literal: A certain Gao family of Fengshengzhou, registered in the Tiger Guard, dominated the countryside by wealth; the father died and the son was young.

entries.zh: 有達官利其財，使其部曲強娶高氏婦。
entries.en: A high official coveted their property and had his retainers forcibly take the widowed Gao woman in marriage.
entries.literal: A high official coveted their wealth and had his retainers forcibly marry the widow of the Gao family.

entries.zh: 勝白帝，斥之，高氏以全。
entries.en: Sheng reported the matter to the emperor, who condemned the official, and the Gao family was spared.
entries.literal: Sheng reported to the Emperor, who repudiated the official, and the Gao family was preserved intact.

entries.zh: 歲大饑，輒發倉廩賑民，乃自劾待罪。
entries.en: During a year of severe famine, he opened the granaries to feed the people, then filed a confession accepting punishment.
entries.literal: In a year of great famine he promptly opened the granaries to relieve the people, then submitted a self-accusation to await punishment.

entries.zh: 帝報曰：「祖宗以上都之民付卿父子，欲安之也。
entries.en: The emperor replied, "Our ancestors entrusted the people of Shangdu to you and your father so that they might live in peace.
entries.literal: The Emperor replied: "Our ancestors entrusted the people of Shangdu to you and your father, desiring their security.

entries.zh: 卿能如此，朕復何憂，卿其視事。」
entries.en: If you act in this way, what have I to worry about? Carry on in your office."
entries.literal: That you are able to act thus, what further worry have I? Continue in your duties."

entries.zh: 民德之，為立祠上都西門外。
entries.en: Grateful, the people erected a shrine to him outside the west gate of Shangdu.
entries.literal: The people were grateful to him and erected a shrine for him outside the west gate of Shangdu.

entries.zh: 帝聞之，復命工寫其像以賜，俾傳示子孫。
entries.en: Learning of this, the emperor ordered a painted portrait made and conferred it on him, so that it could be passed down to his descendants.
entries.literal: When the Emperor heard of it, he again ordered artists to paint his portrait and bestow it, so that it might be transmitted to posterity.

entries.zh: 未幾，以足疾請老，不許，曰：「卿臥護足矣。」
entries.en: Not long after, he asked to retire on account of a foot ailment. The request was denied. The emperor said, "It is enough that you guard the city from your bed."
entries.literal: Before long, citing foot ailment, he requested retirement; it was refused, and the Emperor said: "It is enough that you protect the city from your bed."

entries.zh: 賜小車，出入禁闥。
entries.en: He was granted a small carriage and allowed to pass in and out of the Forbidden Gates.
entries.literal: A small carriage was granted him, and he was permitted to enter and leave the Forbidden Gates.

entries.zh: 子二人：惟一，開府儀同三司、中書左丞相、監修國史；
entries.en: He had two sons: Weiyi, Grand Preceptor with Honored Ceremony Equal to the Three Dukes, Left Chief Minister of the Secretariat, and Supervisor of the National History;
entries.literal: He had two sons: Weiyi, Grand Preceptor with Honored Ceremony Equaling the Three Dukes, Left Chief Minister of the Secretariat, and Supervisor of the National History;

entries.zh: 惟賢，太中大夫、同知上都留守司事。
entries.en: and Weixian, Grand Master for Discussion of Governance and Vice Administrator of the Shangdu Governorate.
entries.literal: Weixian, Grand Master for Discussion of Governance, and Vice Administrator of the Shangdu Governorate.

entries.zh: 孫均，太子詹事。
entries.en: His grandson Jun served as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: His grandson Jun was Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 又明年，為中統元年，世祖即位，阿里不哥反，遣使召主將渾都海。
entries.en: Another year passed—the first year of the Zhongtong reign. Kublai ascended the throne, Ariq Böke rose in revolt, and dispatched envoys to summon the commander Hunduhai.
entries.literal: The year after that was the first year of Zhongtong; the Shizu Emperor took the throne, Ariq Böke rebelled, and sent envoys to summon the commander-in-chief Hunduhai.

entries.zh: 鑄說渾都海等入朝，皆不從，則棄其妻子，挺身來歸。
entries.en: Zhu urged Hunduhai and his officers to present themselves at court, but they refused. He then left his wife and children behind and came alone to Kublai's side.
entries.literal: Zhu urged Hunduhai and the others to come to court; none obeyed, so he abandoned his wife and children and came alone to submit.

entries.zh: 既而渾都海知鑄去，怒，遣百騎追之不及。
entries.en: When Hunduhai learned of Zhu's defection, he flew into a rage and sent a hundred horsemen in pursuit, but they failed to catch him.
entries.literal: When Hunduhai learned that Zhu had gone, he was angry and sent a hundred horsemen in pursuit but could not overtake him.

entries.zh: 乃使百人監視希亮母子，迫脅使從行，自靈武過應吉里城，至西涼甘州。
entries.en: He then placed a hundred men to guard Xiliang and his mother, forcing them to march with the army from Lingwu through Yingjili to Ganzhou in the Hexi corridor.
entries.literal: He then set a hundred men to watch Xiliang and his mother, coercing them to march along, from Lingwu past Yingjili City to Ganzhou in the Hexi corridor (Xiliang).

entries.zh: 阿里不哥遣大將阿藍答兒自和林帥師至焉支山，希亮見之。
entries.en: Ariq Böke sent his general Alamdar from Karakorum with an army to Yanzhi Mountain, where Xiliang was brought before him.
entries.literal: Ariq Böke sent the great general Alamdar from Karakorum leading troops to Yanzhi Mountain; Xiliang met him.

entries.zh: 阿藍答兒問：「而父安在？」
entries.en: Alamdar asked, "Where is your father?"
entries.literal: Alamdar asked: "Where is your father?"

entries.zh: 希亮曰：「不知，與吾父同任事者宜知之。」
entries.en: Xiliang replied, "I do not know. Those who served with my father should know."
entries.literal: Xiliang said: "I do not know; those who served together with my father ought to know."

entries.zh: 渾都海怒，詬曰：「我焉得知之，其父今亡命東見皇帝矣！」
entries.en: Hunduhai flew into a rage and shouted, "How should I know? His father has already fled east to pay court to the emperor!"
entries.literal: Hunduhai grew angry and reviled him, saying: "How should I know? His father has now fled east to see the Emperor!"

entries.zh: 希亮曰：「若然，則何謂不知！」
entries.en: Xiliang said, "If that is so, what do you mean by saying you do not know!"
entries.literal: Xiliang said: "If that is so, then what do you mean by not knowing!"

entries.zh: 阿藍答兒熟視渾都海曰：「此言深有意焉。」
entries.en: Alamdar fixed a long look on Hunduhai and said, "Those words carry a pointed meaning."
entries.literal: Alamdar stared intently at Hunduhai and said: "These words carry deep meaning."

entries.zh: 詰希亮甚急。
entries.en: He pressed Xiliang hard for an answer.
entries.literal: He pressed Xiliang very sharply.

entries.zh: 希亮曰：「使吾知之，亦從而去，安得獨留！」
entries.en: Xiliang said, "If I had known, I would have gone with him. How could I have been left behind alone!"
entries.literal: Xiliang said: "Had I known, I would have gone away with him too—how could I alone have been left behind!"

entries.zh: 阿藍答兒以為實，免其監蒞。
entries.en: Alamdar accepted this as the truth and lifted the close guard over him.
entries.literal: Alamdar took this as truth and released him from close guard.

entries.zh: 既而阿藍答兒、渾都海為大兵所殺，其殘卒北走，眾推哈剌不花為帥。
entries.en: Before long Alamdar and Hunduhai were killed by Kublai's main forces. The survivors fled north and chose Hala Buqa as their leader.
entries.literal: Before long Alamdar and Hunduhai were killed by the main army; their remnant troops fled north, and the multitude made Hala Buqa commander.

entries.zh: 希亮潛匿甘州北黑水東沙陀中。
entries.en: Xiliang went into hiding in the Shatuo country east of the Black River, north of Ganzhou.
entries.literal: Xiliang hid secretly in the Shatuo east of the Black Water north of Ganzhou.

entries.zh: 殿兵已過十餘里，有尋馬者適至，老婢漏言，眾奄至，驅至肅州。
entries.en: The rearguard had already marched more than ten li on when men sent to find horses arrived. An old servant woman let the secret slip, the pursuers fell upon them at once, and they were driven to Suzhou.
entries.literal: The rearguard had already passed more than ten li when horse-seekers happened to arrive; an old maidservant let slip word, the crowd suddenly came upon them, and they were driven to Suzhou.

entries.zh: 哈剌不花與鑄有婚姻之好，又哈剌不花在蜀時，嘗疾病，鑄召醫視之,遺以酒食， 因釋希亮縛，謂曰：「我受恩於汝父，此圖報之秋也。」
entries.en: Hala Buqa was related to Zhu by marriage, and when Hala Buqa had fallen ill in Shu, Zhu had sent a physician and provisions. He now released Xiliang from his bonds and said, "Your father once showed me kindness. This is my chance to repay it."
entries.literal: Hala Buqa and Zhu were joined by marriage ties; moreover, when Hala Buqa had been ill in Shu, Zhu summoned a physician to treat him and sent wine and food. He therefore released Xiliang's bonds and said: "I received favor from your father—this is the season to repay it."

entries.zh: 及抵沙州北川，希亮與兄弟徒步負任，不火食者數日。
entries.en: When they reached the northern reaches of Shazhou, Xiliang and his brothers went on foot carrying their loads and went several days without a cooked meal.
entries.literal: When they reached the north stream of Shazhou, Xiliang and his brothers went on foot carrying burdens and went several days without cooked food.

entries.zh: 是冬，涉雪逾天山，至北庭都護府。
entries.en: That winter they crossed the snow-covered Tianshan and reached Beiting.
entries.literal: That winter they crossed snow over the Tianshan and reached the Protectorate General of Beiting.

entries.zh: 二年，至昌八里城。
entries.en: In the second year they came to Changbali.
entries.literal: In the second year they reached Changbali City.

entries.zh: 夏，逾馬納思河，抵葉密里城，乃定宗潛邸湯沐之邑也。
entries.en: In summer they crossed the Manasi River and reached Yemili, the appanage town of Güyük before he became khan.
entries.literal: In summer they crossed the Manasi River and reached Yemili City—the fief granted for the maintenance of Emperor Dingzong when he was heir apparent.

entries.zh: 時六皇后之妹主後位，與宗王火忽皆欲東覲。
entries.en: The Sixth Empress Dowager's younger sister then held the empress's position, and she and Prince Huohu both wished to travel east to pay homage at court.
entries.literal: At that time the younger sister of the Sixth Empress Dowager held the rear palace, and she and the prince Huohu both wished to go east to pay court.

entries.zh: 希亮母密知其事，攜希亮入見，已而事不果。
entries.en: Xiliang's mother learned of the plan in secret and brought Xiliang to an audience, but in the end nothing came of it.
entries.literal: Xiliang's mother secretly learned of the matter, took Xiliang in to see her, but in the end the plan did not succeed.

entries.zh: 冬，至於火孛之地。
entries.en: In winter they reached the Huobie region.
entries.literal: In winter they reached the land of Huobie.

entries.zh: 三年，定宗幼子大名王閔其不能歸，遺以幣帛鞍馬，乃從大名王至忽只兒之地。
entries.en: In the third year Prince Daming, Güyük's youngest son, took pity on his inability to return home and gave him silks, saddles, and horses. Xiliang then followed the prince to Huzhier.
entries.literal: In the third year, Daming Wang, the young son of Emperor Dingzong, pitying that he could not return home, gave him silks, cloth, saddles, and horses; he then followed Daming Wang to the land of Huzhier.

entries.zh: 會宗王阿魯忽至，誅阿里不哥所用鎮守之人唆羅海，欲附世祖。
entries.en: Prince Alughu then arrived, executed Suoluohai, Ariq Böke's garrison commander, and declared his intent to join Kublai.
entries.literal: When Prince Alughu arrived, he executed Suoluohai, whom Ariq Böke had placed in charge of the garrison, wishing to attach himself to the Shizu Emperor.

entries.zh: 復從大名王及阿魯忽二王還至葉密里城。
entries.en: He again followed Princes Daming and Alughu back to Yemili.
entries.literal: He again followed the two princes Daming Wang and Alughu back to Yemili City.

entries.zh: 王遺以耳環，其二珠大如榛，實價直千金，欲穿其耳使帶之。
entries.en: The prince gave him earrings set with pearls as large as hazelnuts, worth a thousand in gold, and wanted to pierce his ears so he could wear them.
entries.literal: The prince gave him ear ornaments; their two pearls were as large as hazelnuts and truly worth a thousand in gold; he wished to pierce his ears to wear them.

entries.zh: 希亮辭曰：「不敢因是以傷父母之遺體也。
entries.en: Xiliang declined, saying, "I dare not mutilate the body my parents gave me for the sake of such a gift.
entries.literal: Xiliang declined, saying: "I dare not for this reason injure the body my parents bequeathed to me.

entries.zh: 且無功受賞，於禮尤不可。」
entries.en: Besides, to accept reward without having earned it is utterly contrary to propriety."
entries.literal: Moreover, to receive reward without merit is especially impermissible in ritual propriety."

entries.zh: 王又解金束帶遺之，且曰：「系此，於遺體宜無傷。」
entries.en: The prince then took off a gold belt and gave it to him, saying, "Wear this—it should not harm the body your parents gave you."
entries.literal: The prince again undid a gold girdle and gave it to him, saying: "Fasten this—it ought not to harm the body bequeathed to you."

entries.zh: 五月，又為阿里不哥兵所驅，西行千五百里，至孛劣撒里之地。
entries.en: In the fifth month Ariq Böke's troops drove them west again for fifteen hundred li to Beliesali.
entries.literal: In the fifth month they were again driven by Ariq Böke's troops, traveling west fifteen hundred li to the land of Beliesali.

entries.zh: 六月，又西至換扎孫之地。
entries.en: In the sixth month they pressed on west to Huanzhasun.
entries.literal: In the sixth month they went west again to the land of Huanzhasun.

entries.zh: 又從至不剌城。
entries.en: They continued on to Bula.
entries.literal: They again followed on to Bula City.

entries.zh: 又西行六百里，至徹徹里澤剌之山，后妃輜重皆留於此，希亮母及兄弟亦在焉。
entries.en: They marched another six hundred li west to Checheli Zelazhi Mountain, where the empresses' baggage was left behind, along with Xiliang's mother and brothers.
entries.literal: They again went west six hundred li to Checheli Zelazhi Mountain; the empresses' and consorts' baggage trains were all left here, and Xiliang's mother and brothers were also there.

entries.zh: 希亮單騎從行二百餘里，至出布兒城。
entries.en: Xiliang rode on alone for more than two hundred li to Chubuer.
entries.literal: Xiliang alone on horseback followed the march more than two hundred li to Chubuer City.

entries.zh: 又百里，至也裡虔城，而哈剌不花之兵奄至，希亮又從二王興師，還至不剌城，與哈剌不花戰，敗之，盡殲其眾。
entries.en: Another hundred li brought them to Yeliqian, where Hala Buqa's army fell upon them. Xiliang again followed the two princes as they raised troops, marched back to Bula, routed Hala Buqa, and destroyed his force to the last man.
entries.literal: Another hundred li on, they reached Yeliqian City, when Hala Buqa's troops suddenly arrived; Xiliang again followed the two princes in raising troops, returned to Bula City, fought Hala Buqa, defeated him, and annihilated his entire force.

entries.zh: 二王乃函其頭，遣使報捷。
entries.en: The two princes sent his head in a box to court with a dispatch announcing their victory.
entries.literal: The two princes then boxed his head and sent envoys to report the victory.

entries.zh: 十月，至於亦思寬之地。
entries.en: In the tenth month they reached Yisikuan.
entries.literal: In the tenth month they reached the land of Yisikuan.

entries.zh: 四年，至可失哈里城。
entries.en: In the fourth year they came to Keshihali.
entries.literal: In the fourth year they reached Keshihali City.

entries.zh: 四月，阿里不哥兵復至，希亮又從征，至渾八升城。
entries.en: In the fourth month Ariq Böke's army returned, and Xiliang again joined the campaign as far as Hunbasheng.
entries.literal: In the fourth month Ariq Böke's troops came again; Xiliang again followed the campaign to Hunbasheng City.

entries.zh: 時希亮母從後避暑於阿體八升山。
entries.en: Meanwhile his mother followed in the rear to spend the summer at Atibasheng Mountain.
entries.literal: At that time Xiliang's mother followed in the rear to escape the heat at Atibasheng Mountain.

entries.zh: 先是，鑄嘗言於世祖：「臣之妻子皆在北邊。」
entries.en: Earlier Zhu had told Kublai, "My wife and children are all still in the north."
entries.literal: Earlier Zhu had once said to the Shizu Emperor: "Your servant's wife and children are all in the north."

entries.zh: 至是，世祖遣不華出至二王所，因以璽書召希亮，馳驛赴闕。
entries.en: At this point Kublai sent Buhua to the two princes with an imperial summons for Xiliang, who raced by relay post to court.
entries.literal: Now the Shizu Emperor sent Buhua out to where the two princes were and, by imperial sealed letter, summoned Xiliang, who sped by post relay to court.

entries.zh: 六月，由苦先城至哈剌火州，出伊州，涉大漠以還。
entries.en: In the sixth month he went from Kuxian to Karahuozhou, passed through Yizhou, and crossed the great desert on his way home.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, from Kuxian City to Karahuozhou, out through Yizhou, crossing the great desert to return.

entries.zh: 八月，入覲世祖於上都之大安閣，備陳邊事，及羈旅困苦之狀。
entries.en: In the eighth month he had audience with Kublai in the Da'an Pavilion at Shangdu, where he gave a full account of frontier affairs and the hardships of his years in exile.
entries.literal: In the eighth month he entered audience with the Shizu Emperor at the Da'an Pavilion in Shangdu, fully setting forth border affairs and the hardships of his long exile.

entries.zh: 世祖憐之，賜鈔千錠、金帶一、幣帛三十，命為速古兒赤、必阇赤。
entries.en: Kublai took pity on him, gave him a thousand ingots of paper money, a gold belt, and thirty lengths of silk, and appointed him suguerchi and bichechi.
entries.literal: The Shizu Emperor pitied him, bestowed a thousand ingots of paper money, one gold belt, and thirty pieces of silks and cloth, and appointed him suguerchi and bichechi.

entries.zh: 至元八年，授奉訓大夫、符寶郎。
entries.en: In the eighth year of the Zhiyuan reign he was made Fengxun dafu and keeper of the imperial seals.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Zhiyuan he was appointed Fengxun dafu and Fubao lang.

entries.zh: 十二年，既平宋，世祖命希亮問諸降將，日本可伐否。
entries.en: In the twelfth year, after the conquest of the Song, Kublai had Xiliang poll the surrendered generals on whether Japan could be invaded.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year, after the Song had been pacified, the Shizu Emperor ordered Xiliang to ask the surrendered generals whether Japan could be attacked.

entries.zh: 夏貴、呂文煥、範文虎、陳奕等皆云可伐。
entries.en: Xia Gui, Lü Wenhuan, Fan Wenhu, Chen Yi, and the others all said it could be done.
entries.literal: Xia Gui, Lü Wenhuan, Fan Wenhu, Chen Yi, and the others all said it could be attacked.

entries.zh: 希亮奏曰：「宋與遼、金攻戰且三百年，干戈甫定，人得息肩，俟數年，興師未晚。」
entries.en: Xiliang submitted, "The Song had been at war with Liao and Jin for nearly three hundred years. Arms have only just been stilled and the people have barely caught their breath. Wait a few years before launching another campaign—it will not be too late."
entries.literal: Xiliang memorialized: "The Song fought with Liao and Jin for nearly three hundred years; arms have only just been laid down and the people have barely rested their shoulders—wait a few years, and raising troops will not be too late."

entries.zh: 世祖然之。
entries.en: The emperor agreed.
entries.literal: The Shizu Emperor approved this.

entries.zh: 十三年，太府監令史盧贄言於監官：「各路所貢布長三丈，唯平陽加一丈，諸怯薛歹以故爭取平陽布。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year the Taifu Directorate clerk Lu Zan told his supervisor, "Each circuit's tribute cloth is three zhang long, but Pingyang's is one zhang longer, so the imperial guards all scramble for Pingyang cloth.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year, the Taifu Directorate clerk Lu Zan said to the supervising official: "The cloth presented from each circuit is three zhang in length; only Pingyang adds one zhang, and for this reason the keshik all vie for Pingyang cloth.

entries.zh: 苟截其長者，與他郡等，則無所爭，而以其所截者為髹漆宮殿器皿之用，甚便。」
entries.en: If we trim the extra length to match the other prefectures, there will be no dispute, and the trimmed pieces can be used for lacquered palace furnishings—a very practical arrangement."
entries.literal: If the excess length were cut off to make it equal to other prefectures, there would be no contention, and the cut portions could be used for lacquered palace vessels—very convenient."

entries.zh: 監官從之。
entries.en: The supervisor agreed.
entries.literal: The supervising official followed this advice.

entries.zh: 適左右以其事聞，帝以詰監官，監官倉皇莫知所以對，歸罪於贄，帝命斬之。
entries.en: Attendants soon reported the matter to the emperor, who questioned the supervisor. Flustered and unable to answer, the supervisor blamed Zan, and the emperor ordered Zan executed.
entries.literal: Just then attendants reported the matter to the emperor, who questioned the supervising official; the official, in panic, did not know how to answer and shifted blame onto Zan; the emperor ordered Zan beheaded.

entries.zh: 希亮遇諸塗，贄以寃告。
entries.en: Xiliang met him on the road, and Zan pleaded that he had been wronged.
entries.literal: Xiliang met him on the road, and Zan pleaded his wrongful case.

entries.zh: 希亮命少緩，具以實入奏。
entries.en: Xiliang asked that execution be delayed and submitted a full report of what had actually happened.
entries.literal: Xiliang ordered a brief delay and entered a full report of the facts.

entries.zh: 有旨令董文用讞之。
entries.en: The emperor ordered Dong Wenyong to review the case.
entries.literal: An edict ordered Dong Wenyong to judge the case.

entries.zh: 竟釋贄，而召御史大夫塔察兒等讓之曰：「此事言官當言而不言，向微禿忽思，不誤誅此人耶！」
entries.en: Zan was released in the end, and the censor-in-chief Tachar and others were summoned and rebuked: "The remonstrating officials should have spoken up on this. Had it not been for Tuhusi, would we not have executed an innocent man!"
entries.literal: In the end Zan was released, and the Censor-in-Chief Tachar and others were summoned and rebuked: "On this matter the remonstrating officials ought to have spoken but did not—had it not been for Tuhusi, would this man not have been wrongly executed!"

entries.zh: 十四年，轉嘉議大夫、禮部尚書，尋遷吏部尚書。
entries.en: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to Jiayi dafu and Minister of Rites, and soon afterward became Minister of Personnel.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to Jiayi dafu and Minister of Rites, and soon moved to Minister of Personnel.

entries.zh: 帝駐蹕察納兒台之地，希亮至，奏對畢，董文用問大都近事。
entries.en: While the emperor was encamped at Chanaiertai, Xiliang had audience and afterward Dong Wenyong asked him about recent affairs in the capital.
entries.literal: The emperor was encamped at Chanaiertai; when Xiliang arrived and finished his audience, Dong Wenyong asked about recent affairs in Dadu.

entries.zh: 希亮曰：「囹圄多囚耳。」
entries.en: Xiliang said, "The prisons are simply overcrowded."
entries.literal: Xiliang said: "The prisons hold many prisoners, that is all."

entries.zh: 世祖方欹枕而臥，忽寤，問其故。
entries.en: Kublai had been dozing on his pillow; he started awake and asked why.
entries.literal: The Shizu Emperor had been reclining on his pillow; he suddenly woke and asked the reason.

entries.zh: 希亮奏曰：「近奉旨：漢人盜鈔六文者殺。
entries.en: Xiliang said, "A recent order decreed that any Han person who steals six cash in paper money is to be executed.
entries.literal: Xiliang memorialized: "Recently there was an order: Han people who steal six cash in paper money are to be killed.

entries.zh: 以是囚多。」
entries.en: That is why the prisons are so full."
entries.literal: Because of this the prisoners are many."

entries.zh: 帝驚問：「孰傳此語？」
entries.en: The emperor asked in alarm, "Who spread such an order?"
entries.literal: The emperor asked in alarm: "Who transmitted these words?"

entries.zh: 省臣曰：「此旨實脫兒察所傳。」
entries.en: The Secretariat officials said, "It was Toercha who transmitted it."
entries.literal: The provincial officials said: "This order was in fact transmitted by Toercha."

entries.zh: 脫兒察曰：「陛下在南坡，以語蒙古兒童。」
entries.en: Toercha said, "Your Majesty said this in jest to some Mongol boys at Nanpo."
entries.literal: Toercha said: "Your Majesty, at Nanpo, spoke thus to Mongol children."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「前言戲耳，曷嘗著為令式？」
entries.en: The emperor said, "That was only a joke. When did I ever turn it into law?"
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Those words were spoken in jest—when were they ever made a formal statute?"

entries.zh: 乃罪脫兒察。
entries.en: He then punished Toercha.
entries.literal: He then punished Toercha.

entries.zh: 希亮因奏曰：「令既出矣，必明其錯誤，以安民心。」
entries.en: Xiliang then said, "Since the order has already gone out, its error must be publicly acknowledged to set the people's minds at ease."
entries.literal: Xiliang then memorialized: "Since the order has already gone forth, its error must be made clear to reassure the people's hearts."

entries.zh: 帝善其言，即命希亮至大都，諭旨中書。
entries.en: The emperor approved and immediately sent Xiliang to Dadu to announce the correction to the Central Secretariat.
entries.literal: The emperor approved his words and at once ordered Xiliang to go to Dadu and proclaim the imperial intent to the Central Secretariat.

entries.zh: 十七年，希亮以跋涉西土，足病痿攣，謝事而去，退居惣陽者二十餘年。
entries.en: In the seventeenth year, worn out by his years in the western regions, Xiliang developed crippling paralysis in his legs. He resigned and lived in retirement at Zongyang for more than twenty years.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year, because of his long journey through the western lands Xiliang's feet were afflicted with flaccid paralysis; he resigned his office and withdrew, living in retirement at Zongyang for more than twenty years.

entries.zh: 至大二年，武宗訪求先朝舊臣，特除翰林學士承旨、資善大夫，尋改授翰林學士承旨、知制誥兼修國史。
entries.en: In the second year of the Zhida reign, Emperor Wuzong sought out veterans of the previous reign and specially appointed him Hanlin expositor-in-chief and Zishan dafu; he was soon given the additional posts of drafter of edicts and compiler of the national history.
entries.literal: In the second year of Zhida, Emperor Wuzong sought out old ministers of the previous reign and specially appointed him Hanlin Academician Expositor-in-Chief and Zishan dafu; soon he was reassigned Hanlin Academician Expositor-in-Chief, Drafter of Imperial Edicts, and Compiler of National History.

entries.zh: 希亮以職在史官，乃類次世祖嘉言善行以進，英宗取其書，置禁中。
entries.en: In his capacity as historiographer, Xiliang compiled Kublai's memorable sayings and worthy deeds and presented them to the throne. Emperor Yingzong took the work into the inner palace.
entries.literal: Because his office was among the historiographers, Xiliang arranged by category the Shizu Emperor's fine words and good deeds and presented them; Emperor Yingzong took the book and placed it in the inner palace.

entries.zh: 久之，閒居京師，四方之士多從之遊。
entries.en: After a time he lived quietly in the capital, and scholars from all directions came to study with him.
entries.literal: After a long while he lived at leisure in the capital, and scholars from all quarters often associated with him.

entries.zh: 泰定四年卒，年八十一。
entries.en: He died in the fourth year of the Taiding reign, at the age of eighty-one.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Taiding he died, aged eighty-one.

entries.zh: 世延天資秀發，喜讀書，究心儒者體用之學。
entries.en: Shiyan was gifted by nature, loved books, and devoted himself to the Confucian study of principle and practical application.
entries.literal: Shiyan's natural endowment was brilliant; he delighted in reading books and devoted himself to the Confucian learning of substance and function.

entries.zh: 弱冠，世祖召見，俾入樞密院御史臺肄習官政。
entries.en: At his coming of age, Kublai received him in audience and had him train in government at the Bureau of Military Affairs and the Censorate.
entries.literal: At the capping age the Shizu Emperor summoned him for audience and had him enter the Bureau of Military Affairs and the Censorate to practice official administration.

entries.zh: 至元二十一年，授承事郎、雲南諸路提刑按察司判官，時年二十有四。
entries.en: In the twenty-first year of the Zhiyuan reign he was made Chengshi lang and judge of the Yunnan Circuit Surveillance Commission, at the age of twenty-four.
entries.literal: In the twenty-first year of Zhiyuan he was appointed Chengshi lang and investigating censorial judge of the Yunnan Circuit Surveillance Commission, aged twenty-four.

entries.zh: 烏蒙蠻酋叛，世延會省臣以軍討之，蠻兵大潰，即請降。
entries.en: When the Wumeng chieftain rebelled, Shiyan joined the provincial officials in a punitive campaign, routed the tribesmen, and accepted their immediate surrender.
entries.literal: The Wumeng tribal chief rebelled; Shiyan joined the provincial officials in leading troops to attack; the tribal troops were utterly routed and at once sought surrender.

entries.zh: 二十六年，擢監察御史，與同列五人劾丞相桑哥不法。
entries.en: In the twenty-sixth year he was promoted to investigating censor and, together with five colleagues, impeached Chancellor Sangge for misconduct.
entries.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was promoted investigating censor and, with five colleagues, impeached the chancellor Sangge for unlawful conduct.

entries.zh: 中丞趙國輔，桑哥黨也，抑不以聞，更以告桑哥。
entries.en: Vice censor-in-chief Zhao Guofu, a partisan of Sangge, suppressed the memorial and reported it to Sangge instead.
entries.literal: The vice censor-in-chief Zhao Guofu, a member of Sangge's faction, suppressed the report and instead informed Sangge.

entries.zh: 於是五人者悉為其所擠，而世延獨倖免。
entries.en: All five of his colleagues were driven from office, but Shiyan alone escaped retribution.
entries.literal: Thereupon all five men were squeezed out by him, while Shiyan alone escaped harm.

entries.zh: 奉旨按平陽郡監也先忽都贓巨萬，鞫左司郎中董仲威殺人獄，皆明允。
entries.en: By imperial order he investigated the Pingyang supervisor Yexian Hudu for embezzling a fortune and tried Left Department Director Dong Zhongwei for murder; in both cases his judgments were fair and clear.
entries.literal: By imperial order he investigated Supervisor Yexian Hudu of Pingyang Commandery for embezzling tens of thousands, and tried the case of Left Department Director Dong Zhongwei for murder—all were clearly adjudicated.

entries.zh: 二十九年，轉奉議大夫，出僉江南湖北道肅政廉訪司事。
entries.en: In the twenty-ninth year he was made Fengyi dafu and dispatched as administrator of the Jiangnan Hubei Circuit Surveillance Commission.
entries.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was transferred to Fengyi dafu and sent out as administrator of the Jiangnan Hubei Circuit Surveillance Commission.

entries.zh: 敦儒學，立義倉，撤淫祠，修澧陽縣壞堤，嚴常、澧掠賣良民之禁，部內晏然。
entries.en: He encouraged Confucian learning, founded charity granaries, abolished illicit shrines, repaired the broken dike at Liyang, and strictly forbade the kidnapping and sale of commoners in Chang and Li; his jurisdiction became notably peaceful.
entries.literal: He promoted Confucian learning, established charity granaries, abolished illicit shrines, repaired the broken dike at Liyang County, and strictly forbade the abduction and sale of commoners in Chang and Li—within his jurisdiction all was tranquil.

entries.zh: 元貞元年，除江南行御史臺都事，丁內艱，不赴。
entries.en: In the first year of the Yuanzhen reign he was appointed secretary of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate but declined the post to observe mourning for his mother.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yuanzhen he was appointed secretary of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate but, mourning his mother, did not take up the post.

entries.zh: 大德元年，复除前官。
entries.en: In the first year of the Dade reign he was reappointed to the same office.
entries.literal: In the first year of Dade he was again appointed to his former office.

entries.zh: 三年，移中臺都事，俄改中書左司都事。
entries.en: In the third year he became secretary of the Central Branch Censorate and soon afterward secretary of the Left Department of the Central Secretariat.
entries.literal: In the third year he was moved to secretary of the Central Branch Censorate and soon changed to secretary of the Left Department of the Central Secretariat.

entries.zh: 臺臣奏，仍為都事中臺。
entries.en: The censors memorialized, and he was returned to his post as secretary of the Central Branch Censorate.
entries.literal: The censorial officials memorialized, and he again became secretary of the Central Branch Censorate.

entries.zh: 六年，由山東肅政廉訪副使改江南行臺治書侍御史。
entries.en: In the sixth year he was transferred from vice commissioner of the Shandong Surveillance Commission to supervising secretary of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate.
entries.literal: In the sixth year, from vice commissioner of the Shandong Surveillance Commission he was changed to supervising secretary of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate.

entries.zh: 十年，除安西路總管。
entries.en: In the tenth year he was appointed prefect of Anxi Circuit.
entries.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed prefect of Anxi Circuit.

entries.zh: 安西，故京兆省臺所治，號稱會府，前政壅滯者三千牘。
entries.en: Anxi had formerly been administered by the Jingzhao provincial government and censorate and was known as a metropolitan prefecture; three thousand cases had piled up under the previous administration.
entries.literal: Anxi was formerly governed by the Jingzhao provincial government and censorate, styled a metropolitan prefecture; the previous administration had a backlog of three thousand cases.

entries.zh: 世延既至，不三月，剖決殆盡。
entries.en: Within three months of Shiyan's arrival he had disposed of nearly all of them.
entries.literal: After Shiyan arrived, within three months he had judged them nearly all.

entries.zh: 陝民飢，省臺議請於朝賑之，世延曰：「救荒如救火，願先發廩以賑，朝廷設不允，世延當傾家財若身以償。」
entries.en: When famine struck Shaan, the provincial authorities debated asking the court for relief. Shiyan said, "Famine relief is like fighting a fire. Let me open the granaries at once; if the court refuses, I will repay the cost from my own estate and person."
entries.literal: The people of Shaan were starving; the provincial government and censorate discussed requesting relief from court; Shiyan said: "Famine relief is like putting out a fire—I wish to open the granaries first to relieve the people; if the court should not approve, Shiyan will repay with his family wealth and even his person."

entries.zh: 省臺從之，所活者眾。
entries.en: The provincial authorities agreed, and a great many lives were saved.
entries.literal: The provincial government and censorate followed this, and those who were saved were many.

entries.zh: 耶律希亮
entries.en: Yelu Xiliang
entries.literal: Yelu Xiliang

entries.zh: 汪澤民，字叔志，徽之婺源州人，宋端明殿學士藻之七世孫也。
entries.en: Wang Zemin (Shuzhi), a native of Wuyuan in Huizhou, was the seventh-generation descendant of the Song academician Wang Zao of the Duanming Hall.
entries.literal: Wang Zemin, courtesy name Shuzhi, was a native of Wuyuan Prefecture in Huizhou, seventh-generation descendant of the Song Duanming Hall Academician Wang Zao.

entries.zh: 少警悟，家貧力學，既長，遂通諸經。
entries.en: Clever and keen from boyhood, he studied hard despite poverty; in adulthood he had mastered the full canon of classics.
entries.literal: In youth he was quick and perceptive; though his family was poor he studied with tireless effort, and once grown he mastered all the Classics.

entries.zh: 延祐初，以《春秋》中鄉貢，上禮部，下第，授寧國路儒學正。
entries.en: Early in Yanyou he qualified in the provincial examinations on the Annals, then failed at the Ministry of Rites; he was appointed Confucian instructor in Ningguo Circuit.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Yanyou reign he passed the provincial examination in the Spring and Autumn Annals, went up to the Ministry of Rites, failed the metropolitan examination, and was appointed Instructor at the Confucian school of Ningguo Circuit.

entries.zh: 五年，遂登進士第，授承事郎、同知岳州路平江州事。
entries.en: Five years later he passed the jinshi examinations and was made gentleman for affairs and vice prefect of Pingjiang under Yuezhou Circuit.
entries.literal: In the fifth year he attained the jinshi degree and was appointed Gentleman for Affairs and Vice Commissioner of the administrative affairs of Pingjiang Prefecture under Yuezhou Circuit.

entries.zh: 以母年八十，上書願奪所授官一等或二等，得近地以便養，不允。
entries.en: His mother being eighty, he petitioned to be demoted one or two ranks in exchange for a nearby post to care for her; the court refused.
entries.literal: Because his mother was eighty, he submitted a memorial asking to be reduced one or two ranks from the office just granted so that he might receive a nearby post to support her; this was not approved.

entries.zh: 南歸奉母之官。
entries.en: He returned south and brought his mother to his office.
entries.literal: He returned south and took her with him to his post.

entries.zh: 州民李氏，以貲雄，其弟死，妻誓不他適，兄利其財，嗾族人誣婦以姦事。
entries.en: A wealthy townsman surnamed Li had a brother who died; the widow swore she would not remarry, but the elder brother coveted her estate and goaded kinsmen to accuse her of adultery.
entries.literal: A commoner of the prefecture surnamed Li, wealthy and overbearing, had a younger brother who died; the wife vowed not to marry another, but the elder brother coveted her property and incited clansmen to accuse the widow of adultery.

entries.zh: 獄成而澤民至，察知其枉，為直之。
entries.en: By the time the case was closed and Zemin arrived, he saw the injustice and reversed the verdict.
entries.literal: The case had been concluded when Zemin arrived; perceiving the injustice, he set the matter right.

entries.zh: 會朝廷徵江南包銀，府檄澤民分辨，民不擾而事​​集。
entries.en: When the court imposed the bao-yin levy on Jiangnan, the prefecture put Zemin in charge of apportioning it; the people were not troubled and the collection was completed.
entries.literal: Just then the court levied the bao-yin silver tax in Jiangnan; the prefecture ordered Zemin to apportion it, and the people were not disturbed while the task was completed.

entries.zh: 尋遷南安路總管府推官。
entries.en: He was soon promoted to reviewing official in the Nan'an chief administrator's office.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to be Reviewing Official in the Chief Administrator's office of Nan'an Circuit.

entries.zh: 鎮守萬戶朵兒赤，持官府短長，郡吏王甲，毆傷屬縣長官，訴郡，同僚畏朵兒赤，托故不視事，澤民獨捕甲，系之獄。
entries.en: The garrison commander Dorbet knew every weakness in the local administration. When a prefectural clerk named Wang Jia assaulted a county magistrate, colleagues feared Dorbet and declined the case; Zemin alone arrested Wang Jia and jailed him.
entries.literal: The garrison commander Wanhu Dorbet, who knew the failings of the government offices, had a prefectural clerk Wang Jia who beat and injured a magistrate of a subordinate county; the case was brought to the prefecture, but colleagues feared Dorbet and excused themselves from hearing it; Zemin alone arrested Jia and imprisoned him.

entries.zh: 朵兒赤賂巡按御史，受甲家人訴，欲出之，澤民正色與辨，御史沮怍，夜竟去，乃卒罪王甲。
entries.en: Dorbet bribed the touring censor, who took the family's petition and tried to free Jia. Zemin argued him down face to face; the censor withdrew in shame that night, and Wang Jia was convicted at last.
entries.literal: Dorbet bribed the touring surveillance censor, who accepted the petition from Jia's family and wished to release him; Zemin spoke sternly in argument, the censor was shamed and abashed and fled in the night, and Jia was finally punished.

entries.zh: 潮州府判官錢珍，以姦淫事殺推官梁楫，事連廣東廉訪副使劉珍，坐系者二百餘人，省府官凡六委官鞫問，皆顧忌淹延弗能白，复檄澤民讞之，獄立具，人服其明。
entries.en: Chaozhou's prefectural judge Qian Zhen murdered reviewing official Liang Ji in a scandal of adultery that implicated Guangdong's deputy surveillance commissioner Liu Zhen. More than two hundred people were held; six rounds of officials sent to investigate shrank back from the powerful interests involved. When Zemin was ordered to try the case, he concluded it at once, and all marveled at his discernment.
entries.literal: Qian Zhen, prefectural judge of Chaozhou, had killed the reviewing official Liang Ji over an affair of debauchery; the case implicated Liu Zhen, deputy surveillance commissioner of Guangdong; more than two hundred persons were detained; six times provincial and circuit officials commissioned officers to interrogate, but all hesitated and delayed and could not clear the matter; again they ordered Zemin to report on the case, and the dossier was immediately complete—men admired his clarity.

entries.zh: 遷信州路總管府推官。
entries.en: He was transferred to reviewing official in the Xinzhou chief administrator's office.
entries.literal: He was transferred to be Reviewing Official in the Chief Administrator's office of Xinzhou Circuit.

entries.zh: 丁母憂，服除，授平江路總管府推官。
entries.en: After mourning his mother, he was appointed reviewing official in the Pingjiang chief administrator's office.
entries.literal: Upon his mother's death he entered mourning; when the mourning period ended he was appointed Reviewing Official in the Chief Administrator's office of Pingjiang Circuit.

entries.zh: 有僧淨廣，與他僧有憾，久絕往來，一日，邀廣飲，廣弟子急欲得師財，且苦其棰楚，潛往它僧所殺之。
entries.en: A monk named Jingguang had a feud with another monk and had long ceased visiting him. One day he invited Guang to drink. Guang's disciple, eager for his master's property and weary of his beatings, stole to the rival monk's quarters and killed him.
entries.literal: There was a monk Jingguang who bore a grudge against another monk and had long ceased visiting him; one day he invited Guang to drink; Guang's disciple, eager to seize his master's property and weary of his beatings, secretly went to the other monk's place and killed him.

entries.zh: 明日訴官，它僧不勝考掠，乃誣服，三經審錄，詞無異，結案等報。
entries.en: The next day the crime was reported. The other monk broke under torture and confessed falsely. After three examinations his story never changed, and the case was closed pending execution.
entries.literal: The next day the case was reported to the authorities; the other monk could not endure the torture and falsely confessed; through three rounds of examination the testimony did not change, and the case was closed awaiting execution.

entries.zh: 澤民取行凶刀視之，刀上有鐵工姓名，召工問之，乃其弟子刀也，一訊吐實，即械之而出他僧，人驚以為神。
entries.en: Zemin inspected the murder weapon and found an ironsmith's mark on the blade. The smith identified it as the disciple's knife. One interrogation brought out the truth; Zemin shackled the disciple and freed the other monk, and people called it uncanny.
entries.literal: Zemin examined the murder weapon and found on the blade the name of the ironsmith; he summoned the smith and learned it was the disciple's knife; on one interrogation the truth came out, and he immediately shackled the disciple and released the other monk—people were astonished and called it divine.

entries.zh: 調濟寧路兗州知州，孔子後衍聖公襲封職三品，澤民建議，以謂宜升其品秩，以示褒崇宣聖之意，廷議從之。
entries.en: Transferred to prefect of Yanzhou in Jining Circuit, he proposed raising the hereditary third-rank title of Confucius's descendant the Yanshenggong to show the court's reverence for the Sage; the proposal was adopted.
entries.literal: He was transferred to be Prefect of Yanzhou in Jining Circuit; the Yanshenggong, lineal descendant of Confucius, held a third-rank hereditary enfeoffment; Zemin proposed that his rank should be raised to show honor to the Sage, and the court deliberation approved.

entries.zh: 呂思誠
entries.en: Lu Sicheng
entries.literal: Lu Sicheng

entries.zh: 至正中，毛貴陷益都，英時年九十有六，乃謂其子弘曰：「我世受國恩，美官厚祿，備嘗享之。
entries.en: During the Zhizheng era Mao Gui seized Yidu. Ying was ninety-six and said to his son Hong, "Our family has enjoyed the dynasty's favor for generations—rank, stipends, and honors in full measure.
entries.literal: In the Zhizheng period Mao Gui took Yidu; Ying was then ninety-six years old, and he said to his son Hong, "Our family for generations has received the state's grace—fine offices and rich stipends—we have fully tasted and enjoyed them.

entries.zh: 今老矣，縱不能事戎馬以報天子，尚忍食異姓之粟以求生乎！」
entries.en: I am old now. Even if I can no longer ride to war for the emperor, how could I eat the rebels' grain to stay alive?"
entries.literal: Now I am old; even if I cannot serve in arms to repay the Son of Heaven, how could I still bear to eat the grain of another surname to seek life!"

entries.zh: 水漿不入口者數日，遂卒。
entries.en: He refused food and drink for days and died.
entries.literal: For several days he took neither water nor broth into his mouth, and thus died.

entries.zh: 毛貴聞之，使具棺衾以葬。
entries.en: Hearing of his death, Mao Gui provided a coffin and shroud for the burial.
entries.literal: When Mao Gui heard of it he had coffin and shroud prepared for burial.

entries.zh: 將斂，舉其屍不動，焚香祝曰：「公子弘請公歸葬先塋。」
entries.en: As they prepared the body it could not be lifted; incense was burned and a prayer offered: "Your son Hong begs you to return to the family grave."
entries.literal: When they were about to enshroud him they lifted his corpse but it did not move; burning incense they prayed, "Your son Hong asks you, sir, to return for burial in the ancestral grave."

entries.zh: 祝畢，屍遂起，觀者莫不驚異。
entries.en: When the prayer ended the body rose, to the astonishment of all who watched.
entries.literal: When the prayer was finished the corpse then rose; none of the onlookers failed to be startled and amazed.

entries.zh: 山東宣慰使普顏不花及憲司請卹典於朝，有曰：「不食寇粟，餓死芹泉，有夷、齊之風，為臣之清者也。」
entries.en: Pacification Commissioner Puyan Buhua and the surveillance officials petitioned for state mourning honors; someone said, "He would not eat rebel grain and starved at Qinquan—conduct worthy of Bo Yi and Shu Qi, the purity of a loyal minister."
entries.literal: The Shandong Pacification Commissioner Puyan Buhua and the surveillance commission requested mourning rites from the court; someone said, "Refusing to eat the bandits' grain, starving to death at Qinquan—he had the air of Bo Yi and Shu Qi; this is the purity of a minister."

entries.zh: 芹泉，谷名，英所居也。
entries.en: Qinquan was the valley where Ying had lived.
entries.literal: Qinquan was the name of a valley where Ying dwelt.

entries.zh: 宜孫性警敏，嗜學問，於書務博覽，而長於詩歌。
entries.en: Yisun was quick-witted and devoted to learning; he read widely and excelled at poetry.
entries.literal: Yisun was by nature alert and keen, fond of learning; in books he aimed at broad reading and excelled in poetry.

entries.zh: 嘗借嫡弟厚孫廕，襲父職，為沿海上副萬戶，守處州。
entries.en: He once used his younger brother Housun's hereditary privilege to inherit his father's post as vice commander of the Coastal Guard and garrison Chuzhou.
entries.literal: He once borrowed his younger brother Housun's hereditary privilege, inherited his father's post, became vice commander of the Coastal Guard, and guarded Chuzhou.

entries.zh: 及弟長，即讓其職還之，退居台州。
entries.en: When his brother came of age he returned the post and retired to Taizhou.
entries.literal: When his brother came of age he immediately yielded the post back to him and withdrew to reside in Taizhou.

entries.zh: 至正十一年，方國珍起海上，江浙行省檄宜孫守溫州，宜孫即起任其事。
entries.en: In Zhizheng 11 (1351), when Fang Guozhen rose at sea, the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat ordered Yisun to defend Wenzhou, and he took up the post at once.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhizheng Fang Guozhen rose on the sea; the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat issued an order to Yisun to guard Wenzhou, and Yisun immediately rose to take up the task.

entries.zh: 其年閩寇犯處州，复檄宜孫以兵平之。
entries.en: Later that year Fujian rebels attacked Chuzhou, and he was ordered to suppress them.
entries.literal: That same year Fujian bandits invaded Chuzhou; again an order was issued to Yisun to pacify them with troops.

entries.zh: 以功升浙東宣慰副使，分府於台州。
entries.en: For his service he was promoted to vice commissioner of the Zhedong Pacification Commission, with headquarters at Taizhou.
entries.literal: For his merit he was promoted to vice commissioner of the Zhedong Pacification Commission, with his separate office at Taizhou.

entries.zh: 頃之，處之屬縣山寇並起，宜孫復奉省檄往討之。
entries.en: Soon mountain rebels rose throughout Chu's subordinate counties, and Yisun was again dispatched to suppress them.
entries.literal: Before long mountain bandits rose together in the subordinate counties of Chu; Yisun again received a Branch Secretariat order to campaign against them.

entries.zh: 至則築處州城，為御敵計。
entries.en: On arrival he fortified Chuzhou city to prepare for enemy attack.
entries.literal: Upon arrival he built the walls of Chuzhou as a plan to resist the enemy.

entries.zh: 十七年，江浙行省左丞相達識鐵睦邇承製升宜孫行樞密院判官，總制處州，分院治於處。
entries.en: In the seventeenth year (1357) Left Chief Minister Dash Timur appointed Yisun vice director of the Branch Bureau of Military Affairs with overall command of Chuzhou and a separate headquarters there.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat left chief minister Dash Timur, by provisional appointment, promoted Yisun to vice director of the Branch Bureau of Military Affairs, placing him in overall control of Chuzhou, with a separate office administering from Chu.

entries.zh: 又以江浙儒學副提舉劉基為其院經歷，蕭山縣尹蘇友龍為照磨，而宜孫又辟郡人胡深、葉琛、章溢參謀其軍事。
entries.en: He also appointed the Jiang-Zhe vice promoter of Confucian learning Liu Ji as director of his bureau and the Xiaoshan magistrate Su Youlong as registrar, while Yisun further recruited the men of his prefecture Hu Shen, Ye Chen, and Zhang Yi to advise on military affairs.
entries.literal: He also appointed the Jiang-Zhe vice promoter of Confucian learning Liu Ji as director of his bureau, the Xiaoshan magistrate Su Youlong as registrar, while Yisun further recruited the men of his prefecture Hu Shen, Ye Chen, and Zhang Yi to advise on military affairs.

entries.zh: 處為郡，山谷聯絡，盜賊憑據險阻，輒竊發，不易平治。
entries.en: Chuzhou's rugged terrain gave bandits natural strongholds from which they struck repeatedly, making pacification difficult.
entries.literal: Chu was a prefecture where valleys and mountains linked together; bandits relied on perilous terrain and repeatedly rose in secret raids, not easy to pacify.

entries.zh: 宜孫用基等謀，或搗以兵，或誘以計，未幾，皆殲殄無遺類。
entries.en: Yisun used the plans of Ji and the others—sometimes striking with troops, sometimes luring with stratagems—and before long all were wiped out without survivors.
entries.literal: Yisun used the plans of Ji and the others—sometimes striking with troops, sometimes luring with stratagems—and before long all were exterminated without survivors.

entries.zh: 尋升同僉行樞密院事。
entries.en: He was soon promoted to associate director of the Branch Bureau of Military Affairs.
entries.literal: Soon he was promoted to associate director of the Branch Bureau of Military Affairs.

entries.zh: 當是之時，天下已多故，所在守將各自為計相保守。
entries.en: By then the realm was in turmoil, and local commanders everywhere looked chiefly to their own survival.
entries.literal: At that time the empire already had many troubles; garrison commanders everywhere each made plans to preserve themselves.

entries.zh: 於是浙東則宜孫在處州，邁里古思在紹興為稱首。
entries.en: In eastern Zhejiang, Yisun at Chuzhou and Mailigusi at Shaoxing were the leading defenders.
entries.literal: Thus in Zhedong, Yisun was at Chuzhou and Mailigusi at Shaoxing as the foremost figures.

entries.zh: 董摶霄弟昂霄
entries.en: Dong Tuanxiao and His Younger Brother Angxiao
entries.literal: Dong Tuanxiao; his younger brother Angxiao

entries.zh: 自古國家上有寬厚之君，然後為政者得以盡其愛民之術，而良吏興焉。
entries.en: From antiquity, whenever a realm was governed by a magnanimous sovereign, those who wielded power could devote themselves wholeheartedly to caring for the people, and worthy officials would flourish.
entries.literal: Since ancient times, when a state had a lenient and generous ruler above, those who held office could then fully apply their techniques of loving the people, and virtuous officials would arise.

entries.zh: 班固有曰：「漢興，與民休息，凡事簡易，禁罔疏闊，以寬厚清靜為天下先，故文、景以後，循吏輩出。」
