entries.en: Ban Gu once wrote: "At the founding of the Han, the dynasty let the people recover from war; government was kept simple, legal restraints were broad and sparse, and the realm was led by clemency and restraint. After Emperors Wen and Jing, capable and honest administrators appeared in succession."
entries.literal: Ban Gu once said: "When the Han rose, it rested with the people; all affairs were kept simple, prohibitions were loose and wide, and taking leniency and quiet as the first principle for the realm—therefore after Wen and Jing, honest officials emerged one after another."

entries.zh: 其言蓋識當時之治體矣。
entries.en: In those lines he had grasped the essence of how the early dynasty was governed.
entries.literal: His words indeed recognized the governing principles of that time.

entries.zh: 元初風氣質實，與漢初相似。
entries.en: The ethos of the early Yuan was plain and robust, much like that of the early Han.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Yuan, the prevailing spirit was simple and solid, similar to the early Han.

entries.zh: 世祖始立各道勸農使，又用五事課守令，以勸農係其銜。
entries.en: Kublai first appointed agricultural commissioners in each circuit and evaluated prefects and county magistrates on five criteria, tying promotion to the encouragement of farming.
entries.literal: Shizu first established agricultural commissioners for each circuit, and also used five matters to assess prefects and magistrates, linking the promotion of agriculture to their official title.

entries.zh: 故當是時，良吏班班可見，亦寬厚之效也。
entries.en: In that period, admirable officials were everywhere to be seen, another fruit of the dynasty's generous policies.
entries.literal: Therefore at that time, virtuous officials could be seen clearly one after another—it was also the effect of leniency.

entries.zh: 然自中世以後，循良之​​政，史氏缺於紀載。
entries.en: From the mid-dynasty onward, however, the histories largely omit accounts of honest and capable governance.
entries.literal: Yet from the middle period onward, honest and good governance was lacking in the historians' records.

entries.zh: 今據其事蹟之可取者，作《良吏傳》。
entries.en: Here I have gathered the deeds of such men that are worth preserving and written this "Biographies of Virtuous Officials."
entries.literal: Now, on the basis of their deeds that are worth taking, I compose the "Biographies of Virtuous Officials."

entries.zh: 甲寅，世祖還自大理，澄進見，留籓府，凡遣使，必以澄偕，而以其弟山阜為交城令。
entries.en: In jiayin, when Kublai returned from Dali, Cheng was summoned to audience and retained at the princely headquarters. Whenever an envoy was dispatched, Cheng went along, while his younger brother Shanfu was appointed magistrate of Jiaocheng.
entries.literal: In jiayin, when Shizu returned from Dali, Cheng came forward for audience, was retained at the princely headquarters, and whenever envoys were dispatched Cheng always accompanied them, while his younger brother Shanfu was made magistrate of Jiaocheng.

entries.zh: 時世祖以皇弟開籓京兆，總天下兵。
entries.en: At that time Kublai, as the emperor's younger brother, had established his princely domain at Jingzhao and commanded all armies under heaven.
entries.literal: At the time Shizu, as the emperor's younger brother, established his fief at Jingzhao and commanded all armies under heaven.

entries.zh: 歲丁巳，有間之者，憲宗疑之，遂解兵柄。
entries.en: In the dingsi year, slanderers turned Möngke against him, and he was stripped of his military command.
entries.literal: In the year dingsi, there were those who sowed discord; Möngke came to suspect him, and he was stripped of military authority.

entries.zh: 遣阿藍答兒往京兆，大集官吏，置計局百四十二條以考核之，罪者甚眾，世祖每遣左丞闊闊與澄周旋其間，以彌縫其缺，及親入朝，事乃釋。
entries.en: Möngke dispatched Ala'er to Jingzhao, summoned a mass gathering of officials, and imposed one hundred and forty-two audit regulations by which to investigate them; a great many were found guilty. Kublai repeatedly sent Left Assistant Minister Kökö and Cheng to intervene and mitigate the damage, and only when he went to court in person was the matter finally settled.
entries.literal: Ala'er was sent to Jingzhao, officials were gathered in great numbers, one hundred and forty-two accounting regulations were established for auditing them, and very many were found guilty; Shizu repeatedly sent Left Assistant Minister Kökö together with Cheng to deal with matters between them, to patch the gaps, and only when he personally went to court was the affair finally resolved.

entries.zh: 中統元年，世祖即位，擢懷孟路總管，俄賜金符，換金虎符。
entries.en: In the first year of the Zhongtong era, when Kublai ascended the throne, Cheng was promoted to administrator of Huaimeng Circuit; he was soon granted a gold tally, then a gold tiger tally.
entries.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong, when Shizu took the throne, Cheng was promoted to administrator of Huaimeng Circuit; soon he was granted a gold tally, then exchanged for a gold tiger tally.

entries.zh: 歲旱，令民鑿唐溫渠，引沁水以溉田，民用不飢。
entries.en: During a drought year, he had the people dig the Tangwen Canal to channel the Qin River for irrigation, and the populace did not go hungry.
entries.literal: In a year of drought, he had the people dig the Tangwen Canal to draw the Qin River to irrigate the fields, and the populace did not go hungry.

entries.zh: 教之種植，地無遺利。
entries.en: He taught the people farming and cultivation until no land was left uncultivated.
entries.literal: He taught them planting and cultivation, and not an acre of land went unused.

entries.zh: 至元二年，遷河南路總管，改平灤路總管。
entries.en: In the second year of Zhiyuan, he was transferred to administrator of Henan Circuit, then reassigned to administrator of Pingluan Circuit.
entries.literal: In the second year of Zhiyuan, he was transferred to administrator of Henan Circuit, then changed to administrator of Pingluan Circuit.

entries.zh: 七年，入為司農少卿，俄出為京兆總管。
entries.en: In the seventh year he was recalled to the capital as Vice Minister of Agriculture, but soon returned to the provinces as administrator of Jingzhao.
entries.literal: In the seventh year, he entered the capital as Vice Minister of Agriculture, and soon went out again as administrator of Jingzhao.

entries.zh: 居一年，改陝西四川道提刑按察使，建言：「不孝有三，無後為大。
entries.en: After a year he was made Intendant of the Judicial Investigation Commission for Shaanxi-Sichuan Circuit and submitted a memorial: "There are three forms of unfilial conduct, but the greatest is having no posterity.
entries.literal: After one year, he was changed to Intendant of the Judicial Investigation Commission for Shaanxi-Sichuan Circuit, and submitted a memorial: "There are three forms of unfilial conduct, but the greatest is having no posterity.

entries.zh: 宜令民年四十無子聽取妾，以為宗祀計。」
entries.en: Men who reach forty without a son should be permitted to take a concubine, for the sake of continuing the ancestral line."
entries.literal: It is fitting to allow men who at forty have no son to take a concubine, for the sake of continuing ancestral rites."

entries.zh: 朝廷從之，遂著為令。
entries.en: The court accepted his proposal, and it was promulgated as law.
entries.literal: The court accepted this, and it was established as a regulation.

entries.zh: 四川僉省嚴忠范守成都，為宋將昝萬壽所敗，退保子城，世祖命澄代之。
entries.en: Yen Zhongfan, Vice Secretariat Commissioner of Sichuan, had been defending Chengdu when he was defeated by the Song general Zan Wanshou and forced to retreat into the inner citadel. Kublai ordered Cheng to replace him.
entries.literal: Yen Zhongfan, Vice Secretariat Commissioner of Sichuan, defended Chengdu but was defeated by the Song general Zan Wanshou; he retreated to defend the inner city; Shizu ordered Cheng to replace him.

entries.zh: 至則葬暴骸，修焚室，賑饑貧，集逋亡，民心稍安。
entries.en: Upon arrival he buried the unburied dead, rebuilt burned homes, relieved the hungry and destitute, and gathered fugitives back to their homes; the people's hearts gradually settled.
entries.literal: When he arrived, he buried the unburied dead, repaired burned dwellings, relieved the hungry and destitute, gathered fugitives, and popular sentiment gradually settled.

entries.zh: 會西南夷羅羅斯內附，帝以撫新國宜擇文武全才，遂以澄為副都元帥，同知宣慰使司事。
entries.en: When the Luolosi tribes of the southwest submitted, the emperor judged that pacifying the newly acquired territory required a man of both civil and military talent, and appointed Cheng Deputy Commander-in-Chief and Associate Commissioner of the Pacification Commission.
entries.literal: It happened that the Yi people of Luolosi in the southwest submitted; the emperor considered that pacifying the newly subject territory required selecting a man complete in both civil and military talent, and thus appointed Cheng Deputy Commander-in-Chief and Associate Commissioner of the Pacification Commission.

entries.zh: 比至，以疾卒，年五十八。
entries.en: But before he could take up the post, he died of illness at the age of fifty-eight.
entries.literal: But before he arrived, he died of illness at fifty-eight.

entries.zh: 世祖嘗與太保劉秉忠論一時牧守，秉忠曰：「若邢之張耕，懷之譚澄，何憂不治哉！」
entries.en: Kublai once discussed the governors and prefects of the day with Grand Mentor Liu Bingzhong, who said: "With men like Zhang Geng of Xingzhou and Tan Cheng of Huai prefecture, what worry would there be about good governance!"
entries.literal: Shizu once discussed with Grand Mentor Liu Bingzhong the governors and prefects of the time; Bingzhong said: "If there were more like Zhang Geng of Xing and Tan Cheng of Huai, what worry would there be about good governance!"

entries.zh: 遊顯宣撫大名，嘗為諸路總管求虎符宣麻，澄至中書辭曰：「皇上不識譚澄耶？
entries.en: You Xian, Pacification Commissioner of Daming, had once sought tiger tallies and imperial appointment edicts on behalf of circuit administrators. When Cheng came to the Central Secretariat to decline, he said: "Does His Majesty not already know Tan Cheng?
entries.literal: You Xian, Pacification Commissioner of Daming, once sought tiger tallies and imperial appointment edicts on behalf of circuit administrators; when Cheng came to the Central Secretariat to decline, he said: "Does His Majesty not know Tan Cheng?

entries.zh: 乃為顯所舉！」
entries.en: And yet you would have me promoted on You Xian's recommendation!"
entries.literal: Yet you would have me promoted by You Xian!"

entries.zh: 中書特為去之。
entries.en: The Central Secretariat accordingly struck his name from the list.
entries.literal: The Central Secretariat specially removed his name from the list.

entries.zh: 其介如此。
entries.en: Such was the integrity of the man.
entries.literal: Such was his integrity.

entries.zh: 許楫，字公度，太原忻州人。
entries.en: Xu Ji, styled Gongdu, came from Xinzhou in Taiyuan.
entries.literal: Xu Ji, courtesy name Gongdu, was a native of Xinzhou in Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 幼從元裕學，年十五，以儒生中詞賦選，河東宣撫司又舉楫賢良方正孝廉。
entries.en: As a youth he studied under Yuan Yu. At fifteen he passed the literary composition examination as a Confucian scholar, and the Hedong Pacification Commission also recommended him as a filial and upright candidate of outstanding talent.
entries.literal: As a youth he studied under Yuan Yu; at fifteen he passed the literary composition examination as a scholar; the Hedong Pacification Commission also recommended Ji as a filial and upright candidate of outstanding talent.

entries.zh: 楫至京師，平章王文統命為中書省掾，以不任簿書辭，改知印。
entries.en: When Ji reached the capital, Grand Councillor Wang Wentong appointed him a clerk of the Central Secretariat, but citing his unsuitability for clerical work, he declined and was reassigned as seal-keeper.
entries.literal: When Ji reached the capital, Grand Councillor Wang Wentong appointed him a clerk of the Central Secretariat; citing unfitness for paperwork, he declined and was changed to seal-keeper.

entries.zh: 丞相安童、左丞許衡深器重之。
entries.en: Chancellor An'tong and Left Assistant Minister Xu Heng held him in the highest regard.
entries.literal: Chancellor An'tong and Left Assistant Minister Xu Heng held him in great esteem.

entries.zh: 一日，從省臣立殿下，世祖見其美髯魁偉，問曰：「汝秀才耶？」
entries.en: One day, as he stood with secretariat officials below the palace steps, Kublai noticed his fine beard and imposing stature and asked: "Are you a xiucai?"
entries.literal: One day, standing with the secretariat officials below the steps, Shizu saw his fine beard and imposing stature and asked: "Are you a xiucai?"

entries.zh: 楫頓首曰：「臣學秀才耳，未敢自謂秀才也。」
entries.en: Ji prostrated himself and said: "Your subject is merely a student of the classics—I would not dare call myself a xiucai."
entries.literal: Ji prostrated himself and said: "Your subject is merely a student of the classics—I would not dare call myself a xiucai."

entries.zh: 帝善其對，授中書省架閣庫管勾，兼承發司事。
entries.en: The emperor was pleased with his reply and appointed him registrar of the Central Secretariat archive depot, with concurrent charge of the dispatch office.
entries.literal: The emperor approved of his reply and appointed him registrar of the archive depot of the Central Secretariat, concurrently in charge of the dispatch office.

entries.zh: 未幾，立大司農司，以楫為勸農副使。
entries.en: Before long the Ministry of Agriculture was established, and Ji was appointed Vice Commissioner for Agriculture.
entries.literal: Before long the Ministry of Agriculture was established, and Ji was made Vice Commissioner for Agriculture.

entries.zh: 時商挺為安西王相，遇於途，楫因言：「京兆之西，荒野數千頃，宋、金皆嘗置屯，如募民立屯田，歲可得谷，給王府之需。」
entries.en: At the time Shang Ting was chancellor to the Prince of Anxi. Meeting him on the road, Ji said: "West of Jingzhao lie several thousand qing of wasteland where both Song and Jin once maintained garrison farms. If farmers were recruited to establish military colonies there, the annual harvest could supply the prince's household."
entries.literal: At the time Shang Ting was chancellor to the Prince of Anxi; meeting him on the road, Ji said: "West of Jingzhao lie several thousand qing of wasteland; both Song and Jin once established garrison farms there; if farmers were recruited to establish military colonies, grain could be harvested each year to supply the prince's household."

entries.zh: 挺以其言入奏，從之。
entries.en: Shang Ting reported this proposal to the throne, and it was approved.
entries.literal: Ting reported his words to the throne and it was approved.

entries.zh: 三年，屯成，果獲其利。
entries.en: Three years later the colonies were established and yielded the expected harvest.
entries.literal: Three years later the colonies were established and they indeed reaped the expected profit.

entries.zh: 尋佩金符，為陝西道勸農使。
entries.en: He was soon granted a gold tally and appointed Commissioner for Agriculture of Shaanxi Circuit.
entries.literal: Soon he wore a gold tally as Commissioner for Agriculture of Shaanxi Circuit.

entries.zh: 至元十三年，宋平，帝命平章廉希憲行中書於荊南府，以楫為左右司員外郎。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year of Zhiyuan, after the Song was pacified, the emperor ordered Grand Councillor Lian Xixian to administer the Central Secretariat at Jingnan Prefecture and appointed Ji Outer Assistant in the Left and Right Offices.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhiyuan, when the Song was pacified, the emperor ordered Grand Councillor Lian Xixian to act as Central Secretariat at Jingnan Prefecture, and appointed Ji as Outer Assistant in the Left and Right Offices.

entries.zh: 荊南父老輿金帛求見，楫曰：「汝等已為大元民矣，今置吏以撫字汝輩，奚用金帛以求見！」
entries.en: Elders of Jingnan came bearing gold and silk in carriages to request an audience. Ji said: "You are already subjects of the Great Yuan. Officials have been appointed to care for you—why bring gold and silk to seek an audience!"
entries.literal: Elders of Jingnan brought gold and silk in carriages seeking an audience; Ji said: "You are already subjects of the Great Yuan; officials have now been appointed to care for you—why use gold and silk to seek an audience!"

entries.zh: 明年，擢嶺北湖南提刑按察副使。
entries.en: The following year he was promoted to Vice Intendant of the Judicial Investigation Commission for Lingbei-Hunan.
entries.literal: The following year he was promoted to Vice Intendant of the Judicial Investigation Commission for Lingbei-Hunan.

entries.zh: 武岡富民有毆死出征軍人者，陰以家財之半誘其佃者，代己款伏。
entries.en: A wealthy man of Wugang had beaten a soldier on campaign to death and secretly offered half his family fortune to entice his tenant to confess in his stead.
entries.literal: A wealthy man of Wugang had beaten to death a soldier on campaign; covertly he used half his family wealth to entice his tenant to confess in his place.

entries.zh: 楫審得其情，釋佃者，系富民，人服其明。
entries.en: Ji investigated and uncovered the truth, released the tenant, and imprisoned the wealthy man; the people admired his clear judgment.
entries.literal: Ji examined the facts and grasped the truth; he released the tenant and imprisoned the wealthy man; people admired his clarity of judgment.

entries.zh: 改江西道提刑按察副使，行省命招討郭昂討叛賊董旗，兵士俘掠甚眾，楫詢究得良民六百口，遣還鄉里。
entries.en: Transferred to Vice Intendant of the Judicial Investigation Commission for Jiangxi Circuit. When the Branch Secretariat ordered Pacifier Guo Ang to suppress the rebel bandit Dong Qi, soldiers captured and plundered in great numbers. Ji investigated and found six hundred ordinary people among the captives, whom he sent back to their hometowns.
entries.literal: Transferred to Vice Intendant of the Judicial Investigation Commission for Jiangxi Circuit; the Branch Secretariat ordered Pacifier Guo Ang to suppress the rebel bandit Dong Qi; soldiers captured and plundered in great numbers; Ji investigated and found six hundred ordinary people, whom he sent back to their hometowns.

entries.zh: 段直，字正卿，澤州晉城人。
entries.en: Duan Zhi, courtesy name Zhengqing, was a native of Jincheng in Ze Prefecture.
entries.literal: Duan Zhi, style name Zhengqing, was a man of Jincheng in Ze Prefecture.

entries.zh: 至元十一年，河北、河東、山東盜賊充斥，直聚其鄉黨族屬，結壘自保。
entries.en: In the eleventh year of Zhiyuan (1274), bandits overran Hebei, Hedong, and Shandong; Zhi rallied his neighbors and clansmen, built a fortified camp, and held out for their safety.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhiyuan bandits filled Hebei, Hedong, and Shandong; Zhi gathered his township, clan, and kin, built a fortified camp, and protected themselves.

entries.zh: 世祖命大將略地晉城，直以其眾歸之，幕府承製，署直潞州元帥府右監軍。
entries.en: When Kublai sent a great general to subdue the Jincheng region, Zhi brought his followers over to the Yuan side; the field headquarters, acting by imperial commission, appointed him right supervising general of the Lu Prefecture Marshal's headquarters.
entries.literal: The Founder ordered a great general to seize territory around Jincheng; Zhi brought his followers and submitted to him, and the field headquarters, acting on imperial authority, appointed Zhi right supervising general of the Lu Prefecture Marshal's Office.

entries.zh: 其後論功行賞，分土世守，命直佩金符，為澤州長官。
entries.en: Later, when merits were rewarded with hereditary fiefs, he was granted a golden tally and appointed chief administrator of Ze Prefecture.
entries.literal: Later, when merits were assessed and rewards distributed and fiefs were granted for hereditary tenure, Zhi was ordered to wear the golden tally and made chief administrator of Ze Prefecture.

entries.zh: 澤民多避兵未還者，直命籍其田廬於親戚鄰人之戶，且約曰：「俟業主至，當析而歸之。」
entries.en: Many in Ze Prefecture had fled the wars and not yet come home; Zhi had their fields and houses registered under the care of relatives and neighbors, with the pledge: "When the owners return, everything shall be divided and given back."
entries.literal: Many people of Ze had fled the warfare and not yet returned; Zhi ordered their fields and dwellings registered to the households of relatives and neighbors, with the stipulation: "When the owners return, the property shall be divided and restored to them."

entries.zh: 逃民聞之，多來還者，命歸其田廬如約，民得安業。
entries.en: Refugees who heard of this came back in large numbers; he restored their land and homes as promised, and the people were able to resume their livelihoods in peace.
entries.literal: When fugitives heard this, many came back; he ordered their fields and dwellings restored as promised, and the people were able to settle in their occupations.

entries.zh: 素無產者，則出粟賑之；
entries.en: Those who had always been destitute he supplied with grain for relief;
entries.literal: Those who had never had property he supplied with grain to relieve them;

entries.zh: 為他郡所俘掠者，出財購之；
entries.en: those seized and carried off into other prefectures he ransomed with his own funds;
entries.literal: those seized and carried off by other prefectures he ransomed with his own funds;

entries.zh: 以兵死而暴露者，收而瘞之。
entries.en: and those who had fallen in battle and lay unburied he gathered in and gave proper burial.
entries.literal: those who had died in battle and lay exposed he gathered in and buried.

entries.zh: 未幾，澤為樂土。
entries.en: Before long Ze had become a peaceful and thriving region.
entries.literal: Before long Ze became a land of peace and prosperity.

entries.zh: 大修孔子廟，割田千畝，置書萬卷，迎儒士李俊民為師，以招延四方來學者。
entries.en: He undertook a major restoration of the Temple of Confucius, endowed a thousand mu of fields, assembled ten thousand scrolls of books, and invited the scholar Li Junmin to serve as master, thereby drawing students from far and wide.
entries.literal: He greatly repaired the Temple of Confucius, set aside a thousand mu of fields, collected ten thousand scrolls of books, welcomed the Confucian scholar Li Junmin as teacher, and thereby drew learners from all quarters.

entries.zh: 不五六年，學之士子，以通經被選者，百二十有二人。
entries.en: Within five or six years, one hundred and twenty-two students who had mastered the classics were selected for office.
entries.literal: Within five or six years, one hundred and twenty-two students of the school who had mastered the classics were selected for office.

entries.zh: 在官二十年，多有惠政。
entries.en: During twenty years in office he carried out many policies that benefited the people.
entries.literal: During twenty years in office he enacted many benevolent policies.

entries.zh: 朝廷特命提舉本州學校事，未拜而卒。
entries.en: The court specially appointed him superintendent of the prefectural schools, but he died before he could assume the post.
entries.literal: The court specially appointed him to supervise the prefectural schools, but before he could take up the post he died.

entries.zh: 耶律伯堅，字壽之，桓州人。
entries.en: Yelü Bojian, courtesy name Shouzhi, was a native of Huanzhou.
entries.literal: Yelü Bojian, style name Shouzhi, was a man of Huanzhou.

entries.zh: 氣豪俠，喜與名士游。
entries.en: He was spirited and chivalrous by nature, and delighted in the company of eminent men of letters.
entries.literal: In temperament he was bold and chivalrous, and delighted in traveling with eminent scholars.

entries.zh: 用薦舉入官，為工部主事。
entries.en: Recommended for office, he was appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Works.
entries.literal: Through recommendation he entered office and served as a principal clerk in the Ministry of Works.

entries.zh: 至元九年，轉保定路清苑縣尹。
entries.en: In the ninth year of the Zhiyuan reign (1272), he was transferred to serve as magistrate of Qingyuan County in Baoding Circuit.
entries.literal: In the ninth year of Zhiyuan he was transferred to be magistrate of Qingyuan County in Baoding Circuit.

entries.zh: 初，安肅州苦徐水之害，訴於大司農司，大司農司欲奪水故道，導水使東。
entries.en: Earlier, Ansu Prefecture had long suffered from flooding on the Xu River and appealed to the Grand Secretariat for Agriculture, which proposed to seize the river's old channel and divert the water eastward.
entries.literal: Earlier Ansu Prefecture had suffered from the harm of the Xu River and appealed to the Grand Secretariat for Agriculture, which wished to seize the river's former course and divert the water eastward.

entries.zh: 東則清苑境也，地勢不利，果導之，則清苑被其害，而水亦必反故道為災。
entries.en: To the east lay Qingyuan territory, where the land lay lower and was ill suited to such a diversion; if the plan went ahead, Qingyuan would be inundated, and the water would inevitably break back into its old course and bring disaster again.
entries.literal: To the east was Qingyuan territory, where the terrain was unfavorable; if the water were in fact diverted, Qingyuan would suffer harm, and the water would also inevitably return to its former course and become a disaster.

entries.zh: 伯堅陳其形勢，圖其利害，要大司農司官及郡守行視可否，事遂得已。
entries.en: Bojian explained the terrain, laid out the advantages and risks in a diagram, and insisted that Grand Secretariat for Agriculture officials and the circuit intendant inspect the site in person before deciding; the project was abandoned.
entries.literal: Bojian set forth the terrain, mapped the advantages and harms, and required officials of the Grand Secretariat for Agriculture and the circuit intendant to go in person and inspect whether it was feasible; the matter was thereby stopped.

entries.zh: 縣西有塘水，溉民田甚廣，勢家據以為磑，民以失利來訴。
entries.en: West of the county stood a reservoir whose waters irrigated a vast stretch of farmland; powerful families had monopolized it to run water mills, and peasants came forward to sue because their irrigation had been cut off.
entries.literal: West of the county was pond water that irrigated the people's fields over a very wide area; powerful families had seized it to operate water mills, and the people came to sue because they had lost their benefit.

entries.zh: 伯堅命毀磑，決其水而注之田，許以溉田之餘月，乃得堰水置磑。
entries.en: Bojian ordered the mills torn down, opened the sluices, and sent the water back into the fields; only in the months when irrigation was not required might the water be dammed again for milling.
entries.literal: Bojian ordered the mills destroyed, released the water and directed it into the fields, and permitted damming the water for mills only in the months when irrigation was not needed.

entries.zh: 仍以其事聞於省部，著為定制。
entries.en: He reported the matter to the provincial and central authorities as well, and it was enacted as a permanent regulation.
entries.literal: He also reported the matter to the provincial and central ministries, and it was established as a standing regulation.

entries.zh: 縣居南北之衝，歲為親王大官治供帳於縣西，限以十月成，至明年復撤而新之，吏得併緣侵漁，其費不貲。
entries.en: The county stood on the main road between north and south; every year temporary lodging for imperial princes and high officials was erected west of the town, to be finished by the tenth month, then torn down and rebuilt the following year—giving clerks endless pretexts for graft until the cost became incalculable.
entries.literal: The county lay on the thoroughfare between north and south; every year quarters for imperial princes and high officials were built west of the county, required to be finished by the tenth month; the next year they would be torn down and rebuilt anew, so clerks could take advantage and embezzle—the expense was beyond reckoning.

entries.zh: 伯堅命築公館，以代供帳，其弊遂絕。
entries.en: Bojian ordered a permanent public lodge built to replace the yearly encampments, and the abuse ceased.
entries.literal: Bojian ordered a public lodge built in place of the temporary quarters, and this abuse was thereby ended.

entries.zh: 凡郡府賦役，於縣有重於他縣者，輒曰：「寧得罪於上，不可得罪於下。」
entries.en: Whenever the circuit or prefecture imposed levies on his county heavier than on others, he would say, "Better to offend my superiors than to wrong the people below."
entries.literal: Whenever tax levies from the circuit or prefecture fell more heavily on his county than on others, he would say, "Better to offend those above than to offend those below."

entries.zh: 必詣府力爭之。
entries.en: He would go in person to the prefectural seat and fight the matter with all his strength.
entries.literal: He would invariably go to the prefectural seat and strive against it with all his force.

entries.zh: 在清苑四年，民親戴之如父母，比去而猶思之，立石頌其德焉。
entries.en: During his four years in Qingyuan the people loved him as their own parents; long after he left they still missed him and set up a stone inscription in praise of his virtue.
entries.literal: During his four years in Qingyuan the people cherished him as they would their own parents; after he left they still thought of him and erected a stone to praise his virtue.

entries.zh: 擢為恩州同知。
entries.en: He was promoted to vice prefect of En Prefecture.
entries.literal: He was promoted to vice prefect of Enzhou.

entries.zh: 世祖即位，以伯八舊臣子孫，擢為萬戶，命領諸部軍馬屯守欠欠州。
entries.en: When Emperor Shizu came to the throne, Bo Ba was raised to commander of ten thousand households as a descendant of an old minister and ordered to garrison Qianqianzhou with the forces of the tribes.
entries.literal: When Emperor Shizu took the throne, because Bo Ba was a descendant of an old minister, he was promoted to commander of ten thousand households and ordered to lead the armies of the various tribes in garrison at Qianqianzhou.

entries.zh: 至元十二年，親王昔列吉、脫鐵木兒叛，奔海都。
entries.en: In Zhiyuan 12 the princes Shiregi and Totemur rose in rebellion and fled to Kaidu.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year of the Zhiyuan era the princes Shiregi and Totemur rebelled and fled to Kaidu.

entries.zh: 伯八以聞，且願提兵往討之，未得命，為彼所襲，死焉。
entries.en: Bo Ba reported the revolt and asked to lead troops against them, but before orders came he was attacked and killed.
entries.literal: Bo Ba reported it and also asked to lead troops to attack them. Before he received orders he was raided by them and died.

entries.zh: 撒吉思深加器重，自謂其才不及，言於世祖，召給宿衛。
entries.en: Sagis held him in high esteem, declaring his own talent inferior, and recommended him to Emperor Shizu, who summoned him to the imperial guard.
entries.literal: Sagis greatly valued him, saying himself that his own talent did not match Helapuhua's, and spoke of him to Emperor Shizu, who summoned him to serve in the imperial guard.

entries.zh: 嘗以事至益都，於四腳山下置廣興、商山二冶，以勞授金符，為商山鐵冶都提舉；
entries.en: On a mission to Yidu he established the Guangxing and Shangshan ironworks at the foot of Four-Legged Mountain. For his service he received the golden tally and was made chief intendant of the Shangshan ironworks;
entries.literal: Once on business he went to Yidu and at the foot of Four-Legged Mountain established the Guangxing and Shangshan ironworks. For his service he was granted the golden tally and made chief intendant of the Shangshan ironworks;

entries.zh: 未及代，以職讓其弟。
entries.en: but before his term ended he yielded the post to his younger brother.
entries.literal: before his term ended he yielded the post to his younger brother.

entries.zh: 時兵南伐，餽運繁興，被選為行都漕運使，帥諸翼兵萬五千人，從事飛輓。
entries.en: With the southern campaigns under way and supply lines strained, he was chosen acting chief transport commissioner and led fifteen thousand wing troops in rapid grain transport.
entries.literal: At that time the army was campaigning south and transport was urgently needed. He was chosen as acting chief transport commissioner, commanding fifteen thousand troops of the various wings to engage in rapid supply transport.

entries.zh: 江南平，上疏言：「親肺腑，禮大臣，以存國家之體。
entries.en: After the south was pacified he submitted a memorial: "Cherish the imperial kin, honor great ministers—to preserve the dignity of the state.
entries.literal: When the Jiangnan region was pacified he submitted a memorial saying: "Cherish those of one's own flesh and blood, honor great ministers—to preserve the state's proper form.

entries.zh: 興學校，獎名節，以勵天下之士。
entries.en: Establish schools and reward integrity—to encourage the scholars of the realm.
entries.literal: Establish schools, reward integrity and reputation—to encourage the scholars of the realm.

entries.zh: 正名分，嚴考課，以定百官之法。
entries.en: Clarify ranks and tighten examinations—to fix the standards for officials.
entries.literal: Rectify ranks and titles, tighten examinations and assessments—to fix the law for the hundred officials.

entries.zh: 通泉幣，却貢獻，以厚生民之本。」
entries.en: Circulate currency and curb excessive tribute—to strengthen the people's livelihood."
entries.literal: Circulate currency, reject excessive tribute—to strengthen the foundation of the people's livelihood."

entries.zh: 又言：「江南新附，宜招舊族，力穡通商，弛征薄入，以撫馴其民，不然，恐尚煩宵旰之慮。」
entries.en: He also urged: "The newly submitted south should have its old families recalled, farming and trade encouraged, and taxes eased—to win over the people. Otherwise Your Majesty may yet lose sleep over it."
entries.literal: He also said: "The newly submitted Jiangnan should have its old clans summoned, agriculture and commerce encouraged, levies relaxed and collections lightened, to soothe and tame its people—otherwise I fear it may still trouble Your Majesty's sleepless cares."

entries.zh: 帝多采用其言。
entries.en: The emperor largely adopted his recommendations.
entries.literal: The emperor largely adopted his words.

entries.zh: 屬漕米二十萬，繇邗溝達于河，舟覆，損十之一，而又每斛視都斛虧三升。
entries.en: He was responsible for two hundred thousand piculs of grain, sent by the Hangou Canal to the Yellow River. Boats capsized and a tenth was lost; moreover each picul fell three sheng short of the capital standard.
entries.literal: He was charged with two hundred thousand piculs of transport grain, conveyed by the Hangou Canal to reach the Yellow River. Boats capsized and one tenth was lost; moreover each picul was short three sheng compared with the capital standard picul.

entries.zh: 時阿合馬專政，責償舟人。
entries.en: Ahmad then held sole power and demanded that the boatmen make good the loss.
entries.literal: At that time Ahmad held sole power and demanded compensation from the boatmen.

entries.zh: 合剌普華伏闕抗言：「量之踦贏，出於元降，而水道之虞，非人力所及。
entries.en: Helapuhua knelt before the palace gate and protested: "Short measure comes from the original allocation, and the hazards of the waterways are beyond human control.
entries.literal: Helapuhua prostrated himself before the palace gate and protested: "Short measure and surplus or deficit arise from the original allocation, while the hazards of the water route are beyond human control.

entries.zh: 且彼雖罄其家，不足以償，苟朝廷必不任虧損，臣獨當其辜。」
entries.en: Even if they sold everything they owned it would not cover the loss. If the court will accept no shortfall, let me bear the blame alone."
entries.literal: Moreover, though they exhaust their households it would not suffice to repay. If the court will certainly not accept any loss, I alone shall bear the guilt."

entries.zh: 詔勿治。
entries.en: An edict ordered that the matter not be pursued.
entries.literal: An edict ordered that the matter not be prosecuted.

entries.zh: 阿合馬憤之，乃出合剌普華為寧海路達魯花赤，後遷江西宣慰使，未至官，改廣東都轉運鹽使，兼領諸番市舶。
entries.en: Ahmad, furious, posted Helapuhua as darughachi of Ninghai Circuit. He was later transferred to Jiangxi pacification commissioner, but before taking office was reassigned as Guangdong chief salt transport commissioner, with oversight of foreign maritime trade.
entries.literal: Ahmad was angry and therefore sent Helapuhua out as darughachi of Ninghai Circuit. Later he was transferred to Jiangxi pacification commissioner, but before he took office was changed to Guangdong chief salt transport commissioner, concurrently overseeing the maritime trade of the various foreign merchants.

entries.zh: 脫鐵木兒虜其二子八剌、不蘭奚，分置左右，居歲餘，待之頗厚。
entries.en: Totemur captured his sons Bala and Bulanxi, kept them at his side, and for more than a year treated them generously.
entries.literal: Totemur captured his two sons Bala and Bulanxi, placed them on his left and right, and for more than a year treated them quite generously.

entries.zh: 八剌陰結脫鐵木兒近侍也里伯禿，謀報父仇，後為也伯里禿家人泄其謀。
entries.en: Bala secretly won over Totemur's attendant Yelibatu to plot revenge for his father, but a member of Yelibatu's household exposed the scheme.
entries.literal: Bala secretly joined with Totemur's close attendant Yelibatu to plan vengeance for his father. Later a member of Yelibatu's household revealed the plot.

entries.zh: 八剌知事不成，將家族南奔，脫鐵木兒遣騎追之，至一河，八剌馬驚，不能渡，回拒之，射中數人，力窮，兄弟就擒。
entries.en: Seeing the plot had failed, Bala fled south with his family. Totemur's horsemen overtook him at a river; his horse panicked and could not cross. He turned to fight, shot down several pursuers, but when his strength gave out he and his brother were taken.
entries.literal: Bala knew the affair would not succeed and was about to flee south with his clan. Totemur sent horsemen in pursuit. At a river Bala's horse panicked and could not cross. He turned back to resist, shot several men, but when his strength was exhausted the brothers were captured.

entries.zh: 脫鐵木兒責之曰：「我待汝厚甚，而汝反為此耶！」
entries.en: Totemur rebuked him: "I treated you generously—yet you do this!"
entries.literal: Totemur rebuked him, saying: "I treated you very generously—yet you turn to this!"

entries.zh: 八剌曰：「汝背叛君上，害我父，掠我親屬，我誓欲殺汝，以報君父之讎，今力窮被執，從汝所為！」
entries.en: Bala said: "You betrayed your lord, killed my father, and seized my kin. I swore to kill you to avenge my sovereign and father. My strength is spent and I am your prisoner—do as you please!"
entries.literal: Bala said: "You betrayed your sovereign, killed my father, and seized my kin. I swore to kill you to avenge my sovereign and father. Now my strength is spent and I am captured—do as you will!"

entries.zh: 逼令跪，不屈，以鐵撾碎其膝，終不跪，與弟不闌奚同被害。
entries.en: They forced him to kneel, but he refused. They smashed his knees with iron clubs, yet he still would not kneel. He and his brother Bulanxi were put to death together.
entries.literal: They forced him to kneel but he would not yield. With iron clubs they shattered his knees, yet he still would not kneel. He and his younger brother Bulanxi were killed together.

entries.zh: 幼子何都兀赤，官至河北河南道肅政廉訪使。
entries.en: His youngest son Hodu'uchi rose to surveillance commissioner of the Hebei-Henan Circuit.
entries.literal: His youngest son Hodu'uchi reached the office of surveillance commissioner of the Hebei-Henan Circuit.

entries.zh: 李伯溫，守賢之孫，彀之子也。
entries.en: Li Bowen was a grandson of Shouxian and the son of Gou.
entries.literal: Li Bowen was the grandson of Shouxian and the son of Gou.

entries.zh: 長兄惟則，懷遠大將軍、平陽征行萬戶；
entries.en: His eldest brother Weize held the ranks of General of Huaiyuan and campaign commander of ten thousand households from Pingyang;
entries.literal: His eldest brother was Weize, General of Huaiyuan and commander of ten thousand households on campaign from Pingyang;

entries.zh: 次伯通。
entries.en: Next came Botong.
entries.literal: The next in order was Botong.

entries.zh: 歲甲戌，錦州張致叛，國王木華黎命擊之，大戰城北，伯通死焉。
entries.en: In the jiaxu year Zhang Zhi rebelled at Jinzhou; Prince Muqali ordered an attack on him, and in a fierce battle north of the city Botong was killed.
entries.literal: In the jiaxu year, Zhang Zhi of Jinzhou rebelled; the prince Muqali ordered an attack on him, and in a great battle north of the city Botong died there.

entries.zh: 伯溫行平陽元帥府事，鎮青龍堡，專任東征。
entries.en: Bowen ran the Pingyang marshal's office, held Qinglong Fort, and bore sole responsibility for operations in the east.
entries.literal: Bowen acted as head of the Pingyang Marshal's headquarters, garrisoned Qinglong Fort, and was solely charged with the eastern campaign.

entries.zh: 知平陽已陷，弟守忠被執，選驍勇拒守，久之，金人盡銳來攻，守卒夜多遁去，李成開水門導敵入，伯溫登堞樓，謂左右曰：「吾兄弟仗節擁麾，受方面之寄，今不幸失利，當以死報國。
entries.en: When he learned that Pingyang had fallen and his brother Shouzhong had been taken, he picked his fiercest troops to hold the fort. After a long siege the Jin threw their full force against it; by night most of the garrison slipped away. Li Cheng opened the water gate and admitted the enemy. Bowen climbed the tower and told his men: "My brothers and I have carried the commander's banner and been entrusted with an entire circuit. Now that we have lost, we must repay the realm with our lives.
entries.literal: Learning that Pingyang had already fallen and that his younger brother Shouzhong had been captured, he chose the bravest men to hold out in defense; after a long time the Jin brought their full strength to attack, and by night many of the defenders fled; Li Cheng opened the water gate and led the enemy in; Bowen mounted the parapet tower and said to those beside him: "We brothers have borne the commander's staff and banner and received the trust of a whole region; now, having met with misfortune and defeat, we ought to repay the state with our deaths.

entries.zh: 吾弟已被執，我不可再辱，汝等宜自逃生。」
entries.en: My brother is already a prisoner; I cannot endure another humiliation. You should escape while you can."
entries.literal: My younger brother has already been captured; I cannot suffer disgrace again—you should each save yourselves and flee."

entries.zh: 士卒皆猶豫不忍去，伯溫即拔劍殺家屬，投井中，以刃植柱，刺心而死。
entries.en: The troops hung back, unwilling to go. Bowen drew his sword, killed his household, threw their bodies down a well, set his blade against a pillar, and drove it into his own heart.
entries.literal: The soldiers all hesitated and were unwilling to leave; Bowen at once drew his sword and killed his family members, cast them into a well, planted his blade in a pillar, and stabbed himself through the heart to die.

entries.zh: 金人登樓，見伯溫抱柱如生，無不嗟歎。
entries.en: The Jin soldiers who mounted the tower found Bowen still clasping the pillar as though he lived, and every one of them sighed in wonder.
entries.literal: When the Jin climbed the tower and saw Bowen embracing the pillar as if still alive, none failed to sigh in admiration.

entries.zh: 是時有申榮者，平章山東行省，守東昌，榮見列郡皆降，告其父曰：「人生世間，不能全忠孝者，兒也。」
entries.en: At this time there was Shen Rong, chief councillor of the Shandong Branch Secretariat, defending Dongchang. When Rong saw that the neighboring prefectures had all surrendered, he told his father, "In this life, if a man cannot fulfill both loyalty and filial piety, that man is his son."
entries.literal: At this time there was Shen Rong, chief councillor of the Shandong Branch Secretariat, defending Dongchang. When Rong saw that the neighboring prefectures had all surrendered, he told his father, "In this life, if one cannot fulfill both loyalty and filial piety, that person is his son."

entries.zh: 父曰：「何為？」
entries.en: His father asked, "What do you mean?"
entries.literal: His father said, "What do you mean?"

entries.zh: 榮曰：「城中兵少不敵，戰則萬人之命由兒而廢，但有一死報國耳。」
entries.en: Rong said, "The garrison is too small to match the enemy. If we fight, ten thousand lives will be ruined because of me. I have only one death with which to repay the state."
entries.literal: Rong said, "The troops in the city are few and cannot match the enemy. If we fight, the lives of ten thousand people will be ruined because of me. I have only one death with which to repay the state."

entries.zh: 遂自經。
entries.en: He then hanged himself.
entries.literal: He then hanged himself.

entries.zh: 普顏不花，字希古，蒙古氏。
entries.en: Puyan Buhua, whose style name was Xigu, was a Mongol.
entries.literal: Puyan Buhua, style name Xigu, was of the Mongol clan.

entries.zh: 倜儻有大志。
entries.en: Free-spirited and ambitious, he aimed high from the start.
entries.literal: He was unconventional and had great ambition.

entries.zh: 至正五年，由國子生登右榜進士第一人，授翰林修撰，調河南行省員外郎。
entries.en: In 1345, as a student of the National University he took first place on the right-board jinshi examination. He was appointed Hanlin reviser and transferred to vice director in the Henan Branch Secretariat.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Zhizheng, as a National University student he placed first among the right-board jinshi, was appointed Hanlin reviser, and was transferred to vice director of the Henan Branch Secretariat.

entries.zh: 十一年，遷江西行省左右司郎中。
entries.en: In 1351 he was transferred to director of the left and right secretariat bureaus in the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year, he was transferred to director of the left and right bureaus of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat.

entries.zh: 蘄黃徐壽輝來寇，普顏不花戰守之功為多，語在《道童傳》。
entries.en: When Xu Shouhui of Qihuang invaded, Puyan Buhua bore the brunt of the fighting and defense; the full account appears in the 《Biography of Daotong》.
entries.literal: When Xu Shouhui of Qihuang came raiding, Puyan Buhua's achievements in fighting and defense were the greatest; the account is in the 《Biography of Daotong》.

entries.zh: 十六年，除江西廉訪副使。
entries.en: In 1356 he was appointed vice surveillance commissioner of Jiangxi.
entries.literal: In the sixteenth year, he was appointed vice surveillance commissioner of Jiangxi.

entries.zh: 頃之，召還，授益都路達魯花赤，遷山東廉訪使，再轉為中書參知政事。
entries.en: Soon after he was recalled and appointed darughachi of Yidu Circuit, then promoted to surveillance commissioner of Shandong and finally transferred to associate administration councilor of the Central Secretariat.
entries.literal: Before long he was recalled, appointed darughachi of Yidu Circuit, promoted to surveillance commissioner of Shandong, and again transferred to associate administration councilor of the Central Secretariat.

entries.zh: 十八年，詔與治書侍御史李國鳳同經略江南。
entries.en: In 1358 he was ordered, together with Supervising Secretary Li Guofeng, to oversee military affairs in Jiangnan.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year, he was ordered together with Supervising Secretary Li Guofeng to oversee military affairs in Jiangnan.

entries.zh: 至建寧，江西陳友諒遣鄧克明來寇，而平章政事阿魯溫沙等皆夜遁。
entries.en: Upon reaching Jianning, he found that Chen Youliang of Jiangxi had sent Deng Keming to attack, while Chief Councillors Aru Wensha and the rest had all fled under cover of night.
entries.literal: When he reached Jianning, Chen Youliang of Jiangxi sent Deng Keming to attack, while the chief councillors Aru Wensha and others all fled by night.

entries.zh: 國鳳時分鎮延平，城陷，遁去。
entries.en: Li Guofeng was then holding Yanping separately; when that city fell he fled as well.
entries.literal: Li Guofeng was then stationed separately at Yanping; when the city fell he fled.

entries.zh: 普顏不花曰：「我承制來此，去將何之？
entries.en: Puyan Buhua said, "I came here on imperial commission. Where would I go if I left?
entries.literal: Puyan Buhua said, "I came here by imperial order—where would I go if I left?

entries.zh: 誓與此城同存亡耳。」
entries.en: I swear to live and die with this city."
entries.literal: I swear to live and die with this city."

entries.zh: 命築各門甕城，前後拒戰六十四日，既而大敗賊眾。
entries.en: He ordered barbicans built at every gate and held the enemy off for sixty-four days in all, then inflicted a crushing defeat on the rebel army.
entries.literal: He ordered barbicans built at each gate, fought off the enemy for sixty-four days in all, and then inflicted a great defeat on the rebel forces.

entries.zh: 明年，召還，授山東宣慰使，再轉知樞密院事、平章山東行省，守禦益都。
entries.en: The following year he was recalled and appointed pacification commissioner of Shandong, then transferred again to privy council vice director and chief councillor of the Shandong Branch Secretariat, with responsibility for defending Yidu.
entries.literal: The next year he was recalled, appointed pacification commissioner of Shandong, again transferred to privy council vice director and chief councillor of the Shandong Branch Secretariat, and charged with defending Yidu.

entries.zh: 大明兵壓境，普顏不花捍城力戰。
entries.en: When Ming forces pressed the frontier, Puyan Buhua held the city and fought with all his strength.
entries.literal: When the Ming army pressed the borders, Puyan Buhua defended the city and fought hard.

entries.zh: 城陷，而平章政事保保出降。
entries.en: When the city fell, Chief Councillor Baobao went out and surrendered.
entries.literal: When the city fell, Chief Councillor Baobao went out and surrendered.

entries.zh: 普顏不花還告其母曰：「兒忠孝不能兩全，有二弟，當為終養。」
entries.en: Puyan Buhua went home and told his mother, "A man cannot fulfill both loyalty and filial piety at once. I have two younger brothers who should see to your care in old age."
entries.literal: Puyan Buhua returned and told his mother, "A son cannot fulfill both loyalty and filial piety at once. I have two younger brothers who should provide for you in your old age."

entries.zh: 拜母，趨官舍，坐堂上。
entries.en: He bowed to his mother, hurried to the government compound, and took his seat in the main hall.
entries.literal: He bowed to his mother, hurried to the government compound, and sat in the main hall.

entries.zh: 主將素聞其賢，召之再三，不往。
entries.en: The commander had long heard of his worth and summoned him repeatedly, but he would not go.
entries.literal: The commander had long heard of his worth and summoned him again and again, but he would not go.

entries.zh: 既而面縛之，普顏不花曰：「我元朝進士，官至極品，臣各為其主。」
entries.en: Before long they bound him and brought him forward. Puyan Buhua said, "I am a Yuan jinshi who rose to the highest rank. A minister serves his own lord."
entries.literal: Before long they bound him face to face. Puyan Buhua said, "I am a jinshi of the Yuan dynasty, risen to the highest rank—a minister serves his own lord."

entries.zh: 不屈，死之。
entries.en: He would not yield and was put to death.
entries.literal: He would not submit and was put to death.

entries.zh: 劉源，歸德中牟人。
entries.en: Liu Yuan came from Zhongmou in Guide Prefecture.
entries.literal: Liu Yuan was a native of Zhongmou in Guide.

entries.zh: 母吳氏，年七十餘，病甚不能行。
entries.en: His mother, Lady Wu, was over seventy, gravely ill and unable to walk.
entries.literal: His mother, the Lady Wu, was over seventy years old, gravely ill and unable to walk.

entries.zh: 適兵火起，且延至其家，鄰里俱逃，源力不能救，乃呼天號泣，趨入抱母，為火所焚而死。
entries.en: War-fires broke out and soon reached his home; neighbors fled, and Yuan, powerless to save her, cried to Heaven, rushed in to embrace his mother, and perished in the flames with her.
entries.literal: Just then war-fires broke out and soon reached his home; the neighbors all fled. Yuan had not the strength to save her, so he cried to Heaven and wept aloud, rushed in and embraced his mother, and was burned to death by the fire.

entries.zh: 姜兼，嚴州淳安人。
entries.en: Jiang Jian came from Chun'an in Yan Prefecture.
entries.literal: Jiang Jian was a native of Chun'an in Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 七歲而孤，與二兄養母至孝。
entries.en: Orphaned at seven, he and his two elder brothers cared for their mother with devoted filial piety.
entries.literal: Orphaned at seven, he and his two elder brothers supported their mother with utmost filial piety.

entries.zh: 母死，兼哀慕幾絕。
entries.en: When his mother died, Jian's grief nearly destroyed him.
entries.literal: When his mother died, Jian's grief and longing nearly killed him.

entries.zh: 既葬，獨居墓下，朝夕哭奠，寂焉荒山中，躬自樵爨，蔬食飲水，一衰麻寒暑不易。
entries.en: After the burial he lived alone at the grave, mourning morning and evening in the lonely mountains; he cut his own firewood, cooked his own food, ate only vegetables and drank only water, and wore the same hemp mourning clothes through winter and summer alike.
entries.literal: After the burial he dwelt alone beneath the grave, weeping and offering sacrifices morning and evening in the silent wild mountains; he himself gathered firewood and cooked, ate vegetables and drank water, and wore the same hemp mourning garb through cold and heat without change.

entries.zh: 同里陳氏、戴氏子不能事其父母，聞兼之行，慚感而悔，皆迎養焉。
entries.en: Young men of the Chen and Dai families nearby who had neglected their parents, hearing of Jian's example, were shamed into repentance and brought their parents home to care for them.
entries.literal: Sons of the Chen and Dai families in the same village who could not serve their parents, hearing of Jian's conduct, were ashamed, moved, and repented, and all brought their parents home to support them.

entries.zh: 靳昺，字克昌，絳州曲沃人。
entries.en: Jin Biao, styled Kechang, came from Quwo in Jiang Prefecture.
entries.literal: Jin Biao, style name Kechang, was a native of Quwo in Jiangzhou.

entries.zh: 兄榮為奎章閣承製學士，奉母王氏官於朝。
entries.en: His elder brother Rong served as Compiler Academician at the Kui Zhang Pavilion, bringing their mother Lady Wang with him to the capital.
entries.literal: His elder brother Rong was a Compiler Academician of the Kui Zhang Pavilion, supporting their mother, the Lady Wang, in office at court.

entries.zh: 母歿，昺與兄榮護喪還家。
entries.en: When their mother died, Biao and Rong escorted her coffin home.
entries.literal: When their mother died, Biao and his elder brother Rong escorted the coffin home.

entries.zh: 至平定，大雷雨，流水驟至，昺伏柩上，榮呼之避水，昺不忍捨去，遂為水所漂沒。
entries.en: At Pingding a thunderstorm sent floodwaters rushing in; Biao clung to the coffin while Rong called him to flee, but Biao would not abandon his mother and was swept away and drowned.
entries.literal: When they reached Pingding, a great thunderstorm broke and floodwaters suddenly arrived; Biao lay upon the coffin, Rong called him to flee the water, but Biao could not bear to leave and was swept away and drowned.

entries.zh: 後得王氏柩於三里外，得昺屍於五里外。
entries.en: Later they found Lady Wang's coffin three li downstream and Biao's body five li away.
entries.literal: Later Lady Wang's coffin was found three li away, and Biao's corpse five li away.

entries.zh: 詔賜《孝子靳昺碑》。
entries.en: The throne granted an inscribed stele titled 《The Filial Son Jin Biao》.
entries.literal: An edict bestowed the 《Stele of the Filial Son Jin Biao》.

entries.zh: 張緝，字士明，益都膠州人。
entries.en: Zhang Ji, styled Shiming, came from Jiaozhou in Yidu.
entries.literal: Zhang Ji, style name Shiming, was a native of Jiaozhou in Yidu.

entries.zh: 性孝友，能詩文。
entries.en: Filial and devoted to his brothers, he was also skilled in poetry and prose.
entries.literal: By nature he was filial and brotherly, and able in poetry and prose.

entries.zh: 至正七年，與兄紳、弟經同領鄉薦，由澤州儒學正轉泰州幕職，棄之，養親居揚州。
entries.en: In the seventh year of Zhizheng he and his brothers Shen and Jing were all recommended for office; he left a post in Taizhou to care for his parents and settled in Yangzhou.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Zhizheng he and his elder brother Shen and younger brother Jing together received provincial recommendation; from Rectifier of Confucian Learning in Ze Prefecture he was transferred to a staff post in Taizhou, which he abandoned to support his parents and live in Yangzhou.

entries.zh: 十五年，揚州亂，緝母姬氏方臥病，賊突入臥內，舉槍欲刺姬，緝以身蔽姬，槍中緝脅，三日而死。
entries.en: In the fifteenth year, as Yangzhou fell into chaos, his mother Lady Ji lay ill when bandits burst in and raised a spear to kill her. Ji shielded her with his body; the spear pierced his side, and he died three days later.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year Yangzhou fell into disorder; Ji's mother, the Lady Ji, lay ill in bed when bandits burst into the sleeping chamber and raised a spear to stab her. Ji shielded Lady Ji with his body; the spear struck his ribs, and he died three days later.

entries.zh: 王庸，字伯常，雄州歸信人。
entries.en: Wang Yong, whose style was Bochang, came from Guixin in Xiong Prefecture.
entries.literal: Wang Yong, style name Bochang, was a native of Guixin in Xiongzhou.

entries.zh: 事母李氏以孝聞。
entries.en: He won fame for filial devotion in caring for his mother, Lady Li.
entries.literal: In serving his mother, Lady Li, he became renowned for filial piety.

entries.zh: 母有疾，庸夜禱北辰，至叩頭出血，母疾遂愈。
entries.en: When his mother fell ill, Yong spent the nights praying to the Pole Star, bowing until his forehead bled; her illness then lifted.
entries.literal: When his mother fell ill, Yong prayed by night to the North Star, until his forehead bled from knocking it on the ground; his mother's illness then recovered.

entries.zh: 及母卒，哀毀幾絕，露處墓前，旦夕悲號。
entries.en: After her death his mourning was so severe he nearly perished, living unsheltered at the grave and lamenting from dawn till dusk.
entries.literal: When his mother died, his grief and emaciation nearly killed him; he dwelt in the open before the grave, wailing morning and evening.

entries.zh: 一夕，雷雨暴至，鄰人持寢席往，欲蔽之，見庸所坐臥之地獨不沾濕，咸嘆異而去。
entries.en: One night a thunderstorm broke over him; neighbors brought bedding to cover him, yet the spot where Yong sat and slept alone stayed dry—everyone marveled and went away.
entries.literal: One night a violent thunderstorm burst upon him; neighbors brought bedding to shelter him, but saw that the ground where Yong sat and lay alone was not wet; all marveled and withdrew.

entries.zh: 復有蜜蜂數十房，來止其家，歲得蜜蠟，以供祭祀。
entries.en: Dozens of beehives also settled at his home, yielding honey and wax each year for his ancestral rites.
entries.literal: Moreover, several dozen hives of bees came to lodge at his home; each year he obtained honey and wax to supply sacrificial offerings.

entries.zh: 歲己未，世祖南伐至相，召見問計，瑛從容對曰：「漢、唐以還，人君所恃以為國者，法與兵、食三事而已。
entries.en: In the jiwei year, Kublai Khan on his southern campaign reached Xiangzhou and summoned Ying to ask his counsel. Ying replied calmly: "Since Han and Tang, what rulers have relied on to sustain a state are only three things: law, arms, and grain.
entries.literal: In the year jiwei, the Founder on his southern campaign reached Xiang, summoned him for audience and asked his plans; Ying answered at ease: "Since Han and Tang, what a ruler relies on to make a state is only three things: law, troops, and provisions.

entries.zh: 國無法不立，人無食不生，亂無兵不守。
entries.en: Without law a state cannot stand; without food the people cannot live; in chaos without arms nothing can be held.
entries.literal: Without law a state cannot stand; without food people cannot live; in disorder without troops it cannot be guarded.

entries.zh: 今宋皆蔑之，殆將亡矣，興之在聖主。
entries.en: Song now scorns all three—it is near ruin; renewal rests with Your Sagely Majesty.
entries.literal: Now Song treats all these with contempt—it will almost perish; the rise lies with the sage ruler.

entries.zh: 若控襄樊之師，委戈下流，以搗其背，大業可定矣。」
entries.en: Hold your forces at Xiangyang and Fancheng, then send troops down the river to strike Song from behind, and the great enterprise will be assured."
entries.literal: If you hold the armies of Xiang and Fan, lay aside weapons and go downstream, to strike their rear, the great enterprise can be settled."

entries.zh: 帝悅，曰：「儒者中乃有此人乎！」
entries.en: The Emperor was pleased and said, "Among scholars there is actually such a man as this!"
entries.literal: The Emperor was pleased and said: "Among Confucians there is actually such a person!"

entries.zh: 瑛复勸帝數事，以謂事不如此，後當如彼。
entries.en: Ying went on to counsel the Emperor on several points, warning that if matters were not handled one way now, they would turn out another way later.
entries.literal: Ying again urged the Emperor on several matters, saying that if things were not thus now, later they would be as that.

entries.zh: 帝納之，心賢瑛，謂可大用，命從行，以疾弗果。
entries.en: The Emperor accepted his advice, came to esteem Ying highly, and judged him fit for great office; he ordered Ying to accompany the campaign, but illness prevented it.
entries.literal: The Emperor accepted it, in his heart esteemed Ying, deemed him fit for great employment, ordered him to follow on the march, but because of illness it did not come to pass.

entries.zh: 中統初，詔徵瑛。
entries.en: Early in the Zhongtong era, an imperial summons called for Ying.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Zhongtong, an edict summoned Ying.

entries.zh: 時王文統方用事，辭不就。
entries.en: Wang Wentong was then in power at court; Ying declined and did not accept office.
entries.literal: At the time Wang Wentong was just then in power; he declined and did not go.

entries.zh: 左丞張文謙宣撫河北，奏為懷孟、彰德、大名等路提舉學校官，又辭，遺執政書，其略曰：「先王之道不明，異端邪說害之也，橫流奔放，天理不絕如線。
entries.en: Left Assistant Zhang Wenqian, pacification commissioner of Hebei, recommended him as supervisor of schools for the Huaimeng, Zhangde, Daming, and other circuits; Ying declined again and sent the chief ministers a letter that read in part: "The Way of the ancient kings is obscured, harmed by heterodox teachings; doctrines run wild, and the moral order hangs by a thread.
entries.literal: Left Assistant Zhang Wenqian as Pacification Commissioner of Hebei memorialized to make him Supervisor of Schools for the Huaimeng, Zhangde, Daming, and other circuits; again he declined, leaving a letter to the chief ministers, its gist saying: "The Way of the former kings is not clear; heterodox and perverse doctrines harm it; flowing wildly and rushing forth, Heavenly principle hangs by a thread not severed.

entries.zh: 今天子神聖，俊乂輻輳，言納計用，先王之禮樂教化，興明修復，維其時矣。
entries.en: Today the Son of Heaven is sage, the worthy gather at court, and counsel is heeded—this is the moment to revive and restore the rites, music, and civilizing teachings of the ancient kings.
entries.literal: Now the Son of Heaven is divine and sage, the worthy and able gather like wheel spokes; words are received and plans employed—the former kings' rites, music, and civilizing transformation may be raised bright and repaired and restored; this is the time.

entries.zh: 若夫簿書期會，文法末節，漢、唐猶不屑也，執事者因陋就簡，此焉是務，良可惜哉！
entries.en: Yet ledgers, deadlines, and petty legal formalities—even Han and Tang scorned such things—while those in office cling to the shabby and the expedient. How regrettable!
entries.literal: As for ledgers and scheduled meetings, literary regulations and minor points—even Han and Tang still disdained these; those in charge, following what is shabby and settling for what is simple, make this their task—truly pitiable!

entries.zh: 夫善始者未必善終，今不能溯流求源，明法正俗，育材興化，以拯數百千年之禍，僕恐後日之弊，將有不可勝言者矣。」
entries.en: A good beginning does not guarantee a good end. If we cannot trace the stream to its source—clarify law, rectify custom, nurture talent, and revive civilization—to redeem centuries of ruin, I fear the evils of later days will be beyond telling."
entries.literal: Those who begin well need not end well; now if one cannot go upstream to seek the source, clarify law and rectify custom, nurture talent and raise transformation, to rescue the calamity of several hundred or a thousand years—I fear later days' abuses will have what cannot be spoken in full."

entries.zh: 人或勉之仕，則曰：「後世去古雖遠，而先王之所設施，本末先後，猶可考見，故為政者莫先於復古。
entries.en: When others urged him to serve, he said: "Though our age is far from antiquity, what the ancient kings instituted—its sequence and structure—can still be studied; for anyone who would govern, nothing comes before restoring the ancient ways.
entries.literal: When some urged him to take office, he said: "Later ages though far from antiquity, yet what the former kings established—root and branch, before and after—can still be examined and seen; therefore for one who governs nothing comes before returning to antiquity.

entries.zh: 苟因習舊弊，以求合乎先王之意，不亦難乎！
entries.en: Yet to cling to entrenched abuses and still hope to match the intent of the ancient kings—is that not impossible?
entries.literal: If one merely follows accustomed old abuses, to seek to accord with the former kings' intent—is it not also difficult!

entries.zh: 吾又不能隨時俯仰以赴機會，將焉用仕！」
entries.en: Nor can I bend with the times to seize opportunity—what use would office be to me!"
entries.literal: I also cannot bend and rise with the times to meet opportunity—of what use is taking office!"

entries.zh: 於是杜門著書，一不以窮通得喪動其志，優游道藝，以終其身。
entries.en: He then shut his doors and devoted himself to writing, never letting fortune or misfortune sway his purpose, and passed his days at ease in learning and the arts until he died.
entries.literal: Thereupon he shut his door and wrote books, never once letting poverty or success, gain or loss move his will, at ease in the Way and the arts until his life's end.

entries.zh: 年七十，遺命其子處立、處願曰：「吾即死，當表吾墓曰'緱山杜處士'。」
entries.en: At seventy he instructed his sons Chuli and Chuyuan: "When I die, let my tombstone read 'Gentleman Du of Goushi Mountain.'"
entries.literal: At age seventy, he left testamentary instructions to his sons Chuli and Chuyuan, saying: "When I am about to die, you should inscribe my tomb tablet 'Goushi Gentleman Du.'"

entries.zh: 天歷中，贈資德大夫、翰林學士、上護軍，追封魏郡公，諡文獻。
entries.en: In the Tianli reign he was posthumously honored as Grand Master of Virtuous Talent, Hanlin Academician, and Senior Guardian of the Army, enfeoffed as Duke of Wei Commandery, with the posthumous name Wenxian.
entries.literal: In the Tianli era, posthumously granted Grand Master of Virtuous Talent, Hanlin Academician, and Senior Guardian of the Army; posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Wei Commandery, posthumous name Wenxian.

entries.zh: 特立通程氏《易》，晚教授諸生，東平嚴實每加禮焉。
entries.en: Teli mastered the Cheng school interpretation of the Changes; in later years he taught students, and Yan Shi of Dongping always treated him with respect.
entries.literal: Teli was versed in the Cheng school Changes; in his later years he taught students, and Dongping's Yan Shi always showed him added courtesy.

entries.zh: 歲丙午，世祖在潛邸受王印，首傳旨諭特立曰：「前監察御史張特立，養素丘園，易代如一，今年幾七十，研究聖經，宜錫嘉名，以光潛德，可特賜號曰中庸先生。」
entries.en: In the bingwu year, when Kublai received the princely seal in his residence, he first sent word to Teli: "The former censor Zhang Teli has lived in rustic seclusion through the change of dynasties unchanged; he is nearly seventy and devoted to the classics. Let an honorable title glorify his hidden virtue: grant him specially the name Master of the Mean (Zhongyong)."
entries.literal: In the bingwu year, the Founder in his princely residence received the princely seal; he first transmitted an order instructing Teli: "Former investigating censor Zhang Teli, nurturing simplicity in hill and garden, the change of dynasties as one, this year nearly seventy, investigating the sage classics—fitting to bestow an excellent name to glorify hidden virtue; he may be specially granted the title Master of the Mean."

entries.zh: 又諭曰：「先生年老目病，不能就道，故令趙寶臣諭意，且名其讀書之堂曰麗澤。」
entries.en: He added: "The Master is aged and his eyes are failing and cannot travel; Zhao Baochen is therefore sent to convey my wishes and to name his study the Hall of Beautiful Marsh (Lize)."
entries.literal: He further instructed: "The master is old and his eyes are ill; he cannot come on the road—therefore Zhao Baochen is sent to convey the intent, and moreover to name his hall of reading Li Ze (Beautiful Marsh)."

entries.zh: 壬子歲，复降璽書諭特立曰：「白首窮經，誨人不倦，無過不及，學者宗之，昔已賜嘉名，今復諭意。」
entries.en: In the renzi year another imperial letter reached him: "White-haired, you exhaust the classics and teach without weariness, neither exceeding nor falling short—scholars look to you as their model. An honorable name was granted before; I send my regards again."
entries.literal: In the renzi year, again an imperial sealed letter was sent instructing Teli: "White-haired, exhausting the classics, teaching people without weariness, neither excess nor shortfall—scholars take him as their model; formerly an excellent name was already granted; now again the intent is conveyed."

entries.zh: 癸丑，特立卒，年七十五。
entries.en: In guichou Teli died at the age of seventy-five.
entries.literal: In guichou, Teli died, age seventy-five.

entries.zh: 中統二年，詔曰：「中庸先生學有淵源，行無瑕玷，雖經喪亂，不改故常，未遂丘園之賁，俄興窀穸之悲。
entries.en: In the second year of Zhongtong an edict read: "Master of the Mean—his learning ran deep, his conduct without blemish; though he lived through chaos he did not change his ways; he had not yet received the full honor due a recluse when suddenly the grief of burial arose.
entries.literal: In the second year of Zhongtong, an edict said: "Master of the Mean—learning has deep springs, conduct without flaw; though passing through mourning and disorder, he did not alter his old constancy; he had not yet attained the adornment of hill and garden, when suddenly arose the grief of the burial mound.

entries.zh: 可復賜前號，以彰寵數。」
entries.en: Let his former title be granted again to display imperial favor."
entries.literal: He may again be granted the former title to display imperial favor."

entries.zh: 特立所著書有《易集說》、《歷年系事記》。
entries.en: Teli's works included Collected Explanations of the Changes and Annals of Events by Year.
entries.literal: Books Teli authored include Collected Explanations of the Changes and Annals of Events by Year.

entries.zh: 張特立，字文舉，東明人。
entries.en: Zhang Teli, courtesy name Wenju, was from Dongming.
entries.literal: Zhang Teli, style name Wenju, was a man of Dongming.

entries.zh: 初名永，避金衛紹王諱，易今名。
entries.en: His original name was Yong; to avoid the taboo name of the Jin Prince Shao of Wei, he adopted his present name.
entries.literal: His original name was Yong; to avoid the taboo of Jin's Prince Shao of Wei, he changed to his present name.

entries.zh: 中泰和進士，為偃師主簿。
entries.en: He passed the jinshi examination in the Taihe era and became chief clerk of Yanshi.
entries.literal: In the Taihe era he passed the jinshi examination and served as chief clerk of Yanshi.

entries.zh: 改宣德州司候。
entries.en: He was later appointed judicial officer of Xuande Prefecture.
entries.literal: He was transferred to be judicial officer of Xuande Prefecture.

entries.zh: 州多金國戚，號難治，特立至官，俱往謁之。
entries.en: The prefecture had many Jin imperial kinsmen and was notoriously hard to govern; when Teli took office, they all came to pay their respects.
entries.literal: The prefecture had many Jin imperial clansmen and was called hard to govern; when Teli arrived in office, all went to pay court calls on him.

entries.zh: 有五將軍率家奴劫民群羊，特立命大索閭里，遂過將軍家，溫言誘之曰：「將軍宅寧有盜羊者邪，聊視之以杜眾口。」
entries.en: A general known as the Fifth General had his household slaves seize villagers' flocks; Teli ordered a thorough search of the neighborhood and then called at the general's house, saying mildly, "Surely there are no sheep thieves in your residence, General—but let us have a look to silence gossip."
entries.literal: There was a Fifth General who led household slaves to rob the people's flocks of sheep; Teli ordered a great search through the lanes and quarters, then passed by the general's house and with gentle words coaxed him, saying: "In the general's residence could there be sheep thieves? Let us just look to silence the crowd's mouths."

entries.zh: 潛使人索其後庭，得羊數十。
entries.en: He secretly had the rear courtyard searched and found several dozen sheep.
entries.literal: Secretly he sent men to search the rear courtyard and obtained several tens of sheep.

entries.zh: 遂縛其奴繫獄，其子匿他舍，捕得之，以近族得減死論。
entries.en: He bound the slaves and jailed them; the son, hiding elsewhere, was captured and, because of near kinship, received a reduced sentence short of death.
entries.literal: Thereupon he bound the slaves and imprisoned them; the son hid in another lodging and was captured; because of near kinship he received reduced sentence from death.

entries.zh: 豪貴由是遵法，民賴以全。
entries.en: The powerful henceforth obeyed the law, and the people were protected.
entries.literal: The powerful and noble from this obeyed the law, and the people relied on this to be preserved whole.

entries.zh: 正大初，遷洛陽令。
entries.en: Early in the Zhengda era he was appointed magistrate of Luoyang.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Zhengda, he was transferred to magistrate of Luoyang.

entries.zh: 時軍旅數起，郡縣窘迫，東帥紇石烈牙兀䚟又侮慢儒士。
entries.en: Armies marched repeatedly, counties were strapped for resources, and the eastern commander He-shilie Yarucha treated scholars with contempt.
entries.literal: At the time armies and campaigns arose repeatedly, commanderies and counties were pressed tight, and the eastern commander He-shilie Yarucha also insulted and slighted Confucian scholars.

entries.zh: 會移鎮陝右，道經洛陽，見特立淳古，不禮之，遽責令治糗具，期三日足，後期如軍法。
entries.en: When he was transferred to garrison western Shaanxi and passed through Luoyang, he found Teli plain and unassuming, showed him no courtesy, and abruptly ordered him to supply army rations within three days on pain of military law.
entries.literal: It happened he was transferred to garrison the right of Shaanxi, his route passing Luoyang; seeing Teli's plain antiquity, he did not treat him with ritual, but abruptly charged him to prepare dried provisions, fixing three days to be sufficient—after the deadline as military law.

entries.zh: 縣民素賢特立，爭輸於庭，帥大奇之。
entries.en: The people of the county, who had long admired Teli, rushed to deliver supplies to the magistrate's court, and the commander was astonished.
entries.literal: The county people had long esteemed Teli and vied to deliver supplies in the courtyard; the commander was greatly astonished.

entries.zh: 既而拜監察御史，首言世宗諸孫不宜幽囚；
entries.en: He was soon appointed investigating censor and first memorialized that Emperor Shizong's grandsons should not be kept in confinement;
entries.literal: Soon after he was appointed investigating censor and first said that Shizong's grandsons should not be held in secret imprisonment;

entries.zh: 尚書右丞顏盞石魯與細民爭田，參知政事徒單兀典諂事近習，皆當罷黜。
entries.en: that Right Assistant Minister Yanzhan Shilu was wrangling over land with commoners, and Participating Administrator Tushan Wudian was currying favor with the emperor's intimates—all should be removed from office.
entries.literal: Right Assistant Minister of the Secretariat Yanzhan Shilu contended for fields with common people, and Participating Administrator Tushan Wudian flattered and served those near at hand—all should be dismissed.

entries.zh: 執政者忌之。
entries.en: The chief ministers resented him.
entries.literal: Those in power resented him.

entries.zh: 會平章政事白撒犒軍陝西，特立又劾其掾不法。
entries.en: When Grand Councilor Bai Sa went to reward the troops in Shaanxi, Teli again impeached his staff for misconduct.
entries.literal: It happened that Grand Councilor Bai Sa was rewarding the army in Shaanxi; Teli again impeached his clerks for unlawful conduct.

entries.zh: 白撒訴於世宗，言特立所言事失實，世宗宥之，遂歸田裡。
entries.en: Bai Sa complained to Emperor Shizong that Teli's charges were false; the emperor pardoned Teli, who then retired to the countryside.
entries.literal: Bai Sa complained to Shizong, saying Teli's stated matters were not factual; Shizong pardoned him, and he thereupon returned to fields and villages.

entries.zh: 古之君子，負經世之術，度時不可為，故高蹈以全其志。
entries.en: Men of old who mastered the arts of governing the realm, when they judged that the times forbade action, would withdraw to lofty seclusion to keep their purpose intact.
entries.literal: The gentleman of antiquity, bearing the arts of ordering the world, gauged that the times would not permit action, and therefore lifted his steps high to preserve his aspirations in full.

entries.zh: 使得其時，未嘗不欲仕，仕而行所學，及物之功豈少哉。
entries.en: Given the right moment, they were always ready to serve; and once in office they applied their learning—the good they did for the world was by no means small.
entries.literal: If they obtained the right time, they had never been unwilling to serve in office; to serve and put what they had learned into practice—how could their achievements reaching others have been slight!

entries.zh: 後世之士，其所蘊蓄或未至，而好以跡為高，當邦有道之時，且遁世離群，謂之隱士。
entries.en: Scholars of later times, whose learning often fell short of the mark, nonetheless prided themselves on lofty withdrawal; even when the realm was well governed they would flee society and call themselves recluses.
entries.literal: Scholars of later ages, whose stored learning had perhaps not yet arrived at completeness, yet loved to take conduct as loftiness; when the state had the Way, they yet withdrew from the world and separated from the crowd, and were called recluses.

entries.zh: 世主亦苟取其名而強起之，及考其實，不如所聞，則曰「是欺世釣譽者也」，上下豈不兩失也哉！
entries.en: Rulers too would seize on their reputations and compel them to office; when scrutiny showed them less than their fame, the verdict was "mere deceivers of the age fishing for praise"—a loss for ruler and subject alike.
entries.literal: The lord of the age also would hastily take their names and force them to rise; when their reality was examined and did not match what was heard, then it was said, "These are those who deceive the world and fish for renown"—would not high and low alike lose doubly!

entries.zh: 段氏，隆興霍榮妻也。
entries.en: Lady Duan was the wife of Huo Rong of Longxing.
entries.literal: Lady Duan was the wife of Huo Rong of Longxing.

entries.zh: 榮無子，嘗乞人為養子。
entries.en: Rong had no son and once begged for someone to be adopted as his heir.
entries.literal: Rong had no son and once begged someone to be an adopted son.

entries.zh: 榮卒，段氏年二十六，養舅姑以孝稱。
entries.en: When Rong died Duan was twenty-six. She supported her parents-in-law and was famed for filial devotion.
entries.literal: When Rong died Duan was twenty-six and nourished her parents-in-law, famed for filial piety.

entries.zh: 舅姑歿，榮諸父仲汶貪其產，謂段曰：「汝子假子也，可令歸宗。
entries.en: When her parents-in-law died Rong's paternal uncle Zhongwen coveted her property and said to Duan, "Your son is a borrowed son. He can be sent back to his clan.
entries.literal: When her parents-in-law died Rong's paternal uncle Zhongwen coveted her property and said to Duan: "Your son is a borrowed son; he can be sent back to his clan.

entries.zh: 汝無子，宜改適，霍氏業汝無預焉。」
entries.en: You have no son. You should remarry. The Huo family property has nothing to do with you."
entries.literal: You have no son; you should remarry; Huo family property has nothing to do with you."

entries.zh: 段曰：「家資不可計，但再醮非義，尚容妾思之。」
entries.en: Duan said, "The family assets are beyond counting, but remarriage is not righteous. Allow me to consider it."
entries.literal: Duan said: "Family assets cannot be counted, but remarriage is not righteous; still allow me to consider it."

entries.zh: 即退入寢室，引針刺面，墨漬之，誓死不貳。
entries.en: She withdrew to her bedchamber, pricked her face with a needle, stained it with ink, and swore she would die rather than take a second husband.
entries.literal: She withdrew to her bedchamber, took a needle and pricked her face, stained it with ink, and swore she would die rather than take a second husband.

entries.zh: 大德二年，府上狀中書，給羊酒幣帛，仍命旌門，复役如製。
entries.en: In the second year of Dade the prefecture reported to the central secretariat. She was granted sheep, wine, silks, and cloth, an honorific gate was erected, and corvée was exempted as prescribed.
entries.literal: In the second year of Dade the prefecture reported upward to the central secretariat, granting sheep, wine, silks, and cloth, and ordering an honorific gate, with corvée exemption as prescribed.

entries.zh: 古者女子之居室也，必有傅姆師保為陳詩書圖史以訓之。
entries.en: In ancient times, a girl's household quarters would always include nurse-governesses and tutors who laid out poetry, books, maps, and histories for her instruction.
entries.literal: In antiquity, in a woman's dwelling there would always be nurse-governesses and tutors who would present poetry, books, charts, and histories to instruct her.

entries.zh: 凡左右佩服之儀，內外授受之別，與所以事父母舅姑之道，蓋無所不備也。
entries.en: The rites governing jewelry and dress, the rules separating inner from outer quarters in exchanges between men and women, and the conduct owed to parents and parents-in-law—all of this was taught in full.
entries.literal: As for the rituals of adornments worn left and right, the distinctions of giving and receiving between inner and outer quarters, and the ways of serving parents and parents-in-law, there was nothing left unprepared.

entries.zh: 而又有天子之后妃，諸侯之夫人，躬行於上，以率化之。
entries.en: Above them, empresses and consorts of the Son of Heaven and the wives of feudal lords embodied these standards themselves, setting an example from which others took their cue.
entries.literal: Moreover, the empresses and consorts of the Son of Heaven and the wives of feudal lords personally practiced these norms at the top to lead and transform others.

entries.zh: 則其居安而有淑順之稱，臨變而有貞特之操者，夫豈偶然哉。
entries.en: That women earned reputations for grace and obedience in ordinary times and showed unwavering resolve in crisis was surely no accident.
entries.literal: Thus those who in peace were called virtuous and compliant and who in crisis showed steadfast integrity—how could this have been mere chance?

entries.zh: 後世此道既廢，女生而處閨闥之中，溺情愛之私，耳不聆箴史之言，目不睹防範之具，由是動逾禮則，而往往自放於邪僻矣。
entries.en: After later ages abandoned this discipline, girls grew up shut in inner quarters, absorbed in private attachments, never hearing the admonitions of the classics, never seeing the safeguards of proper training—and so they routinely overstepped ritual propriety and often drifted into wayward conduct.
entries.literal: Later ages, once this practice was abandoned, girls were born and lived within inner chambers, drowning in private passions of affection, their ears not hearing words of admonition from histories, their eyes not seeing instruments of restraint; thus when they moved they transgressed ritual norms and often let themselves loose into depravity.

entries.zh: 苟於是時而有能以懿節自著者焉，非其生質之美，則亦豈易致哉。
