entries.en: When a woman in such an age nonetheless distinguished herself by exemplary constancy, it was either because her nature was exceptional or because such virtue was anything but easy to attain.
entries.literal: If at such a time someone could distinguish herself by admirable integrity, unless her innate character was excellent, how could it have been easily achieved?

entries.zh: 史氏之書，所以必錄而弗敢略也。
entries.en: That is why historical chronicles insist on recording such women and dare not pass them over.
entries.literal: This is why the books of the historians must record them and dare not omit them.

entries.zh: 劉氏二女，長曰貞，年十九；
entries.en: The Liu family had two daughters. The elder was named Zhen and was nineteen;
entries.literal: The two daughters of the Liu family: the elder was named Zhen, age nineteen;

entries.zh: 次曰孫，年十七。
entries.en: the younger was named Sun and was seventeen.
entries.literal: the younger was named Sun, age seventeen.

entries.zh: 龍興人，皆未許嫁。
entries.en: They were from Longxing, and neither had yet been betrothed.
entries.literal: They were from Longxing; neither had yet been betrothed.

entries.zh: 陳友諒寇龍興，其母泣謂二女曰：「城或破，置汝何所？」
entries.en: When Chen Youliang attacked Longxing, their mother wept and asked the two girls, "If the city falls, where can I keep you safe?"
entries.literal: Chen Youliang attacked Longxing; their mother weeping said to the two daughters, "If the city should fall, where shall I place you?"

entries.zh: 二女曰：「寧死不辱父母也。」
entries.en: The two daughters answered, "We would rather die than bring shame on our parents."
entries.literal: The two daughters said, "Better to die than to disgrace our parents."

entries.zh: 城陷，二女登樓，相繼自縊。
entries.en: When the city fell, the two girls went up to a tower and hanged themselves, one after the other.
entries.literal: When the city fell, the two daughters ascended a tower and hanged themselves one after the other.

entries.zh: 婢鄭奴，亦自縊。
entries.en: Their maid Zhengnu hanged herself as well.
entries.literal: The maid Zhengnu also hanged herself.

entries.zh: 汪琰妻潘氏，徽州婺源人。
entries.en: Wang Yan's wife, Lady Pan, came from Wuyuan in Huizhou prefecture.
entries.literal: Wang Yan's wife Lady Pan was a native of Wuyuan in Huizhou.

entries.zh: 年二十八而琰卒，潘氏誓不他適，以其夫從兄之子元圭為後。
entries.en: When she was twenty-eight, Wang Yan died. Lady Pan vowed never to remarry and adopted her husband's first cousin's son Yuangui as her heir.
entries.literal: At twenty-eight Yan died; Lady Pan vowed not to marry another, and made her husband's first cousin's son Yuangui her heir.

entries.zh: 元圭時始三歲，鞠之不啻己出。
entries.en: Yuangui was only three at the time, and she reared him as tenderly as if he were her own.
entries.literal: Yuangui was then only three years old; she raised him no differently than if he were her own child.

entries.zh: 潘氏卒年六十二。
entries.en: Lady Pan died at sixty-two.
entries.literal: Lady Pan died at the age of sixty-two.

entries.zh: 元圭之子良垕，有子燕山。
entries.en: Yuangui's son Lianghou had a son named Yanshan.
entries.literal: Yuangui's son Lianghou had a son Yanshan.

entries.zh: 燕山卒時，妻李氏年二十四，無子，乃守志自誓，父母欲奪而嫁之，不聽。
entries.en: When Yanshan died, his wife Lady Li was twenty-four and had no children. She vowed to remain faithful. Her parents tried to compel her to remarry, but she refused.
entries.literal: When Yanshan died, his wife Lady Li was twenty-four, childless; she then vowed to preserve her chastity; her parents wished to force her into another marriage, but she would not listen.

entries.zh: 燕山兄子惟德，娶俞氏，惟德早死，二子甚幼，俞氏守節辛勤，不墜家業。
entries.en: Yanshan's elder brother's son Weide married Lady Yu. Weide died young, leaving two very small sons. Lady Yu endured hardship to remain faithful and kept the family fortunes from collapsing.
entries.literal: Yanshan's elder brother's son Weide married Lady Yu; Weide died early, the two sons were very young; Lady Yu preserved her chastity with arduous effort and did not let the family estate fall into ruin.

entries.zh: 故人賢汪氏之門，而稱曰三節。
entries.en: People therefore revered the Wang household for its virtue and called them the "Three Chaste Women."
entries.literal: Therefore people praised the virtue of the Wang clan's household and called them "Three Chaste Women."

entries.zh: 武用妻蘇氏，真定人，徙家京師。
entries.en: Wu Yong's wife, Lady Su, came from Zhending; the family later moved to the capital.
entries.literal: Wu Yong's wife, Lady Su, was a person of Zhending; [her family] moved their residence to the capital.

entries.zh: 用疾，蘇氏刲股為粥以進，疾即愈。
entries.en: When Yong fell sick, Lady Su sliced flesh from her own thigh to prepare porridge for him, and he soon recovered.
entries.literal: Yong fell ill; Lady Su cut flesh from her thigh to make gruel and presented it; the illness then immediately healed.

entries.zh: 生子德政，四歲而寡。
entries.en: She gave birth to a son named Dezheng and was widowed when the boy was four.
entries.literal: She bore a son, Dezheng; when he was four she became a widow.

entries.zh: 夫之兄利其資，欲逼而嫁之，不聽。
entries.en: Her husband's older brother wanted her wealth and tried to pressure her into marrying again, but she refused.
entries.literal: Her husband's elder brother coveted her property and wished to force her to remarry; she would not listen.

entries.zh: 未幾夫兄舉家死，惟餘三弱孫，蘇氏取而育之。
entries.en: Soon afterward her brother-in-law's entire family perished, leaving only three frail grandsons, whom Lady Su took in and reared.
entries.literal: Before long the husband's brother's whole household died; only three weak grandsons remained; Lady Su took them and raised them.

entries.zh: 德政長，事蘇氏至孝。
entries.en: When Dezheng came of age, he treated Lady Su with the utmost devotion.
entries.literal: Dezheng grew up and served Lady Su with utmost filial piety.

entries.zh: 蘇氏死時，天大旱，德政方掘地求水以供葬事，忽二蛇躍出，德政因默禱焉。
entries.en: Lady Su died during a severe drought. While Dezheng was digging for water for her funeral, two snakes suddenly sprang from the ground, and he prayed to them in silence.
entries.literal: When Lady Su died, the sky was greatly drought-stricken; Dezheng was just digging the earth seeking water to supply the burial affairs; suddenly two serpents leaped out; Dezheng thereupon silently prayed.

entries.zh: 二蛇一東一北，隨其地掘之，果得泉。
entries.en: One snake went east and the other north; he dug where they led and found a spring.
entries.literal: The two serpents, one [going] east and one north—following their directions in digging—indeed obtained a spring.

entries.zh: 有司上其事。
entries.en: The authorities reported the affair to the court.
entries.literal: The officials reported this matter upward.

entries.zh: 旌復其家。
entries.en: The court honored the family and granted it tax relief.
entries.literal: [They] commended and exempted her household [from corvée and taxes].

entries.zh: 帝師八思巴者，土番薩斯迦人，族款氏也。
entries.en: The Imperial Preceptor Phagpa was a Tibetan of the Sakya school and the Khön clan.
entries.literal: The Imperial Preceptor Phagpa was a Tibetan of Sakya, of the Khön clan.

entries.zh: 相傳自其祖朵栗赤，以其法佐國主霸西海者十餘世。
entries.en: Tradition holds that for more than ten generations, beginning with his ancestor Drogön, his forebears had used their religious teachings to help local rulers dominate the western regions.
entries.literal: It is transmitted that from his ancestor Drogön, using his dharma to assist the prince in dominating the Western Sea — for more than ten generations.

entries.zh: 八思巴生七歲​​，誦經數十萬言，能約通其大義，國人號之聖童，故名曰八思巴。
entries.en: At the age of seven Phagpa could recite hundreds of thousands of words of scripture and grasp their essential meaning. His countrymen hailed him as a holy child, and from this he received the name Phagpa.
entries.literal: When Phagpa was seven years old, he recited scriptures of several hundred thousand words, and could roughly penetrate their great meaning; the people of his country called him the Holy Child, hence he was named Phagpa.

entries.zh: 少長，學富五明，故又稱曰班彌怛。
entries.en: As he matured he mastered the five branches of learning and came to be known as Pandita as well.
entries.literal: As he grew somewhat older, his learning was rich in the five sciences; therefore he was also styled Pandita.

entries.zh: 歲癸丑，年十有五，謁世祖於潛邸，與語大悅，日見親禮。
entries.en: In the guichou year, at the age of fifteen, he called on Kublai Khan at his private residence. The prince delighted in their conversation and thereafter treated him with growing intimacy and honor.
entries.literal: In the year guichou, at age fifteen, he visited the Founder of the Dynasty at his princely residence; speaking with him, [the prince] was greatly pleased and daily received him with intimate honors.

entries.zh: 中統元年，世祖即位，尊為國師，授以玉印。
entries.en: When Kublai took the throne in the first year of the Zhongtong era, he honored Phagpa as State Preceptor and bestowed on him a jade seal.
entries.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong, the Founder of the Dynasty ascended the throne, honored him as State Preceptor, and conferred a jade seal upon him.

entries.zh: 命製蒙古新字，字成上之。
entries.en: The emperor ordered him to create a new Mongol script, and when it was finished Phagpa presented it to the court.
entries.literal: He was ordered to devise a new Mongol script; when the script was completed, it was presented to the throne.

entries.zh: 其字僅千餘，其母凡四十有一。
entries.en: The script contained just over a thousand characters, built from forty-one basic elements.
entries.literal: Its characters were merely a thousand-odd, and its mother elements numbered forty-one in all.

entries.zh: 其相關紐而成字者，則有韻關之法；
entries.en: Characters formed by combining related elements followed rules of rhyming linkage;
entries.literal: For those formed by linking related elements into characters, there was a method of rhyme linkage;

entries.zh: 其以二合三合四合而成字者，則有語韻之法；
entries.en: those built from two, three, or four combined elements followed rules of spoken rhyme;
entries.literal: for those formed by combining two, three, or four elements into characters, there was a method of spoken rhyme;

entries.zh: 而大要則以諧聲為宗也。
entries.en: but in essence the system was founded on phonetic representation.
entries.literal: yet in the great essentials it took harmonizing sound as its foundation.

entries.zh: 至元六年，詔頒行於天下。
entries.en: In the sixth year of the Zhiyuan era an edict ordered the script promulgated throughout the empire.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Zhiyuan, an edict ordered its promulgation throughout the realm.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「朕惟字以書言，言以紀事，此古今之通制。
entries.en: The edict read: "We hold that writing exists to fix speech in visible form, and speech exists to record affairs — a principle as old as civilization itself.
entries.literal: The edict said: "We consider that characters are used to write speech, and speech is used to record affairs — this is the universal regulation of past and present.

entries.zh: 我國家肇基朔方，俗尚簡古，未遑製作，凡施用文字，因用漢楷及畏吾字，以達本朝之言。
entries.en: Our dynasty arose in the northern steppe, where custom favored simplicity, and we had not yet devised a script of our own. For written communication we relied on Chinese characters and the Uighur script to express the language of the court.
entries.literal: Our state, establishing its foundation in the northern frontier, customarily valued simplicity and antiquity and had not yet had leisure to create [a script]; whenever applying written characters, it borrowed Han regular script and Uighur script to convey the speech of our court.

entries.zh: 考諸遼、金，以及遐方諸國，例各有字，今文治浸興，而字書有闕，於一代制度，實為未備。
entries.en: The Liao, the Jin, and the distant states beyond our borders each possessed their own writing systems. Now that civil administration is expanding, the lack of a proper script leaves our dynastic institutions incomplete.
entries.literal: Examining Liao, Jin, and the various distant countries, each in precedent had its own script; now civil governance is gradually rising, yet the character books have gaps — for the institutions of an age, this is truly incomplete.

entries.zh: 故特命國師八思巴創為蒙古新字，譯寫一切文字，期於順言達事而已。
entries.en: We therefore charged State Preceptor Phagpa with devising a new Mongol script capable of rendering all languages, so that speech might be faithfully recorded and affairs clearly communicated.
entries.literal: Therefore we specially ordered State Preceptor Phagpa to create the new Mongol script, to transliterate all scripts, aiming only at following speech and conveying affairs.

entries.zh: 自今以往，凡有璽書頒降者，並用蒙古新字，仍各以其國字副之。」
entries.en: Henceforth all imperial edicts shall be issued in the new Mongol script, with translations appended in the appropriate national scripts."
entries.literal: From now onward, whenever there are imperial writs issued and sent down, all shall use the new Mongol script, while still appending each in its own national script."

entries.zh: 遂升號八思巴曰大寶法王，更賜玉印。
entries.en: Phagpa was then elevated to the title Great Precious Dharma King and presented with a new jade seal.
entries.literal: Thereupon his title was raised: Phagpa was called Great Precious Dharma King, and a jade seal was again bestowed.

entries.zh: 八思巴時，又有國師膽巴者，一名功嘉葛剌思，西番突甘斯旦麻人。
entries.en: During Phagpa's lifetime there was also State Preceptor Dam-pa, also known as Kun-dga' rgyal-mtshan, a Tibetan from the region of Tu-gsum-brtan-ma.
entries.literal: In Phagpa's time there was also State Preceptor Dam pa, also named Kun dga' rgyal mtshan, a Tibetan of Tu gsum brtan ma.

entries.zh: 幼從西天竺古達麻失利傳習梵秘，得其法要。
entries.en: As a boy he studied esoteric Sanskrit teachings under the Indian master Gu-da-ma-shi-li and mastered their essentials.
entries.literal: In youth he followed the Western Indian Gu da ma shi li in transmitting and studying Sanskrit secrets, obtaining the essentials of his methods.

entries.zh: 中統間，帝師八思巴薦之。
entries.en: During the Zhongtong era Imperial Preceptor Phagpa recommended him to the court.
entries.literal: During the Zhongtong period, Imperial Preceptor Phagpa recommended him.

entries.zh: 時懷孟大旱，世祖命禱之，立雨。
entries.en: When a severe drought struck Huai and Meng prefectures, Kublai ordered him to pray for rain, and rain fell at once.
entries.literal: At that time Huai prefecture and Meng prefecture suffered great drought; the Founder of the Dynasty ordered him to pray, and rain fell immediately.

entries.zh: 又嘗咒食投龍湫，頃之奇花異果上尊湧出波面，取以上進，世祖大悅。
entries.en: On another occasion he consecrated food and cast it into the Dragon Pool. Moments later rare flowers, exotic fruits, and fine wine rose to the surface; he gathered them and presented them to the emperor, who was delighted.
entries.literal: He also once charmed food and cast it into the Dragon Pool; in a moment rare flowers and exotic fruits and superior wine surged up on the wave surface; taking them, he presented them upward — the Founder of the Dynasty was greatly pleased.

entries.zh: 至元末，以不容於時相桑哥，力請西歸。
entries.en: Near the end of the Zhiyuan era he fell out with the chief minister Sangge and pressed hard for permission to return to Tibet.
entries.literal: Near the end of Zhiyuan, because he was not tolerated by the chief minister Sangge, he strenuously requested to return west.

entries.zh: 既復召還，謫之潮州。
entries.en: When he was summoned back to court he was instead banished to Chaozhou.
entries.literal: After being summoned back again, he was banished to Chaozhou.

entries.zh: 時樞密副使月的迷失鎮潮，而妻得奇疾，膽巴以所持數珠加其身，即愈。
entries.en: The vice commissioner of military affairs Yüede-shizhi was then stationed at Chaozhou. When his wife fell gravely ill, Dam-pa laid his prayer beads upon her and she recovered at once.
entries.literal: At that time Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Yuedishizhi was stationed at Chao, and his wife contracted a strange illness; Dam pa placed the prayer beads he carried upon her body, and she was immediately cured.

entries.zh: 又嘗為月的迷失言異夢及己還朝期，後皆驗。
entries.en: He also told Yüede-shizhi of strange dreams and predicted the date of his own return to the capital — predictions that later came true.
entries.literal: He also once told Yuedishizhi of strange dreams and the date of his own return to court — afterward all were verified.

entries.zh: 元貞間，海都犯西番界，成宗命禱於摩訶葛剌神，已而捷書果至；
entries.en: During the Yuanzhen era, when Haidu invaded the Tibetan frontier, Emperor Chengzong ordered prayers offered to the god Mahākāla. Victory dispatches soon followed;
entries.literal: During Yuanzhen, Haidu violated the Tibetan border; Emperor Chengzong ordered prayers to the Mahākāla deity — before long victory reports indeed arrived;

entries.zh: 又為成宗禱疾，遄愈，賜與甚厚，且詔分御前校尉十人為之導從。
entries.en: and when he prayed for Chengzong's recovery from illness the emperor was quickly restored to health. The court rewarded him lavishly and assigned ten officers from the imperial guard as his personal escort.
entries.literal: he also prayed for Chengzong's illness, which swiftly healed; gifts were very generous, and an edict additionally assigned ten Imperial Bodyguard officers from the personal guard as his escorts.

entries.zh: 成宗北巡，命膽巴以像輿前導。
entries.en: When Chengzong made his northern tour, he ordered Dam-pa to precede the procession bearing a sacred image in a palanquin.
entries.literal: When Chengzong toured north, he ordered Dam pa to lead the way with an image palanquin.

entries.zh: 過雲州，語諸弟子曰：「此地有靈怪，恐驚乘輿，當密持神咒以厭之。」
entries.en: Passing through Yunzhou, he told his disciples, "This region harbors malevolent spirits that may frighten the imperial procession. Keep your protective spells ready in secret."
entries.literal: Passing Yun prefecture, he told his disciples: "This place has spirit monsters; fearing they may startle the imperial carriage, you should secretly hold divine spells to subdue them."

entries.zh: 未幾，風雨大至，眾咸震懼，惟幄殿無虞，复賜碧鈿杯一。
entries.en: Before long a violent storm broke. Everyone was terrified, yet the imperial pavilion remained untouched. The emperor again bestowed on him a cup inlaid with green gems.
entries.literal: Before long, wind and rain came greatly; the multitude all trembled with fear, but only the curtained hall was unharmed; he was again bestowed one cup of green inlay.

entries.zh: 大德七年夏卒。
entries.en: He died in the summer of the seventh year of the Dade era.
entries.literal: In the summer of the seventh year of Dade he died.

entries.zh: 皇慶間，追號大覺普惠廣照無上膽巴帝師。
entries.en: During the Huangqing era he was posthumously honored as Imperial Preceptor Dam-pa of Great Awakening, Universal Beneficence, and Broad Illumination.
entries.literal: During Huangqing, he was posthumously titled Great Awakening, Universal Beneficence, Broad Illumination, Supreme Imperial Preceptor Dam pa.

entries.zh: 元起朔方，固已崇尚釋教。
entries.en: From its origins on the northern steppe the Yuan dynasty had already embraced Buddhism.
entries.literal: The Yuan arose in the northern frontier and from the outset already venerated Buddhism.

entries.zh: 及得西域，世祖以其地廣而險遠，民獷而好鬥，思有以因其俗而柔其人，乃郡縣土番之地，設官分職，而領之於帝師。
entries.en: After conquering the western territories Kublai saw that the region was vast, remote, and perilous, its inhabitants fierce and warlike. Seeking to govern them through their own customs, he organized Tibetan lands into administrative units under officials appointed by the Imperial Preceptor.
entries.literal: When they obtained the Western Regions, the Founder of the Dynasty, because that land was broad yet perilous and distant, and the people fierce and fond of fighting, thought to have some means of following their customs to soften their people; thereupon in the Tibetan lands they established prefectures and counties, set officials and divided duties, and placed them under the leadership of the Imperial Preceptor.

entries.zh: 乃立宣政院，其為使位居第二者，必以僧為之，出帝師所辟舉，而總其政於內外者，帥臣以下，亦必僧俗並用，而軍民通攝。
entries.en: The court established the Xuanzheng Commission, whose second-ranking commissioner was always a monk nominated by the Imperial Preceptor. Regional commanders and their subordinates combined monastic and lay officials, exercising authority over both military and civilian affairs.
entries.literal: Thereupon they established the Xuanzheng Commission; for its commissioner, whoever held the second rank must be a monk, nominated by the Imperial Preceptor, while those overseeing affairs within and without — commanders and below — also had to employ monks and laity together, with military and civil jointly administered.

entries.zh: 於是帝師之命，與詔敕並行於西土。
entries.en: Henceforth the Imperial Preceptor's orders carried equal weight with imperial edicts throughout the western territories.
entries.literal: Thus the commands of the Imperial Preceptor proceeded in parallel with imperial edicts throughout the western lands.

entries.zh: 百年之間，朝廷所以敬禮而尊信之者，無所不用其至。
entries.en: For a century the court spared no gesture of reverence and trust toward the Imperial Preceptor.
entries.literal: Within a hundred years, in all the court's showing of respect and honoring trust toward him, there was nothing to which they did not bring their utmost.

entries.zh: 雖帝后妃主，皆因受戒而為之膜拜。
entries.en: Even empresses and imperial consorts received ordination from him and bowed before him in worship.
entries.literal: Even empresses and imperial consorts all, because of receiving precepts, performed prostration before him.

entries.zh: 正衙朝會，百官班列，而帝師亦或專席於坐隅。
entries.en: At formal court audiences, while officials stood in their ranks, the Imperial Preceptor sometimes occupied a seat of honor apart from them.
entries.literal: At regular court assemblies in the main hall, the hundred officials stood in ranks, yet the Imperial Preceptor also sometimes had a special seat in a corner of the seating.

entries.zh: 且每帝即位之始，降詔褒護，必敕章佩監絡珠為字以賜，蓋其重之如此。
entries.en: At the start of every new reign the court issued edicts of praise and protection, invariably ordering the Directorate of Seals to inscribe his titles in pearls for presentation — such was the esteem in which he was held.
entries.literal: Moreover, at the beginning of each emperor's accession, edicts of praise and protection were sent down, invariably ordering the Directorate of Seals and Credentials to inscribe pearl characters to bestow — such was the weight they placed upon him.

entries.zh: 其未至而迎之，則中書大臣馳驛累百騎以往，所過供億送迎。
entries.en: To welcome him before his arrival, a chief minister of the Central Secretariat would ride out with a hundred mounted escorts, and every post station along the route would supply provisions and attendants.
entries.literal: Before his arrival, to welcome him, a chief minister of the Central Secretariat would gallop post-horses with a cumulative hundred riders to go forth; wherever he passed, provisions and escort were furnished.

entries.zh: 比至京師，則敕大府假法駕半仗，以為前導，詔省、台、院官以及百司庶府，並服銀鼠質孫。
entries.en: Upon reaching the capital the Grand Provisionery lent half the imperial procession as his escort, and officials of the Secretariat, Censorate, Court, and all government offices wore silver-rat fur robes in his honor.
entries.literal: When he reached the capital, the Grand Provisionery was ordered to lend half the imperial regalia as vanguard; officials of the Secretariat, Censorate, and Court, and the hundred offices and various bureaus all wore silver-rat zhisun.

entries.zh: 用每歲二月八日迎佛，威儀往迓，且命禮部尚書、郎中專督迎接。
entries.en: Each year on the eighth day of the second month the court welcomed the Buddha with full ceremonial escort, the Minister of Rites and a director being specially assigned to oversee the reception.
entries.literal: Using the eighth day of the second month each year to welcome the Buddha, with full ceremonial retinue going to meet him, and additionally ordering the Minister of Rites and a director to supervise the reception exclusively.

entries.zh: 及其卒而歸葬舍利，又命百官出郭祭餞。
entries.en: When he died and his relics were escorted home for burial, all officials were ordered to go beyond the city walls to offer farewell sacrifices.
entries.literal: When he died and his relics were returned for burial, the hundred officials were again ordered to go beyond the walls to offer sacrificial farewell.

entries.zh: 大德九年，專遣平章政事鐵木兒乘​​傳護送，賻金五百兩、銀千兩、幣帛萬匹、鈔三千錠。
entries.en: In the ninth year of the Dade era the court specially dispatched Grand Councillor Temür by relay post to escort the remains, with funeral gifts of five hundred taels of gold, a thousand taels of silver, ten thousand bolts of silk, and three thousand ingots of paper money.
entries.literal: In the ninth year of Dade, a special dispatch sent the Grand Councillor Temür traveling post-horses to escort and protect; funeral gifts were five hundred taels of gold, a thousand taels of silver, ten thousand bolts of silks, and three thousand ingots of paper money.

entries.zh: 皇慶二年，加至賻金五千兩、銀一萬五千兩、錦綺雜彩共一萬七千匹。
entries.en: In the second year of the Huangqing era the standard was raised to five thousand taels of gold, fifteen thousand taels of silver, and seventeen thousand bolts of brocade and colored silk.
entries.literal: In the second year of Huangqing, it was increased to funeral gifts of five thousand taels of gold, fifteen thousand taels of silver, and brocades and miscellaneous silks totaling seventeen thousand bolts.

entries.zh: 雖其昆弟子姓之往來，有司亦供億無乏。
entries.en: Even the comings and goings of his disciples, nephews, and kinsmen were supplied with provisions at public expense.
entries.literal: Even for the coming and going of his disciples, nephews, and clansmen, the responsible offices also furnished provisions without shortage.

entries.zh: 泰定間，以帝師弟公哥亦思監將至，詔中書持羊酒郊勞；
entries.en: During the Taiding era, when the Imperial Preceptor's younger brother Kun-dga' ye-shes was expected, the Central Secretariat was ordered to greet him in the suburbs with sheep and wine;
entries.literal: During Taiding, because the Imperial Preceptor's younger brother Kun dga' ye shes was about to arrive, an edict ordered the Central Secretariat to hold sheep and wine for suburban welcome;

entries.zh: 而其兄瑣南藏卜遂尚公主，封白蘭王，賜金印，給圓符。
entries.en: while his elder brother Sog-bzang-po married an imperial princess, was enfeoffed as Prince of Bailan, and received a gold seal and round tallies of authority.
entries.literal: while his elder brother Sog bzang po then married an imperial princess, was enfeoffed as Prince of Bailan, bestowed a gold seal, and given round tallies.

entries.zh: 其弟子之號司空、司徒、國公，佩金玉印章者，前後相望。
entries.en: His disciples who held titles such as Minister of Works, Minister of Education, and State Duke, wearing gold and jade seals, formed an unbroken succession.
entries.literal: His disciples bearing the titles Minister of Works, Minister of Education, and State Duke, wearing gold and jade seals — one after another in sight.

entries.zh: 為其徒者，怙勢恣睢，日新月盛，氣焰熏灼，延於四方，為害不可勝言。
entries.en: His followers abused their power with growing arrogance day by day. Their influence blazed across the realm, and the harm they inflicted is beyond reckoning.
entries.literal: Those who were his followers, relying on power and acting wantonly, daily grew in new abundance; their aura scorched and extended to the four directions — the harm cannot be fully told.

entries.zh: 有楊璉真加者，世祖用為江南釋教總統，發掘故宋趙氏諸陵之在錢唐、紹興者及其大臣塚墓凡一百一所；
entries.en: Yang Lianzhenjia, whom Kublai appointed president of the Buddhist clergy in Jiangnan, desecrated one hundred and one tombs — including the Song imperial Zhao tombs at Qiantang and Shaoxing and the graves of Song ministers;
entries.literal: There was Yang Lianzhenjia, whom the Founder of the Dynasty employed as Jiangnan Buddhist President; he excavated the former Song Zhao clan tombs located at Qiantang and Shaoxing and their great ministers' graves — one hundred and one places in all;

entries.zh: 戕殺平民四人；
entries.en: murdered four commoners;
entries.literal: slaughtered four common civilians;

entries.zh: 受人獻美女寶物無算；
entries.en: accepted countless bribes of beautiful women and precious goods;
entries.literal: received from people offerings of beautiful women and treasures beyond counting;

entries.zh: 且攘奪盜取財物，計金一千七百兩、銀六千八百兩、玉帶九、玉器大小百一十有一、雜寶貝百五十有二、大珠五十兩、鈔一十一萬六千二百錠、田二萬三千畝；
entries.en: and plundered property totaling one thousand seven hundred taels of gold, six thousand eight hundred taels of silver, nine jade belts, one hundred eleven jade vessels large and small, one hundred fifty-two miscellaneous gems and shells, fifty taels of large pearls, one hundred eleven thousand six hundred ingots of paper money, and twenty-three thousand mu of farmland;
entries.literal: moreover plundered and stole property, totaling: gold one thousand seven hundred taels, silver six thousand eight hundred taels, nine jade belts, large and small jade vessels one hundred and eleven, miscellaneous treasures and shells one hundred and fifty-two, large pearls fifty taels, paper money one hundred eleven thousand six hundred ingots, fields twenty-three thousand mu;

entries.zh: 私庇平民不輸公賦者二萬三千戶。
entries.en: and sheltered twenty-three thousand households who evaded public taxes.
entries.literal: privately sheltered twenty-three thousand households of common people who did not pay public taxes.

entries.zh: 他所藏匿未露者不論也。
entries.en: To say nothing of what he concealed and was never discovered.
entries.literal: What he concealed elsewhere and did not expose is not reckoned.

entries.zh: 又至大元年，上都開元寺西僧強市民薪，民訴諸留守李璧。
entries.en: In the first year of the Zhida era, at Shangdu's Kaiyuan Temple a Tibetan monk forcibly seized firewood from townspeople, who appealed to the resident commissioner Li Bi.
entries.literal: Moreover, in the first year of Zhida, at Shangdu's Kaiyuan Temple a Western monk forcibly seized firewood from townspeople; the people complained to the resident commissioner Li Bi.

entries.zh: 璧方詢問其由，僧已率其黨持白梃突入公府，隔案引璧發，捽諸地，捶撲交下，拽之以歸，閉諸空室，久乃得脫，奔訴於朝，遇赦以免。
entries.en: While Bi was still investigating, the monk led his followers armed with clubs into the government office, seized Bi by the hair across his desk, threw him to the ground, and beat him severely. They dragged him away and locked him in a room; he eventually escaped and appealed to the capital, but received amnesty before punishment could be imposed.
entries.literal: Bi was just inquiring into the cause when the monk already led his faction holding white cudgels to burst into the government office, pulled Bi by the hair across the desk, threw him to the ground, beatings raining down, dragged him back, shut him in an empty room — only after long could he escape, ran to complain at court, and met an amnesty and was spared punishment.

entries.zh: 二年，復有僧龔柯等十八人，與諸王合兒八剌妃忽禿赤的斤爭道，拉妃墮車毆之，且有犯上等語，事聞，詔釋不問。
entries.en: The following year eighteen monks led by Gong'e disputed the right of way with the consort Hutuchidijin of Prince Her-bala, pulled her from her carriage, beat her, and uttered words of lese-majesty. When the matter was reported, an edict ordered them released without punishment.
entries.literal: In the second year, again there were eighteen monks including Gong'e and others who disputed the road with the consort Hutuchidijin of Prince Herbala; they pulled the consort from her carriage and beat her, and moreover had words offending superiors — when the matter was reported, an edict released them without inquiry.

entries.zh: 而宣政院臣方奏取旨：凡民毆西僧者，截其手；
entries.en: Meanwhile the Xuanzheng Commission was petitioning for an edict: any commoner who struck a Tibetan monk was to have his hand cut off;
entries.literal: Meanwhile members of the Xuanzheng Commission were just memorializing to obtain instructions: whenever commoners beat Western monks, cut off their hands;

entries.zh: 詈之者，斷其舌。
entries.en: anyone who cursed them was to have his tongue cut out.
entries.literal: who reviled them, cut off their tongues.

entries.zh: 時仁宗居東宮，聞之，亟奏寢其令。
entries.en: Crown Prince Renzong, residing in the Eastern Palace, heard of this and immediately memorialized to have the order withdrawn.
entries.literal: At that time Emperor Renzong resided in the Eastern Palace; hearing of it, he urgently memorialized to suspend the order.

entries.zh: 歲己卯，太祖自乃蠻命近臣札八兒、劉仲祿持詔求之。
entries.en: In the jimao year the Founder, then campaigning against the Naiman, ordered his close attendant Zhaba'er and Liu Zhonglu to bring an edict summoning him.
entries.literal: In the year jimao, the Founder of the Dynasty, from the Naiman, ordered his close attendant Zhaba'er and Liu Zhonglu to hold an edict seeking him.

entries.zh: 處機一日忽語其徒，使促裝，曰：「天使來召我，我當往。」
entries.en: One day Chuji suddenly told his disciples to pack quickly, saying, "Envoys have come to summon me. I must go."
entries.literal: Chuji one day suddenly told his disciples to hurry their packing, saying: "Envoys have come to summon me; I must go."

entries.zh: 翌日，二人者至，處機乃與弟子十有八人同往見焉。
entries.en: The next day the two envoys arrived, and Chuji set out with eighteen disciples to meet them.
entries.literal: The next day the two arrived; Chuji then went with eighteen disciples together to meet them.

entries.zh: 明年，宿留山北，先馳表謝，拳拳以止殺為勸。
entries.en: The following year, while lodging north of the mountains, he sent a memorial of thanks earnestly urging the emperor to stop killing.
entries.literal: The following year, lodging north of the mountains, he first sent a memorial of thanks, earnestly urging cessation of killing.

entries.zh: 又明年，趣使再至，乃發撫州，經數十國，為地萬有餘里。
entries.en: The year after, envoys came again to urge him onward. He set out from Fuzhou and traveled through dozens of states — a journey of more than ten thousand li.
entries.literal: The year after, envoys urging him came again; he then set out from Fuzhou, passing through dozens of states — a journey of more than ten thousand li.

entries.zh: 蓋蹀血戰場，避寇叛域，絕糧沙漠，自崑崙歷四載而始達雪山。
entries.en: He crossed blood-soaked battlefields, skirted rebel-held territories, and nearly starved in the desert; from Kunlun it took four years to reach the Snow Mountain.
entries.literal: He tramped through bloody battlefields, skirted rebel territories, and ran out of food in the desert; from Kunlun it took four years before he reached Snow Mountain.

entries.zh: 常馬行深雪中，馬上舉策試之，未及積雪之半。
entries.en: Often riding through snow so deep that when he raised his whip from horseback it did not reach halfway to the surface.
entries.literal: Often riding through deep snow, he would raise his whip from horseback to test it — yet not reach half the depth of the accumulated snow.

entries.zh: 既見，太祖大悅，賜食、設廬帳甚飭。
entries.en: When he met the Founder, the emperor was greatly pleased, bestowed food upon him, and set up a tent with great care.
entries.literal: Upon meeting [the Founder], the Founder was greatly pleased, bestowed food, and set up a tent lodging with great care.

entries.zh: 太祖時方西征，日事攻戰，處機每言欲一天下者，必在乎不嗜殺人。
entries.en: The Founder was then on western campaigns, fighting daily. Chuji repeatedly said that whoever wishes to unify the realm must begin by ceasing to delight in killing.
entries.literal: The Founder was then on western campaigns, daily engaged in attack and battle; Chuji each time said that whoever wishes to unify the realm must lie in not being fond of killing people.

entries.zh: 及問為治之方，則對以敬天愛民為本。
entries.en: When asked how to govern, he answered that revering Heaven and loving the people were the foundation.
entries.literal: When asked the method of governing, he replied that revering Heaven and loving the people were the foundation.

entries.zh: 問長生久視之道，則告以清心寡欲為要。
entries.en: Asked about the path to longevity, he said that purifying the mind and reducing desires were essential.
entries.literal: Asked about the Way of long life and long vision, he told them that purifying the mind and reducing desires were essential.

entries.zh: 太祖深契其言，曰：「天錫仙翁，以寤朕志。」
entries.en: The Founder was deeply moved and said, "Heaven has sent the Immortal Elder to awaken my will."
entries.literal: The Founder deeply matched his words, saying: "Heaven bestows the Immortal Elder to awaken Our will."

entries.zh: 命左右書之，且以訓諸子焉。
entries.en: He ordered attendants to write this down and used it to instruct his sons.
entries.literal: He ordered attendants to write it down, and moreover used it to instruct his sons.

entries.zh: 於是錫之虎符，副以璽書，不斥其名，惟曰「神仙」。
entries.en: He then bestowed on him a tiger tally and imperial writ, addressing him only as "Immortal" without using his personal name.
entries.literal: Thereupon he bestowed on him a tiger tally, with imperial writ as supplement, not addressing him by his personal name but only calling him "Immortal."

entries.zh: 一日雷震，太祖以問，處機對曰：「雷，天威也。
entries.en: One day thunder crashed. The Founder asked its meaning, and Chuji replied, "Thunder is Heaven's majesty.
entries.literal: One day thunder crashed; the Founder asked about it, and Chuji replied: "Thunder is Heaven's majesty.

entries.zh: 人罪莫大於不孝，不孝則不順乎天，故天威震動以警之。
entries.en: No human crime is greater than unfilial piety. Unfilial conduct defies Heaven, and so Heaven shakes with thunder to warn the people.
entries.literal: Among human crimes none is greater than unfilial conduct; unfilial conduct then is not compliant with Heaven — therefore Heaven's majesty shakes to warn them.

entries.zh: 似聞境內不孝者多，陛下宜明天威，以導有眾。」
entries.en: I hear that unfilial conduct is widespread within the realm. Your Majesty should make Heaven's majesty clear to guide the people."
entries.literal: It seems I have heard that within the borders unfilial persons are many; Your Majesty should clarify Heaven's majesty to guide the multitude."

entries.zh: 太祖從之。
entries.en: The Founder followed his advice.
entries.literal: The Founder followed this.

entries.zh: 歲癸未，太祖大獵於東山，馬踣，處機請曰：「天道好生，陛下春秋高，數畋獵，非宜。」
entries.en: In the guiwei year the Founder held a great hunt on the Eastern Mountain. When his horse stumbled, Chuji said, "Heaven's Way cherishes life. Your Majesty is advanced in years, and frequent hunting is unfitting."
entries.literal: In the year guiwei, the Founder made a great hunt on the Eastern Mountain; his horse stumbled, and Chuji requested: "Heaven's Way loves life; Your Majesty's years are high, and frequent hunting is not fitting."

entries.zh: 太祖為罷獵者久之。
entries.en: The Founder accordingly refrained from hunting for a long time.
entries.literal: The Founder for this reason ceased hunting for a long time.

entries.zh: 時國兵踐蹂中原，河南、北尤甚，民罹俘戮，無所逃命。
entries.en: At that time the armies trampled the Central Plain, and Henan and Hebei suffered most grievously. The people faced capture and slaughter with nowhere to flee.
entries.literal: At that time the state's armies trampled the Central Plain; Henan and Hebei suffered especially — the people met capture and slaughter with nowhere to flee for their lives.

entries.zh: 處機還燕，使其徒持牒招求於戰伐之餘，由是為人奴者得復為良，與濱死而得更生者，毋慮二三萬人。
entries.en: Chuji returned to Yan and sent his disciples out with documents to seek survivors in the war-ravaged lands. Those who had been enslaved were restored to free status, and those snatched from death numbered no fewer than twenty or thirty thousand.
entries.literal: Chuji returned to Yan and had his disciples hold documents to recruit and seek out survivors in the aftermath of warfare — thereby those who had become others' slaves could again become good commoners, and those on the brink of death who obtained renewed life numbered no less than twenty or thirty thousand.

entries.zh: 中州人至今稱道之。
entries.en: People of the Central Plain still speak of this with praise.
entries.literal: People of the Central Plain to this day speak of it with praise.

entries.zh: 歲乙酉，熒惑犯尾，其占在燕，處機禱之，果退舍。
entries.en: In the yiyou year the Sparkling Deluder invaded the Tail constellation, whose omen concerned the Yan region. Chuji prayed, and the star indeed retreated.
entries.literal: In the year yiyou, the Sparkling Deluder invaded the Tail constellation; its omen lay in Yan, and Chuji prayed — it indeed retreated.

entries.zh: 丁亥，又為旱禱，期以三日雨，當名瑞應，已而亦驗。
entries.en: In the dinghai year he prayed for rain during a drought, promising three days' rain as an auspicious sign — and it came to pass.
entries.literal: In dinghai, he again prayed on account of drought; he set a term of three days' rain as an auspicious response — afterward it was also verified.

entries.zh: 有旨改賜宮名曰長春，且遣使勞問，制若曰：「朕常念神仙，神仙毋忘朕也。」
entries.en: An edict renamed his monastery Changchun and sent envoys to inquire after him, writing, "We constantly think of the Immortal; let the Immortal not forget us."
entries.literal: An order changed and bestowed on his palace the name Changchun, and moreover sent envoys to comfort and inquire, writing: "We constantly think of the Immortal; let the Immortal not forget Us."

entries.zh: 六月，浴於東溪，越二日，天大雷雨，太液池岸北水入東湖，聲聞數里，魚鱉盡去，池遂涸，而北口高岸亦崩，處機歎曰：「山其摧乎，池其涸乎，吾將與之俱乎！」
entries.en: In the sixth month, while bathing in the Eastern Stream, two days later a great thunderstorm struck. The northern waters of the Great Liquid Pool flooded into the Eastern Lake with a roar heard for several li. Fish and turtles fled, the pool dried up, and the high northern bank collapsed. Chuji sighed, "Will the mountain fall? Will the pool dry up? Must I perish with them?"
entries.literal: In the sixth month, bathing in the Eastern Stream — two days later heaven sent great wind and thunder; the northern waters of the Great Liquid Pool entered the Eastern Lake, the sound heard for several li, fish and turtles all departed, the pool thereby dried up, and the high northern bank also collapsed. Chuji sighed: "Will the mountain be destroyed? Will the pool dry up? Shall I perish together with them!"

entries.zh: 遂卒，年八十。
entries.en: He died at the age of eighty.
entries.literal: Thereupon he died, age eighty.

entries.zh: 其徒尹志平等世奉璽書襲掌其教，至大間加賜金印。
entries.en: His disciple Yin Zhiping and successors for generations received imperial writ and inherited his teaching; during the Zhida era a gold seal was additionally bestowed.
entries.literal: His disciple Yin Zhiping and others for generations received imperial writ and inherited his teaching; during the Zhida period a gold seal was additionally bestowed.

entries.zh: 處機之四傳有曰祁志誠者，居雲州金閣山，道譽甚著。
entries.en: Among Chuji's fourth-generation disciples was Qi Zhicheng, who lived on Mount Jinge in Yun prefecture and enjoyed a renowned reputation.
entries.literal: Among Chuji's fourth-generation transmitters was one named Qi Zhicheng, who dwelt on Mount Jinge in Yun prefecture; his Way's reputation was very prominent.

entries.zh: 丞相安童嘗過而問之，志誠告以修身治世之要。
entries.en: Grand Councillor An Tong once visited him, and Zhicheng taught him the essentials of self-cultivation and governance.
entries.literal: Grand Councillor An Tong once passed by and questioned him; Zhicheng told him the essentials of cultivating the self and ordering the age.

entries.zh: 安童感其言，故其相世祖也，以清靜忠厚為主。
entries.en: Moved by his words, when An Tong served as Kublai's chancellor he made purity, tranquility, and loyalty his guiding principles.
entries.literal: An Tong was moved by his words; therefore when he served as chancellor to the Founder of the Dynasty, he took purity, tranquility, and loyalty as his main principles.

entries.zh: 及罷還第，退然若無與於世者，人以為有得於志誠之言。
entries.en: When dismissed and returned home, he lived in retirement as if removed from worldly affairs. People believed he had gained wisdom from Zhicheng's teaching.
entries.literal: When dismissed and returned to his residence, he was retiring as if he had no part in worldly affairs — people thought he had gained something from Zhicheng's words.

entries.zh: 其後安童復被召入相，辭，不可，遂往決於志誠。
entries.en: Later An Tong was summoned back to the chancellorship. He wished to decline but could not refuse, and went to consult Zhicheng.
entries.literal: Afterward An Tong was again summoned to enter the chancellorship; he declined but could not refuse, and thereupon went to decide at Zhicheng's.

entries.zh: 志誠曰：「昔與子同列者何人？
entries.en: Zhicheng asked, "In former days, who were your colleagues of equal rank?
entries.literal: Zhicheng said: "In former days, who were your colleagues in the same rank?

entries.zh: 今同列者何人？」
entries.en: And who are your colleagues of equal rank now?"
entries.literal: Who are your colleagues in the same rank now?"

entries.zh: 安童悟，入見世祖，辭曰：「臣昔為宰相，年尚少，幸不失陛下事者，丞佐皆臣所師友。
entries.en: An Tong understood. He went to see Kublai and declined, saying, "When I formerly served as chancellor I was still young, and was fortunate not to fail Your Majesty's affairs because my colleagues were all my teachers and friends.
entries.literal: An Tong understood, entered to see the Founder of the Dynasty, and declined, saying: "Your subject formerly served as chancellor when still young, and was fortunate not to fail Your Majesty's affairs because my assisting colleagues were all my teachers and friends.

entries.zh: 今事臣者，皆進與臣俱，則臣之為政能有加於前乎！」
entries.en: Those who now serve under me were all promoted together with me. How can my governance surpass what it was before?"
entries.literal: Those who now serve me are all promoted together with me — how can my governance surpass what it was before!"

entries.zh: 世祖曰：「誰為卿言是？」
entries.en: The emperor asked, "Who told you this is correct?"
entries.literal: The Founder of the Dynasty said: "Who told you this is right?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「祁真人。」
entries.en: He answered, "Master Qi the Perfected One."
entries.literal: He replied: "The Perfected One Qi."

entries.zh: 世祖嘆異者久之。
entries.en: Kublai marveled at this for a long time.
entries.literal: The Founder of the Dynasty sighed in wonder for a long time.

entries.zh: 正一天師者，始自漢張​​道陵，其後四代曰盛，來居信之龍虎山。
entries.en: The Zhengyi Heavenly Master lineage began with Zhang Daoling of the Han dynasty. The fourth generation, Sheng, came to dwell at Dragon-Tiger Mountain in Xin prefecture.
entries.literal: The Zhengyi Heavenly Master began with Zhang Daoling of Han; afterward the fourth generation, named Sheng, came to dwell at Dragon-Tiger Mountain in Xin.

entries.zh: 相傳至三十六代宗演，當至元十三年，世祖已平江南，遣使召之。
entries.en: The line descended to the thirty-sixth generation, Zhang Zongyan. In the thirteenth year of the Zhiyuan era, after Kublai had pacified the south, he sent envoys to summon him.
entries.literal: The transmission reached the thirty-sixth generation, Zongyan; in the thirteenth year of Zhiyuan the Founder of the Dynasty had already pacified Jiangnan and sent envoys to summon him.

entries.zh: 至則命廷臣郊勞，待以客禮。
entries.en: Upon his arrival the court ordered officials to greet him in the suburbs and received him with the honors due a guest.
entries.literal: When he arrived, court ministers were ordered to welcome him in the suburbs and he was received with guest ceremony.

entries.zh: 及見，語之曰：「昔歲己未，朕次鄂渚，嘗令王一清往訪卿父，卿父使報朕曰：後二十年天下當混一。
entries.en: When they met, the emperor said, "In the jiwei year I was stationed at Ezhou and sent Wang Yiqing to visit your father. Your father sent word that within twenty years the realm would be unified.
entries.literal: When he was received, [the emperor] said to him: "In former years jiwei, We were stationed at Ezhu and once ordered Wang Yiqing to visit your father; your father sent word to Us saying: within twenty years the realm will be unified.

entries.zh: 神仙之言驗於今矣。」
entries.en: The immortal's prophecy has been fulfilled today."
entries.literal: The immortal's words are verified today."

entries.zh: 因命坐，錫宴，特賜玉芙蓉冠、組金無縫服，命主領江南道教，仍賜銀印。
entries.en: He was seated and feasted, presented with a jade hibiscus crown and seamless gold-thread robe, appointed to head Daoism in Jiangnan, and given a silver seal.
entries.literal: Thereupon he was ordered to be seated, granted a feast, specially bestowed a jade hibiscus crown and seamless gold-thread robe, ordered to head Jiangnan Daoism, and still given a silver seal.

entries.zh: 十八年、二十五年再入覲。
entries.en: He returned to court in the eighteenth and twenty-fifth years.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth and twenty-fifth years he again entered court audience.

entries.zh: 世祖嘗命取其祖天師所傳玉印、寶劍觀之，語侍臣曰：「朝代更易已不知其幾，而天師劍印傳子若孫尚至今日，其果有神明之相矣乎！」
entries.en: Kublai once ordered the jade seal and precious sword handed down from the founding Heavenly Master brought for inspection and told his ministers, "Dynasties have changed countless times, yet the Heavenly Master's sword and seal have passed from father to son down to this day. Can there truly be divine power in them?"
entries.literal: The Founder of the Dynasty once ordered the jade seal and precious sword transmitted by his ancestor the Heavenly Master brought for viewing, and told attending ministers: "Dynasties have changed — who knows how many times — yet the Heavenly Master's sword and seal transmitted son to grandson still reach today; do they truly have the aspect of divine intelligence!"

entries.zh: 嗟嘆久之。
entries.en: He sighed in wonder for a long time.
entries.literal: He sighed in admiration for a long time.

entries.zh: 二十九年卒，子與棣嗣，為三十七代，襲掌江南道教。
entries.en: He died in the twenty-ninth year. His son Yudi succeeded him as the thirty-seventh generation and inherited leadership of Jiangnan Daoism.
entries.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he died; his son Yudi succeeded as the thirty-seventh generation, inheriting control of Jiangnan Daoism.

entries.zh: 三十一年入覲，卒於京師。
entries.en: He came to court in the thirty-first year and died in the capital.
entries.literal: In the thirty-first year he entered court audience and died in the capital.

entries.zh: 元貞元年，弟與材嗣，為三十八代，襲掌道教。
entries.en: In the first year of the Yuanzhen era his younger brother Yucai succeeded as the thirty-eighth generation and inherited leadership of the Daoist clergy.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yuanzhen, his younger brother Yucai succeeded as the thirty-eighth generation, inheriting control of Daoism.

entries.zh: 時潮囓鹽官、海鹽兩州，為患特甚，與材以術治之。
entries.en: At that time tidal flooding ravaged Yan'guan and Haiyan prefectures with particular severity, and Yucai treated it with ritual methods.
entries.literal: At that time the tide gnawed at Yan'guan and Haiyan prefectures, the harm being especially severe; Yucai treated it with his arts.

entries.zh: 一夕大雷電以震，明日見有物魚首龜形者磔於水裔，潮患遂息。
entries.en: One night a great thunderstorm struck. The next day a creature with a fish's head and tortoise's body was found dismembered on the shore, and the tidal flooding ceased.
entries.literal: One night great thunder and lightning shook; the next day they saw a creature with a fish head and tortoise body dismembered on the water's edge, and the tidal harm ceased.

entries.zh: 大德五年，召見於上都幄殿。
entries.en: In the fifth year of the Dade era he was summoned to audience at Shangdu.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Dade he was summoned for audience in the curtained hall at Shangdu.

entries.zh: 八年，授正一教主，主領三山符籙。
entries.en: In the eighth year he was appointed Lord of the Zhengyi Teaching and placed in charge of the talismans of the Three Mountains.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed Zhengyi Teaching Lord, heading the talismans of the Three Mountains.

entries.zh: 武宗即位，來覲，特授金紫光祿大夫，封留國公，錫金印。
entries.en: When Emperor Wuzong took the throne, Yucai came to court and was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Purple, enfeoffed as Duke of Liu, and given a gold seal.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wuzong ascended, he came to audience, was specially appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Purple, enfeoffed as Duke of Liu, and bestowed a gold seal.

entries.zh: 仁宗即位，特賜寶冠、組織文金之服。
entries.en: When Emperor Renzong took the throne, he received a precious crown and gold-thread ceremonial robe.
entries.literal: When Emperor Renzong ascended, he was specially bestowed a precious crown and gold-thread patterned robe.

entries.zh: 延祐三年卒。
entries.en: He died in the third year of the Yanyou era.
entries.literal: In the third year of Yanyou he died.

entries.zh: 四年，子嗣成嗣，為三十九代，襲領江南道教，主領三山符籙如故。
entries.en: The following year his son Sicheng succeeded as the thirty-ninth generation, inheriting leadership of Jiangnan Daoism and the Three Mountains talismans as before.
entries.literal: In the fourth year his son Sicheng succeeded as the thirty-ninth generation, inheriting leadership of Jiangnan Daoism and heading the Three Mountains talismans as before.

entries.zh: 其徒張留孫者，字師漢，信州貴溪人。
entries.en: Among his disciples was Zhang Liusun, styled Shihan, a native of Guixi in Xin prefecture.
entries.literal: His disciple Zhang Liusun, styled Shihan, was a man of Guixi in Xin prefecture.

entries.zh: 少時入龍虎山為道士，有道人相之曰：「神仙宰相也。」
entries.en: As a youth he became a Daoist priest on Dragon-Tiger Mountain. A fellow priest read his features and declared, "He will be both immortal and chancellor."
entries.literal: In youth he entered Dragon-Tiger Mountain as a Daoist priest; a Daoist physiognomized him, saying: "Immortal and chancellor both."

entries.zh: 至元十三年，從天師張宗演入朝，世祖與語，稱旨，遂留侍闕下。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year of the Zhiyuan era he accompanied Heavenly Master Zhang Zongyan to court. Kublai spoke with him, was pleased, and retained him at the palace.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhiyuan he followed Heavenly Master Zhang Zongyan to court; the Founder of the Dynasty spoke with him, found his words pleasing, and thereupon retained him to attend below the palace gates.

entries.zh: 世祖嘗親祠幄殿，皇太子侍。
entries.en: Kublai once performed sacrifice at the curtained hall with the crown prince in attendance.
entries.literal: The Founder of the Dynasty once personally sacrificed at the curtained hall, with the Crown Prince in attendance.

entries.zh: 忽風雨暴至，眾駭懼，留孫禱之立止。
entries.en: A violent storm suddenly broke. Everyone was terrified, but Liusun prayed and it stopped at once.
entries.literal: Suddenly wind and rain came violently; the multitude were terrified, but Liusun prayed and it immediately stopped.

entries.zh: 又嘗次日月山，昭睿順聖皇后得疾危甚，亟召留孫請禱。
entries.en: On another occasion, while encamped at Sun-Moon Mountain, Empress Zhaorui Shunsheng fell gravely ill and urgently summoned Liusun to pray for her.
entries.literal: He also once stopped at Sun-Moon Mountain when Empress Zhaorui Shunsheng fell gravely ill; she urgently summoned Liusun to pray.

entries.zh: 既而后夢有朱衣長髯，從甲士，導朱輦白獸行草間者。
entries.en: The empress then dreamed of a man in red robes with a long beard, followed by armored soldiers guiding a red carriage drawn by a white beast through the grass.
entries.literal: Afterward the empress dreamed of one in red robes with long beard, followed by armored soldiers, guiding a red carriage and white beast walking through grass.

entries.zh: 覺而異之，以問留孫，對曰：「甲士導輦獸者，臣所佩法籙中將吏也；
entries.en: Awakening, she found it strange and asked Liusun. He replied, "The armored soldiers guiding the carriage and beast are the generals and officers in the talisman registers I wear.
entries.literal: Awakening, she found it strange and asked Liusun; he replied: "The armored soldiers guiding the carriage and beast are the generals and officers in the talisman registers I wear;

entries.zh: 硃衣長髯者，漢祖天師也；
entries.en: The man in red robes with a long beard is the founding Heavenly Master of the Han.
entries.literal: the one in red robes with long beard is the founding Heavenly Master of Han;

entries.zh: 行草間者，春時也。
entries.en: Walking through the grass signifies the season of spring.
entries.literal: walking through grass signifies the season of spring.

entries.zh: 殿下之疾，其及春而瘳乎！」
entries.en: Your Highness's illness should recover by spring!"
entries.literal: Your Highness's illness — will it recover by spring!"

entries.zh: 後命取所事畫像以進，視之果夢中所見者。
entries.en: She later ordered the portrait he venerated brought forth — and it was indeed what she had seen in the dream.
entries.literal: Later she ordered the portrait he venerated brought forth; viewing it, it was indeed what she had seen in the dream.

entries.zh: 帝后大悅，即命留孫為天師，留孫固辭不敢當，乃號之上卿，命尚方鑄寶劍以賜，建崇真宮於兩京，俾留孫居之，專掌祠事。
entries.en: The emperor and empress were delighted and offered to make Liusun Heavenly Master. He firmly declined, and was instead styled Supreme Minister. The Imperial Workshop cast a precious sword for him, and Chongzhen Palaces were built in both capitals for him to reside in and oversee sacrificial affairs.
entries.literal: The emperor and empress were greatly pleased and immediately ordered Liusun made Heavenly Master; Liusun firmly declined and dared not accept, so he was styled Supreme Minister instead; the Imperial Workshop was ordered to cast a precious sword to bestow; Chongzhen Palaces were built in both capitals for Liusun to dwell in, exclusively overseeing sacrificial affairs.

entries.zh: 十五年，授玄教宗師，錫銀印。
entries.en: In the fifteenth year he was appointed Patriarch of the Xuan Teaching and given a silver seal.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed Xuanjiao Patriarch and bestowed a silver seal.

entries.zh: 又特任其父信州路治中，尋复升江東道同知宣慰司事。
entries.en: His father was specially appointed administrative vice-commissioner of Xin circuit and soon promoted to associate commissioner of the Jiangdong Pacification Commission.
entries.literal: His father was also specially appointed administrative vice-commissioner of Xin prefecture circuit, and soon afterward promoted to associate commissioner of the Jiangdong Pacification Commission.

entries.zh: 是時天下大定，世祖思與民休息，留孫待詔尚方，因論黃老治道貴清淨、聖人在宥天下之旨，深契主衷。
entries.en: The realm was now largely pacified, and Kublai wished to let the people rest. Liusun attended at court and expounded how the governance of Huang-Lao values purity and tranquility and how the sage leaves the realm in repose — teachings that deeply matched the emperor's intent.
entries.literal: At that time the realm was greatly settled; the Founder of the Dynasty wished to let the people rest. Liusun awaited edicts at the Imperial Workshop and, discussing how the Yellow Emperor and Laozi's way of governance values purity and tranquility and how the sage leaves the realm in repose, deeply matched the sovereign's heart.

entries.zh: 及將以完澤為相，命留孫筮之，得《同人》之《豫》，留孫進曰：「'《同人》，柔得位而應乎乾'，君臣之合也；
entries.en: When Kublai was about to appoint Wanze as chancellor, he ordered Liusun to divine. The hexagram was Tongren changing to Yu. Liusun said, "'Tongren: the yielding obtains position and responds to Qian' — this signifies the union of ruler and minister.
entries.literal: When about to appoint Wanze as chancellor, he ordered Liusun to divine by milfoil; he obtained Tongren changing to Yu. Liusun advanced and said: "'Tongren — the yielding obtains position and responds to Qian' — the union of ruler and minister;

entries.zh: '《豫》，利建侯'，命相之事也。
entries.en: Yu: favorable to establishing lords' — this concerns appointing a chancellor.
entries.literal: Yu — favorable to establishing lords' — the matter of appointing a chancellor.

entries.zh: 何吉如之，願陛下勿疑。」
entries.en: What could be more auspicious? I beg Your Majesty not to hesitate."
entries.literal: What could be more auspicious? I beg Your Majesty not to doubt."

entries.zh: 及拜完澤，天下果以為得賢相。
entries.en: When Wanze was appointed, the realm indeed regarded it as the choice of a worthy chancellor.
entries.literal: When Wanze was appointed, the realm indeed regarded it as obtaining a worthy chancellor.

entries.zh: 大德中，加號玄教大宗師，同知集賢院道教事，且追封其三代皆魏國公，官階品俱第一。
entries.en: During the Dade era he received the added title Great Patriarch of the Xuan Teaching and was made associate commissioner of the Hall of Worthies for Daoist affairs. His three generations of ancestors were posthumously enfeoffed as Dukes of Wei with first-grade ranks.
entries.literal: During Dade, he was given the added title Great Patriarch of the Xuan Teaching, Associate Commissioner of the Hall of Worthies for Daoist affairs, and his three generations were posthumously enfeoffed all as Dukes of Wei, official ranks all of the first grade.

entries.zh: 武宗立，召見，賜坐，升大真人，知集賢院，位大學士上。
entries.en: When Wuzong took the throne, Liusun was summoned, granted a seat, promoted to Great Perfected One, made director of the Hall of Worthies, and ranked above the grand academicians.
entries.literal: When Wuzong ascended, he was summoned for audience, granted a seat, promoted to Great Perfected One, made director of the Hall of Worthies, ranking above Grand Academician.

entries.zh: 尋又加特進。
entries.en: He was soon given the additional rank of Special Advancement.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he was additionally made Special Advancement.

entries.zh: 進講老子推明謙讓之道。
entries.en: He lectured on Laozi, expounding the way of humility and yielding.
entries.literal: He advanced to lecture on Laozi, extending and clarifying the Way of humility and yielding.

entries.zh: 及仁宗即位，猶恆誦其言，且諭近臣曰：「累朝舊德，僅餘張上卿爾。」
entries.en: When Renzong took the throne he still often quoted Liusun's teachings and told his close ministers, "Of the accumulated virtue of successive reigns, only Supreme Minister Zhang remains."
entries.literal: When Renzong ascended, he still constantly recited his words, and moreover instructed close ministers: "The accumulated virtue of successive reigns — only Supreme Minister Zhang remains."

entries.zh: 進開府儀同三司，加號輔成贊化保運玄教大宗師，刻玉為玄教大宗師印以賜。
entries.en: He was promoted to Honorary Three Excellencies of the First Rank and given the added title Great Patriarch of the Xuan Teaching, Assisting Completion, Praising Transformation, and Protecting the Fortune. A jade seal of the Great Patriarch of the Xuan Teaching was carved and bestowed upon him.
entries.literal: He was advanced to Opening the Mansion, Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, with the added title Great Patriarch of the Xuan Teaching, Assisting Completion, Praising Transformation, Protecting the Fortune; a jade seal of Great Patriarch of the Xuan Teaching was carved and bestowed.

entries.zh: 至治元年十二月卒，年七十四。
entries.en: He died in the twelfth month of the first year of the Zhizhi era at the age of seventy-four.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Zhizhi he died, age seventy-four.

entries.zh: 天曆元年，追贈道祖神德真君。
entries.en: In the first year of the Tianli era he was posthumously honored as Perfected Lord of the Dao Ancestor's Divine Virtue.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianli he was posthumously granted the title Perfected Lord of the Dao Ancestor's Divine Virtue.

entries.zh: 其徒吳全節嗣。
entries.en: His disciple Wu Quanjie succeeded him.
entries.literal: His disciple Wu Quanjie succeeded him.

entries.zh: 全節字成季，饒州安仁人。
entries.en: Quanjie, styled Chengji, was a native of Anren in Rao prefecture.
entries.literal: Quanjie, styled Chengji, was a man of Anren in Rao prefecture.

entries.zh: 年十三學道於龍虎山。
entries.en: At thirteen he began studying the Way on Dragon-Tiger Mountain.
entries.literal: At age thirteen he studied the Way on Dragon-Tiger Mountain.

entries.zh: 至元二十四年至京師，從留孫見世祖。
entries.en: In the twenty-fourth year of the Zhiyuan era he came to the capital and, accompanying Liusun, met Kublai.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Zhiyuan he reached the capital and, following Liusun, met the Founder of the Dynasty.

entries.zh: 三十一年，成宗至自朔方，召見，賜古雕玉蟠螭環一，敕每歲侍從行幸，所司給廬帳、車馬、衣服、廩餼，著為令。
entries.en: In the thirty-first year, when Chengzong returned from the north, Quanjie was summoned and given an ancient carved jade ring with coiled dragons. He was ordered to accompany the emperor on annual tours, with tents, horses, clothing, and provisions supplied by regulation.
entries.literal: In the thirty-first year, when Chengzong returned from the northern frontier, he was summoned for audience and bestowed one ancient carved jade coiled-dragon ring; he was ordered each year to attend the emperor on tours, with the responsible offices supplying tents, horses, clothing, and provisions — established as regulation.

entries.zh: 大德十一年，授玄教嗣師，錫銀印，視二品。
entries.en: In the eleventh year of the Dade era he was appointed Successor Master of the Xuan Teaching, given a silver seal, and treated as second rank.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year of Dade he was appointed Successor Master of the Xuan Teaching, bestowed a silver seal, treated as second rank.

entries.zh: 至大元年，賜七寶金冠、織金文之服。
entries.en: In the first year of the Zhida era he received a seven-treasure gold crown and gold-thread ceremonial robe.
entries.literal: In the first year of Zhida he was bestowed a seven-treasure gold crown and gold-thread patterned robe.

entries.zh: 三年，贈其祖昭文館大學士，封其父司徒、饒國公，母饒國太夫人，名其所居之鄉曰榮祿，裡曰具慶。
entries.en: In the third year his grandfather was posthumously made Grand Academician of the Zhaowen Hall; his father was enfeoffed as Minister of Education and Duke of Rao; his mother as Grand Lady of Rao; his home village was named Ronglu and his hamlet Jiqing.
entries.literal: In the third year his grandfather was posthumously granted Grand Academician of the Zhaowen Hall; his father was enfeoffed as Minister of Education and Duke of Rao; his mother as Grand Lady of Rao; his home village was named Ronglu and his hamlet Jiqing.

entries.zh: 至治元年，留孫卒。
entries.en: Liusun died in the first year of the Zhizhi era.
entries.literal: In the first year of Zhizhi, Liusun died.

entries.zh: 二年，制授特進、上卿、玄教大宗師、崇文弘道玄德真人、總攝江淮荊襄等處道教、知集賢院道教事，玉印一、銀印二並授之。
entries.en: The following year he was appointed Special Advancement, Supreme Minister, Great Patriarch of the Xuan Teaching, and Perfected One of Honoring Culture, Expanding the Way, and Mysterious Virtue, placed in charge of Daoism throughout Jianghuai, Jingxiang, and other regions, and made director of the Hall of Worthies for Daoist affairs, with one jade seal and two silver seals.
entries.literal: In the second year, by regulation he was appointed Special Advancement, Supreme Minister, Great Patriarch of the Xuan Teaching, Perfected One of Honoring Culture and Expanding the Way with Mysterious Virtue, General Overseer of Daoism in Jianghuai, Jingxiang, and other regions, and Director of the Hall of Worthies for Daoist affairs — one jade seal and two silver seals were all bestowed.

entries.zh: 全節嘗代祀岳瀆還，成宗問曰：「卿所過郡縣，有善治民者乎？」
entries.en: Once, returning from substituting in sacrifice to the mountains and rivers, Chengzong asked him, "Among the prefectures and counties you passed through, did you find any who govern the people well?"
entries.literal: Quanjie once returned from substituting in sacrifice to the mountains and rivers; Chengzong asked: "Among the prefectures and counties you passed, are there any who govern the people well?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「臣過洛陽，太守盧摯平易無為，而民以安靖。」
entries.en: He answered, "I passed through Luoyang. The prefect Lu Zhi governs with plain ease and non-action, yet the people are peaceful and settled."
entries.literal: He replied: "Your subject passed Luoyang; the prefect Lu Zhi is plain and easy, practicing non-action, yet the people are thereby peaceful and settled."

entries.zh: 成宗曰：「吾憶其人。」
entries.en: Chengzong said, "I remember that man."
entries.literal: Chengzong said: "We recall that man."

entries.zh: 即日召拜集賢學士。
entries.en: That same day Lu Zhi was summoned and appointed Academician of the Hall of Worthies.
entries.literal: That same day he was summoned and appointed Academician of the Hall of Worthies.

entries.zh: 成宗崩，仁宗至自懷孟，有狂士以危言訐翰林學士閻复者，事叵測。
entries.en: When Chengzong died and Renzong arrived from Huai-Meng, a madman denounced Hanlin Academician Yan Fu with alarming words, and the affair's outcome was uncertain.
entries.literal: When Chengzong died, Renzong arrived from Huai-Meng; a madman used alarming words to denounce Hanlin Academician Yan Fu — the affair was hard to fathom.

entries.zh: 全節力為言於李孟，孟以聞，仁宗意解，復告老而去。
entries.en: Quanjie spoke earnestly on Yan Fu's behalf to Li Meng, who reported it to Renzong. The emperor's anger eased, and Yan Fu retired and departed.
entries.literal: Quanjie strenuously spoke on his behalf to Li Meng; Meng reported it, Renzong's mind was eased, and Fu requested retirement and departed.

entries.zh: 當時以為朝廷得敬大臣體，而不以口語傷賢者，全節蓋有力焉。
entries.en: At the time people credited the court with showing proper respect for great ministers and not harming the worthy on loose charges — in which Quanjie had played a significant part.
entries.literal: At the time it was thought the court had obtained the proper respect for great ministers and did not harm the worthy through loose words — Quanjie had strength in this.

entries.zh: 全節雅好結士大夫，無所不傾其交，長者尤見親而敬，推轂善類，唯恐不盡其力。
entries.en: Quanjie delighted in befriending scholar-officials and gave his friendship unstintingly. He was especially intimate with and respectful toward elders, promoting worthy men and exhausting every effort on their behalf.
entries.literal: Quanjie elegantly loved forming ties with scholar-officials, sparing nothing to pour out his friendship; elders he especially treated with intimacy and respect, promoting the good, fearing only that he had not exhausted his strength.

entries.zh: 至於振窮周急，又未嘗以恩怨異其心，當時以為頗有俠氣云。
entries.en: In relieving the poor and aiding those in distress he never let personal favor or resentment sway him. At the time he was regarded as possessing a chivalrous spirit.
entries.literal: As for relieving the poor and aiding the urgent, he also never altered his heart because of favor or resentment; at the time he was thought to possess quite a chivalrous spirit.

entries.zh: 全節卒，年八十有二，其徒夏文泳嗣。
entries.en: Quanjie died at the age of eighty-two. His disciple Xia Wenyong succeeded him.
entries.literal: Quanjie died at age eighty-two; his disciple Xia Wenyong succeeded him.

entries.zh: 真大道教者，始自金季，道士劉德仁之所立也。
entries.en: The True Great Way teaching was founded during the Jin dynasty by the Daoist priest Liu Deren.
entries.literal: The True Great Way teaching began in the Jin season; it was established by the Daoist priest Liu Deren.

entries.zh: 其教以苦節危行為要，而不妄取於人、不苟侈於己者也。
entries.en: Its teaching emphasized austere discipline and rigorous conduct, taking nothing recklessly from others and indulging nothing in oneself.
entries.literal: Its teaching takes bitter discipline and perilous conduct as essential, not taking from others recklessly nor being extravagant with oneself.

entries.zh: 五傳而至酈希成，居燕城天寶宮，見知憲宗，始名其教曰真大道，授希成太玄真人，領教事，內出冠服以賜；
entries.en: After five generations the line reached Li Xicheng, who lived at the Tianbao Palace in Yan. Emperor Xianzong took notice of him, named the teaching the True Great Way, appointed Xicheng Perfected One of the Great Mystery to head it, and bestowed court caps and robes;
entries.literal: After five transmissions it reached Li Xicheng, who dwelt at the Tianbao Palace in Yan city; he came to the notice of Emperor Xianzong, who first named the teaching the True Great Way, appointed Xicheng Perfected One of the Great Mystery, placed him in charge of teaching affairs, and issued from within court caps and robes to bestow;

entries.zh: 仍給紫衣三十襲，賜其從者。
entries.en: and gave thirty purple robes for his followers.
entries.literal: still giving thirty suits of purple robes to bestow on his followers.

entries.zh: 至元五年，世祖命其徒孫德福統轄諸路真大道，錫銅章。
entries.en: In the fifth year of the Zhiyuan era Kublai ordered his disciple Sun Defu to oversee the True Great Way in all circuits and bestowed a bronze seal.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Zhiyuan, the Founder of the Dynasty ordered his disciple Sun Defu to oversee the True Great Way in all circuits and bestowed a bronze seal.

entries.zh: 二十年，改賜銀印二。
entries.en: In the twentieth year he received two silver seals in place of the bronze one.
entries.literal: In the twentieth year, two silver seals were changed and bestowed instead.

entries.zh: 又三傳而至張清志，其教益盛，授演教大宗師、凝神衝妙玄應真人。
entries.en: Three generations later the line reached Zhang Qingzhi, under whom the teaching flourished further. He was appointed Great Patriarch of the Expounding Teaching and Perfected One of Concentrating Spirit and Piercing Mystery.
entries.literal: After three more transmissions it reached Zhang Qingzhi; the teaching grew still more prosperous; he was appointed Great Patriarch of the Expounding Teaching, Perfected One of Concentrating Spirit, Piercing Mystery, and Mysterious Response.

entries.zh: 清志事親孝，尤耐辛苦，制行堅峻。
entries.en: Qingzhi was filial toward his parents, exceptionally enduring of hardship, and sternly disciplined in conduct.
entries.literal: Qingzhi was filial in serving his parents, especially enduring hardship; his regulated conduct was stern and severe.

entries.zh: 東海珠、牢山舊多虎，清志往結茅居之，虎皆避徙，然頗為人害。
entries.en: East of the sea at Zhuhai and Mount Lao tigers were once numerous. Qingzhi built a thatched hut and lived there; the tigers all fled, yet they still harmed people elsewhere.
entries.literal: East of the sea at Zhuhai and Mount Lao there were formerly many tigers; Qingzhi went and built a thatched dwelling to live there — the tigers all avoided and moved away, yet they still harmed people considerably.

entries.zh: 清志曰：「是吾奪其所也！」
entries.en: Qingzhi said, "I have seized their dwelling place!"
entries.literal: Qingzhi said: "This is because I seized their dwelling place!"

entries.zh: 遂去之。
entries.en: So he departed.
entries.literal: Thereupon he left.

entries.zh: 後居臨汾，地大震，城郭邑屋摧壓，死者不可勝計，獨清誌所居裂為二，無少損焉。
entries.en: Later he lived at Linfen. A great earthquake struck, crushing cities and towns beyond count. Only Qingzhi's dwelling split in two without the slightest damage.
entries.literal: Later he dwelt at Linfen; a great earthquake struck — city walls, towns, and houses were crushed; the dead could not be counted — only Qingzhi's dwelling split in two without the slightest damage.

entries.zh: 乃遍巡木石間，聽呻吟聲，救活者甚眾。
entries.en: He searched everywhere among the rubble, listening for groans, and saved many lives.
entries.literal: Thereupon he went everywhere among timbers and stones, listening for groaning sounds — those he saved alive were very many.

entries.zh: 朝廷重其名，給驛致之掌教事。
entries.en: The court valued his reputation and sent relay horses to bring him to the capital to head the teaching.
entries.literal: The court valued his reputation and sent relay horses to bring him to head teaching affairs.

entries.zh: 清志舍傳徒步至京師，深居簡出，人或不識其面。
entries.en: Qingzhi abandoned the relay posts and walked to the capital on foot. He lived in seclusion and rarely went out, so that some did not know his face.
entries.literal: Qingzhi abandoned the relay posts and walked on foot to the capital, dwelling deeply and going out rarely — some did not know his face.

entries.zh: 貴人達官來見，率告病，伏臥內不起。
entries.en: When nobles and high officials came to visit, he invariably pleaded illness and would not rise from his bed.
entries.literal: When nobles and high officials came to see him, he invariably pleaded illness and lay prostrate within, not rising.

entries.zh: 至於道德縉紳先生，則納屣杖屨求見，不以為難。
entries.en: But for cultivated gentlemen of learning and virtue he would put on his shoes and take his staff to visit them without hesitation.
entries.literal: As for cultivated gentlemen of virtue and girdled sashes, he would put on shoes and take staff to seek them out, not considering it difficult.

entries.zh: 時人高其風，至畫為圖以相傳焉。
entries.en: Contemporaries admired his character, and paintings of him were passed down.
entries.literal: People of the time admired his bearing, even painting pictures to pass down.

entries.zh: 太一教者，始金天眷中道士蕭抱珍，傳太一三元法​​籙之術，因名其教曰太一。
entries.en: The Supreme Unity teaching was founded by the Daoist priest Xiao Baozhen during the Tianjuan era of the Jin dynasty, who transmitted the arts of the Supreme Unity Three Origins talismans and named the teaching accordingly.
entries.literal: The Supreme Unity teaching began with the Daoist priest Xiao Baozhen in the Tianjuan period of Jin, transmitting the arts of the Supreme Unity Three Origins talismans — therefore naming the teaching Supreme Unity.

entries.zh: 四傳而至蕭輔道。
entries.en: After four generations the line reached Xiao Fudao.
entries.literal: After four transmissions it reached Xiao Fudao.

entries.zh: 世祖在潛邸聞其名，命史天澤召至和林，賜對稱旨，留居宮邸。
entries.en: Kublai, while still at his princely residence, heard of him and ordered Shi Tianze to summon him to Helin. An audience found his words pleasing, and he was retained at the palace.
entries.literal: The Founder of the Dynasty, while at his princely residence, heard his name and ordered Shi Tianze to summon him to Helin; an imperial audience found his words pleasing, and he was retained to dwell at the palace residence.

entries.zh: 以老，請授弟子李居壽掌其教事。
entries.en: On account of age he asked that his disciple Li Jushou take charge of the teaching.
entries.literal: Because of age, he requested that his disciple Li Jushou take charge of teaching affairs.

entries.zh: 至元十一年，建太一宮於兩京，命居壽居之，領祠事，且禋祀六丁，以繼太保劉秉忠之術。
entries.en: In the eleventh year of the Zhiyuan era Supreme Unity Palaces were built in both capitals. Jushou was placed in residence to head sacrificial affairs and perform suburban rites to the Six Ding, continuing the arts of Grand Guardian Liu Bingzhong.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhiyuan, Supreme Unity Palaces were built in both capitals; Jushou was ordered to dwell there, heading sacrificial affairs, and moreover performing suburban sacrifice to the Six Ding — continuing the arts of Grand Guardian Liu Bingzhong.

entries.zh: 十三年，賜太一掌教宗師印。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year he received the seal of Supreme Unity Patriarch in Charge of Teaching.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year, the seal of Supreme Unity Patriarch in Charge of Teaching was bestowed.

entries.zh: 十六年十月辛丑，月直元辰，敕居壽祠醮，奏赤章於天，凡五晝夜。
entries.en: On the xinchou day of the tenth month of the sixteenth year, when the moon aligned with the primordial spirit, Jushou was ordered to perform temple rites and present red memorials to Heaven for five days and nights.
entries.literal: In the tenth month, xinchou day, of the sixteenth year, when the moon was directly on the primordial spirit, Jushou was ordered to perform temple sacrifice and deliverance rites, presenting red memorials to Heaven — in all five days and nights.

entries.zh: 事畢，居壽請間曰：「皇太子春秋鼎盛，宜參預國政。」
entries.en: When the rites were concluded, Jushou requested a private audience and said, "The crown prince is in the prime of life and ought to participate in state affairs."
entries.literal: When the affair was concluded, Jushou requested a private audience and said: "The Crown Prince is in the full vigor of spring and autumn; he ought to participate in state affairs."

entries.zh: 且又因典瑞董文忠以為言，世祖喜曰：「行將及之。」
entries.en: He also spoke through Court Regalia Officer Dong Wenzhong. Kublai was pleased and said, "It shall soon be done."
entries.literal: Moreover, through Court Regalia Officer Dong Wenzhong he also spoke on this; the Founder of the Dynasty was pleased and said: "It will soon be carried out."

entries.zh: 其後詔太子參決朝政，庶事皆先啟後聞者，蓋居壽為之先也。
entries.en: Thereafter an edict ordered the crown prince to participate in deciding government affairs, with all routine matters reported to him first — Jushou had been the initiator of this.
entries.literal: Afterward an edict ordered the Crown Prince to participate in deciding court governance; for ordinary affairs all were first reported to him and then announced — Jushou was the one who initiated this.

entries.zh: 釋、老之教，行乎中國也千數百年，而其盛衰每系乎時君之好惡。
entries.en: Buddhist and Taoist teachings have flourished in China for well over a thousand years, yet their rise and fall have always hinged on whether the reigning sovereign favored or disdained them.
entries.literal: The teachings of Buddhism and the Old Master have been practiced in China for a thousand-odd years, and their flourishing and decline each depend on the likes and dislikes of the ruler of the time.

entries.zh: 是故佛於晉、宋、梁、陳，黃、老於漢、魏、唐、宋，而其效可睹矣。
entries.en: One need only look at Buddhism under the Jin, Song, Liang, and Chen, or at Huang-Lao Taoism under the Han, Wei, Tang, and Song, to see how this worked in practice.
entries.literal: Therefore Buddhism in Jin, Song, Liang, and Chen, and Huang-Lao in Han, Wei, Tang, and Song — their effects can be seen.

entries.zh: 元興，崇尚釋氏，而帝師之盛，尤不可與古昔同語。
entries.en: When the Yuan dynasty rose, it embraced Buddhism with a fervor unmatched in earlier ages — above all in the unprecedented eminence of the Imperial Preceptor.
