entries.literal: When the Yuan arose, they venerated the Buddhist clan, and the grandeur of the Imperial Preceptor especially cannot be spoken of in the same terms as antiquity.

entries.zh: 維道家方士之流，假禱祠之說，乘時以起，曾不及其什一焉。
entries.en: Taoist priests and occult specialists who rode the tide with their rites of prayer and sacrifice never attained even a tenth of that influence.
entries.literal: As for the stream of Daoist masters and fangshi, borrowing the doctrine of prayer and sacrifice, they rose by seizing the moment — yet never reached a tenth of it.

entries.zh: 宋舊史嘗志老、釋，厥有旨哉。
entries.en: The former Song dynastic histories devoted separate treatises to Taoism and Buddhism — and with good reason.
entries.literal: The old Song histories once recorded Lao and Buddhism — how apt indeed!

entries.zh: 乃本其意，作《釋老傳》。
entries.en: Following that precedent, we have written this "Biography of Buddhists and Taoists."
entries.literal: Thereupon, based on this intent, [we] composed the "Biographies of Buddhists and Taoists."

entries.zh: 田忠良，字正卿，其先平陽趙城人，金亡，徙中山。
entries.en: Tian Zhongliang, styled Zhengqing, came from a family originally of Zhaocheng in Pingyang; when the Jin dynasty fell, they relocated to Zhongshan.
entries.literal: Tian Zhongliang, courtesy name Zhengqing, was originally from Zhaocheng in Pingyang; after the fall of the Jin, his family moved to Zhongshan.

entries.zh: 忠良好學，通儒家、雜家言。
entries.en: Zhongliang was a devoted scholar, well versed in both Confucian classics and the eclectic learning of the miscellaneous schools.
entries.literal: Zhongliang loved learning and was versed in Confucian and miscellaneous school teachings.

entries.zh: 嘗識太保劉秉忠於微時。
entries.en: He had known Grand Preceptor Liu Bingzhong long before Liu rose to power.
entries.literal: He had once known Grand Preceptor Liu Bingzhong in his days of obscurity.

entries.zh: 秉忠薦於世祖，遣使召至，帝視其狀貌步趨，顧謂侍臣曰：「是雖以陰陽家進，必將為國用。」
entries.en: Liu Bingzhong recommended him to Kublai Khan, who sent for him. When Zhongliang arrived, the emperor studied his bearing and stride and told his attendants, "He may have come up through the arts of yin and yang, but he will prove indispensable to the realm."
entries.literal: Bingzhong recommended him to Shizu; the emperor sent an envoy to summon him. The emperor observed his appearance and gait, turned to his attendants and said: "Though this man advances through the Yin-Yang school, he will surely serve the state."

entries.zh: 俄指西序第二人謂忠良曰： 「彼手中握何物？」
entries.en: Then he pointed to the second man seated on the west side and asked Zhongliang, "What is he holding in his hand?"
entries.literal: Shortly he pointed to the second man on the western side and said to Zhongliang: "What is that man holding in his hand?"

entries.zh: 忠良對曰：「雞卵也。」
entries.en: Zhongliang answered, "A hen's egg."
entries.literal: Zhongliang replied: "A chicken egg."

entries.zh: 果然。
entries.en: And so it proved.
entries.literal: It was indeed so.

entries.zh: 帝喜，又曰：「朕有事縈心，汝試占之。」
entries.en: Delighted, the emperor said, "Something has been troubling me — try your divination on it."
entries.literal: The emperor was pleased and said again: "I have something weighing on my mind — try divining it."

entries.zh: 對曰：「以臣術推之，當是一名僧病耳。」
entries.en: He replied, "By my reckoning, it concerns the illness of a monk."
entries.literal: He replied: "By my art I infer it must be the illness of a certain monk."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「然，國師也。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "Exactly — the Imperial Preceptor."
entries.literal: The emperor said: "So it is — the Imperial Preceptor."

entries.zh: 遂遣左侍儀奉御也先乃送忠良司天台，給筆札，令秉忠試星曆、遁甲諸書。
entries.en: He then had Yexianai, attendant of the Left Ceremonial Office, escort Zhongliang to the Directorate of Astronomy, supplied him with writing materials, and ordered Liu Bingzhong to examine him in astronomy, calendrics, and the dunjia arts.
entries.literal: He then sent the Left Attendant of Ceremonial Yexianai to escort Zhongliang to the Directorate of Astronomy, provided writing materials, and had Bingzhong test him on books of astronomy, calendrics, and dunjia.

entries.zh: 秉忠奏曰：「所試皆通，司天諸生鮮有及者。」
entries.en: Liu Bingzhong reported, "He has mastered every subject tested — few students at the Directorate of Astronomy can equal him."
entries.literal: Bingzhong memorialized: "In all that was tested he is thoroughly versed; few among the students of the Directorate of Astronomy can match him."

entries.zh: 詔官之司天。
entries.en: The emperor appointed him to a post at the Directorate of Astronomy.
entries.literal: An edict appointed him to office in the Directorate of Astronomy.

entries.zh: 帝曰：「朕用兵江南，困於襄樊，累年不決，奈何？」
entries.en: The emperor said, "Our armies in the south have been stalled at Xiangyang and Fancheng for years with no end in sight — what can be done?"
entries.literal: The emperor said: "I am campaigning in the south against Jiangnan, bogged down at Xiang and Fan for years without resolution — what is to be done?"

entries.zh: 忠良對曰：「在酉年矣。」
entries.en: Zhongliang answered, "Victory will come in the year of the rooster."
entries.literal: Zhongliang replied: "It will be in the year of the rooster."

entries.zh: 至元十一年，阿里海牙奏請率十萬眾渡江，朝議難之，帝密問曰：「汝試筮之，濟否？」
entries.en: In the eleventh year of Zhiyuan (1274), Alihaiya petitioned to lead a hundred thousand troops across the Yangtze; the court was divided. The emperor asked Zhongliang privately, "Divine for me — will the crossing succeed?"
entries.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhiyuan, Alihaiya memorialized requesting to lead a hundred thousand men across the Yangtze; the court deliberated and found it difficult. The emperor secretly asked: "Try divining for me — will they succeed in crossing?"

entries.zh: 忠良對曰：「濟。」
entries.en: "They will," Zhongliang replied.
entries.literal: Zhongliang replied: "They will succeed."

entries.zh: 帝獵於柳林，禦幄殿，侍臣甚眾，顧忠良曰：「今拜一大將取江南，朕心已定，果何人耶？」
entries.en: While hunting at Willow Grove, the emperor sat in his tent surrounded by attendants and asked Zhongliang, "I have decided to appoint a great general to conquer the south — who is it, in your judgment?"
entries.literal: The emperor was hunting at Willow Grove, in the imperial tent hall with many attendants present. He turned to Zhongliang and said: "I am now appointing a great general to take Jiangnan; my mind is already made up — who is it in truth?"

entries.zh: 忠良環視左右，目一人，對曰：「是偉丈夫，可屬大事。」
entries.en: Zhongliang scanned those around him, fixed on one man, and said, "There stands the man — a commanding figure fit to bear a great charge."
entries.literal: Zhongliang looked around to left and right, fixed his gaze on one man, and replied: "This is a great man who can be entrusted with a great affair."

entries.zh: 帝笑曰：「此伯顏也，為西王旭烈兀使，朕以其才留用之，汝識朕心。」
entries.en: The emperor laughed. "That is Bayan — he came as envoy from Prince Hulagu in the west, and I kept him for his ability. You read my thoughts well."
entries.literal: The emperor laughed and said: "This is Bayan — he came as envoy for the Western Prince Hulagu; I kept him for his talent. You know my mind."

entries.zh: 賜鈔五百貫、衣一襲。
entries.en: He was rewarded with five hundred strings of paper money and a suit of robes.
entries.literal: He was granted five hundred strings of paper money and one suit of clothing.

entries.zh: 七月十五日夜，白氣貫三台，帝問何祥，忠良對曰：「三公其死乎！」
entries.en: On the night of the fifteenth day of the seventh month, a white vapor pierced the Three Terraces. When the emperor asked what it portended, Zhongliang replied, "Might the Three Dukes be about to die?"
entries.literal: On the night of the fifteenth day of the seventh month, a white vapor pierced the Three Terraces; the emperor asked what omen this was. Zhongliang replied: "Will the Three Dukes die?"

entries.zh: 未幾，太保劉秉忠卒。
entries.en: Soon afterward Grand Preceptor Liu Bingzhong died.
entries.literal: Before long, Grand Preceptor Liu Bingzhong died.

entries.zh: 八月，帝出獵，駐輦召忠良曰：「朕有所遺，汝知何物，還可復得否？」
entries.en: In the eighth month, while out hunting, the emperor halted his carriage and called Zhongliang. "I have lost something," he said. "Do you know what it is, and whether I shall get it back?"
entries.literal: In the eighth month the emperor went out hunting; halting his carriage he summoned Zhongliang and said: "I have lost something — do you know what it is, and whether it can be recovered?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「其數珠乎？
entries.en: "Your prayer beads?" he replied.
entries.literal: He replied: "Is it your prayer beads?

entries.zh: 明日，二十里外人當有得而來獻者。」
entries.en: Tomorrow someone twenty li distant will find them and bring them to you."
entries.literal: Tomorrow someone twenty li away will find them and come to present them."

entries.zh: 已而果然。
entries.en: And so it happened.
entries.literal: And so it indeed came to pass.

entries.zh: 帝喜，賜以貂裘。
entries.en: The emperor was delighted and gave him a sable fur coat.
entries.literal: The emperor was pleased and bestowed a sable fur coat on him.

entries.zh: 十月，有旨問忠良：「南征將士能渡江否？
entries.en: In the tenth month the emperor asked Zhongliang by edict, "Can our southern expedition cross the Yangtze?
entries.literal: In the tenth month an edict questioned Zhongliang: "Can the southern campaign troops cross the Yangtze?

entries.zh: 勞師費財，朕甚憂之。」
entries.en: The campaign strains our troops and drains our treasury — I am deeply worried."
entries.literal: The army is worn and finances exhausted — I am deeply troubled."

entries.zh: 忠良奏曰：「明年正月當奏捷矣。」
entries.en: Zhongliang replied, "Victory will be reported in the first month of next year."
entries.literal: Zhongliang memorialized: "In the first month of next year victory will be reported."

entries.zh: 十二年正月，師取鄂州，丞相伯顏遣使來獻宋寶，有玉香爐，輟以賜忠良，及金織文十匹。
entries.en: In the first month of the twelfth year (1275) the army captured Ezhou. Chancellor Bayan sent tribute from the Song, including a jade incense burner, which he reserved for Zhongliang along with ten bolts of gold brocade.
entries.literal: In the first month of the twelfth year the army took Ezhou; Chancellor Bayan sent an envoy to present Song treasures, including a jade incense burner, which he set aside to bestow on Zhongliang, along with ten bolts of gold brocade.

entries.zh: 二月，帝不豫，召忠良謂曰：「或言朕今歲不嘉，汝術云何？」
entries.en: In the second month the emperor fell ill and summoned Zhongliang. "Some say this year bodes ill for me," he said. "What does your art tell you?"
entries.literal: In the second month the emperor was unwell; he summoned Zhongliang and said: "Some say this year is inauspicious for me — what does your art say?"

entries.zh: 忠良對曰：「聖體行自安矣。」
entries.en: "Your Majesty will soon recover," Zhongliang answered.
entries.literal: Zhongliang replied: "Your sacred person will soon be at ease."

entries.zh: 三月，帝疾愈，賜銀五百兩、衣材三十匹。
entries.en: In the third month the emperor recovered and rewarded him with five hundred taels of silver and thirty bolts of fabric for robes.
entries.literal: In the third month the emperor's illness abated; he granted five hundred taels of silver and thirty bolts of clothing material.

entries.zh: 五月，車駕清暑上都，遣使來召曰：「叛者浸入山陵，久而不去，汝與和禮霍孫率眾往視之。」
entries.en: In the fifth month the court retired to Shangdu for the summer. An envoy summoned Zhongliang: "Rebels have entered the imperial tombs and will not leave — take Holihosun and a force to investigate."
entries.literal: In the fifth month the imperial carriage went to Shangdu for summer respite; an envoy was sent to summon him with the message: "Rebels have penetrated the imperial tombs and linger without departing — you and Holihosun lead troops to inspect."

entries.zh: 既至，山陵如故，俄而叛兵大至，圍之三匝，三日不解。
entries.en: When they arrived the tombs were undisturbed, but rebel forces soon appeared in strength, surrounding them three deep for three days without relief.
entries.literal: When they arrived the tombs were as before; soon rebel troops came in great force, encircling them three deep, and for three days the siege was not lifted.

entries.zh: 忠良引眾夜歸，敵殊不覺，和禮霍孫以為神，白其事於帝，賜黃金十兩。
entries.en: Zhongliang led his men out by night without the enemy detecting them. Holihosun took it for a miracle, reported the exploit to the emperor, and Zhongliang received ten taels of gold.
entries.literal: Zhongliang led his men back by night; the enemy did not notice at all. Holihosun regarded it as miraculous, reported the affair to the emperor, and he was granted ten taels of gold.

entries.zh: 八月，以海都為邊患，遣皇子北平王那木罕、丞相安童征之，忠良奏曰：「不吉，將有叛者。」
entries.en: In the eighth month, with Haidu threatening the frontier, the Prince of Beiping Namuhan and Chancellor Antong were dispatched against him. Zhongliang warned, "The omens are bad — rebellion will follow."
entries.literal: In the eighth month, because Haidu was a border menace, the Prince of Beiping Namuhan and Chancellor Antong were sent to campaign against him. Zhongliang memorialized: "It is inauspicious — there will be rebels."

entries.zh: 帝不悅。
entries.en: The emperor was displeased.
entries.literal: The emperor was displeased.

entries.zh: 十二月，諸王昔里吉劫皇子、丞相以入海都，帝召忠良曰：「朕幾信讒言罪汝，今如汝言，汝祀神致禱，雖黃金朕所不吝。」
entries.en: In the twelfth month Prince Shiregi seized the prince and chancellor and delivered them to Haidu. The emperor summoned Zhongliang: "I nearly believed your enemies and punished you; events have proved you right. Pray to the spirits on our behalf — ask for whatever gold you need."
entries.literal: In the twelfth month Prince Shiregi seized the prince and chancellor and took them to Haidu. The emperor summoned Zhongliang and said: "I nearly believed slander and punished you; now it is as you said. Offer sacrifices to the spirits and pray — though it be gold, I shall not be sparing."

entries.zh: 忠良對曰：「無事於神，皇子未年當還。」
entries.en: "No need to trouble the spirits," Zhongliang said. "The prince will return before year's end."
entries.literal: Zhongliang replied: "There is no need to trouble the spirits — the prince will return before the year is out."

entries.zh: 後果然。
entries.en: And so it proved.
entries.literal: And afterward it was indeed so.

entries.zh: 十四年八月，車駕駐隆興北，忠良奏曰：「昔里吉之叛，以安童之食不彼及也。
entries.en: In the eighth month of the fourteenth year, while the court was encamped north of Longxing, Zhongliang said, "Shiregi's rebellion stemmed from Antong's troops going without adequate rations.
entries.literal: In the eighth month of the fourteenth year the imperial carriage halted north of Longxing. Zhongliang memorialized: "Shiregi's rebellion arose because Antong's provisions did not reach them.

entries.zh: 今宿衛之士，日食一瓜，豈能充飢，竊有怨言矣。」
entries.en: Today the palace guards receive only one melon a day — hardly enough to sustain them — and discontent is already spreading."
entries.literal: Now the palace guards eat but one melon a day — how can that fill their hunger? There are already private complaints."

entries.zh: 帝怒，笞主膳二人，俾均其食。
entries.en: The emperor was furious, had the two chief provisioners flogged, and ordered rations distributed fairly.
entries.literal: The emperor was angry, flogged the two chief provisioners, and ordered rations to be distributed equally.

entries.zh: 十五年三月，汴梁河清三百里，帝曰：「憲宗生，河清；
entries.en: In the third month of the fifteenth year the Yellow River at Bianliang ran clear for three hundred li. The emperor said, "When Emperor Xianzong was born, the river ran clear;
entries.literal: In the third month of the fifteenth year the Yellow River at Bianliang ran clear for three hundred li. The emperor said: "When Emperor Xianzong was born, the river ran clear;

entries.zh: 朕生，河又清；
entries.en: when I was born, it ran clear again;
entries.literal: when I was born, the river ran clear again;

entries.zh: 今河又清，何耶？」
entries.en: and now it runs clear once more — what does this mean?"
entries.literal: now the river runs clear again — why?"

entries.zh: 忠良對曰：「應在皇太子宮矣。」
entries.en: "The omen concerns the Heir Apparent," Zhongliang replied.
entries.literal: Zhongliang replied: "The omen applies to the Heir Apparent's palace."

entries.zh: 帝語符寶郎董文忠曰：「是不妄言，殆有徵也。」
entries.en: The emperor told Dong Wenzhong, Keeper of the Imperial Seals, "He does not speak lightly — there may be something to this."
entries.literal: The emperor said to the Keeper of Seals Dong Wenzhong: "This man does not speak idly — there is likely a sign in it."

entries.zh: 德進為人材辨，幼讀書，能通大義，父歿，益自刻勵，尤精於星曆之學。
entries.en: Dejin was a man of keen discernment. He read widely from youth and grasped essential principles. After his father's death he applied himself with redoubled discipline, becoming especially expert in astronomy and calendrics.
entries.literal: Dejin was discerning in talent; from youth he read books and could grasp great principles. After his father's death he redoubled his self-discipline, especially mastering the study of astronomy and calendrics.

entries.zh: 世祖命太保秉忠選太史官屬，德進以選授天文、星曆、卜筮三科管勾，凡交蝕躔次、六氣侵沴，所言休咎輒應。
entries.en: Kublai ordered Liu Bingzhong to select staff for the Directorate of Astronomy. Dejin was chosen and made superintendent of its three divisions — astronomy, calendrics, and divination. Whether predicting eclipses, planetary movements, or atmospheric disturbances, his forecasts of fortune and misfortune invariably proved correct.
entries.literal: Shizu ordered Grand Preceptor Bingzhong to select staff for the Directorate of Astronomy; Dejin was chosen and appointed superintendent of the three sections of astronomy, calendrics, and divination. In all matters of eclipses, planetary positions, and the six qi in conflict — whatever he said of fortune or misfortune invariably came to pass.

entries.zh: 時因天象以進規諫，多所裨益。
entries.en: He often used celestial omens as occasions to offer remonstrance to the throne, to considerable benefit.
entries.literal: At the time he used celestial phenomena to offer remonstrance and admonition, greatly benefiting the state.

entries.zh: 累遷秘書監，掌司天事。
entries.en: He rose through successive promotions to Director of the Palace Library, overseeing all astronomical affairs.
entries.literal: Through successive promotions he reached Director of the Palace Library, in charge of astronomical affairs.

entries.zh: 從征叛王乃顏，揆度日時，率中機會。
entries.en: On the campaign against the rebel prince Nayan, his calculations of timing and auspicious moments proved consistently accurate.
entries.literal: Accompanying the campaign against the rebel prince Nayan, in calculating days and times he generally hit the opportune moment.

entries.zh: 諸將欲剿絕其黨，德進獨陳天道好生，請緩師以待其降。
entries.en: When the generals wanted to annihilate Nayan's followers, Dejin alone appealed to heaven's preference for preserving life and urged them to hold back and await surrender.
entries.literal: The generals wished to exterminate his faction entirely; Dejin alone cited heaven's way of cherishing life and requested slowing the army to await their surrender.

entries.zh: 俄奏言：「叛始由惑於妖言，遂謀不軌，宜括天下術士，設陰陽教官，使訓學者，仍歲貢有成者一人。」
entries.en: He soon memorialized, "This rebellion began with men led astray by occult prophecy. We should register diviners throughout the realm, appoint Yin-Yang instructors to train students properly, and each year present one accomplished graduate to the court."
entries.literal: Shortly he memorialized: "The rebellion began from being deluded by demonic talk and thus plotting treason. It is fitting to gather occult specialists throughout the realm, establish Yin-Yang instruction officials to train students, and each year present one who has achieved mastery."

entries.zh: 帝從之，遂著為令。
entries.en: The emperor agreed, and the policy was enacted as law.
entries.literal: The emperor followed this and it was established as a statute.

entries.zh: 成宗以皇孫撫軍北邊，帝遣使授皇太子寶，德進預在行，凡攻戰取勝，皆豫剋期日，無不驗者。
entries.en: When Emperor Chengzong, as imperial grandson, garrisoned the northern frontier, the court sent envoys to invest the heir with the imperial seal. Dejin accompanied the expedition, and in every battle won he predicted the day of victory in advance — and none failed to come true.
entries.literal: When Chengzong as imperial grandson garrisoned the northern frontier, the emperor sent envoys to invest the heir apparent with the imperial seal; Dejin accompanied the expedition, and in every battle won he predicted the day of victory in advance — none failed to come true.

entries.zh: 亦間言事得失，多所裨益。
entries.en: He also occasionally offered counsel on affairs of state, to considerable benefit.
entries.literal: He also occasionally spoke on the rights and wrongs of affairs, greatly benefiting the state.

entries.zh: 成宗即位，歷陳世祖進賢納諫、咨詢治亂之原，帝嘉納之。
entries.en: When Emperor Chengzong succeeded, Dejin repeatedly urged the emperor to follow Kublai's example of advancing worthies, accepting remonstrance, and inquiring into the roots of order and disorder — counsel the emperor praised and adopted.
entries.literal: When Chengzong took the throne, he repeatedly set forth how the Shizu emperor advanced worthies, accepted remonstrance, and inquired into the roots of order and disorder; the emperor praised and adopted his counsel.

entries.zh: 授昭文館大學士，知太史院，領司天臺事，賜金帶宴服。
entries.en: He was appointed Grand Academician of the Hall for the Diffusion of Literature, given charge of the Directorate of Astronomy and placed in charge of its observatory affairs, and granted a gold belt and banquet robes.
entries.literal: He was appointed Grand Academician of the Hall for the Diffusion of Literature, given charge of the Directorate of Astronomy, and placed in charge of the Directorate of Astronomy affairs; he was granted a gold belt and banquet robes.

entries.zh: 都城以荻苫廩，或請以瓦易之，帝以問德進，對曰：「若是役驟興，物必踴貴，民力重困，臣愚未見其可。」
entries.en: The capital's granaries were thatched with reeds, and some proposed replacing the thatch with tile. When the emperor asked Dejin, he replied, "If such a project were launched suddenly, materials would surely soar in price and the people would be heavily burdened. I see no merit in it."
entries.literal: The capital's granaries were thatched with reeds, and some proposed replacing them with tile; the emperor asked Dejin, who replied, "If such a project were suddenly launched, materials would surely soar in price and the people's strength would be heavily burdened. Your subject's dull wit sees no merit in it."

entries.zh: 議遂寢。
entries.en: The proposal was then dropped.
entries.literal: The proposal was then dropped.

entries.zh: 敕中書自今凡集議政事，必使德進預焉。
entries.en: An edict ordered that from then on, whenever the Central Secretariat assembled to deliberate state affairs, Dejin must participate.
entries.literal: An edict ordered the Central Secretariat that from then on, whenever state affairs were deliberated in assembly, Dejin must participate.

entries.zh: 所建明多見於施行。
entries.en: Most of his proposals were put into practice.
entries.literal: Most of what he proposed was seen in implementation.

entries.zh: 尋以病丐閑。
entries.en: Soon afterward he asked to be relieved on grounds of illness.
entries.literal: Before long, on grounds of illness he requested a less demanding post.

entries.zh: 仁宗時在東宮，特令中書加官以留之。
entries.en: While the future Emperor Renzong was still heir apparent, he specially ordered the Central Secretariat to promote Dejin in order to keep him at court.
entries.literal: When Renzong was still in the Eastern Palace, he specially ordered the Central Secretariat to add to his rank in order to keep him.

entries.zh: 會車駕自上京還，召見白海行宮，授資德大夫、中書右丞，議通政院事。
entries.en: When the emperor returned from Shangdu, Dejin was summoned to audience at the traveling palace at Bai Hai and appointed grand master for virtuous conduct and right vice director of the Central Secretariat, with responsibility for deliberating affairs of the Bureau of Transmission.
entries.literal: When the imperial carriage returned from Shangdu, he was summoned to audience at the traveling palace at Bai Hai and appointed Grand Master for Virtuous Conduct, Right Vice Director of the Central Secretariat, and assigned to deliberate affairs of the Bureau of Transmission.

entries.zh: 仁宗即位，命領太史院事，力辭不允。
entries.en: When Emperor Renzong succeeded, he was ordered to head the Directorate of Astronomy; he strenuously declined but was not permitted to refuse.
entries.literal: When Renzong took the throne, he was ordered to head the Directorate of Astronomy; he strenuously declined but was not permitted.

entries.zh: 以疾卒于位。
entries.en: He died of illness in office.
entries.literal: He died of illness in office.

entries.zh: 贈推誠贊治功臣、榮祿大夫、大司徒、柱國、魏國公，諡文穆。
entries.en: Posthumously he was honored as meritorious minister who promoted loyalty and supported governance, grandee of glorious emolument, grand minister of education, pillar of state, and Duke of Wei, with the posthumous name Wenmu (Cultured and Solemn).
entries.literal: Posthumously he was granted the title Meritorious Minister Who Promoted Loyalty and Supported Governance, Grandee of Glorious Emolument, Grand Minister of Education, Pillar of State, and Duke of the State of Wei, with the posthumous name Wenmu.

entries.zh: 子泰，工部侍郎。
entries.en: His son Tai served as vice minister of the Ministry of Works.
entries.literal: His son Tai served as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Works.

entries.zh: 十八年，特命為太常丞。
entries.en: In the eighteenth year he was specially appointed Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year he was specially appointed Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.

entries.zh: 少府為諸王昌童建宅於太廟南，忠良往僕其柱，少府奏之，帝問忠良，對曰：「太廟前豈諸王建宅所耶？」
entries.en: The Palace Provisioner was building a mansion for Prince Changtong south of the Imperial Ancestral Temple. Zhongliang leaned against its pillars in protest. When the Provisioner reported this and the emperor questioned him, Zhongliang said, "Is the ground before the Imperial Ancestral Temple fit for a prince's residence?"
entries.literal: The Palace Provisioner built a residence for Prince Changtong south of the Imperial Ancestral Temple. Zhongliang went to lean against its pillars; the Provisioner reported this. The emperor questioned Zhongliang, who replied: "Before the Imperial Ancestral Temple — is that a place for princes to build residences?"

entries.zh: 帝曰：「卿言是也。」
entries.en: "You are right," the emperor said."
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Your words are correct."

entries.zh: 又奏曰：「太廟前無馳道，非禮也。」
entries.en: He added, "There is no imperial roadway before the temple — this violates ritual propriety."
entries.literal: He further memorialized: "Before the Imperial Ancestral Temple there is no imperial roadway — this is not according to ritual."

entries.zh: 即敕中書辟道。
entries.en: The emperor immediately ordered the Secretariat to open one.
entries.literal: An edict immediately ordered the Secretariat to open a roadway.

entries.zh: 國製，十月上吉，有事於太廟。
entries.en: By dynastic custom, sacrifices at the Imperial Ancestral Temple are held on an auspicious day early in the tenth month.
entries.literal: By national custom, on an auspicious day in the upper part of the tenth month, sacrifices are performed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

entries.zh: 或請牲不用牛，忠良奏曰：「梁武帝用面為犧牲，後如何耶？」
entries.en: Some proposed dispensing with cattle as sacrificial victims. Zhongliang objected, "Emperor Wu of Liang offered dough in place of livestock — and what became of his dynasty?"
entries.literal: Some requested that sacrificial victims not use cattle. Zhongliang memorialized: "Emperor Wu of Liang used dough for sacrificial victims — what became of him afterward?"

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The court accepted his view.
entries.literal: His view was followed.

entries.zh: 遷太常少卿。
entries.en: He was promoted to Junior Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Junior Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.

entries.zh: 二十年，將徵日本國，召忠良擇日出師，忠良奏曰：「僻陋海隅，何足勞天戈。」
entries.en: In the twentieth year, as an expedition against Japan was being planned, Zhongliang was asked to select an auspicious departure date. He urged, "Why waste the imperial armies on a remote island at the edge of the sea?"
entries.literal: In the twentieth year, when an expedition against Japan was planned, Zhongliang was summoned to choose the day for the army's departure. He memorialized: "A remote corner of the sea — why trouble the imperial arms?"

entries.zh: 不聽。
entries.en: The emperor would not listen.
entries.literal: His advice was not heeded.

entries.zh: 二十四年，請建太社於朝右，建郊壇於國南。
entries.en: In the twenty-fourth year he petitioned to erect the Grand Earth Altar to the right of the palace and the suburban sacrifice altar south of the capital.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he requested building the Grand Earth Altar to the right of the court and the suburban altar south of the capital.

entries.zh: 俄兼引進使。
entries.en: Soon afterward he was also appointed Introducing Commissioner.
entries.literal: Shortly he also served concurrently as Introducing Commissioner.

entries.zh: 二十九年，遷太常卿。
entries.en: In the twenty-ninth year he was promoted to Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.
entries.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was transferred to Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.

entries.zh: 張康，字汝安，號明遠，潭州湘潭人。
entries.en: Zhang Kang, styled Ru'an and known as Mingyuan, came from Xiangtan in Tan Prefecture.
entries.literal: Zhang Kang, courtesy name Ru'an, style name Mingyuan, was a native of Xiangtan in Tan Prefecture.

entries.zh: 祖安厚，父世英。
entries.en: His grandfather was named Anhou and his father was named Shiying.
entries.literal: His grandfather was Anhou, and his father was Shiying.

entries.zh: 康早孤力學，旁通術數。
entries.en: Orphaned young, Kang devoted himself to study and became widely versed in divination and numerology.
entries.literal: Kang lost his father early and studied diligently, broadly mastering numerology and the occult arts.

entries.zh: 宋呂文德、江萬里、留夢炎皆推重之，辟置幕下。
entries.en: During the Song, Lü Wende, Jiang Wanli, and Liu Mengyan all held him in high regard and brought him onto their staffs.
entries.literal: Under the Song, Lü Wende, Jiang Wanli, and Liu Mengyan all esteemed him highly and recruited him into their staffs.

entries.zh: 宋亡，隱衡山。
entries.en: After the Song dynasty fell, he withdrew to live in seclusion on Mount Heng.
entries.literal: When the Song fell, he went into seclusion on Mount Heng.

entries.zh: 至元十四年，世祖遣中丞崔彧祀南嶽，就訪隱逸。
entries.en: In 1277, Emperor Shizu sent Censor-in-Chief Cui Yu to perform rites at Mount Heng and to inquire after reclusive worthies on the way.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhiyuan, the Shizu emperor dispatched Censor-in-Chief Cui Yu to sacrifice at the Southern Peak and, while there, to seek out recluses.

entries.zh: 彧兄湖南行省參政崔斌言康隱衡山，學通天文地理。
entries.en: Yu's elder brother Cui Bin, a vice administrator of the Hunan Branch Secretariat, told him that Kang was living in seclusion on Mount Heng and was versed in astronomy and geography.
entries.literal: Yu's elder brother Cui Bin, Vice Administrator of the Hunan Branch Secretariat, reported that Kang was hiding on Mount Heng and that his learning embraced astronomy and geography.

entries.zh: 彧還，具以聞，遣使召康，與斌偕至京師。
entries.en: On his return, Yu reported this in full to the court, which dispatched an envoy to summon Kang; he and Bin traveled together to the capital.
entries.literal: When Yu returned, he reported everything in full, and an envoy was sent to summon Kang; together with Bin he arrived at the capital.

entries.zh: 十五年夏四月，至上都見帝，親試所學，大驗，授著作佐郎，仍以內嬪松夫人妻之。
entries.en: In the fourth month of summer 1278 he appeared before the emperor at Shangdu; the emperor personally tested his skills and found them remarkably accurate. He was appointed Assistant Compiler, and the court also gave him Lady Song of the inner palace in marriage.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of summer in the fifteenth year, he went to the Upper Capital to see the emperor; his learning was tested in person and proved greatly accurate; he was appointed Assistant Compiler and moreover given Lady Song of the inner palace as his wife.

entries.zh: 凡召對，禮遇殊厚，呼以明遠而不名。
entries.en: Whenever he was summoned to audience, he received exceptional honors; the emperor called him Mingyuan and never used his personal name.
entries.literal: Whenever he was summoned for audience, the courtesy shown was exceptionally generous; he was addressed as Mingyuan rather than by name.

entries.zh: 嘗面諭：凡有所問，使極言之。
entries.en: The emperor once told him face to face, "When I question you about anything, speak your mind fully."
entries.literal: Once the emperor personally instructed him: "Whatever you are asked, speak to the utmost."

entries.zh: 十八年，康上奏：「歲壬午，太一理艮宮，主大將客、參將囚，直符治事，正屬燕分。
entries.en: In 1281 Kang submitted a memorial: "In the year renwu, Taiyi occupies the Gen Palace, with the Grand General as guest, the Deputy General imprisoned, and the Direct Talisman in charge of affairs — precisely the sphere of the Yan region.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year, Kang memorialized: "In the year renwu, Taiyi governs the Gen Palace; the Grand General is guest, the Deputy General is imprisoned, and the Direct Talisman handles affairs — this directly corresponds to the Yan region.

entries.zh: 明年春，京城當有盜兵，事干將相。」
entries.en: Next spring the capital will see armed rebels, and the affair will touch generals and chief ministers."
entries.literal: Next spring, the capital will have bandit-soldiers; the affair will involve generals and ministers."

entries.zh: 十九年三月，盜果起京師，殺阿合馬等。
entries.en: In March 1282 rebels did arise in the capital and killed Ahmad and others.
entries.literal: In the third month of the nineteenth year, bandits indeed rose in the capital and killed Ahmad and others.

entries.zh: 帝欲徵日本，命康以太一推之，康奏曰：「南國甫定，民力未蘇，且今年太一無算，舉兵不利。」
entries.en: When the emperor planned a campaign against Japan, he had Kang read the Taiyi charts. Kang replied, "The south has only just been subdued and the people are not yet restored. This year Taiyi offers no favorable reckoning; to mobilize now would be ill-advised."
entries.literal: The emperor wished to campaign against Japan and ordered Kang to calculate by Taiyi; Kang memorialized, saying: "The southern lands have only just been pacified and the people's strength has not yet recovered; moreover, this year Taiyi is unfathomable — raising troops would be unpropitious."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The court accepted his view.
entries.literal: His view was followed.

entries.zh: 嘗賜太史院錢，分千貫以與康，不受，眾服其廉。
entries.en: Once, when the Astrological Academy received a grant, Kang was offered a thousand strings of cash; he refused, and everyone respected him for his integrity.
entries.literal: Once funds were granted to the Astrological Academy and a share of one thousand strings of cash was given to Kang; he did not accept it, and the multitude admired his integrity.

entries.zh: 久之，乞歸田裡，優詔不許，遷奉直大夫、秘書監丞。
entries.en: After some years he asked to retire to his home village, but an exceptional edict denied the request and he was promoted to Grand Master for Fostering Integrity and Deputy Director of the Palace Library.
entries.literal: After a long time he requested to return to his fields and village; an indulgent edict did not permit this; he was transferred to Grand Master for Fostering Integrity and Deputy Director of the Palace Library.

entries.zh: 年六十五卒。
entries.en: He died at the age of sixty-five.
entries.literal: He died at age sixty-five.

entries.zh: 子天祐。
entries.en: He left a son named Tianyou.
entries.literal: His son was Tianyou.

entries.zh: 子拱，為監察御史，後襲順天安平懷州河南等路甲匠都總管。
entries.en: His son Gong served as an investigating censor and later inherited the post of Grand Supervisor of Armor Artisans for Shuntian, Anping, Huaizhou, Henan, and related circuits.
entries.literal: His son Gong served as Investigating Censor and later inherited the post of Grand Supervisor of Armor Artisans for the circuits of Shuntian, Anping, Huaizhou, Henan, and others.

entries.zh: 巧思如其父，嘗制甲二百八十襲以獻。
entries.en: He inherited his father's ingenuity and once presented two hundred eighty suits of armor to the court.
entries.literal: His ingenuity matched his father's; once he made two hundred eighty suits of armor and presented them.

entries.zh: 至元十一年，別制疊盾，其制，張則為盾，斂則合而易持。
entries.en: In 1274 he invented a folding shield: spread open it served as a shield, folded shut it was compact and easy to carry.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhiyuan he separately devised folding shields; in their design, when spread they served as shields, when folded they closed together and were easy to carry.

entries.zh: 世祖以為古所未有，賜以幣帛。
entries.en: Emperor Shizu declared that nothing like it had existed in antiquity and rewarded him with silks and cloth.
entries.literal: Shizu considered that antiquity had never had such a thing and bestowed silks and cloth.

entries.zh: 丞相伯顏南征，以甲冑不足，詔諸路集匠民分製。
entries.en: When Chancellor Bayan marched south, armor ran short; the court ordered every circuit to mobilize craftsmen and divide production among them.
entries.literal: When Chancellor Bayan campaigned south, because armor was insufficient, an edict ordered the circuits to gather artisan households to manufacture it in shares.

entries.zh: 拱董順天、河間甲匠，先期畢工，且象虎豹異獸之形，各殊其制，皆稱旨。
entries.en: Gong oversaw the armor craftsmen of Shuntian and Hejian. They finished ahead of schedule and fashioned pieces in the shapes of tigers, leopards, and other exotic beasts, each with a unique design — all to the emperor's satisfaction.
entries.literal: Gong supervised the armor artisans of Shuntian and Hejian; they finished the work ahead of schedule, and moreover modeled tiger, leopard, and other exotic beasts, each with a distinct design — all met with approval.

entries.zh: 十五年，授保定路治中。
entries.en: In 1278 he was appointed administrative assistant of Baoding Circuit.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed Administrative Assistant of Baoding Circuit.

entries.zh: 適歲饑，議開倉賑民，或曰：「宜請於朝。」
entries.en: That year brought famine, and officials debated opening the granaries to feed the people. Some said, "We should request permission from the court."
entries.literal: It happened to be a year of famine; they deliberated opening the granaries to relieve the people; someone said: "It is fitting to request permission from the court."

entries.zh: 拱曰：「救荒事不可緩也，若得請而後發粟以賑之，則民餒死矣。
entries.en: Gong replied, "Famine relief cannot wait. If we hold back grain until permission arrives, people will die of hunger.
entries.literal: Gong said: "Relief in famine cannot be delayed; if one waits to obtain permission before issuing grain to relieve them, the people will starve to death.

entries.zh: 苟見罪，吾自任之。」
entries.en: If I am punished for this, I will accept the blame myself."
entries.literal: If I am punished, I shall bear it myself."

entries.zh: 遂發粟四千五百石以賑饑民。
entries.en: He immediately released four thousand five hundred shi of grain to feed the starving population.
entries.literal: He then issued four thousand five hundred shi of grain to relieve the starving people.

entries.zh: 高陽土豪據沙河橋取行者錢，人以為病，拱執而罪之。
entries.en: A local bully in Gaoyang controlled Shahe Bridge and extorted tolls from travelers, a grievance widely resented. Gong arrested him and punished him.
entries.literal: A local strongman of Gaoyang held Shahe Bridge and took money from travelers; people regarded this as a plague; Gong seized him and punished him.

entries.zh: 二十二年，除武備少卿，遷大都路軍器人匠總管，升工部侍郎。
entries.en: In 1285 he was made Vice Commissioner of the Armory Court, then transferred to Grand Supervisor of Military Equipment and Artisan Households in Dadu, and promoted to Vice Minister of Works.
entries.literal: In the twenty-second year he was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Armory Court, transferred to Grand Supervisor of Military Equipment and Artisan Households of Dadu Circuit, and promoted to Vice Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 成宗即位，典朝會供給，賜銀百兩、織紋段五十匹、帛二十五匹、鈔萬貫。
entries.en: When Emperor Chengzong took the throne, Gong managed provisions for court assemblies and was rewarded with a hundred taels of silver, fifty bolts of brocade, twenty-five bolts of silk, and ten thousand strings of paper money.
entries.literal: When Chengzong ascended the throne, he managed supplies for court assemblies and was granted one hundred taels of silver, fifty bolts of brocade, twenty-five bolts of silk, and ten thousand strings of paper money.

entries.zh: 元貞二年，授大同路總管，兼府尹。
entries.en: In 1296 he was appointed prefect of Datong Circuit, serving concurrently as prefectural governor.
entries.literal: In the second year of Yuanzhen he was appointed Prefect of Datong Circuit, concurrently serving as Prefectural Governor.

entries.zh: 大德五年，遷兩浙都轉運使。
entries.en: In 1301 he was transferred to Commissioner of Transport for the Two Zhe region.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Dade he was transferred to Commissioner of Transport for the Two Zhe Circuits.

entries.zh: 鹽課舊二十五萬引，歲不能足，拱至增五萬引，遂為定額。
entries.en: The salt quota had stood at two hundred fifty thousand yin, but collections routinely fell short. Under Gong it rose by fifty thousand yin and that figure became the fixed quota.
entries.literal: The salt levy had formerly been two hundred fifty thousand yin; each year it could not be filled; when Gong arrived he increased it by fifty thousand yin, and it then became the fixed quota.

entries.zh: 九年，改益都路總管，兼府尹，仍出內府弓矢寶刀賜之。
entries.en: In 1305 he was reassigned as prefect of Yidu Circuit, again serving concurrently as prefectural governor, and the inner palace bestowed bows, arrows, and treasured swords upon him.
entries.literal: In the ninth year he was changed to Prefect of Yidu Circuit, concurrently serving as Prefectural Governor, and moreover the inner palace issued bows, arrows, and precious swords as gifts.

entries.zh: 卒於官。
entries.en: He died while still in office.
entries.literal: He died in office.

entries.zh: 贈大司農、神川郡公，諡文莊。
entries.en: He was posthumously honored as Grand Minister of Agriculture and Duke of Shenchuan, with the posthumous name Cultured and Upright.
entries.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Minister of Agriculture, made Duke of Shenchuan Commandery, and given the posthumous title Wenzhuang.

entries.zh: 阿老瓦丁，回回氏，西域木發里人也。
entries.en: Ala al-Din was a Muslim from Mayafarikin in the Western Regions.
entries.literal: Ala al-Din was of the Hui Muslim people; he was a native of Mayafarikin in the Western Regions.

entries.zh: 至元八年，世祖遣使砲匠於宗王阿不哥，王以阿老瓦丁、亦思馬因應詔，二人舉家馳驛至京師，給以官舍。
entries.en: In 1271 Emperor Shizu sent envoys to Prince Abagha seeking artillery craftsmen. The prince dispatched Ala al-Din and Ismail in answer to the imperial summons; both men rushed their entire households by relay to the capital, where the court lodged them in official residences.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Zhiyuan, Shizu sent envoys to seek artillery craftsmen from the Prince of the Blood Abagha. The prince offered Ala al-Din and Ismail in response to the imperial summons; the two men brought their whole families posthaste by relay station to the capital, where official residences were provided.

entries.zh: 首造大砲豎於五門前，帝命試之，各賜衣段。
entries.en: They built great cannons first and set them up before the Five Gates. The emperor ordered trials, then rewarded each man with bolts of cloth.
entries.literal: They first built great cannons and erected them before the Five Gates. The emperor ordered them tested and rewarded each with bolts of cloth.

entries.zh: 十一年，國兵渡江，平章阿里海牙遣使求砲手匠，命阿老瓦丁往，破潭州、靜江等郡，悉賴其力。
entries.en: In 1274, as the imperial army crossed the Yangtze, Pingzhang Alihaiya sent for cannon masters and craftsmen and dispatched Ala al-Din. The fall of Tanzhou, Jingjiang, and other commanderies owed everything to his skill.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year the national army crossed the Yangtze. Pingzhang Alihaiya sent envoys requesting cannon masters and craftsmen; Ala al-Din was ordered to go. The capture of Tanzhou, Jingjiang, and other commanderies all depended on his strength.

entries.zh: 十五年，授宣武將軍、管軍總管。
entries.en: In 1278 he was made General Who Proclaims Martiality and commander-in-chief of troops under his charge.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed General Who Proclaims Martiality and Commander-in-Chief Who Manages Troops.

entries.zh: 十七年，陛見，賜鈔五千貫。
entries.en: In 1280 he was received in audience and granted five thousand strings of paper money.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year he had an audience with the emperor and was granted five thousand strings of paper money.

entries.zh: 十八年，命屯田於南京。
entries.en: In 1281 he was ordered to establish military colonies at Nanjing.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year he was ordered to establish military colonies at Nanjing.

entries.zh: 二十二年，樞密院奉旨，改元帥府為回回砲手軍匠上萬戶府，以阿老瓦丁為副萬戶。
entries.en: In 1285 the Privy Council, acting on imperial orders, reorganized the marshal's office as the Upper Myriarchate of Muslim Artillerymen and Military Craftsmen and appointed Ala al-Din deputy myriarch.
entries.literal: In the twenty-second year, on orders from the Privy Council, the Marshal's Office was renamed the Upper Myriarchate of Muslim Artillerymen and Military Craftsmen; Ala al-Din was made Deputy Myriarch.

entries.zh: 大德四年告老。
entries.en: In 1300 he retired on grounds of age.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Dade he requested retirement on grounds of age.

entries.zh: 子富謀只，襲副萬戶。
entries.en: His son Fumouzhi inherited the deputy myriarchate.
entries.literal: His son Fumouzhi inherited the post of Deputy Myriarch.

entries.zh: 皇慶元年卒，子馬哈馬沙襲。
entries.en: He died in 1312; his son Mahmushah succeeded him.
entries.literal: He died in the first year of Huangqing; his son Mahmushah inherited.

entries.zh: 自昔帝王勃興，雖星曆醫卜方術異能之士，莫不過絕於人，類非後來所及，蓋天運也。
entries.en: Whenever emperors have risen to power in ages past, experts in astronomy, medicine, divination, and the occult arts have invariably stood head and shoulders above their contemporaries — gifts few later generations could match, shaped by heaven's own design.
entries.literal: From antiquity when emperors rose vigorously, even specialists in astronomy, medicine, divination, arts, and extraordinary abilities all surpassed ordinary men; such men were generally not matched by those who came later — this was heaven's mandate.

entries.zh: 元有中土，巨公異人，身兼數器者，皆應期而出，相與立法創制，開物成務，以輔成大業，亦云盛哉。
entries.en: Under the Yuan in China, remarkable men who mastered many disciplines appeared as if on cue, joining together to frame laws, devise institutions, and advance civilization in support of the dynasty's founding triumph — a flourishing age indeed.
entries.literal: When the Yuan held the Central Plains, great lords and extraordinary men who combined many skills all appeared in response to the times, together establishing laws and creating institutions, opening things and completing affairs, to assist in accomplishing the great enterprise — how splendid indeed.

entries.zh: 若道流釋子，所挾多方，事適逢時，既皆別為之傳。
entries.en: Taoist priests and Buddhist monks, each with their own wide-ranging arts and timely rise to prominence, already have separate biographies elsewhere in these annals.
entries.literal: As for Taoist clergy and Buddhist monks, who possessed many methods and whose affairs happened to suit the times, separate biographies have already been written for them.

entries.zh: 其他以術數言事輒驗，及以醫著效，被光寵者甚眾。
entries.en: Countless others won imperial favor by foretelling events through divination with uncanny accuracy, or by achieving conspicuous success in medicine.
entries.literal: Others who spoke of affairs through numerology and arts and were immediately verified, and those who achieved renown through medicine, were very numerous in receiving imperial favor.

entries.zh: 舊史多闕弗錄，今取其事蹟可見者，為《方技篇》。
entries.en: Earlier histories largely passed them over; here we gather those whose careers can still be traced into this chapter on medicine, divination, and the technical arts.
entries.literal: The old histories mostly omitted and did not record them; now we take those whose deeds are visible and compile the "Treatise on Arts and Techniques."

entries.zh: 而以工藝貴顯，亦附見焉。
entries.en: Those who rose to distinction through the practical arts are included here as well.
entries.literal: Those who attained eminence through craftsmanship are also appended here.

entries.zh: 前世宦者之禍嘗烈矣，元之初興，非能有鑑乎古者，然歷十有餘世，考其亂亡之所由，而初不自閹人出，何哉？
entries.en: In earlier dynasties, eunuchs had repeatedly brought ruin on the state. When the Yuan dynasty first rose, its founders surely knew that history — yet across more than ten reigns, if one traces the causes of chaos and collapse, at first those troubles did not spring from palace eunuchs. How was this so?
entries.literal: In previous ages the calamities of eunuchs were often severe. When the Yuan first arose, could they not take warning from antiquity? Yet passing through more than ten reigns, examining the causes of disorder and ruin, at the outset it did not arise from castrated men — why?

entries.zh: 蓋自太祖選貴臣子弟給事內廷，凡飲食、冠服、書記，上所常御者，各以其職典之，而命四大功臣世為之長，號四怯薛。
entries.en: The reason lay in Taizu’s policy: he chose sons of eminent ministers to serve in the inner court. Everything the emperor routinely used — food and drink, caps and robes, written records — was kept by men assigned to those duties, while four great founding ministers and their descendants were made permanent chiefs of the establishment, known as the Four Kheshig.
entries.literal: Generally, from the time the Taizu selected sons of noble ministers to serve in the inner court, for all food, drink, headgear, robes, and clerical records that the sovereign commonly used, each was managed according to its office, and he appointed the four great meritorious officials to be heads in perpetuity, called the Four Kheshig.

entries.zh: 故天子前後左右，皆世家大臣及其子孫之生而貴者，而宦官之擅權竊政者不得有為於其間。
entries.en: Thus the men at the emperor’s side, before and behind, left and right, were scions of great ministerial houses born to rank — and eunuchs who might seize power and meddle in government had no room to act.
entries.literal: Therefore before and behind and to the left and right of the Son of Heaven were all great ministers of hereditary families and their sons and grandsons born to nobility, and eunuchs who usurped power and stole governance could accomplish nothing among them.

entries.zh: 雖或有之，然不旋踵而遂敗。
entries.en: When such men did appear, they were crushed almost at once.
entries.literal: Although there were sometimes such cases, yet before turning the heel they then failed.

entries.zh: 此其詒謀，可謂度越前代者矣。
entries.en: In foresight for later ages, this arrangement truly went beyond anything earlier dynasties had done.
entries.literal: This planning for posterity may be said to have surpassed previous ages.

entries.zh: 如李邦寧者，以亡國閹豎，遭遇世祖，進齒薦紳，遂躋極品，然其言亦有可稱者焉。
entries.en: Li Bangning, for example, was a eunuch of a fallen kingdom who won favor under Shizu, rose among the scholar-officials, and climbed to the highest ranks — yet some of what he said still deserves respect.
entries.literal: Such as Li Bangning — as a castrated man of a perished state, encountering Shizu, advancing to rank with the gentry, then ascending to the highest grade — yet his words also had what could be praised.

entries.zh: 至於樸不花，乃東夷之人，始以西宮同里，因緣柄用，遂與權奸同惡相濟，訖底於誅戮，則固有以致之也。
entries.en: Po Buhua, by contrast, came from the eastern borderlands. He had grown up in the same hometown as the empress of the Western Palace; through that connection he gained power, then joined forces with corrupt ministers until he was put to death — a fate he had largely brought on himself.
entries.literal: As for Po Buhua, he was a man of the eastern Yi. At first, being from the same village as the Western Palace, by circumstance he grasped use of power, then with powerful villains aided each other’s wickedness, ending in execution and punishment — there were indeed causes that brought this about.

entries.zh: 用特著之於篇。
entries.en: For these reasons they are given special treatment in this chapter.
entries.literal: Therefore they are specially set forth in this chapter.

entries.zh: 李邦寧字叔固，錢唐人，初名保寧，宋故小黃門也。
entries.en: Li Bangning, courtesy name Shugu, was a native of Qiantang. Originally named Baoning, he had served the Song as a junior palace eunuch.
entries.literal: Li Bangning, courtesy name Shugu, was a native of Qiantang. His original name was Baoning. He had been a junior yellow-gate attendant of the Song.

entries.zh: 宋亡，從瀛國公入見世祖，命給事內庭，警敏稱上意。
entries.en: After the fall of the Song, he accompanied the Duke of Ying to an audience with Shizu. The emperor assigned him to the inner court; sharp and responsive, he won the sovereign's favor.
entries.literal: When the Song perished, he followed the Duke of Ying to have an audience with Shizu. He was ordered to serve in the inner court; alert and quick-witted, he pleased the sovereign's intent.

entries.zh: 令學國書及諸蕃語，即通解，遂見親任。
entries.en: Ordered to study the Mongol script and the languages of various foreign peoples, he quickly mastered them and won the emperor's personal trust.
entries.literal: He was ordered to study the national script and the languages of various foreign peoples; he immediately mastered and understood them, and came to be personally trusted.

entries.zh: 授御帶庫提點，陞章佩少監，遷禮部尚書，提點太醫院事。
entries.en: He was appointed intendant of the Imperial Belt Treasury, promoted to junior supervisor of the Seals and Insignia Office, transferred to minister of rites, and made intendant of the Imperial Medical Office.
entries.literal: He was appointed Intendant of the Imperial Belt Treasury, promoted to Junior Supervisor of the Seals and Insignia Office, transferred to Minister of Rites, and made Intendant of the Imperial Medical Office.

entries.zh: 成宗即位，進昭文館大學士、太醫院使。
entries.en: When Chengzong came to the throne, he was promoted to grand academician of the Zhaowen Hall and made commissioner of the Imperial Medical Office.
entries.literal: When Chengzong succeeded to the throne, he was advanced to Grand Academician of the Zhaowen Hall and made Commissioner of the Imperial Medical Office.

entries.zh: 帝嘗寢疾，邦寧不離左右者十餘月。
entries.en: When the emperor once fell seriously ill, Bangning stayed at his side without leaving for more than ten months.
entries.literal: The emperor once fell ill and lay abed; Bangning did not leave his side for more than ten months.

entries.zh: 武宗立，命為江浙行省平章政事，邦寧辭曰：「臣以閹腐餘命，無望更生，先朝幸赦而用之，使得承乏中涓，高爵厚祿，榮寵過甚。
entries.en: When Wuzong took the throne, he was appointed pingzhang political commissioner of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat. Bangning declined, saying, "I am only a castrated man spared from death; I have no hope of a new life. The previous emperor mercifully pardoned and employed me, letting me fill a post among the palace attendants — rank, salary, and honors already far beyond my deserts.
entries.literal: When Wuzong ascended the throne, he was appointed Pingzhang Political Commissioner of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat. Bangning declined, saying: "Your servant, by the remnant life of a castrated and corrupted man, has no hope of renewal. The previous court fortunately pardoned and employed me, allowing me to fill a vacancy among the palace attendants — high rank, thick salary, glory and favor beyond measure.

entries.zh: 陛下復欲置臣宰輔，臣何敢當？
entries.en: Your Majesty now wishes to make me a chief minister — how could I dare accept?
entries.literal: Your Majesty now wishes again to place your servant among the chief ministers — how would your servant dare accept?

entries.zh: 宰輔者，佐天子共治天下者也，奈何辱以寺人？
entries.en: Chief ministers assist the Son of Heaven in governing the realm — how can that office be disgraced by appointing a temple eunuch?
entries.literal: Chief ministers are those who assist the Son of Heaven in jointly governing all under Heaven — how can one insult that office with a temple eunuch?

entries.zh: 陛下縱不臣惜，如天下後世何！
entries.en: Even if Your Majesty does not care for me, what will the realm and posterity think!
entries.literal: Even if Your Majesty does not pity your servant, what of all under Heaven and later ages!

entries.zh: 誠不敢奉詔。」
entries.en: I truly dare not obey the edict."
entries.literal: I truly dare not obey the edict."

entries.zh: 帝大悅，使大臣白其言于太后及皇太子，以彰其善。
entries.en: The emperor was greatly pleased and had a senior minister repeat his words to the empress dowager and the crown prince, to display his merit.
entries.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and had a great minister report his words to the empress dowager and the crown prince, to make manifest his virtue.

entries.zh: 帝嘗奉皇太后燕大安閣，閣中有故篋，問邦寧曰：「此何篋也？」
entries.en: Once, while hosting the empress dowager at a feast in the Great Peace Pavilion, the emperor noticed an old chest in the hall and asked Bangning, "What is this chest?"
entries.literal: The Emperor once attended the Empress Dowager at a banquet in the Great Peace Pavilion. In the pavilion was an old box. He asked Bangning: "What box is this?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「此世祖貯裘帶者。
entries.en: Bangning answered, "That is the chest in which Shizu kept his fur robes and belts.
entries.literal: He replied: "This is where Shizu stored fur robes and belts.

entries.zh: 臣聞有聖訓曰：'藏此以遺子孫，使見吾樸儉，可為華侈之戒。
entries.en: I have heard that he left a sacred instruction: 'Keep these for our descendants, so they may see how plain and frugal I was — let it warn them against luxury and excess.'
entries.literal: Your servant has heard there was a sage instruction saying: 'Store these to bequeath to descendants, so that they may see my plainness and frugality, and it may serve as a warning against splendor and extravagance.'

entries.zh: '」帝命發篋視之，歎曰：「非卿言，朕安知之。」
entries.en: " The emperor had the chest opened and sighed. "If you had not told me, how would I ever have known?"
entries.literal: '" The Emperor ordered the box opened to view it, and sighed: "Had it not been for your words, how would We have known?"

entries.zh: 時有宗王在側，遽曰：「世祖雖神聖，然嗇於財。」
entries.en: A prince standing nearby blurted out, "Shizu may have been a sage, but he was miserly with money."
entries.literal: At the time a imperial clansman was at the side and hastily said: "Shizu, though divine and sagely, was nevertheless stingy with wealth."

entries.zh: 邦寧曰：「不然。
entries.en: Bangning replied, "That is not so.
entries.literal: Bangning said: "It is not so.

entries.zh: 世祖一言，無不為後世法；
entries.en: Every word Shizu spoke became a model for later generations;
entries.literal: Shizu’s every word was without exception a model for later generations;

entries.zh: 一予奪，無不當功罪。
entries.en: every reward or punishment matched true merit and fault.
entries.literal: every grant or withdrawal was without exception appropriate to merit and guilt.

entries.zh: 且天下所入雖富，苟用不節，必致匱乏。
entries.en: Besides, however rich the empire’s income, spending without restraint would soon drain the treasury.
entries.literal: Moreover, although the empire’s receipts were abundant, if use were not restrained, it would necessarily lead to depletion.

entries.zh: 自先朝以來，歲賦已不足用，又數會宗籓，資費無算，旦暮不給，必將橫斂掊怨，豈美事耶。」
entries.en: Since the previous reign, annual revenue has already fallen short, and repeated gatherings of the imperial clan have cost sums beyond counting. If income cannot meet daily needs, harsh levies will breed popular resentment — is that anything to admire?"
entries.literal: From the previous reign onward, the annual levies were already insufficient for use; moreover there were repeatedly assemblies of the imperial clan, with expenses beyond reckoning. If morning and evening there were not enough, there would necessarily be harsh exactions and accumulated resentment — how could this be a fine affair?"

entries.zh: 太后及帝深然其言。
entries.en: The empress dowager and the emperor were both deeply impressed.
entries.literal: The Empress Dowager and the Emperor deeply approved his words.

entries.zh: 俄加大司徒、尚服院使，遙授丞相，行大司農，領太醫院事，階金紫光祿大夫。
entries.en: Soon afterward he was further appointed Grand Minister of Education and commissioner of the Imperial Wardrobe Office, given the nominal title of chancellor, acting as Grand Minister of Agriculture and supervising the Imperial Medical Office, with the rank of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness bearing the golden seal and purple ribbon.
entries.literal: Shortly he was further appointed Grand Minister of Education, Commissioner of the Imperial Wardrobe Office, given the title of Chancellor at a distance, acting as Grand Minister of Agriculture, and overseeing the Imperial Medical Office, with rank as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

entries.zh: 中統元年，世祖即位，加璮江淮大都督。
entries.en: In the first year of Zhongtong, when Shizu ascended the throne, Tan was made Grand Commander of the Jianghuai region.
entries.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong, when Shizu took the throne, Tan was given the additional title of Grand Commander of the Jianghuai region.

entries.zh: 璮言：「近獲生口，知宋調兵將攻漣水。
entries.en: Tan reported, "We have lately taken prisoners who say the Song are massing troops to attack Lianshui.
entries.literal: Tan reported: "Recently we captured prisoners and learned that Song is mobilizing troops and is about to attack Lianshui.

entries.zh: 且諜見許浦、射陽湖舟艦相望，勢欲出膠西，向益都，請繕城塹以備。」
entries.en: Spies also report warships massed at Xupu and Sheyang Lake, poised to break out of Jiaoxi toward Yidu. I ask that the walls and ditches be repaired in preparation."
entries.literal: Moreover spies have seen ships at Xupu and Sheyang Lake facing one another in formation, with the intent to come out of Jiaoxi toward Yidu; I request that the walls and moats be repaired for defense."

entries.zh: 詔出金符十、銀符五授璮，以賞將士有功者，且賜銀三百錠，降詔獎諭。
entries.en: The court issued ten gold tallies and five silver tallies for Tan to reward meritorious troops, granted three hundred ingots of silver, and sent a commendatory edict.
entries.literal: An edict issued ten gold tallies and five silver tallies to Tan to reward officers and soldiers who had merit, and also bestowed three hundred ingots of silver, with an imperial decree of commendation.

entries.zh: 蒙古、漢軍之在邊者，咸聽節制。
entries.en: All Mongol and Han forces on the frontier were placed under his command.
entries.literal: Mongol and Han troops on the frontier were all placed under his command.

entries.zh: 璮復揚言：「宋呂文德合淮南兵七萬五千，來攻漣水，且規築堡以臨我。
entries.en: Tan again spread word: "Song's Lü Wende has combined seventy-five thousand Huainan troops to attack Lianshui and moreover plans to build forts to press upon us.
entries.literal: Tan again spread word: "Song's Lü Wende has combined seventy-five thousand Huainan troops to attack Lianshui, and moreover plans to build forts to press upon us.

entries.zh: 及得賈似道、呂文德書，辭甚悖傲。
entries.en: Letters from Jia Sidao and Lü Wende that he obtained were brazenly insulting.
entries.literal: When letters from Jia Sidao and Lü Wende were obtained, the wording was extremely insolent and arrogant.

entries.zh: 知朝廷近有內顧之憂，必將肆志於我。
entries.en: They know the court has lately been preoccupied with internal troubles and will surely turn on us in earnest.
entries.literal: Knowing that the court lately has worries looking inward, they will surely vent their designs upon us.

entries.zh: 乞選將益兵，臣當帥先渡淮，以雪慢書之辱。」
entries.en: I ask that you choose commanders and reinforce the army; I will lead the crossing of the Huai myself to avenge this insult."
entries.literal: I beg that generals be selected and troops increased; your subject will lead the vanguard across the Huai to wipe away the shame of these contemptuous letters."

entries.zh: 執政得奏，諭以「朝廷方通和議，邊將惟當固封圉。
entries.en: When the chief ministers received the memorial, they instructed him: "The court is presently pursuing peace talks; frontier commanders should only secure the borders.
entries.literal: When the chief ministers received the memorial, they instructed him: "The court is presently pursuing peace talks; frontier commanders should only secure the borders.

entries.zh: 且南人用間，其詐非一，彼既不至，毋或妄動」。
entries.en: The southerners are skilled in deception; if they have not yet attacked, do not stir rashly."
entries.literal: Moreover the southerners employ stratagems; their deceptions are not of one kind. Since they have not yet come, do not act rashly."

entries.zh: 璮乃上言：「臣所領益都，土曠人稀，自立海州，今八載，將士未嘗釋甲，轉輓未嘗息肩，民力凋耗，莫甚斯時，以一路之兵，抗一敵國，衆寡不侔，人所共患。
entries.en: Tan then memorialized: "The Yidu circuit I hold is thinly peopled. For eight years since we took Haizhou my men have never doffed their armor and the transport trains have never stopped; the people are exhausted as never before. One circuit's army against an entire enemy state is a hopeless mismatch, as everyone knows.
entries.literal: Tan then submitted a memorial: "The Yidu region I command has broad land and sparse population; since establishing Haizhou, it is now eight years. Officers and soldiers have never laid aside armor, transport and supply have never ceased, and the people's strength is exhausted—never more than at this time. With the troops of one circuit to resist one enemy state, few and many do not match; this is a worry shared by all.

entries.zh: 賴陛下神武，既克漣、海二州，復破夏貴、孫虎臣十餘萬之師。
entries.en: Thanks to Your Majesty's prowess we have taken Lian and Hai and routed Xia Gui and Sun Huchen's force of more than a hundred thousand.
entries.literal: Relying on Your Majesty's divine martial prowess, we have already taken the two prefectures of Lian and Hai, and again defeated the armies of Xia Gui and Sun Huchen numbering more than a hundred thousand.

entries.zh: 然臣豈敢恃此必敵人之不再至哉！
entries.en: Yet how dare I assume the enemy will not return!
entries.literal: Yet how would your subject dare rely on this that the enemy will certainly not come again!

entries.zh: 且宋人今日西無掣肘，宜得并力而東。
entries.en: The Song are no longer tied down in the west and can now concentrate and strike eastward.
entries.literal: Moreover the Song today have no restraint in the west and ought to be able to combine their strength and advance east.

entries.zh: 若以水陸綴漣，而遣舟師遵海以北，擣膠、萊之虛，然後帥步騎直指沂、莒、滕、嶧，則山東非我有矣，豈可易視而不為備哉。
entries.en: If they pin us at Lian by land and sea, send a fleet north along the coast to raid undefended Jiao and Lai, then march infantry and cavalry on Yi, Ju, Teng, and Yi, Shandong will be lost. How can we treat that lightly or fail to prepare?
entries.literal: If they link land and water forces at Lian and send a fleet along the sea northward to strike the undefended parts of Jiao and Lai, then lead infantry and cavalry straight at Yi, Ju, Teng, and Yi, then Shandong will no longer be ours—how can this be lightly regarded and not prepared against?

entries.zh: 臣昨追敵至淮安，非不能乘勝取揚、楚，徒以執政止臣，故臣不敢深入。
entries.en: When I pursued the enemy to Huai'an I could have pressed on to Yang and Chu, but the chief ministers held me back, so I did not dare advance further.
entries.literal: Your subject yesterday pursued the enemy to Huai'an; it was not that he could not take advantage of victory to seize Yang and Chu, but only because the chief ministers stopped your subject, so he did not dare go deep.

entries.zh: 若以棗陽、唐、鄧、陳、蔡諸軍攻荊山，取壽、泗，以亳、宿、徐、邳諸軍，合臣所統兵，攻揚、楚，則兩淮可定。
entries.en: If the Zaoyang, Tang, Deng, Chen, and Cai armies strike Jingshan and take Shou and Si, while the Bo, Su, Xu, and Pi armies join my command to attack Yang and Chu, both Huai regions can be secured.
entries.literal: If the armies of Zaoyang, Tang, Deng, Chen, and Cai attack Jingshan and take Shou and Si, and the armies of Bo, Su, Xu, and Pi combine with the troops your subject commands to attack Yang and Chu, then the two Huai can be settled.

entries.zh: 兩淮既定，則選兵以取江南，自守以寬民力，將無施不可，此上策也。」
entries.en: Once the two Huai are secure, chosen troops can take Jiangnan while we hold our ground and spare the people; then every military move will succeed. That is the best plan."
entries.literal: Once the two Huai are settled, then select troops to take Jiangnan, hold defensively to ease the people's strength, and generals will have nothing they cannot deploy—this is the superior strategy."

entries.zh: 因上將校馮泰等功第狀，詔以益都官銀分賞之。
entries.en: He also submitted a merit roll for officers such as Feng Tai, and the court ordered Yidu official silver distributed as rewards.
entries.literal: He thereupon submitted a register of merit ranks for officers such as Feng Tai, and an edict ordered that official silver of Yidu be distributed to reward them.

entries.zh: 又明年二月，李璮反，以漣、海三城獻于宋。
entries.en: In the second month of the following year Li Tan rebelled and surrendered the three Lian-Hai cities to the Song.
entries.literal: In the second month of the year after next, Li Tan rebelled and presented the three cities of Lian and Hai to Song.

entries.zh: 先是，其子彥簡，由京師逃歸，璮遣人白之中書。
entries.en: Earlier his son Yanjian had escaped from the capital; Tan sent word to the Secretariat.
entries.literal: Earlier, his son Yanjian had fled from the capital and returned; Tan sent a man to report this to the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 及反書聞，人多言文統嘗遣子蕘與璮通音耗。
entries.en: When news of the rebellion arrived, many said Wentong had sent his son Rao to exchange messages with Tan.
entries.literal: When news of the rebellion was heard, many said Wentong had once sent his son Rao to exchange messages with Tan.

entries.zh: 世祖召文統問之曰：「汝教璮為逆，積有歲年，舉世皆知之。
entries.en: Shizu summoned Wentong and said, "You taught Tan to rebel; everyone has known it for years.
entries.literal: Shizu summoned Wentong and questioned him, saying: "You taught Tan to rebel; this has accumulated for years and the whole world knows it.

entries.zh: 朕今問汝所策云何，其悉以對。」
entries.en: I ask what your plans were—tell me everything."
entries.literal: I now ask what your stratagems were—report them all fully."

entries.zh: 文統對曰：「臣亦忘之，容臣悉書以上。」
entries.en: Wentong replied, "I have forgotten; let me write it all out and submit it."
entries.literal: Wentong answered: "Your subject has also forgotten; allow your subject to write it all out and submit it above."

entries.zh: 書畢，世祖命讀之，其間有曰：「螻蟻之命，苟能存全，保為陛下取江南。」
entries.en: When he finished writing, Shizu had it read aloud; it included, "If this wretch's life is spared, I guarantee to take Jiangnan for Your Majesty."
entries.literal: When the writing was finished, Shizu ordered it read aloud; among its passages was: "This ant's life, if it can be preserved whole, I guarantee to take Jiangnan for Your Majesty."

entries.zh: 世祖曰：「汝今日猶欲緩頰於朕耶？」
entries.en: Shizu said, "Do you still think you can talk your way out?"
entries.literal: Shizu said: "Do you still today wish to plead for your cheeks before me?"

entries.zh: 會璮遣人持文統三書自洺水至，以書示之，文統始錯愕駭汗。
entries.en: Just then Tan's messenger arrived from Ming River with three letters from Wentong; when they were shown him, Wentong turned pale and broke into a sweat.
entries.literal: Just then Tan sent a man bearing three letters of Wentong from Ming River; when the letters were shown him, Wentong at last was startled and broke into terrified sweat.

entries.zh: 書中有「期甲子」語，世祖曰：「甲子之期云何？」
entries.en: The letters mentioned a "jiazi appointment"; Shizu asked, "What does the jiazi date mean?"
entries.literal: In the letters was the phrase "appointed on jiazi"; Shizu said: "What is the meaning of the jiazi appointment?"

entries.zh: 文統對曰：「李璮久蓄反心，以臣居中，不敢即發，臣欲告陛下縛璮久矣，第緣陛下加兵北方，猶未靖也。
entries.en: Wentong answered, "Li Tan long planned rebellion but dared not act while I was at court. I meant to tell Your Majesty to arrest him, but you were still campaigning in the north.
entries.literal: Wentong answered: "Li Tan long harbored rebellious intent; because your subject was at the center, he did not dare launch at once. Your subject wished to tell Your Majesty to bind Tan long ago, but only because Your Majesty was adding troops in the north and it was not yet settled.

entries.zh: 比至甲子，猶可數年，臣為是言，姑遲其反期耳。」
entries.en: The jiazi day was still years away; I said that only to delay his rebellion."
entries.literal: By the time jiazi came it would still be several years; your subject made this statement merely to postpone his time of rebellion for a while."

entries.zh: 世祖曰：「無多言。
entries.en: Shizu said, "Enough.
entries.literal: Shizu said: "Say no more.

entries.zh: 朕拔汝布衣，授之政柄，遇汝不薄，何負而為此？」
entries.en: I raised you from the ranks and gave you power; I treated you generously—what grievance made you do this?"
entries.literal: I raised you from common cloth and gave you the reins of government; I treated you not thinly—what did I fail in that you did this?"

entries.zh: 文統猶枝辭傍說，終不自言「臣罪當死」，乃命左右斥去，始出就縛。
entries.en: Wentong still hedged and would not say, "Your subject's crime deserves death"; attendants were ordered to remove him, and only then did he go out to be bound.
entries.literal: Wentong still branched into side arguments and in the end did not himself say "your subject's crime deserves death"; he was then ordered dismissed by attendants and only then went out to be bound.

entries.zh: 猶召竇默、姚樞、王鶚、僧子聰及張柔等至，示以前書曰：「汝等謂文統當得何罪？」
entries.en: He then summoned Dou Mo, Yao Shu, Wang E, the monk Zicong, Zhang Rou, and others, showed them the document, and asked, "What punishment does Wentong deserve?"
entries.literal: He still summoned Dou Mo, Yao Shu, Wang E, the monk Zicong, and Zhang Rou and others, showed them the earlier writing, and said: "What crime do you say Wentong deserves?"

entries.zh: 文臣皆言「人臣無將，將而必誅」。
entries.en: The civil officials said, "A subject who rebels must die."
entries.literal: The civil officials all said: "A minister must not harbor rebellion; if he does, he must be executed."

entries.zh: 柔獨疾聲大言曰：「宜剮！」
entries.en: Zhang Rou alone shouted, "He should be dismembered!"
entries.literal: Rou alone cried out in a loud voice: "He should be dismembered!"

entries.zh: 世祖又曰：「汝同辭言之。」
entries.en: Shizu said, "Say it together."
entries.literal: Shizu again said: "Speak in the same words."

entries.zh: 諸臣皆曰：「當死。」
entries.en: All said, "Death."
entries.literal: All the ministers said: "He should die."

entries.zh: 世祖曰：「渠亦自服朕前矣。」
entries.en: Shizu said, "He has already submitted before me."
entries.literal: Shizu said: "He has also himself submitted before me."

entries.zh: 癸卯，帝聞璮反，遂下詔暴其罪。
entries.en: On the guimao day the emperor learned of the rebellion and issued an edict listing Tan's crimes.
entries.literal: On guimao day the emperor heard Tan had rebelled and thereupon issued an edict exposing his crimes.

entries.zh: 甲辰，命諸軍討璮。
entries.en: On the jiachen day he ordered all armies to suppress Tan.
entries.literal: On jiachen day he ordered all armies to suppress Tan.

entries.zh: 己酉，以璮故，戮中書平章王文統。
entries.en: On the jiyou day, because of Tan's rebellion, Grand Councillor Wang Wentong of the Secretariat was executed.
entries.literal: On jiyou day, on account of Tan, the Secretariat Grand Councillor Wang Wentong was executed.

entries.zh: 壬子，璮盜據濟南。
entries.en: On the renzi day Tan seized Jinan.
entries.literal: On renzi day Tan seized and occupied Jinan by force.

entries.zh: 癸酉，命史樞、阿朮帥師赴濟南。
entries.en: On the guiyou day Shi Shu and Azhu were ordered to march on Jinan.
entries.literal: On guiyou day Shi Shu and Azhu were ordered to lead armies to Jinan.

entries.zh: 璮帥衆出掠輜重，將及城，官軍邀擊，大敗之，斬首四千級，璮退保濟南。
entries.en: Tan led his men out to raid supply trains near the city; government troops intercepted him, inflicted a crushing defeat with four thousand heads taken, and Tan fell back to defend Jinan.
entries.literal: Tan led his masses out to plunder baggage trains; when he was about to reach the city, government troops intercepted and attacked, inflicting a great defeat, beheading four thousand, and Tan withdrew to hold Jinan.

entries.zh: 五月庚申，築環城圍之；
entries.en: On the gengshen day of the fifth month they built a ring wall to besiege the city;
entries.literal: In the fifth month on gengshen day, a encircling wall was built to besiege it;

entries.zh: 甲戌，圍合。
entries.en: On the jiaxu day the encirclement closed.
entries.literal: On jiaxu day the encirclement closed.

entries.zh: 璮自是不得復出，猶日夜拒守，取城中子女賞將士，以悅其心；
entries.en: Tan could no longer break out but still held day and night, giving the city's sons and daughters to his officers as rewards to keep their loyalty;
entries.literal: From this Tan could not come out again; he still resisted day and night, took the sons and daughters within the city to reward officers and soldiers and please their hearts;

entries.zh: 且分軍就食民家，發其蓋藏以繼，不足，則家賦之鹽，令以人為食。
entries.en: He also sent troops to live off civilian households, seized hidden stores to keep supplies going, and when that failed levied salt per household and ordered cannibalism.
entries.literal: Moreover he divided troops to take food from civilian households, opened their stored goods to continue supply, and when insufficient, levied salt per household and ordered that people be used as food.

entries.zh: 至是，人情潰散，璮不能制，各什伯相結，縋城以出。
entries.en: By then morale collapsed beyond Tan's control; men banded in tens and hundreds and lowered themselves from the walls to escape.
entries.literal: By this time morale collapsed and Tan could not control it; men formed groups of tens and hundreds, lowered themselves from the wall by rope, and went out.

entries.zh: 璮知城且破，乃手刃愛妾，乘舟入大明湖，自投水中，水淺不得死，為官軍所獲，縛至諸王合必赤帳前。
entries.en: Knowing the city would fall, Tan killed his favorite concubine with his own hand, took a boat onto Daming Lake, and threw himself into the water; the lake was shallow and he survived, was captured, bound, and brought before Prince Habichi's tent.
entries.literal: Tan knew the city was about to fall; he then personally killed his beloved concubine, boarded a boat into Daming Lake, and threw himself into the water; the water was shallow and he did not die, was captured by government troops, bound, and brought before the tent of Prince Habichi.

entries.zh: 丞相史天澤言：「宜即誅之，以安人心。」
entries.en: Chancellor Shi Tianze said, "He should be executed at once to reassure the people."
entries.literal: Chancellor Shi Tianze said: "He should be executed at once to settle people's hearts."

entries.zh: 遂與蒙古軍官囊家并誅焉。
entries.en: He was then executed together with the Mongol officer Nangia.
entries.literal: He was then executed together with the Mongol officer Nangia.

entries.zh: 世祖在潛藩，訪問才智之士，素聞其名。
entries.en: While Shizu was still heir apparent he sought men of talent and had long heard of Wentong.
entries.literal: When Shizu was in his princely establishment, he sought out men of talent and wisdom and had long heard his name.

entries.zh: 及即位，厲精求治，有以文統為薦者，亟召用之。
entries.en: When he took the throne and threw himself into reform, someone recommended Wentong and he was summoned at once.
entries.literal: When he took the throne, he applied himself diligently to good government; when someone recommended Wentong, he quickly summoned and employed him.

entries.zh: 乃立中書省，以緫內外百司之政，首擢文統為平章政事，委以更張庶務。
entries.en: He established the Secretariat to govern all departments, made Wentong its first Grand Councillor, and charged him with overhauling administration.
entries.literal: He then established the Secretariat to oversee the government of all inner and outer offices; Wentong was first promoted to Grand Councillor and entrusted with reforming all routine affairs.

entries.zh: 建元為中統，詔諭天下，立十路宣撫司，示以條格，欲差發辦而民不擾，鹽課不失常額，交鈔無致阻滯。
entries.en: The era was named Zhongtong; edicts went out to establish Pacification Commissions in ten circuits with regulations so corvée could be met without harassing the people, salt revenues kept steady, and paper currency kept flowing.
entries.literal: The era name was established as Zhongtong; an edict announced this to all under Heaven, ten-circuit Pacification Commissions were established, regulations were displayed, with the aim that corvée assignments be carried out yet the people not be disturbed, salt levies not fall below the regular quota, and paper notes not meet obstruction.

entries.zh: 尋詔行中書省造中統元寶交鈔，立互市于潁州、漣水、光化軍。
entries.en: Soon the Branch Secretariat was ordered to issue Zhongtong treasure notes and open trade markets at Yingzhou, Lianshui, and Guanghua Army.
