entries.literal: Shortly afterward an edict ordered the Branch Secretariat to mint Zhongtong yuanbao paper notes and establish mutual markets at Yingzhou, Lianshui, and Guanghua Army.

entries.zh: 是年冬，初行中統交鈔，自十文至二貫文，凡十等，不限年月，諸路通行，稅賦並聽收受。
entries.en: That winter Zhongtong notes were first issued in ten denominations from ten cash to two strings, valid everywhere without expiry, and accepted for taxes.
entries.literal: That winter the Zhongtong notes were first put in circulation, from ten cash to two strings, ten denominations in all, with no limit on year or month, circulating in all circuits, and taxes and levies were all permitted to be received in them.

entries.zh: 明年二月，世祖在開平，召行中書省事禡禡與文統，親率各路宣撫使俱赴闕。
entries.en: The following second month, while Shizu was at Kaiping, he summoned Branch Secretariat chief Mamma and Wentong and had all circuit Pacification Commissioners come to court with him.
entries.literal: In the second month of the following year Shizu was at Kaiping; he summoned the Branch Secretariat chief Mamma and Wentong, and personally led the Pacification Commissioners of all circuits together to the court.

entries.zh: 世祖自去秋親征叛王阿里不哥于北方，凡民間差發、宣課鹽鐵等事，一委文統等裁處。
entries.en: Since the previous autumn Shizu had been campaigning north against the rebel prince Ariq Böke; all corvée, salt, iron, and related levies were left entirely to Wentong and his colleagues.
entries.literal: Since the previous autumn Shizu had personally campaigned against the rebel prince Ariq Böke in the north; all matters of civilian corvée, salt and iron levies, and the like were entirely entrusted to Wentong and others to decide.

entries.zh: 及振旅還宮，未知其可否何若，且以往者，急於用兵，事多不暇講究，所當振其紀綱者，宜在今日。
entries.en: When the army returned he did not yet know how well these measures had worked; wartime urgency had left much undone, and the time to restore discipline was now.
entries.literal: When the army returned in triumph to the palace, it was not known how effective these had been; moreover in the past, urgent with military use, many matters had no leisure for thorough study—what should restore discipline ought to be done today.

entries.zh: 故召文統等至，責以成效，用游顯、鄭鼎、趙良弼、董文炳等為各路宣撫司，復以所議條格詔諭各路，俾遵行之。
entries.en: He therefore summoned Wentong and demanded results, appointed You Xian, Zheng Ding, Zhao Liangbi, Dong Wenbing, and others as circuit Pacification Commissioners, and reissued the regulations for all circuits to follow.
entries.literal: Therefore Wentong and others were summoned and charged with results; You Xian, Zheng Ding, Zhao Liangbi, Dong Wenbing, and others were appointed to Pacification Commissions of the circuits, and again the regulations they had deliberated were proclaimed to all circuits to be obeyed.

entries.zh: 未幾，又詔諭宣撫司，并達魯花赤管民官、課稅所官，申嚴私鹽、酒醋、麯貨等禁。
entries.en: Soon another edict told Pacification Commissions, darughachi, civilian officials, and tax officers to enforce bans on private salt, liquor, vinegar, and yeast products.
entries.literal: Before long, another edict instructed the Pacification Commissions, together with darughachi, civilian officials, and tax-office officials, to strictly enforce prohibitions on private salt, wine, vinegar, yeast goods, and the like.

entries.zh: 文統為人忌刻，初立中書時，張文謙為左丞。
entries.en: Wentong was jealous by nature; when the Secretariat was first set up Zhang Wenqian was Left Chancellor.
entries.literal: Wentong was jealous and harsh by nature; when the Secretariat was first established, Zhang Wenqian was Left Chancellor.

entries.zh: 文謙素以安國利民自負，故凡講論建明，輒相可否，文統積不能平，思有以陷之，文謙竟以本職行大名等路宣撫司事而去。
entries.en: Wenqian prided himself on serving state and people and constantly disputed Wentong's proposals; Wentong brooded until he found a way to remove him, and Wenqian was sent off to handle Pacification affairs in Daming and other circuits.
entries.literal: Wenqian had always prided himself on securing the state and benefiting the people; therefore whenever policies were discussed and proposed, they constantly opposed each other. Wentong's resentment could not be settled and he sought means to trap him; Wenqian in the end left to carry out Pacification Commission affairs for Daming and other circuits in his original post.

entries.zh: 時姚樞、竇默、許衡，皆世祖所敬信者，文統諷世祖授樞為太子太師，默為太子太傅，衡為太子太保，外佯尊之，實不欲使朝夕備顧問於左右也。
entries.en: Yao Shu, Dou Mo, and Xu Heng were men Shizu trusted; Wentong had him appoint them Grand Tutor, Grand Mentor, and Grand Guardian of the Heir—honors in name meant to keep them from daily counsel at court.
entries.literal: At that time Yao Shu, Dou Mo, and Xu Heng were all men Shizu respected and trusted; Wentong urged Shizu to appoint Shu as Grand Tutor of the Heir, Mo as Grand Mentor of the Heir, and Heng as Grand Guardian of the Heir—outwardly feigning honor while in fact not wishing them to attend day and night as advisers at his side.

entries.zh: 默嘗與王鶚及樞、衡俱侍世祖，面詆文統曰：「此人學術不正，必禍天下，不可處以相位。」
entries.en: Mo once attended Shizu with Wang E, Yao Shu, and Xu Heng and denounced Wentong to his face: "This man's learning is unsound; he will ruin the realm and must not hold the chancellorship."
entries.literal: Mo once attended Shizu together with Wang E and Shu and Heng, and to his face denounced Wentong, saying: "This man's learning is not correct; he will surely bring calamity on all under Heaven and must not be placed in the chancellorship."

entries.zh: 世祖曰：「若是，則誰可為者？」
entries.en: Shizu asked, "If so, who can?"
entries.literal: Shizu said: "If so, then who can do it?"

entries.zh: 默以許衡對，世祖不懌而罷。
entries.en: Mo named Xu Heng; Shizu was displeased and ended the audience.
entries.literal: Mo answered with Xu Heng; Shizu was displeased and dismissed the session.

entries.zh: 鶚嘗請以右丞相史天澤監修國史，左丞相耶律鑄監修遼史，文統監修金史。
entries.en: Wang E once proposed that Right Chancellor Shi Tianze supervise the dynastic history, Left Chancellor Yelü Zhu the Liao history, and Wentong the Jin history.
entries.literal: E once requested that Right Chancellor Shi Tianze supervise compilation of the national history, Left Chancellor Yelü Zhu supervise compilation of the Liao history, and Wentong supervise compilation of the Jin history.

entries.zh: 世祖曰：「監修階銜，俟修史時定之。」
entries.en: Shizu replied, "Supervisory titles will be fixed when the histories are actually compiled."
entries.literal: Shizu said: "The supervisory rank and title will be fixed when the histories are compiled."

entries.zh: 阿魯輝帖木兒，滅里大王之裔也。
entries.en: Arugh Temür was a descendant of Great Prince Mieli.
entries.literal: Arugh Temür was a descendant of Great Prince Mieli.

entries.zh: 初，太宗生七子，而滅里位第七。
entries.en: At the outset, Taizong had seven sons, and Mieli ranked seventh.
entries.literal: At the outset, Taizong had seven sons, and Mieli ranked seventh.

entries.zh: 世祖既定天下，乃大封宗親為王，滅里其一也。
entries.en: After Shizu had settled the realm, he enfeoffed many kinsmen as princes, and Mieli was one of them.
entries.literal: After Shizu had settled the realm, he greatly enfeoffed kinsmen as princes, and Mieli was one of them.

entries.zh: 滅里生脫忽，脫忽生俺都剌，俺都剌生禿滿，至大元年，始封陽翟王，賜金印螭紐，俾鎮北藩。
entries.en: Mieli begot Toqhu; Toqhu begot Andula; Andula begot Tuman. In the first year of Zhida, Tuman was first enfeoffed as Prince of Yangdi, granted a gold seal with dragon knob, and charged to guard the northern frontier.
entries.literal: Mieli begot Toqhu; Toqhu begot Andula; Andula begot Tuman. In the first year of Zhida, Tuman was first enfeoffed as Prince of Yangdi, granted a gold seal with dragon knob, and charged to guard the northern frontier.

entries.zh: 禿滿傳曲春，曲春傳太平，太平傳帖木兒赤，而阿魯輝帖木兒襲其封。
entries.en: Tuman passed the title to Quchun; Quchun to Taiping; Taiping to Temürchi; and Arugh Temür inherited the enfeoffment.
entries.literal: Tuman passed the title to Quchun; Quchun to Taiping; Taiping to Temürchi; and Arugh Temür inherited the enfeoffment.

entries.zh: 李璮小字松壽，濰州人，李全子也。
entries.en: Li Tan, whose childhood name was Songsou, was from Weizhou and was the son of Li Quan.
entries.literal: Li Tan, whose childhood name was Songsou, was a man of Weizhou and the son of Li Quan.

entries.zh: 或曰璮本衢州徐氏子，父嘗為揚州司理參軍，全蓋養之為子云。
entries.en: Some accounts hold that he was originally a Xu from Quzhou, whose father had served as judicial administrator in Yangzhou and whom Li Quan adopted as his son.
entries.literal: Some say Tan was originally a son of the Xu clan of Quzhou; his father had once served as judicial administrator of Yangzhou, and Quan had adopted him as a son, it is said.

entries.zh: 太祖十六年，全叛宋，舉山東州郡歸附，太師、國王孛魯承制拜全山東淮南楚州行省，而以其兄福為副元帥。
entries.en: In Taizu's sixteenth year, Li Quan defected from the Song and submitted the Shandong prefectures. The Grand Tutor and King Pelu, exercising imperial authority, appointed him regional commissioner for Shandong, Huainan, and Chuzhou, with his elder brother Fu as deputy marshal.
entries.literal: In the sixteenth year of Taizu, Quan rebelled against Song, bringing the prefectures and districts of Shandong over in submission; the Grand Tutor and King Pelu, acting by imperial commission, appointed Quan Pacification Commissioner for Shandong, Huainan, and Chuzhou, and made his elder brother Fu vice marshal.

entries.zh: 太宗三年，全攻宋揚州，敗死。
entries.en: In Taizong's third year, Quan attacked the Song at Yangzhou, was defeated, and died.
entries.literal: In the third year of Taizong, Quan attacked Yangzhou of Song and was defeated and died.

entries.zh: 璮遂襲為益都行省，仍得專制其地。
entries.en: Tan then inherited the Yidu commission and continued to rule the territory as he saw fit.
entries.literal: Tan thereupon succeeded as Pacification Commissioner of Yidu and still obtained sole control over that territory.

entries.zh: 朝廷數徵兵，輒詭辭不至。
entries.en: Whenever the court called for troops, he found excuses and did not report.
entries.literal: When the court repeatedly summoned troops, he always made deceptive excuses and did not come.

entries.zh: 憲宗七年，又調其兵赴行在，璮親詣帝言曰：「益都乃宋航海要津，分軍非便。」
entries.en: In Xianzong's seventh year the court again ordered his forces to the capital. Tan went in person and said, "Yidu is a critical Song maritime choke point; splitting the army would be unwise."
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Xianzong, troops were again mobilized to the imperial headquarters; Tan personally went before the emperor and said: "Yidu is a vital route for Song navigation by sea; to divide the army would not be convenient."

entries.zh: 帝然之，命璮歸取漣海數州。
entries.en: The emperor agreed and ordered him to go back and take several prefectures in the Lianhai region.
entries.literal: The emperor approved, and ordered Tan to return and take several prefectures in Lianhai.

entries.zh: 璮遂發兵攻拔漣水相連四城，大張剋捷之功。
entries.en: He marched out, seized four linked cities including Lianshui, and loudly advertised his triumphs.
entries.literal: Tan then dispatched troops, captured and took four contiguous cities including Lianshui, and greatly trumpeted the merit of his victories.

entries.zh: 秋八月癸亥，英宗自上都南還，駐蹕南坡。
entries.en: In the eighth month of autumn, on the guihai day, Emperor Yingzong returned south from Shangdu and halted at Nanpo.
entries.literal: In the eighth month of autumn, on the guihai day, Emperor Yingzong returned south from Shangdu and halted at Nanpo.

entries.zh: 是夕，鐵失與知樞密院事也先鐵木兒、大司農失禿兒、前中書平章政事赤斤鐵木兒、前雲南行省平章政事完者、前治書侍御史鎖南、鐵失之弟宣徽使鎖南、典瑞院使脫火赤、樞密副使阿散、僉書樞密院事章台、衞士禿滿，及諸王按梯不花、孛羅、月魯鐵木兒、曲律不花、兀魯思不花等，以鐵失所領阿速衞兵為外應，殺右丞相拜住，而鐵失直犯禁幄，手弒英宗于臥所。
entries.en: That night Tie Shi, together with privy council administrator Yesen Timur, Minister of Revenue Shitu'er, former central pingzhang Chijin Timur, former Yunnan pingzhang Wanzhe, former associate censor Suonan, Tie Shi's younger brother Huizheng commissioner Suonan, Ceremonial Regalia Court commissioner Tuohuochi, privy council vice director Asan, privy council secretary Zhangtai, guard Tumian, and the princes Atibuhua, Boluo, Yuelu Timur, Qulvuhua, and Ulusibuhua, used Tie Shi's Asud guards as accomplices, killed right chancellor Bayiju, then burst into the forbidden tent and personally assassinated Emperor Yingzong in his sleeping quarters.
entries.literal: That evening Tie Shi, together with Privy Council administrator Yesen Timur, Minister of Revenue Shitu'er, former Pingzhang of the Central Secretariat Chijin Timur, former Pingzhang of the Yunnan Branch Secretariat Wanzhe, former Associate Censor Suonan, Tie Shi's younger brother Huizheng Court commissioner Suonan, Ceremonial Regalia Court commissioner Tuohuochi, Vice Director of the Privy Council Asan, Privy Council Secretary Zhangtai, guard Tumian, and the princes Atibuhua, Boluo, Yuelu Timur, Qulvuhua, Ulusibuhua, and others, using the Asud guard troops Tie Shi commanded as external support, killed Right Chancellor Bayiju; Tie Shi then directly breached the forbidden tent and personally assassinated Emperor Yingzong in his sleeping quarters.

entries.zh: 九月四日，晉王即位，鐵失及其黨皆伏誅。
entries.en: On the fourth day of the ninth month the Prince of Jin took the throne; Tie Shi and his confederates were all executed.
entries.literal: On the fourth day of the ninth month the Prince of Jin ascended the throne; Tie Shi and his faction were all executed.

entries.zh: 孛羅帖木兒，荅失八都魯之子也。
entries.en: Boluo Timur was the son of Dashi-Baturu.
entries.literal: Boluo Timur was the son of Dashi-Baturu.

entries.zh: 從父討賊，屢立戰功，其語見父傳。
entries.en: He followed his father against rebels and won repeated victories; those campaigns are recorded in his father's biography.
entries.literal: He followed his father in suppressing bandits and repeatedly achieved military merit; the account appears in his father's biography.

entries.zh: 父既歿，孛羅帖木兒引兵退駐井陘口。
entries.en: After his father's death Boluo Timur withdrew his army and encamped at Jingxing Pass.
entries.literal: After his father died, Boluo Timur led his troops back and encamped at Jingxing Pass.

entries.zh: 至正十八年正月，命孛羅帖木兒為河南行省平章政事，仍緫領其父元管諸軍。
entries.en: In the first month of Zhizheng 18 he was made pingzhang of the Henan branch secretariat while continuing to command all the forces his father had once held.
entries.literal: In the first month of the eighteenth year of Zhizheng, Boluo Timur was appointed Pingzhang of the Henan Branch Secretariat and still commanded overall the various armies his father had originally administered.

entries.zh: 三月，擊劉福通於衛輝，走之，進克濮州。
entries.en: In the third month he attacked Liu Futong at Weihui, routed him, and went on to take Puzhou.
entries.literal: In the third month he attacked Liu Futong at Weihui, drove him off, and advanced to capture Puzhou.

entries.zh: 四月，屯兵真定。
entries.en: In the fourth month he encamped at Zhending.
entries.literal: In the fourth month he encamped his troops at Zhending.

entries.zh: 六月，自武安由彭城邀截沙劉等，敗之。
entries.en: In the sixth month he marched from Wu'an through Pengcheng, intercepted Sha Liu and his followers, and defeated them.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, setting out from Wu'an and passing through Pengcheng, he intercepted Sha Liu and others and defeated them.

entries.zh: 九月，命統領諸軍夾攻曹州。
entries.en: In the ninth month he was ordered to lead a converging assault on Caozhou.
entries.literal: In the ninth month he was ordered to command all armies in a converging attack on Caozhou.

entries.zh: 十月，遣參政匡福統苗軍自西門入，孛羅帖木兒自北門入，四門並進，克復曹州，擒殺偽官武宰相、仇知院，獲偽印信金牌等物。
entries.en: In the tenth month he sent Vice Administrator Kuang Fu with Miao troops through the west gate while he himself entered from the north. All four gates attacked together, Caozhou was retaken, the rebel officials Wu the chancellor and Qiu the director were captured and killed, and false seals, gold tallies, and other booty were seized.
entries.literal: In the tenth month he sent Vice Administrator Kuang Fu to lead the Miao army in through the west gate while Boluo Timur entered through the north gate; all four gates advanced together, recovered Caozhou, captured and killed the rebel officials the false Chancellor Wu and the false Director Qiu, and obtained false seals, gold tallies, and other objects.

entries.zh: 鐵失者，當英宗即位之初，以翰林學士承旨、宣徽院使，為太醫院使。
entries.en: At the start of Emperor Yingzong's reign Tie Shi was Hanlin grand secretary and Huizheng Court commissioner, and was appointed superintendent of the Imperial Medical Academy.
entries.literal: Tie Shi, at the beginning of Emperor Yingzong's accession, was Hanlin Academician Grand Secretary and Huizheng Court commissioner, and was made superintendent of the Imperial Medical Academy.

entries.zh: 未逾月，特命領中都威衞指揮使。
entries.en: Within a month he was specially ordered to take command of the Capital Might Guard.
entries.literal: Within less than a month he was specially ordered to command the Capital Might Guard.

entries.zh: 明年，改元至治，有珍珠燕服之賜。
entries.en: The next year the era name was changed to Zhizhi, and he was granted a pearl swallow robe.
entries.literal: The next year the era name was changed to Zhizhi, and he received the gift of a pearl swallow robe.

entries.zh: 三月，特授光祿大夫、御史大夫，仍金虎符、忠翊侍衞親軍都指揮使，依前太醫院使。
entries.en: In the third month he was specially made grand master of splendid happiness and grand censor, keeping his gold tiger tally, command of the Loyal and Supporting palace guard personal army, and post as imperial medical superintendent.
entries.literal: In the third month he was specially granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Grand Censor, retaining the gold tiger tally and the posts of commander of the Loyal and Supporting Palace Guard Personal Army, and continuing as before as superintendent of the Imperial Medical Academy.

entries.zh: 英宗嘗御鹿頂殿，謂鐵失曰：「徽政雖隸太皇太后，朕視之與諸司同，凡簿書宜悉令御史檢覈。」
entries.en: Emperor Yingzong once held court at Deer Peak Hall and told Tie Shi, "Though Huizheng falls under the empress dowager, I treat it like any other office. All its accounts should be fully audited by the censors."
entries.literal: Emperor Yingzong once held court at Deer Peak Hall and said to Tie Shi: "Though Huizheng is subordinate to the Empress Dowager, I regard it the same as the other offices; all accounts ought to be ordered examined in full by the censors."

entries.zh: 既而又命領左右阿速衞。
entries.en: Soon afterward he was again ordered to command the left and right Asud guards.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he was again ordered to command the Left and Right Asud Guards.

entries.zh: 冬十月，英宗親祀太廟，以中書左丞相拜住為亞獻官，鐵失為終獻官。
entries.en: In the tenth month of winter Emperor Yingzong sacrificed in person at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, with central left chancellor Bayiju as secondary offering officer and Tie Shi as final offering officer.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of winter Emperor Yingzong personally sacrificed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, appointing Left Chancellor of the Central Secretariat Bayiju as secondary offering officer and Tie Shi as final offering officer.

entries.zh: 明年冬十月，江南行臺御史大夫脫脫以疾請于朝，未得旨輒去職，鐵失奏罷之，杖六十七，謫居雲南。
entries.en: In the tenth month of winter the following year, Tuo Tuo, the Jiangnan regional censor-in-chief, asked the court for sick leave. He quit his post before any reply arrived. Tie Shi had him dismissed, beaten sixty-seven strokes, and sent into exile in Yunnan.
entries.literal: The next year, in the tenth month of winter, Tuo Tuo, Grand Censor of the Jiangnan Regional Secretariat, requested leave from court on grounds of illness; without obtaining an edict he abruptly left his post. Tie Shi memorialized to dismiss him; he was beaten sixty-seven strokes and banished to reside in Yunnan.

entries.zh: 治書侍御史鎖南，鐵木迭兒之子也，罷為翰林侍講學士，鐵失奏復其職，英宗不允。
entries.en: Suonan, an associate censor of the Secretariat, was Temuder's son. After his dismissal to a Hanlin lecturing post, Tie Shi asked that he be reinstated, but Emperor Yingzong refused.
entries.literal: Suonan, Associate Censor of the Secretariat, was Temuder's son; he had been dismissed and made Hanlin Academician Explaining the Classics. Tie Shi memorialized to restore his office; Emperor Yingzong did not consent.

entries.zh: 十二月，鐵失以御史大夫、忠翊親軍都指揮使、左右衛阿速親軍都指揮使、太醫院使，兼領廣惠司事。
entries.en: In the twelfth month Tie Shi was appointed grand censor, commander of the Loyal and Supporting personal army and of the Asud guards of the left and right, superintendent of the Imperial Medical Academy, and concurrent head of the Broad Beneficence Office.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, Tie Shi held the posts of Grand Censor, Commander-in-Chief of the Loyal and Supporting Personal Army, Commander-in-Chief of the Left and Right Guards' Asud Personal Army, and Superintendent of the Imperial Medical Academy, and concurrently directed the affairs of the Broad Beneficence Office.

entries.zh: 三月，太祖遣大將軍、魏安公尉遲迥率衆伐梁武陵王蕭紀於蜀。
entries.en: In the third month Yuwen Tai sent Yuchi Jiong, duke of Wei'an, against Xiao Ji, Liang prince of Wuling, in Shu.
entries.literal: In the third month the Grand Duke sent Grand General Duke of Wei'an Yuchi Jiong with troops to campaign against Liang's Prince of Wuling Xiao Ji in Shu.

entries.zh: 五月，蕭紀潼州刺史楊乾運以州降，引迥軍向成都。
entries.en: In the fifth month Yang Qianyun, Xiao Ji's governor of Tong Province, surrendered and guided Yuchi Jiong toward Chengdu.
entries.literal: In the fifth month Xiao Ji's Tong Province governor Yang Qianyun surrendered the province and led Jiong's army toward Chengdu.

entries.zh: 文帝下
entries.en: The Annals of Emperor Wen, Part Two
entries.literal: Emperor Wen, Part Two

entries.zh: 元年春正月辛丑，即天王位。
entries.en: In the first year, on xinchou in the first month of spring, he took the throne as Heavenly King.
entries.literal: In the first year, spring, first month, on the day xinchou, he took the position of Heavenly King.

entries.zh: 柴燎告天，朝百官於路門。
entries.en: He offered the firewood sacrifice to announce to Heaven and received the hundred officials at the Lumen Gate.
entries.literal: He offered the firewood sacrifice to announce to Heaven and received the hundred officials at the Lumen Gate.

entries.zh: 追尊皇考文公為文王，皇妣為文后。
entries.en: He posthumously honored his late father Duke Wen as King Wen and his late mother as Empress Wen.
entries.literal: He posthumously honored his late father Duke Wen as King Wen and his late mother as Empress Wen.

entries.zh: 大赦天下。
entries.en: A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
entries.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.

entries.zh: 封魏帝為宋公。
entries.en: The Wei emperor was enfeoffed as Duke of Song.
entries.literal: The Wei emperor was enfeoffed as Duke of Song.

entries.zh: 是日，槐里獻赤雀四。
entries.en: That same day Huaili presented four red sparrows.
entries.literal: That same day Huaili presented four red sparrows.

entries.zh: 百官奏議云：「帝王之興，罔弗更正朔，明受之於天，革民視聽也。
entries.en: The hundred officials memorialized, saying: “When emperors and kings rise, none fail to correct the calendar—it makes clear that they receive the mandate from Heaven and renew what the people see and hear.
entries.literal: The hundred officials memorialized, saying: “When emperors and kings rise, none fail to correct the calendar—it makes clear that they receive the mandate from Heaven and renew what the people see and hear.

entries.zh: 逮於尼父，稽諸陰陽，云行夏之時，後王所不易。
entries.en: Down to the Master, when he examined yin and yang, he said to follow the seasons of Xia—a rule later kings did not alter.
entries.literal: Down to the Master, when he examined yin and yang, he said to follow the seasons of Xia—a rule later kings did not alter.

entries.zh: 今魏曆告終，周室受命，以木承水，實當行錄，正用夏時，式遵聖道。
entries.en: Now the calendar of Wei has reached its end and the house of Zhou has received the mandate; wood succeeding water, green is truly the color to be employed; the Xia calendar should be used, following the sage way.
entries.literal: Now the calendar of Wei has reached its end and the house of Zhou has received the mandate; wood succeeding water, green is truly the color to be employed; the Xia calendar should be used, following the sage way.

entries.zh: 惟文王誕玄氣之祥，有黑水之讖，服色宜烏。」
entries.en: King Wen bore the auspice of dark vapor and the prophecy of black water; ceremonial attire should honor black.”
entries.literal: King Wen bore the auspice of dark vapor and the prophecy of black water; ceremonial attire should honor black.”

entries.zh: 制曰可。
entries.en: The decree answered: Approved.
entries.literal: The decree answered: Approved.

entries.zh: 以大司徒、趙郡公李弼為太師，大宗伯、南陽公趙貴為太傅、大冢宰，大司馬、河內公獨孤信為太保、大宗伯，柱國、中山公護為大司馬。
entries.en: Li Bi, Duke of Zhao and Grand Minister of the Masses, became Grand Preceptor; Zhao Gui, Duke of Nanyang and Grand Director of Ritual, Grand Tutor and Grand Chancellor; Dugu Xin, Duke of Henei and Grand Marshal, Grand Protector and Grand Director of Ritual; and Hu of Zhongshan, Pillar of State and Grand Marshal.
entries.literal: Grand Minister of the Masses Li Bi, Duke of Zhao commandery, was made Grand Preceptor; Grand Director of Ritual Zhao Gui, Duke of Nanyang, Grand Tutor and Grand Chancellor; Grand Marshal Dugu Xin, Duke of Henei, Grand Protector and Grand Director of Ritual; and Pillar of State Hu of Zhongshan, Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 以大將軍寧都公毓、高陽公達奚武、武陽公豆盧寧、小司寇陽平公李遠、小司馬博陵公賀蘭祥、小宗伯魏安公尉遲迥等並柱國。
entries.en: Grand General Yuwen Yu of Ningdu; Daxi Wu of Gaoyang; Doulu Ning of Wuyang; Li Yuan of Yangping, Junior Minister of Justice; Helan Xiang of Boling, Junior Army Marshal; Yuchi Jiong of Wei'an, Junior Director of Ritual; and others were all made Grand Dukes General of the Army.
entries.literal: Grand General the Duke of Ningdu, Yuwen Yu; Daxi Wu of Gaoyang; Doulu Ning of Wuyang; Junior Minister of Justice Li Yuan of Yangping; Junior Army Marshal Helan Xiang of Boling; Junior Director of Ritual Yuchi Jiong of Wei'an; and others were all made Grand Dukes General of the Army.

entries.zh: 及武帝誅護後，乃詔曰：「慎始敬終，有國彝典；
entries.en: After Emperor Wu killed Hu, he issued an edict: “Care at the beginning and reverence at the end are the enduring laws of statecraft;
entries.literal: After Emperor Wu executed Hu, an edict said: “To be careful at the beginning and respectful at the end is the constant canon of a state;

entries.zh: 事亡如存，哲王通制。
entries.en: to honor the dead as though they still lived is the way of the sage kings.
entries.literal: to treat the departed as if they still lived is the universal rule of sage kings.

entries.zh: 義崇追遠，禮貴尊親。
entries.en: Duty bids us honor those who went before; ritual demands that we revere our kin.
entries.literal: Righteousness exalts honoring the distant past; ritual values revering one’s kin.

entries.zh: 故略陽公至德純粹，天姿秀傑。
entries.en: Duke of Lueyang possessed supreme virtue, pure and unalloyed, and a heaven-given brilliance.
entries.literal: Therefore Duke of Lueyang’s supreme virtue was pure and unmixed, his heavenly endowment outstanding and eminent.

entries.zh: 屬魏祚告終，寶命將改，謳歌允集，歷數攸歸，上協蒼靈之慶，下昭后祇之錫。
entries.en: When the house of Wei ended and the mandate was about to pass, the people’s acclaim gathered and the throne was rightfully his—blessed by Heaven above and sanctioned by Earth below.
entries.literal: When Wei’s fortune reached its end and the precious mandate was about to change, songs of praise gathered truly, and the calendar of rule was his; above he accorded with the blessing of the azure spirit, below he manifested the gift of the earthly lord.

entries.zh: 而禍生肘腋，釁起蕭牆，白獸噬驂，蒼鷹集殿，幽辱神器，弒酷乘輿，冤結生民，毒流㝢縣。
entries.en: Yet disaster struck at his very side and treason rose within the palace—a white beast savaged the team, a dark hawk alighted on the hall; the sacred regalia was defiled, the sovereign brutally slain, the people left in bitter wrong, and poison spread across the realm.
entries.literal: Yet calamity arose at the elbow and trouble sprang within the palace walls; a white beast devoured the paired horses, a dark hawk gathered on the hall; the sacred vessel was shamed, the imperial carriage cruelly murdered, grievance bound the living people, and poison spread through the realm.

entries.zh: 今河海澄清，氛沴消蕩，追尊之禮，宜崇徽號。」
entries.en: Now that the realm is pacified and evil dispelled, his posthumous honors should be raised to a lofty title.”
entries.literal: Now the rivers and seas are clear, malignant vapors dispersed; the rites of posthumous honor should be raised with a lofty title.”

entries.zh: 遣太師、蜀國公
entries.en: He dispatched Grand Preceptor the Duke of Shu
entries.literal: He sent Grand Preceptor the Duke of Shu

entries.en: (Guo [Jiong])
entries.literal: (Guo)

entries.zh: 迥於南郊上諡曰孝閔皇帝，陵曰靜陵。
entries.en: Jiong to offer at the southern suburb the posthumous title Emperor Xiaomin; his mausoleum is named Jingling.
entries.literal: Jiong to present at the southern suburb the posthumous title Emperor Xiaomin; his tomb is called Jingling.

entries.zh: 孝閔皇帝諱覺，字陁羅尼，太祖第三子也。
entries.en: The Xiaomin Emperor, taboo name Jue and styled Tuoluoni, was the third son of the Grand Duke.
entries.literal: Emperor Xiaomin’s taboo name was Jue, his style Tuoluoni, and he was the Grand Duke’s third son.

entries.zh: 母曰元皇后。
entries.en: His mother was the Empress Yuan.
entries.literal: His mother was Empress Yuan.

entries.zh: 大統八年，生於同州官舍。
entries.en: In the eighth year of Datong he was born in the government quarters at Tong Province.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Datong, he was born in the official residence at Tong Province.

entries.zh: 九歲，封略陽郡公。
entries.en: At the age of nine he was made Duke of Lueyang commandery.
entries.literal: At nine sui he was enfeoffed as Duke of Lueyang commandery.

entries.zh: 時有善相者史元華見帝，退謂所親曰：「此公子有至貴之相，但恨其壽不足以稱之耳。」
entries.en: A skilled physiognomist named Shi Yuanhua once looked upon the future emperor and told his intimates afterward: “This boy bears the marks of the highest eminence—yet his lifespan will fall short of what his face promises.”
entries.literal: At the time there was a skilled physiognomist, Shi Yuanhua, who saw the emperor and, on withdrawing, said to those close to him: “This young lord has the countenance of supreme nobility, but I regret that his allotted years are not enough to match it.”

entries.zh: 魏恭帝三年三月，命為安定公世子。
entries.en: In the third month of the third year of Emperor Gong of Wei he was named heir to the Duke of Anding.
entries.literal: In the third month of the third year of Emperor Gong of Wei, he was appointed heir to the Duke of Anding.

entries.zh: 四月，拜大將軍。
entries.en: In the fourth month he received appointment as General-in-Chief.
entries.literal: In the fourth month he was appointed General-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 十月乙亥，太祖崩，丙子，嗣位太師、大冢宰。
entries.en: On yihai in the tenth month the Grand Duke died; on the following day, bingzi, Jue succeeded him as Grand Preceptor and Grand Chancellor.
entries.literal: On the day yihai of the tenth month the Grand Duke died; on the day bingzi [Jue] succeeded to the posts of Grand Preceptor and Grand Chancellor.

entries.zh: 十二月丁亥，魏帝詔以岐陽之地封帝為周公。
entries.en: On dinghai in the twelfth month the Wei emperor decreed that Jue should be enfeoffed as Duke of Zhou with the lands of Qiyang.
entries.literal: On the day dinghai of the twelfth month the Wei emperor issued an edict enfeoffing the emperor as Duke of Zhou with the territory of Qiyang.

entries.zh: 庚子，禪位於帝。
entries.en: On gengzi the Wei emperor abdicated in his favor.
entries.literal: On the day gengzi [the Wei emperor] abdicated the throne to the emperor.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「予聞皇天之命不于常，惟歸於德。
entries.en: The edict read: “We have heard that Heaven’s command is not constant—it rests only with the virtuous.
entries.literal: The edict said: “We have heard that Heaven’s mandate is not fixed, but goes to the virtuous.

entries.zh: 故堯授舜，舜授禹，時其宜也。
entries.en: Yao yielded to Shun, and Shun to Yu, each in season with Heaven’s intent.
entries.literal: Thus Yao gave the throne to Shun, and Shun to Yu, because the time was fitting.

entries.zh: 天厭我魏邦，垂變以告，惟爾罔弗知。
entries.en: Heaven has grown weary of the house of Wei and shows its displeasure in portents—yet you alone seem not to see.
entries.literal: Heaven is weary of our Wei state and sends down change to announce it—yet you alone do not know.

entries.zh: 予雖不明，敢弗龔天命，格有德哉。
entries.en: Though We lack wisdom, how dare We refuse Heaven’s command or fail to yield to worth?
entries.literal: Though We are not enlightened, how dare We fail to respect Heaven’s mandate and seek out the virtuous?

entries.zh: 今踵唐虞舊典，禪位於周，庸佈告遐邇焉。」
entries.en: We therefore follow the ancient precedent of Tang and Yu and yield the throne to Zhou—let this be proclaimed throughout the realm.”
entries.literal: Now We follow the old model of Tang and Yu and abdicate the throne to Zhou—let this be proclaimed far and near.”

entries.zh: 使大宗伯趙貴持節奉冊書曰：「咨爾周公，帝王之位弗有常，有德者受命，時乃天道。
entries.en: The Grand Director of Ritual Zhao Gui was sent with the staff of authority and the book of investiture, which declared: “O Duke of Zhou, the throne is not forever fixed; the virtuous receive the mandate—such is Heaven’s way.
entries.literal: He sent the Grand Director of Ritual Zhao Gui to bear the staff of authority and present the book of investiture, saying: “O Duke of Zhou, the position of emperor and king is not fixed; he who has virtue receives the mandate—such is Heaven’s way.

entries.zh: 予式時庸，荒求于唐虞之彝踵。
entries.en: At this time We earnestly seek to follow the models left by Tang and Yu.
entries.literal: We at this time broadly seek to follow the constant patterns of Tang and Yu.

entries.zh: 曰我魏德之終舊矣，我邦小大罔弗知，今其可久怫於天道而不歸有德歟。
entries.en: The virtue of Wei has run its course, and none in the realm doubts it—how can the throne long defy Heaven and refuse the worthy?
entries.literal: We say: the end of Wei virtue is already old; great and small in our state all know it—how can it long resist Heaven’s way and not return to the virtuous?

entries.zh: 時用詢謀。
entries.en: Counsel was now sought throughout the court.
entries.literal: At this time counsel was sought.

entries.zh: 僉曰公昭考文公，格勳德於天地，丕濟生民。
entries.en: All declared: Your late father Duke Wen matched Heaven and Earth in merit and brought vast benefit to the people.
entries.literal: All said: Your late father, Duke Wen, achieved meritorious virtue matching Heaven and Earth and greatly aided the people.

entries.zh: 洎公躬，又宣重光。
entries.en: In your own person you have renewed that glory.
entries.literal: When it reached Your person, you again spread a doubled radiance.

entries.zh: 故玄象徵見於上，謳訟奔走於下，天之歷數，用實在焉。
entries.en: Heaven’s signs have appeared above and songs of praise below—the mandate is manifest for all to see.
entries.literal: Therefore celestial signs appeared above and songs of praise rushed below—the calendar of Heaven is truly manifest.

entries.zh: 予安敢弗若。
entries.en: How could We dare do otherwise?
entries.literal: How could We dare not follow?

entries.zh: 是以欽祗聖典，遜位於公。
entries.en: We therefore reverently bow to the sacred precedent and yield the throne to you.
entries.literal: Therefore We reverently received the sacred canon and yielded the throne to you.

entries.zh: 公其享茲大命，保有萬國，可不慎歟。」
entries.en: Receive this great mandate, preserve the myriad realms, and govern with care.”
entries.literal: You shall receive this great mandate and preserve the myriad states—can you not be cautious?”

entries.zh: 魏帝臨朝，遣民部中大夫、濟北西元迪致皇帝璽紱。
entries.en: The Wei emperor came to court and sent Yuan Di of Western Jibei, Gentleman of the Ministry of the People, to present the imperial seal and cord.
entries.literal: The Wei emperor attended court and sent Yuan Di of the Western Commandery of Jibei, Gentleman of the Ministry of the People, to present the imperial seal and cord.

entries.zh: 固辭。
entries.en: Jue firmly declined.
entries.literal: [Jue] firmly declined.

entries.zh: 公卿百辟勸進，太
entries.en: The dukes, ministers, and all officials pressed him to ascend; the Grand
entries.literal: The dukes, ministers, and hundred officials urged him to accept; the Grand

entries.en: (Grand Preceptor)
entries.literal: (Preceptor)

entries.zh: 史陳祥瑞，乃從之。
entries.en: the historian Chen presented auspicious omens, and only then did he accept.
entries.literal: Historian Chen presented auspicious omens, and only then did he consent.

entries.zh: 是日，魏帝遜于大司馬府。
entries.en: That same day the Wei emperor retired to the Grand Marshal’s residence.
entries.literal: That day the Wei emperor withdrew to the residence of the Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 世宗明皇帝諱毓，小名統萬突，太祖長子也。
entries.en: Emperor Ming, canonically titled Shizong, bore the taboo name Yu and in childhood was called Tongwantu; he was the eldest son of Yuwen Tai.
entries.literal: Emperor Shizong Ming, taboo name Yu, childhood name Tongwantu, was the eldest son of the Grand Progenitor.

entries.zh: 母曰姚夫人，永熙三年，太祖臨夏州，生帝於統萬城，因以名焉。
entries.en: His mother was Lady Yao. In the third year of Yongxi (534), while Yuwen Tai was in Xia Province, the future emperor was born at Tongwan and took his childhood name from the city.
entries.literal: His mother was Lady Yao; in the third year of Yongxi, when the Grand Progenitor was stationed at Xia Province, the Emperor was born at Tongwan city, whence he received his name.

entries.zh: 大統十四年，封寧都郡公。
entries.en: In the fourteenth year of Datong (548) he was enfeoffed as duke of Ningdu commandery.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year of Datong, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Ningdu commandery.

entries.zh: 十六年，行華州事。
entries.en: In the sixteenth year (550) he acted as administrator of Hua Province.
entries.literal: In the sixteenth year, he administered Hua Province affairs.

entries.zh: 尋拜開府儀同三司、宜州諸軍事、宜州刺史。
entries.en: He was soon made commissioner with Three Excellencies protocol, commander of all Yi Province forces, and governor of Yi Province.
entries.literal: Soon after he was appointed commissioner with protocol equal to the Three Excellencies, commander of all military affairs in Yi Province, and governor of Yi Province.

entries.zh: 魏恭帝三年，授大將軍，鎮隴右。
entries.en: In the third year of Western Wei Emperor Gong (556) he was made grand general and posted to Longyou.
entries.literal: In the third year of Emperor Gong of Wei, he was granted the post of grand general and garrisoned Longyou.

entries.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，進位柱國，轉岐州諸軍事、岐州刺史。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne he was promoted to pillar-of-state and transferred to command of Qi Province forces and the governorship of Qi Province.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin acceded, he was advanced to pillar-of-state and transferred to commander of all military affairs in Qi Province and governor of Qi Province.

entries.zh: 治有美政，黎民懷之。
entries.en: His rule won praise; the people held him in affection.
entries.literal: His governance had fine policies; the common people cherished him.

entries.zh: 及孝閔帝廢，晉公護遣使迎帝於岐州。
entries.en: After Emperor Xiaomin was deposed, Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu sent envoys to bring the future emperor from Qi Province.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin was deposed, the Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu sent envoys to welcome the Emperor from Qi Province.

entries.zh: 秋九月癸亥，至京師，止於舊邸。
entries.en: In the ninth month of autumn, on guihai day, he reached the capital and stayed at his old residence.
entries.literal: In autumn, ninth month, day guihai, he reached the capital and lodged at his former residence.

entries.zh: 甲子，羣臣上表勸進，備法駕奉迎。
entries.en: On jiazi day the ministers memorialized urging him to ascend the throne and came with the full imperial escort to receive him.
entries.literal: On jiazi day the ministers submitted memorials urging his accession, fully equipped with the imperial carriage to escort him.

entries.zh: 帝固讓，羣臣固請，是日，即天王位，大赦天下。
entries.en: He refused firmly; the court pressed him again; that day he accepted the throne as heavenly king and proclaimed a general amnesty.
entries.literal: The Emperor firmly declined; the ministers firmly urged him; on that day he took the throne as Heavenly King and proclaimed a general amnesty.

entries.zh: 乙丑，朝羣臣於延壽殿。
entries.en: On yichou day he held audience with his ministers in the Hall of Extended Life.
entries.literal: On yichou day he held court with the ministers in the Hall of Extended Life.

entries.zh: 九月乙卯，以大將軍、天水公廣為梁州總管。
entries.en: In the ninth month, on yimao day, Grand General Yuwen Guang, Duke of Tianshui, was made governor-general of Liang Province.
entries.literal: In the ninth month, day yimao, Grand General, Duke of Tianshui Yuwen Guang was made governor-general of Liang Province.

entries.zh: 辛未，進封輔城公邕為魯國公，安城公憲為齊國公，秦郡公直為衛國公，正平公招為趙國公。
entries.en: On xinwei day Yuwen Yong, Duke of Fucheng, was promoted to Duke of Lu; Yuwen Xian of Ancheng to Duke of Qi; Yuwen Zhi of Qin commandery to Duke of Wei; and Yuwen Zhao of Zhengping to Duke of Zhao.
entries.literal: On day xinwei, Duke of Fucheng Yuwen Yong was advanced to Duke of Lu State, Duke of Ancheng Yuwen Xian to Duke of Qi State, Duke of Qin Commandery Yuwen Zhi to Duke of Wei State, Duke of Zhengping Yuwen Zhao to Duke of Zhao State.

entries.zh: 封皇弟儉為譙國公，純為陳國公，盛為越國公，達為代國公，通為冀國公，逌為滕國公。
entries.en: The emperor's younger brothers were enfeoffed: Yuwen Jian as Duke of Qiao, Yuwen Chun as Duke of Chen, Yuwen Sheng as Duke of Yue, Yuwen Da as Duke of Dai, Yuwen Tong as Duke of Ji, and Yuwen You as Duke of Teng.
entries.literal: The emperor's younger brothers—Jian was enfeoffed Duke of Qiao State, Chun Duke of Chen State, Sheng Duke of Yue State, Da Duke of Dai State, Tong Duke of Ji State, and You Duke of Teng State.

entries.zh: 進封天水公廣為蔡國公，高陽公達奚武為鄭國公，武陽公豆盧甯為楚國公，博陵公賀蘭祥為涼國公，甯蜀公尉遲迥為蜀國公，化政公宇文貴為許國公，陳留公楊忠為
entries.en: Yuwen Guang of Tianshui was promoted to Duke of Cai; Daxi Wu of Gaoyang to Duke of Zheng; Doulu Ning of Wuyang to Duke of Chu; Helan Xiang of Boling to Duke of Liang; Yuchi Jiong of Ningshu to Duke of Shu; Yuwen Gui of Huazheng to Duke of Xu; and Chenliu Duke Yang Zhong as
entries.literal: Yuwen Guang, Duke of Tianshui, was advanced to Duke of Cai State; Daxi Wu, Duke of Gaoyang, to Duke of Zheng State; Doulu Ning, Duke of Wuyang, to Duke of Chu State; Helan Xiang, Duke of Boling, to Duke of Liang State; Yuchi Jiong, Duke of Ningshu, to Duke of Shu State; Yuwen Gui, Duke of Huazheng, to Duke of Xu State; Chenliu Duke Yang Zhong as

entries.en: (Sui)
entries.literal: (Sui)

entries.zh: 隨國公，昌平公尉遲綱為吳國公，武威公王雄為庸國公。
entries.en: Duke of Sui State; Yuchi Gang of Changping as Duke of Wu, and Wang Xiong of Wuwei as Duke of Yong.
entries.literal: Duke of Sui State; Yuchi Gang of Changping as Duke of Wu, and Wang Xiong of Wuwei as Duke of Yong.

entries.zh: 邑各萬戶。
entries.en: Each fief held ten thousand households.
entries.literal: Each fief was ten thousand households.

entries.zh: 其詔即帝口授也。
entries.en: The edict was dictated by the emperor himself.
entries.literal: This edict was dictated from the emperor's own mouth.

entries.zh: 辛丑，崩於延壽殿，時年二十七，諡曰明皇帝，廟稱世宗。
entries.en: On xinchou day he died in the Yanshou Hall, aged twenty-seven; he was posthumously titled Emperor Ming and given the temple name Shizong.
entries.literal: On day xinchou, he died in the Yanshou Hall, aged twenty-seven; his posthumous title was Emperor Ming, his temple name Shizong.

entries.zh: 五月辛未，葬於昭陵。
entries.en: In the fifth month, on xinwei day, he was buried at Zhaoling.
entries.literal: In the fifth month, day xinwei, he was buried at Zhaoling.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：世宗寬仁遠度，叡哲博聞。
entries.en: The historiographer writes: Shizong was generous and far-seeing, wise and widely learned.
entries.literal: The historiographer states: Shizong was generous, far-sighted, wise, intelligent, and broadly informed.

entries.zh: 處代邸之尊，實文昭之長。
entries.en: While he held the honored place of heir at the princely lodge, he was in truth Wen's eldest son.
entries.literal: Dwelling in the honored station of the prince's lodge, he was in truth the eldest son of Wen.

entries.zh: 豹姿已變，龍德猶潛，而百辟傾心，萬方注意。
entries.en: Though still young in years and not yet fully revealed in power, the hundred officials already turned to him and the realm already watched him.
entries.literal: The leopard's form had already changed, yet the dragon's virtue still lay hidden—and still the hundred officials bent their hearts to him and the ten thousand directions fixed their gaze upon him.

entries.zh: 及乎迎宣黜賀，入纂大宗，而禮貌功臣，敦睦九族，率由恭儉，崇尚文儒，亹亹焉其有君人之德者矣。
entries.en: Once he was brought from Qizhou and proclaimed, with the former emperor deposed, he took up the great succession; he honored meritorious ministers, kept the clan at peace, lived in reverence and frugality, and cherished scholars—earnestly showing the virtue of a ruler.
entries.literal: When it came to welcoming the proclamation and deposing He, entering to inherit the great lineage, then he treated meritorious ministers with courtesy, harmonized the nine kin groups, conducted himself in reverence and frugality, and honored scholars and Confucians—in earnest diligence he showed the virtue of one who rules men.

entries.zh: 始則權臣專制，政出私門；
entries.en: At first a powerful minister ruled alone and policy came from his house;
entries.literal: At first the powerful minister held sole sway and government issued from private doors;

entries.zh: 終乃鴆毒潛加，享年不永。
entries.en: in the end poison was set in his food, and his life was cut short.
entries.literal: At the end poison was secretly added, and his years were not long.

entries.zh: 惜哉！
entries.en: Alas!
entries.literal: Alas!

entries.zh: 秋八月己亥，改天王稱皇帝，追尊文王為帝，大赦改元。
entries.en: On jihai day in the eighth month of autumn he took the title Emperor instead of Heavenly King, posthumously raised Wen Wang to emperor, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name.
entries.literal: In the eighth month of autumn, day jihai, he changed the title of Heavenly King to Emperor, posthumously honored Wen Wang as emperor, granted a general amnesty, and changed the era name.

entries.zh: 壬子，以大將軍、安城公憲為益州總管。
entries.en: On renzi day Grand General Yuwen Xian, Duke of Ancheng, was made governor-general of Yi Province.
entries.literal: On day renzi, Grand General, Duke of Ancheng Yuwen Xian was made governor-general of Yi Province.

entries.zh: 癸丑，增御正四人，位上大夫。
entries.en: On guichou day four Imperial Rectifiers were appointed, each with the rank of Senior Grand Master.
entries.literal: On day guichou, four Imperial Rectifiers were added, with rank of Senior Grand Master.

entries.zh: 帝寬明仁厚，敦睦九族，有君人之量。
entries.en: He was open, clear, benevolent, and generous, kept the imperial clan in harmony, and had the bearing of a true ruler.
entries.literal: The emperor was broad, clear, benevolent, and generous, harmonizing the nine kin groups, and possessed the measure of one who rules men.

entries.zh: 幼而好學，博覽羣書，善屬文，詞彩溫麗。
entries.en: From youth he loved learning, read widely, wrote well, and his prose ran warm and fine.
entries.literal: From youth he loved learning, broadly reading the multitudinous books, skilled at literary composition, his phrasing warm and beautiful.

entries.zh: 及即位，集公卿已下有文學者八十餘人於麟趾殿，刊校經史。
entries.en: After his accession he brought more than eighty literate officials of civil and military rank to the Linzhi Hall to edit and collate the classics and histories.
entries.literal: After he took the throne, he gathered more than eighty civil and military officials below the rank of grandee who had literary ability in the Linzhi Hall to edit and collate the classics and histories.

entries.zh: 又捃采衆書，自羲、農以來，訖於魏末，敘為世譜，凡五百卷雲。
entries.en: He also collected books from the age of Fuxi and Shennong down to the end of Wei and compiled them into a genealogical record of five hundred scrolls.
entries.literal: He also gathered and collected the multitudinous books from Fuxi and Shennong down to the end of Wei, arranged them as a genealogical record of generations—five hundred scrolls in all, it is said.

entries.zh: 所著文章十卷。
entries.en: His own writings filled ten scrolls.
entries.literal: Literary works he composed filled ten scrolls.

entries.zh: 二年春正月乙未，以大冢宰、晉公護為太師。
entries.en: In spring of the second year, first month, on yiwei day, Grand Preceptor Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu was made grand tutor.
entries.literal: In spring of the second year, first month, day yiwei, the Grand Preceptor, Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu was made Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 辛亥，親耕籍田。
entries.en: On xinhai day he performed the ceremonial plowing at the sacred field.
entries.literal: On xinhai day he personally plowed the sacred field.

entries.zh: 癸丑，立王后獨孤氏。
entries.en: On guichou day he installed Lady Dugu as queen.
entries.literal: On guichou day he established Lady Dugu as queen.

entries.zh: 丁巳，雍州置十二郡。
entries.en: On dingsi day twelve commanderies were set up within Yong Province.
entries.literal: On dingsi day twelve commanderies were established in Yong Province.

entries.zh: 又於河東置蒲州，河北置虞州，弘農置陝州，正平置絳州，宜陽置熊州，邵郡置邵州。
entries.en: Pu Province was also established in Hedong, Yu Province in Hebei, Shan Province in Hongnong, Jiang Province in Zhengping, Xiong Province in Yiyang, and Shao Province in Shao commandery.
entries.literal: Also in Hedong Pu Province was established, in Hebei Yu Province, in Hongnong Shan Province, in Zhengping Jiang Province, in Yiyang Xiong Province, and in Shao commandery Shao Province.

entries.zh: 武成元年春正月己酉，太師、晉公護上表歸政，帝始親覽萬機。
entries.en: In spring of Wucheng year one, on jiyou of the first month, Grand Tutor Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu submitted a memorial returning government, and the emperor began personally overseeing state affairs.
entries.literal: In spring of the first year of Wucheng, on jiyou of the first month, Grand Tutor Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu submitted a memorial returning government; the emperor began personally handling the myriad affairs of state.

entries.zh: 軍旅之事，護猶總焉。
entries.en: Military affairs remained under Hu's overall command.
entries.literal: As for military affairs, Hu still held overall command.

entries.zh: 初改都督諸州軍事為總管。
entries.en: For the first time the title of commander of military affairs of the various provinces was changed to governor-general.
entries.literal: For the first time the title of commander of military affairs of the various provinces was changed to governor-general.

entries.zh: 丙辰，封大將軍、章武孝公導子亮為永昌公，翼為西陽公。
entries.en: On bingchen day Grand General Zhangwu Xiaogong Dao's son Liang was enfeoffed Duke of Yongchang, and Yi was made Duke of Xiyang.
entries.literal: On bingchen day Grand General Zhangwu Xiaogong Dao's son Liang was enfeoffed Duke of Yongchang, and Yi was made Duke of Xiyang.

entries.zh: 二年春正月癸丑朔，大會羣臣於紫極殿，始用百戲焉。
entries.en: In spring of the second year, on the new moon of the first month, the court gathered all ministers in the Ziji Hall and for the first time staged the hundred entertainments.
entries.literal: In the second year, spring, first month, day guichou (new moon), a great assembly of the multitudinous ministers was held in the Ziji Hall; the hundred entertainments were used for the first time.

entries.zh: 夏四月，帝因食遇毒。
entries.en: In the fourth month of summer the emperor was poisoned at a meal.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of summer, the emperor was poisoned through food.

entries.zh: 庚子，大漸。
entries.en: On gengzi day he fell gravely ill.
entries.literal: On day gengzi, he sank critically ill.

entries.zh: 詔曰：
entries.en: He issued a death edict:
entries.literal: An edict stated:

entries.zh: 夏四月己巳，以太師、晉公護為雍州牧。
entries.en: In summer, fourth month, on jisi day, Grand Tutor Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu was made governor-general of Yong Province.
entries.literal: In summer, fourth month, day jisi, the Grand Tutor, Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu was made governor-general of Yong Province.

entries.zh: 庚午，熒惑入軒轅。
entries.en: On gengwu day Mars entered the Xuanyuan asterism.
entries.literal: On gengwu day Mars entered the Xuanyuan constellation.

entries.zh: 辛未，降死罪一等，五歲刑已下皆原之。
entries.en: On xinwei day death sentences were commuted one grade, and punishments of five years or less were all forgiven.
entries.literal: On xinwei day capital crimes were reduced one grade; punishments of five years or less were all remitted.

entries.zh: 甲戌，王后獨孤氏崩。
entries.en: On jiaxu day Queen Lady Dugu died.
entries.literal: On jiaxu day Queen Lady Dugu died.

entries.zh: 甲申，葬敬后。
entries.en: On jiashen day Empress Jing was buried.
entries.literal: On jiashen day Empress Jing was buried.

entries.zh: 今大位虛曠，社稷無主。
entries.en: The throne is empty and the altars of state have no ruler.
entries.literal: Now the great throne stands vacant and the altars of state have no master.

entries.zh: 朕兒幼稚，未堪當國。
entries.en: My son is still a child and cannot yet rule.
entries.literal: My son is young and tender and cannot yet bear the realm.

entries.zh: 魯國公邕，朕之介弟，寬仁大度，海內共聞，能弘我周家，必此子也。
entries.en: Yuwen Yong, Duke of Lu, is my younger brother—generous, open, and famed throughout the realm. He can carry our Zhou house forward, and he must be the one.
entries.literal: Duke of Lu State Yu Gong is my younger brother by the same mother—generous, benevolent, and magnanimous, known throughout the seas; he can expand our Zhou house—it must be this man.

entries.zh: 夫人貴有始終，公等事太祖，輔朕躬，可謂有始矣，若克念世道艱難，輔邕以主天下者，可謂有終矣。
entries.en: A man's honor lies in finishing what he begins. You served the Grand Progenitor and supported me—that was the beginning. If you remember how hard these times are and help Yu Gong rule the realm, that will be the end.
entries.literal: In human affairs, nobility lies in having a beginning and an end; you served the Grand Progenitor and supported my person—that may be called a beginning. If you keep in mind the world's bitter hardship and support Yu Gong in ruling all under Heaven—that may be called an end.

entries.zh: 哀死事生，人臣大節，公等思念此言，令萬代稱歎。
entries.en: To honor the dead and serve the living is a minister's highest duty. Keep these words in mind, and let later ages praise you for them.
entries.literal: Grieving the dead and serving the living is the great integrity of a minister—think upon these words and let ten thousand generations sigh in admiration.

entries.zh: 三月癸巳，陳六軍，帝親擐甲冑，迎太白於東方。
entries.en: Third month, on guisi day, the six armies were drawn up; the emperor personally donned armor and helmet and welcomed Venus in the east.
entries.literal: Third month, day guisi, the six armies were arrayed; the Emperor personally donned armor and helmet and welcomed the White Planet in the east.

entries.zh: 秦郡公直鎮蒲州。
entries.en: Yuwen Zhi, Duke of Qin commandery, garrisoned Pu Province.
entries.literal: Duke of Qin commandery Zhi garrisoned Pu Province.

entries.zh: 吐谷渾寇邊，庚戌，遣大司馬、博陵公賀蘭祥率衆討之。
entries.en: Tuyuhun raided the frontier; on gengxu day he sent Grand Marshal Helan Xiang, Duke of Boling, with troops to punish them.
entries.literal: Tuyuhun raided the border; on gengxu day he dispatched Grand Marshal, Duke of Boling Helan Xiang to lead troops to suppress them.

entries.zh: 三月甲午，齊北豫州刺史司馬消難舉州來附，遣柱國、高陽公達奚武與大將軍楊忠率衆迎之。
entries.en: Third month, on jiawu day, Northern Qi's governor of North Yu Province, Sima Xiaonan, surrendered the province; the court sent Pillar-of-State Daxi Wu, Duke of Gaoyang, and Grand General Yang Zhong with troops to receive him.
entries.literal: Third month, day jiawu, Northern Qi's governor of North Yu Province Sima Xiaonan raised the province in submission; he dispatched Pillar-of-State, Duke of Gaoyang Daxi Wu and Grand General Yang Zhong to lead troops to welcome him.

entries.zh: 改雍州刺史為雍州牧，京兆郡守為京兆尹。
entries.en: The Yong Province governor was retitled governor-general of Yong Province, and the Jingzhao commandery prefect became intendant of Jingzhao.
entries.literal: The governor of Yong Province was changed to governor-general of Yong Province, and the prefect of Jingzhao commandery to intendant of Jingzhao.

entries.zh: 以廣業、脩城二郡置康州，葭蘆郡置文州。
entries.en: Guangye and Xiucheng commanderies were combined into Kang Province, and Jialu commandery into Wen Province.
entries.literal: The two commanderies of Guangye and Xiucheng were made into Kang Province, and Jialu commandery into Wen Province.

entries.zh: 戊申，長安獻白雀。
entries.en: On wushen day Chang'an presented a white sparrow.
entries.literal: On wushen day a white sparrow was presented from Chang'an.

entries.zh: 庚申，詔曰：「三十六國，九十九姓，自魏氏南徙，皆稱河南之民。
entries.en: On gengshen day an edict said: "The thirty-six states and ninety-nine surnames, since the Wei dynasty moved south, were all called people of Henan.
entries.literal: On gengshen day an edict said: "The thirty-six states and ninety-nine surnames, since the Wei house moved south, all were called the people of Henan.

entries.zh: 今周室旣都關中，宜改稱京兆人。」
entries.en: Now that Zhou holds the capital in Guanzhong, they should be called people of Jingzhao."
entries.literal: Now that the Zhou house has its capital in Guanzhong, they should be renamed people of Jingzhao."

entries.zh: 十一月庚子，祠太廟。
entries.en: In the eleventh month, on gengzi day, he offered sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestors' Temple.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month, day gengzi, he sacrificed at the Imperial Ancestors' Temple.

entries.zh: 丁未，祠圓丘。
entries.en: On dingwei day he sacrificed at the Circular Mound.
entries.literal: On dingwei day he sacrificed at the Circular Mound.

entries.zh: 丁巳，詔曰：「帝王之道，以寬仁為大。
entries.en: On dingsi day an edict declared: "The way of kings and emperors rests above all on clemency and benevolence.
entries.literal: On dingsi day an edict said: "The way of emperors and kings takes lenity and benevolence as supreme.

entries.zh: 魏政諸有輕犯未至重罪、及諸村民一家有犯乃及數家而被遠配者，並宜放還。」
entries.en: Under Wei law, all who had committed minor offenses not amounting to grave crime, and all villages where one family's guilt had sent several households into distant exile, should be released and sent home."
entries.literal: Under Wei rule, all those who had committed light offenses short of serious crime, and villages where one household's offense had drawn exile upon several families, should all be released and returned."

entries.zh: 十二月庚午，謁成陵。
entries.en: In the twelfth month, on gengwu day, he visited Chengling Mausoleum.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, day gengwu, he visited Chengl Mausoleum.

entries.zh: 癸酉，還宮。
entries.en: On guiyou day he returned to the palace.
entries.literal: On guiyou day he returned to the palace.

entries.zh: 庚辰，以大將軍、輔城公邕為柱國。
entries.en: On gengchen day he made Grand General Yuwen Yong, Duke of Fucheng, a pillar-of-state.
entries.literal: On gengchen day he made the grand general, Duke of Fucheng Yong, a pillar-of-state.

entries.zh: 戊子，赦長安見囚。
entries.en: On wuzi day he pardoned prisoners then held in Chang'an.
entries.literal: On wuzi day he pardoned prisoners held in Chang'an.

entries.zh: 甲午，詔曰：「善人之後，猶累世獲宥，況魏氏以德讓代終，豈容不加隱恤。
entries.en: On jiawu day an edict said: "The descendants of the virtuous still win pardon generation after generation; how much more when the Wei dynasty yielded the throne in virtue—can we withhold compassion?
entries.literal: On jiawu day an edict said: "The descendants of good men still receive pardon generation after generation; how much more when the Wei house ended by yielding the throne in virtue—can we fail to show hidden care and pity?

entries.zh: 元氏子女自坐趙貴等事以來，所有沒入為官口者，悉宜放免。」
entries.en: Since the Yuan imperial clan was implicated in the Zhao Gui affair and after, all sons and daughters confiscated as government bond-slaves should be released and freed."
entries.literal: Since the Yuan clan sons and daughters were implicated in the Zhao Gui affair and afterward, all who had been confiscated as government bond-slaves should be released and freed."

entries.zh: 二月癸未，詔曰：「王者之宰民也，莫不同四海，一遠近，為父母而子之。
entries.en: Second month, on guiwei day, an edict said: "In governing the people, a king must make the four seas one and near and far alike, acting as a parent to his children.
entries.literal: Second month, day guiwei, an edict said: "When kings rule the people, none fail to treat all within the four seas alike, making near and far one, acting as parents and treating them as children.

entries.zh: 一物失所，若納于隍。
entries.en: If one thing is out of place, it is as into a gutter.
entries.literal: If one thing loses its proper place, it is as into a gutter.

entries.zh: 賊之境土，本同大化，往因時難，致阻東西。
entries.en: Rebel-held lands once shared the same civilizing rule; wartime hardship had cut east from west.
entries.literal: The rebel territories originally shared the same great transformation; in the past because of the difficulties of the times they came to be blocked east and west.

entries.zh: 遂使疆埸之間，互相抄掠。
entries.en: Border districts therefore raided and plundered one another.
entries.literal: Thus at the borders they raided and plundered one another.

entries.zh: 興言及此，良可哀傷。
entries.en: To speak of it is truly heartbreaking.
entries.literal: To speak of this is truly cause for grief.

entries.zh: 自元年以來，有被掠入賊者，悉可放免。」
entries.en: Since the first year of the reign, all who were seized and carried into enemy territory may be released and sent home."
entries.literal: Since the first year, all who were captured and taken into rebel territory may be released and freed."

entries.zh: 自冬不雨，至於是月方大雪。
entries.en: Rain had failed since winter; only in this month did heavy snow come.
entries.literal: From winter there had been no rain; only in this month did heavy snow fall.

entries.zh: 八月甲子，羣臣上表稱慶。
entries.en: Eighth month, on jiazi day, the ministers submitted memorials of congratulation.
entries.literal: In the eighth month, day jiazi, the ministers submitted memorials of congratulation.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「夫天不愛寶，地稱表瑞，莫不威鳳巢閣，圖龍躍沼，豈直日月珠連，風雨玉燭。
entries.en: An edict said: "Heaven does not hoard its treasures; earth displays auspicious signs—the awe-inspiring phoenix nests in the tower, the patterned dragon leaps in the pool; how much more than sun and moon strung like pearls, wind and rain like jade candles?
entries.literal: An edict said: "Heaven does not hoard treasures; earth is said to display auspicious signs—all witness the phoenix nesting in the tower, the dragon leaping in the pool; how much more than sun and moon strung like pearls, wind and rain like jade candles?

entries.zh: 是以《鈎命決》曰『王者至孝則出』，元命苞曰『人君至治所有』。
entries.en: Thus Hooks Life Verdict says, "When the king is supremely filial, it appears," and Primordial Mandate Bud says, "When the ruler's governance is supreme, he possesses it."
entries.literal: Thus Hooks Life Verdict says 'When the king is supremely filial it appears,' and Primordial Mandate Bud says 'When the ruler's governance is supreme it is possessed.'

entries.zh: 虞舜烝烝，來茲異趾；
entries.en: Yu Shun, utterly filial, here received the strange foot;
entries.literal: Yu Shun in utmost filial piety, here came the strange foot;

entries.zh: 周文翼翼，翔此靈禽。
entries.en: King Wen of Zhou, reverent and careful, here saw this numinous bird soar.
entries.literal: Zhou Wen diligent and reverent, this numinous bird soared here.

entries.zh: 文考至德下覃，遺仁爰被，遠符千載，降斯三足。
entries.en: King Wen's utmost virtue spread below; his surviving benevolence still reaches abroad; a thousand years matched, this three-footed bird was sent down.
entries.literal: Our late father of utmost virtue spread below, his remaining benevolence therein extended, matching a thousand years afar, sent down this three-footed bird.

entries.zh: 將使三方歸本，九州翕定。
entries.en: It will bring the three regions back to their root and settle the nine provinces in harmony.
entries.literal: It will cause the three directions to return to the root and the nine provinces to be harmoniously settled.

entries.zh: 惟此大體，景福在民。
entries.en: In this great cause, bright fortune rests with the people.
entries.literal: In this great matter alone, bright fortune rests on the people.

entries.zh: 予安敢讓宗廟之善，弗宣大惠。
entries.en: How dare I withhold the ancestral temple's blessing and fail to proclaim a great grace?
entries.literal: How dare I decline the goodness of the ancestral temple and fail to proclaim a great grace?

entries.zh: 可大赦天下，文武官普進二級。」
entries.en: Let there be a general amnesty throughout the realm, and let civil and military officials all advance two ranks."
entries.literal: A general amnesty may be proclaimed for the empire; civil and military officials may all advance two ranks."

entries.zh: 五月戊子，詔曰：「皇王之迹不一，因革之道已殊，莫不播八政以成物，兆三元而為紀。
entries.en: Fifth month, on wuzi day, an edict said: "The ways of emperors and kings are not one; paths of reform already differ; all spread the eight governances to complete creation and take the three origins as their measure.
entries.literal: In the fifth month, day wuzi, an edict said: "The traces of emperors and kings are not one; the paths of change and reform already differ; none fail to spread the eight governances to complete things and take the three origins as their standard.

entries.zh: 是以容成創定於軒轅，羲和欽若於唐世，《鴻範》九疇，大弘五法。
entries.en: Thus Rongcheng first fixed the calendar under the Yellow Emperor, and Xihe reverently kept time in the age of Tang; the nine categories of Great Plan greatly extended the five methods.
entries.literal: Thus Rongcheng first established at Xuanyuan, Xihe reverently observed in the Tang age; the nine categories of Great Plan greatly extended the five methods.

entries.zh: 《易》曰：「澤中有火，革，君子以治曆明時。」
entries.en: The Changes says: "Fire in the marsh—innovation; the gentleman uses it to regulate the calendar and clarify the seasons."
entries.literal: The Changes says: 'Fire in the marsh—innovation; the gentleman uses it to regulate the calendar and clarify the seasons.'

entries.zh: 故歷之為義大矣。
entries.en: Thus the meaning of the calendar is indeed great.
entries.literal: Thus the meaning of the calendar is great indeed.

entries.zh: 但忽微成象，象極則差；
entries.en: Yet subtle signs become phenomena, and when phenomena reach their limit error follows;
entries.literal: But subtle signs become phenomena; when phenomena reach their limit there is error;

entries.zh: 分積命時，時積斯舛。
entries.en: Fractions accumulate to fix the seasons; as seasons accumulate, discrepancies arise.
entries.literal: Fractions accumulate to determine time; when time accumulates, then come discrepancies.

entries.zh: 開闢至於獲麟，二百七十六萬歲，晷度推移，餘分盈縮，南正無聞，疇人靡記。
entries.en: From the world's opening to the Capture of the Unicorn, 2,760,000 years—the gnomon and degrees shifted, remainders waxed and waned, the south-first month went unmarked, and calendar officers left no record.
entries.literal: From the opening of the world until the Capture of the Unicorn, 2,760,000 years—the gnomon and degrees shifted, fractional remainders waxed and waned, the south-first month was unheard of, calendar specialists had no record.

entries.zh: 暑往寒來，理乖攸序，敬授民時，何其積謬。
entries.en: Summer passes and winter comes—the order is wrong; to reverently grant seasons to the people—how piled the errors!
entries.literal: Summer gone, winter come—the principle deviates from proper order; reverently bestowing seasons on the people—how accumulated the errors!

entries.zh: 昔漢世巴郡洛下閎善治歷，云後八百歲，當有聖人定之。
entries.en: In Han times Luoxia Hong of Ba commandery was skilled at calendrics; he said that eight hundred years later a sage would fix the calendar.
entries.literal: Formerly in Han times Luoxia Hong of Ba commandery was skilled at regulating the calendar; he said that eight hundred years later a sage would fix it.

entries.zh: 自火行至今，木德應其運矣，朕何讓焉。
entries.en: From the Fire phase until now the Wood virtue answers its turn; why should I decline?
entries.literal: From the Fire phase until now, the Wood virtue answers its turn; why should I decline?

entries.zh: 可命有司，傍稽六曆，仰觀七曜，博推古今，造我周曆，量定以聞。」
entries.en: Let the responsible offices consult the six calendars, observe the seven luminaries, compare past and present broadly, create the Zhou calendar, measure and fix it, and report."
entries.literal: Let the relevant offices be ordered to consult the six calendars at hand, look up to the seven luminaries, broadly compare past and present, create our Zhou calendar, measure and fix it, and report."

entries.zh: 己亥，聽訟於正武殿。
entries.en: On jihai day he heard lawsuits at the Hall of Righteous Martialness.
entries.literal: On jihai day he heard cases at the Hall of Righteous Martialness.

entries.zh: 辛亥，以大宗伯、梁國公侯莫陳崇為大司徒，大司寇、高陽公達奚武為大宗伯，武陽公豆盧甯為大司寇，柱國、輔城公邕為大司空。
entries.en: On xinhai day Grand Director of Ceremonies Houmochen Chong, Duke of Liang, was made grand minister of education; Grand Minister of Justice Daxi Wu, Duke of Gaoyang, was made grand director of ceremonies; Doulu Ning, Duke of Wuyang, was made grand minister of justice; and Pillar-of-State Yuwen Yong, Duke of Fucheng, was made grand minister of works.
entries.literal: On xinhai day the Grand Director of Ceremonies, Duke of Liang Yuwen Houmochen Chong was made Grand Minister of Education; Grand Minister of Justice, Duke of Gaoyang Daxi Wu was made Grand Director of Ceremonies; Duke of Wuyang Doulu Ning was made Grand Minister of Justice; Pillar-of-State, Duke of Fucheng Yu was made Grand Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 乙卯，詔曰：「比屢有糾發官司赦前事。
entries.en: On yimao day an edict said: "Lately offices have repeatedly been impeached for offenses committed before the amnesty.
entries.literal: On yimao day an edict said: "Recently offices have repeatedly been impeached for pre-amnesty matters.

entries.zh: 此雖意在疾惡，但先王制肆眚之道，令天下自新，若又推問，自新何由哉。
entries.en: That may aim at hating evil, but former kings instituted amnesty so the realm could renew itself; if cases are pursued again, how can anyone begin anew?
entries.literal: This though intended to abhor evil, yet the former kings established the way of granting amnesty to let the empire renew itself; if one again investigates, how can renewal be achieved?

entries.zh: 如此之徒，有司勿為推究。
entries.en: Officials are not to pursue cases of this kind.
entries.literal: Persons such as these—the relevant offices should not investigate them.

entries.zh: 惟庫廄倉廩與海內所共，漢帝有云『朕為天下守財耳』。
entries.en: The imperial stores and granaries belong to the realm as a whole. A Han emperor put it plainly: "I am only the empire's treasurer."
entries.literal: Only the treasury stables, granaries, and storehouses are held in common with all within the seas. A Han emperor once said, "I merely keep treasure for the empire."

entries.zh: 若有侵盜公家財畜錢粟者，魏朝之事，年月旣遠，一不須問。
entries.en: Theft of public property dating to Wei times is too remote to investigate.
entries.literal: Should anyone have plundered public livestock, money, or grain, as for Wei-dynasty matters long past, there is no need to inquire at all.

entries.zh: 自周有天下以來，雖經赦宥，而事蹟可知者，有司宜即推窮。
entries.en: Since our dynasty began, even when pardon has covered a crime, officials must still investigate any case whose facts remain clear.
entries.literal: Since Zhou gained the realm, even if amnesty was granted, wherever the facts can still be established, the relevant offices should at once pursue the case to the end.

entries.zh: 得實之日，但免其罪，徵備如法。」
entries.en: Once guilt is proved, the offender is spared punishment but must make full restitution by law."
entries.literal: When guilt is established, only the punishment is remitted; restitution is exacted according to law."

entries.zh: 賀蘭祥攻拔洮陽、洪和二城，吐谷渾遁走。
entries.en: Helan Xiang took Taoyang and Honghe, and the Tuyuhun withdrew.
entries.literal: Helan Xiang attacked and captured the cities of Taoyang and Honghe; the Tuyuhun fled.

entries.zh: 六月戊子，大雨霖。
entries.en: In the sixth month, on wuzi day, torrential rains set in.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, day wuzi, great rains fell in succession.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「昔唐咨四嶽，殷告六眚，睹災興懼，咸寘時雍。
entries.en: An edict read: "In antiquity Yao questioned the Four Peaks and the Yin court reported the six calamities; seeing disaster, rulers grew fearful and restored harmony to the age.
entries.literal: An edict stated: "Of old, Tang Yao questioned the Four Peaks, and the Yin dynasty reported the six portents; seeing calamities, they were stirred to fear, and all brought about timely harmony.

entries.zh: 朕撫運應圖，作民父母，弗敢怠荒，以求民瘼。
entries.en: I have taken up the mandate and stand as father and mother to the people, never daring to slacken in seeking out their hardships.
entries.literal: I have received the mandate and answered the chart, acting as parent to the people, not daring to be lax or negligent, seeking the people's afflictions.

entries.zh: 而霖雨作沴，害麥傷苗，隤屋漂垣，洎于昏墊。
entries.en: Yet unending rain has brought ruin: wheat spoiled, seedlings destroyed, roofs fallen and walls swept away, until the land lies drowned.
entries.literal: Yet successive rains bring baleful influence, harming the wheat and injuring the seedlings, houses collapsing and walls washed away, reaching to waterlogged ground.

entries.zh: 諒朕不德，蒼生何咎。
entries.en: The fault is mine, not the people's.
entries.literal: Knowing my lack of virtue, why should the common people bear guilt?

entries.zh: 刑政所失，罔識厥由。
entries.en: Where law and rule have gone wrong, I cannot see the reason.
entries.literal: Where governance and punishments have failed, I know not the cause.

entries.zh: 公卿大夫士爰及牧守黎庶等，今宜各上封事，讜言極諫，罔有所諱。
entries.en: Dukes, ministers, officials, governors, and commoners alike should now submit sealed memorials—speak frankly, remonstrate fully, and hide nothing.
entries.literal: Dukes, grandees, ministers, and scholar-officials, extending to provincial governors and the common folk—today each should submit sealed memorials with candid words and utmost remonstrance, hiding nothing.

entries.zh: 朕將覽察，以答天譴。
entries.en: I will read them and answer Heaven's rebuke.
entries.literal: I shall examine them and answer Heaven's reproof.

entries.zh: 其遭水者，有司可時巡檢，條列以聞。」
entries.en: For those harmed by the floods, officials should inspect promptly and report each case."
entries.literal: Those who have suffered from the waters—the relevant offices may inspect in a timely manner and set forth the cases in reports."

entries.zh: 庚子，詔曰：「潁川從我，是曰元勳；
entries.en: On gengzi day an edict read: "Yingchuan stood with me—that was the first of founding merits;
entries.literal: On day gengzi, an edict stated: "Yingchuan followed me—that is called a founding merit;

entries.zh: 無忘父城，實起王業。
entries.en: Do not forget Fucheng—that is where the royal enterprise began.
entries.literal: Do not forget Fucheng—there the kingly enterprise truly began.

entries.zh: 文考屬天地草昧，造化權輿，拯彼橫流，匡茲頹運。
entries.en: My late father, in the chaos when Heaven and Earth were still unformed, saved the realm from the flood and turned back a failing age.
entries.literal: My late father, amid the darkness between Heaven and Earth when creation was still in its first stirrings, rescued the torrent and righted the failing fortune.

entries.zh: 賴英賢盡力，文武同心，翼贊大功，克隆帝業。
entries.en: Worthy men gave all their strength, civil and military leaders stood as one, and together they raised the great work and founded the imperial house.
entries.literal: Relying on worthy heroes giving their full strength and civil and military men of one mind, they winged and supported the great achievement and jointly established the imperial enterprise.

entries.zh: 而被堅執銳，櫛風沐雨，永言疇昔，良用憮然。
entries.en: Those who wore armor and bore arms, who endured wind and rain—to speak of them even now moves me deeply.
entries.literal: Yet those who wore armor and wielded sharp weapons, wind-combed and rain-washed—in speaking always of days past, I am deeply moved.

entries.zh: 至若功成名遂，建國剖符，予惟休也。
entries.en: As for merit fulfilled, states founded, and fiefs granted—that was their reward and my comfort.
entries.literal: As for achieving merit and completing the task, founding states and carving tallies—in that I find only repose.

entries.zh: 其有致死王事，妻子無歸者，朕甚傷之。
entries.en: Those who died in the king's service, leaving wives and children with nowhere to go—I grieve for them deeply.
entries.literal: Those who gave their lives in the king's service whose wives and children had nowhere to return—I grieve deeply for them.

entries.zh: 凡是從先王向夏州，發夏州從來，見在及薨亡者，並量賜錢帛，稱朕意焉。」
entries.en: All who marched with the late king to Xia Province, and all who came from Xia Province and are still living or have since died—each shall receive money and silk as I intend."
entries.literal: All who followed the late king toward Xia Province, and all who set out from Xia Province and are now living or who have died—each shall be granted money and silk in measure, in accord with my wish."

entries.zh: 是月，陳武帝薨，兄子蒨立，是謂文帝。
entries.en: That month Chen Wudi died; his nephew Chen Qian succeeded him, known as Emperor Wen of Chen.
entries.literal: That month, Chen Wudi died; his elder brother's son Qian succeeded him—this is known as Emperor Wen.

entries.zh: 人生天地之間，稟五常之氣，天地有窮已，五常有推移，人安得長在。
entries.en: Human life draws breath from the five constants between Heaven and Earth; Heaven and Earth themselves pass away, and the five constants change—how then can any man endure forever?
entries.literal: Between Heaven and Earth, human life receives the breath of the five constants; Heaven and Earth have their end, the five constants shift and change—how can man long remain?

entries.zh: 是以生而有死者，物理之必然。
entries.en: That the living must die is the way of nature.
entries.literal: Thus that there is death for those born is the necessary way of things.

entries.zh: 處必然之理，修短之間，何足多恨。
entries.en: Once one accepts that law, what matter whether life is long or short?
entries.literal: Facing the way of necessity, between long and short life—what is there greatly to regret?

entries.zh: 朕雖不德，性好典墳，披覽聖賢餘論，未嘗不以此自曉。
entries.en: I am not a virtuous man, but I have always loved the classics; reading the words left by sages, I have tried to take their lesson to heart.
entries.literal: Though I lack virtue, by nature I love the classic texts; perusing the leftover teachings of sages and worthies, never have I failed to use this to enlighten myself.

entries.zh: 今乃命也，夫復何言。
entries.en: Now my hour has come, and there is nothing more to say.
entries.literal: Now it is fate—what more is there to say?

entries.zh: 諸公及在朝卿大夫士，軍中大小督將、軍人等，並立勳效，積有年載，輔翼太祖，成我周家。
entries.en: You dukes, ministers, and officials at court, and every commander and soldier in the armies—you have served with merit for years, supporting the Grand Progenitor and building our Zhou house.
entries.literal: You dukes, ministers, and officials at court, and every commander and soldier in the armies—you have served with merit for years, supporting the Grand Progenitor and building our Zhou house.

entries.zh: 今朕纘承大業，處萬乘之上，此乃上不負太祖，下不負朕躬，朕得啟手啟足，從先帝於地下，實無恨於心矣。
entries.en: I have inherited the great enterprise and held the throne; in that I have not failed the Grand Progenitor above nor my own duty below. I may die whole of limb and join the former emperors below with no regret.
entries.literal: Now I have continued the great enterprise and stand above the ten thousand chariots—thus above I have not failed the Grand Progenitor, below I have not failed my person; I may close my hands and feet and follow the Former Emperor beneath the earth, truly without regret in my heart.

entries.zh: 所可恨者，朕享大位，可謂四年矣，不能使政化循理，黎庶豐足，九州未一，二方猶梗，顧此懷恨，目用不瞑。
entries.en: What I regret is that in nearly four years on the throne I could not bring good order to government, make the people secure, or reunite the realm while two regions still hold out. That grief will not let me close my eyes in peace.
entries.literal: What I regret is that, enjoying the great throne for what may be called four years, I could not make government and teaching run in order, the common people rich and sufficient, the Nine Regions not yet one, two regions still blocked—and considering this I harbor regret, my eyes at daily's close will not close.

entries.zh: 唯冀仁兄冢宰，洎朕先正、先父、公卿大臣等，協和為心，勉力相勸，勿忘太祖遺志，提挈後人，朕雖沒九泉，形體不朽。
entries.en: I ask my elder brother the Chief Minister, together with the worthies who served before, my late father's ministers, and you all, to stand as one, keep one another to the task, and honor the Grand Progenitor's last wish by guiding those who come after. Though I go down to the grave, my purpose need not die with me.
entries.literal: I only hope my benevolent elder brother the Chief Minister, together with my former worthies, my late father, dukes and grand ministers and the rest, will join hearts in harmony and strive to encourage one another, not forgetting the Grand Progenitor's dying wish, to guide those who come after—though I sink into the nine springs, my form will not perish.
