entries.zh: 朕稟生儉素，非能力行菲薄，每寢大布之被，服大帛之衣，凡是器用，皆無雕刻。
entries.en: I was raised in plain ways, not from any special strength of mine; I slept under coarse cloth and wore plain silk, and kept every vessel and tool undecorated.
entries.literal: My upbringing was plain and simple—not that I could by strength practice austerity; every night I slept under coarse-cloth quilts and wore plain-silk robes; all vessels and implements had no carving whatsoever.

entries.zh: 身終之日，豈容違棄此好。
entries.en: At my death I cannot abandon that habit.
entries.literal: On the day my life ends, how could I abandon this preference?

entries.zh: 喪事所須，務從儉約，斂以時服，勿使有金玉之飾。
entries.en: Let the funeral be spare: dress me in ordinary clothes and put no gold or jade on my body.
entries.literal: What the funeral requires must follow frugality: enshroud in seasonal dress and do not let there be ornaments of gold or jade.

entries.zh: 若以禮不可闕，皆令用瓦。
entries.en: Where ritual cannot be omitted, use pottery only.
entries.literal: If ritual cannot be omitted, let everything be of pottery.

entries.zh: 小斂訖，七日哭。
entries.en: After the initial laying-out, mourn for seven days.
entries.literal: When the lesser enshrouding is complete, mourn for seven days.

entries.zh: 文武百官各權辟衰麻，且以素服從事。
entries.en: All civil and military officials shall wear mourning hemp for the time being and carry on affairs in plain dress.
entries.literal: Civil and military officials of every rank shall provisionally don hemp mourning, and for the time being attend affairs in plain dress.

entries.zh: 葬日，選擇不毛之地，因地勢為墳，勿封勿樹。
entries.en: Bury me on barren ground, shaping the grave to the terrain—no mound raised, no trees planted.
entries.literal: On the burial day, choose barren ground; according to the terrain form the mound—no sealing mound, no planted trees.

entries.zh: 且厚葬傷生，聖人所誡，朕旣服膺聖人之教，安敢違之。
entries.en: Lavish burial harms the living, and the sages warned against it. I have taken that teaching to heart and dare not break it.
entries.literal: Moreover, lavish burial harms the living—the sages warned of this; since I have taken the sages' teaching to heart, how dare I disobey it?

entries.zh: 凡百官司，勿異朕此意。
entries.en: Every office must follow this intent.
entries.literal: All the hundred offices—do not diverge from my meaning here.

entries.zh: 四方州鎮使到，各令三日哭，哭訖，悉權辟凶服，還以素服從事，待大例除。
entries.en: Envoys from the provinces and border posts shall mourn three days on arrival; when that ends, they too shall wear mourning briefly, then return to plain dress until the general rule for ending mourning.
entries.literal: When envoys from the four directions and from provinces and garrisons arrive, each shall be ordered to mourn three days; when mourning ends, all shall provisionally don mourning garb, then return to plain dress for affairs, until the great precedent for removing mourning.

entries.zh: 非有呼召，各按部自守，不得輒奔赴闕庭。
entries.en: Unless called, each man is to stay at his post and not rush to court.
entries.literal: Unless summoned, each shall remain at his post and guard it—none may rashly hurry to the court.

entries.zh: 禮有通塞隨時之義，葬訖，內外悉除服從吉。
entries.en: Rites may be tightened or relaxed as times require; once burial is done, mourning ends throughout the court and the realm.
entries.literal: Rites have the meaning of opening or closing according to the time; once the burial is complete, within and without all shall remove mourning dress and follow auspicious custom.

entries.zh: 三年之內，勿禁婚娶，飲食一令如平常也。
entries.en: For three years do not forbid marriage, and let food and drink continue as in normal times.
entries.literal: Within three years do not forbid marriage and taking wives; food and drink shall altogether be as in ordinary times.

entries.zh: 時事殷猥，病困心亂，止能及此。
entries.en: Affairs pressed hard upon me; sick and confused, I could only set down this much.
entries.literal: Affairs of the time were pressing and numerous; sick and troubled in mind, I could only reach this far.

entries.zh: 如其事有不盡，准此以類為斷。
entries.en: If anything remains unsettled, decide like cases by what is written here.
entries.literal: Should any matter remain incomplete, use this as the standard and decide similar cases thereby.

entries.zh: 死而近思，古人有之。
entries.en: The ancients spoke of reflecting hard upon death while still alive.
entries.literal: To think near thoughts upon death—the ancients had this.

entries.zh: 朕今忍死，書此懷抱。
entries.en: I now force myself to live long enough to set these thoughts down.
entries.literal: I now bear death and write down these thoughts in my bosom.

entries.zh: 九月辛卯，以大將軍楊忠、大將軍王雄並為柱國。
entries.en: Ninth month, on xinmao day, Grand Generals Yang Zhong and Wang Xiong were both made pillars-of-state.
entries.literal: In the ninth month, day xinmao, Grand Generals Yang Zhong and Wang Xiong were both made pillars-of-state.

entries.zh: 甲辰，封少師元羅為韓國公，以紹魏後。
entries.en: On jiachen day Junior Tutor Yuan Luo was enfeoffed as Duke of Han to continue the Wei line.
entries.literal: On jiachen day Junior Tutor Yuan Luo was enfeoffed as Duke of Han and appointed to continue the Wei line.

entries.zh: 丁未，幸同州。
entries.en: On dingwei day he visited Tong Province.
entries.literal: On dingwei day he visited Tong Province.

entries.zh: 過故宅，賦詩曰：「玉燭調秋氣，金輿曆舊宮。
entries.en: Passing his old home, he composed a poem: "Jade candles tune the autumn air; the gold carriage passes the old palace.
entries.literal: Passing his former residence, he composed a poem: "Jade candles adjust the autumn air, the gold carriage traverses the old palace.

entries.zh: 還如過白水，更似入新豐。
entries.en: Turning back is like crossing Baishui again; it feels even more like entering Xinfeng.
entries.literal: Returning as if crossing Baishui again, more like entering Xinfeng.

entries.zh: 霜潭漬晚菊，寒井落疏桐。
entries.en: Frosted pools steep the late chrysanthemums; a cold well sheds sparse paulownia leaves.
entries.literal: Frost pools soak the late chrysanthemums; the cold well drops sparse paulownia.

entries.zh: 舉杯延故老，令聞歌《大風》。」
entries.en: Raising his cup to old friends present, he had them sing Great Wind."
entries.literal: Raising the cup to invite old friends, he ordered them to hear the singing of Great Wind."

entries.zh: 十二月辛酉，突厥遣使獻方物。
entries.en: Twelfth month, on xinyou day, the Turks sent envoys with tribute.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, day xinyou, the Turks sent envoys presenting tribute goods.

entries.zh: 癸亥，太廟成。
entries.en: On guihai day the Imperial Ancestors' Temple was completed.
entries.literal: On guihai day the Imperial Ancestors' Temple was completed.

entries.zh: 辛巳，以功臣琅邪貞獻公賀拔勝等十三人配享太祖廟庭。
entries.en: On xinsi day thirteen meritorious ministers, including Helba Sheng, Duke of Langye Zhenxian, were granted paired sacrifice in Yuwen Tai's temple court.
entries.literal: On xinsi day thirteen meritorious ministers including Helba Sheng, Duke of Langye Zhenxian, and others were given paired sacrifice in the Grand Progenitor's temple court.

entries.zh: 壬午，大赦天下。
entries.en: On renwu day a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
entries.literal: On renywu day a general amnesty was proclaimed for the empire.

entries.zh: 冬十月癸酉，太師、趙國公李弼薨。
entries.en: In winter, on guiyou in the tenth month, Grand Tutor Li Bi, Duke of Zhao, died.
entries.literal: In winter, tenth month, on guiyou day Grand Tutor Li Bi, Duke of Zhao, died.

entries.zh: 己卯，以大將軍、昌平公尉遲綱為柱國。
entries.en: On jimao day Grand General Yuchi Gang, Duke of Changping, was made pillar of state.
entries.literal: On jimao day Grand General Yuchi Gang, Duke of Changping, was made pillar of state.

entries.zh: 乙酉，祠圓丘。
entries.en: On yiyou day he sacrificed at the Circular Mound.
entries.literal: On yiyou day sacrifice was offered at the Circular Mound.

entries.zh: 丙戌，祠方丘。
entries.en: On bingxu day he sacrificed at the Square Mound.
entries.literal: On bingxu day sacrifice was offered at the Square Mound.

entries.zh: 甲午，祠太社。
entries.en: On jiawu day he sacrificed at the Great Altar of Soil.
entries.literal: On jiawu day sacrifice was offered at the Great Altar of Soil.

entries.zh: 柱國、陽平公李遠賜死。
entries.en: Pillar-of-State Li Yuan, Duke of Yangping, was ordered to take his own life.
entries.literal: Pillar-of-State Li Yuan, Duke of Yangping, was granted death.

entries.zh: 是月，梁相陳霸先廢其主蕭方智而自立，是為陳武帝。
entries.en: That month Liang chancellor Chen Baxian deposed his ruler Xiao Fangzhi and took the throne himself as Chen Wudi.
entries.literal: That month Liang Chancellor Chen Baxian deposed his ruler Xiao Fangzhi and established himself—this was Chen Wudi.

entries.zh: 靜皇帝諱衍，後改為闡，宣帝長子也。
entries.en: Emperor Jing, taboo name Yan, later changed to Chan, was Emperor Xuan's eldest son.
entries.literal: Emperor Jing's taboo name was Yan; later it was changed to Chan; he was Emperor Xuan's eldest son.

entries.zh: 母曰朱皇后。
entries.en: His mother was Empress Zhu.
entries.literal: His mother was Empress Zhu.

entries.zh: 建德二年六月，生於東宮。
entries.en: In the sixth month of Jiande year two he was born in the Eastern Palace.
entries.literal: In the sixth month of Jiande year two he was born in the Eastern Palace.

entries.zh: 大象元年正月癸卯，封魯王。
entries.en: In the first month of Daxiang year one, on guimao day, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Lu.
entries.literal: In the first month of Daxiang year one, on guimao day, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Lu.

entries.zh: 戊午，立為皇太子。
entries.en: On wuwu day he was installed as crown prince.
entries.literal: On wuwu day he was installed as crown prince.

entries.zh: 二月辛巳，宣帝於鄴宮傳位授帝，居正陽宮。
entries.en: In the second month, on xinsi day, Emperor Xuan at Ye palace transmitted the throne to Emperor Jing, who took residence at Zhengyang Palace.
entries.literal: In the second month, on xinsi day, Emperor Xuan at Ye palace transmitted the throne to the emperor, who dwelt in Zhengyang Palace.

entries.zh: 二年夏五月乙未，宣帝寢疾，詔帝入宿於露門學。
entries.en: Second year, fifth month of summer, on yiwei day, Emperor Xuan fell gravely ill and ordered Emperor Jing to lodge at the Lumen Gate Academy.
entries.literal: Second year, fifth month of summer, on yiwei day, Emperor Xuan fell gravely ill and ordered the emperor to enter and lodge at the Lumen Gate Academy.

entries.zh: 己酉，宣帝崩，帝入居天臺，廢正陽宮。
entries.en: On jiyou day Emperor Xuan died; Emperor Jing moved into the Celestial Terrace and Zhengyang Palace was abolished.
entries.literal: On jiyou day Emperor Xuan died; the emperor entered and took up residence at the Celestial Terrace, and Zhengyang Palace was abolished.

entries.zh: 大赦天下，停洛陽宮作。
entries.en: A general amnesty was proclaimed; work on the Luoyang palace was halted.
entries.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed for all under Heaven; construction of the Luoyang palace was halted.

entries.zh: 庚戌，上天元上皇太后尊號為太皇太后。
entries.en: On gengxu day the Tianyuan Upper Empress Dowager was honored as Grand Empress Dowager.
entries.literal: On gengxu day the Tianyuan Upper Empress Dowager was honored with the title Grand Empress Dowager.

entries.zh: 天元聖皇太后李氏為太帝太后，天元大皇后楊氏為皇太后，天大皇后朱氏為帝太后。
entries.en: Tianyuan Sage Empress Dowager Lady Li was made Grand Imperial Empress Dowager; Tianyuan Grand Empress Yang was made empress dowager; and Tian Grand Empress Zhu was made imperial empress dowager.
entries.literal: Tianyuan Sage Empress Dowager Lady Li was made Grand Imperial Empress Dowager; Tianyuan Grand Empress Yang was made empress dowager; and Tian Grand Empress Zhu was made imperial empress dowager.

entries.zh: 其天中大皇后陳氏、天右大皇后元氏、天左大皇后尉遲氏竝出俗為尼。
entries.en: Tian Central Grand Empress Chen, Tian Right Grand Empress Yuan, and Tian Left Grand Empress Yuchi were all released from the palace and became nuns.
entries.literal: Tian Central Grand Empress Chen, Tian Right Grand Empress Yuan, and Tian Left Grand Empress Yuchi were all released from the palace and became nuns.

entries.zh: 柱國、漢王贊為上柱國、右大丞相，上柱國、揚州總管、隨國公楊堅為假黃鉞、左大丞相，柱國、秦王贄為上柱國。
entries.en: Pillar-of-State Yuwen Zan, Prince of Han, was made superior pillar-of-state and right grand chancellor; Superior Pillar-of-State Yang Jian, Duke of Sui and inspector-general of Yang Province, received acting yellow battle-axe and was made left grand chancellor; and Pillar-of-State Yuwen Bi, Prince of Qin, was made superior pillar-of-state.
entries.literal: Pillar-of-State Yuwen Zan, Prince of Han, was made superior pillar-of-state and right grand chancellor; Superior Pillar-of-State Yang Jian, Duke of Sui and inspector-general of Yang Province, was given acting yellow battle-axe and made left grand chancellor; and Pillar-of-State Yuwen Bi, Prince of Qin, was made superior pillar-of-state.

entries.zh: 帝居諒闇，百官總己以聽於左大丞相。
entries.en: Emperor Jing observed mourning seclusion; the hundred offices entrusted all affairs to the left grand chancellor.
entries.literal: The emperor dwelt in mourning seclusion; the hundred offices entrusted their affairs to the left grand chancellor.

entries.zh: 壬子，以上柱國、鄖國公韋孝寬為相州總管。
entries.en: On renzi day Superior Pillar-of-State Wei Xiaokuan, Duke of Yun, was made inspector-general of Xiang Province.
entries.literal: On renzi day Superior Pillar-of-State Wei Xiaokuan, Duke of Yun, was made inspector-general of Xiang Province.

entries.zh: 罷入市稅錢。
entries.en: The market-entry tax coin was abolished.
entries.literal: Market-entry tax coin was abolished.

entries.zh: 隋氏奉帝為介國公，邑萬戶，車服禮樂一如周制，上書不為表，答表不稱詔。
entries.en: The Sui installed Emperor Jing as Duke of Jie with a fief of ten thousand households; chariots, robes, rites, and music were all as under the Zhou system; documents sent upward were not called memorials, and replies to memorials were not called edicts.
entries.literal: The Sui installed the emperor as Duke of Jie with a fief of ten thousand households; chariots, robes, rites, and music were all as under the Zhou system; documents sent upward were not called memorials, and replies to memorials were not called edicts.

entries.zh: 有其文，事竟不行。
entries.en: There was such a text, but the matter in the end was not carried out.
entries.literal: There was such a text, but the matter in the end was not carried out.

entries.zh: 開皇元年五月壬申，崩，時年九歲，隋志也。
entries.en: On renshen day in the fifth month of Kaihuang year 1 he died, aged nine according to Sui records.
entries.literal: On renshen day in the fifth month of Kaihuang year 1 he died, aged nine according to Sui records.

entries.zh: 諡曰靜皇帝，葬恭陵。
entries.en: He was posthumously titled Emperor Jing and buried at Gongling.
entries.literal: His posthumous title was Emperor Jing; he was buried at Gongling.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：靜帝越自幼沖，紹茲衰緒。
entries.en: The historian writes: Emperor Jing, still in early childhood, took up this declining succession.
entries.literal: The historian writes: Emperor Jing, still in early childhood, took up this declining succession.

entries.zh: 內相挾孫、劉之詐，戚藩無齊、代之強。
entries.en: Inner ministers wielded the craft of Sun and Liu; among the imperial princes there was none with Qi or Dai's strength.
entries.literal: Inner ministers wielded the craft of Sun and Liu; among the imperial princes there was none with Qi or Dai's strength.

entries.zh: 隋氏因之，遂遷龜鼎。
entries.en: The Sui seized upon this and moved the sacred vessel.
entries.literal: The Sui seized upon this and moved the sacred vessel.

entries.zh: 雖復岷峨投袂，翻成陵奪之威；
entries.en: Though men of Min and E threw up their sleeves in anger, it turned only into the usurper's power over the tomb;
entries.literal: Though men of Min and E threw up their sleeves in anger, it turned only into the usurper's power over the tomb;

entries.zh: 漳滏勤王，無救宗周之殞。
entries.en: Though loyalists rallied at Zhang and Fu, they could not save Zong Zhou from its fall.
entries.literal: Though loyalists rallied at Zhang and Fu, they could not save Zong Zhou from its fall.

entries.zh: 嗚呼，以太祖之克隆景業，未踰二紀，不祀忽諸。
entries.en: Alas! Grand Progenitor's great flourishing enterprise had not lasted two generations before sacrifices suddenly ceased.
entries.literal: Alas! Grand Progenitor's great flourishing enterprise had not lasted two generations before sacrifices suddenly ceased.

entries.zh: 斯蓋宣帝之餘殃，非孺子之罪戾也。
entries.en: This was surely the baleful aftermath of Emperor Xuan, not the young emperor's fault.
entries.literal: This was surely the baleful aftermath of Emperor Xuan, not the young emperor's fault.

entries.zh: 二月庚申，大丞相、隨王楊堅為相國，總百揆，更封十郡，通前二十郡，劍履上殿，入朝不趨，贊拜不名，備九錫之禮，加璽、鉞、遠遊冠，相國印綠綟綬，位在諸王上。
entries.en: Second month, on gengshen day, Grand Chancellor Yang Jian, Prince of Sui, was made chancellor of state and directed all affairs; ten more commanderies were enfeoffed, twenty in all together with the former; he was granted entry to the hall with sword and shoes, no need to hasten when entering court, no naming when assisting at obeisance, and the full rites of the nine bestowments; he received the seal, battle-axe, and cap of distant travel; the chancellor's seal with green-black sash; and his rank was placed above all princes.
entries.literal: Second month, on gengshen day, Grand Chancellor Yang Jian, Prince of Sui, was made chancellor of state and directed all affairs; ten more commanderies were enfeoffed, twenty in all together with the former; he was granted entry to the hall with sword and shoes, no need to hasten when entering court, no naming when assisting at obeisance, and the full rites of the nine bestowments; he received the seal, battle-axe, and cap of distant travel; the chancellor's seal with green-black sash; and his rank was placed above all princes.

entries.zh: 又加冕十有二旒，建天子旌旗，出警入蹕，乘金根車，駕六馬，備五時副車，置旄頭雲罕，樂舞八佾，設鐘虛宮懸。
entries.en: He was further given a twelve-tassel crown, imperial banners and flags, guards when going out and clearance when entering, the golden root chariot drawn by six horses, auxiliary chariots for the five seasons, yak-tail banner and cloud net, eight rows of music and dancers, and bell chimes set in the suspended palace orchestra.
entries.literal: He was further given a twelve-tassel crown, imperial banners and flags, guards when going out and clearance when entering, the golden root chariot drawn by six horses, auxiliary chariots for the five seasons, yak-tail banner and cloud net, eight rows of music and dancers, and bell chimes set in the suspended palace orchestra.

entries.zh: 王后、王子爵命之號，竝依魏晉故事。
entries.en: The titles and commands of queen, princes, and nobles all followed Wei and Jin precedent.
entries.literal: The titles and commands of queen, princes, and nobles all followed Wei and Jin precedent.

entries.zh: 甲子，隨王楊堅稱尊號，帝遜于別宮。
entries.en: On jiazi day Yang Jian, Prince of Sui, proclaimed his exalted title; Emperor Jing abdicated to a separate palace.
entries.literal: On jiazi day Yang Jian, Prince of Sui, proclaimed his exalted title; Emperor Jing abdicated to a separate palace.

entries.zh: 大定元年春正月壬午，詔曰：「朕以不天，夙遭極罰。
entries.en: Spring, first month, on renwu day of Dading year 1, an edict said: "I, bereft of Heaven, early suffered deepest loss.
entries.literal: Spring, first month, on renwu day of Dading year 1, an edict said: "I, bereft of Heaven, early suffered deepest loss.

entries.zh: 光陰遄速，遽及此辰。
entries.en: Light and shadow race past, and suddenly this moment has come.
entries.literal: Light and shadow race past, and suddenly this moment has come.

entries.zh: 窮慕纏綿，言增號絕。
entries.en: Grief boundless and unending, words fail and cries cease.
entries.literal: Grief boundless and unending, words fail and cries cease.

entries.zh: 踰祀革號，憲章前典，可改大象三年為大定元年。」
entries.en: Crossing the mourning period and changing the reign title, following former canons—Daxiang year 3 may be changed to Dading year 1."
entries.literal: Crossing the mourning period and changing the reign title, following former canons—Daxiang year 3 may be changed to Dading year 1."

entries.zh: 乙酉，歲星逆行，守右執法；
entries.en: On yiyou day Jupiter retrograded and guarded the Right Law-Enforcer;
entries.literal: On yiyou day Jupiter retrograded and guarded the Right Law-Enforcer;

entries.zh: 熒惑掩房北第一星。
entries.en: Mars concealed the first northern star of the Room.
entries.literal: Mars concealed the first northern star of the Room.

entries.zh: 丙戌，詔曰：「帝王設官，惟才是務，人臣報國，薦賢為重。
entries.en: On bingxu day an edict said: "Emperors and kings establish offices with talent as the sole concern; ministers serve the state, and recommending the worthy is paramount.
entries.literal: On bingxu day an edict said: "Emperors and kings establish offices with talent as the sole concern; ministers serve the state, and recommending the worthy is paramount.

entries.zh: 去歲已來，屢有妖寇，宰臣英算，咸得清蕩。
entries.en: Since last year bandits have repeatedly risen; chief ministers with heroic plans have all cleared and pacified them.
entries.literal: Since last year bandits have repeatedly risen; chief ministers with heroic plans have all cleared and pacified them.

entries.zh: 逆亂之後，兵車始朅，遐邇勞役，生民未康。
entries.en: After the rebellion, war-chariots have only just ceased; near and far corvée labor continues, and the people are not yet at ease.
entries.literal: After the rebellion, war-chariots have only just ceased; near and far corvée labor continues, and the people are not yet at ease.

entries.zh: 居官之徒，致治者寡。
entries.en: Those holding office who achieve good governance are few.
entries.literal: Those holding office who achieve good governance are few.

entries.zh: 斯故上失其道，以至於茲，亦由下有幽人，未展其力。
entries.en: This is because above the Way was lost, reaching to this point; it is also because below there are recluses whose power has not yet been deployed.
entries.literal: This is because above the Way was lost, reaching to this point; it is also because below there are recluses whose power has not yet been deployed.

entries.zh: 今四海寧一，八表無塵，元輔執鈞，垂風揚化。
entries.en: Now the four seas are tranquil and united; the eight directions are without disturbance; the chief minister holds authority and spreads transforming influence.
entries.literal: Now the four seas are tranquil and united; the eight directions are without disturbance; the chief minister holds authority and spreads transforming influence.

entries.zh: 若使天下英傑，盡升於朝，銓衡陟降，量才而處，垂拱無為，庶幾可至。」
entries.en: If all the realm's heroes were raised to court, balances of office promoted and demoted them, talents measured and placed—folding the arms and acting without exertion—perhaps that state might nearly be reached."
entries.literal: If all the realm's heroes were raised to court, balances of office promoted and demoted them, talents measured and placed—folding the arms and acting without exertion—perhaps that state might nearly be reached."

entries.zh: 於是遣戎秩上開府以上，職事下大夫以上，外官刺史以上，各舉清平勤幹者三人。
entries.en: Thereupon officials of military rank superintending grand prefecture and above, office-holders assistant grandee and above, and external officials provincial governor and above were each to recommend three men of purity, fairness, diligence, and competence.
entries.literal: Thereupon officials of military rank superintending grand prefecture and above, office-holders assistant grandee and above, and external officials provincial governor and above were each to recommend three men of purity, fairness, diligence, and competence.

entries.zh: 被舉之人，居官三年有功過者，所舉之人，隨加賞罰。
entries.en: For those recommended, after three years in office with merit or fault, the recommender would be rewarded or punished accordingly.
entries.literal: For those recommended, after three years in office with merit or fault, the recommender would be rewarded or punished accordingly.

entries.zh: 以大司馬、長寧公楊勇為洛州總管。
entries.en: Grand Marshal Yang Yong, Duke of Changning, was made inspector-general of Luo Province.
entries.literal: Grand Marshal Yang Yong, Duke of Changning, was made inspector-general of Luo Province.

entries.zh: 秋七月甲申，突厥送齊范陽王高紹義。
entries.en: Seventh month, on jiashen day, the Turks delivered Gao Shaoyi, Prince of Fanyang of Northern Qi.
entries.literal: Seventh month, on jiashen day, the Turks delivered Gao Shaoyi, Prince of Fanyang of Northern Qi.

entries.zh: 庚寅，申州刺史李慧起兵。
entries.en: On gengyin day Li Hui, inspector of Shen Province, raised troops in rebellion.
entries.literal: On gengyin day Li Hui, inspector of Shen Province, raised troops.

entries.zh: 辛卯，月掩氐東南星。
entries.en: On xinmao day the moon encroached upon the southeastern star of Di.
entries.literal: On xinmao day the moon encroached upon the southeastern star of Di.

entries.zh: 甲午，月掩南斗第六星。
entries.en: On jiawu day the moon encroached upon the sixth star of the Southern Dipper.
entries.literal: On jiawu day the moon encroached upon the sixth star of the Southern Dipper.

entries.zh: 庚子，詔趙、陳、越、代、滕五王入朝不趨，劍履上殿。
entries.en: On gengzi day an edict granted Princes Zhao, Chen, Yue, Dai, and Teng exemption from hurrying at court and permission to wear sword and shoes in the palace audience.
entries.literal: On gengzi day an edict granted Princes Zhao, Chen, Yue, Dai, and Teng exemption from hurrying at court approach and permission to wear sword and shoes in the palace audience.

entries.zh: 滎州刺史、邵國公宇文冑舉兵，遣大將軍、清河公楊素討之。
entries.en: Yuwen Zhou, Duke of Shao and inspector of Xing Province, raised troops; Grand General Yang Su, Duke of Qinghe, was sent to suppress him.
entries.literal: Yuwen Zhou, Duke of Shao and inspector of Xing Province, raised troops; Grand General Yang Su, Duke of Qinghe, was dispatched to attack him.

entries.zh: 青州總管尉遲勤舉兵。
entries.en: Yuchi Qin, inspector-general of Qing Province, raised troops in rebellion.
entries.literal: Inspector-General of Qing Province Yuchi Qin raised troops.

entries.zh: 丁未，隨公楊堅為都督內外諸軍事。
entries.en: On dingwei day Yang Jian, Duke of Sui, was made commander-in-chief of all military affairs at home and abroad.
entries.literal: On dingwei day Duke of Sui Yang Jian was made commander-in-chief of all military affairs at home and abroad.

entries.zh: 己酉，䢵州總管司馬消難舉兵，以柱國、楊國公王誼為行軍元帥，率軍討之。
entries.en: On jiyou day Sima Xiaonan, inspector-general of Ying Province, raised troops; Pillar-of-State Wang Yi, Duke of Yang, was made campaign commander and led troops to suppress him.
entries.literal: On jiyou day Inspector-General of Ying Province Sima Xiaonan raised troops; Pillar-of-State Wang Yi, Duke of Yang, was made campaign commander and led troops to attack him.

entries.zh: 壬子，歲星與太白合于張，有流星大如斗，出五
entries.en: On renzi day Jupiter and Venus conjoined at Zhang; a meteor as large as a dipper appeared from Wu
entries.literal: On renzi day Jupiter and Venus conjoined at Zhang; a meteor as large as a dipper appeared from Wu

entries.en: (Jun)
entries.literal: (Jun)

entries.zh: 車，東北流，光明燭地。
entries.en: Che, flowing northeast, its light illuminating the earth.
entries.literal: Che, flowing northeast, its light illuminating the earth.

entries.zh: 趙王招、越王盛以謀執政被誅。
entries.en: Yuwen Zhao, Prince of Zhao, and Yuwen Sheng, Prince of Yue, were executed for plotting to seize power.
entries.literal: Yuwen Zhao, Prince of Zhao, and Yuwen Sheng, Prince of Yue, were executed for plotting to seize the government.

entries.zh: 癸丑，封皇弟術為鄴王，衎為郢王。
entries.en: On guichou day the emperor's younger brother Shu was enfeoffed as Prince of Ye and Kan as Prince of Ying.
entries.literal: On guichou day the emperor's younger brother Shu was enfeoffed as Prince of Ye, and Kan as Prince of Ying.

entries.zh: 是月，豫州、荊州、襄州三總管內諸蠻，各率種落反，焚燒村驛，攻亂郡縣。
entries.en: That month within the inspectorates of Yu, Jing, and Xiang provinces various Man tribes each led their clans in revolt, burning villages and post stations and attacking commanderies and counties.
entries.literal: That month within the inspectorates of Yu, Jing, and Xiang provinces various Man tribes each led their clans in revolt, burning villages and post stations and attacking and disordering commanderies and counties.

entries.zh: 九月甲申，熒惑與歲星合於翼。
entries.en: Ninth month, on jiashen day, Mars and Jupiter conjoined at Wings.
entries.literal: Ninth month, on jiashen day, Mars and Jupiter conjoined at Wings.

entries.zh: 丙戌，廢河陽總管為鎮，隸洛州。
entries.en: On bingxu day the Heyang inspector-generalate was abolished and made a garrison subordinate to Luo Province.
entries.literal: On bingxu day the Heyang inspector-generalate was abolished and made a garrison subordinate to Luo Province.

entries.zh: 以小宗伯、竟陵公
entries.en: Junior director of ancestral sacrifices, Duke of Jingling
entries.literal: Junior director of ancestral sacrifices, Duke of Jingling

entries.en: (Yang)
entries.literal: (Yang)

entries.zh: 楊慧為大宗伯。
entries.en: Yang Hui was made grand director of ancestral sacrifices.
entries.literal: Yang Hui was made grand director of ancestral sacrifices.

entries.zh: 壬辰，廢皇后司馬氏為庶人。
entries.en: On renchen day Empress Sima was deposed and reduced to commoner status.
entries.literal: On renchen day Empress Sima was deposed and made a commoner.

entries.zh: 甲午，熒惑入太微。
entries.en: On jiawu day Mars entered the Supreme Palace.
entries.literal: On jiawu day Mars entered the Supreme Palace.

entries.zh: 戊戌，以柱國、楊國公王誼為上柱國。
entries.en: On wuxu day Pillar-of-State Wang Yi, Duke of Yang, was made superior pillar-of-state.
entries.literal: On wuxu day Pillar-of-State Wang Yi, Duke of Yang, was made superior pillar-of-state.

entries.zh: 辛丑，分潼州管內新遂普合及瀘州管內瀘戎六州竝隸信州總管府。
entries.en: On xinchou day the prefectures of Xin, Sui, Pu, and He within Tong Province and the prefectures of Lu and Rong within Lu Province were all placed under the Xin Province inspector-generalate.
entries.literal: On xinchou day the prefectures of Xin, Sui, Pu, and He within Tong Province and the prefectures of Lu and Rong within Lu Province were all placed under the inspector-generalate of Xin Province.

entries.zh: 己酉，熒惑犯左執法。
entries.en: On jiyou day Mars encroached upon the Left Law-Enforcer.
entries.literal: On jiyou day Mars encroached upon the Left Law-Enforcer.

entries.zh: 庚戌，以柱國常山公于翼、化政公宇文忻竝為上柱國。
entries.en: On gengxu day Pillar-of-State Yu Yi, Duke of Changshan, and Yuwen Xin, Duke of Huazheng, were both made superior pillars-of-state.
entries.literal: On gengxu day Pillar-of-State Yu Yi, Duke of Changshan, and Yuwen Xin, Duke of Huazheng, were both made superior pillars-of-state.

entries.zh: 進封翼為任國公，忻為英國公。
entries.en: Yu Yi was promoted to Duke of Ren; Yuwen Xin was promoted to Duke of Ying.
entries.literal: Yu Yi was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Ren; Yuwen Xin was advanced to Duke of Ying.

entries.zh: 壬子，丞相去左右之號，隨公楊堅為大丞相。
entries.en: On renzi day the titles of left and right were removed from grand chancellor; Yang Jian, Duke of Sui, was made grand chancellor.
entries.literal: On renzi day the titles of left and right were removed from grand chancellor; Duke of Sui Yang Jian was made grand chancellor.

entries.zh: 八月庚申，益州總管王謙舉兵不受代，即以梁睿為行軍元帥，率軍討之。
entries.en: Eighth month, on gengshen day Wang Qian, inspector-general of Yi Province, raised troops and refused to be replaced; Liang Rui was immediately made campaign commander and led troops to suppress him.
entries.literal: Eighth month, on gengshen day Inspector-General of Yi Province Wang Qian raised troops and refused to relinquish his post; Liang Rui was immediately made campaign commander and led troops to attack him.

entries.zh: 丁卯，封上柱國、枹罕公辛威為宿國公，開府怡昂為鄯國公。
entries.en: On dingmao day Superior Pillar-of-State Xin Wei, Duke of Baohan, was enfeoffed as Duke of Su; and Kai Fu Yi Ang was enfeoffed as Duke of Shan.
entries.literal: On dingmao day Superior Pillar-of-State Xin Wei, Duke of Baohan, was enfeoffed as Duke of Su; and Kai Fu Yi Ang was enfeoffed as Duke of Shan.

entries.zh: 庚午，韋孝寬破尉遲迥於鄴城，迥自殺，相州平。
entries.en: On gengwu day Wei Xiaokuan defeated Yuchi Jiong at Ye city; Jiong killed himself and Xiang Province was pacified.
entries.literal: On gengwu day Wei Xiaokuan defeated Yuchi Jiong at Ye city; Jiong killed himself and Xiang Province was pacified.

entries.zh: 移相州於安陽，其鄴城及邑居皆毀廢之。
entries.en: Xiang Province was moved to Anyang; Ye city and its settlements were all destroyed and abandoned.
entries.literal: Xiang Province was moved to Anyang; Ye city and its settlements were all destroyed and abandoned.

entries.zh: 分相州陽平郡置毛州，昌黎郡置魏州。
entries.en: From Xiang Province, Yangping commandery was split off to establish Mao Province; Changli commandery was split off to establish Wei Province.
entries.literal: From Xiang Province, Yangping commandery was split off to establish Mao Province; Changli commandery was split off to establish Wei Province.

entries.zh: 丙子，以漢王贊為太師，上柱國并州總管申國公李穆為太傅，宋王實為大前疑，秦王贄為大右弼，燕國公于寔為大左輔。
entries.en: On bingzi day Yuwen Zan, Prince of Han, was made grand preceptor; Superior Pillar-of-State Li Mu, Duke of Shen and inspector-general of Bing Province, grand tutor; Yuwen Shi, Prince of Song, grand front advisor; Yuwen Bi, Prince of Qin, grand right assistant; and Yu Shi, Duke of Yan, grand left assistant.
entries.literal: On bingzi day Yuwen Zan, Prince of Han, was made grand preceptor; Superior Pillar-of-State Li Mu, Duke of Shen and inspector-general of Bing Province, grand tutor; Yuwen Shi, Prince of Song, grand front advisor; Yuwen Bi, Prince of Qin, grand right assistant; and Yu Shi, Duke of Yan, grand left assistant.

entries.zh: 己卯，詔曰：
entries.en: On jimao day an edict said:
entries.literal: On jimao day an edict said:

entries.zh: 朕祗承洪業，二載於茲。
entries.en: I reverently inherit the great enterprise; two years have now passed.
entries.literal: I reverently inherit the great enterprise; two years have now passed.

entries.zh: 藉祖考之休，憑宰輔之力，經天緯地，四海晏如。
entries.en: Relying on the blessing of forefathers and ancestors, and leaning on the strength of chief ministers, we align Heaven and earth and the four seas are tranquil.
entries.literal: Relying on the blessing of forefathers and ancestors, and leaning on the strength of chief ministers, we align Heaven and earth and the four seas are tranquil.

entries.zh: 逆賊尉遲迥，才質凡庸，志懷奸慝，因緣戚屬，位冠朝倫。
entries.en: The rebel Yuchi Jiong, talent and quality commonplace, heart harboring treacherous wickedness, leveraged kinship ties, and his rank stood above the court.
entries.literal: The rebel Yuchi Jiong, talent and quality commonplace, heart harboring treacherous wickedness, leveraged kinship ties, and his rank stood above the court.

entries.zh: 屬上天降禍，先皇晏駕，萬國深鼎湖之痛，四海窮遏密之悲。
entries.en: Just when Heaven sent disaster and the late emperor passed away, the myriad states felt deeply the pain of Ding Lake; the four seas exhausted their grief at the prohibition of speech.
entries.literal: Just when Heaven sent disaster and the late emperor passed away, the myriad states felt deeply the pain of Ding Lake; the four seas exhausted their grief at the prohibition of speech.

entries.zh: 獨幸天災，欣然放命，稱兵擁衆，便懷問鼎。
entries.en: Alone taking advantage of heaven's disaster, he joyfully cast off restraint, raised troops and gathered masses, and at once harbored intent to seize the throne.
entries.literal: Alone taking advantage of heaven's disaster, he joyfully relinquished restraint, raised troops and gathered masses, and at once harbored intent to seize the throne.

entries.zh: 乃詔六師，肅茲九伐，而凶徒孔熾，充原蔽野。
entries.en: Thereupon the six armies were ordered, and the nine punitive campaigns were solemnly undertaken; yet the wicked band was exceedingly fierce and filled the plains, covering the wilds.
entries.literal: Thereupon the six armies were ordered, and the nine punitive campaigns were solemnly undertaken; yet the wicked band was exceedingly fierce and filled the plains, covering the wilds.

entries.zh: 諸將肆雷霆之威，壯士縱貔貅之勢，芟夷縈拂，所在如莽，直指漳濱，擒斬元惡，讐醜喪魄，咸集鼓下。
entries.en: Generals unleashed the might of thunder; brave warriors let loose the momentum of tiger-leopards; cutting down and sweeping away, wherever they reached it was like clearing scrub—pressing straight to the Zhang riverside, capturing and beheading the chief villain; the wicked horde lost their souls and all gathered beneath the war drums.
entries.literal: Generals unleashed the might of thunder; brave warriors let loose the momentum of tiger-leopards; cutting down and sweeping away, wherever they reached it was like clearing scrub—pressing straight to the Zhang riverside, capturing and beheading the chief villain; the wicked horde lost their souls and all gathered beneath the war drums.

entries.zh: 順高秋之氣，就上天之誅，兩河妖孽，一朝清蕩。
entries.en: Following the spirit of deep autumn, submitting to heaven's punishment, the demonic spawn of the two rivers were in one morning swept clean.
entries.literal: Following the spirit of deep autumn, submitting to heaven's punishment, the demonic spawn of the two rivers were in one morning swept clean.

entries.zh: 自朝及野，喜抃相趨。
entries.en: From court to countryside, joy and applause converged.
entries.literal: From court to countryside, joy and applause converged.

entries.zh: 昔上皇之時，不言為治，聖人宰物，有教而已。
entries.en: In former times during the Retired Sovereign's era, he did not speak yet achieved governance; the sage rules the world through teaching alone.
entries.literal: In former times during the Retired Sovereign's era, he did not speak yet achieved governance; the sage rules the world through teaching alone.

entries.zh: 未戢干戈，實深慚德。
entries.en: War has not yet been laid aside; this truly deepens shame for our virtue.
entries.literal: War has not yet been laid aside; this truly deepens shame for our virtue.

entries.zh: 思弘寬簡之政，用副億兆之心，可大赦天下。
entries.en: We wish to spread broad and simple government, to match the hearts of the hundred millions; a great amnesty is proclaimed for all under Heaven.
entries.literal: We wish to spread broad and simple government, to match the hearts of the hundred millions; a great amnesty is proclaimed for all under Heaven.

entries.zh: 其共迥元謀，執迷不悟，及迥子侄，逆人司馬消難、王謙等，不在赦例。
entries.en: Those who originally conspired with Jiong, clung to error without awakening, and Jiong's sons and nephews, and the rebels Sima Xiaonan, Wang Qian, and others, are not within the amnesty.
entries.literal: Those who originally conspired with Jiong, clung to error without awakening, and Jiong's sons and nephews, and the rebels Sima Xiaonan, Wang Qian, and others, are not within the amnesty.

entries.zh: 十二月壬子，以柱國、蔣國公梁睿為上柱國。
entries.en: Twelfth month, on renzi day, Pillar-of-State Liang Rui, Duke of Jiang, was made superior pillar-of-state.
entries.literal: Twelfth month, on renzi day, Pillar-of-State Liang Rui, Duke of Jiang, was made superior pillar-of-state.

entries.zh: 癸丑，熒惑入氐。
entries.en: On guichou day Mars entered Di.
entries.literal: On guichou day Mars entered Di.

entries.zh: 丁巳，以柱國邗國公楊雄、
entries.en: On dingsi day Pillar-of-State Yang Xiong, Duke of Hang,
entries.literal: On dingsi day Pillar-of-State Yang Xiong, Duke of Hang,

entries.en: (Wei)
entries.literal: (Wei)

entries.zh: 普安公賀蘭暮、郕國公梁士彥、上大將軍新
entries.en: Helan Mu, Duke of Pu'an; Liang Shiyan, Duke of Xi; Grand General Xin
entries.literal: Pu'an Gong Helan Mu, Duke of Xi State Liang Shiyan, Grand General Xin

entries.en: (An)
entries.literal: (An)

entries.zh: 寧公叱列長
entries.en: Ning Gong Chilü Chang
entries.literal: Ning Gong Chilü Chang

entries.en: (Wen)
entries.literal: (Wen)

entries.zh: 釜、武鄉公崔弘度、大將軍中山公宇文恩、濮陽公宇文述、渭原公和幹子、任城公王景、漁陽公楊銳、上開府廣宗公李崇、隴西公李詢竝為上柱國。
entries.en: Fu, Cui Hongdu, Duke of Wuxiang; Yuwen En, Grand General and Duke of Zhongshan; Yuwen Shu, Duke of Puyang; He Ganzhi, Duke of Weiyuan; Wang Jing, Duke of Rencheng; Yang Rui, Duke of Yuyang; Li Chong, Shang Kai Fu and Duke of Guangzong; and Li Xun, Duke of Longxi, were all made superior pillars-of-state.
entries.literal: Fu, Wuxiang Gong Cui Hongdu, Grand General Zhongshan Gong Yuwen En, Puyang Gong Yuwen Shu, Weiyuan Gong He Ganzhi, Rencheng Gong Wang Jing, Yuyang Gong Yang Rui, Shang Kai Fu Guangzong Gong Li Chong, and Longxi Gong Li Xun were all made superior pillars-of-state.

entries.zh: 庚申，以柱國、楚國公豆盧勣為上柱國。
entries.en: On gengshen day Pillar-of-State Doulu Ji, Duke of Chu, was made superior pillar-of-state.
entries.literal: On gengshen day Pillar-of-State Doulu Ji, Duke of Chu, was made superior pillar-of-state.

entries.zh: 癸亥，詔曰：「《詩》稱『不如同姓』，《傳》曰『異姓為後』。
entries.en: On guihai day an edict said: "The 《Poetry》 says, 'Nothing equals those of the same surname,' and the 《Commentary》 says, 'Those of different surnames serve as heirs.'
entries.literal: On guihai day an edict said: "The 《Poetry》 says, 'Nothing equals those of the same surname,' and the 《Commentary》 says, 'Those of different surnames serve as heirs.'

entries.zh: 蓋明辯親疏，皎然不雜。
entries.en: It is to clarify near and distant kin, bright and unmixed.
entries.literal: For it clarifies near and distant kin, bright and unmixed.

entries.zh: 太祖受命，龍德猶潛。
entries.en: When Grand Progenitor received the mandate, dragon virtue was still concealed.
entries.literal: When Grand Progenitor received the mandate, dragon virtue was still concealed.

entries.zh: 籙表革代之文，星垂除舊之象，三分天下，志扶魏室，多所改作，冀允上玄。
entries.en: The [He] River chart showed texts of dynastic change; stars displayed omens of removing the old; dividing the realm in three parts, he intended to support the Wei house, making many reforms in hope of accord with high Heaven.
entries.literal: The [He] River chart showed texts of dynastic change; stars displayed omens of removing the old; dividing the realm in three parts, he intended to support the Wei house, making many reforms in hope of accord with high Heaven.

entries.zh: 文武讐官，賜姓者衆，本殊國邑，實乖胙土。
entries.en: Civil and military officials given surnames were many; their original states and fiefs differed, contrary to the principle of enfeoffment.
entries.literal: Civil and military officials given surnames were many; their original states and fiefs differed, contrary to the principle of enfeoffment.

entries.zh: 不歆非類，異骨肉而共烝嘗；
entries.en: One does not offer sacrifices to non-kin; different flesh-and-blood now share joint offerings;
entries.literal: One does not offer sacrifices to non-kin; different flesh-and-blood now share joint offerings;

entries.zh: 不愛其親，在行路而敘昭穆。
entries.en: One does not honor one's kin; on the road senior and junior are set in order.
entries.literal: One does not honor one's kin; on the road senior and junior are set in order.

entries.zh: 且神徵革姓，本為曆數有歸；
entries.en: Moreover, divine signs of changing surnames were originally because the dynastic term had a destination;
entries.literal: Moreover, divine signs of changing surnames were originally because the dynastic term had a destination;

entries.zh: 天命在人，推讓終而弗獲。
entries.en: Heaven's mandate lies with men; yielding at the end was never obtained.
entries.literal: Heaven's mandate lies with men; yielding at the end was never obtained.

entries.zh: 故君臨區宇，累世於茲。
entries.en: Therefore rulers have presided over the realm, generation after generation here.
entries.literal: Therefore rulers have presided over the realm, generation after generation here.

entries.zh: 不可仍遵謙挹之旨，久行權宜之制。
entries.en: We cannot still follow humble yielding, nor long maintain expedient measures.
entries.literal: We cannot still follow humble yielding, nor long maintain expedient measures.

entries.zh: 諸改姓者，悉宜復舊。」
entries.en: All who changed surnames should entirely restore their former ones."
entries.literal: All who changed surnames should entirely restore their former ones."

entries.zh: 甲子，大丞相、隨國公楊堅進爵為王，以十郡為國。
entries.en: On jiazi day Grand Chancellor Yang Jian, Duke of Sui, was advanced in rank to prince, with ten commanderies as his state.
entries.literal: On jiazi day Grand Chancellor Yang Jian, Duke of Sui, was advanced in rank to prince, with ten commanderies as his state.

entries.zh: 辛未，代王達、滕王逌竝以謀執政被誅。
entries.en: On xinwei day Yuwen Da, Prince of Dai, and Yuwen You, Prince of Teng, were both executed for plotting to seize power.
entries.literal: On xinwei day Yuwen Da, Prince of Dai, and Yuwen You, Prince of Teng, were both executed for plotting to seize power.

entries.zh: 壬申，以大將軍、長寧公楊勇為上柱國、大司馬，小冢宰、始平西元孝矩為大司寇。
entries.en: On renshen day General Yang Yong, Duke of Changning, was made superior pillar-of-state and grand marshal; Junior Steward of Tombs Yuan Xiaoju, Duke of Shiping, was made grand minister of justice.
entries.literal: On renshen day General Yang Yong, Duke of Changning, was made superior pillar-of-state and grand marshal; Junior Steward of Tombs Yuan Xiaoju, Duke of Shiping West, was made grand minister of justice.

entries.zh: 冬十月甲寅，日有蝕之。
entries.en: Tenth month of winter, on jiayin day, there was a solar eclipse.
entries.literal: Tenth month of winter, on jiayin day, there was a solar eclipse.

entries.zh: 乙卯，有流星大如五斗，出張，南流，光明燭地。
entries.en: On yimao day a meteor as large as five dou appeared from Zhang, flowing south; its light illuminated the earth.
entries.literal: On yimao day a meteor as large as five dou appeared from Zhang, flowing south; its light illuminated the earth.

entries.zh: 壬戌，陳王純以怨執政，被誅。
entries.en: On renxu day Yuwen Chun, Prince of Chen, was executed for resentment against the government.
entries.literal: On renxu day Yuwen Chun, Prince of Chen, was executed for resentment against the government.

entries.zh: 大丞相、隨國公楊堅加大冢宰，五府總於天官。
entries.en: Grand Chancellor Yang Jian, Duke of Sui, was additionally made grand counsellor; the five offices were all placed under the Celestial Office.
entries.literal: Grand Chancellor Yang Jian, Duke of Sui, was additionally made grand counsellor; the five offices were all placed under the Celestial Office.

entries.zh: 戊寅，梁睿破王謙于劍南，追斬之，傳首京師。
entries.en: On wuyin day Liang Rui defeated Wang Qian in Jiannan, pursued and beheaded him, and sent his head to the capital.
entries.literal: On wuyin day Liang Rui defeated Wang Qian in Jiannan, pursued and beheaded him, and sent his head to the capital.

entries.zh: 益州平。
entries.en: Yi Province was pacified.
entries.literal: Yi Province was pacified.

entries.zh: 文帝元皇后 文宣叱奴皇后 孝閔帝元皇后 明帝獨孤皇后 武帝阿史那皇后 武帝李皇后 宣帝楊皇后 宣帝朱皇后 宣帝陳皇后 宣帝元皇后 宣帝尉遲皇后 靜帝司馬皇后
entries.en: Empress Yuan, consort of Emperor Wen Yuwen Tai; Empress Chinu, consort of Emperor Wen Yuwen Tai; Empress Yuan, consort of Emperor Min Yuwen Jue; Empress Dugu, consort of Emperor Ming Yuwen Yu; Empress Ashina, consort of Emperor Wu Yuwen Yong; Empress Li, consort of Emperor Wu Yuwen Yong; Empress Yang, consort of Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun; Empress Zhu, consort of Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun; Empress Chen, consort of Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun; Empress Yuan, consort of Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun; Empress Yuchi, consort of Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun; Empress Sima, consort of Emperor Jing Yuwen Chan
entries.literal: Empress Yuan, consort of Emperor Wen  Empress Chinu, consort of Emperor Wen  Empress Yuan, consort of Emperor Min  Empress Dugu, consort of Emperor Ming  Empress Ashina, consort of Emperor Wu  Empress Li, consort of Emperor Wu  Empress Yang, consort of Emperor Xuan  Empress Zhu, consort of Emperor Xuan  Empress Chen, consort of Emperor Xuan  Empress Yuan, consort of Emperor Xuan  Empress Yuchi, consort of Emperor Xuan  Empress Sima, consort of Emperor Jing

entries.zh: 明帝獨孤皇后，太保、衛國公信之長女。
entries.en: Empress Dugu, consort of Emperor Ming Yuwen Yu, was the eldest daughter of Grand Guardian and Duke of Weiguo Dugu Xin.
entries.literal: Empress Dugu, consort of Emperor Ming Yuwen Yu, was the eldest daughter of Grand Guardian and Duke of Weiguo Xin.

entries.zh: 帝之在藩也，納為夫人。
entries.en: While Emperor Ming Yuwen Yu was still in his princely domain, she was taken as lady.
entries.literal: While the emperor was still in his princely domain, she was taken as lady.

entries.zh: 二年正月，立為王后。
entries.en: Second year, first month, she was installed as queen.
entries.literal: Second year, first month, she was installed as queen.

entries.zh: 四月，崩，葬昭陵。
entries.en: Fourth month, she died and was buried at Zhaoling.
entries.literal: Fourth month, she died and was buried at Zhaoling.

entries.zh: 武成初，追崇為皇后。
entries.en: At the beginning of Wucheng, she was posthumously honored as empress.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Wucheng, she was posthumously honored as empress.

entries.zh: 世宗崩，與后合葬。
entries.en: When Emperor Ming Yuwen Yu died, she was buried with him.
entries.literal: When Emperor Ming Yuwen Yu died, she was buried with him.

entries.zh: 周氏率由姬制，內職有序。
entries.en: The Zhou house followed the Zhou institutional model, and the inner palaces were well ordered.
entries.literal: The Zhou house followed the Ji system, and the inner offices were orderly.

entries.zh: 太祖創基，修衽席以儉約；
entries.en: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai laid the foundation and kept the inner quarters in frugal simplicity;
entries.literal: The Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai founded the base and maintained the marital bedchamber in frugality;

entries.zh: 高祖嗣曆，節情欲於矯枉。
entries.en: High Ancestor Yuwen Yong succeeded to the throne and checked excess by restraining his passions.
entries.literal: High Ancestor Yuwen Yong succeeded to the throne and restrained passions in correcting excess.

entries.zh: 宮闈有貫魚之美，戚里無私溺之尤，可謂得人君體也。
entries.en: The inner palaces showed the ordered beauty of "the lined fish," and the imperial kindred knew no gross favoritism—this may be called understanding the ruler's proper bearing.
entries.literal: The inner palaces had the beauty of "the lined fish," and the imperial kindred had no extreme indulgence in favoritism—this may be called grasping the ruler's proper style.

entries.zh: 宣皇外行其志，內逞其欲，溪壑難滿，采擇無厭。
entries.en: Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun outwardly pursued his ambitions while inwardly indulging his desires; his appetite was insatiable, and his taking of consorts never ceased.
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun outwardly pursued his ambitions while inwardly indulging his desires; gullies and ravines could not be filled, and selection never ceased.

entries.zh: 恩之所加，莫限廝皂；
entries.en: Those whom his favor reached were not limited to the lowest servants;
entries.literal: Those whom favor reached were not limited to menials;

entries.zh: 榮之所及，無隔險詖。
entries.en: Those whom glory touched knew no barrier of distance or partiality.
entries.literal: Those whom glory touched knew no barrier of remoteness or partiality.

entries.zh: 於是升蘭殿而正位，踐椒庭而齊體者，非一人焉；
entries.en: Thus those who ascended the Orchid Hall to take formal rank and shared the pepper courtyard as full equals were not one person alone;
entries.literal: Thus those who ascended the Orchid Hall to take proper rank and tread the pepper courtyard as full equals were not one person alone;

entries.zh: 階房帷而拖青紫，承恩幸而擁玉帛者，非一族焉。
entries.en: Those who in side chambers donned purple and crimson and, receiving favor, grasped jade and silk were not one clan alone.
entries.literal: Those who in side chambers donned purple and crimson and, receiving favor, clutched jade and silk were not one clan alone.

entries.zh: 雖辛、癸之荒淫，趙、李之傾惑，曾未足比其髣髴也。
entries.en: Even the debauchery of Kings Zhou and Li of old and the seductive sway of Zhao Feiyan and Lady Li of Han barely approach this in likeness.
entries.literal: Even the debauchery of Xin and Gui and the deluding influence of Zhao and Li barely approach this in likeness.

entries.zh: 民厭苛政，弊事實多，太祖之祚忽諸，特由於此。
entries.en: The people grew weary of harsh government, and abuses were many; the Zhou mandate established by Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai ended in a flash, largely for this reason.
entries.literal: The people grew weary of harsh government, and abuses were truly many; the mandate of the Grand Progenitor ended in a flash, chiefly because of this.

entries.zh: 故敘其事以為《皇后傳》云。
entries.en: Therefore I narrate these affairs as the Biographies of Empresses.
entries.literal: Therefore I narrate these affairs as the Biographies of Empresses.

entries.zh: 文宣叱奴皇后，代人也。
entries.en: Empress Chinu, consort of Emperor Wen Yuwen Tai, was a native of Dai.
entries.literal: Empress Chinu, consort of Emperor Wen Yuwen Tai, was a native of Dai.

entries.zh: 太祖為丞相，納后為姬，生高祖。
entries.en: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai was chief minister, he took her as consort; she bore High Ancestor Yuwen Yong.
entries.literal: When the Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai was chief minister, he took her as consort; she bore High Ancestor Yuwen Yong.

entries.zh: 天和
entries.en: Tianhe
entries.literal: Tianhe

entries.en: (first)
entries.literal: (first)

entries.zh: 年六月，尊為皇太后。
entries.en: year, sixth month, she was honored as empress dowager.
entries.literal: year, sixth month, she was honored as empress dowager.

entries.zh: 建德
entries.en: Jiande
entries.literal: Jiande

entries.en: (second)
entries.literal: (second)

entries.zh: 年三月癸酉，崩。
entries.en: year, third month, on guiyou day, she died.
entries.literal: year, third month, on guiyou day, she died.

entries.zh: 四月丁巳，葬永固陵。
entries.en: Fourth month, on dingsi day, she was buried at Yonggu Mausoleum.
entries.literal: Fourth month, on dingsi day, she was buried at Yonggu Mausoleum.

entries.zh: 武帝阿史那皇后，突厥木扞可汗俟斤之女。
entries.en: Empress Ashina, consort of Emperor Wu Yuwen Yong, was the daughter of Irkin, khan of the Turks, Muhan Khan.
entries.literal: Empress Ashina, consort of Emperor Wu Yuwen Yong, was the daughter of Irkin, khan of the Turks, Muhan Khan.

entries.zh: 突厥滅茹茹之後，盡有塞表之地，控弦數十萬，志陵中夏。
entries.en: After the Turks destroyed the Rouran, they held all the lands beyond the frontier and commanded several hundred thousand bowmen, with their ambition set on dominating China.
entries.literal: After the Turks destroyed the Rouran, they held all the lands beyond the frontier and commanded several hundred thousand bowmen, their ambition set on dominating China.

entries.zh: 太祖方與齊人爭衡，結以為援。
entries.en: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai was then contending with Northern Qi for supremacy and sought alliance with the Turks.
entries.literal: The Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai was then contending with the Qi for supremacy and sought alliance with them.

entries.zh: 俟斤初欲以女配帝，旣而悔之。
entries.en: Irkin at first wished to give his daughter to the Zhou emperor, but afterward changed his mind.
entries.literal: Irkin at first wished to give his daughter to the emperor, but afterward regretted it.

entries.zh: 高祖卽位，前後累遣使要結，乃許歸后於我。
entries.en: When High Ancestor Yuwen Yong ascended the throne, envoys were repeatedly sent to renew the alliance, and Irkin finally agreed to send the empress to Zhou.
entries.literal: When High Ancestor Yuwen Yong ascended the throne, envoys were repeatedly sent to renew the alliance, and he finally agreed to send the empress to us.

entries.zh: 保定五年二月，詔陳國公純、許國公宇文貴、神武公竇毅、南
entries.en: Second month of the fifth year of Baoding, an edict ordered Duke of Chen Yuwen Chun, Duke of Xu Yuwen Gui, Duke of Shenwu Dou Yi, and Nan
entries.literal: Second month of the fifth year of Baoding, an edict ordered Duke of Chen Yuwen Chun, Duke of Xu Yuwen Gui, Duke of Shenwu Dou Yi, and Nan

entries.en: (Yang)
entries.literal: (Yang)

entries.zh: 安公楊薦等，奉備皇后文物及行殿，幷六宮以下百二十人，至俟斤牙帳所，迎后。
entries.en: An Duke Yang Jian and others, bearing the empress's regalia and traveling hall, together with one hundred twenty persons of the six palaces and below, went to Irkin's encampment to welcome the empress.
entries.literal: An Duke Yang Jian and others, bearing the empress's regalia and traveling hall, together with one hundred twenty persons of the six palaces and below, went to Irkin's encampment to welcome the empress.

entries.zh: 俟斤又許齊人以婚，將有異志。
entries.en: Irkin again promised his daughter in marriage to Northern Qi, and was about to shift his allegiance.
entries.literal: Irkin again promised his daughter in marriage to the Qi, and was about to change his allegiance.

entries.zh: 純等在彼累載，不得反命。
entries.en: Yuwen Chun and the others remained there for years and could not return with their mission accomplished.
entries.literal: Chun and the others remained there for years and could not return with their mission accomplished.

entries.zh: 雖諭之以信義，俟斤不從。
entries.en: Although they admonished him with faith and righteousness, Irkin would not comply.
entries.literal: Although they admonished him with faith and righteousness, Irkin would not comply.

entries.zh: 會大雷風起，飄壞其穹廬等，旬日不止。
entries.en: Then great thunder and wind arose, blowing down their felt tents and the like, and did not cease for ten days.
entries.literal: Then great thunder and wind arose, blowing down their felt tents and the like, and did not cease for ten days.

entries.zh: 俟斤大懼，以為天譴，乃備禮送后。
entries.en: Irkin was greatly frightened, taking it for heavenly punishment, and thereupon prepared full rites to send the empress off.
entries.literal: Irkin was greatly frightened, taking it for heavenly punishment, and thereupon prepared full rites to send the empress off.

entries.en: (And)
entries.literal: (And)

entries.zh: 純等設行殿，列羽儀，奉之以歸。
entries.en: Yuwen Chun and the others set up the traveling hall, arrayed the guard of honor, and escorted her back.
entries.literal: Chun and the others set up the traveling hall, arrayed the guard of honor, and escorted her back.

entries.zh: 天和三年三月，后至，高祖行親迎之禮。
entries.en: Third month of the third year of Tianhe, the empress arrived; High Ancestor Yuwen Yong performed the rite of greeting her in person.
entries.literal: Third month of the third year of Tianhe, the empress arrived; High Ancestor Yuwen Yong performed the rite of greeting her in person.

entries.zh: 后有姿貌，善容止，高祖深敬焉。
entries.en: The empress had fine appearance and graceful bearing; High Ancestor Yuwen Yong deeply respected her.
entries.literal: The empress had fine appearance and graceful bearing; High Ancestor Yuwen Yong deeply respected her.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：孔子稱「夷狄之有君，不如諸夏之亡也」。
entries.en: The historian writes: Confucius said, "The barbarians may have their rulers, but they cannot compare with the Central States when they lack them."
entries.literal: The historian writes: Confucius said, "The barbarians may have their rulers, but they cannot compare with the Central States when they lack them."

entries.zh: 是以周納狄后，富辰謂之禍階；
entries.en: Hence when Zhou accepted the Di empress, Fuchen called it the steps to disaster;
entries.literal: Hence when Zhou accepted the Di empress, Fuchen called it the steps to disaster;

entries.zh: 晉升戎女，卜人以為不吉。
entries.en: when Jin elevated a Rong woman, the diviners considered it inauspicious.
entries.literal: when Jin elevated a Rong woman, the diviners considered it inauspicious.

entries.zh: 斯固非謬焉。
entries.en: This was certainly not mistaken.
entries.literal: This was certainly not mistaken.

entries.zh: 自周氏受命，逮乎高祖，年踰三紀，世歷四君。
entries.en: From when the Zhou house received the mandate until High Ancestor Yuwen Yong, more than three decades passed and four rulers succeeded one another.
entries.literal: From when the Zhou house received the mandate until High Ancestor Yuwen Yong, more than three decades passed and four rulers succeeded one another.

entries.zh: 業非草昧之辰，事殊權宜之日，乃弃同卽異，以夷亂華。
entries.en: The enterprise was no longer in its founding period; affairs differed from days of expedient measure—yet they abandoned kin for outsiders and used barbarians to disorder the Chinese.
entries.literal: The enterprise was no longer in its founding period; affairs differed from days of expedient measure—yet they abandoned the same for the different and used barbarians to disorder the Chinese.

entries.zh: 捐婚姻之彝序，求豺狼之外利。
entries.en: They cast aside the canonical order of marriage and sought external profit from wolves.
entries.literal: They cast aside the canonical order of marriage and sought external profit from wolves.

entries.zh: 旣而報者倦矣，施者無厭，向之所謂和親，未幾已成讐敵。
entries.en: Before long those who repaid grew weary and those who bestowed were insatiable; what had been called harmony-through-kinship before, in no time had become sworn enemies.
entries.literal: Before long those who repaid grew weary and those who bestowed were insatiable; what had been called harmony-through-kinship before, in no time had become sworn enemies.

entries.zh: 奇正之道，有異於斯。
entries.en: The way of the orthodox and the unorthodox differs from this.
entries.literal: The way of the orthodox and the unorthodox differs from this.

entries.zh: 于時高祖雖受制於人，未親庶政，而謀士韞奇，直臣鉗口。
entries.en: At that time, although High Ancestor Yuwen Yong was controlled by others and did not personally attend to general government, yet strategists hoarded their plans and upright ministers were silenced.
entries.literal: At that time, although High Ancestor Yuwen Yong was controlled by others and did not personally attend to general government, yet strategists hoarded their plans and upright ministers were silenced.

entries.zh: 過矣哉！
entries.en: An error indeed!
entries.literal: An error indeed!

entries.zh: 武帝李皇后名娥姿，楚人也。
entries.en: Empress Li, consort of Emperor Wu Yuwen Yong, was named Ezi; she was a native of Chu.
entries.literal: Empress Li, consort of Emperor Wu Yuwen Yong, was named Ezi; she was a native of Chu.

entries.zh: 于謹平江陵，后家被籍沒。
entries.en: When Yu Jin captured Jiangling, the empress's family was confiscated and registered.
entries.literal: When Yu Jin captured Jiangling, the empress's family was confiscated and registered.

entries.zh: 至長安，太祖以后賜高祖，後稍得親幸。
entries.en: Reaching Chang'an, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai bestowed the empress upon High Ancestor Yuwen Yong; afterward she gradually gained his favor.
entries.literal: Reaching Chang'an, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai bestowed the empress upon High Ancestor Yuwen Yong; afterward she gradually gained his favor.

entries.zh: 大象元年二月，改為天元帝太后。
entries.en: Second month of the first year of Daxiang, she was retitled Empress Dowager of the Heavenly Primordial Emperor.
entries.literal: Second month of the first year of Daxiang, she was retitled Empress Dowager of the Heavenly Primordial Emperor.

entries.zh: 七月，又尊為天皇太后。
entries.en: Seventh month, she was again honored as Heavenly Sovereign Empress Dowager.
entries.literal: Seventh month, she was again honored as Heavenly Sovereign Empress Dowager.

entries.zh: 二年，尊為天元聖皇太后。
entries.en: Second year, she was honored as Heavenly Primordial Sage Empress Dowager.
entries.literal: Second year, she was honored as Heavenly Primordial Sage Empress Dowager.

entries.zh: 冊曰：「天元皇帝臣贇，奉璽綬冊，謹上天皇太后尊號曰天元聖皇太后。
entries.en: The edict of investiture stated: "The Heavenly Primordial Emperor, your subject Yun, reverently presents the seal and cord of investiture and respectfully bestows upon the Heavenly Sovereign Empress Dowager the honorific title Heavenly Primordial Sage Empress Dowager.
entries.literal: The edict of investiture stated: "The Heavenly Primordial Emperor, your subject Yun, reverently presents the seal and cord of investiture and respectfully bestows upon the Heavenly Sovereign Empress Dowager the honorific title Heavenly Primordial Sage Empress Dowager.

entries.zh: 伏惟月精効祉，坤靈表貺，瑞肇丹陵，慶流華渚。
entries.en: I consider that the essence of the moon brings blessings, the spirit of earth displays favor, auspicious signs arose at Red Mound, and celebration flowed upon the Flower Ford.
entries.literal: I consider that the essence of the moon brings blessings, the spirit of earth displays favor, auspicious signs arose at Red Mound, and celebration flowed upon the Flower Ford.

entries.zh: 雖率由令典，夙奉徽號，而因心盡敬，未極尊名。
entries.en: Though following established statutes and long bearing honorific titles, heartfelt reverence has not yet reached the full measure of exalted title.
entries.literal: Though following established statutes and long bearing honorific titles, heartfelt reverence has not yet reached the full measure of exalted title.

entries.zh: 是用思弘稱首，上昭聖德，敢竭誠敬，永綏福履。
entries.en: Therefore I intend to expand this foremost title, manifest your sage virtue above, dare to exhaust sincerity and reverence, and forever secure blessings.
entries.literal: Therefore I intend to expand this foremost title, manifest your sage virtue above, dare to exhaust sincerity and reverence, and forever secure blessings.

entries.zh: 顯揚慈訓，貽厥孫謀。」
entries.en: May your compassionate instruction shine forth and your counsel be bequeathed to descendants."
entries.literal: May your compassionate instruction shine forth and your counsel be bequeathed to descendants."

entries.zh: 宣帝崩，靜帝尊為太帝太后。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun died, Emperor Jing Yuwen Chan honored her as Grand Imperial Empress Dowager.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun died, Emperor Jing Yuwen Chan honored her as Grand Imperial Empress Dowager.

entries.zh: 隋開皇元年三月，出俗為尼，改名常悲。
entries.en: Third month of the first year of Kaihuang of Sui, she left the lay life to become a nun, changing her name to Changbei (Ever Grieved).
entries.literal: Third month of the first year of Kaihuang of Sui, she left the lay life to become a nun, changing her name to Changbei (Ever Grieved).

entries.zh: 八年殂，年五十三，以尼禮葬于京城南。
entries.en: In the eighth year she died, aged fifty-three; she was buried south of the capital by rites for nuns.
entries.literal: In the eighth year she died, aged fifty-three; she was buried south of the capital by rites for nuns.

entries.zh: 孝閔帝元皇后名胡摩，魏文帝第五女。
entries.en: Empress Yuan, consort of Emperor Min Yuwen Jue, was named Hu Mo, the fifth daughter of Emperor Wen of Wei.
entries.literal: Empress Yuan, consort of Emperor Min Yuwen Jue, was named Hu Mo, the fifth daughter of Emperor Wen of Wei.

entries.zh: 初封晉安公主。
entries.en: Initially she was enfeoffed as Princess of Jin'an.
entries.literal: Initially she was enfeoffed as Princess of Jin'an.

entries.zh: 帝之為略陽公也，尚焉。
entries.en: When Emperor Min Yuwen Jue was Duke of Lueyang, she was married to him.
entries.literal: When Emperor Min Yuwen Jue was Duke of Lueyang, she was married to him.

entries.zh: 及踐祚，立為王后。
entries.en: When he ascended the throne, she was installed as queen.
entries.literal: When he ascended the throne, she was installed as queen.

entries.zh: 帝被廢，后出俗為尼。
entries.en: When the emperor was deposed, the empress left the lay life to become a nun.
entries.literal: When the emperor was deposed, the empress left the lay life to become a nun.

entries.zh: 建德初，高祖誅晉國公護，上帝尊號為孝閔帝，以后為孝閔皇后，居崇義宮。
entries.en: At the beginning of Jiande, High Ancestor Yuwen Yong executed Duke of Jin Guo Yuwen Hu and elevated the emperor's honorific title to Emperor Min; the empress was made Empress Min and resided at Chongyi Palace.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Jiande, High Ancestor Yuwen Yong executed Duke of Jin Guo Yuwen Hu and elevated the emperor's honorific title to Emperor Min; the empress was made Empress Min and resided at Chongyi Palace.

entries.zh: 隋氏革命，后出居里第。
entries.en: When the Sui house revolutionized the dynasty, the empress moved out to a private residence.
entries.literal: When the Sui house revolutionized the dynasty, the empress moved out to a private residence.

entries.zh: 大業十二年，殂。
entries.en: In the twelfth year of Daye she died.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year of Daye she died.

entries.zh: 宣帝楊皇后名麗華，隋文帝長女。
entries.en: Empress Yang, consort of Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun, named Lihua, was the eldest daughter of Sui Emperor Wen Yang Jian.
entries.literal: Empress Yang, consort of Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun, named Lihua, was the eldest daughter of Sui Emperor Wen Yang Jian.

entries.zh: 帝在東宮，高祖為帝納后為皇太子妃。
entries.en: While Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun was in the Eastern Palace, High Ancestor Yuwen Yong had her taken as crown prince consort for him.
entries.literal: While the emperor was in the Eastern Palace, High Ancestor Yuwen Yong had the empress taken as crown prince consort for him.

entries.zh: 宣政元年閏六月，立為皇后。
entries.en: Intercalary sixth month of the first year of Xuanzheng, she was installed as empress.
entries.literal: Intercalary sixth month of the first year of Xuanzheng, she was installed as empress.

entries.zh: 帝后自稱天元皇帝，號后為天元皇后。
entries.en: Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun styled himself Heavenly Primordial Emperor and titled the empress Heavenly Primordial Empress.
entries.literal: The emperor and empress styled themselves Heavenly Primordial Emperor and Heavenly Primordial Empress.

entries.zh: 尋又立天皇后及左右皇后，與后為四皇后焉。
entries.en: Soon afterward Heavenly Empress and the Left and Right Empresses were also installed, making four empresses together with her.
entries.literal: Soon afterward Heavenly Empress and the Left and Right Empresses were also installed, making four empresses together with her.

entries.zh: 二年，詔曰：「帝降二女，后德所以儷君；
entries.en: Second year, an edict stated: "The emperor descended his two daughters; the empress's virtue therefore matches the ruler;
entries.literal: Second year, an edict stated: "The emperor descended his two daughters; the empress's virtue therefore matches the ruler;

entries.zh: 天列四星，妃象於焉垂耀。
entries.en: Heaven arrayed four stars; the consort's image there sheds its radiance.
entries.literal: Heaven arrayed four stars; the consort's image there sheds its radiance.

entries.zh: 朕取法上玄，稽諸令典，爰命四后，內正六宮，庶弘贊柔德，廣修粢盛。
entries.en: We take the Way of High Heaven as model and examine the present statutes; we therefore appoint four empresses to govern the six palaces within, that they may broadly assist in gentle virtue and widely maintain the sacrificial grain.
entries.literal: We take the Way of High Heaven as model and examine the present statutes; we therefore appoint four empresses to govern the six palaces within, that they may broadly assist in gentle virtue and widely maintain the sacrificial grain.

entries.zh: 比殊禮雖降，稱謂曷宜，其因天之象，增錫嘉名。」
entries.en: Although special rites were reduced, how could the titles be fitting? Let them follow Heaven's image and be granted enhanced honorable names."
entries.literal: Although special rites were reduced, how could the titles be fitting? Let them follow Heaven's image and be granted enhanced honorable names."

entries.zh: 於是后與三皇后並加
entries.en: Thereupon the empress and the three empresses were all additionally given
entries.literal: Thereupon the empress and the three empresses were all additionally given

entries.en: (Grand)
entries.literal: (Grand)

entries.zh: 大焉。
entries.en: Great titles.
entries.literal: Great titles.

entries.zh: 帝遣使持節册后為天元大皇后曰：「咨爾含章載德，體順居貞，肅恭享祀，儀刑邦國，是用嘉茲顯號，式暢徽音。
entries.en: The emperor dispatched an envoy bearing credentials to invest the empress as Heavenly Primordial Grand Empress, stating: "You who embrace virtue and bear emblem, embody compliance and hold to rectitude, reverently perform sacrifice and serve as model to the realm—for this we grant this illustrious title and extend this fine renown.
entries.literal: The emperor dispatched an envoy bearing credentials to invest the empress as Heavenly Primordial Grand Empress, stating: "You who embrace virtue and bear emblem, embody compliance and hold to rectitude, reverently perform sacrifice and serve as model to the realm—for this we grant this illustrious title and extend this fine renown.

entries.zh: 爾其敬踐厥猷，寅荅靈命，對揚休烈，可不慎歟。」
entries.en: Reverently carry out your charge, respectfully answer the sacred mandate, and respond to this glorious enterprise—can you not be careful?"
entries.literal: Reverently carry out your charge, respectfully answer the sacred mandate, and respond to this glorious enterprise—can you not be careful?"

entries.zh: 尋又立
entries.en: Soon afterward she was also installed
entries.literal: Soon afterward she was also installed

entries.en: (as)
entries.literal: (as)

entries.zh: 天中大皇后，與后為五皇后。
entries.en: Heavenly Central Grand Empress, making five empresses together with her.
entries.literal: Heavenly Central Grand Empress, making five empresses together with her.

entries.zh: 后父山提本高氏之隸。
entries.en: The empress's father Shanti was originally a bondservant of the Gao clan.
entries.literal: The empress's father Shanti was originally a bondservant of the Gao clan.

entries.zh: 仕齊，官至特進、開府、東兗州刺史、謝陽王。
entries.en: Serving Qi, he rose to Superintendent of Forecourt Honors, opening-the-feudatory, regional inspector of Eastern Yanzhou, and Prince of Xieyang.
entries.literal: Serving Qi, he rose to Superintendent of Forecourt Honors, opening-the-feudatory, regional inspector of Eastern Yanzhou, and Prince of Xieyang.

entries.zh: 高祖平齊，拜大將軍，封
entries.en: When High Ancestor Yuwen Yong pacified Qi, he appointed him Grand General and enfeoffed him as Duke of
entries.literal: When High Ancestor Yuwen Yong pacified Qi, he appointed him Grand General and enfeoffed him as Duke of

entries.en: (Zhe)
entries.literal: (Zhe)

entries.zh: 〔淅〕陽郡公。
entries.en: Xiyang Commandery.
entries.literal: Xiyang Commandery.

entries.zh: 大象元年，以后父超授上柱國，進封鄅國公，除大宗伯。
entries.en: First year of Daxiang, as father of the empress he was exceptionally granted Senior Pillar of State, advanced to Duke of Yu State, and appointed Grand Director of Ceremonial.
entries.literal: First year of Daxiang, as father of the empress he was exceptionally granted Senior Pillar of State, advanced to Duke of Yu State, and appointed Grand Director of Ceremonial.

entries.zh: 宣帝元皇后名樂尚，河南洛陽人也。
entries.en: Empress Yuan, consort of Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun, was named Yue Shang, a native of Luoyang in Henan.
entries.literal: Empress Yuan, consort of Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun, was named Yue Shang, a native of Luoyang in Henan.

entries.zh: 開府晟之第二女。
entries.en: She was the second daughter of opening-the-feudatory Sheng.
entries.literal: She was the second daughter of opening-the-feudatory Sheng.

entries.zh: 年十五，被選入宮，拜為貴妃。
entries.en: At age fifteen she was selected to enter the palace and appointed Noble Consort.
entries.literal: At age fifteen she was selected to enter the palace and appointed Noble Consort.

entries.zh: 大象元年七月，立為天右皇后。
entries.en: Seventh month of the first year of Daxiang, she was installed as Heavenly Right Empress.
entries.literal: Seventh month of the first year of Daxiang, she was installed as Heavenly Right Empress.

entries.zh: 二年二月，改為天右大皇后。
entries.en: Second month of the second year, she was retitled Grand Heavenly Right Empress.
entries.literal: Second month of the second year, she was retitled Grand Heavenly Right Empress.

entries.zh: 冊曰：「咨爾資靈姜水，載德塗山，懿淑內融，徽音潛暢。
entries.en: The edict of investiture stated: "I address you thus: Your endowment draws upon the spiritual waters of Jiang, your virtue is borne upon Mount Tu; gentle grace inwardly suffuses, and fine renown quietly flows.
entries.literal: The edict of investiture stated: "I address you thus: Your endowment draws upon the spiritual waters of Jiang, your virtue is borne upon Mount Tu; gentle grace inwardly suffuses, and fine renown quietly flows.

entries.zh: 是用加茲寵數，式光踐禮。
entries.en: Therefore I add this measure of favor and extend the splendor of your investiture.
entries.literal: Therefore I add this measure of favor and extend the splendor of your investiture.

entries.zh: 爾其聿修儀範，肅膺顯冊，祗承休命，可不慎歟。」
entries.en: Adorn your bearing and walk the model, reverently receive the manifest investiture, respectfully accept this blessed mandate—can you not be careful?"
entries.literal: Adorn your bearing and walk the model, reverently receive the manifest investiture, respectfully accept this blessed mandate—can you not be careful?"

entries.zh: 帝崩，后出俗為尼，改名華勝。
entries.en: When the emperor died, the empress left the lay life to become a nun, changing her name to Huasheng (Floral Victory).
entries.literal: When the emperor died, the empress left the lay life to become a nun, changing her name to Huasheng (Floral Victory).

entries.zh: 初，后與陳后同時被選入宮，俱拜為妃，及升后位，又同日受冊，帝寵遇二后，禮數均等，年齒復同，特相親愛。
entries.en: Initially the empress and Empress Chen were selected together to enter the palace, both appointed as consorts; when elevated to empress rank they received investiture on the same day. The emperor favored both empresses equally in ceremonial treatment; their ages were likewise the same, and they were especially close.
entries.literal: Initially the empress and Empress Chen were selected together to enter the palace, both appointed as consorts; when elevated to empress rank they received investiture on the same day. The emperor favored both empresses equally in ceremonial treatment; their ages were likewise the same, and they were especially close.

entries.zh: 及為尼後，李、朱及尉遲后等並相繼殞沒，而二后于今尚存。
entries.en: After becoming nuns, Empresses Li, Zhu, and Yuchi and others all died in succession, but the two empresses remain alive to this day.
entries.literal: After becoming nuns, Empresses Li, Zhu, and Yuchi and others all died in succession, but the two empresses remain alive to this day.

entries.zh: 后父晟，少以元氏宗室，拜開府。
entries.en: The empress's father Sheng, in youth on account of his status in the Yuan imperial clan, was appointed opening-the-feudatory.
entries.literal: The empress's father Sheng, in youth on account of his status in the Yuan imperial clan, was appointed opening-the-feudatory.

entries.zh: 大象
entries.en: Daxiang
entries.literal: Daxiang

entries.en: (end)
entries.literal: (end)

entries.zh: 〔元〕年七月，以后父進位上柱國，封翼國公。
entries.en: first year, seventh month, as father of the empress he was advanced to Senior Pillar of State and enfeoffed as Duke of Yi State.
entries.literal: first year, seventh month, as father of the empress he was advanced to Senior Pillar of State and enfeoffed as Duke of Yi State.

entries.zh: 宣帝卽位，尊為皇太后。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun ascended the throne, she was honored as empress dowager.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun ascended the throne, she was honored as empress dowager.

entries.zh: 大象元年二月，改為天元皇太后。
entries.en: Second month of the first year of Daxiang, she was retitled Heavenly Primordial Empress Dowager.
entries.literal: Second month of the first year of Daxiang, she was retitled Heavenly Primordial Empress Dowager.

entries.zh: 二年二月，又尊為天元上皇太后。
entries.en: Second month of the second year, she was again honored as Heavenly Primordial Upper Empress Dowager.
entries.literal: Second month of the second year, she was again honored as Heavenly Primordial Upper Empress Dowager.

entries.zh: 册曰：「天元皇帝臣贇，奉璽綬册，謹上天元皇太后尊號曰天元上皇太后。
entries.en: The edict of investiture stated: "The Heavenly Primordial Emperor, your subject Yun, reverently presents the seal and cord of investiture and respectfully bestows upon the Heavenly Primordial Empress Dowager the honorific title Heavenly Primordial Upper Empress Dowager.
entries.literal: The edict of investiture stated: "The Heavenly Primordial Emperor, your subject Yun, reverently presents the seal and cord of investiture and respectfully bestows upon the Heavenly Primordial Empress Dowager the honorific title Heavenly Primordial Upper Empress Dowager.

entries.zh: 伏惟窮神盡智，含弘載物，道洽萬邦，儀刑四海。
entries.en: I consider that you exhaust the divine and exhaust wisdom, embrace and carry all things, your Way harmonizing with ten thousand states, your model governing the four seas.
entries.literal: I consider that you exhaust the divine and exhaust wisdom, embrace and carry all things, your Way harmonizing with ten thousand states, your model governing the four seas.

entries.zh: 聖慈訓誘，恩深明德，雖册徽號，未極尊嚴。
entries.en: Your sage compassion instructs and guides; your grace is deep and your virtue bright—though an honorific title is conferred, it does not reach the full measure of your dignity.
entries.literal: Your sage compassion instructs and guides; your grace is deep and your virtue bright—though an honorific title is conferred, it does not reach the full measure of your dignity.

entries.zh: 是用增奉鴻名，光縟常禮。
entries.en: Therefore I add this great name and extend the constant rites.
entries.literal: Therefore I add this great name and extend the constant rites.

entries.zh: 俾誠敬有展，歡慰在茲，福祉無疆，億兆斯賴。」
entries.en: May sincerity and reverence be fully displayed, joy and comfort rest here, blessings without limit, and the hundred millions rely upon you."
entries.literal: May sincerity and reverence be fully displayed, joy and comfort rest here, blessings without limit, and the hundred millions rely upon you."

entries.zh: 宣帝崩，靜帝尊為太皇太后。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun died, Emperor Jing Yuwen Chan honored her as grand empress dowager.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun died, Emperor Jing Yuwen Chan honored her as grand empress dowager.

entries.zh: 隋開皇二年殂，年三十二。
entries.en: In the second year of Kaihuang of Sui she died, aged thirty-two.
entries.literal: In the second year of Kaihuang of Sui she died, aged thirty-two.

entries.zh: 隋文帝詔有司備禮册，祔葬於孝陵。
entries.en: Sui Emperor Wen Yang Jian ordered the officials to prepare rites of investiture and had her buried at Xiaoling.
