entries.literal: Sui Emperor Wen Yang Jian ordered the officials to prepare rites of investiture and had her buried at Xiaoling.

entries.zh: 后性柔婉，不妒忌，四皇后及嬪禦等咸愛而仰之。
entries.en: The empress was gentle and compliant by nature and free of jealousy; the four empresses and the consorts and imperial ladies all loved and looked up to her.
entries.literal: The empress was gentle and compliant by nature and free of jealousy; the four empresses and the consorts and imperial ladies all loved and looked up to her.

entries.zh: 帝後昏暴滋甚，喜怒乖度。
entries.en: Afterward Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun grew ever more benighted and violent, and joy and anger departed from measure.
entries.literal: Afterward the emperor grew ever more benighted and violent, and joy and anger departed from measure.

entries.zh: 嘗譴后，欲加之罪，后進止詳閑，辭色不撓。
entries.en: Once he rebuked the empress and wished to charge her with a crime; the empress in her movements was composed and detailed, and her words and expression did not waver.
entries.literal: Once he rebuked the empress and wished to charge her with a crime; the empress in her movements was composed and detailed, and her words and expression did not waver.

entries.zh: 帝大怒，遂賜后死，逼令引訣。
entries.en: The emperor was greatly enraged and thereupon ordered the empress to die, forcing her to commit suicide.
entries.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and thereupon ordered the empress to die, forcing her to take farewell.

entries.zh: 后母獨孤氏聞之，詣閤陳謝，叩頭流血，然後得免。
entries.en: When the empress's mother, Lady Dugu, heard of it, she came to the gate to offer apology, knocking her head until blood flowed, and only then was the empress spared.
entries.literal: When the empress's mother, Lady Dugu, heard of it, she came to the gate to offer apology, knocking her head until blood flowed, and only then was the empress spared.

entries.zh: 帝崩，靜帝尊後為皇太后，居弘聖宮。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun died, Emperor Jing Yuwen Chan honored her as empress dowager, and she resided at Hongsheng Palace.
entries.literal: When the emperor died, Emperor Jing Yuwen Chan honored her as empress dowager, and she resided at Hongsheng Palace.

entries.zh: 初，宣帝不豫，詔后父入禁中侍疾。
entries.en: Initially, when Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun fell ill, an edict ordered the empress's father to enter the inner palace to attend him.
entries.literal: Initially, when Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun fell ill, an edict ordered the empress's father to enter the inner palace to attend him.

entries.zh: 及大漸，劉昉、鄭譯等因矯詔以后父受遺輔政。
entries.en: When he was near death, Liu Fang, Zheng Yi, and others used a forged edict so that the empress's father received the dying charge and assisted in government.
entries.literal: When he was near death, Liu Fang, Zheng Yi, and others used a forged edict so that the empress's father received the dying charge and assisted in government.

entries.zh: 后初雖不預謀，然以嗣主幼沖，恐權在他族，不利於己，聞昉、譯已行此詔，心甚悅之。
entries.en: The empress at first had not taken part in the plot, but because the successor ruler was young and she feared power would fall to another clan to her own detriment, when she heard Liu Fang and Zheng Yi had already carried out this edict her heart was greatly pleased.
entries.literal: The empress at first had not taken part in the plot, but because the successor ruler was young and she feared power would fall to another clan to her own detriment, when she heard Liu Fang and Zheng Yi had already carried out this edict her heart was greatly pleased.

entries.zh: 後知其父有異圖，意頗不平，形於言色。
entries.en: Later, when she learned her father had other designs, she was somewhat displeased and showed it in her words and expression.
entries.literal: Later, when she learned her father had other designs, she was somewhat displeased and showed it in her words and expression.

entries.zh: 及行禪代，憤惋逾甚。
entries.en: When the abdication and dynastic change took place, her indignation and resentment grew ever greater.
entries.literal: When the abdication and dynastic change took place, her indignation and resentment grew ever greater.

entries.zh: 隋文帝旣不能譴責，內甚愧之。
entries.en: Sui Emperor Wen Yang Jian could not bring himself to reprimand her; inwardly he felt deeply ashamed toward her.
entries.literal: Sui Emperor Wen Yang Jian could not bring himself to reprimand her; inwardly he felt deeply ashamed toward her.

entries.zh: 開皇六年，封后為樂平公主。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Kaihuang, the empress was enfeoffed as Princess of Leping.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Kaihuang, the empress was enfeoffed as Princess of Leping.

entries.zh: 后又議奪其志，后誓不許，乃止。
entries.en: Others again proposed that she abandon her resolve; the empress vowed she would not consent, and the matter stopped.
entries.literal: Others again proposed that she abandon her resolve; the empress vowed she would not consent, and the matter stopped.

entries.zh: 大業五年，從煬帝幸張掖，殂於河西，年四十九。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Daye, accompanying Sui Emperor Yang on a visit to Zhangye, she died in Hexi, aged forty-nine.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Daye, accompanying Sui Emperor Yang on a visit to Zhangye, she died in Hexi, aged forty-nine.

entries.zh: 煬帝還京，詔有司備禮，祔葬后於定陵。
entries.en: When Sui Emperor Yang returned to the capital, an edict ordered the responsible offices to prepare rites and had her buried by joint interment at Dingling.
entries.literal: When Sui Emperor Yang returned to the capital, an edict ordered the responsible offices to prepare rites and had her buried by joint interment at Dingling.

entries.zh: 宣帝朱皇后名滿月，吳人也。
entries.en: Empress Zhu, consort of Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun, was named Manyue; she was a native of Wu.
entries.literal: Empress Zhu, consort of Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun, was named Manyue; she was a native of Wu.

entries.zh: 其家坐事，沒入東宮。
entries.en: Her family was implicated in a crime and confiscated into the Eastern Palace.
entries.literal: Her family was implicated in a crime and confiscated into the Eastern Palace.

entries.zh: 帝之為太子，后被選掌帝衣服。
entries.en: While Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun was crown prince, she was selected to manage his clothing.
entries.literal: While Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun was crown prince, she was selected to manage his clothing.

entries.zh: 帝年少，召而幸之，遂生靜帝。
entries.en: The emperor was young; he summoned and favored her, and she bore Emperor Jing Yuwen Chan.
entries.literal: The emperor was young; he summoned and favored her, and she bore Emperor Jing Yuwen Chan.

entries.zh: 大象元年，立為天元帝后，尋改為天皇后。
entries.en: First year of Daxiang, she was installed as empress of the Heavenly Primordial Emperor; soon after she was retitled Heavenly Empress.
entries.literal: First year of Daxiang, she was installed as empress of the Heavenly Primordial Emperor; soon after she was retitled Heavenly Empress.

entries.zh: 二年，又改為天大皇后。
entries.en: Second year, she was again retitled Grand Heavenly Empress.
entries.literal: Second year, she was again retitled Grand Heavenly Empress.

entries.zh: 册曰：「咨爾彌宣四德，訓范六宮，軒庭列序，堯門表慶，嘉稱旣降，盛典宜膺。
entries.en: The edict of investiture stated: "I address you thus: You have fully displayed the four virtues and set the pattern for the six palaces; the court ranks in proper order, and the Gate of Yao proclaims celebration. Worthy acclaim has descended; the grand ceremony is fittingly yours to receive.
entries.literal: The edict of investiture stated: "I address you thus: You have fully displayed the four virtues and set the pattern for the six palaces; the court ranks in proper order, and the Gate of Yao proclaims celebration. Worthy acclaim has descended; the grand ceremony is fittingly yours to receive.

entries.zh: 爾其飾性履道，無愆禮正，永固休祉，可不慎歟。」
entries.en: Adorn your nature and walk the Way, without fault in ritual propriety; may blessed fortune endure forever—can you not be careful?"
entries.literal: Adorn your nature and walk the Way, without fault in ritual propriety; may blessed fortune endure forever—can you not be careful?"

entries.zh: 后本非良家子，又年長於帝十餘歲，疎賤無寵。
entries.en: The empress was not originally from a good family; she was also more than ten years older than the emperor, distant and lowly, and without favor.
entries.literal: The empress was not originally from a good family; she was also more than ten years older than the emperor, distant and lowly, without favor.

entries.zh: 以靜帝故，特尊崇之，班亞楊皇后焉。
entries.en: Because of Emperor Jing Yuwen Chan, she was specially honored and ranked just below Empress Yang.
entries.literal: Because of Emperor Jing Yuwen Chan, she was specially honored and ranked just below Empress Yang.

entries.zh: 宣帝崩，靜帝尊為帝太
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun died, Emperor Jing Yuwen Chan honored her as Imperial
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun died, Emperor Jing Yuwen Chan honored her as Imperial

entries.en: (Empress)
entries.literal: (Empress)

entries.zh: 后。
entries.en: Empress Dowager.
entries.literal: Dowager.

entries.zh: 隋開皇元年，出俗為尼，名法淨。
entries.en: In the first year of Kaihuang of Sui, she left the lay life to become a nun, taking the name Fajing.
entries.literal: In the first year of Kaihuang of Sui, she left the lay life to become a nun, taking the name Fajing.

entries.zh: 六年殂，年四十，以尼禮葬京城。
entries.en: In the sixth year she died, aged forty; she was buried in the capital by rites for nuns.
entries.literal: In the sixth year she died, aged forty; she was buried in the capital by rites for nuns.

entries.zh: 宣帝陳皇后名月儀，自云潁川人，大將軍山提第八女也。
entries.en: Empress Chen, consort of Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun, was named Yueyi; she claimed to be from Yingchuan, the eighth daughter of Grand General Shanti.
entries.literal: Empress Chen, consort of Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun, was named Yueyi; she claimed to be from Yingchuan, the eighth daughter of Grand General Shanti.

entries.zh: 大象元年六月，以選入宮，拜為德妃。
entries.en: Sixth month of the first year of Daxiang, selected to enter the palace, she was appointed Virtuous Consort.
entries.literal: Sixth month of the first year of Daxiang, selected to enter the palace, she was appointed Virtuous Consort.

entries.zh: 月餘，立為天左皇后。
entries.en: After a month and more, she was installed as Heavenly Left Empress.
entries.literal: After a month and more, she was installed as Heavenly Left Empress.

entries.zh: 二年二月，改天左大皇后。
entries.en: Second month of the second year, she was retitled Grand Heavenly Left Empress.
entries.literal: Second month of the second year, she was retitled Grand Heavenly Left Empress.

entries.zh: 册曰：「咨爾儀範柔閑，操履凝潔，淑問彰於遠近，令則冠於宮闈。
entries.en: The edict of investiture stated: "I address you thus: Your bearing is gentle and serene, your conduct pure and unstained; your fine reputation shines near and far, and your exemplary rule crowns the inner palace.
entries.literal: The edict of investiture stated: "I address you thus: Your bearing is gentle and serene, your conduct pure and unstained; your fine reputation shines near and far, and your exemplary rule crowns the inner palace.

entries.zh: 是用申彼寵章，加茲徽號。
entries.en: Therefore I extend this favor and bestow this honored title.
entries.literal: Therefore I extend this favor and bestow this honored title.

entries.zh: 爾其復禮問詩，披圖顧史，永隆嘉命，可不慎歟。」
entries.en: Return to rites and to the Book of Odes, unfold the charts and consult the histories; may this honored mandate flourish forever—can you not be careful?"
entries.literal: Return to rites and to the Book of Odes, unfold the charts and consult the histories; may this honored mandate flourish forever—can you not be careful?"

entries.zh: 三月，又詔曰：「正內之重，風化之基，嘉耦之制，代多殊典。
entries.en: Third month, another edict stated: "The weight of the inner court is the foundation of transformation by custom; the institution of worthy marriage differs in each age with many distinct precedents.
entries.literal: Third month, another edict stated: "The weight of the inner court is the foundation of transformation by custom; the institution of worthy marriage differs in each age with many distinct precedents.

entries.zh: 軒、嚳繼軌，次妃並四；
entries.en: Xuan and Ku continued the precedent, and secondary consorts numbered four together;
entries.literal: Xuan and Ku continued the precedent, and secondary consorts numbered four together;

entries.zh: 虞舜受命，厥娶猶三。
entries.en: when Shun of Yu received the mandate, his marriages still numbered three.
entries.literal: when Shun of Yu received the mandate, his marriages still numbered three.

entries.zh: 禮非相襲，隨時不無。
entries.en: Rites are not simply inherited; in keeping with the times there is always change.
entries.literal: Rites are not simply inherited; in keeping with the times there is always change.

entries.zh: 朕祗承寶圖，載弘徽號，自我改作，超革先古。
entries.en: We reverently receive the sacred chart, bearing forth grand titles; from now we remake them, surpassing and reforming antiquity.
entries.literal: We reverently receive the sacred chart, bearing forth grand titles; from now we remake them, surpassing and reforming antiquity.

entries.zh: 曰天元居極，五帝所以仰崇；
entries.en: Thus the Heavenly Primordial occupies the apex, and the Five Emperors were therefore revered on high;
entries.literal: Thus the Heavenly Primordial occupies the apex, and the Five Emperors were therefore revered on high;

entries.zh: 王者稱尊，列後於焉上儷。
entries.en: when the king is called exalted, the ranked consorts stand paired with him above.
entries.literal: when the king is called exalted, the ranked consorts stand paired with him above.

entries.zh: 且坤儀比德，土數惟五，旣縟恒典，宜取斯儀。
entries.en: Moreover the queenly figure matches virtue, and the earth's number is five; since the constant rites are already elaborate, this measure should be taken.
entries.literal: Moreover the queenly figure matches virtue, and the earth's number is five; since the constant rites are already elaborate, this measure should be taken.

entries.zh: 四大皇后外，可增置天中大皇后一人。
entries.en: Beyond the four great empresses, one Heavenly Central Grand Empress may additionally be established.
entries.literal: Beyond the four great empresses, one Heavenly Central Grand Empress may additionally be established.

entries.zh: 天中大皇后爰主粢盛，徽音日躋，肇建嘉名，宜膺顯册。」
entries.en: The Heavenly Central Grand Empress shall preside over the sacrificial grain; her fine renown daily ascends; this auspicious title is newly established and fittingly receives the manifest proclamation."
entries.literal: The Heavenly Central Grand Empress shall preside over the sacrificial grain; her fine renown daily ascends; this auspicious title is newly established and fittingly receives the manifest proclamation."

entries.zh: 於是以后為天中大皇后。
entries.en: Thereupon the empress was made Heavenly Central Grand Empress.
entries.literal: Thereupon the empress was made Heavenly Central Grand Empress.

entries.zh: 帝崩，后出家為尼，改名華光。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun died, the empress left home to become a nun, changing her name to Huaguang.
entries.literal: When the emperor died, the empress left home to become a nun, changing her name to Huaguang.

entries.zh: 宣帝尉遲皇后名熾繁，蜀國公迥之孫女。
entries.en: Empress Yuchi, consort of Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun, was named Chifan, granddaughter of Duke of Shu Yuchi Jiong.
entries.literal: Empress Yuchi, consort of Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun, was named Chifan, granddaughter of Duke of Shu Yuchi Jiong.

entries.zh: 有美色。
entries.en: She had beautiful features.
entries.literal: She had beautiful features.

entries.zh: 初適杞國公亮子西陽公溫，以宗婦例入朝，帝逼而幸之。
entries.en: Initially she married Wen, Duke of Xiyang, son of Liang, Duke of Qi State; entering court by the precedent for consorts of the imperial clan, Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun forced and favored her.
entries.literal: Initially she married Wen, Duke of Xiyang, son of Liang, Duke of Qi State; entering court by the precedent for consorts of the imperial clan, the emperor forced and favored her.

entries.zh: 及亮謀逆，帝誅溫，進後入宮，拜為長貴妃。
entries.en: When Liang plotted rebellion, the emperor executed Wen and had her enter the palace, appointing her Senior Noble Consort.
entries.literal: When Liang plotted rebellion, the emperor executed Wen and had her enter the palace, appointing her Senior Noble Consort.

entries.zh: 大象二年三月，立為天左大皇后。
entries.en: Third month of the second year of Daxiang, she was installed as Grand Heavenly Left Empress.
entries.literal: Third month of the second year of Daxiang, she was installed as Grand Heavenly Left Empress.

entries.zh: 册曰：「咨爾門膺積善，躬表靈貺，徽音茂德，朕實嘉之。
entries.en: The edict of investiture stated: "I address you thus: Your house has received accumulated merit; your person displays heaven's favor; your fine renown and abundant virtue—I truly commend them.
entries.literal: The edict of investiture stated: "I address you thus: Your house has received accumulated merit; your person displays heaven's favor; your fine renown and abundant virtue—I truly commend them.

entries.zh: 是用弘茲盛典，申彼寵章。
entries.en: Therefore I extend this grand ceremony and convey this favor.
entries.literal: Therefore I extend this grand ceremony and convey this favor.

entries.zh: 爾其克慎厥猷，寅荅景命，永承休烈，可不慎歟。」
entries.en: Diligently heed your course, reverently answer heaven's mandate, and forever inherit glorious fortune—can you not be careful?"
entries.literal: Diligently heed your course, reverently answer heaven's mandate, and forever inherit glorious fortune—can you not be careful?"

entries.zh: 帝崩，后出俗為尼，改名華首。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun died, the empress left the lay life to become a nun, changing her name to Huashou.
entries.literal: When the emperor died, the empress left the lay life to become a nun, changing her name to Huashou.

entries.zh: 隋開皇十五年，殂，年三十。
entries.en: In the fifteenth year of Kaihuang of Sui, she died, aged thirty.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year of Kaihuang of Sui, she died, aged thirty.

entries.zh: 靜帝司馬皇后名令姬，柱國、滎陽公消難之女。
entries.en: Empress Sima, consort of Emperor Jing Yuwen Chan, was named Lingji, daughter of Pillar of State and Duke of Xingyang Xiaonan.
entries.literal: Empress Sima, consort of Emperor Jing Yuwen Chan, was named Lingji, daughter of Pillar of State and Duke of Xingyang Xiaonan.

entries.zh: 大象元年二月，宣帝傳位於帝，七月，為帝納為皇后。
entries.en: Second month of the first year of Daxiang, Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun transferred the throne to Emperor Jing; seventh month, she was taken in marriage for the emperor as empress.
entries.literal: Second month of the first year of Daxiang, Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun transferred the throne to Emperor Jing; seventh month, she was taken in marriage for the emperor as empress.

entries.zh: 冊曰：「坤道成形，厚德於焉載物；
entries.en: The edict of investiture stated: "The way of earth takes form; thick virtue therein bears all things;
entries.literal: The edict of investiture stated: "The way of earth takes form; thick virtue therein bears all things;

entries.zh: 陰精迭運，重光所以麗天。
entries.en: the essence of yin cycles in succession; double glory thereby adorns heaven.
entries.literal: the essence of yin cycles in succession; double glory thereby adorns heaven.

entries.zh: 在昔皇王，膺乾御曆，內政為助，昭被圖篆。
entries.en: In former ages emperors and kings received heaven's mandate to govern the calendar; inner governance assisted, manifest upon the imperial registers.
entries.literal: In former ages emperors and kings received heaven's mandate to govern the calendar; inner governance assisted, manifest upon the imperial registers.

entries.zh: 惟爾門積慶靈，家韜休烈，徽音令範，無背一時。
entries.en: Your clan has accumulated blessed spirit, your house harbors glorious merit, fine renown and worthy example without peer in the age.
entries.literal: Your clan has accumulated blessed spirit, your house harbors glorious merit, fine renown and worthy example without peer in the age.

entries.zh: 是用命爾，作儷皇極。
entries.en: Therefore I command you to be consort at the imperial apex.
entries.literal: Therefore I command you to be consort at the imperial apex.

entries.zh: 爾其克勵婉心，肅膺盛典，追皇、英之逸軌，庶任、姒之芳塵，褘翟有光，粢盛無怠，雖休勿休，以隆嘉祚。」
entries.en: Diligently cultivate a gentle heart, reverently undertake the grand ceremony; follow the exalted tracks of Huangdi and Yingdi, approach the fragrant traces of Ren and Si; may your ceremonial robes shine, sacrificial grain never neglected—though at rest, do not rest, to elevate blessed fortune."
entries.literal: Diligently cultivate a gentle heart, reverently undertake the grand ceremony; follow the exalted tracks of Huangdi and Yingdi, approach the fragrant traces of Ren and Si; may your ceremonial robes shine, sacrificial grain never neglected—though at rest, do not rest, to elevate blessed fortune."

entries.zh: 二年九月，隋文帝以后父擁眾奔陳，廢后為庶人。
entries.en: Ninth month of the second year, because the empress's father rallied troops and fled to Chen, Sui Emperor Wen Yang Jian deposed the empress to commoner status.
entries.literal: Ninth month of the second year, because the empress's father rallied troops and fled to Chen, Sui Emperor Wen Yang Jian deposed the empress to commoner status.

entries.zh: 後嫁為隋司
entries.en: Later she married as wife of Sui's
entries.literal: Later she married as wife of Sui's

entries.en: (Zhou)
entries.literal: (Zhou)

entries.zh: 〔隸〕刺史李丹妻，于今尚存。
entries.en: Sili Inspector Li Dan; she remains alive to this day.
entries.literal: Sili Inspector Li Dan; she remains alive to this day.

entries.zh: 文帝元皇后，魏孝武帝之妹。
entries.en: Empress Yuan, consort of Emperor Wen Yuwen Tai, was a younger sister of Emperor Xiaowu of Wei.
entries.literal: Empress Yuan, consort of Emperor Wen Yuwen Tai, was a younger sister of Emperor Xiaowu of Wei.

entries.zh: 初封平原公主，適開府張歡。
entries.en: Initially enfeoffed as Princess of Pingyuan, she was given in marriage to Zhang Huan, opening-the-feudatory.
entries.literal: Initially enfeoffed as Princess of Pingyuan, she was given in marriage to Zhang Huan, opening-the-feudatory.

entries.zh: 歡性貪殘，遇后無禮，又嘗殺后侍婢。
entries.en: Huan was greedy and cruel; he treated the empress without courtesy, and once even killed one of her serving maids.
entries.literal: Huan was greedy and cruel; he treated the empress without courtesy, and once even killed her serving maid.

entries.zh: 后怒，訴之於帝，帝乃執歡殺之。
entries.en: The empress in anger appealed to the emperor, and the emperor had Huan seized and executed.
entries.literal: The empress in anger complained to the emperor, and the emperor had Huan seized and executed.

entries.zh: 改封后為馮翊公主，以配太祖，生孝閔帝。
entries.en: The empress was re-enfeoffed as Princess of Fengyi and given in marriage to Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai; she bore Emperor Min Yuwen Jue.
entries.literal: The empress was re-enfeoffed as Princess of Fengyi and given as wife to the Grand Progenitor; she bore Emperor Min Yuwen Jue.

entries.zh: 大統七年，薨。
entries.en: In the seventh year of Datong she died.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Datong she died.

entries.zh: 魏恭帝三年十二月，合葬成陵。
entries.en: In the twelfth month of the third year of Emperor Gong of Wei, she was buried with him at Chengling.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month of the third year of Emperor Gong of Wei, she was buried with him at Chengling.

entries.zh: 孝閔帝踐祚，追尊為王后。
entries.en: When Emperor Min Yuwen Jue ascended the throne, she was posthumously honored as queen.
entries.literal: When Emperor Min Yuwen Jue ascended the throne, she was posthumously honored as queen.

entries.zh: 武成初，又追尊為皇后。
entries.en: At the beginning of Wucheng, she was again posthumously honored as empress.
entries.literal: In the beginning of Wucheng, she was again posthumously honored as empress.

entries.zh: 什肥年十五而惠公歿，自傷早孤，事母以孝聞。
entries.en: Shifen was fifteen when Duke Hui died; grieving his early loss, he served his mother with a filial devotion that became renowned.
entries.literal: Shifen was fifteen when Duke Hui died; grieving his early orphanhood, he served his mother with filial piety that became renowned.

entries.zh: 永安中，太祖入關，什肥不能離母，遂留晉陽。
entries.en: In the Yong'an era (528–530), when Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai entered Guan, Shifen could not leave his mother and remained at Jinyang.
entries.literal: In the Yong'an era (528–530), the Grand Progenitor entered Guan; Shifen could not leave his mother and therefore remained at Jinyang.

entries.zh: 及太祖定秦、隴，什肥為齊神武所害。
entries.en: After Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai had pacified Qin and Long, Shifen was killed by Gao Huan.
entries.literal: When the Grand Progenitor had pacified Qin and Long, Shifen was killed by Emperor Shenwu of Northern Qi.

entries.zh: 保定初，追贈大將軍、小冢宰、大都督、冀定等州諸軍事、冀州刺史。
entries.en: At the beginning of Baoding (561), Shifen was posthumously granted grand general, junior grand chancellor, chief commander, commander of all military affairs in Ji and Ding provinces, and governor of Ji Province.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Baoding, he was posthumously granted grand general, junior grand chancellor, chief commander, commander of all military affairs in Ji and Ding provinces, and governor of Ji Province.

entries.zh: 襲爵邵國公。
entries.en: He inherited the title Duke of Shao.
entries.literal: He inherited the title Duke of Shao state.

entries.zh: 諡曰景。
entries.en: His posthumous title was Jing (Resplendent).
entries.literal: His posthumous title was Jing.

entries.zh: 子冑嗣。
entries.en: His son Yuwen Zhou succeeded.
entries.literal: His son Zhou succeeded.

entries.zh: 導字菩薩。
entries.en: Yuwen Dao, style name Pusa.
entries.literal: Dao, style name Pusa.

entries.zh: 少雄豪，有仁惠，太祖愛之。
entries.en: In youth he was bold and heroic, possessed benevolence and kindness, and Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai loved him.
entries.literal: In youth he was bold and heroic, possessed benevolence and kindness, and the Grand Progenitor loved him.

entries.zh: 初與諸父在葛榮軍中，榮敗，遷晉陽。
entries.en: At first he was with his uncles in Ge Rong's army; when Ge Rong was defeated, they were relocated to Jinyang.
entries.literal: At first he was with his uncles in Ge Rong's army; when Rong was defeated, they were relocated to Jinyang.

entries.zh: 及太祖隨賀拔岳入關，導從而西，常從征伐。
entries.en: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai followed Helba Yue into Guan, Yuwen Dao followed west and constantly joined the campaigns.
entries.literal: When the Grand Progenitor followed Helba Yue into Guan, Dao followed west and constantly joined the campaigns.

entries.zh: 太祖討侯莫陳悅，以導為都督，鎮原州。
entries.en: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai campaigned against Houmochen Yue, he made Yuwen Dao commander and garrisoned Yuan Province.
entries.literal: The Grand Progenitor campaigned against Houmochen Yue and made Dao commander, garrisoning Yuan Province.

entries.zh: 及悅敗，北走出故塞，導率騎追之，至牽屯山及悅，斬之，傳首京師。
entries.en: When Houmochen Yue was defeated and fled north through the old frontier pass, Yuwen Dao led cavalry in pursuit, caught him at Qiantun Mountain, beheaded him, and sent his head to the capital.
entries.literal: When Yue was defeated and fled north through the old frontier pass, Dao led cavalry in pursuit, reached Qiantun Mountain, caught Yue, beheaded him, and sent his head to the capital.

entries.zh: 以功封饒陽縣侯，邑五百戶，拜冠軍將軍，加通直散騎常侍。
entries.en: For his merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Raoyang county with a fief of five hundred households, appointed Champion General, and given the additional post of Regular Attendant through direct connection.
entries.literal: For his merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Raoyang county, fief of five hundred households, appointed Champion General, and given the additional post of Regular Attendant through direct connection.

entries.zh: 魏文帝卽位，以定策功，進爵為公，增邑五百戶，拜使持節、散騎常侍、車騎大將軍、左光祿大夫。
entries.en: When Western Wei Emperor Wen acceded, for merit in settling the succession he was advanced to duke, his fief was increased by five hundred households, and he was appointed bearer of staff of authority, Regular Attendant Imperial Secretary, chariots-and-cavalry grand general, and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
entries.literal: When Wei Emperor Wen acceded, for merit in settling the succession he was advanced to duke, his fief was increased by five hundred households, and he was appointed bearer of staff of authority, Regular Attendant Imperial Secretary, chariots-and-cavalry grand general, and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

entries.zh: 三年，太祖東征，導入宿衛，拜領軍將軍、大都督。
entries.en: In the third year (535), when Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai marched east, Yuwen Dao entered palace guard service and was appointed director of the guard and chief commander.
entries.literal: In the third year, the Grand Progenitor marched east; Dao entered palace guard service and was appointed director of the guard and chief commander.

entries.zh: 齊神武渡河侵馮翊，太祖自弘農引軍入關，導督左右禁旅會於沙苑，與齊神武戰，大破之。
entries.en: When Gao Huan crossed the Yellow River and invaded Fengyi, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai led his army into the passes from Hongnong. Yuwen Dao led the imperial guards to join him at Shayuan, where they fought Gao Huan and inflicted a crushing defeat.
entries.literal: Emperor Shenwu of Northern Qi crossed the river and invaded Fengyi; the Grand Progenitor led his army into Guan from Hongnong. Dao directed the left and right imperial guard, joined at Shayuan, fought Emperor Shenwu of Northern Qi, and inflicted a great defeat.

entries.zh: 進位儀同三司。
entries.en: He was advanced to commissioner equal to Three Excellencies.
entries.literal: He was advanced to commissioner equal to Three Excellencies.

entries.zh: 明年，魏文帝東征，留導為華州刺史。
entries.en: The next year, when Western Wei Emperor Wen marched east, Yuwen Dao was left as governor of Hua Province.
entries.literal: The next year, when Wei Emperor Wen marched east, Dao was left as governor of Hua Province.

entries.zh: 及趙青雀、于伏德、慕容思慶等作亂，導自華州率所部兵擊之，擒伏德，斬思慶。
entries.en: When Zhao Qingque, Yu Fude, Murong Siqing, and others rebelled, Yuwen Dao from Hua Province led his troops against them, captured Yu Fude, and beheaded Murong Siqing.
entries.literal: When Zhao Qingque, Yu Fude, Murong Siqing, and others rebelled, Dao from Hua Province led his troops against them, captured Fude, and beheaded Siqing.

entries.zh: 進屯渭橋，會太祖軍。
entries.en: He advanced to camp at Wei Bridge and joined Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's army.
entries.literal: He advanced to camp at Wei Bridge and joined the Grand Progenitor's army.

entries.zh: 事平，進爵章武郡公，增邑並前二千戶。
entries.en: When the affair was pacified, he was advanced to Duke of Zhangwu commandery, and his fief together with the former totaled two thousand households.
entries.literal: When the affair was pacified, he was advanced to Duke of Zhangwu commandery, and his fief together with the former totaled two thousand households.

entries.zh: 尋加侍中、開府、驃騎大將軍、太子少保。
entries.en: Soon he was additionally given palace attendant, commissioner, flying-cavalry grand general, and junior tutor of the crown prince.
entries.literal: Soon he was additionally given palace attendant, commissioner, flying-cavalry grand general, and junior tutor of the crown prince.

entries.zh: 高仲密以北豫降，太祖率諸將輔魏皇太子東征，復以導為大都督、華東雍二州諸軍事，行華州刺史。
entries.en: When Gao Zhongmi surrendered Beiyu, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai led the generals in supporting the Western Wei crown prince on an eastern campaign; Yuwen Dao was again made chief commander of military affairs in Hua, East Yong, and the two Yong provinces, and acting governor of Hua Province.
entries.literal: When Gao Zhongmi surrendered Beiyu, the Grand Progenitor led the generals in supporting the Wei crown prince on an eastern campaign; Dao was again made chief commander of military affairs in Hua, East Yong, and the two Yong provinces, and acting governor of Hua Province.

entries.zh: 導治兵訓卒，得守捍之方。
entries.en: Yuwen Dao trained troops and drilled soldiers and mastered methods of defense.
entries.literal: Dao trained troops and drilled soldiers and mastered methods of defense.

entries.zh: 及大軍不利，東魏軍追至稠桑，知關中有備，乃退。
entries.en: When the main army suffered a setback, the Eastern Wei army pursued as far as Chousang; learning that Guanzhong was prepared, they withdrew.
entries.literal: When the main army suffered a setback, the Eastern Wei army pursued as far as Chousang; learning that Guanzhong was prepared, they then withdrew.

entries.zh: 會侯景舉河南來附，遣使請援，朝議將應之，乃徵為隴右大都督、秦南等十五州諸軍事、秦州刺史。
entries.en: When Hou Jing surrendered Henan and came over, sending envoys to request aid, the court debated responding; Yuwen Dao was then summoned as chief commander of Longyou, commander of all military affairs in fifteen provinces including Qinnan, and governor of Qin Province.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing surrendered Henan and came over, sending envoys to request aid, the court debated responding; Dao was then summoned as chief commander of Longyou, commander of all military affairs in fifteen provinces including Qinnan, and governor of Qin Province.

entries.zh: 及齊氏稱帝，太祖發關中兵討之，魏文帝遣齊王廓鎮隴右，徵導還朝。
entries.en: When Northern Qi declared itself emperor, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai dispatched Guanzhong troops to campaign against it; Western Wei Emperor Wen sent Prince of Qi Kuo to garrison Longyou and summoned Yuwen Dao back to court.
entries.literal: When the Qi house declared itself emperor, the Grand Progenitor dispatched Guanzhong troops to campaign against it; Wei Emperor Wen sent Prince of Qi Kuo to garrison Longyou and summoned Dao back to court.

entries.zh: 拜大將軍、大都督、三雍二華等二十三州諸軍事，屯咸陽。
entries.en: He was appointed grand general, chief commander of all military affairs in twenty-three provinces including the Three Yong and Two Hua, and garrisoned Xianyang.
entries.literal: He was appointed grand general, chief commander of all military affairs in twenty-three provinces including the Three Yong and Two Hua, and garrisoned Xianyang.

entries.zh: 大軍還，乃旋舊鎮。
entries.en: When the main army returned, he returned to his former post.
entries.literal: When the main army returned, he then returned to his former post.

entries.zh: 杞簡公連，幼而謹厚，臨敵果毅。
entries.en: Duke Lian of Qi, Yuwen Lian, was careful and honest from childhood and resolute in battle.
entries.literal: Duke Lian of Qi, Lian, from youth was careful and honest, and in battle resolute and daring.

entries.zh: 隨德皇帝逼定州，軍於唐河，遂俱歿。
entries.en: He followed Emperor De in the advance on Ding Province, camped on the Tang River, and there both died.
entries.literal: He followed Emperor De in pressing Ding Province, encamped at the Tang River, and there both perished.

entries.zh: 保定初，追贈使持節、太傅、柱國大將軍、大司徒、大都督、定冀等十州諸軍事、定州刺史；
entries.en: At the opening of Baoding he was posthumously made commissioner bearing credentials, grand tutor, pillar-of-state general, grand minister of education, governor-general, commander-in-chief over Ding, Ji, and ten other provinces, and inspector of Ding Province;
entries.literal: At the beginning of Baoding he was posthumously granted commissioner bearing credentials, grand tutor, pillar-of-state general, grand minister of education, governor-general, commander-in-chief of military affairs in Ding, Ji, and ten other provinces, and inspector of Ding Province;

entries.zh: 封杞國公，邑五千戶；
entries.en: enfeoffed Duke of Qi, with a fief of five thousand households;
entries.literal: enfeoffed as Duke of Qi, with a fief of five thousand households;

entries.zh: 諡曰簡。
entries.en: and given the posthumous title Jian.
entries.literal: posthumous title Jian.

entries.zh: 子
entries.en: His son
entries.literal: Son

entries.en: (Guang)
entries.literal: (Guang)

entries.zh: 元寶為齊神武所害。
entries.en: Yuwen Yuanbao was killed by Gao Huan.
entries.literal: Yuanbao was killed by Emperor Shenwu of Northern Qi.

entries.zh: 保定初，追贈大將軍、小司徒、大都督、幽燕等六州諸軍事、幽州刺史。
entries.en: At the opening of Baoding he was posthumously made grand general, junior minister of education, grand governor-general, commander-in-chief over You, Yan, and six other provinces, and inspector of You Province.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Baoding he was posthumously granted grand general, junior minister of education, grand governor-general, commander-in-chief of military affairs in You, Yan, and six other provinces, and inspector of You Province.

entries.zh: 襲爵杞國公，諡曰烈。
entries.en: He inherited the dukedom of Qi and received the posthumous title Lie.
entries.literal: He inherited the title Duke of Qi; posthumous title Lie.

entries.zh: 以章武公導子亮嗣。
entries.en: Yuwen Liang, son of Duke of Zhangwu Dao, became heir.
entries.literal: Liang, son of Duke of Zhangwu Dao, succeeded to the line.

entries.zh: 子菩提，為齊神武所害。
entries.en: His son Puti was killed by Gao Huan.
entries.literal: His son Puti was killed by Emperor Shenwu of Northern Qi.

entries.zh: 保定初，追贈大將軍、小宗伯、大都督、肆恆等六州諸軍事、肆州刺史，襲爵莒國公，諡曰穆。
entries.en: At the opening of Baoding he was posthumously made grand general, junior clan elder, governor-general, commander-in-chief over Si, Heng, and six other provinces, and inspector of Si Province; he inherited the dukedom of Ju and received the posthumous title Mu.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Baoding he was posthumously granted grand general, junior clan elder, governor-general, commander-in-chief of military affairs in Si, Heng, and six other provinces, and inspector of Si Province; he inherited the title Duke of Ju; posthumous title Mu.

entries.zh: 以晉公護子至為嗣。
entries.en: Yuwen Zhi, son of Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu, succeeded to the line.
entries.literal: Zhi, son of Duke of Jin Hu, was made his heir.

entries.zh: 冑少而孤貧，頗有幹略。
entries.en: Yuwen Zhou was orphaned young and poor, yet showed considerable drive and strategic ability.
entries.literal: Zhou was orphaned young and poor, yet had considerable initiative and strategic ability.

entries.zh: 景公之見害也，以年幼下蠶室。
entries.en: When Duke Jing was killed, Yuwen Zhou, because of his youth, was sent to the castration quarters.
entries.literal: When Duke Jing was killed, because of his young age he was sent to the castration quarters.

entries.zh: 保定初，詔以晉公護子會紹景公封。
entries.en: At the beginning of Baoding (561), an edict ordered that Yuwen Hui, son of Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu, should succeed to Duke Jing's enfeoffment.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Baoding, an edict ordered that Duke of Jin Hu's son Hui should succeed to Duke Jing's enfeoffment.

entries.zh: 天和中，與齊通好，冑始歸關中。
entries.en: In the Tianhe era (566–572), when peace was made with Northern Qi, Yuwen Zhou first returned to Guanzhong.
entries.literal: In the Tianhe era (566–572), when peace with Qi was established, Zhou first returned to Guanzhong.

entries.zh: 授大將軍、開府儀同三司，襲爵邵公。
entries.en: He was granted grand general and commissioner with Three Excellencies protocol, and inherited the title Duke of Shao.
entries.literal: He was granted grand general and commissioner with Three Excellencies protocol, and inherited the title Duke of Shao.

entries.zh: 尋除宗師中大夫，進位大將軍，出為原州刺史，轉滎州刺史。
entries.en: He was soon appointed master-of-clans middle grandee, advanced to grand general, sent out as governor of Yuan Province, and transferred to governor of Xing Province.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed master-of-clans middle grandee, advanced to grand general, sent out as governor of Yuan Province, and transferred to governor of Xing Province.

entries.zh: 大象末，隋文帝輔政，冑舉州兵應尉遲迥，與清河公楊素戰，敗，遂走，追獲於石濟，遂斬之。
entries.en: At the end of the Daxiang era (579–581), when Yang Jian, Duke of Sui, served as regent, Yuwen Zhou raised provincial troops to support Yuchi Jiong; he fought Yang Su, Duke of Qinghe, was defeated, fled, was captured at Shiji, and beheaded.
entries.literal: At the end of the Daxiang era (579–581), when Emperor Wen of Sui served as regent, Zhou raised the provincial troops to support Yuchi Jiong and fought Yang Su, Duke of Qinghe. Defeated, he fled, but was caught at Shiji and beheaded.

entries.zh: 國除。
entries.en: The ducal fief was abolished.
entries.literal: The state was abolished.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「省充信等表，但增哀悼。
entries.en: The edict said: "Having read Chongxin and the others' memorial, mourning is only increased.
entries.literal: The edict said: "Having read Chongxin and the others' memorial, mourning is only increased.

entries.zh: 豳國公廣藩屏令望，宗室表儀，言著身文，行成士則。
entries.en: Yuwen Guang, Duke of Bin, screen of the realm and excellent reputation, model of the imperial clan, words manifest in conduct, conduct forms a gentleman's standard.
entries.literal: Duke of Bin state Guang, screen of the realm and excellent reputation, model of the imperial clan, words manifest in conduct, conduct forms a gentleman's standard.

entries.zh: 方憑懿戚，用匡朝政，奄丁荼蓼，便致毀滅。
entries.en: Just when one relied on excellent kin to assist court government, he suddenly met bitter hardship and was destroyed.
entries.literal: Just when one relied on excellent kin to assist court government, he suddenly met bitter hardship and was destroyed.

entries.zh: 啟手歸全，無忘雅操。
entries.en: He opened his hands and returned whole, never forgetting elegant integrity.
entries.literal: He opened his hands and returned whole, never forgetting elegant integrity.

entries.zh: 言念旣往，震于厥心。
entries.en: Speaking of the past, the heart is shaken.
entries.literal: Speaking of the past, the heart is shaken.

entries.zh: 昔河間才藻，追敘於中尉；
entries.en: Formerly Hejian's literary talent was commemorated by the Commandant of Justice;
entries.literal: Formerly Hejian's literary talent was commemorated by the Commandant of Justice;

entries.zh: 東海謙約，見稱於身後。
entries.en: Donghai's modest restraint was praised after death.
entries.literal: Donghai's modest restraint was praised after death.

entries.zh: 可斟酌前典，率由舊章。
entries.en: May former canons be consulted and old regulations followed.
entries.literal: May former canons be consulted and old regulations followed.

entries.zh: 使易簀之言，得申遺志；
entries.en: Let the words of changing the mat fulfill his dying wish;
entries.literal: Let the words of changing the mat fulfill his dying wish;

entries.zh: 黜殯之請，無虧令終。」
entries.en: the request to dismiss lavish burial not mar his fine end."
entries.literal: the request to dismiss lavish burial not mar his fine end."

entries.zh: 於是贈本官，加太保。
entries.en: Thereupon he was granted his former office and additionally made Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: Thereupon he was granted his former office and additionally made Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 葬於隴西。
entries.en: He was buried in Longxi.
entries.literal: He was buried in Longxi.

entries.zh: 所司一遵詔旨，竝存儉約。
entries.en: The responsible offices all followed the edict and together kept frugal simplicity.
entries.literal: The responsible offices all followed the edict and together kept frugal simplicity.

entries.zh: 子洽嗣。
entries.en: His son Qia succeeded.
entries.literal: His son Qia succeeded.

entries.zh: 大定中，隋文輔政，以宗室被害，國除。
entries.en: In the Dading era (581), when Yang Jian served as regent, because members of the imperial clan were killed, the ducal fief was abolished.
entries.literal: In the Dading era (581), when Sui Wen served as regent, because members of the imperial clan were killed, the state was abolished.

entries.zh: 衆字乾道。
entries.en: Zhong, styled Qiandao.
entries.literal: Zhong, style Qiandao.

entries.zh: 保定初，封天水郡公。
entries.en: At the opening of the Baoding era he was enfeoffed Duke of Tianshui Commandery.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Baoding he was enfeoffed as Duke of Tianshui Commandery.

entries.zh: 少而不惠，語默不常，人莫能測。
entries.en: From boyhood he was slow-witted; his words and silences were erratic, and no one could read him.
entries.literal: From youth he was dull-witted; in speech and silence he was unpredictable, and no one could fathom him.

entries.zh: 隋文帝踐極，初欲封為介公，後復誅之，幷二子仲和、孰倫。
entries.en: When Sui Emperor Wen Yang Jian ascended, he first meant to make Zhong Duke of Jie, but later had him killed along with his sons Zhonghe and Shulun.
entries.literal: When Sui Emperor Wen Yang Jian took the throne, at first he intended to enfeoff Zhong as Duke of Jie, but later executed him together with his two sons Zhonghe and Shulun.

entries.zh: 椿字乾壽。
entries.en: Yuwen Chun, style name Qianshou.
entries.literal: Chun, style name Qianshou.

entries.zh: 初封永昌郡公。
entries.en: At first he was enfeoffed as Duke of Yongchang commandery.
entries.literal: At first he was enfeoffed as Duke of Yongchang commandery.

entries.zh: 保定中，授開府儀同三司、宗師中大夫。
entries.en: During Baoding (561–565), he was granted commissioner with Three Excellencies protocol and master-of-clans middle grandee.
entries.literal: During Baoding, he was granted commissioner with Three Excellencies protocol and master-of-clans middle grandee.

entries.zh: 建德初，加大將軍。
entries.en: At the beginning of Jiande (572), he was advanced to grand general.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Jiande (572), he was advanced to grand general.

entries.zh: 尋除岐州刺史。
entries.en: Soon he was appointed governor of Qi Province.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed governor of Qi Province.

entries.zh: 四年，關中民饑，椿表陳其狀，璽書勞慰。
entries.en: In the fourth year (575), the people of Guanzhong suffered famine; Chun memorialized describing the situation, and an imperial letter commended and comforted him.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, the people of Guanzhong suffered famine; Chun memorialized describing the situation, and an imperial letter commended and comforted him.

entries.zh: 因令所在開倉賑卹。
entries.en: Thereupon orders were issued to open granaries everywhere for relief.
entries.literal: Thereupon orders were issued to open granaries everywhere for relief.

entries.zh: 四年，高祖東伐，椿與齊王憲攻拔武濟等五城。
entries.en: In the fourth year (575), when High Ancestor Yuwen Yong marched east, Chun together with Prince of Qi Yuwen Xian captured Wuji and four other cities.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, when High Ancestor marched east, Chun together with Prince of Qi Xian captured Wuji and four other cities.

entries.zh: 五年，高祖出晉州，椿率眾屯棲雞原。
entries.en: In the fifth year (576), when High Ancestor Yuwen Yong advanced from Jin Province, Chun led his forces to camp at Qijiyuan.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, when High Ancestor advanced from Jin Province, Chun led his forces to camp at Qijiyuan.

entries.zh: 宣帝即位，拜大司寇。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun acceded, he was appointed grand minister of justice.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan acceded, he was appointed grand minister of justice.

entries.zh: 亮誅後，詔令紹烈公封。
entries.en: After Liang was executed, an edict ordered him to continue the enfeoffment of Duke Lie.
entries.literal: After Liang was executed, an edict ordered him to continue the enfeoffment of Duke Lie.

entries.zh: 尋進位上柱國，轉大司徒。
entries.en: Soon he was advanced to superior pillar-of-state and transferred to Grand Minister of Education.
entries.literal: Soon he was advanced to superior pillar-of-state and transferred to Grand Minister of Education.

entries.zh: 大定初，為隋文帝所害，并其五子西陽公道宗、本、仁隣、武子、禮獻。
entries.en: At the beginning of Dading (581), he was killed by Yang Jian, Duke of Sui, together with his five sons: Daozong, Duke of Xiyang; Ben; Renlin; Wuzi; and Lixian.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Dading (581), he was killed by Emperor Wen of Sui, together with his five sons: Daozong, Duke of Xiyang; Ben; Renlin; Wuzi; and Lixian.

entries.zh: 莒莊公洛生，少任俠，尚武藝，及壯，有大度，好施愛士。
entries.en: Duke Luosheng of Ju, Yuwen Luosheng, was a young bravo who loved arms; grown, he was magnanimous, generous, and fond of nurturing talent.
entries.literal: Duke Luosheng of Ju, from youth was chivalrous and martial; when grown he had great breadth of mind and loved to be generous and cherish men of talent.

entries.zh: 北州賢俊，皆與之遊，而才能多出其下。
entries.en: The best men of the northern provinces sought his company, yet few matched his ability.
entries.literal: Worthy and outstanding men of the northern provinces all associated with him, yet in talent most fell below him.

entries.zh: 及葛榮破鮮于修禮，乃以洛生為漁陽王，仍領德皇帝餘衆。
entries.en: After Ge Rong defeated Xianyu Xiuli, he made Luosheng Prince of Yuyang and left him in command of Emperor De's remaining troops.
entries.literal: When Ge Rong defeated Xianyu Xiuli, he thereupon made Luosheng Prince of Yuyang and still commanded the remaining forces of Emperor De.

entries.zh: 時人皆呼為洛生王。
entries.en: Contemporaries called him the Luosheng Prince.
entries.literal: People of the time all called him Prince Luosheng.

entries.zh: 洛生善將士，帳下多驍勇。
entries.en: Luosheng knew how to lead soldiers, and many bold fighters served under his banner.
entries.literal: Luosheng was skilled in commanding troops; under his banner were many fierce warriors.

entries.zh: 至於攻戰，莫有當其鋒者，是以克獲常冠諸軍。
entries.en: In battle none could stand before his vanguard, and his victories usually topped those of every other army.
entries.literal: In attack and battle none could withstand his spearhead; therefore his captures and gains usually led all the armies.

entries.zh: 爾朱榮定山東，收諸豪傑，遷於晉陽，洛生時在虜中。
entries.en: When Erzhu Rong settled Shandong he gathered local strongmen and moved them to Jinyang; Luosheng was among the prisoners.
entries.literal: When Erzhu Rong pacified Shandong he gathered the regional champions and relocated them to Jinyang; Luosheng was then among the captives.

entries.zh: 榮雅聞其名，心憚之。
entries.en: Erzhu Rong had long known his reputation and feared him in his heart.
entries.literal: Rong had long heard his name and inwardly feared him.

entries.zh: 尋為榮所害。
entries.en: Before long Erzhu Rong had him killed.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he was killed by Rong.

entries.zh: 保定初，追贈使持節、太保、柱國大將軍、大冢宰、大宗伯、大都督、幷肆等十州諸軍事、幷州刺史；
entries.en: At the opening of Baoding he was posthumously made commissioner bearing credentials, grand guardian, pillar-of-state general, grand minister of tombs, grand clan elder, governor-general, commander-in-chief over Bing, Si, and ten other provinces, and inspector of Bing Province;
entries.literal: At the beginning of Baoding he was posthumously granted commissioner bearing credentials, grand guardian, pillar-of-state general, grand minister of tombs, grand clan elder, governor-general, commander-in-chief of military affairs in Bing, Si, and ten other provinces, and inspector of Bing Province;

entries.zh: 封莒國公，邑五千戶；
entries.en: enfeoffed Duke of Ju, with a fief of five thousand households;
entries.literal: enfeoffed as Duke of Ju, with a fief of five thousand households;

entries.zh: 諡曰莊。
entries.en: and given the posthumous title Zhuang.
entries.literal: posthumous title Zhuang.

entries.zh: 導性寬明，善於撫御，凡所引接，人皆盡誠。
entries.en: Yuwen Dao was magnanimous and clear-sighted, skilled at governing and winning people; all whom he received gave him their full loyalty.
entries.literal: Dao was magnanimous and clear-sighted, skilled at governing and winning people; all whom he received gave him their full loyalty.

entries.zh: 臨事敬慎，常若弗及。
entries.en: In affairs he was reverent and cautious, as though always falling short.
entries.literal: In affairs he was reverent and cautious, as though always falling short.

entries.zh: 太祖每出征討，導恆居守，深為吏民所附，朝廷亦以此重之。
entries.en: Whenever Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai campaigned, Yuwen Dao always remained to guard; officials and commoners were deeply attached to him, and the court valued him for this.
entries.literal: Whenever the Grand Progenitor campaigned, Dao always remained to guard; officials and commoners were deeply attached to him, and the court valued him for this.

entries.zh: 魏恭帝元年十二月，薨於上邽，年四十四。
entries.en: In the twelfth month of the first year of Western Wei Emperor Gong (554), he died at Shanggui, aged forty-four.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Wei Emperor Gong (554), he died at Shanggui, aged forty-four.

entries.zh: 魏帝遣侍中、漁陽王繩監護喪事。
entries.en: The Wei emperor sent palace attendant Prince of Yuyang Yuwen Sheng to oversee the funeral.
entries.literal: The Wei emperor sent palace attendant Prince of Yuyang Sheng to oversee the funeral.

entries.zh: 贈本官，加尚書令、秦州刺史，諡曰孝。
entries.en: He was granted his former office and additionally made Minister over the Masses and governor of Qin Province; his posthumous title was Xiao (Filial).
entries.literal: He was granted his former office and additionally made Minister over the Masses and governor of Qin Province; his posthumous title was Xiao.

entries.zh: 朝議以導撫和西戎，威恩顯著，欲令世鎮隴右，以彰厥德，乃葬於上邽城西無疆原。
entries.en: The court held that because Yuwen Dao had pacified the western Rong and his authority and kindness were conspicuous, they wished his line to command Longyou for generations to manifest his virtue; he was therefore buried on Wujiang plain west of Shanggui.
entries.literal: Court discussion held that because Dao had pacified the western Rong and his authority and kindness were prominent, they wished his line to command Longyou for generations to manifest his virtue; he was therefore buried on Wujiang plain west of Shanggui.

entries.zh: 華戎會葬有萬餘人，奠祭於路，悲號滿野，皆曰「我君捨我乎」。
entries.en: More than ten thousand Chinese and frontier peoples attended the funeral; offerings lined the road and wailing filled the wilds; all cried, "Has our lord abandoned us?"
entries.literal: More than ten thousand Chinese and frontier peoples attended the funeral; offerings lined the road and wailing filled the wilds; all cried, "Has our lord abandoned us?"

entries.zh: 大小相率，負土成墳，高五十餘尺，周迴八十餘步。
entries.en: Young and old together carried earth to form a tumulus more than fifty chi high and more than eighty paces around.
entries.literal: Young and old together carried earth to form a tumulus more than fifty chi high and more than eighty paces around.

entries.zh: 為官司所止，然後泣辭而去。
entries.en: Government officers stopped them; only then did they weep and take their leave.
entries.literal: Government officers stopped them; only then did they weep and take their leave.

entries.zh: 其遺愛見思如此。
entries.en: The affection he left behind and the longing for him were like this.
entries.literal: The affection he left behind and the longing for him were like this.

entries.zh: 天和五年，重贈太師、柱國、豳國公。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Tianhe (568), he was again posthumously granted Grand Preceptor, pillar-of-state, and Duke of Bin.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Tianhe (568), he was again posthumously granted Grand Preceptor, pillar-of-state, and Duke of Bin.

entries.zh: 導五子，廣、亮、翼、椿、眾。
entries.en: Yuwen Dao had five sons: Guang, Liang, Yi, Chun, and Zhong.
entries.literal: Dao had five sons: Guang, Liang, Yi, Chun, and Zhong.

entries.zh: 亮、椿並出後於杞。
entries.en: Liang and Chun were both given in adoption to the Qi line.
entries.literal: Liang and Chun were both given in adoption to the Qi line.

entries.zh: 廣字乾歸。
entries.en: Yuwen Guang, style name Qiangui.
entries.literal: Guang, style name Qiangui.

entries.zh: 少方嚴，好文學。
entries.en: In youth he was stern and proper and loved literature.
entries.literal: In youth he was stern and proper and loved literature.

entries.zh: 初封永昌郡公。
entries.en: At first he was enfeoffed as Duke of Yongchang commandery.
entries.literal: At first he was enfeoffed as Duke of Yongchang commandery.

entries.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，改封天水郡公。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaomin Yuwen Jue acceded, his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Tianshui commandery.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin acceded, his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Tianshui commandery.

entries.zh: 世宗即位，授驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，出為秦州刺史。
entries.en: When Shizong Yuwen Yu acceded, he was appointed flying-cavalry grand general and commissioner with Three Excellencies protocol, and sent out as governor of Qin Province.
entries.literal: When Shizong acceded, he was appointed flying-cavalry grand general and commissioner with Three Excellencies protocol, and sent out as governor of Qin Province.

entries.zh: 武成初，進位大將軍，遷梁州總管，進封蔡國公，增邑萬戶。
entries.en: In the early Wucheng era (559), he was advanced to grand general, transferred to governor-general of Liang Province, advanced to Duke of Cai, and his fief was increased by ten thousand households.
entries.literal: In the early Wucheng era (559), he was advanced to grand general, transferred to governor-general of Liang Province, advanced to Duke of Cai, and his fief was increased by ten thousand households.

entries.zh: 保定初，入為小司寇。
entries.en: At the beginning of Baoding (561), he entered court service as junior minister of justice.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Baoding (561), he entered court service as junior minister of justice.

entries.zh: 尋以本官鎮蒲州，兼知潼關等六防諸軍事。
entries.en: Soon, retaining his office, he garrisoned Pu Province and concurrently directed military affairs at Tong Pass and the six garrisons.
entries.literal: Soon, retaining his office, he garrisoned Pu Province and concurrently directed military affairs at Tong Pass and the six garrisons.

entries.zh: 二年，除秦州總管、十三州諸軍事、秦州刺史。
entries.en: In the second year (562), he was appointed governor-general of Qin Province, commander of military affairs in thirteen provinces, and governor of Qin Province.
entries.literal: In the second year (562), he was appointed governor-general of Qin Province, commander of military affairs in thirteen provinces, and governor of Qin Province.

entries.zh: 廣性明察，善綏撫，民庶畏而悅之。
entries.en: Yuwen Guang was clear-sighted and skilled at comforting and governing; the people revered and delighted in him.
entries.literal: Guang was clear-sighted and skilled at comforting and governing; the people revered and delighted in him.

entries.zh: 時晉公護諸子及廣弟杞國公亮等，服玩侈靡，踰越制度，廣獨率由禮則，又折節待士，朝野以是稱焉。
entries.en: At the time the sons of Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu and Guang's younger brother Duke of Qi Yuwen Liang and others were extravagant in dress and luxuries beyond regulations; Guang alone followed ritual propriety, humbled himself to treat scholars, and court and countryside praised him for it.
entries.literal: At the time the sons of Duke of Jin Hu and Guang's younger brother Duke of Qi Liang and others were extravagant in dress and luxuries beyond regulations; Guang alone followed ritual propriety, humbled himself to treat scholars, and court and countryside praised him for it.

entries.zh: 曾侍食於高祖，所食瓜美，持以奉進，高祖悅之。
entries.en: Once while attending a meal with High Ancestor Yuwen Yong, he found the melon delicious, presented it to the emperor, and pleased him.
entries.literal: Once while attending a meal with High Ancestor, he found the melon delicious, held it out to present it, and High Ancestor was pleased.

entries.zh: 四年，進位柱國。
entries.en: In the fourth year, he was advanced to pillar-of-state.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, he was advanced to pillar-of-state.

entries.zh: 廣以晉公護久擅威權，勸令挹損，護不能納。
entries.en: Because Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu had long monopolized authority, Guang urged him to restrain himself; Hu would not heed him.
entries.literal: Guang, because Duke of Jin Hu had long monopolized authority, urged him to restrain himself; Hu could not accept the advice.

entries.zh: 天和三年，除陝州總管，以病免。
entries.en: In the third year of Tianhe (568), he was appointed governor-general of Shan Province and was dismissed because of illness.
entries.literal: In the third year of Tianhe (568), he was appointed governor-general of Shan Province and was dismissed because of illness.

entries.zh: 及孝公追封豳國公，詔廣襲爵。
entries.en: When Duke Xiao was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Bin, an edict summoned Yuwen Guang to inherit the title.
entries.literal: When Duke Xiao was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Bin, an edict summoned Guang to inherit the title.

entries.zh: 初，廣母李氏以廣患彌年，憂而成疾，因此致沒。
entries.en: At first, Yuwen Guang's mother Lady Li, because Guang's illness had lasted years, worried herself into sickness and thereby died.
entries.literal: At first, Guang's mother Lady Li, because Guang's illness had lasted years, worried herself into sickness and thereby died.

entries.zh: 廣旣居喪，更加綿篤，乃以毀薨。
entries.en: Yuwen Guang having entered mourning, his illness grew still worse, and he died from grief-induced destruction.
entries.literal: Guang having entered mourning, his illness grew still worse, and he died from grief-induced destruction.

entries.zh: 世稱母為廣病，廣為母亡，慈孝之道，極於一門。
entries.en: The age said the mother died of Guang's illness and Guang died for his mother—filial piety and kindness reached their utmost in one clan.
entries.literal: The age said the mother died of Guang's illness and Guang died for his mother—filial piety and kindness reached their utmost in one clan.

entries.zh: 高祖素服親臨，百僚畢集。
entries.en: High Ancestor Yuwen Yong in plain white mourning garb personally attended; the hundred officials all assembled.
entries.literal: High Ancestor in plain white mourning garb personally attended; the hundred officials all assembled.

entries.zh: 其故吏儀同李充信等上表曰：臣聞資孝成忠，生民高義；
entries.en: His former subordinate commissioner-equal Li Chongxin and others submitted a memorial, saying: We have heard that nurturing filial piety completes loyalty, the highest duty among the people;
entries.literal: His former subordinate commissioner-equal Li Chongxin and others submitted a memorial, saying: We have heard that nurturing filial piety completes loyalty, the highest duty among the people;

entries.zh: 旌德樹善，有國常規。
entries.en: honoring virtue and fostering goodness is a constant rule of state.
entries.literal: honoring virtue and fostering goodness is a constant rule of state.

entries.zh: 竊惟故豳國公臣廣，懿親令望，具瞻攸在，道冠羣后，功懋維城。
entries.en: We venture to consider the late Yuwen Guang, Duke of Bin: an excellent kinsman of fine reputation, the focus of all eyes, whose conduct surpassed the feudal lords and whose merit fortified the realm.
entries.literal: We venture to consider the late Duke of Bin, subject Guang: an excellent kinsman of fine reputation, the focus of all eyes, whose conduct surpassed the feudal lords and whose merit fortified the realm.

entries.zh: 受脤建斾，威行秦、隴；
entries.en: Receiving the sacrificial flesh and raising his banner, his authority extended through Qin and Long;
entries.literal: Receiving the sacrificial flesh and raising his banner, his authority extended through Qin and Long;

entries.zh: 班條驅傳，化溢崤、函。
entries.en: dispensing regulations and dispatching couriers, his transforming influence overflowed Xiaoshan and Hangu.
entries.literal: dispensing regulations and dispatching couriers, his transforming influence overflowed Xiaoshan and Hangu.

entries.zh: 比腠理舛和，奉詔還闕，藥石所及，沉痾漸愈。
entries.en: Recently when his bodily harmony was disturbed, he obeyed an edict and returned to the capital; where medicine reached him, his grave illness gradually improved.
entries.literal: Recently when his bodily harmony was disturbed, he obeyed an edict and returned to the capital; where medicine reached him, his grave illness gradually improved.

entries.zh: 而災釁仍集，丁此窮憂，至性過人，遂增舊疾，因茲毀頓，以至薨殂。
entries.en: Yet calamities still gathered; meeting this extreme grief, his surpassing filial nature aggravated his old illness, and through this ruin and collapse he died.
entries.literal: Yet calamities still gathered; meeting this extreme grief, his surpassing filial nature aggravated his old illness, and through this ruin and collapse he died.

entries.zh: 尋繹貫切，不能自已。
entries.en: Reflecting on this, our grief is penetrating and we cannot restrain ourselves.
entries.literal: Reflecting on this, our grief is penetrating and we cannot restrain ourselves.

entries.zh: 亮字乾德。
entries.en: Yuwen Liang, style name Gandé.
entries.literal: Liang, style name Gandé.

entries.zh: 武成初，封永昌郡公。
entries.en: In the early Wucheng era (559), he was enfeoffed as Duke of Yongchang commandery.
entries.literal: In the early Wucheng era (559), he was enfeoffed as Duke of Yongchang commandery.

entries.zh: 後襲烈公爵，除開府儀同三司、梁州總管。
entries.en: Later he inherited the title Duke Lie and was appointed commissioner with Three Excellencies protocol and governor-general of Liang Province.
entries.literal: Later he inherited the title Duke Lie and was appointed commissioner with Three Excellencies protocol and governor-general of Liang Province.

entries.zh: 天和末，拜宗師中大夫，進位大將軍。
entries.en: At the end of Tianhe (572), he was appointed master-of-clans middle grandee and advanced to grand general.
entries.literal: At the end of Tianhe, he was appointed master-of-clans middle grandee and advanced to grand general.

entries.zh: 豳國公薨，以亮為秦州總管，廣之所部，悉以配焉。
entries.en: When Yuwen Guang, Duke of Bin, died, Yuwen Liang was made governor-general of Qin Province, and all troops formerly under Guang were assigned to him.
entries.literal: When the Duke of Bin died, Liang was made governor-general of Qin Province, and all troops formerly under Guang were assigned to him.

entries.zh: 亮在州甚無政績。
entries.en: Yuwen Liang achieved very little in governing the province.
entries.literal: Liang in the province had very little administrative achievement.

entries.zh: 尋進位柱國。
entries.en: Soon he was advanced to pillar-of-state.
entries.literal: Soon he was advanced to pillar-of-state.

entries.zh: 晉公護誅後，亮心不自安，唯縱酒而已。
entries.en: After Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu was executed, Yuwen Liang's heart was uneasy, and he indulged only in wine.
entries.literal: After Duke of Jin Hu was executed, Liang's heart was uneasy, and he indulged only in wine.

entries.zh: 高祖手勑讓之。
entries.en: High Ancestor Yuwen Yong personally wrote a reprimanding edict.
entries.literal: High Ancestor personally wrote a reprimanding edict.

entries.zh: 建德中，高祖東伐，以亮為右第二軍總管。
entries.en: During Jiande (572–578), when High Ancestor Yuwen Yong marched east, Yuwen Liang was made commander of the second army on the right.
entries.literal: During Jiande (572–578), when High Ancestor marched east, Liang was made commander of the second army on the right.

entries.zh: 幷州平，進位上柱國。
entries.en: When Bing Province was pacified, he was advanced to superior pillar-of-state.
entries.literal: When Bing Province was pacified, he was advanced to superior pillar-of-state.

entries.zh: 仍從平鄴，遷大司徒。
entries.en: He still followed in pacifying Ye and was transferred to Grand Minister of Education.
entries.literal: He still followed in pacifying Ye and was transferred to Grand Minister of Education.

entries.zh: 宣帝卽位，出為安州總管。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun acceded, he was sent out as governor-general of An Province.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan acceded, he was sent out as governor-general of An Province.

entries.zh: 大象初，詔以亮為行軍總管，與元帥、鄖國公韋孝寬等伐陳。
entries.en: Early in the Daxiang era (579), an edict made Yuwen Liang campaign commander-in-chief; with the supreme commander Wei Xiaokuan, Duke of Yun, and others he marched against Chen.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Daxiang, an edict appointed Liang campaign commander-in-chief; together with the commander-in-chief Wei Xiaokuan, Duke of Yun, and others he attacked Chen.

entries.zh: 亮自安陸道攻拔黃城，輒破江側民村，掠其生口，以賜士卒。
entries.en: Liang took the Anlu route, captured Huangcheng, repeatedly plundered riverside villages, seized captives, and gave them to his soldiers as booty.
entries.literal: Liang by the Anlu route captured Huangcheng, repeatedly raided villages on the river's south bank, took captives, and distributed them to the troops as reward.

entries.zh: 軍還至豫州，亮密謂長史杜士峻曰：「主上淫縱滋甚，社稷將危。
entries.en: When the army reached Yu Province, Liang secretly told Chief Clerk Du Shijun: "The emperor's excess grows worse by the day and the realm is in danger.
entries.literal: When the army returned to Yu Province, Liang secretly said to Chief Clerk Du Shijun: "The sovereign's debauchery grows ever worse; the altars of state are in peril.

entries.zh: 吾旣忝宗枝，不忍坐見傾覆。
entries.en: As a member of the royal house, I cannot sit idle while everything collapses.
entries.literal: I am already of the imperial clan; I cannot bear to sit by and watch ruin.

entries.zh: 今若襲取鄖國公而幷其衆，推諸父為主，鼓行而前，誰敢不從。」
entries.en: If we surprise the Duke of Yun, take his army, set up one of our uncles as ruler, and march forward to the drum, who would refuse to follow?"
entries.literal: If we now seize the Duke of Yun and merge his forces, install one of the paternal uncles as ruler, and advance with drums beating, who would dare not follow?"

entries.zh: 遂夜將數百騎襲孝寬營。
entries.en: That night he led several hundred riders in a night assault on Xiaokuan's camp.
entries.literal: Thereupon by night he led several hundred horsemen in a surprise attack on Xiaokuan's camp.

entries.zh: 會亮國官茹寬知其謀，先以馳告，孝寬乃設備。
entries.en: Liang's household officer Ru Kuan learned of the plot, sent word ahead by fast courier, and Xiaokuan made ready.
entries.literal: As it happened, Liang's household officer Ru Kuan learned of the plot and first sent a fast rider to report it; Xiaokuan thereupon made preparations.

entries.zh: 亮不克，遯走，孝寬追斬之。
entries.en: Liang failed, fled, and Xiaokuan ran him down and executed him.
entries.literal: Liang did not succeed, fled, and Xiaokuan pursued and beheaded him.

entries.zh: 子明坐亮誅。
entries.en: His son Ming was put to death on account of Liang's rebellion.
entries.literal: His son Ming was executed because of Liang's crime.

entries.zh: 詔以亮弟椿為烈公後。
entries.en: An edict made Liang's younger brother Chun heir to Duke Lie.
entries.literal: An edict appointed Liang's younger brother Chun to continue the line of Duke Lie.

entries.en: (Zhen)
entries.literal: (Zhen)

entries.zh: 貢字乾禎。
entries.en: Gong, styled Qianzhen.
entries.literal: Gong, courtesy name Qianzhen.

entries.zh: 宣帝初，被誅，國除。
entries.en: At the opening of Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun's reign he was executed and the fief abolished.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xuan's reign he was executed and the fief abolished.

entries.zh: 虞國公仲，德皇帝從父兄也。
entries.en: Duke Zhong of Yuguo, Yuwen Zhong, was a paternal cousin of Emperor De.
entries.literal: Duke Zhong of Yuguo, Zhong, was a paternal cousin of Emperor De.

entries.zh: 卒於代。
entries.en: He died in Dai.
entries.literal: He died in Dai.

entries.zh: 保定初，追贈使持節、太傅、柱國大將軍、大司徒、大都督、燕平等十州諸軍事、燕州刺史；
entries.en: At the opening of Baoding he was posthumously made commissioner bearing credentials, grand tutor, pillar-of-state general, grand minister of education, governor-general, commander-in-chief over Yan, Ping, and ten other provinces, and inspector of Yan Province;
entries.literal: At the beginning of Baoding he was posthumously granted commissioner bearing credentials, grand tutor, pillar-of-state general, grand minister of education, governor-general, commander-in-chief of military affairs in Yan, Ping, and ten other provinces, and inspector of Yan Province;

entries.zh: 封虞國公，邑三千戶。
entries.en: enfeoffed Duke of Yuguo, with a fief of three thousand households.
entries.literal: enfeoffed as Duke of Yuguo, with a fief of three thousand households.

entries.zh: 子興嗣。
entries.en: His son Xing succeeded.
entries.literal: His son Xing succeeded.

entries.zh: 興生，兵亂，與仲相失，年又冲幼，莫知其戚屬遠近。
entries.en: Xing was born amid military turmoil; he was separated from Zhong while still very young and did not know the nearness or distance of his kinship.
entries.literal: Xing was born amid military turmoil; he was separated from Zhong while still very young and did not know the nearness or distance of his kinship.

entries.zh: 與太祖兄弟，初不相識。
entries.en: He and Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's brothers at first did not know one another.
entries.literal: He and the Grand Progenitor's brothers at first did not know one another.

entries.zh: 齊神武寇沙苑，興預在行間，軍敗被虜，隨例散配諸軍。
entries.en: When Gao Huan attacked at Shayuan, Yuwen Xing was serving in the ranks. His army was defeated and he was captured; under the usual practice for captives, he was assigned to one of the army units.
entries.literal: When Emperor Shenwu of Northern Qi attacked Shayuan, Xing was in the ranks; his army was defeated, he was captured, and according to standard practice he was dispersed and assigned to one of the armies.

entries.zh: 興性弘厚，有志度，雖流離世故，而風範可觀。
entries.en: Xing was broad and generous by nature, with breadth of purpose; though adrift through worldly vicissitudes, his bearing was admirable.
entries.literal: Xing's nature was broad and generous, with purpose and measure; though adrift through worldly vicissitudes, his bearing was admirable.

entries.zh: 魏恭帝二年，舉賢良，除本郡丞，徙長𨻽縣令。
entries.en: In the second year of Western Wei Emperor Gong (555), he was recommended as worthy and good, appointed assistant administrator of his home commandery, and transferred to magistrate of Changshi county.
entries.literal: In the second year of Wei Emperor Gong (555), he was recommended as worthy and good, appointed assistant administrator of his home commandery, and transferred to magistrate of Changshi county.

entries.zh: 保定二年，詔仲子興始附屬籍。
entries.en: In the second year of Baoding (562), an edict had Zhong's son Xing entered on the clan register.
entries.literal: In the second year of Baoding (562), an edict had Zhong's son Xing entered on the clan register.

entries.zh: 高祖以興宗戚近屬，尊禮之甚厚，拜使持節、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、都督，封大寧郡公。
entries.en: High Ancestor Yuwen Yong, because Xing was a close imperial kinsman, honored and treated him very generously, appointing him bearer of staff of authority, flying-cavalry grand general, commissioner with Three Excellencies protocol, and commander, and enfeoffing him as Duke of Daning commandery.
entries.literal: High Ancestor, because Xing was a close imperial kinsman, honored and treated him very generously, appointing him bearer of staff of authority, flying-cavalry grand general, commissioner with Three Excellencies protocol, and commander, and enfeoffing him as Duke of Daning commandery.

entries.zh: 尋除宗師中大夫。
entries.en: Soon he was appointed master-of-clans middle grandee.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed master-of-clans middle grandee.

entries.zh: 四年，出為涇州刺史。
entries.en: In the fourth year (565), he was sent out as governor of Jing Province.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, he was sent out as governor of Jing Province.

entries.zh: 五年，又徵拜宗師，加大將軍，襲爵虞國公。
entries.en: In the fifth year (566), he was again summoned and appointed master-of-clans, advanced to grand general, and inherited the title Duke of Yuguo.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, he was again summoned and appointed master-of-clans, advanced to grand general, and inherited the title Duke of Yuguo.

entries.zh: 天和二年薨，高祖親臨，慟焉。
entries.en: In the second year of Tianhe (567) he died; High Ancestor Yuwen Yong came in person and grieved.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tianhe (567) he died; High Ancestor came in person and grieved.

entries.zh: 詔大司空、申國公李穆監護喪事。
entries.en: An edict appointed Li Mu, Duke of Shen and grand minister of works, to oversee the funeral.
entries.literal: An edict appointed Li Mu, Duke of Shen and grand minister of works, to oversee the funeral.

entries.zh: 贈使持節、柱國大將軍、大都督、恆幽等六州諸軍事、恆州刺史，諡曰靖。
entries.en: He was posthumously granted bearer of staff of authority, pillar-of-state grand general, chief commander, commander of military affairs in six provinces including Heng and You, and governor of Heng Province; his posthumous title was Jing (Tranquil).
entries.literal: He was posthumously granted bearer of staff of authority, pillar-of-state grand general, chief commander, commander of military affairs in six provinces including Heng and You, and governor of Heng Province; his posthumous title was Jing.

entries.zh: 子洛嗣。
entries.en: His son Luo succeeded.
entries.literal: His son Luo succeeded.

entries.zh: 洛字永洛。
entries.en: Luo, styled Yongluo.
entries.literal: Luo, courtesy name Yongluo.

entries.zh: 九歲，命為虞國公世子。
entries.en: At nine he was appointed heir to the Duke of Yuguo.
entries.literal: At nine years of age he was appointed heir to the Duke of Yuguo.

entries.zh: 天和四年，詔襲興爵。
entries.en: In Tianhe 4 (569) an edict made him inherit Xing's title.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Tianhe, an edict had him inherit Xing's title.

entries.zh: 建德初，拜使持節、車騎大將軍、儀同三司。
entries.en: At the opening of Jiande he was made commissioner bearing credentials, chariot-and-cavalry general, and grandmaster with privilege equal to the Three Excellencies.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Jiande he was appointed commissioner bearing credentials, chariot-and-cavalry general, and grandmaster with privilege equal to the Three Excellencies.

entries.zh: 及靜帝崩，隋文帝以洛為介國公，為隋室賓云。
entries.en: When Emperor Jing Yuwen Chan died, Sui Emperor Wen Yang Jian made Luo Duke of Jie, declaring that he would be a guest of the Sui house.
entries.literal: When Emperor Jing Yuwen Chan died, Sui Emperor Wen Yang Jian made Luo Duke of Jie, [saying he would be] a guest of the Sui house.

entries.zh: 邵惠公顥 子什肥 導
entries.en: Duke Hui of Shao Yuwen Hao; sons Shifen and Yuwen Dao
entries.literal: Duke Hui of Shao Hao; sons Shifen, Dao

entries.en: (Hu)
entries.literal: (Hu)

entries.zh: 什肥子胄 導子廣 亮 翼 椿 衆 杞簡公連 莒莊公洛生 子菩提 虞國公仲 子興
entries.en: Shifen's son Yuwen Zhou; Yuwen Dao's sons Guang, Liang, Yi, Chun, and Zhong; Duke Jian of Qi Yuwen Lian; Duke Zhuang of Ju Yuwen Luosheng; son Puti; Duke Zhong of Yuguo Yuwen Zhong; son Xing
entries.literal: Shifen's son Zhou; Dao's sons Guang, Liang, Yi, Chun, Zhong; Duke Jian of Qi Lian; Duke Zhuang of Ju Luosheng; son Puti; Duke Zhong of Yuguo Zhong; son Xing

entries.zh: 其秋，高祖幸雲陽宮，遂寢疾。
entries.en: That autumn High Ancestor Yuwen Yong visited Yunyang Palace and there fell gravely ill.
entries.literal: That autumn High Ancestor visited Yunyang Palace and there fell gravely ill.

entries.zh: 衞王直於京師舉兵反。
entries.en: Prince of Wei Yuwen Zhi raised troops in rebellion at the capital.
entries.literal: Prince of Wei Zhi raised troops in rebellion at the capital.

entries.zh: 高祖召憲謂曰：「衞王搆逆，汝知之乎？」
entries.en: High Ancestor Yuwen Yong summoned Yuwen Xian and said: "Prince of Wei Yuwen Zhi has plotted rebellion—do you know of it?"
entries.literal: High Ancestor summoned Xian and said: "Prince of Wei has plotted rebellion—do you know of it?"

entries.zh: 憲曰：「臣初不知，今始奉詔。
entries.en: Yuwen Xian replied: "Your servant at first did not know; now I have received the edict.
entries.literal: Xian replied: "Your servant at first did not know; now I have received the edict.

entries.zh: 直若逆天犯順，此則自取滅亡。」
entries.en: If Yuwen Zhi defies Heaven and violates order, this is to bring destruction upon himself."
entries.literal: If Zhi defies Heaven and violates order, this is to bring destruction upon himself."

entries.zh: 高祖：「汝即為前軍，吾亦續發。」
entries.en: High Ancestor Yuwen Yong said: "You shall be the forward army; I too shall follow in dispatch."
entries.literal: High Ancestor: "You shall be the forward army; I too shall follow in dispatch."

entries.zh: 直尋敗走。
entries.en: Yuwen Zhi soon was defeated and fled.
entries.literal: Zhi soon was defeated and fled.

entries.zh: 高祖至京師，憲與趙王招俱入拜謝。
entries.en: When High Ancestor Yuwen Yong reached the capital, Yuwen Xian with Yuwen Zhao, Prince of Zhao, both entered to bow in thanks.
entries.literal: When High Ancestor reached the capital, Xian with Zhao, Prince of Zhao, both entered to bow in thanks.

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「管蔡為戮，周公作輔，人心不同，有如其面。
entries.en: High Ancestor Yuwen Yong said: "Guan and Cai were executed; the Duke of Zhou then served as regent—hearts differ as faces differ.
entries.literal: High Ancestor said: "Guan and Cai were executed; the Duke of Zhou then served as regent—hearts differ as faces differ.

entries.zh: 但愧兄弟親尋干戈，於我為不足耳。」
entries.en: I only regret that brothers turned kinship to arms; for me this is not enough."
entries.literal: I only regret that brothers turned kinship to arms; for me this is not enough."

entries.zh: 初，直內深忌憲，憲隱而容之。
entries.en: Earlier Yuwen Zhi deeply resented Yuwen Xian inwardly; Xian concealed and tolerated him.
entries.literal: Earlier Zhi deeply resented Xian inwardly; Xian concealed and tolerated him.

entries.zh: 且以帝之母弟，每加友敬。
entries.en: Moreover, because Zhi was the emperor's younger brother by the same mother, Xian always treated him with friendship and respect.
entries.literal: Moreover as the emperor's younger brother by the same mother, he always treated him with friendship and respect.

entries.zh: 晉公護之誅也，直固請及憲。
entries.en: When Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu was executed, Yuwen Zhi firmly requested that Yuwen Xian be included.
entries.literal: When Duke of Jin Hu was executed, Zhi firmly requested that Xian be included.

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「齊公心跡，吾自悉之，不得更有所疑也。」
entries.en: High Ancestor Yuwen Yong said: "Yuwen Xian, Duke of Qi's intentions and conduct—I know them myself; there must be no further suspicion."
entries.literal: High Ancestor said: "Duke of Qi's intentions and conduct—I know them myself; there must be no further suspicion."

entries.zh: 及文宣皇后崩，直又密啟云：「憲飲酒食肉，與平日不異。」
