entries.en: When Empress Dowager Wenxuan died, Yuwen Zhi again secretly reported: "Yuwen Xian drinks wine and eats meat no differently from ordinary days."
entries.literal: When Empress Dowager Wenxuan died, Zhi again secretly reported: "Xian drinks wine and eats meat no differently from ordinary days."

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「吾與齊王異生，俱非正嫡，特為吾意，今袒括是同。
entries.en: High Ancestor Yuwen Yong said: "I and Prince of Qi Yuwen Xian were born of different mothers; neither of us was the legitimate heir; it was specially my wish—now baring the arm we are the same.
entries.literal: High Ancestor said: "I and Prince of Qi were born of different mothers; neither of us was the legitimate heir; it was specially my wish—now baring the arm we are the same.

entries.zh: 汝當愧之，何論得失。
entries.en: You ought to feel ashamed; why discuss gain and loss?
entries.literal: You ought to feel ashamed; why discuss gain and loss?

entries.zh: 汝親太后之子，偏荷慈愛。
entries.en: You are the empress dowager's own son and have received her loving care in special measure.
entries.literal: You are the empress dowager's son by partial favor and specially cherished.

entries.zh: 今但須自勗，無假說人。」
entries.en: Now you need only encourage yourself; do not borrow words to speak of others."
entries.literal: Now you need only encourage yourself; do not borrow words to speak of others."

entries.zh: 直乃止。
entries.en: Yuwen Zhi thereupon stopped.
entries.literal: Zhi thereupon stopped.

entries.zh: 齊煬王憲
entries.en: Prince Xian of Qiyang Yuwen Xian
entries.literal: Prince Xian of Qiyang Xian

entries.zh: 文帝十三子。
entries.en: Emperor Wen had thirteen sons.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen had thirteen sons.

entries.zh: 姚夫人生世宗，後宮生宋獻公震，文元皇后生孝閔皇帝，文宣皇后叱奴氏生高祖、衛剌王直，達步干妃生齊王憲，王姬生趙僭王招，後宮生譙孝王儉、陳惑王純、越野王盛、代奰王達、冀康公通、滕聞王逌。
entries.en: Consort Yao bore Shizong; ladies of the rear palace bore Duke of Song the Exalted Zhen; Empress Wen Yuan bore Emperor Xiaomin; Empress Wen Xuan of the Chilu clan bore Yuwen Yong (the future Emperor Wu) and Prince of Wei the Impetuous Zhi; Consort Tabghan bore Prince of Qi Yuwen Xian; a royal lady bore Prince of Zhao the Presumptuous Zhao; the rear palace bore Prince of Qiao the Filial Jian, Prince of Chen the Bewildered Chun, Prince of Yue the Wild Sheng, Prince of Dai the Proud Da, Duke of Ji the Peaceful Tong, and Prince of Teng the Cultivated You.
entries.literal: Consort Yao bore Shizong; the rear palace bore Duke of Song Xian Zhen; Empress Wen Yuan bore Emperor Xiaomin; Empress Wen Xuan, the Chilu clan, bore the High Ancestor and Prince of Wei Zhi; Consort Tabghan bore Prince of Qi Xian; a royal lady bore Prince of Zhao Zhao; the rear palace bore Prince of Qiao Xiao Jian, Prince of Chen Huo Chun, Prince of Yue Ye Sheng, Prince of Dai Yi Da, Duke of Ji Kang Tong, and Prince of Teng Wen You.

entries.zh: 齊煬王別有傳。
entries.en: Prince of Qi the Flamboyant (Yuwen Xian) has a separate biography.
entries.literal: Prince of Qi the Flamboyant has a separate biography.

entries.zh: 文閔明武宣諸子
entries.en: The Sons of Emperor Wen, Emperor Xiaomin, Emperor Ming, Emperor Wu, and Emperor Xuan
entries.literal: Princes of Wen, Xiaomin, Ming, Wu, and Xuan

entries.zh: 宋獻公震，字彌俄突。
entries.en: Duke of Song the Exalted Yuwen Zhen, styled Mi'etu.
entries.literal: Duke of Song the Exalted Zhen, styled Mi'etu.

entries.zh: 幼而敏達，年十歲，誦孝經、論語、毛詩。
entries.en: Clever and perceptive from childhood, at ten he could recite the Classic of Filial Piety, the Analects, and the Mao Odes.
entries.literal: Clever and perceptive from childhood; at age ten he could recite the Classic of Filial Piety, the Analects, and the Mao version of the Odes.

entries.zh: 後與世宗俱受禮記、尚書於盧誕。
entries.en: Later he and Shizong together studied the Record of Rites and the Venerated Documents under Lu Dan.
entries.literal: Later he and Shizong together received instruction in the Record of Rites and the Venerated Documents from Lu Dan.

entries.zh: 大統十六年，封武邑公，二千戶。
entries.en: In the sixteenth year of Datong (550), he was enfeoffed Duke of Wuyi with a fief of two thousand households.
entries.literal: In the sixteenth year of Datong, he was enfeoffed Duke of Wuyi, fief two thousand households.

entries.zh: 尚魏文帝女，其年薨。
entries.en: He married a daughter of Emperor Wen of Wei and died that same year.
entries.literal: He married a daughter of Emperor Wen of Wei and died that same year.

entries.zh: 保定元年，追贈使持節、柱國大將軍、少師、大司馬、大都督、青徐等十州諸軍事、青州刺史；
entries.en: In the first year of Baoding (561), he was posthumously granted bearer of the staff of authority, pillar-of-state grand general, junior preceptor, grand marshal, grand governor, commander-in-chief of military affairs in ten provinces including Qing and Xu, and governor of Qing Province;
entries.literal: In the first year of Baoding, he was posthumously granted bearer of the staff of authority, pillar-of-state grand general, junior preceptor, grand marshal, grand governor, commander-in-chief of military affairs in ten provinces including Qing and Xu, and governor of Qing Province;

entries.zh: 進封宋國公，增邑并前一萬戶。
entries.en: He was advanced to Duke of Song, the fief increased to ten thousand households in all.
entries.literal: He was advanced to Duke of Song state, the fief increased to ten thousand households in all.

entries.zh: 無子，以世宗第三子寔為嗣。
entries.en: Having no son, Shizong's third son Shi was made his heir.
entries.literal: Having no son, Shizong's third son Shi was made his heir.

entries.zh: 寔字乾辯，建德三年，進爵為王。
entries.en: Shi, styled Qianbian; in the third year of Jiande (574), he was advanced to prince.
entries.literal: Shi, styled Qianbian; in the third year of Jiande, he advanced in rank to prince.

entries.zh: 大象中，為大前疑。
entries.en: During Daxiang (579–581), he was grand front advisor.
entries.literal: During Daxiang, he was grand front advisor.

entries.zh: 尋為隋文帝所害，國除。
entries.en: Soon he was killed by Yang Jian; the fief was abolished.
entries.literal: Soon he was killed by Emperor Wen of Sui; the state was abolished.

entries.zh: 建德三年，進爵為王。
entries.en: In the third year of Jiande (574), he was advanced to prince.
entries.literal: In the third year of Jiande, he advanced in rank to prince.

entries.zh: 初，高祖以直第為東宮，更使直自擇所居。
entries.en: Initially Yuwen Yong had assigned Yuwen Zhi's residence as the Eastern Palace and had him choose another dwelling.
entries.literal: Initially the High Ancestor had given Zhi's residence as the Eastern Palace; he had Zhi choose his own dwelling anew.

entries.zh: 直歷觀府署，無稱意者，至廢陟屺佛寺，欲居之。
entries.en: Yuwen Zhi toured the government compounds and found none satisfactory; coming to the abandoned Siji Buddhist temple, he wished to live there.
entries.literal: Zhi went through all government offices and found none to his liking; arriving at the abandoned Siji Buddhist temple, he wished to live there.

entries.zh: 齊王憲謂直曰：「弟兒女成長，理須寬博，此寺褊小，詎是所宜。」
entries.en: Prince of Qi Yuwen Xian said to him: "Younger brother, your children are grown; they need room—this temple is cramped; how can it be suitable?"
entries.literal: Prince of Qi Xian said to Zhi: "Younger brother, your sons and daughters are grown; by reason they need spacious quarters—this temple is cramped; how is it suitable?"

entries.zh: 直曰：「一身尚不自容，何論兒女！」
entries.en: Yuwen Zhi said: "I can hardly fit myself—what of children!"
entries.literal: Zhi said: "One body cannot even accommodate itself—what talk of sons and daughters!"

entries.zh: 憲怪而疑之。
entries.en: Xian was startled and grew suspicious.
entries.literal: Xian was astonished and suspicious.

entries.zh: 直嘗從帝校獵而亂行，帝怒，對衆撻之。
entries.en: Yuwen Zhi once followed the emperor on a hunt and broke formation; the emperor was angry and had him beaten before the company.
entries.literal: Zhi once followed the emperor on a hunting review and went out of line; the emperor was angry and flogged him before the assembly.

entries.zh: 自是憤怨滋甚。
entries.en: From then his resentment deepened.
entries.literal: From then resentment and anger grew ever more.

entries.zh: 及帝幸雲陽宮，直在京師，舉兵反，攻肅章門。
entries.en: When the emperor was at Yunyang Palace, Yuwen Zhi was in the capital, raised troops in revolt, and attacked Suzhang Gate.
entries.literal: When the emperor visited Yunyang Palace, Zhi was in the capital and raised troops in rebellion, attacking Suzhang Gate.

entries.zh: 司武尉遲運閉門拒守，直不得入。
entries.en: Director of Martial Affairs Yuchi Yun shut the gate and held it; Yuwen Zhi could not enter.
entries.literal: Director of Martial Affairs Yuchi Yun closed the gate and held defense; Zhi could not enter.

entries.zh: 語在《運傳》。
entries.en: The account is in the "Biography of Yuchi Yun."
entries.literal: The account is in the "Biography of Yun."

entries.zh: 直遂遁走，追至荊州，獲之，免為庶人，囚於別宮。
entries.en: Yuwen Zhi then fled; pursued to Jing Province, he was captured, reduced to commoner status, and imprisoned in a separate palace.
entries.literal: Zhi then fled; pursued to Jing Province, he was captured, demoted to commoner, and imprisoned in a separate palace.

entries.zh: 尋而更有異志，遂誅之，及其子賀、貢、塞、響、賈、秘、津、乾理、乾璪、乾悰等十人，國除。
entries.en: Before long he showed further treasonous intent; he was executed together with his sons He, Gong, Sai, Xiang, Jia, Mi, Jin, Qianli, Qianzao, Qiancong, and ten others in all; the fief was abolished.
entries.literal: Soon he again harbored different intent; he was then executed, together with his sons He, Gong, Sai, Xiang, Jia, Mi, Jin, Qianli, Qianzao, Qiancong, and ten others in all; the state was abolished.

entries.zh: 趙僭王招，字豆盧突。
entries.en: Prince of Zhao the Presumptuous Yuwen Zhao, styled Douluotu.
entries.literal: Prince of Zhao the Presumptuous Zhao, styled Douluotu.

entries.zh: 幼聰慧，博涉羣書，好屬文。
entries.en: Clever from youth, widely read, and fond of literary composition.
entries.literal: Clever from youth, widely read in many books, fond of literary composition.

entries.zh: 學庾信體，詞多輕豔。
entries.en: He studied the style of Yu Xin; his diction was often light and ornate.
entries.literal: He studied the style of Yu Xin; his diction was often light and ornate.

entries.zh: 魏恭帝三年，封正平郡公，邑一千戶。
entries.en: In the third year of Emperor Gong of Wei (556), he was enfeoffed Duke of Zhengping with a fief of one thousand households.
entries.literal: In the third year of Emperor Gong of Wei, he was enfeoffed Duke of Zhengping commandery, fief one thousand households.

entries.zh: 武成初，進封趙國公，邑萬戶。
entries.en: At the beginning of Wucheng (559), he was advanced to Duke of Zhao with a fief of ten thousand households.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Wucheng, he advanced to Duke of Zhao state, fief ten thousand households.

entries.zh: 保定中，拜為柱國，出為益州總管。
entries.en: During Baoding (561–565), he was appointed pillar-of-state and went out as commander-in-chief of Yizhou.
entries.literal: During Baoding, he was appointed pillar-of-state and went out as Yizhou commander-in-chief.

entries.zh: 建德元年，授大司空，轉大司馬。
entries.en: In the first year of Jiande (572), he was granted grand minister of works and transferred to grand marshal.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jiande, he was granted grand minister of works and transferred to grand marshal.

entries.zh: 三年，進爵為王，除雍州牧。
entries.en: In the third year of Jiande (574), he was advanced to prince and made governor of Yong Province.
entries.literal: In the third year, he advanced in rank to prince and was made governor of Yong Province.

entries.zh: 四年，大軍東討，招為後三軍總管。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Jiande (575), when the great army marched east, Zhao served as rear third army commander-in-chief.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, when the great army marched east, Zhao was rear third army commander-in-chief.

entries.zh: 五年，又從高祖東伐，率步騎一萬出華谷，攻齊汾州。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Jiande (576), again following Yuwen Yong east, he led ten thousand infantry and cavalry out through Huagu to attack Qi's Fen Province.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, again following the High Ancestor east, he led ten thousand infantry and cavalry out through Huagu to attack Qi's Fen Province.

entries.zh: 及幷州平，進位上柱國。
entries.en: When Bingzhou was pacified, he advanced to senior pillar-of-state.
entries.literal: When Bingzhou was pacified, he advanced to senior pillar-of-state.

entries.zh: 東夏底定，又為行軍總管，與齊王討稽胡。
entries.en: When the eastern regions were settled, he again became mobile commander-in-chief and, with Prince of Qi Yuwen Xian, suppressed the Ji Hu.
entries.literal: When the eastern Xia was settled, he again became mobile commander-in-chief and, with Prince of Qi, suppressed the Ji Hu.

entries.zh: 招擒賊帥劉沒鐸，斬之，胡寇平。
entries.en: Zhao captured the bandit chief Liu Moduo and beheaded him; the Hu raiders were pacified.
entries.literal: Zhao captured the bandit chief Liu Moduo and beheaded him; the Hu raiders were pacified.

entries.zh: 宣政中，拜太師。
entries.en: During Xuanzheng (578), he was appointed grand preceptor.
entries.literal: During Xuanzheng, he was appointed grand preceptor.

entries.zh: 大象元年五月，詔以洺州襄國郡邑萬戶為趙。
entries.en: In the fifth month of the first year of Daxiang (579), an edict made Xiangguo commandery in Mozhou, with ten thousand households, Zhao's fief.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Daxiang, an edict made Xiangguo commandery in Mozhou, ten thousand households, Zhao's fief.

entries.zh: 招出就國。
entries.en: Zhao went out to take up his fief.
entries.literal: Zhao went out to take up his state.

entries.zh: 二年，宣帝不豫，徵招及陳、越、代、滕五王赴闕。
entries.en: In the second year of Daxiang (580), Emperor Xuan fell ill; Zhao and the princes of Chen, Yue, Dai, and Teng were summoned to court.
entries.literal: In the second year, Emperor Xuan was indisposed; Zhao and the princes of Chen, Yue, Dai, and Teng—five princes in all—were summoned to court.

entries.zh: 比招等至而帝已崩。
entries.en: By the time Zhao and the others arrived, the emperor had already died.
entries.literal: By the time Zhao and the others arrived, the emperor had already died.

entries.zh: 直高祖母弟，性浮詭，貪狠無賴。
entries.en: Yuwen Zhi was a uterine younger brother of the High Ancestor; by nature he was frivolous and deceitful, greedy and ruthless, and unrestrained.
entries.literal: Zhi was the High Ancestor's younger brother by the same mother; by nature he was frivolous and deceitful, greedy and ruthless, without restraint.

entries.zh: 以晉公護執政，遂貳於帝而昵護。
entries.en: Because Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu held the government, he sided against the emperor while currying favor with Hu.
entries.literal: Because Duke of Jin Hu held the government, he then turned against the emperor while drawing close to Hu.

entries.zh: 及沌口還，慍於免黜，又請帝除之，冀得其位。
entries.en: When he returned from Dun mouth, he resented his dismissal; he also urged the emperor to remove Hu, hoping to take his place.
entries.literal: When he returned from Dun mouth, he was angry at being dismissed; he also asked the emperor to remove Hu, hoping to obtain his position.

entries.zh: 帝夙有誅護之意，遂與直謀之。
entries.en: The emperor had long intended to kill Yuwen Hu; he then plotted with Yuwen Zhi.
entries.literal: The emperor had long harbored intent to execute Hu; he then plotted with Zhi.

entries.zh: 及護誅，帝乃以齊王憲為大冢宰。
entries.en: After Hu was executed, the emperor made Prince of Qi Yuwen Xian grand minister of war.
entries.literal: When Hu was executed, the emperor then made Prince of Qi Xian grand minister of war.

entries.zh: 直旣乖本望，又請為大司馬，意欲總知戎馬，得擅威權。
entries.en: Yuwen Zhi, disappointed in his original ambition, again asked to be made grand marshal, intending to command all military affairs and wield power at will.
entries.literal: Zhi, having missed his original hope, again requested to be grand marshal, intending to oversee all military affairs in general and wield authority at will.

entries.zh: 帝揣知其意，謂之曰：「汝兄弟長幼有序，寧可反居下列也？」
entries.en: The emperor perceived his intent and said to him: "You brothers have an order of senior and junior—how could you willingly rank below?"
entries.literal: The emperor guessed his intent and said to him: "You brothers have an order of seniority and juniority—how could you turn and stand below in rank?"

entries.zh: 乃以直為大司徒。
entries.en: He then made Yuwen Zhi grand minister of education.
entries.literal: He then made Zhi grand minister of education.

entries.zh: 隋文帝輔政，加招等殊禮，入朝不趨，劍履上殿。
entries.en: When Yang Jian (later Emperor Wen of Sui) directed the government, he granted Zhao and others extraordinary honors: they need not quicken their step at court and might enter the hall with sword and shoes.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui assisted the government, he added extraordinary honors for Zhao and others: they need not hurry in court audience and might wear sword and shoes in the hall.

entries.zh: 隋文帝將遷周鼎，招密欲圖之，以匡社稷。
entries.en: When Yang Jian was about to seize the Zhou throne, Zhao secretly plotted against him to save the dynasty.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was about to shift Zhou's mandate, Zhao secretly wished to plot against him to restore the altars of state.

entries.zh: 乃邀隋文帝至第，飲於寢室。
entries.en: He invited Yang Jian to his mansion and entertained him in the bedroom.
entries.literal: He then invited Emperor Wen of Sui to his residence and drank with him in the bedchamber.

entries.zh: 招子員、貫及妃弟魯封、所親人史冑，皆先在左右，佩刀而立。
entries.en: Zhao's sons Yuan and Guan, his consort's younger brother Lu Feng, and his confidant Shi Zhou stood by with swords drawn.
entries.literal: Zhao's sons Yuan and Guan and his consort's younger brother Lu Feng, together with his intimate Shi Zhou, were all beforehand at his side, wearing swords and standing.

entries.zh: 又藏兵刃于帷席之間，後院亦伏壯士。
entries.en: He also hid weapons in the curtains and bedding, and posted strong men in the rear courtyard.
entries.literal: He also hid weapons among the curtains and bedding; in the rear courtyard brave men lay in ambush as well.

entries.zh: 隋文帝從者多在合外，唯楊弘、元冑、冑弟威及陶徹坐於戶側。
entries.en: Most of Yang Jian's attendants waited outside; only Yang Hong, Yuan Zhou, Zhou's younger brother Wei, and Tao Che sat beside the door.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui's attendants were mostly outside the compound; only Yang Hong, Yuan Zhou, Zhou's younger brother Wei, and Tao Che sat by the door.

entries.zh: 招屢以佩刀割瓜啖隋文帝，隋文帝未之疑也。
entries.en: Zhao repeatedly cut melon with his belt knife and offered it to Yang Jian, who suspected nothing.
entries.literal: Zhao repeatedly used his girdle knife to cut melon and feed Emperor Wen of Sui; Emperor Wen of Sui did not suspect him.

entries.zh: 元冑覺變，扣刀而入。
entries.en: Yuan Zhou sensed danger, struck his blade, and entered.
entries.literal: Yuan Zhou sensed something amiss, knocked his knife and entered.

entries.zh: 招乃以大觴親飲冑酒，又命冑向廚中取漿。
entries.en: Zhao then personally offered Zhou a large cup of wine and ordered him to the kitchen for broth.
entries.literal: Zhao then personally drank to Zhou with a great goblet and also ordered Zhou to go to the kitchen for broth.

entries.zh: 冑不為之動。
entries.en: Zhou did not move.
entries.literal: Zhou did not stir for it.

entries.zh: 滕王逌後至，隋文帝降階迎之，元冑因得耳語曰：「形勢大異，公宜速出。」
entries.en: Prince of Teng You arrived later; Yang Jian went down the steps to greet him, and Yuan Zhou whispered: "Everything has changed—you must leave at once."
entries.literal: Prince of Teng You arrived afterward; Emperor Wen of Sui descended the steps to welcome him, and Yuan Zhou thus got to whisper in his ear: "The situation is greatly changed—you should leave quickly."

entries.zh: 隋文帝共逌等就坐，須臾辭出。
entries.en: Yang Jian sat briefly with You and the others, then excused himself and left.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui with You and the others took seats; after a little while he excused himself and went out.

entries.zh: 後事覺，陷以謀反。
entries.en: Later the plot was discovered; he was charged with treason.
entries.literal: Later the affair was discovered; he was framed on a charge of rebellion.

entries.zh: 其年秋，誅招及其子德廣公員、永康公貫、越攜公乾銑、弟乾鈴、乾鏗等，國除。
entries.en: That autumn Yang Jian executed Zhao together with his sons Duke of Deguang Yuan, Duke of Yongkang Guan, Duke of Yuexie Qianxian, and younger brothers Qianling and Qianheng; the fief was abolished.
entries.literal: That autumn he executed Zhao together with his sons Duke of Deguang Yuan, Duke of Yongkang Guan, Duke of Yuexie Qianxian, younger brothers Qianling and Qianheng, and others; the state was abolished.

entries.zh: 招所著文集十卷，行於世。
entries.en: Zhao's collected writings in ten scrolls circulated in his day.
entries.literal: Collected writings by Zhao in ten scrolls circulated in the world.

entries.zh: 譙孝王儉，字侯幼突。
entries.en: Prince of Qiao the Filial Yuwen Jian, styled Houyoutu.
entries.literal: Prince of Qiao the Filial Jian, styled Houyoutu.

entries.zh: 武成初，封譙國公，邑萬戶。
entries.en: At the beginning of Wucheng (559), he was enfeoffed Duke of Qiao with a fief of ten thousand households.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Wucheng, he was enfeoffed Duke of Qiao state, fief ten thousand households.

entries.zh: 天和中，拜大將軍，尋遷柱國，出為益州總管。
entries.en: During Tianhe (566–572), he was appointed grand general; soon transferred to pillar-of-state and went out as commander-in-chief of Yizhou.
entries.literal: During Tianhe, he was appointed grand general; soon transferred to pillar-of-state and went out as Yizhou commander-in-chief.

entries.zh: 建德三年，進爵為王。
entries.en: In the third year of Jiande (574), he was advanced to prince.
entries.literal: In the third year of Jiande, he advanced in rank to prince.

entries.zh: 五年，東伐，以本官為左一軍總管，攻永固城，拔之。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Jiande (576), on the eastern campaign, he served as left first army commander-in-chief, attacked Yonggu fortress, and took it.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, on the eastern campaign, with his existing office he was left first army commander-in-chief, attacked Yonggu fortress, and took it.

entries.zh: 進平并、鄴，拜大冢宰。
entries.en: Advancing, he helped pacify Bing and Ye and was appointed grand minister of war.
entries.literal: Advancing he pacified Bing and Ye and was appointed grand minister of war.

entries.zh: 是歲，稽胡反，詔儉為行軍總管，與齊王憲討之。
entries.en: That year the Ji Hu rebelled; an edict made Jian mobile commander-in-chief to suppress them with Prince of Qi Yuwen Xian.
entries.literal: That year the Ji Hu rebelled; an edict made Jian mobile commander-in-chief to suppress them with Prince of Qi Xian.

entries.zh: 有胡帥自號天柱者，據守河東，儉攻破之，斬首三千級。
entries.en: A Hu leader styling himself Heavenly Pillar held Hedong; Jian defeated him and took three thousand heads.
entries.literal: A Hu leader who styled himself Heavenly Pillar held Hedong; Jian broke him and beheaded three thousand.

entries.zh: 宣政元年二月，薨。
entries.en: In the second month of the first year of Xuanzheng (578), he died.
entries.literal: In the second month of the first year of Xuanzheng, he died.

entries.zh: 子乾惲嗣。
entries.en: His son Qianyun succeeded.
entries.literal: His son Qianyun succeeded.

entries.zh: 大定中，為隋文帝所害，國除。
entries.en: During Dading (581), he was killed by Yang Jian; the fief was abolished.
entries.literal: During Dading, he was killed by Emperor Wen of Sui; the state was abolished.

entries.zh: 陳惑王純，字堙智突。
entries.en: Prince of Chen the Bewildered Yuwen Chun, styled Yinzhitu.
entries.literal: Prince of Chen the Bewildered Chun, styled Yinzhitu.

entries.zh: 武成初，封陳國公，邑萬戶。
entries.en: At the beginning of Wucheng (559), he was enfeoffed Duke of Chen with a fief of ten thousand households.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Wucheng, he was enfeoffed Duke of Chen state, fief ten thousand households.

entries.zh: 保定中，除岐州刺史，加開府儀同三司。
entries.en: During Baoding, he was made governor of Qi Province and granted the Three Excellencies of the Opening Office.
entries.literal: During Baoding, he was made governor of Qi Province and granted the Three Excellencies of the Opening Office.

entries.zh: 使於突厥迎皇后，拜大將軍。
entries.en: Sent to the Turks to welcome the empress, he was appointed grand general.
entries.literal: Sent to the Turks to welcome the empress, he was appointed grand general.

entries.zh: 尋進位柱國，出為秦州總管，轉陝州總管，督鴈門公田弘拔齊宜陽等九城。
entries.en: Soon advanced to pillar-of-state; he went out as commander-in-chief of Qinzhou, transferred to Shanzhou, and supervised Yanmen Duke Tian Hong in capturing nine Qi cities including Yiyang.
entries.literal: Soon advanced to pillar-of-state; went out as Qinzhou commander-in-chief, transferred to Shanzhou commander-in-chief, and supervised Yanmen Duke Tian Hong in capturing nine Qi cities including Yiyang.

entries.zh: 建德三年，進爵為王。
entries.en: In the third year of Jiande (574), he was advanced to prince.
entries.literal: In the third year of Jiande, he advanced in rank to prince.

entries.zh: 四年，大軍東伐，純為前一軍總管。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Jiande (575), when the great army marched east, Chun was front first army commander-in-chief.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, when the great army marched east, Chun was front first army commander-in-chief.

entries.zh: 以帝寢疾，班師。
entries.en: Because the emperor fell gravely ill, the army withdrew.
entries.literal: Because the emperor fell gravely ill, the army withdrew.

entries.zh: 五年，大軍復東討，詔純為前一軍，率步軍二萬守千里徑。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Jiande (576), when the great army again marched east, an edict made Chun front first army, leading twenty thousand infantry to hold Qianli Path.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, when the great army again marched east, an edict made Chun front first army, leading twenty thousand infantry to hold Qianli Path.

entries.zh: 幷州平，進位上柱國，即拜幷州總管。
entries.en: When Bingzhou was pacified, he advanced to senior pillar-of-state and was at once appointed commander-in-chief of Bingzhou.
entries.literal: When Bingzhou was pacified, he advanced to senior pillar-of-state and was at once appointed Bingzhou commander-in-chief.

entries.zh: 宣政中，除雍州牧，遷太傅。
entries.en: During Xuanzheng, he was made governor of Yong Province and transferred to grand tutor.
entries.literal: During Xuanzheng, he was made governor of Yong Province and transferred to grand tutor.

entries.zh: 大象元年五月，以濟南郡邑萬戶為陳。
entries.en: In the fifth month of the first year of Daxiang (579), Jinan commandery with ten thousand households was made Chen's fief.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Daxiang, Jinan commandery with ten thousand households was made Chen's fief.

entries.zh: 純出就國。
entries.en: Chun went out to take up his fief.
entries.literal: Chun went out to take up his state.

entries.zh: 二年，朝京師。
entries.en: In the second year of Daxiang (580), he attended court in the capital.
entries.literal: In the second year, he attended court in the capital.

entries.zh: 時隋文帝專政，翦落宗枝，遂害純，并世子謙及弟扈公讓、讓弟議等，國除。
entries.en: At that time Yang Jian monopolized the government and cut away the imperial house; he killed Chun together with heir Qian and younger brothers Duke of Hu Rang and Rang's younger brother Yi; the fief was abolished.
entries.literal: At that time Emperor Wen of Sui monopolized the government and cut away the imperial branches; he then killed Chun, together with heir Qian and younger brothers Duke of Hu Rang and Rang's younger brother Yi; the state was abolished.

entries.zh: 越野王盛，字立久突。
entries.en: Prince of Yue the Wild Yuwen Sheng, styled Lijiutu.
entries.literal: Prince of Yue the Wild Sheng, styled Lijiutu.

entries.zh: 武成初，封越國公，邑萬戶。
entries.en: At the beginning of Wucheng (559), he was enfeoffed Duke of Yue with a fief of ten thousand households.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Wucheng, he was enfeoffed Duke of Yue state, fief ten thousand households.

entries.zh: 天和中，進爵為王。
entries.en: During Tianhe (566–572), he was advanced to prince.
entries.literal: During Tianhe, he advanced in rank to prince.
